# Treatise

...they are <note>original: *ri⁹* (completing a word from the previous page, likely *hiberni*) </note> cold and wintry; and because the affinity between these figures, which arises from opposition, is not suitable and is unfortunate.

And because Saturn is naturally cold, and this is [opposed] to heat, and his sphere is more removed from the spheres of the Luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> than any of the others, they gave him Capricorn and Aquarius as his houses, which are opposite to Cancer and Leo; for these two signs, namely Capricorn and Aquarius, are cold and wintry. And also, because they are figured with the form of opposition, their participation is harmonious.

He <note>The commentator</note> wishes to say that the work of Saturn is to make things cold, and he causes dryness by accident through his great coldness. For this reason, he called it "winter cold" so it might stand out from any other description. Since Saturn is cold and dry, he does not harmonize with the wintry signs which are cold and moist. He also said that Saturn’s sphere is the most distant from the spheres of the Luminaries. He means that nature placed his sphere further from the Earth than any other so that, through this distance, the cold on Earth might be diminished. And because Capricorn and Aquarius are wintry and cold signs, it was necessary for his coldness to be of a very great degree, fitting for Saturn. And because these two signs are opposite to the houses of the two Luminaries, and the Luminaries cause all generation and the growth of things, it was necessary for these two signs to cause corruption and such diminution as befits the work of Saturn. Therefore, for this reason, they gave Saturn Capricorn and Aquarius as houses: because his nature is the opposite of the nature of the Luminaries. And because Capricorn is wintry and the Sun is hot and dry, while Saturn is cold and dry, he [Saturn] is at home in Capricorn <note>original: *cacꝛo*, likely a scribal error for *capricorno*</note> and causes cold because it is wintry. And Aquarius, because it is in the lunar half, needed to be moist; and by tempering the great coldness of Saturn, it is [relatively] warm. For this reason, **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer</note> says that the ancient sages said Saturn works better in Aquarius than in Capricorn and rejoices more in it, because the heat and moisture of Aquarius greatly diminish his great cold and dryness. Saturn also moistens by accident sometimes, as we said before. Likewise, because Saturn is masculine and diurnal, Aquarius suits him better. For this reason, they said that Aquarius is the indicator of running waters, such as springs and streams.

And because Jupiter is of a temperate complexion, and his sphere is beneath that of Saturn, the two signs that follow Capricorn and Aquarius—namely Sagittarius and Pisces—were attributed to him. This is because they produce winds and compel all things [to grow]; and because they are at a trine <term>trine: a harmonious astrological aspect where two signs are 120 degrees apart</term> distance from the houses of the Luminaries, which is suitable and fortunate.

And because Jupiter is of a temperate complexion and is below the sphere of Saturn, they gave him the two signs located around Capricorn and Aquarius, which are Sagittarius and Pisces, pertaining to the winds of generation. They are at the length of a trine from the houses of the two Luminaries, which is the distance of concord and fortune.

When he said that Jupiter is under the sphere of Saturn, he means that nature ordered Jupiter below Saturn so that his tempering influence might diminish the harm of Saturn's coldness. And what he says about Sagittarius and Pisces pertaining to winds and generation can be understood because the ancient sages found it to be so through experience. It can also be understood because when the Sun is in Sagittarius, it is the end of autumn, and then the dryness ends and the moisture begins, from which winds are made and many things are generated. Pisces is also the end of winter, where the cold ceases and heat begins, whence winds and many other things arise. And the winds which **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the *Tetrabiblos*</note> attributes to Jupiter act through his vapors, such as the generative vapors of phlegm and the seeds of others. For we see animals and plants grow mostly during these two times; for when the Sun is in Sagittarius, seeds for the most part begin to be born. And when it is in Pisces, it is so great... And because the trine is an aspect of concord and fortune, it is because these signs harmonize in one nature with the two signs of the Luminaries. And Jupiter’s sphere follows that of Saturn, and Jupiter creates winds by which things are generated. The ancient sages gave these two signs to Jupiter because his temperance harmonizes with the two Luminaries in all good and fortune. And for this reason, he says that Sagittarius is in accord with the nature of the 

<column-break/>

Sun, because Jupiter has a participation in it with the Sun. Likewise, Pisces is in accord with the nature of the Moon because Jupiter has a participation in it with the Moon. And because Jupiter is [the ruler] of these things and of stable things, when they are mixed with others similar to themselves, they grow in their goodness and profit. For this reason, **Dorotheus** said that Jupiter rejoices more in Sagittarius than in Pisces, because Jupiter is masculine and diurnal, tending more toward the nature of the Sun, and Sagittarius is of this nature.

After these, however, because Mars naturally dries things out, and his sphere is under Jupiter's sphere, he [nature] wished to give him the two signs located after Jupiter's dwellings: these are Aries and Scorpio. Their distance from the houses of the Luminaries is quadrate <term>quadrate: also known as a 'square,' a 90-degree angle considered tense or destructive</term>, just as befits a destructive and contradictory quality, for it is likened to the nature of Mars.

Likewise, because Mars dries naturally, and his sphere is truly under the sphere of Jupiter, they gave him the two signs held together with the two signs of Jupiter, which are Aries and Scorpio, distant from the houses of the Luminaries by a fourth-part distance <note>90 degrees</note>, which results in corruption and loss. For such a thing belongs to the nature of Mars.

He means that because Mars dries so much, he naturally exceeds in misfortune and harm. Nature placed his sphere under Jupiter's sphere so that with his heat he might help in diminishing the vanity of Saturn's coldness. And for this reason, they gave him the two signs held with those of Jupiter. These are distant from the houses of the Luminaries by the fourth distance, which is the distance of corruption and enmity, which belongs to the nature of Mars. And because Scorpio is [related] to this house of the Sun <note>original: *h̃u’ domui solis*, likely referring to the aspectual relationship</note>, it results that it is cold and moist, thereby diminishing the harm of Mars' dryness. For this same reason, Mars is nocturnal. Likewise, Aries, because it is [related] to this house of the Moon, results in being hot and dry. For this reason, **Dorotheus** said that Mars rejoices more in Scorpio than in Aries, because it is nocturnal like himself and his nature is tempered in it.

Venus’s star, which is of a temperate complexion and revolves under the sphere of Mars, was attributed the two signs that follow Mars' habitations, because they make things arise; these are Taurus and Libra. Their distance from the houses of the Luminaries is a sextile <term>sextile: a 60-degree angle representing harmony and opportunity</term>, which is the distance of similarity and suitability. And because Venus is never found to be more than two signs distant from the Sun.

And because Venus is temperate and her sphere is under the sphere of Mars, they gave her the two signs held together with the two signs of Mars, and they are generative signs: Libra and Taurus. They are distant from the two signs of the Luminaries by a sextile distance, which is of concord and friendship. And also because Venus is never distant from the Sun in any of the two parts by more than two signs.

Because Venus is temperate, it follows that she should have houses that harmonize with the houses of the two Luminaries. Likewise, because Libra is [the sign] in which the day is equal with the night, it harmonizes with animals, plants, and all generation. Likewise, because Taurus is the sign in which the time of spring is firmed, it is suitable for those things we have said. For this reason, it follows that the two houses of Venus are Taurus and Libra because of the concord that is between them and the two Luminaries. It also follows that Libra is hot, masculine, and diurnal, as pertains to the Sun; and that Taurus is feminine and nocturnal, as pertains to the Moon. And not without reason did nature act, for Venus is never distant from the Sun beyond the space between her houses and the houses of the Luminaries in this concord. And she helps the Sun to do good through her moisture, which diminishes the dryness of the Sun. Whence **Dorotheus** said that Venus rejoices more in Taurus than in Libra because of the concord she has with the nature of the Moon.

Finally, since of the wandering stars <note>planets</note> Mercury remained, who is never distant from the Sun in either direction by more than the space of one sign, and is carried under the other stars, the two remaining signs were given to him, which are located after the Luminaries...

...and they are Gemini and Virgo.
¶ And because Mercury is one of the <term>erratic stars</term><note>The "wandering stars" or planets.</note> and never moves away from the sun at any time in either direction by more than one sign: because he is lower than the other planets, they gave him the two remaining signs which border the houses of the two luminaries: and they are Gemini and Virgo.
¶ For the temperament of Mercury was made such that he does not stray from the sun by more than one sign, so that his power might mix with the power of the sun: and he placed his sphere below the spheres of the other planets so that his nature might turn toward the nature of whichever planet he applies to, changing the power of the sun according to the movement of that planet. And because of this, it happens that the houses of Mercury are the midpoint between fortune and misfortune, and between agreement [and disagreement]: because the sign of Gemini does not have an agreement with Cancer, as they do not "behold" <note>Original: *aspiciūt*. In astrology, signs "behold" each other if they form a geometric aspect.</note> each other, but it agrees with Leo by a <term>sextile aspect</term><note>An aspect of 60 degrees, considered harmonious.</note>. And the sign of Virgo has no agreement with Leo because they do not behold each other, but it agrees with Cancer because they behold each other in a sextile. And because of this, Virgo is of the sun's nature and Gemini of the moon's nature. Whence <note>original: *Doroth²*</note> Dorotheus said that Mercury rejoices more in Virgo than in Gemini because of the kinship of Virgo with the sun’s nature: for the sun is always firm in one state, and Mercury is not. For he indeed placed a temperament in these houses between the others: because they placed the two houses of Venus as agreeing with the houses of Jupiter, and the two houses of Mars as disagreeing with the houses of Saturn because of their contrary natures; and he placed the houses of Mercury in a different category: because Gemini disagrees with Sagittarius, and agrees with Aries, Libra, Aquarius, and Leo. And Virgo disagrees with Pisces and Sagittarius, and agrees with Scorpio, Capricorn, and Taurus, as suits the nature of Mercury.

### On the triplicities and their lords. Chapter 19.

-> Haly says. <-

**In ordering** the lords of the <term>triplicities</term><note>Groups of three signs of the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note> there were various opinions among astrologers: for one sect of them says they ought to be ordered after the houses, as Ptolemy does; and others are those who order them after the lords of the <term>terms</term><note>Subdivisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets.</note>; and commonly before. Those who speak in the first way say this: that the power of a planet in its own house is like the power of a man in his own house, who goes wherever he wishes and does what pleases him. And the power of a planet in its triplicity is like the power of a man among his vassals and helpers. And the power of a planet in its exaltation is like the power of a man in his kingdom. And the power of a planet in its term is like the power of a man in his village: and the power of a planet in its <term>face</term><note>The smallest subdivision of a sign, also called a decan.</note> is like the power of a man in his craft. And according to this they said that the power of the lord of the triplicity follows the power of the lord of the house. And in this Dorotheus agrees in the chapter on form. For I will tell you how you shall act and you will not err: look to the sign and the degree: and if it happens that there is in it any of the lords of the dignities, or that [the lord] beholds it, whatever it may be, you shall accept that place above all; and if it happens that there are 2 or 3 or more there, look closely to use the greater and give it lordship rather than the weaker.

<image-desc>Decorative initial letter T featuring a man's face wearing a hood or skullcap.</image-desc> **The Triplicities'** affinities with the planets are good. Since, therefore, the figure of an equilateral triangle is in itself equal and fitting.

¶ The agreement of the triplicities with the planets is because the figure of a triangle with equal sides is in itself harmonious and equal.

**He wishes** to say that a triangle of equal sides also has equal angles. And when the zodiac is divided into a triangle, each angle of the triangle falls upon a sign of such a nature as the other two angles. And thus the agreement of the two signs is equal: so that if one of them is masculine and diurnal, the other two will be as well; and if it is feminine, the other two will be feminine.

¶ And because three circles are the boundaries of the zodiac circle: namely the equinoctial circle and the two solstitial circles.

¶ And because the angles determining the zodiac are three: and these are the two circles of the tropics.

<column-break/>

¶ He wishes to say that the greater circle of the zodiac is that in which all the stars move upon two poles from the east to the west, determining three parallel circles: the greatest of these is the equinoctial circle; the other two are equal; one passes through the head of the summer tropic, and the other through the head of the winter tropic.

¶ To divide the twelve parts of the zodiac circle into four equilateral triangles.

¶ And he divides the firmament through twelve parts into four triangles of equal sides.

¶ He wishes to say that the 12 signs are divided between any two of those circles into three equal signs. And the first of them falls upon one of those three circles, and the last upon the circle that follows. And according to this, the first of the fourth sign will be upon the second circle. And thus it happens that the 12 signs are divided into four triangles of equal sides. And when we join the words of Ptolemy and look well into them, we shall know the reason before us; and these triangles have a prerogative and greater force than the signs falling upon the angles of a hexagon of equal sides.

¶ Therefore the first triplicity consists of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius: which are masculine signs; and they are the dwellings of the Sun, Jupiter, and Mars.

¶ The first triangle is Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius: and the first signs are masculine, and the houses of the Sun, Jupiter, and Mars.

¶ See how Ptolemy first began with the Sun, according to the order by which he always accustomed to begin through the significance of the Sun.

¶ Wherefore they gave this triplicity to the Sun and Jupiter, Mars being rejected, because Mars is of a <term>haiz</term><note>Original: *haiz*. An Arabic astrological term referring to a planet's "sect" or preferred condition (e.g., a diurnal planet in a diurnal sign above the horizon by day).</note> and not the Sun's <term>haiz</term>.

¶ And because of this they placed these three signs for the Sun and Jupiter and not Mars: because Mars is of a different <term>haiz</term> than the Sun.

¶ Since Aries is the house of Mars, and it falls in the half of the luminaries in the triplicity of the house of the Sun and the house of Jupiter (which is in the solar half), and Mars is in a different <term>haiz</term> from the nature of the Sun and Jupiter; and this triplicity is diurnal; and Mars being of the "corruptors," it was fitting that the first governor of this triplicity be the Sun, and afterward Jupiter, without Mars.

¶ The first lord of this triplicity is the Sun by day, but Jupiter by night. The sign of Aries also follows the equinoctial circle; and Leo is closest to the summer circle. Sagittarius, however, exists closer to the winter circle. This triplicity is also northern, because Jupiter has lordship there; Aries is also a sign of the equinoctial circle and compels things to rise, as well as bringing northern winds.

¶ The governor of this triplicity is the Sun by day, and Jupiter by night: for Aries follows the equinox, and Leo is more around the summer tropic, and Sagittarius around the winter tropic; this triplicity is northern because of the power it has there and it creates northern winds.

¶ He wishes to say that Jupiter makes northern winds like generative winds; he placed this triplicity as northern. And other astrologers hold that this triplicity is eastern because of the governance the Sun has there; yet Ptolemy's view is more direct, because the Sun performs natural works. And after Jupiter has a participation with him in this triplicity, he draws those same natural works toward a nature pertaining to himself.

¶ Except that when the house of Mars is in it, which is said to have a partnership there with the northern wind, they are somewhat mixed from the west. Wherefore that same wind is gathered from a mixture of the north and west. For Mars brings winds of this kind; also the western part is feminine.

### Treatise

...in which way <term>sect</term><note>Original: *haiz*. An Arabic astrological term referring to a planet being in a favorable "home" or condition based on day/night and gender.</note> exists in this triplicity, so that it is composed of North and West winds: because Mars generates such winds, and the Western part is feminine. And the reason why Mars rules in the Western part is because his temperament is balanced by the great moisture found there, for the Moon appears there after exiting from beneath the sun’s rays. It is clear that **Ptolemy** holds that Mars shares in the governance of this triplicity with the Sun and Jupiter. However, others hold that Saturn is the chief ruler, believing this triplicity to be Eastern. Indeed, the words of Ptolemy are more to be believed, for they come through many experiences combined with rational arguments; and we have seen, even to this day, that what he says agrees through experience with what we have spoken.

The **second triplicity**, which is gathered from the three feminine signs—namely **Taurus**, **Virgo**, and **Capricorn**—is assigned to the Moon and Venus, because it belongs to the <term>sect</term> of the Moon. Of this triplicity, the ruler by day is the Moon, and by night, it is Venus.

The second triangle, composed of the three feminine signs of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn, is given to the Moon and Venus: because they are nocturnal planets, which is the sect of the Moon; and the governors of the entire triplicity are the Moon by night and Venus by day.

Observe first how he spoke of the Moon, since she is nocturnal. Taurus is closer to the **summer circle** <note>The Tropic of Cancer.</note>, Virgo to the **equinoctial circle**, and Capricorn to the **winter circle** <note>The Tropic of Capricorn.</note>.

Taurus is more toward the summer circle, Virgo more toward the equinox circle, and Capricorn more toward the winter circle.

Taurus is not more toward the summer circle than the equinox. The same reasoning applies to Leo, Aquarius, and Scorpio regarding the winter circle; he wished to bring to our minds the solar half and the lunar half. Because Leo is in the solar half, he placed it more toward the summer circle. And because Taurus is in the lunar half, he likewise placed it more toward the summer circle, since at that time the works of the two luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> appear most clearly. He did the same in Scorpio and Aquarius, because they are the houses of the two **malefics** <note>original: *infortunas*. Saturn and Mars.</note>; for the nature of the two malefics agrees with the winter circle, because that part of the earth is depopulated <note>Likely referring to the harsh, uninhabitable cold of the deep south/winter.</note>.

Moreover, this triplicity is more associated with the South because Venus rules in it; for this star brings such winds, because her power effects this through heat and moisture.

And this triplicity belongs more to the South because of the power Venus has in it; since this planet generates such winds, because her virtue produces such a thing with her heat and moisture.

He has already said that Venus is of a temperate complexion, and a temperate complexion is one in which there is natural heat and moisture.

Except that because of the house of Saturn, which is Capricorn, and because of his partnership in it, the winds born of this triplicity will be gathered from the South and the East, in a manner contrary to the first triplicity: for this reason, Saturn brings Eastern winds, because he belongs to the sect of the Sun.

And because Capricorn is the house of Saturn, due to the participation he has in this triplicity, the winds of this triplicity were Southern and Eastern, contrary to the first triplicity: because Saturn generates Eastern winds, as he is of the Sun's sect.

Because Saturn creates a slight dryness such as is the dryness of the Sun. And Saturn is to the Sun as the sect of the Sun is. And because Eastern winds are dry winds, it happens that the Sun and Saturn generate them. This is the opinion in which he differs from other astrologers regarding this triplicity. For astrologers hold that Mars is the partner of Venus and the Moon in

<column-break/>

governing this triplicity: because Capricorn is his **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet's influence is particularly strong, distinct from its 'house'.</note>.

Ptolemy holds that Saturn is the partner in this triplicity of Venus and the Moon: because Capricorn is his house; and his governance is more direct, because the power of a lord in his own house is greater than the power of a lord in his exaltation.

The **third triplicity**, which is gathered from the three masculine signs—namely **Gemini**, **Libra**, and **Aquarius**—is attributed to Saturn and Mercury, because their houses are contained within it.

The third triangle, which is composed of the three masculine signs of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius, belongs to Saturn and Mercury: since these two have more houses in this triplicity.

And even if Venus has a house in this triplicity <note>Libra.</note>, it does not follow that she has governance in it: because she is feminine and nocturnal.

Moreover, the diurnal ruler of this is Saturn, since he is of the day sect; and the nocturnal ruler is Mercury.

And the governor of this triplicity by day is Saturn: because he is of the day sect; and by night, it is Mercury.

Because Mercury is of a diverse nature and Saturn is diurnal, it follows that Mercury governs this triplicity by night: and likewise because he is of a weaker power than Saturn.

The sign of Gemini is more toward the summer circle; Libra follows the equinoctial circle; and Aquarius is considered closer to the winter circle. This triplicity is more associated with the East wind, because of the lordship of Saturn; and Jupiter is likened to Saturn in sect, for he is diurnal; the winds that come about by occasion of this triplicity will be between the North and the East.

And the sign of Gemini is more toward the summer circle; the sign of Libra follows the equinox; and the sign of Aquarius is more toward the winter circle. Whence this triplicity results more in the East wind <note>original: *vētō oriētali*</note> because of the governance Saturn has there; and because Jupiter is of such a sect as Saturn—since he is diurnal—the winds of this triplicity become between the East wind <note>original: *solanum*</note> and the North-West wind <note>original: *zierzum / cierzo*</note>.

Because Venus has no lordship in this triplicity and Mercury is of a mixed complexion, and none of the masculine planets remain except Jupiter: it follows that in governing this triplicity, he is the partner of Saturn and Mercury. Because the Sun does not have [power] in this triplicity, as he has only one house. It is clear that he [Ptolemy] disagrees with other astrologers in all of this triplicity; but he does not disagree on the part where he rules, since they say it is Western, and Ptolemy holds it to be Eastern because of the lordship Saturn has there; and he holds that Mercury has greater power when he is Eastern than when he is Western. In this place there is one doubt: for some have asked how Jupiter makes North-West winds <note>original: *çierços*</note> since he is hot and moist; the answer is this: because the North-West wind is healthier and more beneficial in preserving health, as physics says, and such things belong to Jupiter.

The **fourth triplicity** is made by **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. It remains, therefore, that they should be under Mars, and that he should exercise lordship in it, because Scorpio is his domicile.

The fourth triangle, which is made of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces, remained for Mars so that he might have governance in it: because Scorpio is his house.

He means that because Mars has no power in the other triplicities, he has dignities in this triplicity: one because Scorpio is his house and he rejoices in it; another because he is nocturnal just as this triplicity is; they gave it to him so that he might govern it by day and by night.

There are associated with him in lordship, because of the sect and because these signs are feminine: by night, the Moon; by day, Venus. And this...

# First [Book]

And she [the Moon] has participation with him [Mars] in governing it for this reason: because these signs are feminine, the Moon by night and Venus by day.

¶ **Ptolemy** holds that the lord of this triplicity by day and by night is **Mars** alone; however, **Venus** is his partner by day, and the **Moon** by night. He claims this triplicity is **Western** because of the governance that Mars, Venus, and the Moon have there. It is clear that its western nature is certain in this regard. Nevertheless, the **Society of Astrologers** <note>This refers to the common consensus of medieval astrologers, often following the Persian or Arabic tradition, which differed from Ptolemy's specific system.</note> holds that Venus governs this triplicity by day and Mars by night, and that the Moon is the partner by day and by night. Likewise, they claim this triplicity is **Northern**; but their opinion is false, as there is no reasoning for it. Therefore, it follows that you should follow the opinion of Ptolemy, because he alone is certain, while all the others are empty and deceptive.

¶ **Cancer** likewise belongs to the summer [circle], and **Scorpio** to the winter [circle], while **Pisces** exists closer to the equinoctial circle.

¶ And the sign of Cancer is more toward the summer circle <note>The Tropic of Cancer</note>; Scorpio is toward the winter circle <note>The Tropic of Capricorn</note>; and Pisces is toward the equinox.

¶ Ptolemy noted these three circles in the triplicities to demonstrate the superiority that the **trine** <note>An aspect of 120 degrees</note> has over the **sextile** <note>An aspect of 60 degrees</note>; because these three circles determine the zodiac, it follows that the trine possesses great improvement and power over the sextile.

¶ Indeed, this triplicity produces Western winds because of the lordship of Mars and the Moon within it; and because Venus is associated with it, the wind will be gathered from the West and the South.

¶ And this triplicity generates the Western wind because of the governance that Mars and the Moon have there; however, because of the participation that Venus has with them, it becomes a composite wind of the West and the **Abrego** <gloss>that is, the South</gloss> <note>Original: "abrego .i. meridionali." Abrego is a traditional name for the South-West wind, here simplified as Southern.</note>.

### On Exaltations. Chapter 20.

<margin>Haly said.</margin>
<margin>Ptolemy.</margin>
[He] holds that the power of the lords of **exaltation** <note>A specific sign where a planet is thought to be "raised" to its highest dignity and strength.</note> follows the power of the lords of the triplicity; and you will understand this when you look at his words.

<image-desc>A decorative drop-cap 'I' featuring a figure in academic or clerical robes, possibly a scholar, holding a book and pointing upwards.</image-desc>
**I**ndeed, they ignore the manner in which the exaltations of the **luminaries** <note>The Sun and Moon</note> and the wandering stars [planets] are described; they are as if subjugated. For when the **Sun** is in the sign of **Aries**, he will be changed toward the higher, northern half of the circle. And when he enters the sign of **Libra**, he directs his journey toward the lower, southern half of the circle.

¶ And the signs which are called the exaltations of the two luminaries and the wandering planets are described in this manner. When the Sun is in Aries, he moves toward the half of the zodiac that is high and northern; and when he is in Libra, he moves toward the half of the zodiac that is southern and low.

->**High** and **low**, as it is said, is the status pertaining to the Sun because of<-
the population of the earth: for when the head of Aries is at our zenith [head], it is the head of the dragon <note>An astronomical reference to the intersection of the ecliptic and the lunar path, but here used to describe the Sun's ascending path</note>; for when the Sun reaches that point and passes through it, he moves toward the northern part. The head of Libra is the tail; for when the Sun reaches it and passes through, he moves toward the southern parts; and the status of the Sun and his power appear greater in the North.

¶ For this reason, they placed the Sun's exaltation in the sign of **Aries**, in which the length of the days and the increase of their natural heat begins; they said **Libra**, however, would be his **fall** <note>Original: *casum*. The sign opposite the exaltation, where a planet's power is most diminished.</note> because of the opposition to the aforementioned conditions.

¶ And because of this, they placed the Sun's exaltation in Aries, where the length of the day and the increase of his natural heat begins, and Libra as his fall, because of

<column-break/>

the contrary reasons we have stated.

¶ He [the author] means to say that the ancient wise men found that when the Sun enters Aries, the day begins to become longer, and in the populated [parts] of the earth, natural heat increases; and going upward toward its peak, they established Aries as the house of his exaltation. They made Libra his fall because then the night begins to become longer, the heat diminishes, and cold is strengthened in the populated parts of the earth; the Sun goes toward the unpopulated part of the earth and toward his depression, which is opposite his peak.

¶ **Saturn**, however, so that his distance from the Sun might be in opposition—just as it is in the [planetary] houses—took the sign of **Libra** for his exaltation and **Aries** for his fall, because where heat increases, cold is released, and where cold is intensified, heat is released.

¶ And so that the distance of Saturn from the Sun might be an oppositional distance, just as it is in the houses (because where heat increases, cold diminishes, and where cold increases, heat diminishes), they placed Libra as his exaltation and Aries as his fall.

¶ This is because an oppositional distance is a distance of corruption and contrariety; because of this, it follows that where heat diminishes, cold begins, which is in Libra; and that Libra is the fall of the Sun and the exaltation of Saturn; and Aries, which is the exaltation of the Sun, is the fall of Saturn. Thus the entire nature of the Sun is contrary to the nature of Saturn, just as they have established in [the nature of] things. In this place, Ptolemy follows his own rules, so that all the natures of the stars follow the nature of the Sun.

¶ Likewise, when the **Moon** has been in the sign of Aries with the Sun (which is his exaltation), since after this she will specifically appear in **Taurus**, where the increase of her light will be as if at its beginning, her exaltation was placed in Taurus, which is the first sign of her own triplicity. In the sign of **Scorpio**, however, which is formed in opposition to that, her fall is designated.

¶ Similarly, after the Moon is with the Sun in Aries (which is his exaltation), she first appears in Taurus and her light begins to grow; and since that is her beginning according to her birth, they placed her exaltation in Taurus, and it is the first sign of her own triplicity. Therefore, according to this, they placed her exaltation in this sign, and Scorpio, which is the opposite of this sign, as her fall.

¶ Because the Moon follows the status of the Sun and her house holds with his, it follows that her exaltation holds with his. And because the first appearance of the Moon's light is when she is born [the New Moon], and Taurus is the first of her triplicity, it follows that Taurus is her exaltation; for when the Sun is in Aries (which is his exaltation), the first of the Moon's light and her status will be in Taurus. And because Scorpio is in the opposite figure, it follows that it is her fall; and by this reasoning, they said that the seventh sign from a planet's house is its misfortune because of the contrariety that exists in them.

¶ But **Jupiter** is the author of northern winds, which they cause to be required; and since his own power appears when he is in the greatest northern declination (which is in **Cancer**), and he produces northern winds, they granted the sign of Cancer as his exaltation and **Capricorn** as his fall.

¶ And because Jupiter creates northern winds that generate things, when he is in the North, he is well-inclined toward that part; and when he is in Cancer, he shows his own power and creates northern winds; because of this, they placed his exaltation in Cancer.

¶ The ancient wise men did this because they saw that the status of Jupiter appears more when he is in Cancer, and he is weakened when he is in Capricorn; for Jupiter, because he is of a temperate nature, is suitable for habitation and generation, and for moving the temperate northern winds from the northern part toward the inhabited [lands]. # Treatise

<note>original: "Iupiter" abbreviated as "ter"</note> **Jupiter** is present and has a stay in it: the work is greatly strengthened, and its own power in causing all things to be born and grow is increased. Nor is there any other sign at the end of the north except Gemini and **Cancer**. Gemini does not belong to him because it is opposite his own house, which is Sagittarius, in the fourth <note>referring to the fourth quadrant or aspect</note> of Pisces. Cancer, however, suits him more because of the **Moon**; for the temperament of the Moon's nature is agreeable to the nature of Jupiter. Furthermore, the great heat and dryness of **Leo** does not suit him. Therefore, for all these reasons, it is fitting in every way that the **exaltation** <term>Exaltation: a specific zodiac sign where a planet's influence is considered to be at its most powerful and harmonious.</term> of Jupiter be Cancer, and its **fall** <term>Fall: the sign opposite a planet's exaltation, where its influence is weakened.</term> be **Capricorn**, because it is the opposite.

¶ **Mars**, however, since he is naturally scorching—and especially when he is in Capricorn, because his declination is then in the southern part—is exalted in Capricorn, which is contrary to Jupiter's exaltation; he falls, however, in Cancer.

¶ And because Mars is burning by nature, and especially when he is in Capricorn he scorches much more because he leans toward the southern part, they placed his exaltation in Capricorn, opposite the exaltation of Jupiter, and his fall in Cancer.

¶ The southern part, which is very hot, suits the nature of Mars, which is scorching. Indeed, in this place, nature wished to temper the power of Mars, because this part is desolate, and because the nature of Mars is contrary to the nature of Jupiter. Therefore, for two reasons, it is fitting that the exaltation of Mars be Capricorn, which is the end of the south, and his fall be Cancer, so that his nature may be in every way contrary to the nature of Jupiter.

¶ Again, because **Venus** naturally moistens, especially in the sign of **Pisces**, in which the humidity of spring appears and her natural power begins to grow, she is exalted in Pisces and falls in **Virgo**.

¶ Similarly, because Venus naturally moistens, and especially when she is in Pisces, because the beginning of spring's humidity appears in it, and there her own power grows; for this reason, her exaltation is in Pisces and her fall is in Virgo.

¶ When Venus enters Pisces, her own power appears because she naturally accords with Pisces, since it is feminine and nocturnal; and in it, the temperate humidity of spring begins to appear. Her nature accords with Jupiter because it is his house; and the limit of her exaltation is the house of the Moon, which are two planets that accord with the nature of Venus. For this reason, it follows that the sign of Pisces should be the exaltation of Venus, and Virgo the fall, because Virgo is contrary to Pisces and is naturally dry.

¶ **Mercury**, however, because he dries out, is exalted in the sign of Virgo, where autumn (which is dry) begins to appear; whereas his own power grows again in the humidity of spring, his fall is in the sign of Pisces.

¶ Because Mercury dries by himself, and in this he is [contrary to] the moisture of Venus, it is fitting that his exaltation be in Virgo, which begins to appear in autumn, which is dry. For in Virgo, his own power grows, being contrary to the nature of Venus; and his fall is in Pisces.

¶ Now **Ptolemy** has taught us that Mercury works more in drying than in moistening, and that he accords more with **Saturn** than with Jupiter, and more with the **Sun** than with the **Moon**; for the two houses of Mercury are in good aspect and accord with the two houses of Saturn, and they are here with their power. Similarly, because autumn always begins in Virgo and is dry and sometimes cold and sometimes hot by the nature of Mercury. And because Mercury is strengthened and his work appears near in Virgo. And because when the Sun is in his house, he appears in the evenings in Virgo, which is his house; for these reasons, it follows that Virgo is his exaltation and Pisces his fall.

### On the Terms. Chapter 21.

->Haly said:<-

**P**erceived through this arrangement, we understand that the power of the lord of the **term** <term>Terms (or Bounds): subdivisions of a zodiac sign (not equal in size) governed by different planets, affecting how a planet behaves while in those degrees.</term> follows the power of the lord of the exaltation.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Ornate decorative initial 'T' inside a square frame with floral scrollwork.</image-desc>
**T**here are indeed two modes of **Terms**. One of these is called **Egyptian**, the other **Chaldean**. The Egyptian system is chiefly taken from the lords of the houses. The Chaldean, however, is assumed from the lords of the **triplicities**.

¶ Terms are of two manners. One is accepted according to the Egyptians; the other according to the Chaldeans. That which is accepted according to the Egyptians is taken from the lords of the houses. The Chaldean, however, is taken from the lords of the triplicities according to the governances of the triplicities.

**I**ndeed, those of Egypt were wise masters who lived in ancient times. For they were of great study and exercise in all sciences and wisdoms by which a person can be helped; and we know this through the chronicles of the ancient wise men who spoke of them, and through those of their works which have remained from many thousands of years ago until the present day. Nevertheless, I will say what I saw from one experience I found in the place called the **Eye of the Sun** <note>original: "oculus solis"</note>, because in a short time I saw great miracles. And the **Chaldeans** are those of **Babylonia** who were followers of the Egyptians in the science of astronomy. For Ptolemy says that the Egyptians took the terms mostly according to the lordships of the houses. For this reason, some astrologers preferred them over those that are according to the lords of the triplicities.

¶ But the Egyptian [system] does not always truly change in its orders, nor in the quantities of each, that which is generally set down as a root in the modes of the terms. For they attribute the first [terms] in order to the lords of the houses, and sometimes to the triplicity, and sometimes to the lords of the exaltations; as in **Libra**, they began not with Venus but with Saturn; in **Aries**, they began not with Mars but with Jupiter. If therefore they followed the lords of the triplicities and no others, why in **Capricorn** did they take the beginning from Mercury and not from Venus? Likewise, if they followed the lordships of the exaltations and no others, why in **Cancer** did they start with Mars and not with Jupiter? Again, if in these they followed only the planets whose strengths were the greatest of those predicted, why in **Aquarius** did they make the beginning from Mercury, who only has triplicity in it, and not from Saturn, who possesses both the house and the triplicity there? Also in Capricorn, they began with Mercury, who has no authority there. The order of the remaining terms is found in this same way. Also, in the quantities of the terms, they seem to observe no order. For in the number of all these terms which is collected for each of the planets—which they announce to be of the same quantity as the number of years of that same planet—there is no reason by which the quantity of life may be proven according to this. But if we should say and grant that the number collected from there is true, or affirmed by the Egyptians, the same number might perhaps be collected even if the quantities of the terms were varied in many and diverse ways.

¶ Nevertheless, according to the opinion of those of Egypt, they do not follow the matter generally, because they did not set down a certified sequence as a root, neither in the arrangement nor in the quantity of any of them. Because first they placed in their arrangement the lords of the houses in some of them, and in others they placed the lords of triplicities, and in others the lords of exaltations. And according to this, they placed Saturn first in Libra, and did not place Venus; and they placed Jupiter first in Aries and did not place Mars. Therefore, if they follow the modes of triplicities, why did they place Mercury first in Capricorn, and did not place Venus first?

<meta>This page continues the critique of the "Egyptian Terms"—specific segments of zodiac signs assigned to different planets—questioning the logical consistency of how these segments and their lengths were determined by ancient astrologers.</meta>

# First Book

And if they follow the lords of exaltations <note>original: "exaltatõis"</note>: why did they place **Mars** first in **Cancer**, and not **Jupiter**? And if they follow in this the planets having more dignities: why did they first place **Mercury** in **Aquarius**, who has nothing there except a single triplicity <term>Triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</term>, and not **Saturn**, who has both a house and a triplicity? And why did they first place **Mercury** in **Capricorn**, who has no dignity in governing this sign? For in this manner, one finds whatever arrangement of terms they made; it also seems that in the quantity of the terms they observed no rule, nor in the number which is joined to each of these planetary terms. For they hold their number to be as many as their years; and he who divides by these find neither reason nor demonstration signifying that life can be that long. And yet, if we were to say that the number is so great—and what those from **Egypt** say is the truth—such a number could easily be reached by changing the quantity of the signs in various ways.

¶ Those of **Egypt** hold that the "greater years" of the planets are as many as each has from the degrees through the terms in all the signs. And that each planet, when it rules in a life and is powerful, gives its greater years to that life. And **Ptolemy** <note>original: "pto."</note> says that in this number there is no reason, nor any natural logic that could signify the time of life is so great. And indeed, this number would be as they said; the number of degrees could well be changed in various ways, and it would still agree with this same number. And through this, it is seen that those of **Egypt** did not follow a single rule for the terms, just as they did not follow one in arranging them. Wherefore this was nothing else than that they had received the terms from another source.

¶ Certain people, however, who seem to affirm this for themselves by a physical reason that they think is sufficient, say that when the times of the ascensions <term>Ascension: The time it takes for a zodiac sign or a portion of it to rise above the eastern horizon.</term> of the terms of each planet are collected, one and the same quantity would be born from them in all climates; which is clearly shown to be false. For in this they have followed what is found in the books of the ignorant, and they took equal additions for the ascensions; but no one doubts that this is contrary to all truth. For it is found in this book that the ascensions of **Virgo** and **Libra** on the equinoctial line <note>The celestial equator.</note>, which passes through the lower part of the Egyptian region, are for each of the two aforesaid signs 37 times and a third <note>In ancient astronomy, "times" refer to degrees of right ascension.</note>; and that the ascensions of each of the two signs **Leo** and **Scorpio** are 35 times. But by geometrical reasoning it is proved that **Leo** and **Scorpio** ascend in more than 35 times, and **Virgo** and **Libra** ascend in less than the aforesaid times. Likewise, those who [seek] this

<column-break/>

to bring forth a reason: they have not followed the quantity of terms which many men have affirmed. In many places also, it is found necessary to lie. But so that their opinion might appear firmer at **Rome**, they divided degrees into minutes; yet we do not for this reason affirm them to be truthful, but rather most deceitful in this, as we said before. However, their terms, which we here blame for the aforesaid reasons, are these as they stated below.

¶ And there were some who wished to state one reason for this, making a likeness of truth through philosophy. For they said that when we add the times of the ascensions of the terms for any planet, it would be one and the same quantity through all climates—and this is a lie. For in this they followed the books of the unskillful who followed equal additions in ascensions for every place; and this is a matter which has no way of being seen as the truth in any respect. For in their books it is found that the ascensions of **Virgo** and **Libra** on the line equidistant from the equinox <note>The equator</note>, which passes through the greater part of the land of **Egypt**, are for each of these two signs 37 degrees and a third; and that the ascensions of **Leo** and **Scorpio** are 35 degrees. And it is already demonstrated by demonstrations of geometry that **Leo** and **Scorpio** ascend in a greater portion of time; because of which they said more in these things that they wished to show, they did not follow the quantity of terms which many have stated. And it is found that they must of necessity lie in many places; or divide the degrees of the terms into minutes to affirm their statement; and with all this, they did not follow the truth, as we said before.

¶ Those who wished to test the terms of the **Egyptians** did not follow the quantity of the degrees of the terms; for the Egyptians spoke and in many places had to lie of necessity, and divide degrees into minutes, which indeed cannot be done in the terms; and with all this, they did not follow the truth, as **Ptolemy** proved. And all these words which **Ptolemy** said, he said for the sake of demonstrating to us that the terms of the Egyptians are not accepted by any rule. And all other terms are after this manner, without any order or rule.

¶ However, the total collected from the aforesaid degrees of each of these planets is this: For **Saturn**, fifty-seven; for **Jupiter**, 79; for **Mars**, 66; for **Venus**, 82; for **Mercury**, 76; the sum of all of which is 360 degrees.

¶ The degrees which are joined to each of the planets are these: To **Saturn**, 57; to **Jupiter**, 78 <note>The text here says 78, though the previous paragraph said 79; 79 is required to reach the sum of 360.</note>; to **Mars**, 66; to **Venus**, 82; to **Mercury**, 76. All these make 360 degrees.

# Treatise

¶ This completes Ptolemy’s <note>Claudius Ptolemy, a 2nd-century scholar whose work "Tetrabiblos" defined Western astrology.</note> discussion on the terms of the Egyptians.

¶ Another method, which they call the Chaldean <note>Refers to the ancient Babylonians, often considered the founders of mathematical astrology.</note>, is reasoned through the lords of the triplicities <term>Triplicity: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element: Fire (Aries, Leo, Sagittarius), Earth (Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn), Air (Gemini, Libra, Aquarius), and Water (Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces).</term>. They find the reasons for this method to be more fitting and sufficient; nonetheless, the planets that rule the triplicities do not always follow a consistent order or quantity.

¶ There is another manner of the Chaldeans who say the reasoning lies in those who rule the triplicities, and their reasoning is clearer; however, it does not perfectly follow the planets governing the triplicities in either order or quantity.

¶ Whoever wishes to follow the opinion of the Chaldeans <note>original: "f mini chaldeoz," likely "finem" or "famam," meaning the tradition or goal of the Chaldeans.</note> finds it is governed with more reason, though it is arranged differently; for some planets rule by day and others by night. Similarly, each of their planets has different quantities [of degrees].

¶ Their opinion can be commended briefly and without labor to the memory. For the first triplicity, which consists of **Aries**, **Leo**, and **Sagittarius**, the division of terms for each of its signs is one and the same. Indeed, they give the first term to the lord of the triplicity, which is **Jupiter**. The second to the lord of the following triplicity, which is **Venus**. The third and fourth to the two lords of the triplicity of **Gemini** [Air], which are **Saturn** and **Mercury**. The fifth they give to the lord of the remaining triplicity, which is **Mars**.

¶ And because of this, the word of these men can be known for certain, liberally and without the need for books, concerning the terms in each of the signs of the [Fire] triplicity—**Aries**, **Leo**, and **Sagittarius**: for it is the same shared arrangement. It places the first term with the lord of the triplicity, **Jupiter**; then the second term with the lord of the triplicity that follows it, **Venus**; afterward, the third and fourth terms with the two lords of the **Gemini** triplicity, **Saturn** and **Mercury**; and finally the fifth term with the lord of the other triplicity, **Mars**.

¶ For they equate among themselves the seven planets that are swift in their motions within their dignities. Afterward, they give half of the sphere to the **Sun** and the other half to the **Moon**. And they assigned the dignity of the terms to the other planets in place of these, the **Sun** and **Moon** being excepted. And for this reason, the ancient wise men said that the significance of the **Sun** when it is in its own half, and the **Moon** when in hers, is equal to the significance of the planets when they are in their own terms. And because of this, the Chaldeans spoke through the triplicity term of **Jupiter**, and assigned nothing to the **Sun**, as it is not meant to have a term; and they assigned the second term to **Venus**, who is mistress of the second triplicity; and the third term they assigned to **Saturn** (who rules by night with **Mercury**), and the fourth term they assigned to **Mercury** (who rules by night with **Saturn**); and the fifth term they assigned to **Mars**, who is lord of the fourth triplicity. They followed this same reasoning for the other triplicities.

¶ Now for the second triplicity, which is gathered from **Taurus**, **Virgo**, and **Capricorn**: they use one and the same division for each of these signs. They assign the first term to **Venus** because of her lordship over it. The second and third they assign to the two lords of the **Gemini** triplicity, which are **Saturn** and **Mercury**; after these, they assigned the fourth to **Mars**, and the remainder to **Jupiter**.

<column-break/>

¶ And for the second triplicity, which is **Taurus**, **Virgo**, and **Capricorn**: they also gave each of these signs one and the same arrangement. They place the first term with **Venus**, who is mistress in this triplicity; they place the second and third terms with the two lords of the **Gemini** triplicity, who are **Saturn** and **Mercury**; and they place the fourth with **Mars**, and the other with **Jupiter**.

¶ If you have understood well everything said before, you do not need a gloss <note>An explanatory note or commentary.</note>; if you did not understand, I tell you that since the first triplicity belongs to **Venus** and the **Moon**, and the **Moon** has no part in the terms, it follows that **Venus** is the mistress of the first term of this triplicity. And that the second term is the term of **Saturn** by day and **Mercury** by night; and the third is the term of **Mercury** by day and **Saturn** by night; and the fourth term is of **Mars**, who is lord of the fourth triplicity; and the fifth term is of **Jupiter**, who rules in the triplicity of **Leo**.

¶ They followed this order most especially in the two remaining triplicities; except that for the third triplicity, which is said to have two lords, namely **Saturn** and **Mercury**: **Saturn** takes the first part in the day, but **Mercury** in the night.

¶ This arrangement goes as is typical in the other two triplicities; and in the third triplicity which has two lords, **Saturn** and **Mercury**, they take the first dignity from **Saturn** by day and from **Mercury** by night.

¶ The Chaldeans followed this same aforementioned way in the arrangement of the terms for the triplicity of **Cancer** [Water]. And because they found the lords of the **Gemini** triplicity to be **Saturn** by day and **Mercury** by night, they placed **Saturn** as lord of the first term of the signs of this triplicity by day, and lord of the second by night. And they placed **Mercury** as lord of the second term of the signs of this triplicity by night, and lord of the second by day. And they placed the third term with **Mars**, who is lord of the fourth triplicity, which is **Cancer**. And they placed **Jupiter** as lord of the fourth triplicity, and **Venus** as mistress of the fifth. And in the fourth triplicity, they placed **Mars** as lord of the first term; and by reason, the lord of the second; and **Venus** the mistress of the third; and **Saturn** the lord of the fourth by day and the fifth by night; and **Mercury** the lord of the fourth by night and the fifth by day.

¶ Regarding the method of the quantities of the terms found in each sign, which observes the aforementioned order, it is a single and manifest rule; their quantities do not differ except by an equal decrease. For each of the terms decreases in quantity by one degree from the one preceding it. They set the first term of each sign at 8 degrees; the second at 7; the third at 6; the fourth at 5; and the fifth at 4, which completes the total of 30 degrees.

¶ And the quantity of the signs runs plainly in each sign and follows the first arrangement we spoke of before. The diversity of its quantity is by an equal lessening: so that each of the terms is diminished from the term before it by one degree. They set the first [term] of any sign at 8 degrees, the second at 7, the third at 6, the fourth at 5, and the fifth at 4, by which they complete 30 degrees.

<summary>This page describes the "Chaldean Terms," a system of dividing each zodiac sign into five segments ruled by different planets. Unlike the Egyptian system, the Chaldean method uses a strict mathematical descent (8, 7, 6, 5, 4 degrees) and bases the order of planets on the lords of the four triplicities.</summary>

# First

¶ Many have spoken well on this subject: that the first ruler of each triplicity <term>Triplicity: A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</term>, since it belongs to the lord of that same triplicity, happens to have a greater share there than all the others. And because the second triplicity is read as such, and the third, and the fourth, there is one triplicity that has two lords, and the second is weaker than the first. Since there are no more than 30 degrees in any sign, it happens that between one and another there is an improvement of one degree. Because of this, the first gets eight degrees and the second seven, and so on according to the ordering of this method.

**1. The first triplicity: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius.** The lords of their terms by day for each of these three signs are: **Jupiter** (8), **Venus** (7), **Saturn** (6), **Mercury** (5), **Mars** (4). By night: **Jupiter** (8), **Venus** (7), **Mercury** (6), **Saturn** (5), **Mars** (4).

**2. The second triplicity: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn.** They have their bounds as follows: By day: **Venus** (8), **Saturn** (7), **Mercury** (6), **Mars** (5), **Jupiter** (4). By night: **Venus** (8), **Mercury** (7), **Saturn** (6), **Mars** (5), **Jupiter** (4).

**3. The third triplicity: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius.** The lords of their terms by day: **Saturn** (8), **Mercury** (7), **Mars** (6), **Jupiter** (5), **Venus** (4). By night: **Mercury** (8), **Saturn** (7), **Mars** (6), **Jupiter** (5), **Venus** (4).

**4. The fourth triplicity: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces.** The lords of their terms by day: **Mars** (8), **Jupiter** (7), **Venus** (6), **Saturn** (5), **Mercury** (4). By night: **Mars** (8), **Jupiter** (7), **Venus** (6), **Mercury** (5), **Saturn** (4). The terms of the Chaldeans <note>The Chaldeans were famous ancient astronomers from Mesopotamia.</note> are arranged in this manner, and there are those who say these terms are better because they say the beginnings of signs are the terms of the "fortunes" <note>The "fortunes" or benefics are Jupiter and Venus, considered lucky planets.</note> and the ends are the terms of the "infortunes" <note>The "infortunes" or malefics are Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with hardship.</note>. We wish to know which opinion of the ancients records their saying.

¶ From all of these, in the day they collect 78 degrees for **Saturn**. In the night, however, 66; for **Jupiter**, 72; for **Mars**, 60; for **Venus**, 75; for **Mercury** in the day 66, but in the night 78.

¶ And to those they add: for **Saturn** by day 77 degrees, and by night 76; and for **Jupiter**, 76; and for **Mars**, 60; and for **Venus**, 75; and for **Mercury** by day 71 and by night 78.

¶ This means to say that the number of degrees for the terms of each planet according to the Chaldeans is different from the number of degrees according to the Egyptians. Since there is such diversity among the ancient sages in the number of the "greater years" <term>Greater Years: A specific span of time assigned to a planet in ancient astrology, used to predict the length of a person's life.</term> of the planets, if those who were intelligent and learned erred so, what will become of us in understanding such a thing?

¶ Between these two, that which was said by the Egyptians agrees more with the truth. This is because the authors of the Egyptian books collected these from what they found recorded in actual nativities <note>A "nativity" is a birth chart or horoscope of a specific person.</note> and wrote them in their books according to the exemplary way they had ordered the degrees of the terms in the works they possessed.

¶ However, the most certain of these opinions we have mentioned is according to the terms of the Egyptians; because the Egyptians compiled books and placed them in their libraries. They took this from what they found said in the nativities which they had arranged as examples through the degrees of the terms in the places where it was appropriate for them.

¶ After he clarified to everyone what was in the terms, he wanted to show us in this place which opinion is most certain. He said that the aforementioned terms of the Chaldeans have a rule that confirms their experience; nonetheless, it does not agree with them, nor did the ancient sages experience them so. We find, however, that the terms of the Egyptians—although they are accepted without a formal rule—are found to be true through experience.

¶ And since those who composed the books did not write down the order of the terms, nor did they number them in any of their books, doubts and deceptions are necessarily found in them.

¶ And because these compilers of books did not place the arrangement of terms there, nor did they name them in their books, it was inevitable that doubt and error would occur in this matter.

¶ He means to say that because the Egyptian compilers did not put the experiences in their books through which they knew the arrangement of the terms—and how many degrees each sign had—doubt occurred there in two ways. One, because perhaps some found them

<column-break/>

afterwards and we do not understand it; the other, because even if it were so, we cannot fully trust what we find therein. This is what Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the famous 2nd-century mathematician and astronomer.</note> said regarding the ancient sages.

¶ We, however, found in a certain very ancient book—the greater part of which had been consumed and perforated by extreme age—the terms. In this book, that which pertained to the order and quantity of the terms had been arranged naturally and reasonably. Likewise, we found in it the degrees of the aforementioned nativities, and also how many each of the planets should have, agreeing with what is found in the books of the ancients.

¶ We found an ancient book about the terms which was itself very old for the most part and broken. Whatever was said there concerning their arrangement and quality followed a natural rule. We also found in it the degrees of nativities which we mentioned before, and the sum that each planet had; it recorded the same as what the books of the ancient sages said.

¶ Many say that what was found in that book was according to a rule and a natural matter, and that the ancient sages had tested it. They knew the certainty of this by verifying and experiencing it. They set down the things they had experienced more than what agreed with the terms of the Egyptians, and the sum of the degrees for each planet agreed with the "greater years" of that planet.

¶ There was also in it a very long discourse in which these terms were proven by many reasons. But on account of its extreme age and the frequent perforation of the leaves <note>This refers to the manuscript being "worm-eaten" or damaged by insects over the centuries.</note>, we were unable to copy it out. All its reasons seemed difficult and obscure to us. Nevertheless, the parts of the terms which helped us greatly to understand this had remained at the end of the book, whole and without damage. Whatever we found of the terms there is added in this place.

¶ And there were in this book very long words and a demonstration of much superfluity, and we were unable to grasp them because the book was broken. It was difficult for us to give a demonstration based on those long reasons. However, because the division of the terms remained at the end of the book, we found that it was neither unorganized nor corrupted. This helped us much in understanding the reasoning; and whatever I found in the book itself concerning the reasoning of the terms was what I shall say.

¶ These words demonstrate the great goodness of Ptolemy and how much he loved the truth; for he did not wish to attribute the glory of others' words to himself, nor was he ashamed to say openly that he could not provide the explanation for those long reasons written in that book.

¶ In the order, he considered in each of the signs the lord of the exaltation, the triplicity, and the house <term>Dignities: These are "strengths" a planet has. A planet is strong if it is in the sign it rules (House), the sign where it is honored (Exaltation), or a sign of its element (Triplicity).</term>. Whichever of them had two of these powers in the sign, even if it were a malefic <note>The "malefics" are Saturn and Mars.</note>, it preceded in the order. But if such a malefic was not found, it was arranged at the end of the signs. Otherwise, the lords of the exaltation preceded, followed by those of the triplicity, and then the lords of the houses followed according to the order of the signs.

¶ And the arrangement in each sign looked to the lord of the exaltation, the triplicity, and the house. Whichever planet they found having two dignities in the sign, they placed first, even if it happened to be a malefic. And if it did not have two, and it was a malefic, they placed it at the end of the sign. They put the lord of the exaltation first, then the lord of the triplicity, then the lord of the house, following the order of the signs.

¶ By this, we understand that these terms of which Ptolemy speaks...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "Bounds" or "Terms"—the specific degrees of a zodiac sign assigned to a planet. Having previously discussed the Chaldean and Egyptian systems, the text now explains Ptolemy’s reasoning for his own system, which seeks to reconcile these ancient traditions through a set of consistent "natural" rules.</meta>

# Treatise

... because they were not truly his own; for if they were his own, he would not have prioritized the lord of exaltation <note>original: "dominum exaltationis"</note> over the lordship of the triplicity and the lordship of the house. For all astrologers agree that the lord of the house, whom those men neglected, should be placed before all others. Since they were discovered through this good man, they attributed them to him, because they knew the name of the wise man who wrote that very book. And it is manifest that Ptolemy confirms these terms and holds them to be correct because they agree greatly with the terms of the Egyptians and similarly agree with the terms of the Chaldeans. And because, in the sum of the degrees of any of the planets, he agrees with their "greater years" <note>A planet’s "Greater Years" refers to a specific span of time used in ancient astrology to predict lifespans or major eras.</note>, and because experience agrees with them.

¶ Whoever had two "powers" <term>Dignities or powers: Various ways a planet can have a special relationship with a sign, such as being its home (house), being honored there (exaltation), or belonging to its elemental group (triplicity).</term> in a sign was placed before the one having only one power in the order—except in Leo and Cancer, which are the domiciles of the Sun and Moon. Because terms are not assigned to these two luminaries, they ascribed the first term of each sign to one of the malefics <note>original: "infortunarum"; the "unlucky" planets, Saturn and Mars.</note>. For they gave the first term of Cancer to Mars, and the first of Leo to Saturn. The order of these two planets is displayed in these two signs because in all other signs they were placed at the very ends.

¶ And they prioritize those having two dignities in a sign over those who held Cancer and Leo; for these are the houses of the two luminaries, and they did not give any term to the luminaries. They placed the first term of each of these signs under one of the malefics, and thus they gave the first term of Cancer to Mars and of Leo to Saturn, and they ordered them first in these two signs.

¶ Some wise men did not give any power in the terms to the Sun and Moon because of the dignity they already hold in the two halves of the zodiac. And the rule followed what was said before: that the first term of Cancer belongs to Jupiter, who is the lord of exaltation; and that Mars is the lord of triplicity; and that they placed him at the end of all the signs. They held that it was better to give the first term of Cancer to Jupiter himself. This now agrees with the opinion of the Egyptians and Chaldeans. However, that Saturn should be the first lord of the first term of Leo is not a natural reason, since that sign is of his own nature <note>original: "naturae suae"; referring to the elemental qualities of the sign and the planet.</note> and does not agree with the opinion of the Egyptians or the Chaldeans. But because Ptolemy loved the truth and did not want to change anything he found written by the ancient sages, he placed them in his book exactly as he found them from the ancient sages. Therefore, according to the rule he understood, we hold that the first term of Leo belongs to Jupiter, who is the lord of the triplicity, and in this, the wise men affirm themselves with Ptolemy. And they said this was the only difference—that these terms belong to Ptolemy, and this agrees with the rule given by the Egyptians and Chaldeans.

¶ The method for determining the quantity of degrees in the terms is as follows: when two powers were found for any of the planets, either in the same sign or in the following signs up to the fourth sign, if it were one of the two benefics <note>original: "fortunas"; the "lucky" planets, Jupiter and Venus.</note> (which are Jupiter and Venus), they assigned seven degrees to it. If, however, it were one of the two malefics (which are Saturn and Mars), they gave it five degrees. To Mercury, however, because he is of a mixed nature, they attributed six degrees, which completes the 30 degrees of a sign.

¶ In this way, they established the quantity of the terms when planets were not found to have two dignities in the same sign or in other signs following the rules up to the fourth sign. If it was one of the two benefics, which are Jupiter and Venus, they gave it seven degrees; and if it was one of the two malefics, which are Saturn and Mars, they gave it five degrees. To Mercury, because he shares characteristics with both, they gave six degrees, making up the full 30 degrees.

¶ Because they naturally follow one another in one way, and always in the 4th sign there

<column-break/>

falls a manifest change for each of them, they established two terms from this according to the ordering of the signs. They gave a larger portion to the benefics than to the malefics, because the nature of the benefics is close to the nature of the two luminaries, each of which holds half of the firmament. And because Mercury is between the benefics, being of an equal number, and similarly between the malefics—even though Mercury is between them—they found no number by which the 30 degrees could be divided in this way except 4, 5, and 6. Thus, two benefics have 14 degrees (2x7), the two malefics have 10 (2x5), and Mercury has 6, totaling 30.

¶ And because some of them have two powers—such as Venus, who has both her house and triplicity in Taurus—her power was increased in it. Therefore, because the Moon has nothing in the terms, one of her degrees is added to those planets so situated, whether in the same sign or in the following ones up to the fourth. We also found in the aforementioned book a single point marked above each of these. Therefore, that degree which is added to the term of a planet having two powers was taken away from the remaining terms of planets having only one power there. It was taken first from Mars or Saturn, then from Jupiter, because their motion is slower. These terms are ordered thus:

¶ Since some of them have two dignities, and because the luminaries have no part in the terms, they added one degree to each planet in such a condition, whether it was in the same sign or up to the fourth sign by the ordering of the signs. We found in that book a mark with a single point above each of these. The degrees they added to the planets having two dignities they subtracted from the others who had only one dignity; and for the most part, they subtracted from Saturn and Jupiter because their motions are slower. The writing of these terms was in this manner:

¶ If you have understood well what was said by Ptolemy regarding these terms, you will find there the rational basis for addition and subtraction, and why they placed some before or after others. For example: because Saturn has two dignities in the sign of Libra, which are exaltation and triplicity, they added one degree to him, making six. They placed him first, because the lord of exaltation is prioritized over the lordship of the triplicity, and the lord of the triplicity is prioritized over the lordship of the house. The second sign is Scorpio, and Mars has two dignities in it, which are house and triplicity; because of this, they added one degree to him, making six. But they placed him last, because the benefics ought to be prioritized over the malefics, and because his nature is very distant from that of Saturn. The third sign from Libra is Sagittarius, and Jupiter has two dignities there, which are triplicity and house; according to his rule, it follows that they should add one degree to him, but they placed him later because of his slow motion. The fourth sign from Libra is Capricorn, and Venus has one dignity in it, which is triplicity. There remained no planets except Venus and Mercury, and only 10 degrees. Mercury is the lord of the triplicity of Libra by night, and Venus is the lady of the triplicity of the fifth sign; because of this, they divided the 10 degrees between them equally. They prioritized Venus because she is a benefic and lady of the house, and they placed Mercury immediately after her because he holds the triplicity in Libra by night. They placed Jupiter after Mercury because he has a greater dignity in Libra than Jupiter. And because benefics must be placed before malefics, they placed Mars at the very end. They followed this rule in all other signs.

¶ From these, when brought together into one total: 57 are assigned to Saturn, 66 to Mars, 82 to Venus, 76 to Mercury, and 79 to Jupiter. When collected together, these make 360 degrees.

¶ According to this, the sum of the degrees held: Saturn 57, Jupiter 79, Mars 66, Venus 82, Mercury 76. The sum of all: 360 degrees.

It concludes with the specific total degree counts for each of the five non-luminary planets across the entire 360-degree zodiac.</summary>
