<meta>This page continues the commentary on Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, moving from the general characteristics of peoples to the specific astrological governance of the four quarters of the inhabited world. It focuses on the "triplicities" (groups of three zodiac signs) and how they correspond to geographic regions.</meta>

# Treatise

Ptolemy did not wish to speak specifically of individual cities; nevertheless, at the end of his words, he provided a reason and a rule by which we can know under what government any city falls. He named those things which cannot be changed, and these are the provinces. In this way, he acts as a wise and well-founded philosopher.

<image-desc>An ornamental drop cap 'Q' contains a small circular diagram with a grid or cross, likely representing the divisions of the zodiac or the world.</image-desc> Since, therefore, the figures of the **triplicities** <note>Groups of three zodiac signs belonging to the same astrological element</note> that are formed in the circle of the signs are four, as was shown in the preceding sections: We have said that the triplicity of **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius** lies between the North and the West. Its first lord is **Jupiter**, for he is Northern, and **Mars** is associated with him in lordship because he is Western. The triplicity of **Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn** lies between the South and the East; its first mistress is **Venus**, because she is Southern, and **Saturn** is associated with her in lordship because he is Eastern. The triplicity of **Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius** lies between the North and the East; its first lord is **Saturn**, because he is Eastern, and **Jupiter** is associated with him in lordship because he is Northern. Also, the triplicity of **Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces** lies between the South and the West; its first lord is **Mars**, for he is Western, to whom **Venus** is associated in lordship because she is Southern.

Because the figures of the **trigons** <note>Another term for triplicities</note> of the zodiac are four, we have spoken thus: and we say that the trigon of Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius belongs to the angle that is between the North and the West. Jupiter governs it primarily because he is Northern, and Mars has a participation with him because he belongs to the Western part. And because the trigon of Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn belongs to the angle that is between the South and the East, Venus governs it first, as she is Southern, and Saturn has a participation with her in its government, as he belongs to the Eastern part. And because the trigon of Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius belongs to the angle that is between the North and the East, Saturn governs it first because he belongs to the East, and Jupiter has a participation in its government because he is Northern. And because the trigon of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces belongs to the angle which is between the South and the West, Mars governs it first because he belongs to the West, and Venus has participation in its government.

Ptolemy returns to the beginning, narrating concerning the trigons that which he said in the first part. His opinion on the lords of the trigons is greater and does not agree with the opinion of other astronomers. However, what he said is the truth, because the matter follows nature and experience verifies it; yet the teaching and experience of others affirm [something else] in this, and their words have wandered from the path of nature. For Ptolemy, in this place, put **Mars** as the governor of the trigon of Aries instead of the **Sun**, because the Sun rules in the eastern part; he did similarly in the other case that preceded this one. For if the Sun had the power of governing the provinces of this trigon, he would be the lord in the greater part of the inhabited world; nevertheless, because Mars is a co-partner in governing this trigon, and the lord of the house of the Sun's exaltation <note>Aries is the sign where the Sun is 'exalted' or most powerful</note>, they gave him power from this along with Jupiter in governing the trigon of Aries. This disagrees with the common opinion, for they hold that the lords of the trigon of Aries are the Sun, Jupiter, and Saturn. Similarly, Ptolemy assigned the government of the trigon of Taurus to Saturn instead of the **Moon**, because the Moon rules in the western part; and Saturn is a partner of Venus in governing this trigon. He holds his opinion because of **Capricorn**, which is the house of Saturn; because of this, he placed him instead of the Moon with Venus. He also placed Jupiter as the governor of the trigon of Gemini instead of **Mercury**, because Mercury is the governor of the middle part of the inhabited world. Hence, if he were likewise the governor of the provinces of the trigon of Gemini, he would have lordship in the whole, or nearly all,

<column-break/>

of the inhabited world. Since Jupiter is the governor in the northern part, he placed him as governor in his stead. His judgment on the trigons disagrees entirely with the sayings of other astronomers. For he says that the trigon of Aries holds power over the angle between North and West, while they hold it to be Eastern. He says the trigon of Taurus holds the angle between East and South, while they say it is Southern. He says the trigon of Gemini is between North and East, while they hold it to be Western. He says the trigon of Cancer holds the angle between South and West, while they hold it to be Northern. He says the planets that are lords of the trigons are others than those they name. We have already shown here in our **gloss** <note>Interpretive commentary</note> upon the words he spoke about the trigons in the first part and in this place; and we have shown that only what he says is the truth. Although the common views are many, they have fallen into error because one followed another without reason.

Since these things are so, the place of our habitation is divided into four parts, which are equal in number to the triplicities. Its latitude is divided by a line that passes through our sea <note>The Mediterranean</note>; it begins at the place called the **Passage of Hercules** <note>The Strait of Gibraltar</note> and reaches to the river called the **Citicon** <note>likely the Tanais or Don River</note>, which is in the eastern mountains that lie below it on the eastern side; by this line is divided that which is between the North and the South. Its longitude, however, is [divided] by a line that passes through the western river and through the sea which is now called the **Aggyion** <note>The Sea of Azov</note>, and through the marsh called **Maeotis** <note>Lake Maeotis, the ancient name for the Sea of Azov</note>; and this line divides that which is between the East and the West.

And after these things are so, and the place of our habitation is divided into four quarters according to the number of its trigons, its latitude is divided by the line that passes through our sea, beginning from the place called the Passage of Hercules and going as far as the arm of the sea called **Citaton**; it is at the back of the mountain ranges that hold themselves with that part of the East. By this line, the North is divided from the Southern part. Its Northern part, which is called longitude, is divided by a line that passes through the western arm [of the sea] and through the gulf called **Aggyion** and **Phoenicia**, and through the marsh which is called **Maeotis**. This is the line that divides between the Eastern and Western parts.

Regarding what he says—that its latitude is divided by the line passing through our sea, beginning at the place called the Passage of Hercules—he means that this is the line that divides the habitation of the earth into two halves: one Northern and the other Southern. For this line begins at the end of the habitation on the western side, at the place called the Passage of Hercules; this is a crossing into Spain (*Hispania*), and it is a strait of the sea such that one standing on one shore can see the person on the other. Around this place are the islands called **Albalidet** <note>The 'Fortunate Isles' or Canaries, from the Arabic 'al-Khalidat'</note>; one is an island that those crossing into Spain through this place see, as do those crossing from Spain through the land of the West. This island has an idol called **Catez** <note>Likely referring to Gades/Cádiz</note>, holding keys in its hand, by which it demonstrates that beyond itself there is no habitation. These islands are three in the sea, of the same size; in each of them is an idol of the kind we mentioned, each being equally distant from the other. This is the end of habitation on the western side. This **Hercules** is the one called the **Giant**; he is the one who reigned in the whole habitable earth, and who in ancient times caused these idols to be placed. This dividing line goes from this place to the end of the habitation in the lands of **Detyon** <note>Possibly a reference to 'Serica' or China</note>. **Alby** is a mountain that passes near the side of an arm of the sea called **Citaton**; and the things that are in this place are idols in an unpopulated area, holding keys and showing by them that from there forward toward the eastern part there is no other habitation. The length of this line is 80 degrees. This line is distant from the **equinoctial line** <note>The Equator</note> by 30 degrees or thereabouts, and it is equidistant with the equinoctial line. It has this number [because] the line is distant from the end of habitation in the northern parts by 7 degrees or thereabouts, which habitation is slightly distant from the equinoctial line. For the ancient wise men...

## Book Second

The ancients measured the habitation <note>The *oikoumene*, or the known inhabited world.</note> of the earth according to what our nature established. And they divided it into two halves: they found one southern half extended 36 degrees from the equinoctial line <note>The Equator.</note> toward the north; and another northern half from 30 degrees latitude up to 66 degrees latitude. And Ptolemy said its longitude is divided by a line that passes through the arm of the western sea, and through the gulf which is called the Aegean and the Pontus <note>Original: *egion z penites*, referring to the Aegean and the Black Sea (Pontus Euxinus)</note>, and through the lake which is called Maeotis <note>Original: *mantis*, the Sea of Azov</note>. He said that this western arm is the arm from the land of Mecca, which is called *al-Hijaz* in Arabic <note>Original: *aligez*</note>; it extends as far as Ebla and the Red Sea, and passes through the gulf called the Aegean, which is directly opposite the branch of the Red Sea and the sea of the Promised Land and of the Romans; and the Pontus is the sea of the Romans on the northern side. For the Red Sea extends from the southern part and comes out of the Indian Sea toward the north until it reaches 27 degrees latitude; it is thus a branch of the sea coming out of the Indian Sea toward the northern part. Similarly, the sea of Africa, Barca <note>Modern Libya</note>, Egypt, the Promised Land, Spain, and the Romans comes out of the Western Sea <note>The Atlantic</note> from the western part near the islands which are called the Fortunate Isles <note>Original: *albalibz z estand*, likely referring to the Canaries</note> and goes toward the east. And the further it goes, the more it widens until it comes directly opposite the branch of the Red Sea. It goes from one side toward the east until it reaches Antioch, and goes from another side toward the north until one great gulf of it is directly opposite the Red Sea. And the latitude that lies between the Red Sea and the sea of the Promised Land is less than 3 degrees. And if these two seas were to be joined into one with the Roman Sea that goes toward the north, two islands would be formed in these two seas: in the north from the Roman Sea, the name of which is Libya <note>Original: *lynoy*</note>. Indeed, the longitude of this line dividing the habitation into two halves—one to the east, the other to the west—is 56 degrees in the old map, and this is 59 degrees in the new map; my opinion is that the old map is more true. For it follows from this number that the eastern half of the habitation extends further than the western half. Although the eastern half extends further, the sea nevertheless takes a large part of it in which there is no habitation at all; for this sea reaches this eastern half in many places up to 31 degrees latitude, wherefore it hinders a great part of the habitation. And if the eastern half of the habitation were measured, it would then be found to be equal in habitation to the western half, even if it is not as long; for if this part is of modest length, it is of greater latitude. And nature did not do this without reason when it made the Red Sea extend toward the north. Directly opposite this sea in the north is another sea from which comes a certain river that falls into the sea of the Promised Land; and from all this, there is thus a sea dividing the eastern part from the western. And a certain king among the ancients <note>Likely referring to Pharaoh Necho II or Darius I, who attempted to build a precursor to the Suez Canal.</note> wished to make the Red Sea reach the Roman Sea, but fearing that the whole land of Egypt would be submerged because of it, he did not do it. This, however, is the opinion of Ptolemy in the partitioning of the fourth of the inhabited earth. And this same is the opinion of all the ancient wise men. For Hippocrates, who was very ancient, and similarly Plato, Aristotle, and Galen, and afterward all physicians and philosophers, understood this partitioning which Ptolemy set down in this book, and in the other book he made concerning the figure of the habitation of the earth. And I wish to say one more thing to you so that you may understand this better: know that the sea of Africa, Egypt, and the Romans comes out of the Western Sea in the manner of a branch, in a place whose longitude is 3 degrees and its latitude 36; and it always goes widening itself and extends to the eastern parts until it reaches Antioch. And the Western Sea extends past Spain and goes past the lands of the Ethiopians in the north toward the eastern parts, the sea which is called Pontus and the lake of Maeotis in the north of Constantinople in its eastern part; and from the Pontus sea comes a stream that falls into the Roman Sea, which is called the branch of Constantinople <note>The Bosphorus</note>; and this determines the quarter of the habitation which is called Europe. Similarly, there comes out of the Indian Sea a western branch that draws to the north until it goes to the city which is called *al-Qulzum* <note>Original: *Alculuz*, a port near Suez</note> or *Ayla* <note>Original: *Alba*, modern Eliat</note>; and there remains between it and the northern sea about 3 degrees; and this determines the quarter of the habitation which is called Libya <note>Original: *lynoy*</note>. And it remains to the east of the Red Sea, from the branch of Constantinople, in the east of the sea as far as the end of the habitation in

<column-break/>

the eastern parts, one part which is called Greater Asia. And in Greater Asia is the Persian branch, the Indian branch, the branch of *Deryn* <note>Perhaps the Caspian or a river system</note>, and the Caspian Sea <note>Original: *mare cozas*</note>. And in the borders of the *Vetryn* <note>Unclear; possibly a region in Central Asia</note> of India and Turkey there is a great unpopulated area and a great void occurs between the habitations; and because of this, that which is added of the habitation in Greater Asia in the eastern part is only half as much as the habitation in the quarter called Europe and in the quarter called Libya. Similarly, in the quarter of Libya there are many mountains and more than in the quarter of Europe. And nature gave it a greater length than it gave to Europe, so that when the length is completed, as much of the habitation as is lost to it because of the unpopulated area within it is made up; and thus the habitation that is in it is equal to that which is in the quarter of Europe, and the whole western half with its habitation is equal to the eastern half in the quantity of habitation. Similarly, Greater Asia is divided into two equal quarters like these two quarters: one is southern, the other northern, just as the western half is divided; yet it is not divided by a sea, nor by a branch, but it is divided by the line which Ptolemy said extends from the Passage of Hercules <note>The Pillars of Hercules/Strait of Gibraltar</note> toward the east; all of which you will find demonstrated in the book *On Airs, Waters, and Places* which Hippocrates made, and in the letters of Aristotle. For this is the opinion of the ancient wise men regarding the part of the inhabited earth. I marvel, however, at those of Persia and at the new wise men <note>Contemporary medieval scholars</note> that they did not understand this thing, and how they divided the habitation with respect to the island of Arin <note>Original: *terradib*, likely *Arin*, a mythical geographical center used in medieval maps</note>. For they divided the longitude of the habitation according to a quadrivial measure <note>The Quadrivium: the mathematical arts of arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy.</note> and did not look at what results from nature; and this is a manifest error, because they divided a natural thing and made it mathematical. And because of this, you ought to see how great an advantage there is between the wisdom of the Greeks and theirs.

### Concerning how the four quarters agree with the triplicities.

### But the four quarters are consistent in position with the four trigons.

We have already made clear what the four quarters are that are consistent in position with the number of the four trigons <note>Triplicities</note>: it happens that each of the four agrees with each trigon. For the quarter which is between the North and the West agrees with the trigon governing this place, and this is the trigon of **Aries** <note>The Fire triplicity: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius</note>. And the quarter which is between the South and the West agrees with the trigon governing this part, and this is the trigon of **Cancer** <note>The Water triplicity: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces</note>. And the quarter which is between the East and the South agrees with the trigon governing this part, and this is the trigon of **Taurus** <note>The Earth triplicity: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn</note>. And the quarter which is between the East and the North agrees with the trigon governing this part, and this is the trigon of **Gemini** <note>The Air triplicity: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius</note>.

The first quarter of the habitable place, which is placed between the North and the West, is in that part of the lands which are called **Celtogalatia** <note>Original: *selitogar latie*</note>, and they are the lands generally called **Europe**.

And one quarter of the quarters of this place, all of which is inhabited, is that which is between the North and the West and is in the part of the provinces which are called **Celtogalatia**; and these are the lands generally called **Europe**.

This quarter is an island which the Western Sea encompasses from the northern and western part, and the Roman Sea from the southern and eastern part, thus before the Moroccan [sea] <note>Original: *mrauinū*</note>; and these provinces are in **Britain** <note>Original: *catidopia*</note>, **Italy**, **Gaul**, **Spain**, **Constantinople**, and the borders of these provinces.

The quarter set in opposition to this, between the South and the East, is in the part of the lands which are now called the **Eastern Ethiopias**, and it is the southern part of the lands which are called **Greater Asia**.

And the quarter opposite to this quarter is that which is between the South and the East and is in the part of the provinces which are called the **Indies** <note>Original: *inoquia*</note> or the East; and this is the southern part which is Greater Asia.

This quarter is the habitation which is northern from the equinoctial line and is eastern from the Red Sea; and its latitude is 36 degrees below; and those who are there are from the nations of the **Arabs**, or this is **al-Hijaz**, **Yemen**, **India**, **Sind**, and from **Al-Buzat** <note>Original: *albozatez*</note>, that whose latitude is less than 36 degrees in the south from the ancient lands.

The third quarter, established between the North and the East, is placed in the part of the lands which is called **Scythia** <note>Original: *sesume*</note>; and it is in the northern part of Greater Asia.

# Treatise

And the third quarter, which is between the north and the east, is in the part of the provinces which are called <note>Original: "Caphonia," likely Cappadocia</note> Cappadocia; and this is the northern part of Greater and Lesser Asia.

¶ This fourth <note>The text uses "4m" as an abbreviation for "quartum," meaning the fourth part or quarter of the world.</note> is in the habitation that is in the east by the Sea of the Romans; its latitude is greater than 33 degrees. And this is Turkey and <note>Original: "cyncozafumir cozia adeylem," likely referring to regions in Central Asia such as Khwarezm or Daylam</note> the regions of Central Asia. And the fourth part is from Alborace <note>Likely referring to the Alborz mountains or a specific region of Persia</note>; its latitude is greater than 36 degrees.

¶ The quarter which is placed in the opposite direction, between the west and south and the blowing of those winds: it is arranged in the part of the lands called the Western Isthofie <note>Perhaps a corruption of Ethiopia or a specific coastal region</note>; which are generally called the "Tongues" <note>Referring to the various linguistic regions of the West</note>.

¶ And the quarter which is opposite to this, which is between the west and the south, is in the part of the provinces which are called Western Inoquia: its general name is the provinces of Delynoy, otherwise known as the <term>Libyan Desert</term> <note>Libya deserta: the vast arid regions of North Africa</note>.

¶ This fourth quarter is the island <note>In medieval geography, large landmasses surrounded by sea were often described as "islands"</note> which encompasses the Western Sea from the west and the south, the Sea of Africa from the north, and the branch of the Red Sea from the east. The provinces that are there are: Egypt, Ethiopia, Nubia, and all the other nations of the blacks, and Barca, Africa, and Tangier. It has come to pass that you may see the subtlety of the intellect of <term>Ptolemy</term> <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the preeminent astronomer and geographer of antiquity</note>, how that prince began from the quarter aligning with the <term>triplicity</term> <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> of **Aries**, because it is the first of the signs according to common opinion. However, in his own opinion, he did so because this triplicity is more noble than the others; and because of its nobility, there were in ancient times in this quarter where he dominates many noble kings who reigned over the whole habitation or the greater part of it, such as **Hercules the giant, Alexander, and Augustus.** For these were from the quarter between the north and the west. Afterward, he placed another quarter opposite to this second one: because opposition is of equal power, and because it aligns with the triplicity of **Taurus**, and Taurus is the second sign. Through this discovery, from these people came **men** who established laws which reach the greater part of the nations of the habitation, such as the **Law of the Christians**, which existed before the Law of the Moors <note>The Law of the Moors refers to Islamic law</note>, and afterward the Law of the Moors. After that, he placed the third quarter which aligns with **Gemini**, because it is the third sign. And because the eastern part is of greater power than the western, there were found among the inhabitant nations those who reigned greatly, such as **Ahasuerus and Darius** before him, who were kings of the Persians. And he placed the fourth quarter which is opposite the third: because the opposition is of equal power, or nearly so, and because **Cancer** is the fourth sign.

¶ Likewise, in each of these aforesaid quarters, that part of its territory which concerns nearly the half of the whole habitable earth will have its order in respect to that quarter of which it is a part. The dominion of that quarter is arranged in respect to the whole habitable earth. Another thing in the quarter which is commonly used, which is established between the north and the west in respect to the entire habitable earth: its order through approximately half of the earth is at the angle which is in opposition to that angle in which this quarter is formed, and it is the eastern meridian. The same will undoubtedly happen in the other quarters, so that each of these quarters is likened to two triplicities opposite to each other. The parts of it which are around the half of the earth belong to that to which that part is assigned, which also belongs to that which that quarter generally approaches. But other parts of it will accord with the general quality of that quarter. It is also necessary that they be taken with the stars of the triplicity of that quarter in the likeness of the star which holds dominion in the other triplicities.

¶ Similarly, any part of the quarters we have mentioned which is in the middle of the habitation of the whole earth is under the dominion of that quarter in respect to the whole quarter to the whole habitation. Because the quarter which is called Europe: one part which is in the middle of the habitation, which is around the opposite angle of the angle... from where that quarter tends more to the south and east. And so it is for all the other quarters, so that each of the quarters has an accordance

<column-break/>

with two opposite triplicities. And the parts that are in the middle tend toward the nature of the other opposite quarter; and it is of a different nature than the whole quarter is by itself. And other parts have the nature of the whole quarter. And it has come to pass that you should take the stars governing those other triplicities and mix them with those that govern the other part of that quarter.

¶ The two lines which we said divide the habitation into four quarters intersect at a point: the latitude of which is 36 degrees, and the longitude according to the old map is 59 degrees, and according to the new map is 56. By this incision, four angles are made: the provinces which are around the incision of these four angles are in the middle of the habitation. And those which are around the point of incision of any quarter are in the opposite part of any quarter; and it is in the opposite part of that quarter with respect to the whole quarter. And by this, in governing this place, the signs and planets governing the opposite quarter have a participation with the sign and planets governing that quarter where that part is. This was said by <term>Ptolemy</term>; the gloss does not need more in this place, yet it is useful that you form it in your imagination.

¶ And it is necessary that in every habitation, those stars be taken which dominate that triplicity alone in each quarter. Especially in those parts which are toward the middle of the habitation, in which the **Star of Mercury** <note>The planet Mercury</note> will be taken along with the stars that dominate the triplicities, since it is of the common class of mixed things.

¶ And it has come to pass that in any inhabited place, the power of those planets is through governing that alone according to the triplicity which dominates in any quarter, except for the parts of those quarters which are around the middle of the habitation. For in those, the power of **Mercury** occurs along with the powers of the planets governing those triplicities, because it is of a common nature having participation with all.

¶ In each of the four quarters, planets dominate as they happen to; however, in the middle of the habitation, all planets have a participation, as said before. And in that which is around the middle of any quarter, the planets of the opposite quarter dominate, and Mercury with them, because it is of a mixed nature. And by this, it is fitting that the part of any quarter which is around the middle should accord with **Mercury**.

¶ It is necessary, therefore, according to this order, that the parts which are between the north and the west of the habitable earth—namely, that quarter which is used by name—be likened to the triplicity which is between the north and the west. That triplicity is gathered from **Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius**. Generally, the lords of this triplicity will be **Jupiter and Mars**, when they are <term>vespertine</term> <note>Visible in the evening, after sunset</note>. The general nations inhabiting these parts are the men of the lands of **Britain, Galatia, Germany, Bastarnia, Italy, Gaul, Apulia, and Sicily, Thuringia, Calite <note>Unclear; perhaps a region in Gaul or Spain</note>, and also Spain.** It is necessary, therefore, that many of the men of these regions hold dominion through this triplicity. By their dominating stars, they are not humbled; they are called according to liberty and they greatly desire arms. They work and are warlike, and also skilled in government; they are polished, clean, and magnanimous. And since **Jupiter and Mars** are associated in their dominion while they are vespertine—and because the first parts of this triplicity are masculine, while the latter are feminine—it happens that these nations are not jealous regarding their women. They hold their sexual encounters in low esteem and rather desire the <note>original: "sodomiticumque scelus"</note> crime of sodomy; and they are more jealous regarding this, and those who have committed it do not think they have done anything shameful. Indeed, he upon whom this is performed, so that he becomes effeminate and soft in it, does not think he should be disparaged at all. They are also accustomed to attempt bold deeds and are occupied in good works and fidelity; they love kinship and do not neglect everything that is good, honest, and praiseworthy.

## Second Book

Of all these aforementioned regions: the regions of **Britain**, **Galatia**, **Germany**, and **Saturnia** <note>original: "saturnie"; likely referring to the northernmost reaches or a specific territory associated with the god Saturn</note> are specifically assimilated to **Aries** and **Mars**. For this reason, those who inhabit them are for the most part wild and fierce, and the qualities of their souls are like the qualities of wild beasts. But the regions of **Italy**, **Apulia**, **Gaul**, and **Sicily** are assimilated to **Leo** and the **Sun**. On account of this, those staying in them are skilled in government and act well; they are also imitators of all laudable works. However, the regions of **Tyrrhenia** <note>original: "tormiēmalte"; a likely corruption of Tyrrhenia or Celtica</note> and **Spain** are assimilated to **Sagittarius** and **Jupiter**; because of this, those who dwell in them desire liberty, are healthy of heart, and love cleanliness and brightness. 

But the parts of this fourth <note>Referring to the fourth division of the habitable world</note> which are arranged around the middle of the habitable region: these are the regions of **Thrace** <note>original: "taralyl"; likely a corruption of Thracia</note>, **Macedonia**, and **Illyria** <note>original: "abelernie"</note>; **Hellas** <note>original: "voles"</note>, **Achaia**, and the island of **Crete**; and the lands called the **Cyclades** <note>original: "duclaus"</note>, as well as the coast of **Asia Minor** and the island of **Cyprus** <note>original: "carbos"</note>. These are therefore the parts placed between the south and the east of this quarter; and in addition to what has been said, they are assimilated to the <term>triplicity</term> <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element; here, the Earth triplicity</note> which is between the south and the east: which is composed of **Taurus**, **Virgo**, and **Capricorn**, and associated with it in lordship are **Venus** and **Mercury**. 

Therefore, the inhabitants of these regions are more similar to one another in form and figure than all other men. Indeed, their souls and bodies are temperate; they are also very strong and skilled in government, and they are not humbled because of **Mars** (who is exalted in Capricorn), and they love liberty. And because **Mars** and **Jupiter** rule the triplicity of this quarter, they are distinguished from one another in their own characters and lordships. They are inventors of laws; they love music and desire to learn; they do not neglect their defenses. In all their works, by reason of **Venus**, they persevere with brightness and cleanliness: they act well and freely host strangers; they love and observe justice; they desire to write and use eloquent speech because of **Mercury**; and because they are assimilated to the evening stars, they hide their own counsel. 

Furthermore, when these regions are divided specifically, those who dwell in the regions of the **Cyclades** and on the shores of **Asia Minor** and the island of **Cyprus** will be specifically assimilated to **Taurus** and **Venus**; therefore, they are for the most part soft, greatly desiring cleanliness and brightness, and seeking after bodily height and ornaments. But those who inhabit **Hellas**, **Achaia**, and **Crete** are assimilated to **Virgo** and **Mercury**; hence they are specifically dialecticians and lovers of the study of doctrine, occupying themselves more with spiritual matters than earthly ones. But those who dwell in **Macedonia**, in **Thrace** (which is called Byzantium), and in **Hellas** are assimilated to **Capricorn** and **Saturn**; therefore they desire to rule, and the qualities of their souls are not mild or domestic, nor are they associated with the matters of laws.

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'S' at the beginning of the column, featuring a face surrounded by vine-like motifs.</image-desc> The second southern quarter is the part of **Greater Asia**: its parts pertaining to the regions of **India**, **Arachosia** <note>original: "arbalui"</note>, **Gedrosia** <note>original: "caurosie"</note>, **Parthia**, **Babylonia**, the islands, and the regions of **Assyria**. The site of all these, in respect to the whole habitable region, is in the south-eastern part; they ought to be assimilated to the triplicity between the south and the east, which is composed of **Taurus**, **Virgo**, and **Capricorn**. The lords of these regions are **Venus** and **Saturn** when they are in their morning phase. 

Wherefore, the natures of those inhabiting these regions imitate the natures of these two lords: for they worship **Venus** and call her **Asis** <note>likely referring to Isis or a local variation of the goddess name</note>. They call **Saturn** the "Bright Sun." There are also some of these who predict fortune and guard and accurately observe the reproductive members <note>original: "mēmbra generātia"</note>, holding those parts as divine; this is because they are assimilated to the aforementioned stars which are naturally generative in the same way; they also venerate their parents. They are hot-blooded men who exercise the acts of Venus much, and are more troubled by them than is proper; they are dancers and leapers, and players of musical instruments; their bodies are also fit for pleasures. They paint and adorn themselves because of **Venus**. Their manners are full because of **Saturn**, and they act openly, not in secret, because of the morning figure <note>the planetary position</note>. They copulate with women; the crime of sodom is strongly abhorred; therefore it happens to many of them to procreate children from their own wives. 

In this, they are also assimilated to the chest <note>a reference to the anatomical associations of the signs</note> because of the morning ascension; and because the ruling power of the bodies which is in their hearts is assimilated to the strength of the **Sun**. They are also, for the most part, soft and effeminate in their ways of living, in their grooming, and in all things pertaining to the body because of the qualities of **Venus**; yet they are also high-minded and strong warriors because **Saturn** is in the east. 

Furthermore, when these regions are divided, those who are from the regions of **Parthia** and its neighbors will be assimilated to **Taurus** and **Venus**. Therefore the inhabitants of these regions use clothing having colors associated with Venus, with which they cover the whole body except the chest, and generally they are effeminate and delicate. But those who are assimilated to **Virgo** and **Mercury** are the **Babylonians**, and the dwellers of the islands and the regions of **Assyria**. Wherefore these are skilled in matters of doctrine and are observers of the motions of the stars. Those who are assimilated to **Capricorn** and **Saturn** are the **Indians**, **Arachosians**, and **Gedrosians**; therefore they are deformed and dirty, and the qualities of their souls are most fierce.

Other parts of this quarter which are toward the middle of the habitable earth are the regions of **Idumaea**, **Syria**, **Judea**, **Phoenicia** <note>original: "cunice"</note>, **Chaldea**, and the inhabited regions of the **Arabs**. The site of all these in respect to this entire quarter is in the part placed between the north and the west; and it is assimilated to the triplicity between the north and the west, which is chosen from **Aries**, **Leo**, and **Sagittarius** <note>The Fire triplicity</note>; its lords are **Jupiter**, **Mars**, and **Mercury**. Wherefore the men inhabiting these regions use trade and exchange; they are deceivers and betrayers and disdainers. In the qualities of their souls, faint-heartedness conquers, and generally they are double-dealing and double-tongued, because they are assimilated to the aforementioned stars. Of these...

### Treatise

Furthermore, those who are in the parts of the lands of **Syria**, **Deep Coelesyria** <note>original: "pfunde acidu"; refers to the "Hollow Syria" valley between the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon mountains</note>, and the regions of the **Judeans** are specifically associated with **Aries** and **Mars**. For this reason, for the most part, they are created as unstable, traitors, and ignorant of the Creator <note>This reflects a common medieval and ancient astrological bias associating certain regions with negative traits based on planetary rulers</note>. But the men of the region of **Cyrenaica** and the **Chaldeans**, and the inhabitants of **Babylonia** <note>original: "vitanie"</note>, are associated with the **Sun** and with **Leo**. Whence they are healthy of heart and merciful; they are diligent in the science of the stars and specifically venerate the **Sun** above the other stars. Those inhabiting the regions of **Arabia** <note>original: "grabū"</note> are associated with **Sagittarius** and **Jupiter**. Wherefore the fertility of those lands is reflected in their name, for their habitation is a place of fertility. There one find also the seasonings of foods. The men of these regions are well-mannered, bold, and desiring to rule.

The third or fourth part is in the northern part of the lands of **Asia Major**. Its parts contain **Armenia**, **Hyrcania**, **Margiana**, **Bactria**, **Sogdiana**, **Parthiene** <note>original: "faluiran"</note>, and **Sarmatia** <note>original: "romaticā / sarmaticas"</note>, which are the regions of the women <note>A reference to the legendary Amazons believed to live in Sarmatia</note>; also **Tushpa** <note>original: "tusciana"</note> and the lands of **Scythia** <note>original: "ascaede"</note>, which are parts of the north-eastern portion of the whole inhabited region. These are associated with the **triplicity** <term>Triplicity: a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element; here, the Air signs</term> that is between the north and the east, which is composed of the signs of **Gemini**, **Libra**, and **Aquarius**. The lords of this triplicity are **Saturn** and **Jupiter** when they are oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note>. Therefore, the inhabitants of these regions venerate **Jupiter** and the **Sun**. Gold and riches flow to them in great abundance, and their deeds are bright and beautiful. Just as they are wise in their works, they inquire into divine matters and observe the qualities of their own souls. They do not turn away from truth and justice; they are liberal, of good intellect, and unchanging, abhorring wickedness. Their friendship is whole and incorruptible; for the sake of their kinsmen and for things that are praiseworthy and honest, they give themselves lightly to death. They are chaste and abstinent, they clothe themselves in the most precious garments, they give grand gifts, and their deeds are illustrious. Here, for the most part, the partnership of **Saturn** and **Jupiter** offers these qualities when they are in the east.

Among these, however, those who are in the part of **Carmania** and **Matiane** <note>original: "mathiate"; a region in Media</note>, and also **Armenia**, are specifically associated with the sign of **Gemini** and **Mercury**. For this reason, they are more mobile and more prone to deceptions. But those who are in the part of the lands of **Parthia** <note>original: "faluire"</note>, **Bactria**, and **Serica** <note>original: "zirice"; the Land of Silk, or China</note> are associated with **Libra** and **Venus**. Therefore, the inhabitants of these regions possess much money and love music and quiet.

Those, however, who dwell in the borders of the lands of **Sarmatia**, **Tushpa**, and the land of **Scythia** are associated with **Aquarius** and **Saturn**, whence they are of greater cruelty and the qualities of their souls are most ferocious. Other parts of this quarter which are toward the middle of the habitable earth are the regions of **Bithynia**, **Phrygia**, **Asia Proper**, **Paphlagonia** <note>original: "filogice"</note>, **Syria** and **Commagene**, **Cappadocia**, **Lydia**, **Cilicia** <note>original: "silyie"</note>, and **Pamphylia**. The site of all of these is toward the south-western parts of this quarter.

We associate these regions with the **triplicity** that is between the south and the west, which is constituted of **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. In its dominion, **Mars**, **Venus**, and **Mercury** are joined together.

<column-break/>

Thus, these regions are associated with the **trigon** <term>Trigon: another word for triplicity, specifically referring to the triangular aspect the signs make to one another</term> that is between the south and the west; this is the trigon of **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. In governing it, **Venus**, **Mars**, and also **Mercury** have a share.

This means to say <note>The text here shifts into a commentary format, likely explaining the preceding astrological principles</note> that in governing these provinces, the trigon of **Gemini** dominates along with the trigon of **Cancer**, and those who have lordship of these trigons have a share in governing them, and **Mercury** has a part in one with them, because he is the governor of the middle of the habitation.

For this reason, many inhabitants of these regions venerate **Venus** and call her by many different names according to the various lands. They call **Mars** by the name **Adonis** <note>original: "idēū"; likely referring to the Idean or a local name for a deity equated with Mars</note> and by certain other names, to which they ascribe many secrets. These are hardworking men, unhappy in their miseries, and prone to wickedness. In battles, expeditions, robberies, and the cutting off of roads they are led; they are reputed among slaves and die in battles because of the dominion of **Mars** and **Venus** over them when they are oriental. Likewise, the exaltation <term>Exaltation: the zodiac sign where a planet is thought to have its strongest or most beneficial influence</term> of **Mars** is in a trine aspect to **Venus**, namely in the sign of **Capricorn**. **Venus**, however, is exalted in a trine aspect of **Mars**, which is the sign of **Pisces**. Wherefore their wives love them with all their hearts and give them very sound counsel. They remain constantly in their own homes; they are of great labor and generally reduced to servitude; they are indeed very hardworking and oppressed.

And because of this, those living in these provinces mostly magnify **Venus** and call her by many and diverse names according to the customs of the places. They call **Mars** *Odiberis* <note>A localized or corrupted name for the god of war</note> and by other names, saying that certain secrets of lamentation and weeping belong to these planets. They are industrious of heart, though prone to being led toward every evil; and they are known for going to battle in an army and for plundering. They are like slaves and die in battles from exhaustion, because **Mars** governs them, and **Venus** in the manner in which they are oriental. Similarly, the exaltation of **Mars** is in one sign of the trigon of **Venus**, which is **Capricorn**, and **Venus** has her exaltation in one sign of the trigon of **Mars**, which is **Pisces**. Because of this, the women of these lands are very faithful to their husbands and truly love them; they are the guardians of their homes, hardworking and serving well; they are generally industrious and humble.

The reverence which they give to **Venus** and **Mars** used to exist in ancient times when the nations held to the law according to nature. Those of **India** today are of these opinions, as are those of **China** <note>original: "detyn"; likely referring to *Thina* or *Sin*</note>, and they use the names of cities according to what he said. He means to say that the people of any city called **Venus** and **Mars** by a specific name which those of another city did not use. And because **Venus** and **Mars** accord with each other when they are oriental, with the participation they have with **Saturn** and **Jupiter**, the **Sun** bestows upon them the character he spoke of before. They hold that the secrets of lamentation belong to **Venus** and to **Mars**, which makes them hardworking and in accord, and all the other things he said. This is because when **Venus** is oriental, the power of **Mars** and **Saturn** overcomes **Venus** and **Jupiter**. And because **Mars** and **Venus** have participation—since each of them has a share with the trigon of the other—the women of these lands are faithful to their husbands. Because of the participation that **Saturn** has with **Mars** and with **Venus**, they are hardworking and subservient.

As for those who are in the regions of **Bithynia** and **Phrygia**...

# Second Book

They are astrologically likened to **Cancer** and the **Moon**. This is because many of their inhabitants are people of fear and humility. Because of the Moon’s oriental position <note>Refers to a planet rising in the east before the sun, considered a position of strength in astrology</note> and the masculinity of that same figure, there is a certain virility, dominance, and segregation in many of their women. These are like the women called **Amazons**, who flee from marriage with men and love weapons. They are even mindful of their lineage from the cradle; they sear their right breasts so that they do not hinder their journeys of expedition. They uncover these members when they set out to wage war, so that their feminine nature is thought to be minimal.

Those who are in the land of **Bithynia** <note>original: "niconie"</note>, **Orcadia** <note>original: "eroquie"</note>, and **Colchis** <note>original: "caligite"</note> have a specific accordance with **Cancer** and the **Moon**. Because of this, the men are for the most part humble and fearful, while their women are for the most part virile, proud, and warlike. This is because the **Moon** governs them when it is oriental and in a masculine figure. They are like the women who were called **Amazons**, who avoid lying with men and love arms, speaking of them always from their infancy. They cut off their own right breasts so they may better manage their weapons. When they go to tournaments, they uncover these parts as they prepare their battle lines for war, so that their enemies might understand they do not have the nature of women.

The fear and humility found in the men of these lands happens because of the **exaltation of Jupiter** <note>Astrological term for a sign where a planet's influence is most harmoniously strengthened</note> which is in **Cancer**, and because of the participation the **Moon** has with **Mars** in governing them. The boldness and masculinity found in these women happens because of the figure of the **Moon**, which is masculine, since these lands are oriental and accord with the oriental planets. Regarding the masculinity of the other women who are called **Amazons**, he spoke by example: that the women of these lands are masculine just as those called **Amazons**. For the aforementioned women live on an island in the sea, near which is another island where men dwell. When the **Sun** is in **Cancer** and **Leo**, they join together for the sake of procreation and afterwards they separate. If a woman gives birth to a son, she nurses him until he is grown and afterwards gives him to the man; if she has a daughter, she keeps her with her.

But those who inhabit the parts of **Syria**, **Commagene** <note>original: "cumachie"</note>, and **Cappadocia** are likened to **Scorpio** and **Mars**. Wherefore many of them are unstable, deceivers, traitors, and great laborers. The men of **Libya** <note>original: "ludbie"</note>, **Cilicia** <note>original: "sylie"</note>, and **Pamphylia** <note>original: "macholie"</note> are likened to **Pisces** and **Jupiter**. Therefore they are specifically men of great wealth, good company, and of liberal trade, as well as being faithful in all their business.

And those of the land of **Syria**, **Commagene**, and **Cappadocia** accord with **Scorpio** and **Mars**; because of this they are for the most part foolish with deceptions and are hard workers. And those of the land of **Lycia** <note>original: "lodie"</note>, **Cilicia**, and **Pamphylia** accord with **Pisces** and **Jupiter**. Because of this they are of great riches, sociable merchants, and diligent in liberty and lawfulness in all their deeds.

The riches they possess are because of **Jupiter**, who governs them in the name by which he is oriental. Their sociability, lawfulness, and commerce are due to **Venus**, who has a great participation with **Jupiter** in governing them, since she has her triplicity and exaltation in **Pisces**.

The remaining fourth part is in the region generally called **Libya** <note>original: "lynoy"</note>, whose parts contain the regions of **Numidia**, **Carthage** <note>original: "iarsinodie"</note>, **Africa**, **Cyrene** <note>original: "cadbante"</note>, the **Garamantes** <note>original: "harmātice"</note>, **Mauritania**, **Getulia** <note>original: "batolie"</note>, and **Metagonitis** <note>original: "metegonate"</note>, all of which are situated in the

<column-break/>

south-western part of the entire habitable region. Another power remains in the part generally called **Libya**, and these are the parts comprising **Hyromandia**, **Iartazonia**, **Africa**, and **Cyrene**. These lands are positioned between the west and the south of the entire inhabited earth.

### Hyromandia

This is in the west from **Africa**; and **Iartazodia** is to its east from **Africa** and **Cyrene**. **Laccacemonia** and **Garinotica** are lands existing in the west. **Africa** and **Mauritania** are at the edge of the habitation on the western side and are associated with **Taurus**, and these are the lands of the southerners. **Metagonitis** is in the east of the **Mecinods**, and this is well-traveled. I am telling you the facts of these lands, for I know that they demonstrate to you what they are. Remember what I told you, so that you may seek all these out in the book of the **Mappa Mundi** <note>A medieval "Map of the World"</note> of **Ptolemy**, and see with which sign they accord and with which planet.

They are likened to the **triplicity** <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> that is between the south and the west, which is gathered from **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. The lords of this are **Mars** and **Venus**, when they are in their evening aspect. Wherefore, in many of these regions, because of the fellowship of these two planets, it happens that a king and queen born of the same mother rule together: namely, the man ruling over the men and the woman over the women, and they always observe this custom of lineage. Their natures are very hot, and they are so excessive in copulation that their marriages are made by force and rape.

Oftentimes their king also enjoys the spouses of others before their own husbands perform the venereal acts; and among some of them, wives are held in common. They also desire paintings and ornaments, and they adorn themselves in a feminine manner because of **Venus**; nevertheless, their minds are virile, crafty, ready for service, diviners, traitors, and deceivers, not fearing dangers because of **Mars**.

And they accord with the **trigon** <note>Another word for triplicity</note> which is between the south and the west: this is the trigon of **Cancer**, **Scorpio**, and **Pisces**. **Mars** and **Venus** govern it in the manner in which they are in the evening. Because of this, it happens in many of these lands—due to the participation of these two planets—that a king and queen born of one mother (as brother and sister) rule there. The man rules over men, and the woman over women. They observe this custom, and the people hold it as an inheritance. The people of these lands are of a very hot nature and have great fornication with women; they are so lewd that they scarcely leave women alone and touch them violently. It frequently happens that kings lie with new brides before their husbands do. For the most part, women are common among them. They love themselves clearly like women, and this is by reason of **Venus**; yet they have the hearts of men, and they are deceptive. As archers, they predict many things and put themselves in mortal danger for the sake of **Mars**.

The participation of these two planets is because the exaltation of each is in the triplicity of the other, and they are the princes in governing this triplicity. For it is said that in these lands two siblings rule, a man and a woman—this is found today in the lands of **Gao** <note>original: "gaue"; likely referring to the Gao Empire in West Africa</note> and in many places. This is because of the participation of **Mars** and **Venus** in governing them. Their natures are hot because of the heat of **Mars**, and they have great fornication with women because of the participation that **Venus** has with **Mars**.

¶ And because of this, there are many women among them held in common; they cleanse themselves just as women do. For it is found today among those who cover their faces like women <note>original: "coopiūt suas facies"</note>; and many of those from these western lands travel covered in linens like women. Yet they have the hearts of men, and this is the cause of **Mars**; and because of this they are also deceptive and treacherous, and they put themselves in deadly peril because **Mars** governs them in a feminine figure. This occurs when he is vespertine <note>A planet is "vespertine" when it sets in the evening after the sun, which was thought to alter its influence</note>, and they possess a gift for divination through the influence of **Jupiter** and **Venus**, which share in the power of **Mars**. This is found among them today, for many of them look into the limbs of animals and learn many things from the livers, hearts, and shoulder blades <note>The practice of divination by inspecting animal entrails is known as extispicy</note>.

¶ Those who are in the regions of **Numidia**, **Farsidonia**, and **Africa** are specifically likened to **Cancer** and the **Moon**. For this reason, they are men of society and commerce, and are of great stoutness.

¶ And those of them who are in the region of **Normandy**, **Sarcazodia**, and **Africa** accord specifically with **Cancer** and the **Moon**; and because of this they are merchants, and their lands are very fertile and abundant.

For the **Moon** has two different influences over these people: one because she is the mistress of the western half of the world, and the other because of the dignity she holds in **Cancer**. For this reason, those from the greater part of these lands are more subtle and more intelligent than other westerners.

¶ And those who are in the region of **Metagonica**, **Mauritania**, and **Italy** have a specific accordance with **Scorpio** and **Mars**. These have the manners of beasts and wild animals; they are mockers, they eat much meat, they put themselves in danger of death, and they despise life, so that one will kill another.

¶ These are the barbarian peoples, those who dwell deep in the West, such as the **Mecinodis** and the **Pagnates**. They have such customs that they kill their own parents; and it has often been told to me that when they see their parents and friends are sick, they usually kill them, saying that they are helping them so they may die quickly without suffering. Many of them do this despite the law of the **Moors** <note>original: "legē mauroƺ"</note> which forbids it from happening.

¶ But those who are in the parts of the lands of **Fadbania**, **Locicemunitis**, and **Barmaneboie** are likened to **Pisces** and **Jupiter**. For this reason, the qualities of their souls are liberal, and they are clearly lovers of work, givers of thanks, and men of Godly fear. Nor are they humbled more than others because of **Jupiter**, whom they worship and call **Hamon** <note>Refers to the Egyptian and Libyan deity Zeus-Ammon</note>.

¶ And those who are from the region of the land of **Decadina**, **Centimonites**, and **Gazmatica** accord specifically with **Pisces** and **Jupiter**. Because of this, they have good and simple manners; they love monasteries, they are grateful and praise good deeds. They are God-fearing and generally humble because of **Jupiter**, whom they revere and name **Ammon**.

¶ Since we have said that these are within the borders of **Africa** and **Pagate**, that which **Ptolemy** said requires no further explanation in this part.

¶ **Coznalira** is the land of **Barca**; and elsewhere we find that **Alcaynamenz** and **Marmarica** are coastal regions like **Alexandria**, **Taraxid**, and **Damietta**. ¶ It is also likened to the triplicity <note>In astrology, a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> which is between the north and the east, which is composed of the signs of **Gemini**, **Libra**, and **Aquarius**. In its dominion, **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mercury** are associated. For in the dominion of these regions, the wandering planets are more frequently associated when they are vespertine. The inhabitants of these places love God, they venerate the truth, and they cling to the things of the Creator. They weep at their funerals and bury their dead hidden under the earth because the planets are vespertine. Their customs are diverse, and the qualities of their souls, their acts, and their laws are many. When someone has dominion over them, they are obedient and humble, and then a certain smallness of soul and humility of speech prevails in them. But when they themselves rule others, their souls are filled with the greatest thoughts. The men take many wives, and the women also marry many men. They are much troubled by sexual acts; they lie with their close relatives and sisters. They procreate many children with men, and their wives conceive quickly, just as in those regions all things grow and increase greatly. Indeed, the souls of many of the men are soft and feminine. Some of them even despise their own generative members because of the association of **Venus** and the "Infortunes" <note>The "Infortunes" or malefic planets are traditionally Saturn and Mars</note> in a vespertine quality.

¶ And they receive accordance with the triplicity that is between the north and the west, which is the triplicity of **Gemini**, **Libra**, and **Aquarius**. **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mercury** have a share in the governance. Because the five planets generally share in the governance of the inhabitants of these regions in a vespertine manner, they are lovers of God; they magnify and love the truth; they restrain themselves, and they love the things that please God. They bury their dead underground and hide them away much because of the vespertine figure. They use various laws, customs, and manners of many kinds. When someone governs them, they are humble and obedient, and concord prevails among them. They speak humbly and endure much labor when it falls upon them. But when they govern others, having good wills and great hearts, the men are joined to many women and the women take many husbands. They are much involved in fornication. The men lie with their sisters and are of great generation; and similarly, the women conceive easily according to the nature of their land, which produces all things in abundance. Many of those males have weak and feminine hearts, and many of them despise their private parts and do not cover them.

# Second [Book]

From all that we have told you, you can easily imagine the location of any province. You can readily know who its governor <note>The "governor" here refers to the celestial body or zodiac sign that holds dominion over a specific geographical area.</note> is. For since **Aries** is the governor, it holds the northern part of the provinces which are in the middle of the inhabited world, positioned in the quadrant between north and west. It follows that it possesses those provinces in the middle that are opposite to these; these are the **Promised Lands**, and **Taurus** governs them. And again, following the provinces that are held in the angle with the quadrant—which is between north and west—all others follow this same rule. For any sign is the ruler in those middle provinces that are opposite to its own provinces located at the edge of the quadrant. It is clear that in governing the provinces located in the middle of the inhabited world, all signs and planets participate. Because of this, there are different laws and religious sects, adopted by the people living in the middle from those at the edges of the inhabited world; for as previously said, the judgment of all comes from these provinces. It is fitting, therefore, that you study this treatise of our gloss <note>original: "glose nostre"; a "gloss" is a commentary written to explain a primary text, in this case, Ptolemy's *Tetrabiblos*.</note> much and often, for you will always understand more.

¶ There are, however, seventy-two in total.

¶ The sum of these provinces is **72**. <note>The number 72 is traditional in medieval geography and theology, often representing the 72 nations or languages arising from the Tower of Babel.</note>

¶ This means that the land in which there is a great nation or many nations is of this number.

¶ And since these things are so, it is necessary to attribute to them these further points: namely, that each of the **fixed stars** is likened to the regions to which their parts of the circle of signs <note>the Zodiac</note> are likened. All things act within them, and there are parts directly above which the fixed stars are positioned, which are arranged upon one of the circles passing through the two poles of the zodiacal circle.

¶ Since these things are so, it is fitting that we add what we shall tell you, which is necessary: and that is, each of these figures <note>constellations</note> corresponds with the provinces aligned with the parts of the zodiac signs, and all things are shared in them. These are the parts that are directly in line with the fixed stars and come over the **zenith** <note>the point directly overhead</note> in a circle among those circles passing through the poles of the zodiac signs.

¶ After he gave us the rules for how the planets govern the seven provinces, he gave us here a similar rule for the fixed stars, saying that each of them governs the place governed by the degree in which the star itself is located—whether the star is north or south of the zodiac. It is fitting that you understand from his words that the **degree** in which a city began to be built is the indicator for that city itself, along with all the fixed stars existing in that same degree. Similarly, the degree of the **midheaven**, the Sun, the Moon, the **Part of Fortune**, and all other principal places have a great concordance with this city. The city will always be fortunate when the "planets of fortune" pass through the principal places of the constellation of its founding. Similarly, it is unfortunate when the "unfortunate planets" pass through the principal places of the rising constellation of its root <note>original: "radicis"; in astrology, the "root" is the original founding chart or birth chart.</note>, just as it is in the birth charts of people.

¶ Also associated in the significance of the **mothers of cities** are those places where the Sun and Moon were at the start of the building of these "mothers," as well as the locations of the angles <note>The four "angles" of a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note>, and especially the angle of the **Ascendant**, just as in birth charts.

¶ The degrees corresponding with the mothers of cities in receiving the work of the zodiac signs are the places where the Sun and Moon were at the beginning of their building, and the locations of the angles, especially the angle of the Ascendant, just as in birth charts.

¶ He means that the things from which prognostications are taken regarding matters contained in the **mothers of cities** are the principal places in the constellation of its rising at its construction. These principal places are the locations of the Sun, the Moon, the angles, and the **Part of Fortune**. And he called them "mothers of

<column-break/>

cities" because small towns follow the greater city within whose boundaries they are located, for the greater power overcomes the lesser. And since this is so, it is fitting that the fixed stars in those parts of the principal places should have concordance with the cities.

¶ And in cities where the times of construction are not known, it is fitting to look to the midheaven of the birth chart of its lord or the king who lived at the time they were built.

¶ He means that cities whose principal locations are not known from the start of their construction take their significance from the **10th house** <term>Medium Coeli: the highest point in a chart, signifying one's career or a ruler's governance</term> of the birth chart of the one who ordered them to be built. For this is his service, since the 10th house signifies "services" or "ministries." **Ptolemy**, however, knew by this saying the thing through which we can know what will happen in any town through the significance of the birth charts of their lords, and the events according to the time when they began to rule in them. For we take from the 10th house the significance of each of them in those things they performed in the cities where they ruled. For that place is his "ministry," and his ministry is in governing all things of the city.

After he showed us the knowledge of the planets and signs pertaining to the government of any province and city, he teaches us other rules by which we may know any of the **universal accidents** <note>General events affecting the whole world or a region, such as weather, plague, or war, as opposed to "particular" events affecting individuals.</note>.

## How one arrives at the prognostic science of general future events. Chapter 4. ##

After this observation of the predicted things, it is necessary that we follow in speaking of how we may know how to prognosticate universal future events generally. Through these, we will set forth the future things that happen generally in lands and regions. The first and strongest cause of these events is nothing other than the **eclipses** of the Sun and lunar conjunctions and preventions <note>Full moons occurring just before a specific event or eclipse.</note>, as well as from the locations of the movements of the planets in those very hours.

¶ And since we will look into these things in such a way, it happens that we follow these opinions generally in our narration: how we can speak of universal accidents before they happen. We will first make known those things to which universal accidents happen in provinces and cities, the inquiry of which will be in this manner: Since the primary things of greatest power in these accidents are the **eclipsal conjunctions and oppositions**—namely of the Sun and Moon—and the places through which the planets pass at that hour.

He has already taught us in the first part that the **Sun** is the lord and victor over all universal and particular accidents, and that the **Moon** follows it in lordship and power. The five "wandering planets" follow the Moon in power, and the fixed stars follow the five wandering planets. He showed us that the work of the two luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> is a natural thing tending toward the work of the planet having participation with the Sun and Moon, or with both. Since this is so, and universal accidents happen because of a greater force, it follows in all ways that universal accidents happen because of the power of the Sun and Moon when they change into another very great power. And it is manifest that when the Sun and Moon are joined in one point, both powers are mixed into one; and from both of them, at that very hour, one mixed power comes to us in a straight line. The same happens when one is opposite the other; for the power of each comes before the earth in a straight line that passes through their two centers and through the earth, and from the mixture, one combination is made. From this, a spiritual power comes forth that works in things. And it is manifest that...
