# Treatise

This spiritual power tends toward the power of the planet or star that has the greatest influence at that hour; for all the powers of the stars mix with one another in earthly matters at any given hour. It happens, however, to any one of them that at one hour it will be stronger, and at another weaker. Since the power of the **two luminaries** <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> is great when they are joined in one point <note>A conjunction, or New Moon.</note>, or when they are in opposition to one another in two opposite points <note>A Full Moon.</note>, the powers of the other stars also happen at that same hour. For then they are all mixed, and there arises a certain great spiritual power which tends more toward the power of the star having the greatest influence at that hour, according to the course of the stars and the locations they occupy at the hour of conjunction or opposition. And since this is the case, it clearly appears that the conjunction and opposition which create great power are especially those which occur with an **eclipse**. And the greater the eclipse, the greater the power will be.

In other conjunctions and oppositions where there is no eclipse, the luminaries are not on a single straight line. It is clear, however, that when other stars are joined with one of the two luminaries—or both—at the hour of an eclipse, or are in opposition to them, the straight line that carries the power of the two luminaries reaches those stars at that very hour, and because of this, the power will be much greater. And the more the stars are of great work and power, the greater and stronger the event will be. For example: a very great eclipse occurs, and simultaneously on the same line occurs a conjunction of **Saturn** and **Jupiter**, specifically when the conjunction first shifts from one [trigon] to another. <note>original: "mutatio coniunctionis"; referring to the "Great Conjunction" shifting elemental triplicities.</note> Indeed, from such an eclipse, a great and very strong event arises in every way; this is because the work of **Saturn** and **Jupiter** is greater than the work of other planets, and the shift of their conjunction is of much greater power than the conjunctions of other planets that happen within the same **trigon**. <note><term>trigon</term>: Also called a triplicity; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> Because of this, a certain power is composed from the power of the eclipse and the power of the conjunction, which is greater than that of the conjunction by itself, or that of the eclipse alone.

Now, in this place, I wish to declare to you the facts of conjunctions so that you may understand them well. I say that **Saturn** and **Jupiter** are joined once every **20 years** or thereabouts, and they are joined twelve times in any given trigon, and four times in any given sign of that trigon. It sometimes happens that they are joined five times in a sign, resulting in 13 conjunctions in that trigon; and it sometimes happens that they exit and join in a different trigon, and afterwards return and join in the former one where they were, so that they complete the conjunction twelve times in that trigon before they shift from it to another. Because of this, it happens that the first time they join in a trigon when they shift from another, this conjunction has a greater power than other conjunctions.

And after **Saturn** and **Jupiter** join once every 20 years or so—twelve times in any trigon over **240 years** or thereabouts—they then shift from that trigon to another once in 13 conjunctions. Certainly, by calculation, they are joined in all signs four times in each sign over **960 years**. Their conjunction always shifts from one trigon to the next following one, and from the sign where it began to the next following sign. For example: when the shift of the conjunction occurs in the sign of **Aries**, the second shift will be at the head of 240 years in the sign of **Taurus**; afterward, according to this, it happens that the third shift is after 960 years. For in that many years they will have been joined in every sign four times, and the shift will return to the ninth sign at the head of **1920 years**, and it will return to the first sign at the head of **2880 years**. In that many years, they will have been joined **144 times**. When we double the number of conjunctions by the number of signs, there will be **1728 conjunctions**, and there will be about **34,000 years**. This is approximately the number of years in which the **fixed stars** complete their course through the whole sphere <note>This refers to the Precession of the Equinoxes, which medieval astronomers calculated at varying rates.</note>; and in all that time, the beginning of the shift returns to each sign only twelve times, which is the number of the signs. Because of this, the conjunction of **Saturn** and **Jupiter** has very great power in changing kingdoms and religious sects, and in moving habitations from one place to another, because both planets are supreme and of great power.

The ancient sages also held the conjunction of **Saturn** and **Mars** to be of very great power when it occurs in the sign of **Cancer**, for it shows great evil and great corruption on the earth. This is because **Cancer** is the house of the **Moon** and the exaltation of **Jupiter**; when two **malefics** <note>Saturn and Mars are traditionally considered "malefic" or "unfortunate" planets due to their associations with cold/restriction and heat/aggression.</note> are joined in it, it destroys its good significance, for it is the opposite of the house of one and the fall of the other. And because of 

<column-break/>

this, its evil grows and its corruption is strengthened, so that this conjunction has a great significance for the corruption of depopulating dwellings, the robbery of children, and wars—especially if its power is mixed with the power of the **two luminaries**, and most of all if a great eclipse is confirmed by a conjunction on a straight line. I say absolutely that the more the celestial powers are mixed, and the greater that mixture is, the greater the events it signifies, as well as the durability and renewal of the degrees of things. And since these events last for many years, it is clear that they perform their operation on the whole, because everything follows the significance; thus all things tend toward and have a part in that universal work.

¶ <gloss>Some of these universal events are also prognostications of place; that is, that which must be sent forth to know in which of the regions and lands the significations of a particular eclipse will fall.</gloss>

¶ <gloss>It remains still to speak of the location where these universal accidents will occur, for it is fitting that a person should know in which province or city that which the particular eclipses signify will take place.</gloss>

¶ <gloss>He means to say that looking at the place where the event itself will happen follows looking at the thing significant of the event. He calls all of them "particular eclipses." He means that some eclipses have great power from the planets and stars, so that they signify a very great universal event that encompasses many provinces and lasts for many years; every eclipse occurring in a particular way in comparison to the greater one signifies an addition to or subtraction from what the greater one signified, or it will happen more in one part than in another, or more in one sect than in another, and similar things.</gloss>

¶ <gloss>Also the **stations** of the wandering stars <note>Planets.</note> at each time of their station; I speak of **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars**: namely, when they stand still and their significations are observed.</gloss>

¶ <gloss>And the five wandering planets signify many things because of their stations and their stability at any time. I wish to say that the station of **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars**, when it occurs, takes away from the events.</gloss>

¶ <gloss>The five wandering planets together have very great works because of the diversity of their states, beyond the natural works they have. These states are when they are stationary or direct; and all other states when they are joined by standing in this manner with a conjunction or opposition have a certain spiritual power of great work. And they operate according to their states. It also happens that when they are joined and are in opposition to one another, they perform very great works according to the powers coming into them. He spoke specifically of **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars**, and did not speak of **Venus** and **Mercury**, because each of those three has a greater power and a more manifest work than **Venus** and **Mercury**. Concerning **Saturn**: because its houses are opposite the houses of the **two luminaries**, and the power of opposition is of contrariety. Concerning **Jupiter**: because its houses are in the third [aspect] from the two luminaries, and the power of Saturn's aspect is the power of concord; because of this, they have concord with the power of the two luminaries. The fourth power is the middle power of opposition. Concerning **Venus**: because its two houses are in the **sextile** aspect <note>An angle of 60 degrees.</note> of the houses of the two luminaries, and the sextile is the middle power of the third. **Mercury** indeed is a mediating state between these. Because of this, it is shown that the power of **Saturn**, **Jupiter**, and **Mars** is of greater power and work in changing the state of this earthly world than the power of **Venus** and **Mercury**. And when **Venus** and **Mercury** have a great work, it is when it happens that these three planets also have a great work.</gloss>

¶ <gloss>Some things, however, are to be said concerning time; that is, the hour of the significance, its span, and its quantity must be known beforehand.</gloss>

¶ <gloss>Another part consists in stating the time; and this must be known before the hour of significance, and for how long a time it can last.</gloss>

Second

[He] means to say that knowing the time of an event follows from knowing the place where it will happen.

¶ Some [parts] involve speaking about the general category: and this is what we ought to know—in what general category the future events will occur.

¶ Another part consists of stating what thing will happen: it is appropriate to know in which general category the event will fall.

¶ It is the custom of the wise to say that matter is a "genus" <note>A general classification.</note> because it is prepared to receive forms: it is compared to a genus which, according to its nature, [is compared] to species. And Ptolemy used the word "genus" because he wanted to indicate that which is prepared to receive the event; for the prediction of this follows the prediction of the time in which it must happen.

¶ Some also involve speaking about the species <note>The specific type or nature.</note> of the future: and this is the last of the parts by which we will grasp the manner of the future, how it might be.

¶ Another part consists of stating in which species it will happen, which is the final part of prognostication: and this is knowing what thing that event will be.

¶ He means to say that by knowing the nature receiving the event, when it happens that we know the form it will receive: whether the thing will be good or evil; and when we have known these things according to our purpose, we will have reached our goal.

<margin>Chapter 5</margin>
¶ Regarding the knowledge of the regions in which future events will happen.

->Haly said:<-

The **rules** that are sought for this reason are of five types. The first is knowing by what reason the event comes. The second is knowing in which provinces it will happen. The third is knowing at what time and for how long it will last. The fourth is knowing the nature that must receive the event itself. The fifth is knowing the thing which the matter itself will receive, such as whether it is good or evil. And after he taught us by what reason a universal event comes—saying that it comes through eclipses and conjunctions and such things—he now begins to teach us the other four types: and he begins to demonstrate the first of the four: and this is knowing the place where the event will occur.

**The first** thing we proposed to relate is the first species of prognostic speaking: namely, concerning the place; but how we can arrive at the knowledge of it, we will indicate here. For in the points of eclipses and the conjunctions and oppositions of the Sun and Moon: and especially in that which is more evident, we ought to observe the location of the eclipse in the circle of the signs <note>The Zodiac.</note>.

¶ The first thing we must note is the first type of prognostication: and that is stating in which place the event will happen: and we can know it from what I wish to say: we must look into the conjunctions and oppositions of eclipses that have occurred involving the Sun and the Moon: and specifically those which appear to the sight, in what place of the zodiac signs they are.

**He means** to say that we must calculate the eclipse: and know in what place of the signs it is: and its ascendant and the other angles: and if the eclipse was above the earth so that it appeared to the sight, it will be of stronger effect; for its power passes through the air all the way to the earth: because the nature of air is to lift all power without any change: just as it lifts smells, colors, and all other powers that can pass through the air; however, if it were below the earth: the thickness of the earth prevents that power from reaching us in the manner in which it stands: but it weakens it much beforehand: and for this reason the work of an eclipse that appears to the sight is of much greater power than that which is hidden from sight.

¶ Also the regions that are similar to that triplicity <note>original: "triplicitati"; refers to the four groups of three zodiac signs based on the elements: fire, earth, air, and water.</note>.
¶ And in the provinces agreeing with each one.

¶ He means to say that when we know the location of the eclipse in the zodiac of the signs: and we seek the provinces agreeing with the triplicity in which the eclipse is, we will select that province which agrees solely with the sign in which the eclipse is.

<column-break/>

¶ Also the lands that are similar to the sign of the eclipse, whether through the ascendant of the hour of the city's foundation: and through the locations of the luminaries at that hour: or through the location of the Midheaven <note>The highest point of the zodiac at a given time.</note> in its birth: which then ruled over them, we must observe.

¶ Similarly, we must seek the cities agreeing with the sign of the eclipse for receiving its effect—which city that will be: whether through the ascendant of the hour of its construction: or through the locations of the luminaries at that same hour: or from the location of the Midheaven of the lord’s birth occurring at that time.

¶ He means to say that when we know the provinces agreeing with the triplicity of the eclipse, we will then take that which is specifically of the sign of the eclipse: and we will join with it the city agreeing with the sign of the eclipse: whether through the ascendant of its construction: or from the locations of the luminaries at that hour: or from the location of the Midheaven of its birth: which was the hour when it began to be built. And when we find any city in which the sign of the eclipse rules through two of these aforesaid parts or through more: we will say that in that city the event will be greater: and in that which we find agreeing with the sign of the eclipse through only one part, the event will be lesser accordingly.

¶ It should also be known that in whatever regions or lands we find this similarity which we have described, in all of them the future signs will come to pass: especially in that which is similar to the sign of the eclipse itself: and in which the eclipse is seen above the earth.

¶ And we must know that in the province and city in which we find the agreement I have described, those very events will happen in all of them, and specifically in that which pertains to the sign of the eclipse, and in that where the eclipse appears above the earth.

¶ He means to say that the event of the eclipse will happen in provinces and cities agreeing with its sign: and that which has the greatest agreement with the sign of the eclipse will receive the eclipse's effect more: and when we have known this, we will look there where the eclipse is above the earth: and we will say that the event will be greater and stronger there. And this is because the power of the two luminaries, which signifies natural things, changes at the hour of an eclipse and tends toward the power of the planets and stars mixing with it: and because of this, it gives to those provinces that same change of their conditions: and when any province or city is joined which is of greater agreement: and where the eclipse appears more to the sight: that place will receive the work of the eclipse more than other provinces; because the power of an eclipse is very weak when it is below the earth: and in its working it does not have as great a power as when it is above the earth.

Tractatus

...completes the hour: since they are not equal in all inhabited provinces in terms of proportional hours. And because the darkening of the sun and the duration of the eclipse will not be equal throughout all provinces, we ought first to set the hour of the eclipse for whoever will be in any inhabited place among the locations participating in that event; and we will set the angles <note>The four cardinal points of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note> according to the altitude of the pole <note>The latitude of the observer.</note> just as we do in nativities <note>Individual birth charts.</note>.
¶ Those who know the use of tables and equations know that the ascendants <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note> of solar and lunar eclipses, and of all conjunctions and oppositions, are different in lands that differ in longitude or latitude. Similarly, the amount of darkness of the solar body and the time of the eclipse's duration vary. For these two are different according to the difference of the "aspect" <note>The visual angle or perspective of the observer on Earth.</note> in any given place; and because of this, the temporal hours <note>Hours based on the 12-fold division of daylight or night, which vary in length by season.</note> passed of the day or night at the hour of the eclipse in any place or city are of a different quantity than those in another place or city. And since this is so, and we know the cities in which the eclipse's effects will strike, it is necessary that we calculate the ascendant of the eclipses for each of those cities, and that we know how many equal hours <note>Standard 60-minute hours.</note> the duration of the eclipse will be. For from temporal hours we will know *when* the eclipse's event will occur. And from equal hours we will know *how long* it will last; and from the ascendant of the beginning of the eclipse, we will know when it starts. And from the ascendant of the middle of the eclipse, we will know when its greatest strength will be. And from the ascendant of the end, we will know when they [the effects] will be completed. And from the ascendant of the conjunction or opposition, we will know the planet which will dominate in the eclipse; and we will inspect which planet will dominate in each of these stellar configurations. For example: If a fortune <note>original: "fortuna"; a benefic or "lucky" planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note> dominates at the start, we say that the beginning of the ascendant is mixed with good and evil. And if a malefic <note>original: "in fortuna" (likely a scribal error for "infortuna"); a "bad" planet like Saturn or Mars.</note> dominates at the start, the damage at the beginning will be greater; and we speak similarly regarding other events of the eclipse. And because of this, Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy (c. 100–170 AD), the most influential ancient authority on astronomy and astrology.</note> gave us one specific rule for the ascendant; he commanded us to calculate the ascendant as he described. We will set the first hour of the eclipse which occurs in any inhabited place that has a share in these ascendants, and the angles according to the altitude of the pole. He meant to say that the ascendants of the eclipse are three or more beyond the number that results from the calculation of the eclipse when done by the tables; because the difference of the hour in various provinces causes the movement to be tracked in different ways in each province, as we have said.
¶ After this, let us observe for how many equal hours the darkness of the eclipse will extend in each of the lands.
¶ After this, let us look at how many equal hours the duration of the eclipse lasts in any of the habitations.
¶ He means to say that when we know the ascendant of the beginning and the ascendant of the end, we will know for how many equal hours the darkness of the eclipse lasts; for an equal hour is 15 degrees, and a temporal hour is the 12th part of the day or night; and sometimes it will be more or less than 15 degrees when the day is longer or shorter than the night. Moreover, we should know the ascendant when it occurs by temporal hours because the effect of a solar eclipse cannot be extended beyond 12 years, and the effect of a lunar eclipse beyond 12 months; you should understand this from what he says next.
¶ Because when we have this knowledge, we will know that the future effects of a solar eclipse will last for as many years as its equal hours were; and a lunar one for the same number of months.
¶ And when we know this, we will know that the ascendant of the eclipse, if it is solar, will last as many years as there were equal hours of darkness; and if lunar, it will last as many months as those same hours were.
¶ And because the sun circles the firmament in one year, it follows that the event of its eclipse lasts for years; and because the moon circles in one month, it is fitting that it lasts for months; for this is the specific nature of each eclipse on its own. However, when something else is joined with the eclipses, 

<column-break/>

the event will last according to that. For example: if there were a conjunction <note>When two planets appear at the same point in the zodiac.</note> of Saturn and Jupiter with the eclipse, we already know by what we have said: that if this conjunction is the beginning of a "mutation" <note>A significant historical or meteorological shift.</note>, that event will last a thousand years or thereabouts, as we have revealed in the [section on] conjunctions. For we will convert these years into months if it were a lunar eclipse, and if solar, they will be years. And as much as is added from this duplication, that will be the time the event lasts. And if the conjunction is not the beginning of a mutation, it will last sixty years, or more according to the number when it returns to that same sign; and you should do this in all conjunctions and applications <note>When a faster planet approaches an aspect with a slower one.</note> that occur with an eclipse or in their oppositions.
For Ptolemy covered up this secret and remained silent about it in the example he gave us regarding eclipses; nor did I recognize any among those who read this book who understood this secret from Ptolemy's words. But I will uncover it for you, and you should apply your mind well until you understand it.
For since the mixture which is made from the combination of the sun’s power with that of the moon creates an event lasting about [a certain number of] years if solar and months if lunar, according to the number by which each of them circles the firmament; it happens that when another power of planets or fixed stars is mixed with the power joined from the sun and moon at the hour of the eclipse—in such a way that another mixture is made of the whole—the time of the event lasts according to what that mixture was: whether for decades or centuries or thousands of years. And because these mixtures are not to be estimated in the same way as the mixtures of the eclipses of the sun and moon, Ptolemy brought forward one example of these mixtures, and this is that which pertains to eclipses; and he considered it sufficient because the rest can be understood from the force of his words, just as good physicians do with medicines and foods. They teach of what "complexion" <note>The balance of qualities (hot, cold, wet, dry) in a person or substance.</note> each of these are in comparison to a balanced man, and the physician understands how he must work upon the complexions that have moved away from balance, to a greater or lesser degree. Ptolemy did the same with eclipses so that the astrologer might work through them according to powers increasing or decreasing their influence.
¶ Wherefore, because the beginning of these hours of events—and the entirety of their span of time—is only perceived according to the proportion of the place of the eclipse to the "angles," when the place of the eclipse is in the eastern part of the horizon, they will signify that the beginning of what is to come will be in the first four months after the hour of the eclipse. The state of its intensity will appear in the first third of the span of the total time in which the significations of that eclipse will manifest. But if it were in the part of the midheaven, they will signify that it will be in the second four months and in the middle third [of the total time]. And if it were in the western part of the horizon, they will signify that it will be in the last four months, in the final third.
¶ And the beginnings of the hours of these times, and generally this time, can be known from the comparison of the place of the eclipse to the angles. For when the place of the eclipse is from the eastern part of the horizon, it demonstrates that the beginning of the event will be in the first four months after the hour of the eclipse; and the greatest strength of the event itself will be in the first term of the whole time in which the eclipse's events will occur. And if it were in the part of the midheaven, it demonstrates it will be in the second four months, and the greatest strength in the middle term. And when it is in the western part toward the horizon, it demonstrates that the event will be in the last four months, and the greatest strength in the final term.
¶ Ptolemy adds in this place all the rules by which we can know when the event will be, how long it will last, and when its strength will be [greatest].

# Second

You will say that the time of these events and the time for which they will endure can be known from the location of the eclipse in comparison to the angles <note>The four cardinal points of an astrological chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli.</note>: for the occurrence of the eclipse is distant [from the Ascendant] by as many hours as the hours it is distant from the Ascendant, and these hours are temporal <note>original: "temporales"; hours that vary in length based on the season.</note>. And you shall know the hours of the eclipse's distance from the Ascendant through the rules which he <note>Ptolemy.</note> stated in the 10th chapter of the 3rd part, when he spoke of how the hours of distance for a significator <note>A planet or point in a chart that represents a specific person or event.</note> are extracted. For when you know how many hours there are between the eclipse and the eighth house: it is manifest that between the 10th house <note>The Midheaven or Zenith.</note> and the Ascendant there are six temporal hours. And when you add the hours by which the eclipse is distant from the tenth, after it has passed over the hours that are between the 10th and the Ascendant, the sum of the hours by which the eclipse is distant from the Ascendant will emerge. And if it has not passed the tenth, you should subtract from six hours: and the distance of the eclipse from the Ascendant at the beginning of the eclipse will remain; and thus you will know when the event of the eclipse begins according to what we showed before. Similarly, when you know the hours of distance of the eclipse from the Ascendant at the midpoint: you will know when the middle of the event will be. And when you know the hours of distance from the Ascendant at the end: you will know when the event of the eclipse will be completed. For we have these things from the eighth [book/chapter] of Ptolemy. And he added there one rule which he took concerning the specific place where the eclipse occurs, saying: if the eclipse is in the eastern part, the strength of the event will be in the first part of the time it lasts. And if it is toward the part of the Midheaven: the strength will be in the second middle of the time it lasts. And if it is toward the western part: the strength of the event will be in the final third of the time it lasts. For this is general in eclipses, conjunctions, and in all "applications" <note>The movement of one planet toward another to form an aspect.</note>. But Ptolemy held that no other conjunctions or applications can produce anything without having the stability of the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> or one of them; and so it appears demonstrated by his words in every place: for this reason, he left off speaking of conjunctions and spoke of eclipses because they are the "roots" in very great events. But when we know well the occurrence of eclipses, we will know the occurrences of all conjunctions. And so that you may understand better, I wish to give you an example: let us suppose there was a lunar eclipse and a conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter degree by degree with it, and that this conjunction is according to the degrees of "mutation" <note>The "Great Mutation" occurs when the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter moves from one zodiacal element (triplicity) to another, roughly every 200 years.</note>; and the darkness of the eclipse lasts for three equal hours. These hours signify three months, which are a fourth part of a year; and when we multiply them by a thousand years—since in that many years the "conjunction of mutation" returns to the sign—the number of 250 years will emerge. And because of this, you ought to consider how a conjunction changes the signification of a lunar eclipse from months to hundreds of years. And if other applications of the planets occur with this eclipse and conjunction, the hundreds will be changed to even more. For let us suppose there was a solar eclipse and a conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter with it degree by degree at the beginning of a degree of mutation; and the darkness of the sun lasts for two equal hours, which two hours signify two years, because one hour of a solar eclipse signifies years. And it is manifest that when we multiply two hours by a thousand years, two thousand years will result; however, the planets that are joined with the sun lose their virtues and perform nothing <note>This refers to "combustion," where a planet is too close to the sun to be visible or effective.</note>. And it is manifest that in such a long time, eclipses and conjunctions will occur which will signify along with that great beginning. Similarly, many eclipses can occur which will affirm the first signification and increase their effects; and because of this, one must take the judgment of one in comparison to another and judge according to the strength which you find to be prevailing, just as Ptolemy will now show you.

### Particular increases and decreases of future things are apprehended from the conjunctions and "preventions" <note>Syzygies, specifically the New or Full Moon occurring just before an event.</note> which will happen between these when they are in the places which are the occasions of future things, or in some place having fellowship with them in the figure.

### And the particular increases and decreases of these events can be known from the conjunctions which will be in the middle of this, when they happen in places having a reason in these events or in some places having participation with them in the figure.

### When we know anything from great events, we can know the increase and decrease through conjunctions and oppositions that occur in the place of that event: or which have concordance with that lo-

<column-break/>

-cation: for from this, the work is moved through that first [influence], inclining toward good or evil according to that which is "adorned" <note>Determined or configured.</note> in them if it is in the place where it is suitable for it; or if the one adorned in them is contrary to that which was adorned in the eclipse. For it will happen that the second will cause the first to lose its power if the second is stronger. And since it is so in conjunctions and oppositions, much more will it be in eclipses and "great conjunctions": because one can make another lose its force or will increase it. For each of them generates among us a supernatural power of great effect. And if it happens that the second "spirit" <note>The astrological influence or planetary character.</note> accords with the first, it will increase in its power, and its work will be renewed. And if it happens that the second is different from the first, they will find their power will be according to what the second spirit was. In this manner are the works of the planets toward us. And it follows for you to know that the second spirit will have the power of adding or subtracting in the work of the first: if it happens that the time of the second event accords with the time promised [by the first], accordingly one will work at a different time than the other adds; it will neither add nor subtract.

### And from the places and the motion of the planets through which future events happen, such as whether they are oriental or occidental, or stationary, or ascending in the first part of the night: and as they are assigned in the figure by aspects to the signs which are the occasions of future events, or in another way predicted.

### And from the places of the courses of the planets, events are joined if they are oriental or occidental: or stationary or ascending in the first night: or if they have participation in the figure with the signs producing the events.

### He says that an event grows or diminishes faster or slower, and lasts more or less, through the logic of what the status of the planets was that are "adorned" there, whether they were oriental or occidental, or direct or retrograde: or stationary or swift or slow. And this is also if they had participation with the signs in which the eclipse occurred, or the one which will work in the eclipse, and absolutely with the sign signifying the events.

### For when they are oriental or stationary, they will increase future things: when they are occidental, or exist under the rays, or are ascending in the evening and retrograde, they will work less upon future things.

### And if they are oriental and stationary, an increase of events will come through them: and if they are occidental or under the rays of the sun, or ascending in the first night and retrograde, a decrease of events will come through them.

### He means to say that when the planets are oriental <note>Rising before the sun.</note>, they are stronger: and because of this, their work will be greater and will appear more; and when they are occidental <note>Setting after the sun</note> or under the rays of the sun <note>Hidden by the sun's light</note>, they are of weaker power, and their work will be more diminished. And similarly when they are retrograde: because when they exist in a bad state, they work evil deeds in another manner than they have by nature, and the powers of their works will be according to the vices happening to them. For we see that the evil of Saturn and Mars increases much when they stand poorly: because the good which is in them is weakened and changed, and it returns in another way; for the predicted good which is in them [departs], and their malice remains. And it is manifest that the work of the planets increases when they have great power and is diminished when they are weak: and when they are swift, their work comes faster, and slower when they are slow. And when they are in the "angles" <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the strongest positions in a chart.</note>, they increase in the power of the event, and it comes faster; and when in the "cadent" houses <note>The 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses, the weakest positions.</note>, it diminishes the event and weakens it. And when in the "succedent" houses <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses.</note> of the angles, they work moderately in this. And it is manifest that the time of the event and how long it will last, and its power in itself, will be prolonged and dilated, increased and diminished according to the conjunctions and oppositions that occur after the eclipse which signified the event: and according to the planets which were "adorned" in the event and how long it will last. And afterward you shall inspect these other things: and you shall add to that which happens, or subtract according to how you see they stand, and that which results after this will be. For we have shown to you in the 13th chapter events lasting for thousands of years, hundreds, tens, and single units: and those which last for days, months, and hours, if you have understood the rules which we taught you, and if you understand those who spoke on events of thousands of years and in hundreds, tens, and units who did not lead by the correct path. <meta>This page continues the discussion on the methodology of astrological prediction, shifting from the timing of events (covered on the previous page) to determining the specific nature or "genus" of the events predicted by an eclipse. It emphasizes the primary authority of the Sun and Moon (the luminaries) over other planetary cycles and introduces the concept of the "Almudbebir" or governor of the eclipse.</meta>

Those who only accepted the indication of conjunctions <note>The alignment of two or more planets in the same zodiacal sign.</note> were mistaken, as were those who assigned a fixed number of years to each planet—claiming a thousand years for one planet and a thousand for another. They possess no certainty in these methods because conjunctions cannot exert any lasting influence without the two luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note>; for the luminaries are the princes over all stars. No one can establish anything firmly without their lord and without his mandate. If one tries to establish something without the lord, the lord will destroy it and establish something else. We have demonstrated this in many places. By all these means, it is clear that the conjunction and operation of the Sun and Moon during eclipses have greater power than all other planetary applications <note>term: application; the movement of a faster planet toward an aspect with a slower one.</note>, because they are always in one straight line. The greatest powers of planetary conjunctions are those joined in both longitude and latitude. Since this is so, it is necessary that eclipses have greater power than all other applications, because they involve the luminaries, which have greater and more manifest power than all other stars. It follows that the one with greater power is lord over the one with less power, as was demonstrated in the third part. Through this, it follows by all means that we receive many great changes from the two eclipses when a "great conjunction" <note>A significant alignment of major planets, usually Jupiter and Saturn, occurring roughly every 20 years.</note> occurs with them, as we have shown. For the conjunctions of planets are changeable by themselves, because planets are more mobile than the Sun and the Moon. As for the thousands of years of the planets that those men speak of, it is a number that follows no rule and has no natural reason. Because of this, everyone who has spoken of these things has spoken without reason and without wisdom, and those who came after followed them. However, when we understand the words of the most wise Ptolemy, we shall know the whole truth in itself, for this good man alone spoke the truth in this whole natural art. We have also shown you through our glosses all his propositions briefly; if we had wished to gloss and demonstrate them fully, the book would have been very large and would not have stood in a volume even twice its current size. Nevertheless, this was sufficient for you, because our wish is for you to understand the words of this good man; when you have understood them well, you will go rightly through all parts of this art. It is fitting that you know that the more you read this book and repeat it, the more you will understand every reason of the things contained within.

### On the Nature of Future Events. Chapter 7.

->Haly said.<-

This chapter follows what was said regarding the time of an event. After giving rules for knowing by what reason events come, and other rules for knowing the time when they happen and how long they will endure, he gives us in this chapter the rules for knowing what thing <note>original: "que res"; referring to the subject or category of life (e.g., kings, crops, weather) affected by the omen.</note> it will be that receives that event, saying:

<margin>The third type of prognostication is that by which we come to know in what category <note>original: "genus"</note> that event will occur. We can know this through the states and figures pertaining to the signs in which the eclipse locations are made, and in which the planets governing the sign of the eclipse and the sign of the angle <note>One of the four pivot points of the sky: the Ascendant (East), Midheaven (South), Descendant (West), or Imum Coeli (North).</note> before the eclipse are found.</margin>

The third type of prognostication is that through which we perceive the category of future events. This is indicated by the qualities and figures which are proper to the signs in which the eclipse is located, and also by the signs in which the wandering stars <note>The planets.</note> and the non-wandering stars <note>The fixed stars.</note> are positioned—specifically those which the lord of the eclipse sign and the sign of the angle preceding the eclipse have arranged.

He means to say that the events themselves are to be received which agree with the states and figures pertaining to the sign of the eclipse and the sign of the lord of the eclipse's location. Now we shall understand that the rule we must take through this involves two things. One is the sign of the eclipse. The other is the sign of the planet ruling in the sign of the eclipse and in the sign of the angle <note>term: angle; the specific houses (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) that represent the most powerful points in an astrological chart.</note> which is before the eclipse. And from these things, it happens among us that whatever agrees with the sign of the eclipse or with the sign of the ruling planet will receive the event. Similarly, it follows that we inspect the figures that are in the sign of the eclipse or with the governing planet, and we shall extract the indication from all these things.

The governor <note>original: "almudbebir"; an Arabic astrological term for the planet that holds the most "dignity" or power over a specific point in a chart.</note> will be known from the wandering stars of these two places, just as we teach here by narrating.

And we shall know which of the planets is the governor of these

<column-break/>

two places in this manner which I shall say.

After he said that the genus receiving the event can be known from the sign of the eclipse, the fixed stars, and the planets ruling in the sign of the eclipse and in the angle before it, he begins first to teach us how we shall know the planet ruling in those locations.

Therefore, the star that has many authorities in the two aforementioned places—that is, in the location of the eclipse and in the other location of the angle preceding the eclipse—and according to how it rules those houses, triplicities <note>term: triplicity; a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, Water).</note>, exaltations <note>term: exaltation; a specific sign where a planet is thought to have its greatest strength, second only to its own house.</note>, and even terms <note>term: term; a subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a specific planet.</note>, that star alone shall be the governor <note>original: "almudbebir".</note>.

I say that the planet which has many dignities in the two places we mentioned—and these are the location of the eclipse and the sign of the angle before the eclipse—is determined through the applications and relationships to the earth, and according to the portion of the division of the sign, and according to the dignity they hold, such as being lords of the houses, or of the triplicities, or of the exaltations, or of the terms. For that one alone shall be the lord of the governance.

These are the many dignities of the essential and accidental states of the planets: the essential ones are house, triplicity, exaltation, and term; the accidental ones are application, separation, being oriental or occidental <note>Whether the planet rises before or after the Sun.</note>, masculinity or femininity, and appearance; or having participation with the Sun or Moon in a figure; or being with the eclipse on one circle or on two equidistant circles; or having such a position as the eclipse has. And this is being with the eclipse in a circle from the circles that are equidistant to the horizon. For example: if the altitude of a planet in the eastern horizon is seven degrees, and the altitude of the eclipse in the western horizon is seven degrees. In this manner, let it have dignities in the angle that ascends before the eclipse—both essential and accidental dignities—for that will be the lord of the eclipse.

But if we do not find one star that rules both the location of the eclipse and the angle, and instead we find two or more stars having authority in these two places as we said before, we must act accordingly: and then the lord of the eclipse is to be preferred.

And if we do not find a single planet that is lord of both the eclipse and the angle, it follows that we take both planets having the most agreement with either of the two places as we said; and we shall choose first the lord of the eclipse and prefer him.

When it happens that there is not just one ruler in the sign of the eclipse and in the sign of the angle that ascends before it, and it happens that each of these two signs has its own planet ruling in it through many dignities it possesses there, it follows that we take the indication from both planets; and we shall prefer the indication of the one that rules in the sign of the eclipse, and afterward the planet that rules in the angle before the eclipse. And it is necessary that you understand that the angle which is before the eclipse is the angle that is to pass through the location of the eclipse by the motion of the equinox <note>original: "motu equinoctii"; the daily rotation of the celestial sphere.</note>.

But if several stars have equal authorities in these two places, we shall choose and prefer that one in the disposition which more appropriately indicates what happens in the angle, or which is of stronger work, or which more appropriately reaches those things.

And if the planets having dignities in these places are more than two, and each of them has equal dignities in these two places, we shall choose first and prefer the one who is closer to the angle, and is stronger in operation and power.

When more than one planet rules in the sign of the eclipse and in the sign of the angle which is before it, it follows that we choose the one among them who is stronger in the angle. And generally I say that we should always choose the one among them who is of greater work and power. And if they are equal in these things, take...

their governor, that which shall be in its *hazz* <note>original: "bazz"; a Latinization of the Arabic term *ḥaẓẓ*, meaning "portion" or "dignity"—a planet's strength in a specific degree.</note>; and in this way we shall face and look into each of them: and we shall count how many dignities it has, both essential and accidental <note>Essential dignities are a planet's strength based on its position in the zodiac; accidental dignities are based on its position in the "houses" or its speed.</note>: and that which we find to have the most dignities, either in an "angle" <note>The four most powerful points of an astrological chart: the East, West, Zenith, and Nadir.</note> or in its *hazz*, or to have the greater power: we shall take its signification if it rules in the sign of the eclipse, or in the sign of the angle which is before it. And this is the end of the rule given for knowing the ruling planet. And Ptolemy noted here that this is done without the Sun and Moon, because the planets incline the work of the Sun and Moon and lead them toward the nature of their own works; and because of this, we always take the "accident" <note>An "accident" here refers to a specific event or effect produced by the eclipse.</note> of the eclipse from the planets.

**And with this again, we shall thus receive the disposition of the non-wandering stars.** <note>Non-wandering stars: the "fixed stars," so called because they do not move through the zodiac like planets.</note>

**And from the governing fixed stars, we shall receive the signification in like manner with the planets.**
He means to say that we should join the signification of the fixed stars—those that are with the eclipse on one circle, or with the angle that is before it—with the significations of the planets; and according to this, we shall mingle the whole signification of the eclipse.

**Therefore, from the brightest stars, we shall first observe that one which appeared with the place of the eclipse in the angle that preceded the eclipse.**

**And what it behooves us to receive more are the stars which are in the place of the eclipse, and the bright stars existing in the angle which is before the eclipse.**
Bright fixed stars are those that are of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, and 5th magnitude; and when any *hazz* <note>original: "bazz"</note> is with the degree of the eclipse on the circle of the horizon or on the meridian circle after the eclipse. And this is in the angle which is before the eclipse; and it always falls westward from the eclipse: it will clearly have the principal power in governing the anterior angle. And in this way will be the signification of the fixed stars when they are with the eclipse: because it always happens that we mingle the signification of the fixed stars with those of the planets ruling them, taking first those which are of the greater magnitude.

**Which will be understood from those things we said in our first book: in which we narrated the nine modes of the associations of the figures which appear to the stars.**

**And we shall know by that which we demonstrated in our own book: when we declared the manners that appear in the planets.**
His first book is the book of the *Almagest* <note>The *Almagest* is Ptolemy's famous 2nd-century treatise on astronomy.</note>: in its eighth treatise he showed through arithmetic and geometry how we can know the participations of the figures that appear to the planets: one in respect to another, and in respect to the Sun and Moon, and in respect to their relation to the Earth. And you will certainly know all this through the eighth treatise.

**And yet again, we shall observe the stars which, at the hour of the eclipse, were with the ascending angle or with the angle of the midheaven together with that—namely, of those two angles which follow the place of the eclipse.**

**And with this let us mingle the signification of the planet which shall be at the second hour of the eclipse in the ascending angle, or with the angle of the midheaven, whichever of them follows the place of the eclipse.**
He means to say that it is necessary that we add to those significations that govern in the place of the eclipse and in the preceding angle, the signification of the planet governing the angle that follows the eclipse and the stars which were in that angle; for that angle places itself in the location of the eclipse by the movement of the firmament through which it creates day and night.

**But after we have apprehended the stars which we observe in this form for the purpose of knowing future events, we shall subjoin the observation of the sign in which the eclipse is, and the sign in which the stars have their disposition; for the knowledge of the "genus" in which the future event will happen cannot be had except through the qualities and properties of these aforesaid places.**

**After we have spoken concerning the stars from which we have the signification, receive it in this way: we wish to follow this by investigating what will be the "figures" <note>The visual representations or symbols of the zodiac signs (e.g., the Ram, the Twins).</note> of the signs in which the eclipse will be, and in which will be**

<column-break/>

the governing stars: because the genus in which the event happens can be known for the most part from the properties of these places.
He means to say that we must inspect the figures of the places in which the eclipse is, and the places in which the governing planets of the eclipse are, and the governors of the preceding angle, and the angle that comes after it: because the subjects in which the event happens are subjects that accord with the figures of the signs in which the ruling planets are; and the fixed stars according with the sign of the eclipse. However, we ought not to inspect the figures of the anterior angle or the one that follows after; for Ptolemy spoke of the figures of the governing signs, and did not speak of the others.

**Therefore, the figures of the signs which are formed in the angle of the zodiacal circle, and those which are according to the fixed stars: when they are figured in the likeness of the human figure, they signify that what is to be will happen in the human race. And if they represent the figure of wild animals, or if they are likened to quadrupeds, they will be found to occur in animals similar to them.**
**And if they are likened to the forms of creeping animals, the events will be among serpents and their like. Likewise, if they bear the likeness of wild beasts, that future event will happen among wild beasts that harm men; and if they represent the forms of domestic animals, it is not doubted that it will be found in domestic animals which men use and which help them in all times of their life—namely, in each species of these animals' forms: that is, in horses, oxen, and flocks, and in those similar to these.**

**So it is that if the figures of the signs in the zodiac, according to the fixed stars that are there, are similar to the figures of men, the event will be in the human race; and if they are similar to the figures of wild beasts or quadrupeds, the event will be in beasts similar to them. And if they are similar to reptiles, the event will be in snakes and their like. Similarly, if they are similar to the figures of savage beasts, the event will be in savage beasts that harm men. And if they are similar to domestic beasts, the event will be in beasts from which men are served and from which they help themselves in their life, according to the species of whatever beasts the figure was; thus are horses, cows, sheep, and such things.**

That which he said regarding the "figures in the zodiac," he said because of the figures of the signs: for among them are those in the figure of men, such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius, and the first half of Sagittarius. And those that are likened to wild quadrupeds, such as Leo and Capricorn <note>note: while Capricorn is often domestic, certain parts or interpretations link it to wilder terrain.</note>. And those likened to domestic ones, such as Aries, Taurus, Capricorn, and the last half of Sagittarius. And those likened to reptiles, such as Scorpio. And those likened to fish, such as Cancer and Pisces. And those likened to birds <note>original: "volatilibus", things that fly.</note>, such as Virgo, Gemini, and Pisces <note>Ptolemy often associates these signs with the air or with winged things in specific technical contexts.</note>. And in each of these, there are specific things with which they accord: for Aries accords with sheep, Taurus with cows and oxen, Leo with every species of wild beast. And the last half of Sagittarius with horses, mules, and donkeys. And Capricorn with goats and kids. And those which, according to the figures of the fixed stars that are outside the zodiac signs in the northern or southern part, each of those figures signifies the things among us that accord with them—just as the figure of the Dolphin signifies marine fish, and as the Ship <note>The constellation Argo Navis.</note> signifies all shipping and all such things. For in this same manner that the signification of the signs works, so also is it for the other figures.

**Likewise, that which from the figures of wild animals is placed toward the northern part especially signifies sudden mutations of the earth. But that which is figured toward the southern part shows alterations of the air that bring fear to no one.**

**Similarly, the figures of wild beasts that are in the northern part specifically signify movements of the earth that occur without warning. Similarly, those that are in the southern part signify the course of the air without warning.**

### Treatise

**These** motions of which he spoke are earthquakes and the ruin of castles and villages; the currents of the air, without any doubt, are strong winds and many unseasonable rains.
**Another** rule: when the locations of the stars that are ruling and disposing events are in figures having wings—such as in Virgo, Sagittarius, the Hen <note>original: "gallina"; refers to the constellation Cygnus, the Swan</note>, the Flying Vulture <note>original: "vulture volante"; refers to the constellation Aquila, the Eagle</note>, and those similar to these—it is manifest that the future event will happen to flying things, and especially to those flying things that are eaten by men.
**Because** if the locations of the planets that rule the governance of events are with the figures of birds—such as Virgo, Aquarius, or the Hen, or the Flying Vulture, or other such figures—the accident will occur to those creatures, especially those which are edible for humans.
**Virgo** and Aquarius, even if they have a human form, possess wings, and for this reason they signify birds which men eat; the Hen represents the figure of other hens that are raised among men; the figure of the Vulture and the figure of Hawks and Falcons and birds of prey represent other edible birds; and because of this, it follows that they signify edible birds.
**And** if they are in the figures of swimming animals—in Pisces and in all aquatic animals—that event will happen. For if they are in figures representing marine animals, such as in Cancer, Capricorn, and the Dolphin, the future event will be in marine animals and in ships of the sea. But if they are in the figures of river animals, such as in Aquarius and Pisces, it will appear in the animals of rivers and springs.
**And** if it is in the figures of swimming animals, the accident will be in fish and in all other animals that are in streams. And if it is in the figures of sea animals, such as Cancer, Capricorn, and the Dolphin, the accident will be in the animals of the sea and its voyages. And if it is in the figure of river animals, such as Aquarius and Pisces, the accident will be in the animals of the rivers and their springs.
**If** the significators are in the figure of swimming animals, there will be an accident in fish and in all other things passing through the water; and if these figures are of sea animals, the accident will be in sea animals and their voyages. And if these figures are of river and spring animals, the accident will be in the animals of rivers and springs. Regarding river animals, Cancer and Capricorn are significators of the sea (for the figure of Cancer is in the sea, and Capricorn is the significator of the greater part of the sea from the southern side), while the figure of Aquarius accords with running waters and signifies rivers; likewise also Pisces. Indeed, you can know these figures and what kind of power they have in the first part of this book, especially in the 9th chapter, where it speaks of the temperaments of the fixed stars. And you shall know the locations of the figures in the 7th and 8th [books] of the *Almagest* <note>The *Almagest* is the definitive 2nd-century mathematical and astronomical treatise by Ptolemy.</note> and in other books of these figures which the wise men have made.
**And** if it is in the figure of the Ship <note>The constellation Argo Navis.</note>, it will be seen in both kinds <note>Meaning both sea and river.</note>.
**And** if they are in the figures of the ship, the rising <note>The "accident" or event.</note> will be in both kinds.
**Because** the figure of the ship is in the sea and in the river, it follows that it signifies things which are in both. And if the significators are in it, there will be an accident in things that are in the sea and in rivers; and by this way you shall know the significations of the other figures.
**Likewise**, if it is in any of the solstitial or equinoctial signs, the signification will generally be in the things of the air and in the seasons appropriate to each of them.
**Likewise**, if it is in the two solstitial signs and in the two equinoctial signs <note>The four cardinal signs: Aries (Vernal Equinox), Cancer (Summer Solstice), Libra (Autumnal Equinox), and Capricorn (Winter Solstice).</note>, its signification will be generally in the states of the air and in the proper times belonging to each of those signs.
**We have said** many times that Ptolemy gives us only general rules. For when he finished speaking of the rules of the figures, he spoke of the figures of the states of the signs, both essential and accidental, saying that two

<column-break/>

solstitial signs and two equinoctial signs, if the significators are in any of them, demonstrate that the accident will be in the states of the air—such as regarding heat or winds or other such things—and it will be in the proper times in which the significator is found: if it is in Aries, it will be in the spring; and if in Cancer, in the summer; and if in Libra, in the autumn; and if in Capricorn, in the winter.
**Their** proper significations will appear in those things which are born from the earth.
**However**, the proper signification will be in the things that are born in the earth.
**When** the significators are in any of these four signs, they demonstrate by their conjunction that the accident will be in the changes of the air and in the seasons; they also demonstrate properly in things that are born from the earth.
**Another** rule: when it is in the vernal equinoctial sign <note>Aries</note>, their significations will be found in the fruits of trees when they begin to arise, as in vineyards and fig trees and those that ripen at the same time. But if it is in the summer solstitial sign <note>Cancer</note>, they signify future events in fruits when they are gathered and stored, except that in the regions of Egypt, they will show their proper significations in the rising of the Nile. But if it is in the autumnal equinoctial sign <note>Libra</note>, the significations will be in seeds when they are sown, and in herbs and similar things. But if they are in the winter solstitial sign <note>Capricorn</note>, their significations will happen in vegetables and in that which appears of birds and fish.
**So** also when it is in the sign of the vernal equinox, its signification will be in the fruits of trees that grow quickly, such as in nuts, figs, and others which are born in these times; and if it is in the sign of the summer solstice, they demonstrate accidents that will be in the fruits which are to be gathered and managed; and in the land of Egypt its signification will be properly in the rising of the Nile; and if it is in the sign of the autumnal equinox, its signification will be in things that are sown, in herbs and such. And if it is in the sign of the winter solstice, its signification will be properly in vegetables, and in what appears of the nature of birds and fish.
**For** since each of these signs has its own proper accident when the significators are in it—and because the principal and more useful beginning always remains in that which comes after, and because of this all things that are generated in any time are changed, and by its beginning it is signified—Ptolemy spoke of this with reason. However, that which he said—that when the significators are in the summer solstice, it demonstrates the rising of the Nile in the land of Egypt—requires a greater explanation. For the Nile comes from springs and rains that are in the southern part around the mountain which is called Len <note>likely "Mons Lunae" or Mountains of the Moon, the legendary source of the Nile</note>; and the nature and increase of rains are much in the part where humidity prevails, as at the end of winter. And it is manifest that when the sun comes to the northern part, the northern part will grow cold, and in it rains and snows increase. And because of this, when the significators are in the summer solstice, and if they have shown humidity, they join with the other humidity; and there becomes much moisture in the southern part; and by this way the rising of the Nile grows; and if the significators show dryness, it will be the opposite. Likewise, if it is in the southern part, a thing signifying dryness in it will demonstrate that the rising of the Nile will be very small; and because of this, it happens that the most proper signification of the Nile is of the summer solstitial sign, and it follows the sign of the vernal equinox itself. And if these two agree in humidity, the rising of the Nile will be very great. And if they are of different manners, it will be diverse according to that; yet these things do not have truth unless the significators show humidity when they are in Cancer. For through this we can know the state of the Nile and of all other rivers coming from the southern part to the north; however, concerning rivers coming from the northern part, it can be known from the significators when they are in the winter solstice, and in the sign of Libra conversely, according to how it is in the Nile.

# Second Book

¶ Also, when [the significator] is in any of the equinoctial signs <note>The equinoctial signs are Aries and Libra, marking the start of Spring and Autumn</note> in churches and in houses established for the honor of God, they will signal future events.
¶ <margin>Similarly, when it is in the two equinoctial signs, they demonstrate those things which will happen in sanctuaries and in the service of God.</margin>
¶ This is another property which the two equinoctial signs have: so that when the signs are in them, they will demonstrate what accident will occur in the air appropriate to it, and in the planting of the earth, and in things pertaining to sanctuaries and the service of God. Such are the churches of the Christians, the mosques <note>original: "moschete"</note> of the Saracens, and synagogues, and other such places. And that which pertains to the service of God is like the laws; because the two equinoctial signs—one being the vernal <note>Spring</note>, the first increase of the day, and the other the autumnal, the first increase of the night—it follows that they accord with the laws, for laws are the first conjunction of men. And because the laws are in accord with these two signs, it follows that the significance of the change that happens in them belongs to these two signs when the significations are within them.
¶ IF, however, it is in any solstitial sign <note>The solstitial signs are Cancer and Capricorn, marking the longest and shortest days of the year</note>, they will judge changes of character <note>original: "morum"; can refer to customs, morals, or habits</note> in those living in that region.
¶ <margin>If it is in the two signs of the solstices, it will demonstrate changes that will happen in the character of citizens.</margin>
¶ This property happens to the two solstitial signs because they diminish from that which the equinox creates, for one of them is very hot and the other very cold; and because of this, a change of character occurs with them.
¶ If it is in fixed signs <note>The "fixed" signs are Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, associated with stability</note>, in foundations and in buildings, they will demonstrate future events to come.
¶ <margin>And if they are in fixed signs, they signify accidents occurring in structures and foundations.</margin>
¶ The reason why fixed signs signify structures <note>original: "frogas"; likely a medieval variant of *fabricae*, meaning buildings or constructions</note> and foundations <note>original: "cimenta"</note> is because of the accord they have with them in stability and many times. I say, therefore, that the general rule in things pertaining to any planet and to any sign is that it has its signification because of the accord it has within itself in another manner of accord. For example: iron, because it is very dry, accords with the nature of Mars; and the sword, because it kills and is made of iron, accords with Mars in two parts—one because it is of the nature of iron, and second because it kills. And since this matter is so natural, it is because the fixed signs, when the significators are in them, have to manifest what accident will be in structures and foundations. Structures are like the building of towns, castles, and houses; and foundations are the roots of all these things, because the root of anything is the foundation upon which it stands.
¶ And if they are in common signs <note>Also known as mutable or "double-bodied" signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note>, they will pre-signify future events to happen in men and kings.
¶ <margin>And if it is in fixed signs of two bodies <note>The translator is using "fixed" loosely here to refer to the "double-bodied" or mutable signs</note>, they will show those things which happen in men and in kings.</margin>
¶ The reason why the signs of two bodies accord with men and kings is because they are intermediaries, having participation with both the fixed and the mobile signs; and their nature is composed of the nature of both signs that surround them. And so are men, because their substance has participation with all other substances. And because of this, the ancient wise men said that "man is a microcosm" <note>original: "homo est minor mundus"; a common medieval philosophical concept that the human body reflects the structure of the universe</note>. Just as kings have to govern all things, it follows that they have participation with the signs of two natures for two reasons: one because they are of human nature, which is composed of all things; the other on account of the kingdom, which has to govern all things.
¶ Similarly, when the hour of the eclipse is in places near the eastern horizon <note>original: "usum orientem altitutis"</note>, they will designate future events in fruits, and in those whose years are of youth, and in foundations.
¶ <margin>Similarly, if they are in places that are on the eastern side at the hour of the eclipse, they demonstrate what accident will be in trees, in the age of youth, and in foundations.</margin>
¶ Trees accord with the significators that will be in the east, because the eastern part is nobler and of greater power than that of the west. Similarly, it is the first place of the rising of all stars; and because of this, all things have their force there, just as childhood and trees accord with this eastern part. Similarly, all first things accord with it, such as foundations and the like.

<column-break/>

¶ But if it is in the middle of heaven <term>Midheaven</term> <note>The highest point in the sky at the time of the event, associated with power and career</note> which is above the earth, the significations will appear in churches and the powerful, and in those whose years are middle-aged.
¶ <margin>And if it be in the Midheaven above the earth, it demonstrates what accident will be in sanctuaries, to kings, and in the age of those in their middle years.</margin>
¶ Signs and stars that are in the Midheaven above the earth have great nobility, power, and lordship; and because of this, those things which are similar accord with them, such as sanctuaries which have great power over men, and kings, and those of middle age who have strength, wisdom, and experience, and have passed through and seen many things. For their strength is around the strength of adolescent boys, but they have passed through that part, and their bodies and senses are healthier than those of the elderly; and because of this, it follows that when significators are in the part of the 10th house <note>The Midheaven</note>, they demonstrate sanctuaries, kings, and those of the middle age.
¶ If, however, it is in the west, the signified events will happen in characters and variations of character, and in those whose years are of old age, and even in the dead.
¶ <margin>And if it be in the west, it demonstrates what accident is in the change of laws, in the age of the elderly, and in the dead.</margin>
¶ Because the western part signifies weakness and the end of light and of all things, it demonstrates that the accident will be in the end of things and their change from one state to another. Ptolemy <note>original: "Ptol."</note> however gave us all the rules by these similarities through which we can know the subject that will receive the accident. For he taught us those things which pertain to the signs as much from accidental properties as from essential ones; because when the signs are in any of these parts which he mentioned, they have an accidental property, and whether a sign is fixed, mobile, or of two natures is its essential property; and it is fitting that you proceed by this path which he gave to you.
¶ Knowledge of the quantity of the parts in which the future events of a specific kind will appear is understood from the quantity of the darkness of the eclipse and from the proportion of the stars that will be the causes to the place of the eclipse.
¶ <margin>We understand the quantity of the parts in which the accident of that subject genus will happen from the quantity of the obscurity of the eclipse, and from the comparison of the planets signifying the accident to the place of the eclipse.</margin>
¶ He gives us rules through this, by which we may know the quantity of the accident which that subject will receive, just as before he gave rules by which we know what the subject receiving it will be. And he says that we can know the quantity in two ways: one by the quantity of the obscurity of the eclipse, because if that light is totally covered by the eclipse, it demonstrates that the accident will receive the whole genus; and if half of the body of the light is obscured, it demonstrates that half of the subject genus will receive the accident; and in all other parts you should understand it in this manner. The other way is perceived from the comparison of the places of the dominant planets to the place of the eclipse; for if they are of great power, it demonstrates that the accident will be in the greater part of that genus, and if weak, in the smaller part, which Ptolemy will reveal to us by what he says next.
¶ Furthermore, if it be in evening figures in a solar eclipse or in morning figures in a lunar eclipse, the future events will happen in a smaller part of that genus; when that which is in opposition by diameter occurs, it will embrace half of that genus. But if in a solar eclipse it be in morning figures, and in a lunar [eclipse] in evening figures, they signify that future events will happen in the greater part.
¶ So that if it be in evening figures in eclipses of the sun, or in morning figures in eclipses of the moon, the accident will be in the smaller part of that genus. And if they are opposite across the diameter, the accident will be in half of the genus. And if they are in morning figures in eclipses of the sun, or in evening figures in eclipses of the moon, the accident will be in the greater part of the genus.

He means to say that the significations are weak when they are in the "evening" position in comparison to a solar eclipse, or "morning" position in comparison to a lunar eclipse; for this reason, their power will be in the lesser half of their kind. And if they are in the opposite position of the eclipse, the event will be moderate.
