# Third Book

in the angles or in the <term>succedent houses</term> <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th houses, which "follow" the primary angles</note>: they are strongest in the first two, which are the ascendant and the <term>midheaven</term> <note>original: "medium celi"; the highest point in the sky at birth</note>. Their greatest weakness in the world occurs when they are in <term>peregrine</term> places <note>original: "locis peregrinis"; signs where the planet has no traditional dignity or "home" advantage</note>, or with signs they have no harmony with, or when they are <term>occidental</term> <note>setting after the sun</note> or diminished in their course. Their greatest weakness in a birth chart is when they are <term>cadent</term> <note>falling away</note> from the angles.

¶ This is the second rule. He has already shown you that we can know the state of an <term>accident</term> <note>an event or circumstance in a person's life</note> through three things: by the planet that acts as its <term>dispositor</term> <note>the planetary "manager" of a specific sign or house</note>, by the sign it is in, and by the location that has harmony with the event. Now he shows us in this section that the magnitude of an event can be known by the degree of strength of these three things. He returns to what he showed us in the first part to make clear everything he demonstrated there. He says that planets have **essential** qualities, through which they have greater power, and **accidental** qualities, which can make them weak. The essential things that give them power are when they are in their own houses, <term>triplicities</term> <note>groups of three signs associated with an element</note>, exaltations, or terms; or when masculine planets are in masculine signs and feminine in feminine. Similarly, if they are <term>oriental</term> <note>rising before the sun</note> or moving quickly, they will have greater power. The opposites of these essential things make them weak: such as when they are in peregrine places or places where they have no harmony. This happens when a masculine planet is in a feminine sign, or when they are occidental or slow in their course; it is necessary to follow what he said in this book according to what he narrated in the first part. The **accidental** things that give planets greater power are when they are in the angles or succedent houses, especially the ascendant or midheaven. The accidents that make them weak are when they are in "cadent" places: these are the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th houses. Of these, the worst are the 6th and 12th because they do not "aspect" <note>form a geometric relationship with</note> the ascendant. It is helpful to keep in your memory everything taught in the first part regarding this section.

¶ We shall also consider the span of future time by investigating whether the planets are <term>matutinal</term> <note>morning stars</note> or <term>vespertine</term> <note>evening stars</note> in relation to the Sun and the ascendant. Two quadrants of each, and the two diametrically opposite to them, are matutinal; the others are vespertine. We will also consider if they are in the angles or approaching the angles. If they are matutinal or in the angles, their effects will be more acute and swift; but if they are vespertine or approaching the angles from behind, they are said to be slower in their operation.

¶ And we will look at the oriental timing, considering if they are matutinal or vespertine in comparison to the Sun and the ascendant. The two quadrants preceding each of them, and the two opposite them, are matutinal, and the other two that follow are vespertine. We will see if they are in the angles or approaching the angles; if they are matutinal or in the angles, they will be of stronger operation; if vespertine or approaching the angles, they will be of slower operation.

¶ This is the third rule: it shows us that the quadrant preceding the ascendant consists of the 10th, 11th, and 12th houses. Its opposite is the 4th, 5th, and 6th houses. These two quadrants are matutinal in relation to the ascendant. The other two quadrants—one being the 7th, 8th, and 9th houses, and the other being the ascendant, 2nd, and 3rd—are vespertine. Regarding the Sun, the quadrant preceding it is the 10th, 11th, and 12th houses from its position, and the other matutinal quadrant is the 4th, 5th, and 6th from the Sun's position. The other two quadrants are vespertine in comparison to the Sun. It is clear that when planets are oriental to the Sun, they have a greater effect. Similarly, when they pass the opposition of the Sun, they grow stronger every day and approach "direction" <note>normal forward motion</note>. We have already demonstrated all of this in the commentary on the first part. When he says they are of "greater operation," he means the effect will come at a time close to the birth. When he says "slower operation," he means it will delay its effect until a later time after the birth. This delay can be known 

<column-break/>

by the amount of strength of the three factors: the planet, its dispositor, and the place that agrees with the matter.

### ¶ On Parents. Chapter 4.

->Haly said:<-

We have already shown the reason why it happens that a person's birth chart holds significations for their parents: we say it is because of the harmony that exists between the births of children and those of their parents. Similarly, we have explained the reason why Ptolemy placed the judgment of parents first.

¶ For the first path which we must always follow in the investigation of each of these species is as follows.

¶ The first proposition which we must always follow in knowing any of the aforementioned modes is in this manner.

He means to say that the scientific way to understand all these modes consists of the three general rules he gave us. One of these is taking the signification of any matter from its place in the firmament, from the dispositor of that place, and from the sign in which the dispositor is found. Another is knowing at what time that event will come, which can be known through the "sharpness" of these stars.

¶ We will therefore now begin from the first chapter, which is the chapter on the discussion of parents, as it seems to suit the order we have just established. We shall say that the **Sun and Saturn** are naturally likened to fathers, while the **Moon and Venus** are likened to mothers.

¶ And we begin first with the primary chapter, which is the chapter on the judgment of parents, as it fits the aforementioned order. And we say that the Sun and Saturn have a natural harmony with fathers, while the Moon and Venus have harmony with mothers.

¶ Since the Sun is of greater cause and strength, and the generation of a creature and the movement of the <term>menses</term> <note>blood/vitality</note> comes from the seed of the man, it is natural that the Sun is in harmony with the father. Similarly, because Saturn shares in strength with the Sun and is also masculine and diurnal, he fits this role; he serves as the dispositor of fathers at times when the Sun cannot well-dispose them. For when the Sun is weak in power, Saturn will be the dispositor of fathers. Likewise, because the Moon follows the Sun in generation, it is fitting that she harmonizes with mothers; and because Venus shares with the Moon more than all others, it follows that she is the significator of mothers after the Moon in the same way.

¶ Therefore, just as the qualities of these stars are found in relation to each other and to others, so it is fitting for us to estimate the qualities of the parents. Indeed, their fortune and misfortune, as well as their rank, must be considered by us from the proximity of the stars to the <term>luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and Moon</note>. For when both luminaries are surrounded by "fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> that are in their same <term>halit</term> <note>original: "baltu" or "halit"; sect or condition</note> and joined in two signs or following them, they signify that the parents' condition will be excellent. This is especially true when the planets surrounding the Sun are matutinal, and those surrounding the Moon are vespertine; for then their position will be most favorable.

¶ And according to the state in which these planets are found, or in their comparison to other things in the same way, we can understand the state of the fathers. Thus, it is necessary that we pay attention to their fortune and wealth based on how the planets surround both luminaries. When the "fortunes" surround both luminaries, and those planets are in their own two signs or in signs following them, they signify that the state of the parents will be excellent and honorable—especially if the planets surrounding the Sun are matutinal and those agreeing with the Moon are vespertine. Then their placement will be good, as we have said.

# Treatise

He has already given us as a certainty that those planets which agree with the <term>parts</term> <note>referring to the specific lots or portions of the zodiac designated for parents</note> are the Sun and the Moon: as we demonstrated in the preceding <term>glosses</term> <note>interpretive comments written in the margins or between lines</note>, the Sun and the Moon are the authors of all generation. And we said a little before that if either of them is not strong in the nativity, the disposition of the nativity will fall to the planet that has participation with them: if the Sun is weak, Saturn will be the <term>dispositor</term> <note>the planet that "manages" or rules the sign where another is located</note> of the father in its place; and if it be the Moon, Venus will be the mother’s dispositress in its place. And the "surrounding" <note>original: "circumdatio"; also known as "spear-bearing" or "doryphory," where a planet is flanked by others</note> of which he spoke is this: that there be another planet or its rays before a planet, and another planet or its rays after it, whether they are in one sign or in two. One must keep in mind this condition: that the virtue of the planet being "besieged" <note>enclosed between two others</note> is mixed with the virtue of those surrounding it. The meaning is that when <term>benefics</term> <note>original: "fortune"; helpful planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> surround a planet, its virtue is mixed with the virtue of fortune with goodness and honor. But if the besieged planet is an <term>unfortunate</term> <note>original: "infortunatus"; a malefic planet like Mars or Saturn</note>, if it is in its own <term>baiz</term> <note>original: "baiz"; a medieval Latinization of an Arabic term referring to a planet's proper dignities or "sect" condition</note> it increases in whichever virtue it desires, and in such a way it will be beneficial; for if its virtue were harmful through dryness, it would benefit greatly if the virtues of the surrounding planets were moist; and if it were harmful through cold, it helps much if they are hot. And we have already demonstrated this rule in the gloss of the first part; nevertheless, we mention it here again so that you may keep it better in mind. It is manifest that when the planets surrounding the Moon are <term>vespertine</term> <note>setting in the evening after the Sun</note>, it is a thing more suitable to the Moon itself, since its virtue is <term>occidental</term> <note>western/evening-related</note>, and every thing is strengthened by its own kind. When you have understood this gloss well, you will understand Ptolemy.

Likewise, if Saturn and Venus are <term>oriental</term> <note>rising in the morning before the Sun</note> in their own proper **almugea** <note>a specific planetary relationship to the Sun or Moon based on their relative distances</note>, or if they are in **angles**, we ought to signify from this the manifest good fortune of the parents according to the quantity fitting for each of them.

Similarly, if Saturn and Venus are oriental and in the **aspect of the face** <note>a specific 10-degree division of a sign</note> that pertains to them, or in **angles**, it is fitting that we understand by this that the fortune of the fathers will be well-apparent according to what agrees with each of them.

In this statement there is a little difficulty: it is fitting that one looks to the state of Venus and Saturn when both are the dispositors of the parents. For if they are the dispositors, it will be necessary that we similarly look at which planets aspect them, and what kind of strength they have in all the other things we mentioned before. And if beyond this it happens that they are in the aspect of the face pertaining to them—and we already demonstrated this aspect of the face in the first part—or that they are in angles: it follows that we understand by this that the fortune of the parents will be clearly visible. We understand this through the two **luminaries** <note>the Sun and the Moon</note> when they are the dispositors and the planets of fortune and good surround them, such as when they are in their own *baiz*; for by this we understand that the status of the parents will be honored. And when he says "according to what agrees with each of them," you should understand what he said regarding "each of them" because he speaks for both parents: for it is necessary for us to look for the father from the planet governing him, and for the mother from the planet disposing her.

But if the opposite of these things occurs—namely, that the luminaries are **void of course** <note>original: "cursu vacua"; moving through a sign without making an aspect to another planet</note> and surrounded by no stars—they will signify the decline and lowliness of the parents. This is especially true if the position of Venus and Saturn is unsuitable.

And if the matter stands in this way, so that the luminaries are void of course nor do any planets surround them, it signifies the debility of the parents and their lowliness, especially if the place of Venus and Saturn is not good.

We have already understood through the words of Ptolemy that the significator of the father is the Sun, and after that Saturn follows it; the Moon is the significatrix of the mother, and Venus follows her. And we understand that when one of them is in a good state as described, and he alone rules over the father or mother, that parent whose significator rules will be in a good state. And if those which follow them in disposition are similarly in a good state, they will increase in the good and honor of that parent whose significators they are, because the significators will be in agreement upon one thing. For example: let us suppose that the Sun signifies the father's prosperity

<column-break/>

and honor: and if Saturn agrees with this same thing, it will help the Sun to give the father the greatest prosperity, honor, and a name. And we will similarly look into the state which Ptolemy described in this place: and we shall distinguish the unhappiness of the parents and their usefulness, just as we did regarding honor and good.

Just as it happens when Mars ascends after the Sun, and Saturn after the Moon, and the places of the fortunes do not aspect the luminaries in a fitting way, nor are they mixed from their *baiz*: it is not unfitting to signify to us from this the destruction of the parents' lives.

And if planets that are not of their *baiz* aspect them—as happens when Mars ascends after the Sun, and Saturn after the Moon—and the place of the fortunes is not good in comparison to the luminaries, and they are not of their *baiz*: it follows that by this we understand the lowliness of the lives of both parents, and the punishment they will have.

Now, regarding what he says, "if he aspects them": he speaks regarding the two significators, whether they are the two luminaries or Saturn and Venus. And we have already demonstrated that these planets are not of the *baiz*. He gives us an example of this and says that when Mars ascends after the Sun, it is "before" it <note>in terms of the daily rotation</note>, and it creates in the virtue of the Sun a harmful virtue through great heat and dryness; and when Saturn ascends after the Moon, it is "before" it, and it creates in the virtue of the Moon a harmful virtue through great cold and moisture. And after he gave us this division and its example, he gives us a summary in what he said: "And the place of the fortunes was not good in comparison to the luminaries," when they were of their own *baiz*. He means that the significators of the parents, when they are corrupted and the fortunes have not testified to them through the two luminaries generally, signify that the parents have lowliness and misery and a laborious life. And after he completed these things, he wishes to give us another rule by which we may know the riches and poverty of the parents.

But if the **Part of Fortune** <note>a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity</note>—which signifies the fate we shall mention—is found in the nativities of the parents to be in fit agreement with the stars surrounding the Sun or Moon, their substance will be preserved and will endure. But if the Part signifying fortune does not stand as we said—or if the opposite of these things occurs, and no fortunes surround the luminaries, or if those surrounding are misfortunes—the possession of the parents will not be perfected, but will suffer harm.

And if the Part signifying fortune (which we shall name hereafter) is suitable in the nativity, agreeing with the planets surrounding the Sun or Moon, the goods will be preserved and the riches of the parents will remain. And if the Part signifying fortune is not as we predicted, or if it is the opposite, and no fortunate planet surrounds the luminaries—or if unfortunate planets surround them—the riches of the parents will not be perfected; rather, they will cause them harm.

Ptolemy distinguishes this reasoning similarly and affirms it. And the division is what he said: "if the Part of Fortune is suitable in the nativity, agreeing with the planets surrounding the Sun and Moon, the goods will be preserved and the riches of the parents will remain." He means in this statement that if the Part of Fortune is in concord with the planets surrounding the significator of the parents, whoever they may be, it signifies that the parents' riches will not be destroyed or lost after this birth. And if it is not in concord, nor of the *baiz* of the parent's significator, it signifies that the parents' riches will be lost and destroyed. And he gave an example in the Sun and the Moon, giving it to be understood that the same happens in Saturn and Venus if they themselves were the significators. And the summary is what he said: "if any planets do not surround the luminaries or unfortunate planets surround them." He means that if the Part of Fortune is not in concord in the nativity with the planets surrounding the significators of the parents, the parents' riches will be lost and destroyed. And what is more, it happens that...

# Book Three

...that the <term>unfortunates</term> <note>original: "infortune"; malefic planets like Mars or Saturn</note> surround the two <term>luminaries</term> <note>the Sun and the Moon</note>: [the parents] will suffer and be weary regarding their riches until they are taken far away and removed from them, and they shall come to great poverty and misfortune. And it is necessary that you understand the same regarding the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>a calculated point in a chart representing prosperity</note> when you wish to judge the wealth of the newborn. And everything that Ptolemy has said up to this point regarding parents is found in the three aforementioned signs. He also told us previously that it is necessary to look at the planets ruling in the places signifying the parents, as well as the places of the planets that rule. And since this is so, it is necessary that we look at the state of the parents from each of these three things. For this reason, we find in the books of Dorotheus <note>original: "Dozomi"; likely a corruption of Dorotheus of Sidon</note> and other judicial astrologers that the state of the parents is judged by the <term>lords of the triplicities</term> <note>planets that rule groups of three zodiac signs of the same element</note> and many other things they spoke of; all of this is included in the words of Ptolemy, if you recall correctly and keep in memory what we told you. And this "Part of Fortune" which he mentioned in this place is that part which is calculated by the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the birth.

**C** <note>original: "C" likely standing for "Capitulum" or Chapter/Section</note> We shall consider the length of the parents' lives and their brevity from the associations of the stars in the <term>figures</term> <note>the astrological charts or planetary arrangements</note>.

**C** And it is useful that we look for the length and brevity of the parents' lives from other participating planetary arrangements.

**C** Ptolemy has shown us how we can know how long the life of the parents will be, and he gave us a completely general rule, which is that we can know this from the <term>significators</term> <note>planets or points that represent a specific person</note> of the parents. He revealed to us that the significators of the parents are three: one is the place of the <term>dispositor</term> <note>the planet ruling the sign where another planet is located</note>; another is the lord of that place; the third is the place of that lord themselves. Of all these, the most powerful is the place of the dispositor, and afterward, the place of the lord itself.

**C** Let us speak, therefore, of the life of the father. Whenever Jupiter and Venus in any figure are associated in some way with the Sun or Saturn, or when Jupiter is associated with Venus, and there is a suitable association of the Sun and Saturn—either if they are <term>conjoined</term> <note>located in the same spot</note> or in <term>trine</term> <note>120 degrees apart</note> or <term>sextile</term> <note>60 degrees apart</note> aspect and both are strong—we shall announce a long life for the father from this.

**C** And if Jupiter or Venus has participation with the Sun or Saturn in the five configurations, or if Jupiter has participation with Venus, and the participation of Saturn with the Sun is harmonious—such that it is in the <term>third</term> <note>sextile</note> or <term>sixth</term> <note>trine</note> from it, or they are conjoined and both are powerful—we understand by this that the life of the parents will be long.

**C** He has already taught us that the natural significator of the father is the Sun, and after the Sun, Saturn. It is necessary, therefore, that we first know which of them is the significator of the father; and when we have known and found which [benefic] forms have participation with him, and by any of the ways we mentioned in the first part, we will understand by this that the life of the father will be prolonged. And if we do not find it so, but there is participation between Venus and Jupiter such that their virtues are mixed, we understand the same by this: for a great virtue of the <term>fortunes</term> <note>benefic planets</note> comes to the earth. If Saturn has a harmonious participation with the Sun as we said, this provides a long life. And if someone should ask how there can be harmony from the conjunction of Saturn and the Sun, we say that the heat of the Sun is tempered by the cold of Saturn, and a good <term>complexion</term> <note>a balanced physical temperament</note> is made from it. As for what he said about both being powerful, this was said for the Sun and Saturn: if both are in a [strong] position in the world or in relation to the <term>angles</term> <note>the four most powerful points in a chart: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and IC</note>, they will signify a long life for the father, and even more strongly if there is participation of Jupiter and Venus there.

**C** If they are not strong, however, it will not be so; yet because of this, they will not truly signify brevity of life.

**C** And if they are not powerful, it will be the opposite; however, they will not because of that demonstrate entirely that the life will be short.

**V** <note>original: "V" likely standing for "Vult dicere," meaning "He [the author/commentator] wishes to say"</note> He wishes to say that if the fortunes do not have participation with the significators of the father, and the Sun and Saturn are not powerful in their places, yet there is still participation between Jupiter and Venus, and between the Sun and Saturn: if things stand thus, we will not judge that the life of the father is long; similarly, for such a small matter, we will not judge it to be short unless there is something else there to say so.

**C** But if it does not happen thus, but over the Sun or Saturn

<column-break/>

Mars is <term>elevated</term> <note>occupying a more dominant or "higher" house position</note> or if he follows them, and Saturn is not in agreement with the Sun but is in a <term>fourth aspect</term> <note>a square, or 90 degrees</note> or opposite through the diameter <note>an opposition, or 180 degrees</note>, or if both are remote from an angle, the debility of the father will be signified.

**C** And if it is not as [the previous positive signs] were, and Mars is elevated over the Sun or Saturn, or if he is following them, or Saturn is not harmonious with the Sun but is in the fourth or in opposition to it on the diameter; or if both are <term>cadent</term> <note>falling away</note> from the angles, debility happens to the father from this.

**C** Because he said "if it is not thus," he means when we do not have a significator demonstrating a long life for the father; rather, we find another sign from which we understand his debility and the infirmity of his body. We shall judge that the father's life will be short, and the reason we understand the father's debility is when Mars is elevated over the father's significator or follows the significator (for this is when he goes to join himself with it). For when it is in this manner, it signifies debility or infirmity of the body—with the Sun, because it increases in its heat and dryness, and with Saturn, because it increases in its evil and harm. And it is necessary that you understand that a planet is "high" which travels by the motion of the <term>equinox</term> <note>the diurnal rotation</note> to the place of the planet existing under it. For example, a planet in the 10th house is elevated over one in the 9th. We shall judge similarly if there is a harmful participation between the Sun and Saturn, such as the square and opposition, because all of this signifies the father's debility and physical infirmity. And if the Sun and Saturn are cadent from the angles, because they will then be weak, they will similarly signify the father's debility and infirmity; and when the father remains in such a state, he will quickly incur death, because his virtue is destroyed by the occasion of great infirmities that will multiply in him.

**C** But if they are in the angles or in places ascending toward the angles, they will signify a short life for the parents or some injury; for when they stand in the first two angles, which are the Ascendant and the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: "mediu celi"</note>, they judge a brevity of life. But when they are in the other two, which are the <term>Descendant</term> <note>original: "occñs"</note> and the <term>angle of the earth</term> <note>the IC or lowest point of the chart</note>, or in places ascending toward them, they are said to impede. When Mars regards the Sun in the aforementioned way, he will pass away by a sudden death, or an impediment will happen in his <term>luminaries</term> <note>often referring to the eyes</note>. If, however, he regards Saturn, they will signify the father's death or a fever with tremors, or an impediment resulting from a cutting or burning. Again, when the configuration of Saturn is unfavorable in respect to the Sun, the father's death will happen by the occasion of diseases occurring from harmful <term>humors</term> <note>the four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile—thought to control health</note>.

**C** And if both are in angles or houses that rise from the angles, the fathers will be of short life, and pestilence and a short life will happen to them. And if they are in the first two angles, which are the Ascendant and the Midheaven, pestilence will happen to them. If they are in the two latter angles, which are the Descendant and the angle of the earth, or those which rise through these angles: when Mars regards the Sun in the way we said, the father will die a sudden death, or pestilence will happen in his eyes. And if he regards Saturn, the father's death or fever with tremors will happen, or some pestilence from the part of an incision or burning. And when the configuration of Saturn is bad with that of the Sun, the father's debility will happen through infirmities coming to them by the occasion of bad humors.

**C** Because he said "if they are in the angles," he spoke because of the impulsiveness of Mars toward the significator of the father, which is the Sun and Saturn, and because of the harm of Saturn to the Sun. And what he said about when Mars regards the Sun "in the way we said," he meant when it is elevated over it, or when it wishes to be joined with it, or when it looks at it with another aspect. And what he said regarding the aspect of the configuration of Saturn with that of the Sun being bad, he meant if it were...

**I**kewise, let us deal with the life of the mother: when, therefore, in the <term>figure</term> <note>the birth chart</note> of the Moon or Venus, Jupiter or Venus is again associated with the Moon—whether with her or in a <term>trine</term> or <term>sextile</term> <note>harmonious astrological aspects of 120 and 60 degrees</note> aspect—and both are strong, they will lengthen the life of the mother.

### Third [Book]

He means that the significator of the father by day is the Sun; and his location, the lord of that location, and the place where the lord of his location resides. And the significator of the mother by day is Venus, in the manner we described: and by night, the Moon in the same aforementioned manner. Here lies a question: why is Venus chosen by day rather than the Moon? To which we respond that the Moon has greater power by night than by day, and Venus greater power by day than by night, because she is very close to the <term>complexion</term><note>The specific blend of qualities—hot, cold, moist, dry—that define a planet's nature.</note> of Jupiter.

Also, what we must observe to investigate the remaining particular matters of the parents is this: that we should place the location of the father or mother—whichever was in the position of the <term>ascendant</term><note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note> according to <term>haiz</term><note>original: "haiz"; an Arabic astrological term for a planet in a favorable position relative to its gender and the sun's position.</note>—and observe all their matters just as we do in the birth charts of the parents themselves. We have proven this in the following sections concerning accidental matters and the technical methods found in the general categories.

And what we must seek in the business of the parents regarding particulars not yet mentioned is to place the location of the father and mother at the <term>house</term><note>original: "albayz"; from the Arabic *al-bayt*, meaning house.</note> according to the ascendant. We will then examine all the other houses just as we do in the birth of the parents, as we will demonstrate later through the "accidental opinions" accepted in general practices.

After Ptolemy gave us the methods for the matter of the parents, he said in that place: when we wish to know through the birth of the children the ascendant that would be valid for each parent—as if it were their own birth chart—so that everything general and particular to them might be known through it, we will take the location of its significator through the ascendant. Through it, we will know all twelve houses and create one separate <term>figure</term><note>A complete astrological chart or diagram.</note> to judge every matter according to what he says in his chapter. When we have applied our minds to what we know from the tenth chapter and you wish to create an ascendant for the father or mother, we will look at the location of the significator. We will take its ascension in the <term>direct circle</term><note>Right ascension; the position along the celestial equator.</note> and its ascension in that specific city, and we will find the difference between them. From there, we will take an eighth part and multiply it by the hours of distance of the significator’s location from the <term>angle</term><note>The four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note>. The number resulting from that multiplication we will add to the ascensions of the direct circle (if those ascensions are less than the city's ascensions) or subtract (if they are more). What remains after addition or subtraction will be the ascensions of the significator upon the horizon where it was. Through it, we will know the tenth house with the ascensions of the direct circle. In this same way, we will extract the ascensions of the seventh house from this same place. Similarly, we will know through this the "parts" of these locations, double them, and extract all twelve houses. We will place in each house the planets as they were at the time of birth, and thus we will have a proper figure for the father or mother. We will do the same for the ascendants of brothers and children, as Ptolemy shows us in his writings.

Now, regarding the method of combining various astrological factors, it is appropriate here and everywhere to remember this: when the planets ruling the investigated locations are not of one kind, but of different kinds or operations, we will take the planet whose powers are of greater authority. Thus, the future event comes through him, and the nature of these matters is reached through him. But if their authorities are equal and stars are rising with them, we will easily come to know the result from the mixture of these different natures.

If, however, they are separate, we will attribute the accidents to each of them according to the particular hours. To those that are <term>matutinal</term><note>Morning stars; planets that rise before the sun.</note>, we attribute the first events; to those that are <term>vespertinal</term><note>Evening stars; planets that set after the sun.</note>, the later events. It is necessary, however, that the event matches them from the beginning; for if it does not, it can produce nothing in the future, as they held no fellowship at the start.

<column-break/>

It is appropriate that we recall the methods of combining causes in this place and in all places. If the planets that are lords of the locations we seek are not of one nature but diverse, or operating in such a way that several of them have lordship, we find the one with the most <term>dignities</term><note>The essential strengths a planet gains from its position in certain signs (House, Exaltation, Triplicity, Term, Face).</note>. He has the greatest right in producing what will happen. If the dignities are equal in weight, we look for other planets with them, and we will easily know the matter through the mixture of these diverse natures. If they are separate, we give to each the accidents fitting to them according to particular times. First, we assign those accidents pertaining to the matutinal parts, and afterward those pertaining to the vespertinal. It must always be that they are in agreement from the beginning; for if not, nothing can be operated later since there was no participation with the first principle.

This is the way and general root through which the composition of planetary virtues can be known: what operates first, second, and third, and when each will act. It is clear that this is a general rule covering all necessary things in this art. For example: if the planets ruling a matter are not of one kind but diverse, we must see which has the most dignities according to the five modes: triplicity, house, exaltation, term, and its appearance/aspect to the Sun. We take the meaning from that one. If the dignities are equal, the ruling planets must be of one complexion and nature, and we will easily know what suits them. If they are of separate complexions, we give to each what belongs to it according to the time of that work. It is also proper to prefer the matutinal planet to the vespertinal. In all ways, the work of both must agree with the "signification of the root" <note>The primary meaning established at the start of the inquiry or birth.</note>. For example: if the ascendant signifies the master's death quickly, and another planet signifies marriage or having a son in a longer time, that [second] meaning will be destroyed if there was a conflict with the first. You must study this section many times until you understand the words of Ptolemy and ours.

The "first disposition" <note>The initial state of the heavens at birth.</note> is not the cause of the timing of the future; rather, it is the quality of the star which, in respect to the Sun and the angles of the world, was the mistress of the disposition at the time of birth.

Nevertheless, whenever an accident occurs, it does not come through the first disposition alone, but in comparison to the Sun and the angles of the world.

He means that we will know the time of a future event not only from the significator itself, but also from its relationship to the Sun and the angles of the world. From this, we will know when the future event will happen. I have already demonstrated this in the gloss of the preceding chapter, and from there you can understand it well.

And he shows us that when we wish to judge how many siblings there are from one mother, we should judge by the sign of the Midheaven and by the location which is the "ascendant of the mother": and similarly when we judge the siblings who will be from one father, we should judge them by the sign of the Midheaven and by that which will be the "ascendant of the father." And where he said "naturally": he means that what we have said in this place accords with the science of natures: because the sign of the Midheaven holds a "participation" with the ascendant just as a sibling does with their own siblings. And the locations of the parents hold a participation with the ascendant of their children. **And because** this sign and the sign that ascends to it are the location of the mother: these are the things by which the matters of her children are grasped: since it is necessary for this to be the location of the siblings.

**And since** this sign and the sign that is elevated to its location are both the "location of the mother": through which a person can know the business of her children: it follows that this is the location of the siblings.

**That which** he said of "this sign": he means the sign of the Midheaven: and what he said of the "sign that is elevated to the location": he means the <term>zodiacal signs</term><note>original: ".z. signoꝝ"</note>: because one of these signs has a participation with the other through a better virtue, and other virtues have participation with others. And that which he said: "the location of the mother through which a person can know the business of her children": he means that the two signs which are the tenth and eleventh houses are the locations through which a person can know the business of children who are from one mother only: because they are not locations belonging to the mother herself: rather they are those which Ptolemy said: by day the location of Venus and by night the location of the Moon: and according to this we can understand from his words that the 4th sign and the 5th sign are the locations through which we can know the business of children who are from one father: and this is according to what we believe. 

And it can be understood through his words that when we join the tenth and eleventh with the location of the mothers—which is Venus by day and the Moon by night—we will be able to know the business of the siblings of the same mother: and when we join the 4th and 5th with the location of the fathers—which is the Sun by day and Saturn by night: we will be able to know the business of siblings who are from the same father. And when he says "it follows that this is the location of the siblings": he means that the tenth house and that which is before it, which is the 11th: and Venus by day and the Moon by night: are three locations. We will also consider if they are in signs of a "single image" or of "two bodies."

**We will be able** to know the number of siblings by the number of fortunate planets. For if they are in a sign of one figure: their power will not be doubled: because for each it grants one sibling: and if they are in signs of two bodies<note>Bicorporeal or dual signs, like Gemini, Sagittarius, or Pisces, which often signify "doubling."</note>: because their power is doubled: they will give two siblings. **But if** the planets of <term>infortune</term><note>Saturn and Mars, considered the "Malefics."</note> are elevated over this place: or when they look upon it from an opposition: they will indicate a small number of siblings: and especially if the Sun is present with them.

**And if** over that place the planets of infortune are elevated: or if they are in its opposition across the diameter: they will signify a lack of siblings: especially if the Sun has entered with them.

**The location which** he mentioned is generally of the nine aforementioned locations: and if an unfortunate planet has participation with any of them: it signifies no siblings: and it follows that you should apply your mind to how Ptolemy demonstrated this so wonderfully to us: because he always demonstrates each of these at its start: so that we may extract from there those that are average through those general rules which he gave us: because he first told us about the fortunate planets: how they signify siblings: and the infortunate ones a lack of siblings: so that if we find a fortune and an infortune having participation with these locations: we will look at which of them has greater strength: and we will judge according to this: and we will say that the other contrary planet will add or diminish.

**If however** they are in the <term>angles</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, where planets have the most power.</note> and specifically in the ascendant: and if the planet in any of these locations is Saturn: it will signify this in the case of signs and older siblings. But if it is Mars: it will shorten the number of other siblings through death.

**And if** it is in the angles in the ascendant: and the planet which is in one of these locations is Saturn: the indication will be regarding older siblings. And if it is Mars, it will diminish the number of other siblings through death.

**He means to say** that the planets of infortune, which are Saturn and Mars, and similarly Mercury if he is of the nature of these two: and the Sun also: if any of them damns the location of the siblings while being in any of the angles, its harm will be stronger: because it remains in a place having greater power: similarly when it looks from the 4th or the opposing 10th house. And if Saturn is in any of the angles, he will harm the older siblings: and if Mars, the younger ones. And it follows that he adds to this place the rule he spoke of before, namely that <term>matutinal</term><note>Rising before the Sun in the morning.</note> planets signify older siblings: <term>vespertinal</term><note>Setting after the Sun in the evening.</note> ones younger: you will place Mercury similarly if he has a mixture with the fortunes or infortunes. You will say similarly of the fortunes if they are in the angles that the good will have greater power: and Jupiter signifies older siblings: Venus and the Moon signify younger ones.

**The quality indeed** of the planets who are the "givers of siblings," if it is favorable in their position: we ought to consider the siblings powerful and exalted. If however it is to the contrary, they will be weak and powerless.

# Third Book

¶ Nevertheless, regarding the planets giving siblings, we judge by their status in their position in the world: if their status is good, we understand that the siblings will be noble and of great praise; if it is contrary, they will be base and of little value.

¶ The planets that give siblings are the <term>benefics</term><note>original: "fortune"; planets traditionally considered "lucky" or positive, such as Jupiter and Venus.</note>: and a good status in their position at the time of birth is for them to be located in the <term>angles</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart.</note> or in the <term>succedent</term><note>The houses following the angles (2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th).</note> houses; all of this was already recounted in the third chapter. Here he wished to show us that the nobility and value of siblings will be according to the status of the planet giving siblings in its position at the birth.

¶ But if the <term>malefic</term><note>original: "infortune"; planets considered difficult or unlucky, like Saturn and Mars.</note> planets are elevated above the "givers," or if they follow them: the siblings will again be short-lived.

¶ And if the malefic planets are the givers of siblings and are elevated, or if they follow them, the siblings will have a short life.

¶ You have already learned that the planets which "elevate" are those that travel by the movement of the firmament toward the location of another. It can also be understood that planets which "elevate" are those that overcome others through their strength. You also learned that planets which "follow" others are those that travel to join themselves with others. It is clear that whether they are benefics or malefics, when they have participation with the locations of the siblings, if the malefics are elevated over the others, the siblings will have a short life; for they will not live except according to the strength of the benefics.

¶ The givers of males are planets that are masculine in their qualities in the world: the givers of females are feminine in their qualities in the world.

¶ And the planets granting males are masculine in their position in the world: and those giving females are feminine in their position in the world.

¶ He means to say that masculine planets—namely those that become masculine by their position in the world—grant brothers. Similarly, feminine planets and those that become feminine by their position in the world grant sisters: and you can understand this whole saying through the first part: and if any planet is masculine in itself but becomes feminine according to its position in the world, you shall judge according to the power of whichever has the greater influence and more <term>dignities</term><note>The essential and accidental strengths a planet possesses based on its zodiacal position.</note>.

¶ Likewise, <term>oriental</term><note>Planets that rise before the Sun.</note> planets grant the first siblings; <term>occidental</term><note>Planets that set after the Sun.</note> planets grant the last. Again, when the givers are associated in the figure with the sign representing their fellowship, they will signify the concord of the resulting siblings: if these again come with the <term>Part of Fortune</term><note>An Arabic Part or calculated point in the chart representing prosperity and well-being.</note>, they will judge the fellowship of the siblings in their affairs: but if they are in signs having no fellowship with each other, or if they have a quality contrary to the predicted quality: they will signify a will toward discord and envy among the siblings, and demonstrate that they are deceivers.

¶ Similarly, oriental planets give the first siblings, and occidental the last. Likewise, if the planets giving siblings have a suitable participation with the sign governing the status of the siblings: it signifies that the siblings will love each other: and if they are in a sign from which there are no <term>aspects</term><note>Specific geometric angles between planets that determine how they interact.</note> between them, or one that is contrary to what we said, it signifies enmity and envy, as well as the deception which they will have—namely, one with another.

¶ In this saying, he demonstrates for us how we shall know what kind of love there will be, or how the love of the siblings will be, namely one with another: and he says that the benefic planets which give siblings, if they have a participation of concord with the tenth house or with the location of the mother, will signify love and friendship. Similarly, if they have concord with the Part of Fortune, they will signify friendship and participation in wealth and life and such things: and those which do not have participation with those locations will signify enmity, ill-will, and deception among the siblings.

¶ But if anyone wishes to investigate and scrutinize each matter further than what is said above, he can do so quite well: if he establishes the "givers" as the location of the <term>Ascendant</term><note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note>: and then observes all their affairs just as we do in nativities (birth charts).

¶ And if anyone wishes to go further regarding the business of siblings beyond this: he can imagine it according to this, by setting the planet giving siblings as the Ascendant and looking into all other matters just as is done in a birth chart.

And when he knows this, he will judge all the statuses of the siblings which that planet gave to him: and predict future things for them, both particular and general.

### On Males and Females. Chapter 6.

->Haly said:<-

In the treatise of the commentary that precedes this, we taught as much as is suitable to know concerning the statuses that can exist before the birth: now, however, we wish to show in this treatise all the statuses we wish to know that happen at the hour of birth concerning things happening to the newborn in himself: and with this we will set down the judgment of the length of life: and we will always place the words of Ptolemy first and comment on them as we have done until now.

¶ After we explained by a natural path the narration of siblings, we shall subjoin the work that follows regarding what will happen in the newborn himself: and let us first indicate the consideration of males and females.

¶ And after we demonstrated the reasoning of siblings according to a natural and agreed-upon opinion: it is suitable for us afterward to speak of this in the reasoning of things happening to the newborn himself: and first let us speak of males and females.

<margin>Ptolemy in this chapter of the 3rd part showed that the reasoning of siblings follows the reasoning of parents: and that the reasoning pertaining to the born siblings follows that reasoning: and therefore we have ordered the chapters of this 3rd part just as he spoke before in the first chapter of this same part: and first he begins with things pertaining to the birth in males and females.</margin>

¶ The observation of this is not of one single mode, nor is it taken from one thing alone, but from both luminaries and from the Ascendant, as well as from the planets having authority in this matter.

¶ Looking into this reasoning is not of one single manner, nor can it be taken from one thing alone, but rather from both <term>luminaries</term><note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> and the Ascendant, and from the planets having dignity in these locations.

¶ He means to say that whether the newborn will be male or female, we ought to take it from the two luminaries according to their status in the world: and according to the birth, and from the Ascendant, and from the planets having dignities in the locations of the luminaries and in the Ascendant.

¶ However, we shall specifically grasp this from the quality which was present at the hour of the <term>descent of the seed</term><note>original: "casui spermatis"; the moment of conception.</note>. In a general way, however, the qualities appearing at the hour of birth will indicate this.

¶ Since male and female are generated in the womb, it is suitable that the judgment of this matter be properly from the beginning: which is the hour of the descent of the seed: and that which we can know of this through the "beginning" which is the exit of the creature is general, because of the participation which this beginning has with the former.

**Treatise**

**I**t also generally happens for us to observe: if these three aforementioned locations and the planets ruling all or most of them are masculine, the newborn will be a male; and if they are feminine, it will be a female; and according to this, we shall judge the nature of the birth.

¶ And it happens for us to look if the three predicted locations and the planets disposing them are all masculine or feminine, or the greater part of them: and according to this will be the judgment.

We will do similarly if we find them feminine or the greater part of them, or those who have the greatest power: we will judge that the newborn will be female. And you already know that the <term>dispositors</term><note>original: "dispositores"; the planets that rule the specific signs where the Sun, Moon, or Ascendant are located.</note> are those who have more <term>dignities</term><note>Essential power or "rights" a planet has over a specific degree of the zodiac.</note> in these three locations according to those five modes which we described in the <term>Animodar</term><note>original: "Animodar"; a specific method used to rectify or find the exact moment of birth.</note>.

¶ It is also necessary that we consider masculine and feminine locations and planets, just as we showed at the beginning of this book; we demonstrated it from the natures of the signs in which they were, and from the natures of the planets themselves, as well as from their qualities with respect to the world: for when they are <term>oriental</term><note>original: "orientales"; rising in the east before the Sun.</note> they become masculine; however, they become feminine when they are <term>occidental</term><note>original: "occidentales"; setting in the west after the Sun.</note>. Likewise, from their qualities with respect to the Sun: they become masculine when they are <term>matutinal</term><note>Rising in the morning before the Sun.</note>, and those being <term>vespertine</term><note>Setting in the evening after the Sun.</note> become feminine. Therefore, from all these things, whichever gender occurs in the constitution of the birth according to the greater part, we make our conjecture of the work.

¶ And it is fitting for us to divide or distinguish between males and females from the locations and from the planets in the way we said recently at the beginning of this book: and this is from the nature of the signs in which they are, and from the nature of the planets themselves, and from their state in comparison to the world: since when they are oriental they are masculine, and when occidental they are feminine. Similarly from their state in comparison to the Sun: because they are masculine when they are matutinal, and feminine when vespertine. And it is fitting that we estimate this as a whole, and know which nature will win in the birth in the greater part.

¶ If you have understood from the beginning of this book up to this place, you should well understand all these words; nevertheless, if you have not understood, you need a <gloss>gloss</gloss>: nor do I know any intellect so <note>original: "grossum"; meaning thick, dull, or unrefined.</note> dense that it would be necessary to repeat these words many times; nonetheless, I wish to explain them to you one time. I say that **Ptolemy** said we should distinguish and know if the three locations which we named in this chapter and their dispositors are masculine or feminine through that which we said in the first part, in which we taught which signs are masculine and which feminine: we also taught how each of the planets is masculine and also each of the signs in comparison to the world: and we said that they are masculine when they are in masculine locations, and feminine when they are in feminine locations. Similarly, they become masculine when they are oriental, and feminine when occidental: they also become masculine when they are matutinal, and feminine when vespertine. And after we have demonstrated all of this to you, you can well meditate on which of these natures wins: and according to that you shall judge. And if both natures are equal, you shall judge that the one born will be of two mixed natures.

### Chapter 8: On Monstrous Signs

<margin>Haly said:</margin>
**The utility** we have from this chapter is in knowing if the one born is a human or not, and if human: whether they are of an imperfect form or not.

That which indeed does not depart at all from reason is the explanation of monstrous figures.

And it is not outside of reason to speak of those who have a changed form <note>original: "permutatam facturam"; this refers to physical deformities or significant deviations from the expected human shape</note>.

<margin>He means to say that speaking of those who have a changed nature follows the reasoning of those who are born three or four at a time, for many of these are born with a changed form.</margin>
We say, therefore, first that in these cases the <term>luminaries</term><note>The Sun and the Moon</note> are frequently found remote or disconnected from the <term>Ascendant</term>, and they are contained in an <term>angle</term><note>The four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note> by the <term>malefics</term><note>original: "infortunijs"; the "unfortunate" or harmful planets, typically Saturn and Mars</note>.

How do we know this first? Because the two luminaries are found for the most part in such a birth falling away from the angles or having no agreement with the Ascendant, while the unfortunate planets are powerful in the angles.

Observe what we said before: that the births of humans are in harmony with the two luminaries. ### Third [Book]

If one of the **malefics** <note>original: "infortunae"; refers to the planets Mars or Saturn</note> afflicts one of the **luminaries** <term>Luminaries: The Sun and the Moon, considered the primary sources of life in astrology.</term> while the other malefic afflicts the other luminary—specifically when one is in opposition and the other has ascended to the position of a luminary—it is not at all doubted that the newborn will not have life.

And even if the configuration is not a perfect square <note>original: "figura duorum laterum equalium"; literally "a figure of two equal sides," referring to a quartile or square aspect of 90 degrees</note>, yet if in the projection of their rays the malefics hold authority over the places of the two luminaries, or if a malefic ascends toward them; or if there are two malefics impeding one luminary or even both; or if a malefic moves toward the positions of both or the position of either one; or if they are in opposition to either or both across the diameter; or if one of the malefics impeding either of the two luminaries is also in opposition across the diameter while the other is ascending toward the location of the luminary: that child will not have life.

The whole point lies in this one thing: that there are three factors—the luminary, the malefic, and the ascendant—as he described. However, the distinction between the first point and the second is that the luminary is not joined to the malefic degree-by-degree, but there are a few degrees between them, whether in longitude or latitude or both, and the malefic "ascends" toward the luminary. He means to say that the malefic moves and places itself in the **angle** <note>Angles: The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a birth chart, where planetary influence is strongest.</note> where the luminary was; and this manner is not a conjunction in a square aspect, but an application through the "projection of rays."

Because the greatest harm in this condition is that the separation from life is achieved through the distance from the place [of the malefic] to the place of the luminaries; this [influence] destroys and hides the life.

And this is because of the great harm found here: it condemns and destroys any usefulness; even the good that might come from the distance of the ascending point to the places of the two luminaries regarding the durability of life is lost.

He means to say that when a malefic condemns a luminary located in the angles, and no **benefic** <note>original: "fortuna"; refers to the planets Jupiter or Venus</note> applies to that luminary; and similarly, the malefic does not apply by longitude or latitude but by rays, or it ascends to its place—this is the greatest harm in a dangerous state. It destroys the benefit and the good that comes from the distance between the malefic and the luminary. And **Ptolemy** <note>original: "Ptol."; referring to Claudius Ptolemy, author of the Quadripartitum</note> wishes to show us through this the reason why this state exists. Similarly, the reason he narrated is now shown to us: that the judgment of those who "do not receive food" <note>This phrase refers to infants who die before they can even be fed for the first time.</note> is through one simple thing. This is that either one or both luminaries are in the exact degree of the angles, while they are condemned by malefics, and the lord of that place is in the dignity of the malefics with no benefic planet looking upon it. And if both luminaries are this way, the effect is stronger; but if one is this way and the other is different, it requires another interpretation. Ptolemy teaches us this rule which he established for those not receiving food through other things he now wishes to say.

However, that which specifically impedes the **Sun** among those things in its place which ascend toward its position is said to be **Mars**; but for the **Moon**, it is **Saturn**. Yet in opposition, or when it ascends toward it, the contrary happens: for Saturn impedes the Sun, while Mars impedes the Moon; especially when they dominate as the rulers of the places of the luminaries and the ascendant.

And if the one condemning the Sun specifically is Mars when it ascends to the place where the Sun is, or Saturn itself which condemns the Moon by opposition or by ascending to its place: this will be the reverse, for the one who condemns the Sun is Saturn and the Moon is Mars; and specifically if they rule in the place of the luminaries and in the ascendant by having their "disposition" <note>The planet that rules the zodiac sign another planet is currently occupying.</note>.

He means to say that the greatest strength of harm and evil is if the malefics are the "dispositors" of the luminaries and the ascendant while also being harmful to the luminaries. And it is manifest that when a malefic

<column-break/>

is in any angle, it offends all four [angles].

And if it has two oppositions, and the luminaries and malefics are in the angles or in an "isosceles" figure <note>original: "equicruria figura"; likely referring to an aspect with equal "legs" or degrees of distance</note>, infants are born dead or half-dead.

And if it has an opposition with them across the diameter, and the two luminaries and the malefics are in the angles and in a figure of two equal sides, then the creatures are born either dead or half-alive.

He says this completes the rule of those who do not receive life and die in the hour they are born. This occurs when both are in malefic influence and in the opposition of both luminaries by longitude and latitude, with both of them in some of the angles. And whenever it is so, it happens that they are born dead or nearly so.

But if it so happens that the luminaries are separated from one of the benefics, or are associated with it in a figure, and the rays reach the preceding parts: the newborn will live according to the marking of the number of degrees that exist between the **Hyleg** <note>original: "albileg" or "hyleg"; the planetary point or planet responsible for giving life to the newborn</note> and the projection of the malefic's rays, counted in months, days, or hours according to the quantity of the maleficence which is the occasion for this.

For if it is not so, and both luminaries share in some authority of the benefics, or have participation with them in a figure, and the ray applies to the first divisions: the child will live only as long as the degrees that are between the Hyleg and the ray of the nearest malefic—so many months, days, and hours—according to the state of the quantity of that malice and the strength of the things causing this.

He means to say that when the malefics and luminaries are in the angles, and it happens that the luminaries are separated from a conjunction with the benefics by only a few degrees, or are separated from the aspect of the benefics: then the benefics will give the strength by which the child lives according to the quantity of degrees between the luminary and the malefic. And if the harm of the malefic is very strong, the units will be hours; if moderate, they will be days; and if weaker, they will be months. And now Ptolemy has proven to us that the luminary one must look at in these matters is the one that is the Hyleg. And similarly, he made it clear by what he said regarding the number of degrees between the Hyleg and the ray of the malefic: because in this state, the malefic is not with the luminary in a figure of two equal sides.

But if the ray of the malefics reaches the preceding parts of the luminaries, while the ray of the benefics reaches the following parts: the child will grow and live.

And if the ray of the malefics is what applies to the first divisions of the luminaries, and the ray of the benefics applies to the following divisions: the child will receive food and live.

Ptolemy means to say that in any place, those "first divisions" are those which ascend before—just as **Pisces** ascends before **Aries**, and the first degrees of Aries before the last degrees of Aries; and thus the 9th house before the 10th; and such things and parts that follow. He means those that come after—just as Aries follows Pisces, and the second degree of Aries follows the first, and the 10th house follows the 9th. And since it is so, he well demonstrates this saying of his: that the luminaries will be separated from the malefics and move toward the benefics. And when they are in this way, the newborn will receive food and live, whether the luminaries and malefics are in the angles or in other places.

Likewise, when the malefics are elevated above the benefics that are associated in a figure: the child will be of a miserable quality and weak.

Similarly, if the malefic planets are elevated above the benefics that are in agreement in a figure, the child will be unlucky and held in low esteem.

### Chapter 10. On the Span of Life.

->Haly said:<-

This **chapter** is separate from the preceding chapters; for those do not go beyond the hour of birth; however, the narration of this chapter and the others that follow do go beyond the hour of birth.

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'E' featuring stylized floral and foliate motifs inside a square border with a hatched background.</image-desc>

**T**he explanation of those things which happen after birth. First is the discourse on life: because regarding those things which were first arranged out of all those things which rarely happen—to treat someone who might not reach the years of life in which those things could be fulfilled—it is fitting for us to have a laugh.

¶ It is fitting to speak first about life when speaking of the accidents that happen after birth; for it is fitting that a laugh be made at the expense of one who first arranges a judgment of every single thing happening to a newborn without having the years of life in which those very things can be observed.

### The accidents that happen to the newborn after birth are those which happen in their body and their spirit:

¶ that which happens regarding honor and mastery, regarding sons and daughters; and if you apply your mind to the words of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text of Western astrology.</note>, you will not need a **gloss** <term>Gloss: An explanatory note or commentary added to a text to clarify difficult passages.</term>.
¶ However, this observation is neither easy nor simple; nonetheless, it is taken and understood from the powers of the dominating places. This is observed in many ways.
¶ The understanding of this matter is a hidden thing; yet it can be known from the lordship of the principal places and their strength, because this is the matter to which we must look through many parts.
¶ The ancient sages of this art have agreed that the **signification of life** <note>original: "signatio vite"</note> must be taken from one principal place and their strength in the birth. However, there are diverse opinions on the ways in which the quantity of life can be known; for there are those who consider that whichever of the luminaries, when it is in any of the angles, is fit in whichever way to be the **hyleg** <term>Hyleg: The "Giver of Life," a specific point in a birth chart used to determine the life span.</term>. And generally, when many dignities are joined to any luminary, they prefer it and take from it the signification of the quantity of life. And there are others who consider that when the hyleg is not observed, it belongs to the other dispositors of the place: then it is that which is called the **alcocoden** <term>Alcocoden: The "Giver of Years," a planet that determines the specific length of life based on its position and relationship to the hyleg.</term> when it is fit to be the hyleg according to their opinion and many other things written in their books. And there are others of them who consider that every **direction** <note>original: "directio"</note> of the hyleg must be made, and where the **atacyr** <term>Atacyr: A method of "directing" or moving a planet forward in time to predict future events.</term> is known through the **ascensions** <note>original: "ascensiones"; the time it takes for a zodiacal sign to rise above the horizon</note> of the city. And there are others who say that this *atacyr* must be made by the ascensions of the direct circle always; and there are others who say it must be made by equal degrees; and others who say that the gift of the Sun must agree with the alcocoden; and if it disagrees, one should look in the **annual revolution** <term>Revolution: A "solar return" chart, cast for the moment the Sun returns to its birth position each year.</term>; and whichever of them agrees with the harm of that year, they will place as the **cutter of life** <note>original: "abscisore vite"; the planet or point that marks the end of the lifespan</note>. And all these ways are of many senses and many entanglements. And Ptolemy casts all these aside and takes one way which follows a natural rule and takes for the hyleg the stronger and nobler of the principal places in the birth: and he makes the direction of that hyleg through mixed ascensions of the city and the direct circle: because he makes the *atacyr* through the ascensions of the circle in which the hyleg is. Nevertheless, since many of those who are noted and authenticated in this art work through the hyleg and alcocoden, it will be good that in this space we have something to reveal to you of their sayings in this place. I say that first they look to the luminary [and its] ways (that is, its path); and if more **dignities** <term>Dignities: The various ways a planet gains strength based on its position in the zodiac (e.g., being in its own sign or exaltation).</term> are joined in it than are joined in another of the principal places, and it happens with this that it looks to one of its **dispositors** <note>A planet that "rules" the sign where another planet is located.</note>, they take that for the hyleg, and that dispositor for the alcocoden. And if this does not happen, they will look to the other luminary in this same manner; and thus they will go searching until they find one that looks to any of its dispositors: and they say that life will be according to the number of revolutions of the dispositor itself looking at it. And if that same alcocoden is strong, it will be according to its **greater number**. And if it is middling, it will be according to its **middling number**. And if it is weak, it will be according to its **lesser number**. And to these numbers they add and subtract according to the benefics and malefics looking at the hyleg and alcocoden: and this is the summary of their opinion: and thus you will find it demonstrated in their books. And after Ptolemy mentioned many things in this book of his concerning the revolutions of the planets, it will be good that we now reveal his saying. I say that the **greater number** of each of the planets is as many as there are degrees of their **terms** <term>Terms: A division of each zodiac sign into five unequal parts, each ruled by one of the five non-luminary planets.</term> through all the signs. **Saturn**: 57. **Jupiter**: 79. **Mars**: 66. **Venus**: 82. **Mercury**: 76. The **lesser number** of each planet is the four degrees <note>likely "years" intended here</note> in which they go to complete equal revolutions. **Saturn**: 30, because in 30 years it completes one revolution. **Jupiter**: 12 years because in...

Afterward, they took half of the major years of the Moon, which is 54, and added to them the size of the Moon's body, which is 12 degrees, making 66 in all; they established these as the average years of the Moon. 

Later, they tested this many times without number, and found that it responded well through experience. They assigned these as years when a planet was powerful, as months when they found it weak, as days when it was very weak, and as hours when it was in extreme debility. They added and subtracted in each case according to the state in which they found each planet. For example, when a planet would give its major years, and they subtracted from its virtue by a quarter, they would subtract a fourth part of its years. **Ptolemy**, however, rejects and avoids this way because of the great complexity that is in it, and he takes one way that follows a natural rule; for that reason, he concludes that this is the only certain and truthful way.

¶ The method, as it results from our estimation and because it imitates the natural path, is as we shall describe. This observation is considered from the location of the **Hyleg** <note>original: "albhileg"; the planet or point in a birth chart that acts as the "giver of life."</note> and those points which have power over the **Hyleg**, as well as the locations of the "killing" stars.

¶ The manner which follows the natural path is that through which we can know the quantity of life, and through it, we can know that which accords with the art of nature. For **Aristotle** proved in his book *On Generation and Corruption* that the equatorial line is what causes all generation to continue and endure, and the line of the zodiac causes generation and corruption. And since Ptolemy knew that his predecessors had shown this matter by right demonstration in their books, he sought a way that would accord with them in this art; when he found it, he placed it in the third chapter for anyone wishing to know. And the first thing he related concerning it is that the general rule in this matter is that life continues and endures through the locations of the **Hylegs** <note>original: "bylegioocum"</note> and the planets disposing them. The things that cause life to be cut off are the locations of the planets and the locations of the **Hylegs**; and then it follows that the quantity of life is as much as the number of degrees of the equator between these two points. He spoke of many "cutting" locations as "killers" because they give death. That which brings death is a "killer," whether from

¶ The knowledge of each of these things is as follows. Then those in **square** <note>original: "tetragono"; a 90-degree aspect.</note> aspect to them, which is the Midheaven above the earth. Also, the degrees that are in **trine** aspect to them, which is the place called *Theos* <note>Greek for "God"; referring to the 9th house.</note>. And finally, the degrees which are in **opposition**, which is the West <note>The Descendant.</note>. Among those that must now be proposed because they possess the strongest authority (that is, in their disposition and lordship), the first is the **Midheaven** above the earth; after that, the **Ascendant**; then that which ascends toward the Midheaven <note>The 11th house</note>; after that, the **West**; and finally, that place toward which the Midheaven proceeds <note>The 9th house</note>.

¶ The distinction of each of these things is according to what I wish to say. Now the first thing we must know is that the locations of the **Hylegs** <note>original: "hylegioocum"</note> are those in which the planet disposing the **Hyleg** happens to be. This is the sign of the **Ascendant**, from five degrees that ascended before the horizon to twenty-five degrees that remain to ascend afterward. Following that, the degrees which are to the right of these thirty degrees in their **sextile**, and these are the **eleventh house of fortune**. Then others which are in the quarter above the earth, and these are the **Midheaven**. Then those that are in their **trine**, which is the place called *Theos* <note>The 9th house</note>. And those which are in their opposite, and these are in the **West**. Those of these points which must now be proposed because of the great power they have in disposition and lordship are those of the **Midheaven** above the earth. Subsequently, those in the **Ascendant**. Afterward, those that ascend toward the Midheaven. Afterward, those in the **West**. And finally, those which are before the Midheaven.

¶ There are two things which we must demonstrate regarding these places: one is the division of the 12 houses, and the other is the ordering of their virtues one to another. The division of the 12 houses is such that each consists of 30 degrees—namely, the 5 degrees preceding the cusp of the house and the 25 that follow. In these 5 preceding degrees is the strength of the house division, because they are near the cusp. With this, the strength of the house division will exist throughout all 30 degrees that make up the house. However, the ordering of the 12 houses one after another is in this manner: first is that which is in the **Midheaven**.
