Because of this, it happens that this house is of the greatest power and lordship. The strength of the **Ascendant**, however, is in that same horizon; it travels over its entire surface and always increases by ascending. Similarly, the strength of the **11th house** is visible and increasing, and it travels toward the 10th by ascending; therefore, it follows the Ascendant in lordship. # Treatise

...the virtues of the other houses: and we shall say that the 4th house is in direct opposition to the 10th; however, its virtue is changed because it is under the earth: it follows that it is in the 6th rank of all. And the 5th is opposite the 11th; thus it follows that it is in the 7th rank of all. And as the 2nd is in comparison to the Ascendant, so is the 11th in comparison to the 10th; it follows therefore that it is in the 8th rank of all. And the 8th is in comparison to the descendant <note>original: "occidentis"; the West or 7th house</note> as the 2nd is in comparison to the ascendant: by which it follows that it is in the 9th rank of all. And the 7th is opposite the 9th: and therefore it follows that it is in the 10th rank of all: and the weakest houses are the 6th and the 12th. And the 6th is weaker than the 12th because it is under the earth: and this is the order of the 12 houses according to the rule of **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century mathematician whose "Tetrabiblos" formed the foundation of Western astrology.</note>.

Regarding that which remains under the earth in a matter so clear and so excellent: we have decided it should be omitted: because the Ascendant appeared above the earth. Those signs which are above the earth but do not connect with the Ascendant are not to be observed: nor even the sign ascending before the Ascendant, which is called the <term>House of Labor</term> <note>The 12th house, traditionally associated with hidden enemies and self-undoing.</note> because of this, that even though it moves away from the <term>angle</term> <note>The four "angles" (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses) are the strongest points in a chart.</note>, the thick and dark vapor which ascends toward it from the humidity of the earth disturbs and destroys its strength as it reaches the earth. And therefore, that which appears from the colors and qualities of the stars existing in this house is doubted for the same reason.

And it follows that we do not work in a noble or direct way through everything that is under the earth, but always through that which ascends and appears above the earth. And it does not follow for us to work through that which is above the earth by a sign which the Ascendant does not <term>aspect</term> <note>An "aspect" is a geometric relationship between signs; if signs cannot "see" each other, their influence is weakened.</note>: nor through the sign that ascends before the Ascendant which is called the House of Labor: since it is cadent from the angle: and furthermore, because the smokiness that rises from the humors of the earth disturbs its virtue as it comes from it to the earth with its thickness and slipperiness and damns it: on account of which the colors and magnitudes of the stars existing in this house appear to be of a different manner than they are by their nature.

We have already demonstrated in the gloss previously that the virtues of celestial things come to us through straight lines: and it is manifest that all natural virtues are changed according to the length through which they come to us: and the greater that length shall be, the more they are weakened and changed by other matters that are mixed with them in that length. And it is also manifest that light virtues pass more easily through subtle and light bodies than thick ones. And since it is so, it follows in every way that the virtues reaching us from heaven from the lower part are much changed and weakened: since the distance is greater by as much as the diameter of the earth: and the earth in itself is gross, thick, and hard throughout. And since the virtues coming from the 12th house are changed and damned by the slippery and thick smokiness that ascends from the humors of the earth—which are significantly more subtle than the earth—it is clearly evident by how much more the virtues existing under the earth ought to be changed and damned on account of its thickness. And **Ptolemy** also shows that this is a thing visibly apparent in what he said: that the virtue passing from the 12th house is changed by these smokinesses: so that the colors and magnitudes of the stars existing in this house cannot be seen as they truly occur: and this is what is shown by these words concerning the weakness of celestial virtues coming from under the earth: it does not follow to work in such a matter as this from the 12th house: because he said that its virtues are changed and damned by what he said: and because it is cadent from the Ascendant: likewise in this matter it does not follow to work from the 8th house: because it has no aspect with the Ascendant: and the virtues that are in it go on diminishing and weakening. And the houses that work in this matter are 5 and no more out of all 12 houses: first and foremost the Ascendant; the 3rd is the 11th; the 4th is the 7th; the 5th is the 9th. And it is manifest that the work is done through these houses: since they have an aspect with the Ascendant.

Afterward, it is agreed that we should establish the four dominant factors—which are the Sun, Moon, Ascendant, and Part of Fortune—and the <term>dispositors</term> <note>A planet that "rules" the sign where another planet is located.</note> of their places as the <term>Alhileg</term> <note>Also known as the Hyleg, the primary planet used to determine the lifespan.</note>.

<column-break/>

**A**nd it follows that we set as the Hyleg four principal things, which are: the Sun, the Moon, the Ascendant, and the Part of Fortune: and the dispositors of the places of these things.

**I**n the preceding words, we said according to **Ptolemy** that the places of the Hylegs are five only: and they are the 10th house, the Ascendant, the 11th, the 7th, and the 9th: now, however, he shows us in these words how many things there are: and he orders them one after another: and he says there are four. The 1st is the Sun. The 2nd is the Moon. The 3rd is the Ascendant. The 4th is the Part of Fortune: and he himself has already shown us in the preceding chapters: that the dispositor of any of them shall be in its place: since the principal will not be suitable for disposing. For example: let there be a significance of the Sun existing in the house of Saturn and in its triplicity: and in a place suitable to be Hyleg. And Saturn, which is the dispositor of the Sun in this state, shall be in the 10th house or in another of the places suitable for the Hyleg: because when we have found it so, it follows that we take Saturn for the Hyleg in place of the Sun: since it has dominion over the Sun: and with this dominion it has the greatest kingdom, equal to the kingdom of the Sun: and since it is so, the principal things are four only: since their dispositors take their place when they are not suitable for the Hyleg. In such a place as this, one doubt arises. For a man might first say that when **Ptolemy** recounted the principal things in the preceding chapters, he said that the things themselves were three: Sun, Moon, and Ascendant: and now, in a place as noble as this, he has placed the Part of Fortune. And since the Part of Fortune has such great significance in the quantity of life, it is quite clear how much more significance it ought to give in those matters which are changed by nature: which do not receive enough nourishment. And I respond to this, saying that the virtue of the Part of Fortune is less than the virtue of the Ascendant: and the virtue of the Ascendant is less than the strength of the Moon: and the virtue of the Moon is less than the virtue of the Sun. And if it should happen in the preceding chapters that the virtues of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant are all corrupted, how can the Part of Fortune escape if both luminaries and the Ascendant were damned? And for as much as this is, **Ptolemy** placed the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant in the past chapters and left out the Part of Fortune. We shall take here, however, from the place of the Part of Fortune the limit of the quantity of life: and we shall not take from it the significance of life itself. And this is well demonstrated to him who has applied his mind to his words: for you will find that **Ptolemy** did not place the virtue of the Ascendant in the preceding chapters when it happened that the virtue of the Sun and Moon were damned: because he knew that when these were damned, the virtue of the Ascendant would not have the power to remove that damnation: and it follows that you should understand his opinion in this way.

**W**e shall know the Part of Fortune, therefore, if we take the number that we find from the place of the Sun to the place of the Moon by day and by night: and starting from the Ascendant, we compute the quantity of that number according to the succession of the signs. In this way, therefore, we shall learn the place of the Part. Which we do for this reason: so that the quality of the Sun in respect to the Ascendant may be as the quality of the Moon in respect to the Part of Fortune. For the Part of Fortune will be, as it were, the "Ascendant of the Moon." Those who say that in nocturnal births we must count from the Moon to the Sun seem to imitate this same reasoning. Then, starting from the Ascendant, let us compute the quantity of that same number in the part of it which we said before—but following the order of the preceding signs. When we have done this, the same place of the Part of Fortune which had come out for us will appear according to this method: and the quality of the company of the figure <note>The "figure" refers to the astrological chart as a whole.</note> will be the same.

**A**nd the Part of Fortune can be known by always taking the number that is from the place of the Sun to the place of the Moon by day and by night: and we shall begin from the Ascendant: and from it we shall number such a count: and by the way of the order of the signs. And with this we shall know the place of this part: for we do this so that the state of the Sun in comparison to the Ascendant is like the state of the Moon in comparison to the Part of Fortune: and the Part of Fortune shall be according to the rising of the Moon: and it is a fitting thing: since he who said it was fitting held this reason: that in nocturnal...

### Third Book
b 3

...in nocturnal births, one should calculate from the Moon to the Sun, and afterward begin counting that same number from the Ascendant in the opposite direction from what we previously said; and this is the forward part of the signs. For when we do this, the location of the <term>Lot of Fortune</term> <note>Also called "Pars Fortune," this is a mathematical point in a horoscope representing luck and well-being.</note> will be revealed to us as it was before, and its participation in the figure will be in this same manner.

¶ These words do not require a commentary <note>original: "glosa"</note>; for anyone who understands anything of this art understands them easily. And regarding what he said—"and its participation in the figure will be in this same manner"—he means that when we have calculated the degrees that are from the Moon to the Sun and projected them from the Ascendant in the reverse of the succession of the signs, the Lot of Fortune will fall in that very same place where it would fall if we had calculated the degrees from the Sun to the Moon and projected them from the Ascendant in the order of the signs. And by these two methods, the Lot of Fortune falls in one and the same place; and it will be in relation to the Moon just as the Ascendant is in relation to the Sun. We have found some who depart from this rule, saying that the Ascendant of the night is the Ascendant of the Moon, because the Moon is the mistress of the night. Therefore, it follows that we should count by night from the Moon to the Sun and project from the Ascendant toward the order of the signs; they said that the location of the Lot of Fortune would then emerge from the Moon's Ascendant at night. But we say to those people that if they understood natural science and that which **Ptolemy** understood, they would agree with him and leave all that aside, for it is empty. This is because **Ptolemy** maintains, through what he taught in this book, that the Sun is that which has the greatest power in the heavens; and this is very much confirmed by many other things demonstrated in natural science and astrology. It is demonstrated in the study of nature that the Sun’s work is more evident than the works of all other stars, and the light that is in all things of the world is through the Sun, for the light of all the stars is nothing except what comes to them from the Sun. In astrology, it is proven that the movements of all stars are in harmony when compared to the movement of the Sun. Since this is so, it follows that the Sun has the lead and lordship over all other stars; and it follows in every way that by day and night, the Ascendant is the Sun’s Ascendant, since the beginning is taken only in comparison to the Sun. Therefore, the Lot of Fortune should be taken by day and night from the Sun to the Moon, and we shall add that to the degree of the Ascendant and project it from the beginning of the ascending sign toward the order of the signs. And if we take from the Moon to the Sun, it follows that we project in reverse of the order of the signs, so that this place is the very same place, and it will be in relation to the Moon according to the relation of the Ascendant to the Sun.

¶ It is also appropriate that from these things we should first choose the Sun during the day, if it should be in the place of the <term>Hyleg</term> <note>The "Giver of Life," a planet or point used to determine the length of the native's life.</note>. If not the Sun, then the Moon; if we cannot choose the Moon, we shall choose the star which has the greatest authorities in the disposition of the Sun's location, and of the preceding conjunction, and also of the Ascendant. That is, a star which has three or more authorities out of the five powers by which the disposition is determined in any of the aforesaid places is to be chosen. If that does not happen, we shall take the degree of the Ascendant.

¶ And it follows that concerning these matters we should similarly choose the Sun first if it is a day birth and the Sun is in a place fit for the Hyleg; and if it is not so, we shall first choose the Moon; and if she is not fit, the planet having more <term>dignities</term> <note>Essential dignities are the "strengths" a planet gains by being in certain parts of the zodiac.</note> in the disposition of the Sun's place, and in the place of the preceding conjunction, and in the Ascendant. I mean when it has three dignities out of the five dignities through which disposition is given in any place we observe, or more; and if this does not happen, we shall take the ascending degree.

¶ If the birth is during the day: we shall first see if the Sun is in any of those places which are fit to be the Hyleg; then the Sun will be the Hyleg. And if it is not in such a place, but rather in the 12th or 8th house, it will not be fit to be the Hyleg, because its virtue is weakened in these two places. And after the Sun is found to lack Hylegiacal fitness, we shall look at the Moon: if she is in any of the

<column-break/>

places having Hylegiacal fitness, she herself will be the Hyleg; and if she is in the 12th or 8th house or under the earth, she will not be fit to be the Hyleg. And then it will be necessary for us to look for the planet having more dignities in the disposition of the Sun's place, and in the disposition of the place of the preceding conjunction, and in the disposition of the Ascendant. And if for any of the planets we find the greater part of the dignities in these three places—the place of the Sun, the previous conjunction, and the Ascendant—and when it also happens that this same planet is in any of the places fit for the Hyleg, that planet itself must be the Hyleg. And if this does not happen, we shall look for the planet having three dignities in any of these three places. And if we find it in any of the places fit for the Hyleg, that planet will be the Hyleg; and if we find nothing of all this, we shall return to the degree of the Ascendant and take it for the Hyleg. And this is what **Ptolemy** wanted to say. Some believe that something was missing in **Ptolemy’s** words, but it is not so, for one of his words teaches another; and this we have clearly shown in this commentary, which should become clear to you, since all this depends on one thing: that we look for the thing having the greatest power. If it is in places fit for the Hyleg, it will be the Hyleg; and if it is not so, we shall look for that which follows it in power and take it; and thus we shall go on until at last we come to the degree of the Ascendant.

¶ In the night, however, it follows that we should first choose the Moon, then the Sun. Thereafter, the stars which have greater authorities in the disposition of the Moon’s place, and the place of the preceding <term>Syzygy</term> <note>A generic term for the previous New or Full Moon.</note>, and the place of the Lot of Fortune. When this does not occur for all of them, if a conjunction <note>New Moon</note> preceded the birth, we shall take the Ascendant. If, however, a Full Moon <note>original: "preuentio"</note> preceded, we shall take the Lot of Fortune.

¶ And it follows that at night we choose the Moon first, subsequently the Sun, then the planet having more dignities in the disposition of the Moon’s place, and in the location of the preceding opposition <note>Full Moon</note>, and in the place of the Lot of Fortune; and if this does not result, we shall look to the Ascendant, finally, if the birth was conjunctional <note>New Moon</note>, or the Lot of Fortune if it was oppositional <note>Full Moon</note>.

¶ He chose the Moon first at night because the Sun will be under the earth, and its virtue will be changed by the earth. When we find the Moon at night in any of the places fit for the Hyleg, she herself will be the Hyleg. And if it is not so, we shall look at the Sun, if it is in those 25 degrees that remain of the Ascendant—as in those 5 degrees that have entered the 12th house—the Sun is the Hyleg. And if we do not find it so, we shall look for the planet having more dignities in the dispositions of the Moon’s place and the place of the preceding opposition; and if it is in any of the places fit for Hyleg, that planet will be the Hyleg. And if it is not so, we shall see if the birth was conjunctional: and then we shall take the planet having three dignities in the place of the Moon or in the place of the preceding opposition, or in the place of the Ascendant. And if it is in any of the places fit for the Hyleg, the planet itself will be the Hyleg. And if it is not so, we shall see if there is any planet having three dignities in the place of the Moon or in the place of the Lot of Fortune. And if it is in any of the places fit for the Hyleg, that planet will be the Hyleg. And if we find nothing of all this, we shall see if the birth was conjunctional: and then we shall take the degree of the Ascendant for the Hyleg; and if it was oppositional, the degree of the Lot of Fortune. And these are the reasons for **Ptolemy’s** words, some of which he hid in his expressions, to which you must pay attention. For I want to teach you this thing: namely, that at times by night the Lot of Fortune must be taken from the Moon to the Sun and projected from the Ascendant in the order of the signs. And this happens when the Sun is under the earth or when its virtue is much weakened. And it happens with this that the birth is oppositional, because the Moon in these places and at the hour of opposition has a much greater and more apparent effect than the Sun, especially if she is above the earth in a strong place and her opposite aspect looks upon her. For **Ptolemy** showed us in all these places that we should first take the indication from the planet that has the greatest power; and if it is not fit, we shall take that which follows it in power, and we should always do so until we come to the last of them. And in this way, you must understand.

### Treatise

...strengths: from that which is in the place of greater and stronger power, we shall take [the Hyleg]. However, choosing a ruler over the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> is by no means appropriate unless it is in a place of greater and stronger dignity. According to the two authorities <note>original: "alabiz," likely referring to specific Arabic astrological methods</note>, it has two dignities in its disposition.

¶ And if both luminaries and the disposer (which is the second authority) are suitable in the appropriate places for the Hyleg, we must take that one of the luminaries which has the greater regency and power. Nevertheless, it is appropriate to choose the disposer before the luminaries when it is in a place of greater regency and power, and when it holds both dignities in its disposition according to the two authorities.

¶ When the Sun and Moon are in suitable places for the Hyleg, either of them can be the Hyleg; however, the one that has more power will prevail, and its influence will appear more clearly. And it has already been demonstrated that whichever of them is in the 10th house <note>The Midheaven, the highest point of the sky.</note> shall prevail. If neither of them is there, the one in the Ascendant shall prevail. If neither is there, the one in the 11th house shall prevail. And if none is there, the one in the 7th house shall prevail. If it happens that both luminaries are in any of the suitable places for the Hyleg, we shall take the one that is closer to the degree of the house's division; that one shall prevail. And if we find the ruler in any of the suitable places for the Hyleg—with both luminaries or one of them in a similarly suitable place—we shall see if the two authorities agree in a single ruler: one being the disposer of the daytime Hylegs and the other of the nighttime ones. If its place is better than the place of the luminaries, we shall choose it before the luminaries, because it has joined many strengths to itself and remains in a better place than the luminaries. It is said that everything Ptolemy spoke of regarding the ordering of Hylegs is perfected here. Others, however, consider that if any disposer of the Hyleg does not aspect the Hyleg itself, it is not fit to be the Hyleg. They do not calculate the number of life from the number of years of the planets that rule the Hyleg as we said before; and since Ptolemy held this path and follows the path that accords with natural science, it was not necessary for us to expand upon those other opinions. We say this: when we find the Sun, the Moon, and the ruling planet all of equal dignity, we shall look in this logic for the one that its own disposer aspects, and that one will be more suitable to be the Hyleg.

¶ When the Hyleg has been made clear, it will be appropriate for us to observe its two types. One of these is according to the succession of the signs only. The other is according to their succession and the nature of the succession. That which is only by succession in quality—which is called the <term>projection of rays</term>—we ought to observe; this is said to happen when the Hyleg is in oriental places (that is, from the Midheaven to the Ascendant). However, the type which exists according to succession and the nature of non-succession, we shall consider in the quality that is called *ozima* <note>original: "ozima," a corruption of the Greek "horimaia," referring to directions using temporal hours</note> in Greek. This occurs when the Hyleg is in a place receding from the Midheaven.

¶ And after we know the Hyleg, it is appropriate for us to work through two methods of the Hyleg. One is according to the order of the signs only in the state called "projection of rays"; and this is when the Hyleg is in oriental places—that is, from the Midheaven to the Ascendant. The other is that which we do not work through the order of signs alone, but through the order of their predecessors; this is similarly in the state called *ozima* in Greek. This means "temporal hours," and this occurs when the Hyleg is falling from the place of the Midheaven.

¶ After he has demonstrated the Hyleg's locations and their order of power—and how it is appropriate for us to take some and leave others—he now wishes to show us the places that kill and the powers that are killers. When he wanted to do this, he began to tell how we should work through the Hylegia, and we now wish to gloss his words as we are accustomed. Regarding what he said about "two methods of the Hyleg," one of which is "according to the order of the signs alone": he means the method by which he makes the <term>atazir</term> <note>A method of "directing" a planet through the zodiac to calculate the timing of events.</note> of the Hyleg, directed according to

<column-break/>

the order of the signs alone until it reaches the degree of an unfortunate planet or the degree of its ray. And regarding what he said—"the other which is according to the order and the nature of inordination"—he means the other method in which the *atazir* of the Hyleg is made, directing it forward and backward together until the forward direction reaches the degree of an unfortunate planet, or the backward direction reaches the degree of the descendant; whichever of these two has greater power in "cutting off" <note>Stopping the life force</note> will prevail. And regarding what he said—that according to the order of the signs alone we should work in the state called "projection of rays" when the Hyleg is in oriental places (from Midheaven to Ascendant)—he means that when the Hyleg is in the 10th, 11th, or in the Ascendant, we shall always make its *atazir* direct according to the order of the signs toward the killing powers. However, regarding what he said—"that which we do not work through the order of signs alone, but through their precursors, similarly in the state called *ozima* in Greek"—he means temporal hours. This occurs when the Hyleg is falling from the Midheaven. He means that when the Hyleg is in the 9th or 7th house, we shall make its *atazir* both forward and backward. We shall not judge by one "cutting" alone unless another agrees with it; if both agree, so it is; if they disagree, we shall know what thing happens to the person's body. The things given by general constellations are called "temporal" for those points falling from the Midheaven because of their return; for we say that the shadow returns, which he calls temporal. And Ptolemy made clear to us both of the *atazir* methods—namely, the direct and the backward—and showed us how we shall number them, so that we may know from them the quantity of life.

¶ And when these things are thus commanded, the degrees signifying death according to the Hyleg found in the type that follows the precedence of the signs will be the degree of the West <note>The Descendant</note> for the sole reason that it hides the lordship of life.

¶ And after these things are so: the degrees signifying death will be, if the Hyleg is in the manner of the forward part of the signs, the western degree only, because it covers the lordship of life and hides it.

¶ The Hyleg which is in the forward part of the signs has its *atazir* backward; he considers that the thing which kills in this Hyleg is the western degree itself. He gives the reason why, saying: because it covers and hides the lordship of life, and exterminates the sequence of its strength (that is, its fortitude), and changes it from appearance to occultation and weakness, and condemns it because it is under the earth.

¶ Secondly, the degrees of the stars themselves applied to or testifying to that same Hyleg found in this way: for this reason, they are added to or subtracted from the collected numbers until the hour when the Hyleg falls. Except if they set, for then they would not go to the place of the Hyleg, but the Hyleg itself goes to their places. Those which always add are called "fortunes," while those which subtract are called "infortunes." Mercury, again, will be with the stars with which it is associated in the figure.

¶ And the degrees of the many [stars] meeting the Hyleg: this is the way. It is affirmed that they are added and subtracted only in the numbers that are joined until the hour the Hyleg falls or kills. For these degrees are not those which are applied to the place of the Hyleg, but the Hyleg itself is applied to their places. When they add, they are the planets of fortune; when they subtract, they are infortunes. Mercury, however, similarly goes with the planets with which it has participation in the figure.

¶ Of the planets meeting the Hyleg in the backward *atazir*, some are fortunes, such as Jupiter and Venus, and the fixed stars that are of their nature; these add to the gift of the backward *atazir*. Others are infortunes, such as Saturn and Mars, and the fixed stars of their nature; these subtract from the gift of the backward *atazir*. And it is required that a fixed star which adds or subtracts should have no latitude, or its latitude should be small, so that its power is within the zodiac of the signs. Mercury and the fixed stars that are of the nature of fortune will add in the gift of the *atazir* if they participate with the fortunes. If they are with the infortunes, they will be infortunes and subtract from the gift of the backward *atazir*. When the Hyleg goes to the places of the stars that add or subtract, it is necessary that we follow this in the direct *atazir*.

# Third Book

### The Direct Progression
<note>original: "azir directo"</note>
Since the parts move toward the locations of the Hyleg. And Ptolemy <note>original: "Ptol."</note> teaches us the quantity of subtraction and addition in this which he wishes to say.

¶ The number of increase or decrease will be determined from the positions of the degrees of each of them. For he himself finds the number of hourly times <note>Astrological hours are not 60 minutes, but 1/12th of the time between sunrise and sunset.</note> that each of their degrees has. For when the time of birth is during the day, we shall attribute the times of the diurnal hours; and when it is at night, we shall attribute the times of the nocturnal hours, according to whose quantity will be the number of completed years. This should be understood to be the case when the planet is in the ascendant; afterwards, as it moves away from the ascendant, the number decreases until it reaches the western point <note>The Descendant or setting point.</note>, and nothing remains.

¶ The number of addition and subtraction for the position of any of their degrees is according to the number of hourly times of any of those degrees. If the time of birth was by day, it will be according to the time of the hours of the day; if by night, it will be according to the time of the hours of the night. And however much this number is, that will be the number of completed years. However, we must understand this matter thus: this is said to be the case if it is in the ascendant; and afterwards, subtract from it according to its distance from the ascendant until it reaches the descendant, and nothing follows from it.

¶ He means that the quantity of addition and subtraction will be according to the distance of the part from the setting point, so that four proportional quantities are formed: one is the hour of the part's distance from the setting; the second is 12 hours; the third is the quantity of addition or subtraction; the fourth is the parts of the hours of the part. And when we multiply the hours of the distance from the setting by the parts of the hours of the part, and divide by 12, the quantity of addition or subtraction will result. This is what we seek: then we shall add or subtract from the quantity that results from the reverse Atazir <note>A method of moving a planet backward through the zodiac to find its "killing" point.</note>, which is the quantity of that which moves through the firmament until the Hyleg reaches the degree of the setting.

¶ But concerning the Hyleg <note>original: "alhileg"</note>, which is in the species we investigate according to the succession of the signs: the locations of the malefic planets <note>original: "stellaꝝ infortunaꝝ"</note>, namely Saturn and Mars, are present when they come bodily to the Hyleg, or when they cast their rays from any of those places—namely from the positions of the square <note>90 degrees away.</note> or the opposite radiation <note>180 degrees away.</note>; and perhaps from the sextiles <note>60 degrees away.</note> which "obey" or behold the Hyleg and are equal in strength. Likewise, the fourth aspect <note>the square</note> of the place of the Hyleg itself, which is according to the succession of signs, will also kill; and perhaps the sextile will work the same when it is with a malefic planet, and when it is in a sign of long ascension <note>Signs that take longer to rise over the horizon.</note>. Similarly, the trine <note>120 degrees away.</note> will do the same when it is in a benefic <note>original: "fortuna"</note> and remains in a sign of short ascension.

¶ This concerning the Hyleg: which is calculated in the same manner according to the order of the signs. That which kills is the location where the malefics are present, and these are the locations of Saturn and Mars: either when the Hyleg meets them bodily, or when they cast their rays from either of these two places—namely from the square or from the opposite place. Sometimes this can be from the "obeying" sextiles where they behold each other and are equal in power. And the fourth place of the Hyleg's own position, which is according to the order of the signs, similarly kills. Sometimes a sextile does this if it is in a benefic and occurs in a sign of long ascensions. So also the trine will do if it is in signs of short ascensions.

¶ He means that the direct Atazir must always be taken from the Hyleg to the place of the malefic or its ray, according to the order of the signs. And he has shown us in every way the effect of the killing places through the ascensions of the Hyleg, whose Atazir is made direct. He said that these are the locations of the presence of the malefic and the places in which their squares and oppositions fall. And what he said: "sometimes it will be similarly from obeying sextiles where they behold each other and are equal in power."

<column-break/>

He means that when the Hyleg is in signs of short ascension, such a sextile as this cuts off the life-force of the Hyleg; because the place of the malefic's sextile is the "killer" and holds power over the Hyleg, and the Hyleg is "obeying" the place of that malefic sextile. And when it similarly happens that the Hyleg is distant from the head of Aries or Cancer, such a sextile cuts off the Hyleg, since it is in a place whose power or force is equal to the power of the Hyleg's place. And what he said—that the fourth place itself or the square is in the direction of the order of the signs—similarly kills. He means that the square of the Hyleg similarly cuts off the Hyleg, because in the square figure there is enmity and harm, and it causes a man to kill himself with his own hands. And he adds here "in the order of the signs" because the Hyleg is always moved in the direct order. And that which he said: "and sometimes the sextile does this if it is in a benefic and in signs of long ascensions"—that is, the place of the sextile or the Hyleg, which is in signs of long ascensions, acts like a square, and this shall be judged as such. Similarly, a trine, when it is in signs of short ascensions, shall be judged as a square. And all this teaches us that Ptolemy always makes the rays of the planets fall on unequal degrees; for if he made them by mixed ascensions as many men have believed, he could not so absolutely say all this that he said: that a sextile in signs of long ascensions and a trine in signs of short ascensions is judged as a killing square.

¶ And when the Moon is the Hyleg, the place of the Sun will sometimes kill, because when the Sun comes to the place of the Hyleg, it will have the power of both killing and saving. For the Sun itself goes to the place of the Hyleg.

¶ And when the Moon is the Hyleg, the Sun's place kills similarly; for when the Sun meets the place of this half of the Hyleg, it will have the power of killing and saving, because the Sun is that which goes to the place of the Hyleg.

¶ The place of the Sun cuts off the Moon <note>Terminates the life force.</note> when their places are dissonant, as when the Moon is in a moist sign and the Sun is in a dry one; or when the Moon is in the "term" <note>A specific subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> of a malefic and the Sun is in the term of a benefic; or when both are in terms of malefics, and both are in the dignities of malefics, and in concordant signs, the Sun will not cut off the Moon. And it happens that this rule is understood regarding Hylegs: namely, one planet with another, because contrary stars always cut off the Hyleg. And a star can be contrary by nature, as Saturn is to Jupiter, or it can be contrary by accident, as when the position of one is contrary to the position of the other.

¶ Nor is it fitting for us to think that these killing places necessarily always end the life; for they will by no means kill unless they are afflicted <note>original: "infortunabuntur"</note> at that time.

¶ And it is not for us to understand that these places always "cut off" in all ways: but they do this only when they are malefic or afflicted.

¶ He means that all things which "cut off" do not do so to the Hyleg unless they are malefic: namely, that the malefic planets are with the Hyleg, or behold them with a hard aspect, or that they are in the terms of the malefics, or that they are in places in which the power of the Hyleg is weakened, and such things.

¶ Because this killing is prevented when the degree is in the term of one of the benefics <note>Jupiter or Venus.</note>, or when one of the benefics casts its rays upon that killing degree, or to the degree which follows after it, from a square, a trine, or from an opposition; provided that in the projection of the rays of Jupiter the influence does not exceed 12 degrees, nor in the case of Venus more than eight degrees.

¶ Because this matter is disturbed when it is the term of any benefic, or when any benefic casts its rays upon them from a trine, square, or opposition aspect to the degree of the "killer" itself, or to the degree that follows it, provided it does not exceed the rays of Jupiter by more than twelve degrees, and does not exceed in Venus more than eight degrees.

¶ When you have performed the Atazir of the Hyleg to the place of the killer, it is necessary that we see if it is the term of any benefic and if any benefic beholds it, which might apply to the killing degree, or to any other degree of those that come before it; and if this degree which is before the killing degree is the degree of Jupiter...

# Treatise

12 degrees or less. And if it should be so, we will know that the "cutting off" <note>original: "abscissio"; the symbolic end of the life-force</note> will not happen at that time, but will be prolonged until another matter looks upon the Hyleg <note>The planet or point designated as the "giver of life."</note>. And regarding the rays of the Fortunes <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter and Venus.</note> which Ptolemy spoke of in the third place, there are only three: for they are the square, the trine, and the opposition. Sometimes any of them, through the great power they possess, can defend against death. But because the sextile aspect <note>A 60-degree angle between planets.</note> is of weaker authority than any of the others, it does not have the power to remove death; and for this reason, Ptolemy did not wish to include it in the calculation. Similarly, we understand through his preceding words that the sextile does not have the power of a square, except when it is in signs of long ascension <note>Signs that take longer to rise over the horizon, which increases their strength in certain calculations.</note>. And then it shall be judged as a square, or as that which occurs in signs that are "obedient" or equal in power. Similarly, when it happens in all the other aspects which we described in the previous treatise—where any of them doubles its virtue in such a way that it is worth as much as a square or a trine—the opposition will have the power of removing death. And a fixed star will do the same thing if it is of a fortunate temperament and has no latitude <note>Distance north or south from the ecliptic/zodiac path.</note> from the signs of the zodiac. And Ptolemy teaches well through this statement that he considers the power of the body of Jupiter to be 12 degrees, and the power of the body of Venus to be 8 degrees; and thus it is proper to be understood.

Similarly, it will happen when the Hyleg is joined to a star to which it adheres in a bodily destruction, and the latitude of those two is not the same.

Similarly, when the Hyleg meets a planet such that they are joined bodily, and the latitude of both is not one and the same.

He means to say that the "killing degree" <note>original: "gradus interficiens"</note> is such that it does not kill unless a "malefic" <note>original: "infortuna"; a harmful planet like Saturn or Mars.</note> is present in it, and not merely by its rays; and its latitude must be distant from the latitude of the Hyleg or moving toward it. If it should be so, the degree in which the malefic stays kills in such a state: because it cannot kill unless the Hyleg is in one of the circles of the greater circles. And if you understand anything of arithmetic, you will know that in some places, when the Hyleg is north of the zodiac and the malefic is south, and the latitudes of both are equal, that same malefic cuts off the Hyleg in such a state as this: when it happens that both are upon one circle.

But when the saving or helping stars, or the killing stars, are two or more in each of these two categories, it follows that we should observe which of the two is stronger according to the multitude of helping things and their strength. Therefore, regarding the multitude: when one of the two types is clearly more increased than the other. Regarding strength: when the stars that help or kill are in places that increase their own power, and no other stars remain in those places; and especially when the stars of one type are "oriental" <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> and the stars of the other type are "occidental" <note>Setting after the Sun.</note>.

And if the planets that remove death and help, or those that kill, are two or more planets in each of these two matters, it follows that we should look at which of these two kinds prevails according to the similarity of the helping things and their power, and according to their own likeness. When one kind is greater than the other in a matter having quantity; and that which is according to power occurs when the helping or killing planets are in places pertaining to them, and the other is not in such a place—specifically if the planets of one kind are oriental and the planets of the other kind are occidental.

He means to say that when we are in doubt about the places in which we find the killing planets and the planets that remove death, then we shall look at the state of each of the two kinds by the power which they have. And by that which we find to prevail over the other in virtue, we shall judge. And we shall know which of them prevails by looking into the being of each of them through two ways. One is the number of affirming things for each of the two kinds: for that which has more helpers in a matter having quantity will prevail. The other is the power of each of these two kinds: because the kind that is itself (or the things helping it) in places pertaining to them prevails over the other which is not so in places pertaining to it. Similarly, we shall look in all their other states, in what

<column-break/>

manner they stand in comparison to the world and in the birth [chart]. For example: oriental planets are of greater power than occidental ones, and other similar things.

Wherefore, regarding those who are "under the rays" <note>original: "sub radijs"; planets so close to the Sun that they are invisible and usually considered weakened.</note> in setting, helping, or saving us, nothing generally ought to be observed except when the Moon is the Hyleg; for then that same place of the Sun will be the place of the killers. And then also we shall consider if a malefic that is with it has hindered it and no fortune has helped it.

So it follows that we should not generally judge by planets existing under the rays, neither in killing nor in delivering, unless the Moon is the Hyleg; and then the place of the Sun itself will be the place of the killers; and we shall judge by the malefic planet existing with it: if it has harmed it and there was no fortunate planet to help at the time and let it escape.

It is not proper for us to judge by any planet existing under the rays of the Sun, neither as killing nor as liberating in any way, unless the Moon is the Hyleg and the place of the Sun kills. For when it is in this manner, and some malefic is under the rays of the Sun which no fortune looks upon, it will itself be the killer: because it harms the place where the Sun stays, on account of which that place will have greater power to kill.

But the numbers which are according to the distance <note>original: "longitudinem"</note> between the place of the Hyleg and the place of the cutting-off: we find them freely and however the sum might reach its minimum. Just as the ancients used to do, who said they were always according to the quantity of the times of the "ascensions of the degrees" of that distance. Nor should we consider them at any time unless the Ascendant <note>The point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon.</note> is the place of the Hyleg itself, or one of the places of those ascending to the Ascendant.

And the number of years that will be and will pass by the distances that will be between the place of the Hyleg and the place of the killer: it does not follow that we should only take it, nor in whatever way it happens. For many men have taken and believed that it was always by the time of the ascensions of the degrees of that distance; but we do not work by this, unless the Ascendant itself was the place of the Hyleg, or some place from those which go toward the Ascendant.

After he has completed for us the places of the Hyleg and the Hyleg itself, and the things that kill, and those that remove death: he begins here to show us how we shall know the quantity of the years of life. And these are according to the number of the distance that is between the place of the Hyleg and the place of the killer. And when he wished to do this, he began first by destroying opinions contrary to the truth in this science, until in this matter he follows the pure and direct truth. For many men have believed we might know this from the number that is between the Hyleg and the killer, through the degrees of ascension of the city of the person born. And Ptolemy said that this is not the truth, unless the degree of the Ascendant itself was the Hyleg, or the degree of some place from those which go toward the Ascendant. And these [Hylegs] are in themselves in the 7th and 9th houses <note>The 7th house is the West/Descendant; the 9th house is the house of long journeys/religion.</note>; because from these places we shall know by the ascensions through their opposites until the Hyleg is placed in the West, just as we did before. Then when the Hyleg is in the degree of the Midheaven <note>original: "medy celi"; the highest point of the chart.</note>, we shall know this through the degrees of the ascensions of the direct circle <note>Right Ascension / the celestial equator.</note>. And when it is similarly in the degree of the 10th or 11th [houses], or in the degrees of the Ascendant which are after the degree itself which ascends: we shall know this through ascensions composed of those of the direct circle and those of the Ascendant. And these are diverse things which do not follow a natural matter, as he shows here in the following statement.

Therefore, for those who have observed this kind by natural consideration, it follows that they observe it in all the last ways: namely, how many times of the equinoctial circle <note>The celestial equator.</note> there will be from the place of the star or the following figure to the place of the star or the preceding figure in the birth. For the times of the equinoctial circle traverse the circle of the horizon and the line of the meridian equally; these are the two through which similar local distances are taken. Each "time" of the equinoctial circle is set as the place of one solar year.

# Third Part

It is appropriate in every way for one wishing to apply their mind to this method according to nature <note>original: "sm nam" / "secundum naturam"</note> that they focus on one thing: looking at what times of the equinox <note>Refers to measuring time along the celestial equator, where each degree equals a specific amount of time.</note> the position of the planet or the preceding figure in the nativity will reach. For the times of the equinox will traverse the entire horizon and the entire meridian line through one equal measure. These are two things by which a person can find the distances of similar signs. They have taken each "time" from the equinoctial times to represent one solar year.

¶ And he said it is appropriate in every way for one wishing to follow this method to apply their mind according to nature to look into this matter. He means to say that one should always perform this same procedure, which does not change. And all that he said is this: the one thing that does not change in this matter is taking the distance between the <term>Hyleg: the planet or point that represents the life force</term> and the <term>Interfector: the point or planet that symbolically ends the life</term>. If the <term>Atazir: a method of "directing" or progressing a planet through the sky to predict timing</term> is direct, it shall be taken through the ascensions of the circle in which the Hyleg was found. If the Atazir is "perverse" <note>original: "pueršuz"; referring to converse or backward direction</note>, we shall take it through the ascensions of the opposite place to which the Hyleg must reach. For this agrees with the lowering of the circle in which the Hyleg was taken, and all of this will be taught to you later. If you understand anything of astrology, you will easily be able to understand all of this without a commentary <note>original: "sine glosa"</note>. And when he said that each "time" from the equinoctial times is taken in place of a solar year, he means that when we have done this, we will take each degree that resulted from our Atazir as one solar year.

It is fitting, therefore, that when the position of the Hyleg has proceeded and is upon the eastern circle of the horizon, the times of the ascensions of the degrees from that hour until the hour of the "killing" point should be taken. This is because after this quantity of time of the equinoctial circle, the Interfector will be in the place of the Hyleg, which is the eastern circle of the horizon. When the Hyleg is on the line of the middle of the day <note>The Meridian or Midheaven</note>, the ascensions of the direct circle <note>Right Ascensions</note>—according to which the time of the passage of that part of the circle of signs occurs—should be taken in the circle of the middle of the day.

¶ And it follows that when the position of the Hyleg is in the preceding part and on the eastern horizon, the times of the ascensions of the degrees should be taken from that same hour until the hour of the Interfector, because the Interfector will reach the place of the Hyleg—that is, the eastern horizon. After this amount of equinoctial time, the Interfector will be in the place of the Hyleg, which is the eastern circle of the horizon. And when the Hyleg is on the line of the Midheaven, the ascensions of the direct circle, through which the time of the passage of that part of the zodiac occurs, should be taken on the meridian circle.

He means to say that when the Hyleg is at the very degree of the location, we will take the distance between it and the position of the Interfector by the ascensions of the city <note>Oblique ascensions specific to the birth latitude</note>. Whatever that amount is, it will proceed from the equinox until the Interfector reaches the place where the Hyleg was. And if the Hyleg is on the meridian line, it follows that the ascensions of the "right sphere" <note>Right Ascensions</note> should be taken, because according to them will be the time in which it passes through the zodiac on the line of the middle of the day. We will take the ascensions that are between it and the position of the Interfector by the ascensions of the direct circle; and whatever that amount is, it will proceed from the equinox until the Interfector reaches the place where the Hyleg was.

But when it is in the western circle of the horizon <note>The Descendant</note>, we will take the number of times in which each of those distances falls and sets. This is like the number of degrees of the ascensions of the parts of the zodiac that are opposite to them.

¶ And if the Hyleg is on the western horizon, we will take the number of times in which any of those distances is lowered and sets. And this is the same as the number of degrees of the ascensions of the parts of the zodiac that are opposite to them.

<column-break/>

He means to say that when the Hyleg is at the very degree of the setting <note>the West</note>, we will take the distance between the ascensions of the Ascendant of the city and the opposite of the place where the Interfector is. Whatever that amount is, it will proceed from the equinox until the Interfector reaches the position of the Hyleg.

¶ And if the position of the Hyleg, as it proceeds, is not in any of these three—but is in the places established between them—then the previously mentioned time of ascensions, the time of settings, and the time of passage through the Midheaven will not be those in which the following places reach the preceding places. Rather, they will be those in which they reach different places. This is because the place to which the following one goes is not similar to, nor of the same kind as, the place where the preceding one was. It cannot be judged except when its position is made to match the original position, and its part in respect to the horizon and the Midheaven is just as the original part was.

¶ And when the Hyleg (which is the opposite point) is not in any of these three boundaries, but is in the places between them, the times of the aforementioned ascensions or the times of descensions or the times of passage through the Midheaven will not be those that apply the following places to the earlier ones. Instead, they apply to different places because the place to which the following point applies is called "similar" to the place where the earlier one was only when its position is similar to the first, and its part is such as the first part was in comparison to the horizon, in comparison to the meridian line, or in both.

The three boundaries <note>original: "tres termini"</note> he mentioned are: the degree of the Ascendant, the degree of the Midheaven, and the very degree of the West <note>The Descendant</note>. And when he spoke of "the places that are between them," he means the Hyleg that is in any place other than these three. For it follows that when it is there, it is similar to those others: in applying the Interfector to the place of the Hyleg according to how it moves from the equinox, it becomes similar to the malefic <note>original: "malus"</note>. And this can be done by comparing the position of the Hyleg to the line of the horizon and the line of the meridian. Because of this, it is necessary that the Atazir be done with "mixed ascensions"—partly from the ascensions of the town in which the person was born and partly from the ascensions of the direct circle—so that through this, the time it takes for the Interfector to reach the circle where the Hyleg stood is determined by the motion of the equinox.

¶ And it also happens that in respect to these two, its position is the same when it is near the places that are above the semicircle of the circles passing through the common place of the meridian and the horizon. These are those circles of which each one produces one "temporal hour," <term>Temporal Hour: a twelfth of the time between sunrise and sunset, varying in length by season</term> and they are nearly equal to one another.

¶ And it happens that the comparison of both is the same when it is near the places in the middle circle of the circles that pass through the sectional intersection of the meridian and the horizon; these are the ones where any of them makes one temporal hour.

¶ And the parts of the hours are circles that are distant from one another by as much as one of the temporal hours. All of them are cut at one intersection. Similarly, the meridian line and half of each of these circles appears above the earth, and the other half is hidden beneath the earth, except for the circle of the horizon itself. For the horizon is always placed between the half of the firmament that appears and the other half that does not appear beneath the earth. And since it is so, we must seek in the whole Hyleg the half of the circle in which it lingers above the earth; and we should take the Atazir according to the ascension of the half of this circle. Whatever that amount is, that will be what proceeds from the equinox until the Interfector reaches the place where the Hyleg was.

But when this semicircle has circled the aforementioned common place, its position will sometimes be like the position of the hemisphere, and sometimes like the position of the meridian circle. And there will be times in which the parts of the circle of signs [pass through] these two places...

And since it is so, it is appropriate for us to know that when we know the hours of distance of the earlier degree from the meridian line, we should also know how much the equinox moves until there are as many hours of distance of the following degree from the meridian line as there are hours of distance of the earlier degree. And however much that was, that will be the quantity of the <term>atazir</term>; and this is the root of the rule of <term>atazir</term>; and Ptolemy now wants to show us how we shall calculate it.

But if the hours that result for us were taken in respect to the midheaven which is above the earth, those by which we multiply will be the times of the diurnal hours. If, however, they were in respect to the midheaven which is below the earth, we will multiply by the times of the nocturnal hours. Afterward, we will multiply the number of hours of elongation by the times of the hours of the following degree. If the hours of elongation were taken by comparison to the midheaven above the earth, we will multiply them by the times of the diurnal <note>daytime</note> hours; if they were in comparison to the angle of the earth <note>the IC or bottom of the sky</note>, we will multiply them by the times of the nocturnal hours. Whatever result comes from this multiplication will be the amount the equinox <note>the equator</note> will travel until the following degree moves from the midheaven, just as much as the preceding degree moves itself from the midheaven. Afterward, we will take the result of the multiplication and the number we set aside and subtract one from the other if both degrees are on one side of the midheaven; if they are on two different sides, we will add one to the other. The result will be what we seek.

Let the beginning of Aries first ascend so that the beginning of **Capricorn** is in the midheaven. Therefore, the following place will move toward the preceding place after as many times as there are in the remainder, which is 46. The times of the ascensions of Aries and Taurus are nearly the same as these times. This is calculated so that the **hyleg** (or **albileg** <note>a variation of the word hyleg</note>) is the ascending degree itself.

And we will take just as much as that part of the residual which we hold between that which fell in the two angles: we will either add it to or subtract it from that which falls for the angle from which we take the comparison.

¶ This means that when the **hyleg** <term>hyleg: the "Life-Giver" point in a birth chart that represents the native's vitality</term> is in other degrees [than] the degrees of the angles, we will take the hours of its elongation from one of the angles and we will see in what part it falls out of the 6 hours that are between one angle and another: and what results from this we will keep aside. ¶ For example: because the residual by reason of these six hours was placed as 12 hours, and we placed the elongation of the previous place of each of the two angles as three temporal hours; and these three hours were half of six hours: we will take half of 12 and add it above 58 or subtract it from 70, and we will find the residual to be 64 times <note>degrees</note>. TREATISE

¶ If both [the Hyleg and its aspect] are good, yet there is a sign of wandering or debility, then it is clear that hindrance, exile, or travels will happen as a result.
¶ And if both these things are good, we should know that there will happen weakness, hindrance, and misfortune, as well as such harms or exiles, and the person departing from his place.
¶ When the **hyleg** <term>hyleg: the "Life-Giver" point in a birth chart, usually a planet or point like the Sun or Moon, used to determine the length of life</term> in any given year reaches a degree that was unfortunate in the **radix** <term>radix: the original birth chart (the "root")</term> by some malefic planet, but some other influence helps that is able to remove the "cutting" <note>original: "abscisionem"; in astrology, a "cutting" refers to a deadly aspect that signifies the end of life</note> of that year; and it similarly happens in that year that the places of the Hyleg are safe from misfortunes in their **complexion** <term>complexion: the "temperament" or balance of the four humors (blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile) within the body</term>, the upcoming event through that misfortune of the radix will be some kind of infirmity, debility, or harm, or the person will leave his place and go to another.
¶ We shall distinguish the specific kinds of these things occurring from the likeness of the place of the thing meeting the factors of the birth.
¶ And we can know the specific manners of the events happening because of any of these things through the agreement of the places of the meeting point with the factors of the birth.
¶ This means that we can know the specific manner of any of these things through the agreement of the place of the thing meeting the hyleg and the lord of the thing causing it: and he will demonstrate all these things later in his discourse.
¶ And whenever we are in doubt which of those places ought to be the "killers," nothing can prevent us from estimating and observing the things that happen in each birth to the **alhyleg** <term>alhyleg: another spelling of hyleg</term>: and in this, what is to come will be that which is similar to what has already happened and appeared from past accidents, for we will consider the mode of all of them because the mode in the perfection of those things which happen through them is of equal strength in all. According to this, therefore, we will establish our investigations and their increase and decrease.
¶ And if at times we are in doubt regarding the places arriving and having the reason of "killing," it does not disturb us if, by weighing them, we look into the things meeting the hyleg in any of the matters of the birth: and if we follow in the things that happen from them the thing suited to that which has happened and appeared from these accidents. And we should apply our minds well to all things, since the matter is in the completing of what has happened from them, equal in power through all times; we will seek out in what way they will increase or decrease according to this.
¶ This means that when we find different things at different times "cutting" the hyleg, we will look at what agrees with the **complexion** <note>the bodily temperament</note> of that man, and other accidents that we know from his history and from final things: and we will judge according to that which agrees with him. For example: let us suppose that to a certain man various "cuttings" happen, and it similarly happens that one of them is in a time of general mortality <note>original: "mortalitatis gñalis"; likely referring to a plague or epidemic affecting everyone in a region</note>; it is fitting then that we judge by that one and not by the others. Or it may happen that the composition of that man's body is such that it cannot last many years: and so it is fitting that we judge by the "cutting" that happens in that year. And you will know the compositions of the body from the rules which he narrated in the chapter on those who do not receive food <note>referring to infants who die shortly after birth</note>, and in chapters 11, 12, and 13 of this 3rd part. And when you understand all these reasons, seeing with this similarly how great a force the "cutter" has and how great are the strengths of the accidents that join it: then, when you have applied your mind well to the increase and decrease, you will understand the quantity of the state that is appropriate. And it is clear that Ptolemy teaches in this chapter only the rules of ascending things so that we may take an example from them regarding things giving fortune. And because this treatise is sufficient in its length of gloss, it is

<column-break/>

fitting that we finish it in this place: and we will gloss what remains of the 3rd part of the book in the 9th treatise of our gloss.

# Here begins the ninth treatise of the gloss of Haly ibn Ridwan.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial 'R' containing a human face in profile looking left.</image-desc>
The things which he has demonstrated to us in this treatise concern judging the accidents that happen to any person. And since man is composed of matter (which is the body) and of form (which is the soul), it is necessary that we always know all these accidents through the state of the body and the soul; therefore Ptolemy divided this into four chapters. The first is that in which he placed the rules through which the state of the body can be known. The second is that in which he placed the rules by which we can know the pestilences <note>original: "pestilētias"; here meaning diseases or afflictions</note> happening to bodies. In the third, he placed the rules by which we can know the state of the soul. In the fourth, he placed the rules by which we can know the pestilences happening to the soul. And he joined these four chapters to the ten preceding ones: and so this 3rd part with these becomes 14 chapters: 10 of which we have already glossed, and now we wish to gloss what he said in these four remaining chapters.

## On the form and figure of the body of the native and on his complexion. Chapter 2.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial 'P' containing a human face in profile looking right.</image-desc>
After the perfection of [the judgment of] the choice of life: we will begin first to relate the form and figure of bodies from particular things, as is orderly and fitting; because the qualities of the body naturally precede the qualities of the soul: for the reason that the body is more dense, and more things are apparent in it which are proper to its gathering together when it is born. In the soul, however, things do not appear except that by the first occasion after birth and creation, it [the soul's quality] exists step by step.

¶ Ptolemy said: after we have perfected the talk concerning the time of life, we wish first to begin in particular things the judgment of the fortune of the native and his build, according to what is fitting and ordered in all books: since the states of the body are prior to the states of the soul by nature: and because the body is more dense, the things appearing in it for the most part regarding what pertains to its composition are born with it. Yet in the soul, the things coming to it from the First Cause do not appear except after birth and generation, little by little.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap initial 'J' containing a human face in profile looking right.</image-desc>
Already many times we have said that the words of Ptolemy clearly demonstrate to us his greatest intellect in philosophy: and his words clearly demonstrated when he spoke on the quantity of life that he was wiser than any other in the art of astrology and medicine <note>original: "iūuialis"; likely a corruption or shorthand for "iuuandi" or similar medical context</note>: and if you understand his words in this place, you will know a very noble thing. For the states of bodies are prior by nature to the states of the soul, because the virtues of the soul follow the complexion of the bodies, as the ancient sages demonstrated: and Haly composed one large separate treatise upon this reason. And this reason is visible and manifest: since we find that he who has a hot body is bolder and more prone to anger than him who has a cold one. We find also that in the complexion of him in whom the melancholic humor <term>melancholic humor: one of the four humors, associated with the element of earth, coldness, and dryness</term> prevails, there appears fear and levity and all other accidents of melancholy. And what else do you seek? Aristotle made this clear in his book *On the Soul* <note>original: "liº suo de aia"; Aristotle's *De Anima*</note>: because the soul is the "completion" <note>entelechy</note> of a natural, artificial, visible body through potentiality: and therefore it is fitting that the states of the body were placed first before the states of the soul, although one is not often [separated] from the other by time. Similarly, the substance of the body is denser than that of the soul: and the accidents happening to bodies are more apparent to the senses than those which happen to the soul. And it is manifest that the proper accidents of the body are born with the body: and it has already been shown and proved in philosophy that the First Cause (whose name be exalted for ever and ever) ordained the soul after the extracted substances and made it more noble; yet it is joined to the bodily virtues just as is the vegetative soul: and the good things that are in matters come from the part of God: and evil things happen to matters through their own nature and their own materials: and after good things happen to matter from the part of God, it is manifest that the thing which the soul receives through God and through the body and through its own nature are according to how the figures of the stars of the birth work in it.
