...is so great: for this portion is the "ascending" of the Moon just as the Moon relates to the "ascending" of the Sun. Indeed, we have already carefully revealed all of this previously in the judgment of life. And since this comparison of this portion to the Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> is based on the comparison of the Moon to the Sun, it is appropriate that it specifically pertains to riches, just as the Ascendant pertains to the person. It is such that the comparison of the Part of Fortune <note original="pars fortune">A mathematical point in a horoscope calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant, used to indicate prosperity</note> entering the Ascendant is like the Ascendant’s relation to the significance of what a person holds in potential, such as riches, wisdom, service, inheritance, and children.

### ¶ The method of this observation is as follows.

We shall therefore observe the stars that rule the specific sign. We will consider what their strength and similarity are, as we said before. Likewise, we will observe the stars associated with them in figure <note>astrological aspects or configurations</note> or those elevated above them, whether they are of the same condition <note original="baiz">Likely a Latinization of the Arabic 'hazz,' meaning dignity or lot</note> or of a contrary condition.

### ¶ The judgments of this matter are of this sort; I mean to say:

You should take the planets that are the governors of the sign and inspect what power and what harmony they have in the manner we have described. And you shall similarly look at the planets having a participation in the figure with them, and those who are elevated above them, whether they are of the same condition or another.

### ¶ He means to say that the rule by which we know the riches of the newborn is to take the planets governing the place of the Part of Fortune. You shall prefer the one who holds more dignities <note>Astrological 'dignities' are positions where a planet is considered strong, such as its home sign</note> there, and you shall inspect its state in comparison to the world—both its relation to the angles <note>The four most powerful points in a chart: East, West, Zenith, and Nadir</note> and to the Sun—so that through these you may know how great is the power of the governor of the place of the Part of Fortune, and in what manner its harmony and significance lie. And when we have done this, we shall look similarly at the planets having participation with it in the figure and those who are elevated above it; for if they are in harmony with it, the significance will be greater and firmer; and if it is otherwise, it will be smaller and weaker.

<margin>
For when the dispositors <note>Planets that rule a specific point or sign</note> of the aforementioned part are strong, the native will possess many riches. This is especially true if the luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> testify to them with a sign of similarity.
</margin>

### ¶ And when the governors of the Part of Fortune are strong and more powerful, the native will be the master of great riches, especially if the two luminaries testify in accord.

### ¶ He means to say that when the planet governing the Part of Fortune is strong and powerful, it signifies that the native will have great riches. And if, along with this, it happens that the two luminaries testify there with a testimony of concord—such as a trine or sextile aspect <note>Harmonious angles of 120 and 60 degrees respectively</note> and in such a way they come into power—it will signify that the native’s riches will be much greater and exceedingly large. Because of this, it is clearly understood that if the governor of the Part of Fortune is weak, the native will have few riches; and if its power is condemned "under the rays" <note>Too close to the Sun to be seen</note> and falling "under the earth," the native will have no riches nor possess anything. And if, in this state, the Sun and Moon do not testify there, the native will be very poor in all things. If these factors are mediocre between strength and weakness, the native’s riches will be of the same sort. Thus, you should judge the quantity of the native's riches from the power or weakness of the governor and from the accorded or discordant testimony of the luminaries.

### ¶ Furthermore, Saturn signifies that the native's riches will come from buildings, or from the cultivation of lands, or from navigation.

### ¶ Know that Saturn signifies that the native's riches will be from the yield of the lands, either through the labor of the earth or through maritime affairs.

Because Saturn is taken in place of the Sun in locations where the Sun has no significance. No matter of riches pertains to the Sun in this place, yet the Sun signifies the marriage of women. They hold Saturn in place of the Sun in the significance of riches for the labor of the earth. And similarly, it signifies regarding large waters, giving great riches through maritime affairs. When we find Saturn as the sole governor of the Part of Fortune, you should inspect if it is semi-audible or if it aspects itself with Venus; and then we shall judge

<column-break/>

that the native's riches will be through women. And if we find it in an earthly sign, we will judge that the riches will be through labor on the lands. And if we find it in a watery sign, we will judge that the riches will be through water or through seafaring. In this way, we will know and distinguish each state we find in the distribution of a single nature.

### ¶ Jupiter truly signifies that his riches will be gathered from commendations, or from a stewardship <note original="baiula">A position of care or guardianship</note>, or from any sort of integrity.

### ¶ And if Jupiter signifies, the riches will be through a seneschalship <note>The office of a steward or major-domo</note> or through gifts of honors and of religious men.

He means to say that when Jupiter is the governor of the Part of Fortune, it signifies that the native's riches will be through a seneschalship or through faithfulness, or through a judgeship <note original="alcaldia">From the Arabic 'al-qadi,' meaning a judge or local magistrate</note>. You can know each of these good states from the things connected to them according to the state in which we find Jupiter.

### ¶ Mars, however, signifies that his riches come from the command of armies and from leadership.

### ¶ And Mars signifies that the riches will be for leading soldiers or governing men-at-arms.

### ¶ If Mars is the lord of the Part of Fortune, it signifies that the native's riches will be for governing or leading armies.

And if it is less powerful, they will be for a minor leadership; and if it is in a sign of the fortunes <note>Signs belonging to Jupiter or Venus</note> or in any of its own dignities, they will be for governing men and things similar to this.

### ¶ Venus denotes that they are gathered from the gifts of friends or from women.

### ¶ And Venus signifies that the riches will be from the gifts of friends or women.

### ¶ If Venus is the governess in this matter and has an aspect of friendship with the lord of the Ascendant or with any governor of the native, it signifies that the riches will be from friends. And if this aspect is with some significator of the native's women, it signifies that his riches will be through women. It is necessary that you inspect each of these states and in what state we find the governing planet, and according to this, we shall judge.

### ¶ Mercury signifies that riches will flow from the industry of trade.

### ¶ And Mercury signifies that the riches will be for sciences and merchandise.

Because Mercury, by its own nature, signifies the state of the rational soul, it holds the significance of the sciences; and because it always revolves around the Sun, it signifies things similar to this, and things that revolve in trade. Later, if it is the governor of the Part of Fortune, inspect it: if it is in the place of sciences, it will signify that riches will be from that side. And if you wish to know for which science the riches will be, inspect in what state Mercury is and the lord of its place. And if it is in the place of journeys or of revolving for profit, it will signify that the riches will be from trade; and you can know what kind of merchandise when you have inspected everything we have said.

### ¶ If Saturn specifically shares in the nature of the place and is associated with Jupiter in figure, it will signify inheritances that he will inherit.

Especially when it is in the high angles, or if Jupiter is in a common sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, or if it has an aspect with the Moon; for then it signifies that the native will profit and will inherit the inheritance of strangers.

### ¶ And if Saturn specifically has significance with the fortune of riches and accords with Jupiter, it will signify the goods of the dead which he will inherit. And this is especially so if it is in the superior angles, or if Jupiter is in a sign of two bodies <note>Another term for a common or mutable sign</note>, or similarly has an aspect with the Moon; and then it will signify that he will inherit the goods of foreigners.

# Fourth [Book]

¶ After he <note>Referring to Ptolemy</note> has given us the nature of the planets separately, each on its own, he now wishes to give us a general rule for when they have a participation with one another in the governance of the place of the Part of Fortune. He has only named the participation of Saturn and Jupiter so that we might take from them an example for all other participations he presents. Whoever has understood his book from the beginning to this point will be able to understand for themselves all the participations occurring between other planets. For what he has established regarding this single participation is sufficient. It suffices for us to see three participations between Saturn and Jupiter which signify a general thing: that we may take from it the indication for all other participations. This will be the indication of three participations by which those born will be wealthy through the goods of the dead <note original="bonorum mortuorum">This refers to inheritances or legacies left by the deceased</note>, which happens after Saturn participates with Jupiter in governing the Part of Fortune; or if Venus is the governor and has an aspect with another; or if she is the governor of her own place, and similar configurations.

The second rule is that if this participation is in the "angles" <note>The most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note> that are above the earth, and especially in the Midheaven <note original="medio celi">The highest point of the southern sky in a horoscope, representing career and public status</note>, it will be an indication of lasting wealth and greater strength. 

The third is that Jupiter be in a <term>bicorporeal sign</term> <note>Also known as dual signs, these are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note> or that he aspects the Moon. The reason why the participation of Jupiter with Saturn signifies wealth from the goods of the dead is this: Saturn gives misfortune and Jupiter gives fortune. Now, this is a good thing granted by the dead, because misfortune gives that which dies, and fortune gives that which is inherited from their property. Similarly, regarding existence in a bicorporeal sign and for aspecting the Moon: as has been said, this signifies foreign men from a strange land; as for one whose son is born of a foreign woman through whom he shall have an inheritance, because a bicorporeal sign signifies the participation of two things, and the aspect of the Moon does the same.

Ptolemy has established these things for us so that they may be "roots" from which we take examples in other planets when one has a participation with another. And if you have understood whatever we have said, you will be able to know well all participations and what each of these signifies. This is the rule: observe what participation the planet has, with which planet it is joined, and what that planet signifies in the character of the native and in their <term>mastery</term> <note original="magistery">Refers to the person's profession, trade, or craft</note>, and you shall judge according to this. For example: if Saturn participates with Mars and has some indication in the character of the native that he is a robber, and it is in his profession that he is a soldier, you shall judge that his wealth will come from plunder or from ambushes on journeys and such. But if it has an indication in the native's character that he is upright and just, and in his profession he cares for the sick, and if the governors of the Part of Fortune are Saturn and Mars, you shall judge that his riches will be because he is a surgeon or from healing wounds and the like. It is manifest that you can know all these things when you have inspected all the states of the planets in what they signify of character and justice. When you wish to judge this matter, it is necessary that you look well at all we have said up to this point in this book, and in that which follows.

¶ Indeed, those stars that are of the <term>domain</term> <note original="haiz / hayyiz">A technical term in medieval astrology meaning a planet is in its preferred 'sect' or 'half' of the sky based on its gender and the time of day</note> of those stars having a disposition with them, will testify that the native's disposition is fit to remain and be saved. But if the stars that are contrary to those domains come upon the primary places or follow them, they will condemn the person to the loss of substance.

¶ And besides those which are of the domain of these planets, the governors of the Part of Fortune will testify to them: those riches will be durable and guarded, nor will they be changed. And if the planets that are of the opposite domain are elevated above the principal places that follow them—meaning where they go—it signifies the loss of riches.

¶ The testimonies of the planets do not have power unless they are in conjunction, opposition, or a <term>square aspect</term> <note original="4.' / quadratum">An aspect of 90 degrees, often considered challenging or intense</note>. Generally, those of the same sect are harmful with any aspect. We have already shown the principal places in the chapter on life, and he said they are four: the place of the Sun, the place of the Moon, the Ascendant, and the place of the Part of Fortune. And it is necessary that you always order and place the one having the greatest power first, as we have said in many places. You can judge all of this well by looking specifically at the first chapter and at what we said in other chapters about the method, provided you understand it well.

¶ Universally, the time in which this shall happen is understood from the aspects of the stars 

<column-break/>

that are to be the occasion, toward the angles or to the places ascending toward the angles.

¶ And generally, the time in which it will happen can be known from the state of the planets doing this in the angles and in the places ascending to the angles.

¶ He <note>Haly</note> wishes to say that we can know the time in which the native will have riches, and the hour in which they will be lost (if they are meant to be lost), from the quantity of the sharpness of power of the planets causing each of these things; we have already glossed this in the previous treatise. # Treatise

From their strength <note>Referring to the planets and luminaries</note>: for if the Sun should be in the tenth house <note>The Midheaven, representing career and public authority</note> in a masculine sign, and all the planets everywhere around it gaze upon it, it must be said that the one born will be wondrous and powerful. But when you find such a figure, it is not necessary for you to ask from what place he proceeds <note>meaning his social origin</note>, but only whether he shall live; he will have sense in the nativities <note>horoscopes</note> of the sons of kings. It happens that you should look to the significator of the kingdom, the people, and the father, and judge in any of these according to the harmony or discord they hold. And when you find this figure of which **Ptolemy** spoke, and you find that the life of the newborn can be completed <note>meaning they will survive to adulthood</note>, and you find him to have such a strength of heart and harmony with it, you shall judge that the one born will be a king, even if he be the son of a merchant or a servant. And so it happens that you may understand, for the matter is manifest. For we have already found many merchants and servants who were kings in many lands, though they were accustomed to be lowly and slaves, or weak merchants. And it happens that you should know that if any of the fixed stars agree with such a figure, such that they are with the two luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note> upon one circle, the power of the newborn will be very great; and it will be swifter and stronger if those fixed stars are in their <term>hayyiz</term> <note original="baiz">From the Arabic 'hayyiz,' referring to a planet being in its preferred astronomical sector or 'favorable condition.'</note> creating good fortune.

But if the stars that surround them are likewise in the angles, or if they have a fellowship in the figure with the angles existing above the earth, the one born will be of great health, most powerful, and a **king of the world**.

Similarly, if the planets surrounding them are in the angles, and have participation in the figure with the angle that is above the earth <note>The Midheaven or Ascendant</note>, the one born will be very wondrous, of great deeds and great power: and a very powerful king in all the earth.

He <note>Ptolemy</note> means to say that the planets and fixed stars surrounding the Sun or Moon—or that one among them which is the Lord of the *hayyiz*—if they are in the angles or have participation with the tenth house in the figure, it will signify a reign. You shall judge that the newborn will be of great power and great deeds in his kingdom, and he shall rule in the greater part of the habitable earth, or in a very large part of it.

His fortune will also be increased when the surrounding stars are to the right <note original="dextre">In astrology, aspects to the right (dexter) are considered more powerful than those to the left (sinister)</note> and are associated with the angles existing above the earth.

And he will increase greatly in his fortune when the planets surrounding the stars have participation in the figure with the angles which are above the earth.

He means to say that when the figure of the planets in any nativity signifies a reign in the angles, that person will increase in fortune in his reign and power. And if the planets and fixed stars surrounding the luminaries are well-empowered—because those to the right have greater power than those to the left, as we have shown—if such powers exist and harmonize with the Ascendant and the tenth house, the one born will be of the greatest power and fortune.

However, when the qualities of the other stars are like this quality, and only the Sun revolves in a masculine sign, but the Moon is in a feminine sign, and one of them is in the angles: the one born will be a leader of a single government and one who executes <note original="interfector">Literally 'killer' or 'slayer,' but here likely referring to the power of life and death or judicial execution</note>.

And if the state of the five planets is in this way, and the Sun is in a masculine sign alone and the Moon in a feminine, and one of them is in an angle: the one born will only be a **governor of the people**, having the power to administer justice and to imprison.

For all the planets will have signified that the newborn will be a king, but they diminish it only because the Sun is in a masculine sign and the Moon in a feminine, and one of them is in an angle and the other is not; such a figure, diminished in proportion, signifies that the newborn will not expand so as to be a king, but only to be a powerful governor for administering justice over many, for killing, and for imprisoning; and **Ptolemy** said similarly that the newborn need not be from a place where such a thing is expected. For I have seen many who were from very lowly servants and they reached this state. And I saw one who was a sergeant <note original="sargetus">An official or officer</note> of a certain village of servants, and his deeds and honor grew un-

For such a fortune as this is the fortune of **vicars, kings, and dukes**, governors of armies; and you will understand if the newborn will be a vicar to a king, or a leader of armies, giving himself wealth in his nativity through the service he will perform. **O**ne’s work and mastery <note>meaning their professional skill or craft</note> are distinguished in two ways: namely, by the Sun and by the sign in the **Midheaven** <note original="medium coeli">the highest point in the sky at the moment of birth, representing career and public life</note>.

<margin>Ptolemy</margin>
He said in this place that for the fortune and service—the state and strength of the service of the person born and their office—it can be known from two things: the Sun and Moon; and the other from the sign existing in the Midheaven. This is because the Sun is more powerful and of greater lordship than the other planets, and the **Tenth House** <note original="decima domus">another term for the Midheaven, governing status and profession</note> is similarly powerful compared to the other houses. And the "service" of a man is the thing with which his fortune lasts, and with which he can obtain other things and profit. It follows that the performance of his office is held according to how he profits from the Sun and the Tenth House—such power with which he may have his nature, so that his works may be more powerful, of greater strength, and more complete.

¶ We must observe the star that, having emerged from under the Sun's rays, appears slightly in the morning, and the one which is in the Midheaven—especially if it has an "application" <note original="ictisal">an Arabic-derived astrological term for the Moon moving toward an aspect with another planet</note> with the Moon.

¶ It is appropriate for us to look at the planet that appears in the morning above the Sun near it, and the one that will be in the Midheaven, and especially if it has an "aspect" <note>a specific geometric relationship or "view"</note> with the Moon.

¶ The **matutinal** <note>morning-rising</note> planet, which is most near the Sun, is the one that rises shortly before it and has greater power from the Sun than the others; similarly, a planet existing in the Tenth House has greater power than others existing in other "angles" <note>the four primary points of the chart: East, West, Zenith, and Nadir</note>. And if it has a participation with the Moon, its power will be greater and of greater lordship.

All that **Ptolemy** <note>original: "Pto."; Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century astronomer whose "Tetrabiblos" is the foundation of this text</note> taught us regarding the action of **Mercury** and **Venus** is that which each of them signifies of its own proper nature, and that which they signify when they participate with **Saturn** or **Jupiter**. # Treatise

...just as laborers are used in agriculture, so it is in the comparison of the wisdom of agriculture: like a physician and an astronomer who go boldly from village to village in comparison to wise physicians and wise astronomers. Aristotle and all those of his sect taught us that the ministries <note>original: "ministeria"; here meaning occupations, services, or branches of knowledge</note> are of four kinds. The first is **Theoretical**, which is to know only, and this is **Philosophy**. The second is **Practical**, and this is how a man is able to know the habits of the soul: how he ought to direct and govern cities and maintain a household. The third is that which completes the works of nature, such as **Physics** <note>In this context, "Physics" refers to natural science or medicine</note> and **Agriculture**. And the fourth is that which directs and prepares, such as the building of houses and habitations, and masonry, and carpentry, and weaving, and other similar ministries. And these they taught us: that one of these good ministries is ordered under another, and one serves the others. Just as the armorer and the bridle-maker serve the soldier, and the soldier serves the leader of the army, and the leader of the army serves the office of the King, and this is to govern cities. And so these offices go upward until all are ordered under **Philosophy**. And because of this, he divided the ministries into four parts. The first is the whole ministry that follows great and proper Philosophy, and this is the Practice we spoke of, which is for the sake of the wisdom that men have need of; and the signs signifying such things are those having figures similar to the figures of humans <note>The "human" signs of the zodiac: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius</note>. ¶ And the signs having the figures of quadrupeds help in the ministries which are the works of metals, and commerce, and carpentry.

¶ This is the third part of the offices: and it is every thing that gives a root for another thing, and it is according to philosophy. ¶ This is the fourth part of the offices: and it is every thing in which there is moisture and

herbs, or working in water, such as a fisherman or a sailor, and working on shipping, making waters flow, dealing with fish and salt, curing meats and fish, selling legumes, and such things.

¶ And if the **Moon** shall be the mistress of the place of mastery, and after its conjunction it goes toward **Mercury**, and it is in **Capricorn**, **Taurus**, or **Cancer**, the native will be wise and an observer of water vessels.

¶ And if the **Moon** shall be the lady of the place of the office, and after its conjunction her path is with **Mercury**, and she is in **Taurus** or **Capricorn** or **Cancer**, the native will be a diviner, a maker of sacrifices, and will look into vessels of water <note>original: "inspiciet in vasis aquarum"; referring to lecanomancy, a form of scrying using water in a basin</note>.

¶ We have said many times that the **Sun** and the **Moon** are princes over the other planets, and their significance is general in all things that happen by nature. Because of this, they provide the preparation in all ministries, and every other ministry receives from them. After it is clear that neither the Sun nor the Moon has a specific significance in a known ministry, they provide cause and help in some ministries and not in others. For the Sun gives help in every ministry that is for power and conquering and for the appearance of rank. And **Ptolemy** taught us this, saying that if it participates with **Mars**, it becomes a single composition which will give every work that is done by fire. Thus we understand that the composition which is made through the Sun and Moon, through any of the others, gives such a ministry as is suitable to that same composition. However, he taught us in this place that the Moon gives help in ministries in which there is **divination**; and he made mention of this in the concordance which she has with Mercury in any of the signs. And we wish to gloss his words so that we may make understood that which was shown before. When he said that it should be the lord of the office, he means to say that the lord shall be the **Tenth House** <note>the astrological house of career and public life</note>, when it is a planet appearing from under the rays of the Sun. And this is what he said: and its path was after the conjunction with Mercury. He said Mercury especially among all planets because here wisdom is found more in Mercury. And that which he said, that these things happen in **Taurus**, or in **Capricorn** or **Cancer**: he said that **Venus** and the signs rule these, and the Moon has proper dignities in these signs. Divinations are proper to the significance of Taurus by reason of the nature of Venus and the Moon; and the nature of sacrifice <note>original: "degulationis"; likely a slaughter or sacrifice</note> is proper to Capricorn by reason of **Saturn** and **Mars**. Looking into the reflections of water is proper to Cancer because it is a sign of water; and the Fortunes <note>the beneficial planets Jupiter and Venus</note> have their dignities there. From water are the vessels in which it is placed, and many things are seen in them; and from these are many who look into clouds, rivers, and wells, and elsewhere. And we have already shown that these offices for the most part are **prohibited**, because universal poisonings happened; laws were given which forbid looking into all these things, but rather command the contrary of them.

¶ But if it shall be in **Sagittarius** or in **Pisces**, he will divine by the dead; and he will also compel evil spirits to be moved from place to place.

¶ And if it shall be in **Sagittarius** or **Pisces**, he is called a diviner by looking into the dead and by moving spirits.

¶ He means to say that when the Moon is the mistress of the office, and Mercury is near the conjunction: if it happens that it is in **Sagittarius** or **Pisces**, it signifies that the native will look into the members of dead animals and will say many future things. Similarly, he will move the spirits which are called devils, or other spirits, because of which he will divine. And this is because Sagittarius and Pisces are the dignities of **Jupiter**, and Mercury is poorly placed in these locations, because they are its "fall" and opposite to its own houses. Because of this, it happens that when it is mixed with the Moon and Mercury, they have such a significance.

¶ But if it shall be in **Virgo** or **Scorpio**, he will be a **necromancer** and an **astrologer**; he will judge hidden things and predict future things.

¶ And if it shall be in **Virgo** or **Scorpio**, he will be a necromancer and an astronomer, saying things that are not just and future things before they happen.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of astrological influences on one's career and social status, specifically focusing on the combinations of Mercury and the Moon in various zodiac signs and how the "Fortunes" or "Infortunes" (benefic or malefic planets) determine success or failure in a profession.</meta>

# Fourth Book

¶ It means to say that if the Moon is the Lady of the Office <note>original: "dña officij"; the planet ruling over one's career or vocation</note> and Mercury is near a conjunction, receiving power from the Sun while being in Virgo or Scorpio: the person born will be a necromancer <note>original: "nigromāticus"; in this context, someone who practices ritual magic or works with spirits</note> and an astronomical diviner of unjust things; they will know things before they happen. For a necromancer is one who performs enchantments, charms, or evil deeds so that people believe they will certainly happen, just as the practitioners themselves believe. And an astronomer is one who knows future things through the figures of the stars. And a diviner is one in whose will things come; they say things that are not apparent and which are in the future, yet they do not know from what part they say them nor by what reason they draw them out. For it is manifest that in the soul of such a person, things come from the significations of the celestial bodies, and they cause them to come into the world at some future time; and at a certain hour, the same figure of the stars forms such a thing. At this hour, that future thing is formed in the will of that diviner. And I have seen many such people; I saw one who said: "When I am sick, I shall die on such a day," and afterwards he groaned, but it was exactly as he said.

¶ And if the planet is in Leo, Aries, or Libra: they will be a prophet and an interpreter of dreams, and a wise man.

¶ And if it is in Libra, Aries, or Leo, they will be a prophet, a solver of dreams, and an enchanter.

¶ It means to say when the Moon is the Lady of the Office and is with Mercury near a conjunction, and it happens to be in Libra, Aries, or Leo: the person born will be a prophet if Venus testifies to it while in a good state; but in a bad state, they will be a solver of dreams. And if Jupiter testifies, they will be an enchanter. And he mentioned Libra because of the dignities <note>In astrology, "dignity" refers to the strength a planet gains by being in a specific sign</note> which Saturn, Mercury, and Venus have in it; and Aries and Leo because of the dignities which the Sun and Jupiter have in them, for they have their triplicity <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> in them. Of all the signs, Gemini and Aquarius remained, which he did not name because the signification of the Moon is lost in them, and only those of Mercury are strengthened there, where Jupiter and Venus have no dignity that holds power.

¶ This, therefore, is the way in which we should observe how to reasonably know the qualities of the masteries <note>professions or skills</note> and their types.

¶ This is the path through which we must go so that we may know the status of offices and of what manner they will be by way of demonstration.

¶ That which he said—"this is the path we must go"—means a well-certained demonstrative way by which we can know what kind of human office the person born will hold.

¶ Furthermore, the quantities of those powers are to be observed through the strengths of the stars that show the disposition. For when they are oriental <note>rising in the east before the sun</note> or are in the angles <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a birth chart, considered the most powerful positions</note>, their masteries will be of dignity, dominance, and strength. But if they are occidental <note>setting in the west</note> or falling from the angles <note>known as "cadent" houses, where planetary influence is thought to be weaker</note>, their masteries will be placed under the power of others.

¶ Then it is fitting that they inspect the quantity of their power through the power of the governing planets; for when they are oriental or in the angles, the office will be principal and powerful, and they will have others under them. And if they are occidental or falling from the angles, their office will be under the hand of another.

¶ It means to say: when we know of what manner the status of the office will be, and we wish to know if that official will be a principal in their own right or under the hand of another, we shall look at the planet and the planets which are Lords of the Office. If they are powerful in their position in the world, they will signify that the position of the person born will be principal in their ministry. And we have already shown in the gloss of the first treatise that the good status of planets in their position in the world is that they be in their dignities, or oriental, or in the angles, and similar things. And likewise, if the Lord of the Office is powerful in the birth chart, it signifies similarly that the person born will be principal in their office. However, if the Lord of the Office is weak in both ways we mentioned, the official will be under the hand of another. As for what Ptolemy said regarding "oriental," he said it because of power according to the world. And what he said regarding "in the angles" is because of power according to the birth chart. And when they are occidental, they are perverse and not in the angles.

<column-break/>

¶ But if the Fortunes <note>benefic planets, usually Jupiter and Venus</note> prevail over them, that person's mastery will be suitable, commendable, and quiet, nor will they be deceived in them. But if the Infortunes <note>malefic planets, usually Saturn and Mars</note> prevail over them, they will be base, despicable, and harmful, and the person will be deceived in them.

¶ And if the Fortunes prevail in the ministry, the ministry will be noble and lucrative, and the official will not fail in it; but if the Infortunes prevail, it will be base and losing, and the official will not profit in it.

¶ He always gives us these contrary states in every place so that we may understand the middle ground through them. For he says in this place: if the Lord of the Ministry is in aspect with the Fortunes, or in its own dignities, or of healthy power, the ministry of the native will be noble and lucrative. And if the Infortunes dominate in it, or are in their dignities, or their powers are intent or hindered, it signifies that the ministry of the native will be base and pernicious, and the official will fail in it. And we have understood well through these other things that if the Lord of the Ministry is in a mediocre state between these two, the ministry will be mediocre.

¶ And if Saturn is among the hinderers, coldness, delay, and laziness will happen there.

¶ And if Saturn is the hinderer, elongation and slowness will happen in the ministry.

¶ He means to say that if Saturn is harming the Lord of the Ministry, or the Lord of the Ministry is of Saturn's nature, the native will be lazy and slow, to the extent that their office becomes base; they will lose and fail in the same.

¶ If Mars, however, is among the hinderers, fear and destruction will occur there.

¶ And if Mars is the hinderer, danger and a bad reputation will happen in the ministry.

¶ It means to say that if Mars is harming the Lord of the Ministry, or the Lord itself is of Mars's nature, the native will be as greedy as they are daring. And they will be so without shame in their office that they will put themselves in great danger for it, in such a way that they lose in it; it will become base and they will fail in it.

¶ And if both are among the hinderers, there will be many inconveniences throughout the entire time of their life.

¶ And if both are harming, all these things will be very bad for their whole life.

¶ It means to say that if the two Infortunes harm the Lord of the Ministry, they signify that the native will never, in their whole life, go to a lord for ministry. And it is manifest that Ptolemy amended in this place what the two Infortunes signify regarding the damage to the Lord of the Ministry, so that we might understand what the two Fortunes signify when they help the Lord of the Ministry. For if Jupiter joins, the ministry will be noble and lucrative, and they will not fail in it because of the good and the fortune—the "good" that Jupiter gives. Likewise, if Venus joins, the official will be fortunate in their office: lucrative and joyful. And because Ptolemy holds in many places that Venus accords with Jupiter in her nature, he gives them one signification in this place: that they make the ministry noble and lucrative; and he made no division between the two of them.

¶ Moreover, their increase and decrease should be understood from the qualities of the stars which are the causes, according to their habit toward the angles, whether they are morning stars or evening stars.

¶ And we shall also know the increase and decrease from the state of the planets making those things: how they stand toward the morning angles and the evening angles.

¶ He means to say that when we wish to know when ministries will increase, or decrease, or weaken, we shall look at what signifies the distance of the planets from the angles that are most near to them.

**Treatise**

We shall take from this a comparison regarding the sharpness of planets that are morning stars, and the slowness when they are evening stars; and we shall evaluate this alongside what signifies life, and with what the planets signify in all the years of life. We shall know all these things: at what times they are strengthened and their service increases, or at what times they will be diminished and weakened.

¶ Here is completed everything that Ptolemy composed regarding the particular matters pertaining to man.

¶ Here begins the eleventh treatise of Haly’s commentary on the book of Ptolemy. Haly said: we wish to gloss that which remains of Ptolemy’s words from his book of judgments <note>This refers to Ptolemy’s *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text of Western astrology</note>.

### ¶ On Marriages. Chapter 4.

->Haly said:<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial A with floral motifs.</image-desc>The components of which a household is composed are four, as Boethius <note>An influential 6th-century philosopher</note> shows: first is riches; second is a wife; third is children; and fourth is servants. Indeed, Ptolemy has already recounted the matter of riches in the four preceding chapters. He still intends to show more in the sixth chapter concerning funerals; however, he could not separate those chapters as he did for other things. Nevertheless, he made mention of the love or hatred one has toward two masters at the end of the chapter on friends. This is because he holds that servants are not things that stand on their own with a man, but are things that belong to and pertain to a man's riches. For the servants of a man possessing riches—and the place they occupy—are counted among his riches. According to the status of those riches, such will be the servants, and from that same place <note>The "place" refers to the specific house or section of the astrological chart</note> their condition can be known. The same applies to the condition of beasts and inheritances. Wives, however, and children are "natural" to men and are those who stand with him; because of this, he gives each of them their own separate chapter.

<image-desc>Decorative initial Q with floral motifs.</image-desc>Since, after the aforementioned things, we must treat marriage, it is fitting for us to observe the legitimate marriage of men and women in the following manner.

¶ And after the judgment of the spouse follows another thing we have said: it is fitting that we look further into the marriage of women and men in this way which I wish to describe.

¶ He means to say that the judgment of one’s office <note>career or social role</note> follows the judgment of marriage, and the judgment of riches follows the virtue of the man’s soul, as does the marriage of women. He means the marriage occurring between people according to their laws, which is neither shameful nor considered evil, such as the marriage of an old woman or a youth for the purpose of producing children.

¶ In the marriages of males, therefore, it is not improper for us to closely inspect the lunar qualities at the hour of the man’s birth.

¶ For it must be observed with the highest care: if the Moon remains in either of the two oriental quarters <note>The quarters of the zodiac from the Ascendant to the Midheaven, or from the Descendant to the Bottom of the Sky</note>, then he will make a marriage in his youth, or after the fullness of his years he will take a young girl as a wife. But if she is in either of the two occidental quarters, he will marry late, or he will join himself to an old woman.

¶ It is fitting that we inspect the state of the Moon at the hour of a man’s birth for his marriage, so that we first look to see if the Moon is in the two oriental quarters; if so, the man’s marriage will be in his childhood, or he will be coupled with a girl after he has entered into his days. And if it is in the two occidental quarters, the marriage will be late or a coupling with an old woman.

¶ He means that the rule by which we know the man’s fate is taken from the state in which the Moon is found at the hour of birth. And he gave us two of the Moon’s states by comparing her to the world and to the birth, and he brought it all together. And he said: if she is in the two oriental quarters, the man will be coupled in his childhood with whomever happens to him, or he will be coupled with a girl after he has aged. And if she is in the two occidental quarters, the man will be coupled with an old woman in his youth, or his marriage will be delayed until he is well along in days, and afterward he will be coupled with whomever happens to him, whether 

<column-break/>

old woman or girl. For it is manifest that the two oriental quarters according to the world are those from the hour of conjunction <note>New Moon</note> until the opposition <note>Full Moon</note>; and the occidental ones are the opposite, namely from the opposition to the conjunction. Or they are such according to the figure <note>the birth chart</note>: from the Ascendant to the Midheaven, and from the angle of the earth <note>Imum Coeli</note> to the seventh house. The other two accidental quarters according to the birth are the two cadent quarters: one quarter is the 7th, 8th, and 9th houses; and the other is the Ascendant, 2nd, and 3rd houses. And since the Moon signifies the marriage of a man, what Ptolemy said—when she is in any of these two states—must signify the joining of men according to all other states. And Ptolemy teaches us this matter in his other sayings.

¶ But if she is "under the rays" <note>Too close to the Sun to be seen, a condition called combustion which weakens the planet</note> and has a partnership in the chart with Saturn, he will never marry.

¶ And if she is under the rays and shares a configuration with Saturn, he will never be coupled.

¶ We already know that planets lose their power when they are under the rays, and that Saturn gives coldness and slowness in matters. And because of this, if the Moon is under the rays, or shared with Saturn in the chart, or is in his dignities <note>In a zodiac sign ruled by Saturn, like Capricorn or Aquarius</note>, it signifies that the man born will never be coupled.

¶ After this, however, we shall observe: if the Moon is in a sign of a single figure <note>A zodiac sign represented by one body, like Leo or Aries</note>, or if she has an <term>ictisal</term> <note>original: "ictisal"; an Arabic astrological term for the "application" or coming together of two planets</note> with only one planet, he will be coupled to only one.

¶ And after this we shall inspect if the Moon is in a sign of one figure, and if she applies to one planet; for if it is so, he will be coupled to only one woman.

¶ This is another of the Moon’s states: after the man has the signification of being coupled, and the Moon is in a sign of a single figure and applies to only one planet while she lasts in that sign, it signifies that the man will be coupled with one woman only.

¶ But if she remains in a sign of two bodies <note>A "bicorporeal" or double-bodied sign like Gemini or Pisces</note> or of many figures, and in that same sign she has an <term>ictisal</term> with more than one planet, he will be betrothed to several.

¶ And if she is in a bicorporeal sign or in a sign of many figures, and in that same sign she applies to more than one planet, he will have many marriages.

¶ This is another state of the Moon: if a man has the signification of coupling, and the Moon at the hour of birth is in a bicorporeal sign or a sign of many figures and applies to more than one planet while she remains in that sign, he will be coupled many times. The number of women can be known from the number of figures in the sign where the Moon stands, and from the number of stars of the figures with which the Moon is joined in that sign, in both longitude and latitude.

¶ But if the planets with which she has an <term>ictisal</term> through conjunction or aspect are "Fortunes" <note>Benefic planets, namely Jupiter and Venus</note>, his spouses will be suitable and fit. But if they are "Infortunes" <note>Malefic planets, namely Mars and Saturn</note>, they will be the opposite.

¶ And if the planets she applies to are Fortunes, whether through joining or any application, the women he is coupled with will be good and chaste; and conversely if they are Infortunes.

¶ There is no other rule by which we can know if the women a man couples with will be good and chaste or evil. Ptolemy taught us these two states, as he was accustomed to do, so that the signification of good women is from the Fortune planets and their locations, and the signification of bad women is from the Infortune planets and their locations. Because of this, we understand well that if the Moon is in the dignities of the Fortunes, they will be better; if in the dignities of the Infortunes, they will be worse. And if the matter is mixed, it will be according to that mixture. Ptolemy teaches us after this the same thing: what each planet signifies by itself, so that you know how to combine the significations if you find them mixed.

¶ For if she has an <term>ictisal</term> with Saturn, his wife will be hardworking, and her qualities will be harsh.

# Fourth [Chapter]

¶ Thus, if the Moon applies <note>In astrology, "applies" refers to a planet moving toward a significant geometric relationship, or aspect, with another</note> to **Saturn**: know that the woman will be hardworking and wicked.
¶ This is what **Saturn** signifies if the Moon applies to him: if he is in his own dignities <note>Dignities are positions in the zodiac where a planet is particularly strong or "at home"</note> and in a good state; but if he is in a bad state, it signifies that the woman will be vile, ugly, and ill-willed.
¶ If, however, she has an encounter with **Jupiter**: she will be suitable, fit, and of a learned disposition.
¶ And if the Moon applies to **Jupiter**: she will be of good restraint and good order, and a keeper of her house.
¶ And if to **Mars**: she will be spirited and untamable.
¶ And if it applies to **Mars**: she will be bold and proud.
¶ This same planet, if it is in a bad state, signifies she will be a disgraced and wicked harlot.
¶ And if to **Venus**: she will be very beautiful and playful.
¶ And if it applies to **Venus**: she will be lovely, joyful, and of a welcoming nature.
¶ And if it is in a bad state, these qualities will be diminished.
¶ But if to **Mercury**: she will be of good intellect.
¶ And if it applies to **Mercury**: she will be good, intelligent, and a woman of fine words.
¶ And if it is in a bad state, these qualities will be diminished, and she will be deceptive and false. And the rule comes to this: you should treat the applications of the Moon just as you do others for the *Hyleg* <note term="Hyleg">The "Hyleg" or "Giver of Life" is a specific point in a birth chart used to determine longevity and vital force</note>. When we find that the Moon applies to the rays of any planet, or to any fixed star, the nature of the woman to whom one is joined in that year will be according to that planet. And if you wish to know if the woman will be a free woman or a servant, look to the planet signifying marriage: when it is in its own dignities, the woman will be free; and if it is in the dignities of another planet, she will be a servant.
¶ Likewise, if **Venus** stands with **Jupiter**, **Saturn**, or **Mercury**: it will benefit her sufficiently in those things pertaining to life. She will also greatly love her husband and children. But if she is with **Mars**, she will be destructive, unstable, and lacking in understanding.
¶ Similarly, if **Venus** is with **Jupiter**, **Saturn**, or **Mercury**: she will be a successful woman, a lover of her husband and her children. And if she is with **Mars**: she will be a woman who destroys her own good, of poor completion, without virtue and without intelligence.
¶ The commentator <note>Haly Abenragel, the author of this commentary</note> means to say that the rule by which we know the state of the woman with whom a man will be joined is similarly taken from the state of **Venus**. If **Venus** is with the aforementioned planets or in her own dignities, she signifies those things described. And it follows that we should ask for what reason the Moon signifies the marriage of men, and the Sun signifies the marriage of women. I say that we have already demonstrated in previous glosses that the **Sun** and **Moon** are the princes and lords of all earthly things; and that which accords with its opposite must signify marriage. For this reason, the **Moon** signifies the marriage of men <note>original: "coniugium virorum"</note> and the **Sun** that of women. This is a matter that accords with the laws of nature.
¶ In the marriages of women, however, the solar qualities of the female birth are to be observed.
¶ And it is appropriate that we examine the marriage of women from the state of the **Sun** at the time of her birth.
¶ This means that we can judge the marriage of women from the state of the **Sun** in their nativities <note term="nativitas">A "nativity" is a birth chart or the moment of birth itself</note>. For if the **Sun** is in a good state, the marriage will be good; and if in a bad state, bad; and if in a mediocre state, it will be so. Generally speaking, whatever the status of a woman's birth chart, such will be the marriage she has.
¶ For when the **Sun** is in either of the two eastern quarters—that is, in the figure <note>the birth chart</note>—she will be betrothed to a husband in her youth, or in her old age she will take a young man for a husband.
¶ So, if the **Sun** is in the two eastern quarters: the marriage of a woman having such a nativity will be in her girlhood, or she will be joined to a boy after many days have passed.

<column-break/>

¶ Ptolemy <note>original: "Pro." for Ptolemaeus</note> notifies us of the states of the **Sun**: things which we ought to take as a rule, just as he did for the states of the **Moon**. The first state he mentions is that if the **Sun** is in the hour of birth in the two eastern quarters of the nativity: it signifies that the woman will be joined in her girlhood with whatever man happens to be for her—either a boy or an old man—or with a boy after time has passed. We have already said that the two eastern quarters according to the state of birth are the 10th, 11th, and 12th houses, and the other is the 4th, 5th, and 6th houses.
¶ But if the **Sun** is in either of the two western quarters, she will be joined to a husband late; or in her early youth she will be betrothed to an old man.
¶ And if it is in the two western quarters: she will be joined late, or with an old woman <note>Note: The text here says "vetula" (old woman), though in the context of a woman's marriage it likely refers to an old man ("vetulo"), reflecting a scribe's error or gender-fluid terminology in the source</note> after many days have passed.
¶ One of the western quarters is the Ascendant, the 2nd, and 3rd houses; the other is the 7th, 8th, and 9th houses. These two quarters are in comparison to the nativity. Because the **Sun** is of greater power and the lord of all celestial things, it is appropriate that all parts have a quarter according to the world in comparison to the **Sun**, even where the **Sun** has no part in those quarters. And you should understand this place: when it happens in the birth of a man and a woman that the **Sun** and **Moon** are in the eastern quarters, he and she will be joined in their youth, a man with a girl and a woman with a boy. And if both are in the western quarters, they will be joined in old age, a man with an old woman and a woman with an old man. And if the **Moon** in a man's birth is in any of the eastern quarters and the **Sun** in any of the western quarters: the man will be joined in his old age with one of the young girls. And if the **Moon** in a woman's birth is in any of the eastern quarters and the **Sun** in any of the western quarters: that woman will be joined to a man after many days have passed.
¶ And in this way it happened to me according to my own nativity <note>Haly adds a personal note here about his own life</note>: because the **Moon** was in the 4th western quarter, my marriage was delayed until about 30 years; and because the **Sun** was in the 4th eastern quarter, the women to whom I was joined were all young girls.
¶ But if the **Sun** is in a sign of a single form, and we find a morning planet <note term="matutinalem">A "morning star" is a planet that rises before the Sun</note> in it: she will be given to only one husband.
¶ And if it is in a sign of this figure and you find in it a morning planet: she will be joined with one husband.
¶ This means: when the **Sun** is in a woman's nativity in a sign of a single form, and she applies in that sign to one planet, that woman will never be joined to more than one husband. And as for what he said about finding a morning planet in it: he means that she will be joined with a boy. And if you find it to be an evening planet <note term="vespertinale">A planet that sets after the Sun</note>: she will be joined with a man of many days <note>an old man</note>. For example: if it happens in a man's nativity that the **Moon** joins three planets while staying in its sign—of which one is an evening star, another a morning star, and another under the Sun's rays—the one that is a morning star signifies that the man will be joined with a girl; the one that is an evening star signifies he will be joined with an old woman; and the one under the rays signifies he will never be joined. And you must understand the state of the **Sun** in the nativities of women in the same way.
¶ And if the **Sun** is in a sign of two bodies or of many forms, or if in the figure it is associated with more than one morning planet: she will have many husbands.
¶ And if it is in a sign of two bodies <note term="duorum corporum">Double-bodied signs like Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> or of many forms, or has participation with more than one morning planet in the figure: she will be joined many times.
¶ This means that when the **Sun** is in a woman's nativity in a double-bodied sign or one of many forms, or shares its sign with more than one planet: it signifies the woman will be joined many times. And because he says "from those which are morning stars," he notifies us of what I glossed in the chapter before this: that it signifies young men. And there is one more thing beyond what I glossed for you: the morning parts, which are of the Sun's power, signify a great multitude. Similarly, we understand by this that the evening parts signify in men's nativities that they will be joined many times when they are in aspect with the **Moon**.

# Treatise

Likewise, if in the chart **Saturn** is associated with the Sun: his man <note>The "man" or husband of the woman whose chart is being read.</note> will be upright, just, and hardworking.
Similarly, if he shares in **Saturn's** influence: he will be a husband of good law <note>Likely meaning principled or law-abiding.</note> and a lover of labor.
It is necessary that this participation comes from a "good aspect" <note term="aspect">A specific geometric angle between planets, like a trine (120°) or sextile (60°), believed to be harmonious.</note>; because if it comes from the contrary <note>Meaning a "hard" aspect like a square (90°) or opposition (180°).</note>, it will be harmful.
**IF** however the Sun has an association with **Jupiter**: he will be humble and magnanimous. But if with **Mars**: he will be cruel, without affection, and will not humble himself. And if with **Venus**: he will be upright and handsome. But if he is associated with **Mercury**: he will prosper in the affairs of life and be hardworking.
**AND** if there is a participation with **Jupiter**: he will be of good restraint and a noble heart. And if with **Mars**: the husband will be of strong heart, without any love, and proud. And if with **Venus**: he will be beautiful and charming. And if with **Mercury**: he will be successful in his knowledge <note>original: "sciis", likely referring to his expertise or skills.</note> and a maker of many things.
We have glossed all of this when we spoke about the Moon.
**BUT** if **Venus** is with **Saturn**: her husband will be weary <note>Perhaps meaning sluggish or lacking vitality.</note> and will refrain from sexual acts. And if she is with **Jupiter**, her husband will be good, just, and modest. And if with **Mars**: he will be of a sharp complexion <note term="complexion">In medieval medicine, this refers to the balance of bodily humors (hot, cold, moist, dry) that determines temperament.</note> and very concerned with sexual acts, and he will be a fornicator. But if she remains with **Mercury**: he will be very pious toward his own children.
**AND** if **Venus** has participation with **Saturn**: the husband will be weary and of little lust. And if with **Jupiter**: he will be good in his law and modest. And if with **Mars**: he will be of a hot complexion and supreme in lust.
All this was demonstrated in the previous glosses.
Regarding what we said above about the two "oriental quarters" <note term="oriental quarters">The sections of the sky rising in the east.</note> in the Sun, it must be understood as referring to the two quarters where one precedes the ascending point and the other the descending point of the zodiac circle. In the Moon, however, we should understand it as the two quarters between the conjunction <note>The New Moon.</note> and the prevention <note>The Full Moon.</note> until that light is at its midpoint. From the two "occidental quarters," we understand those which are opposite to the ones mentioned.
**TO** this we wish to say in this place that concerning the two oriental quarters of the Sun, they are the two forward quarters from the ascending point and from the descending point of the zodiac. And in the Moon, they are the two quarters between conjunction and opposition while it is halved in light; and the two occidental quarters are composed of the two we previously mentioned.
**CONCERNING** what someone <note>indicated by the letter "B"</note> added in the margin of Ptolemy’s book <note term="Ptolemaeus">Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the "Tetrabiblos," the foundational text for Western astrology.</note> as a gloss: the one who extracted this book put it into the text, and it has remained so ever since. For Ptolemy never used to gloss his own words in any place; rather, it was always his custom to enclose his words—as Aristotle <note term="Aristoteles">The famous Greek philosopher whose natural philosophy underpinned medieval astrology.</note> did—and cover one thing with another. And since it is so: the two oriental and two occidental quarters are in the Moon according to its position in the world, and in the Sun according to its position at the birth <note term="nativity">A birth chart or horoscope.</note>. This matter is seen as vain: that the Sun should have a status according to the birth and not the Moon. And because of this, it is understood that these words were written in the margin of Ptolemy’s book as a gloss and later placed in the text.
**WHENEVER** the luminaries <note term="luminaries">The Sun and the Moon.</note> are suitably associated with each other in both birth charts by aspect: if they look at each other from a trine or sextile, especially when this occurs through "exchange" <note>original: "tabdil", an Arabic astrological term for mutual reception where planets exchange places or dignities.</note>, and most of all when the Moon in the man’s birth chart is suitably associated with the Sun in the woman’s birth chart: their marriage shall never be dissolved.
The bond of this marriage will be even more firm and fixed if the two luminaries have participation in the chart

<column-break/>

in both birth charts with such a participation that is of concord: so that both are in trine or sextile, and especially if this happens with an exchange <note>original: "cambiamento".</note>, and even more so if the Moon in the man's birth chart has participation with the Sun in the woman's birth chart in a concordant participation.
**NOW** we know that the marriage of men is determined by the Moon in their birth charts, and women by the Sun in theirs. And the goodness or malice of the woman and man will likewise be according to the state in which **Venus** is found. And what we must show on this occasion is: that if the Sun and Moon look at each other in any birth chart by trine or sextile, it signifies that there will be love and friendship. And if it happens along with this that there is an exchange—meaning the Moon is in concord with the Sun in the man's birth chart, and similarly in the woman's birth chart, by a good aspect—and likewise if the Sun in the woman's birth chart is in concord with the Moon, and further that the Sun of her birth chart is in concord with the Moon of the man's birth chart by a good aspect. For such a constellation as this signifies great love and friendship between the man and the woman: so that their marriage shall never be separated. And after he has given us the rule of love, friendship, and the firmness of marriage, he wishes to give us the rule of disagreement and hatred.
**BY ANY** occasion it shall also be dissolved: when the aforementioned places of the luminaries are in signs that do not connect to each other, or which are diametrically opposed to one another, or if they look at each other from a square radiation <note term="tetragona">A square aspect, an angle of 90 degrees, considered a source of tension.</note>.
**AND** the marriage is destroyed and lost because of what happens when the places of the luminaries we mentioned are in discordant signs, or are in opposition or in the fourth <note>The square aspect.</note>.
**HE WISHES** to say that when the Sun and Moon in the man's or woman's birth chart are discordant with one another, or are in the fourth or opposition: this signifies to the man that he will be a bachelor <note>original: "solcero", a solitary person or one who remains single.</note> and to the woman that she will not be firm with the men to whom she is coupled. And it is manifest: that because of what we said above, when in such a state the place of the Moon in the man's birth chart has no participation with the place of the Sun in the woman's birth chart: the man himself will abhor that woman, and he will not be firm or stable in any way with her. And if the place of the Sun in the woman's birth chart is discordant with the place of the Moon in her own birth chart with such discordance—and similarly if there is discordance toward the place of the Moon in the husband's birth chart—the woman herself will abhor that husband and will not remain with him.
But if the "fortunes" <note term="fortunes">The benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus, thought to bring good luck.</note> direct their rays toward the luminaries which come together in a suitable figure: the marriage will remain in mutual affection, joy, and health. But if the "misfortunes" <note term="infortuna">The malefic planets, Saturn and Mars, thought to bring difficulty.</note> look at them, it will indeed persist, but in strife, hatred, and loss.
**AND** if the aforementioned fortunes look upon the luminaries that are in concord by participation in the figure: that marriage will remain with goodwill, love, and profit. And if the misfortunes look upon them, its perseverance will be with bitter causes, abhorrence, and ruin.
**AFTER** we know that a marriage will be firm and of friendship, we shall see if the fortunes testify to the place of the Sun and the Moon. And if it is so, that marriage will be with goodwill, love, and profit. And if they testify only to the place of the Sun: there will be goodwill and love for the woman but not the man. And if they testify only to the place of the Moon: there will be love and profit for the man but not the woman. And if the misfortunes testify, the perseverance of that marriage will be with causes, judgments, abhorrence, and ruin. And the distinction of this state will be according to the distinction of the first state. And it is manifest that when both fortunes and misfortunes testify: the matter will likewise be mixed.
**SIMILARLY** it also happens in their unsuitable qualities. For if the fortunes testify to the luminaries: the marriage will not be given up entirely, but after a separation they will be reconciled and will endure with affection.

# Treatise

Behold, inspect the increase and improvement which one [planet] has over another in the quantity of planets, or in the strength of power, or in its position in the world, or in its position at birth: as we have said many times: and we shall judge by that which prevails: and this is manifest through the preceding glosses. <note>The author is explaining how to weigh different astrological factors to see which planet "wins" the dominant influence over the subject of children.</note>

And if the aforementioned signs which give children, and the ruling stars in their own proper places, are oriental <note term="oriental">A planet is 'oriental' when it rises before the Sun, which traditionally increases its strength and active influence.</note>, the native will be powerful and of great name.

And if the planets which are lords of the signs giving children—those which we said before were oriental in their own places—the son will be noble and of great value.

**He means to say** that when any planet gives a signature in the nativity for the granting of children, and we wish to know what the general state of the children will be, we will inspect the governor of the place of those planets giving children: and we will see in what state it is: and if it be strong and oriental, the son will be noble and of great value; and if it be not so, the son will be according to that lesser state.

If they are occidental <note term="occidental">A planet is 'occidental' when it sets after the Sun, often interpreted as a more passive or weakened state.</note> or in places of their *hayz* <note term="hayz">original: "haiz". An Arabic astrological term describing a planet in a favorable position relative to its gender and the time of day (sect).</note> contrary to them, the native will be wretched and unknown. But if the hours and the Part of Fortune <note term="Part of Fortune">A calculated mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being.</note> align, the native will remain until he takes a wife and will be loved by his parents, and made their heir.

And if they are occidental or in places contrary to their *hayz*, the son will be base and of modest value. And if they are in accord with the hour and with the Part of Fortune, the son will be loved by his father and will endure until he enters into marriage and will inherit the substance of his father.

When he says "if they are in accord," he speaks for the governors of the parts of the places of other planets ruling the children. And he says this so that if these governors agree with the ascendant <note term="ascendant">The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth.</note> and the Part of Fortune, the son will live and his father will love him: he will marry and inherit his father's wealth. This accord of the planets between the ascendant and the Part of Fortune is when they behold each other by trine or sextile <note term="trine/sextile">Harmonious astrological aspects (angles) of 120 and 60 degrees respectively.</note> or when they are in their suitable *hayz*.

If they do not gather together or exist in opposition to one another, the native will be litigious and will accumulate the greatest hatred toward his parents, and will treat them badly, nor will he succeed them in inheritance.

And if they are discordant or diverse, the son will be contending with his parents and harmful to them, nor will he inherit their goods.

When the governing planets he mentioned do not accord with the ascendant, nor with the Part of Fortune in preceding harmony, or if the ascendant and Part of Fortune are at odds, the son will hate the father nor will he inherit his possessions. And thus he gave us two contrary rules, so that we might know that which is mediocre between these two extremes.

Likewise, if the planets giving children are suitably associated with one another in the figure [the chart], the brothers will love and honor one another. But if they do not gather together, or are positioned in opposition through the diameter [the 180-degree aspect], the native will be the cause and bringer of adversity to his brothers.

Similarly, if the planets giving children have participation in a harmonious figure, the brothers will love each other, and one will honor the other; and if they are discordant or opposite across the diameter, the son will abhor his brothers and seek how he might kill them.

When the planets giving children are many and they accord in harmonious participation, it signifies that they will love one another. And if they behold each other with a bad aspect, it signifies the opposite.

The particular matters of the children can be grasped by estimation when we place the planet giving children in the place of the ascendant. For then all the particularities of the children, 

<column-break/>

just as they are known from a nativity, we shall generally recognize.

The particular matters of the children you will be able to know through consideration when you have well inspected each of them in relation to the planet giving children, such that you place it in the location of the ascendant: and you will know the other particularities of the children generally as if through a nativity. <note>This is a technical instruction to treat the 'child-giving' planet as a new starting point (a derived ascendant) to read the children's individual fortunes.</note>

If you understood the first and second chapters and the glosses that passed, you will not need a gloss on what he said: and if you did not understand, look to these glosses and you will understand. What he wishes to show in this place is what happened in my own nativity: I inspected it and found Jupiter in the 10th house and in the 25th degree of Capricorn beholding itself with the Moon and Saturn: and this signified that I would have children, and that they would die: because Saturn was with Jupiter in the 10th house and Jupiter was in a feminine sign and the Moon similarly: it signified that more than one would come, and that they would be mostly female. And because Jupiter was oriental it signified that I would have some male: and so I had three children: one male and two daughters, and all died. The degree of the ascendant of the male's birth was around the degree of Saturn in my own nativity: and because of this he died quickly: and the degree of the ascendant of one female was in Pisces in sextile to Jupiter in my nativity: and in trine to my Moon: and the Sun was the *hyleg* <note term="hyleg">original: "byleg" (OCR error for hyleg). The planet or point that acts as the 'giver of life' or vital force in a birth chart.</note> in the sign of Capricorn: and the degree of the ascendant of the other female was in Capricorn: and this is a wonder because of this, that it can be known that nativities always accord one with another and are divided in particular things: and because of this it happens that a master has judgment both general and particular of that which nature gives more than the law. For you will hear many times people say, "My father was such a man," and "That other one came from a noble first lineage," and "That other from such and such a progeny," and similar things. And similarly, this participation is found in provinces, for every province has its own proper place in the firmament falling directly above it, which gives the people living there some participation and similarity in many things: and we have already distinguished this in the glosses of the preceding second part.

**P**rofit lies in this chapter regarding which man it is suitable to be associated with, and who is to be kept away from society because of his enmity.

The qualities of friendship and enmity, those which are more lasting, are called "friendships and enmities." Those which are less lasting are called "common applications and repulsions."

The state which is of love and hate, which is called friendship and enmity: regarding this, that which is greater and of longer time, and it is said that what is lesser and of a shorter portion of time has life in one [instance], or they quickly disagree with one another.

Ptolemy divided love in these words into two parts and disagreement into two parts: that which lasts a long time is called enmity: and that which lasts a short time is called removal [or distancing].

It is suitable to investigate in such a manner. In those qualities which we consider in greater matters: the locations which in both nativities are entirely powerful agree more. That is, it is necessary for us to observe the locations of the Sun and the Moon, and the ascendant, and the Part of Fortune.

It is suitable that we inquire in this way: and it is that if it be in great matters, we should inspect the locations having the greatest power of beginning in the two nativities: and these are the locations of the Sun and the Moon, the ascendant, and the Part of Fortune.
