# Fourth Book

¶ It is said through these words: that the judgment of friendship and enmity is taken from four principal places: the positions of the Sun, the Moon, the Ascendant, and the Part of Fortune. And if there is harmony among these in the births of friends, the love between them will be an inseparable friendship. But if there is a contrary placement in the births of enemies, or a bad aspect, the enmity will endure forever; and this is what Ptolemy <note>original: "Pto."</note> recalls.

¶ When all these things are in the same sign, or if they have exchanged places either partially or completely. Especially when the Ascendants of both people are within about seventeen degrees of each other, we shall say there will be a firm love that will neither be separated nor disturbed. But if they are in places that are not linked together, or are positioned diametrically opposite to one another, they will disagree extremely, or will be adversaries to one another for a long time.

¶ Thus, if these are in one and the same sign, or in places of unity—all or most of them, and especially if the distance between the two Ascendants is within seventeen degrees—there will be a very firm friendship between them, which will never be taken away, changed, nor destroyed. And if they are in places of discord or in places of opposition across the diameter, there will happen between them a very great enmity and a contrariety lasting for a long time.

¶ When these four principal things are in the same place in the births of two friends. For example: if the position of the Sun of one is the exact same position as the Sun of the other; and the position of the Moon of one is the same position as the other; and the Ascendant of one is the same as the Ascendant of the other. Similarly, let the Part of Fortune be in the same manner and the same place. And even if they are different but exchanged, such as if the position of the Sun of one is the position of the Moon of the other, and the position of the Moon of one is the position of the Sun of the other. And the place of the Ascendant of one is the place of the Part of Fortune of the other, and the place of the Part of Fortune is the same as the Ascendant of the other: when things are this way, the places are "mutated" (exchanged). And Ptolemy sets a limit in these matters: when they are in one sign, or when they are exchanged, the distance from one to the other should be 17 degrees or [at least] one degree, which is a fitting thing. However, all that Ptolemy said cannot be understood without such a commentary <note>original: "glosa"</note>.

¶ But if it is in neither of these ways, but only in signs that associate with each other in turn.

¶ And if they are not in any of these manners which we have spoken of, let them at least be specifically in signs having participation in the "figure" <note term="figure">The geometric relationship or aspect between signs of the zodiac.</note>.

¶ One manner is that which gives durable friendship; another is that which gives durable enmity; and this is when the places of the principal things are contrary and the signs participating in the figure are those that behold each other from the opposite, the third, the fourth, or the sixth, as we said in the first part.

¶ If they regard each other from a trine or sextile <note term="aspects">A trine is a 120-degree angle and a sextile is 60 degrees; both are considered harmonious.</note>, there will be a lesser affection between them. If, however, they see each other from a fourth <note term="square">A 90-degree angle, or "quadrate," typically indicating tension or friction.</note>, we do not doubt there will be lesser discords between them.

¶ If they have participation from a trine or sextile, the friendship will be of a minor sort; and in the fourth, the enmity will be of a minor sort.

¶ What he says about "participation," he says regarding the four principal places, which are: the Sun, the Moon, the Ascendant, and the Part of Fortune. This means they do not have participation in both births in this participation which I wish to explain. And it will be that the position of the Sun in one birth is in trine to the position of the Sun in the other birth; and similarly for all the other two; and the same for the sextile and the fourth. And those who are in the third [sign] in their births, or in sextile, have a lesser friendship than if they were in the same place or in exchanged places as said before. And those who are in the fourth in both births have a lesser enmity than if they were contrary in both births or if they did not behold each other at all; and this matter increases and decreases according to the state of the participation. And Ptolemy will show you this.

¶ So that sometimes in their love, interruptions of words

<column-break/>

will occur, and they will value each other poorly in turns. This happens when the "unfortunate" stars <note term="malefics">Planets like Saturn and Mars, which were traditionally thought to bring challenges or disruptions.</note> pass through the places of the figures. In discord, however, peace and harmony will be interposed even when the "fortunate" stars <note term="benefics">Planets like Jupiter and Venus, which were thought to bring growth and harmony.</note> run through the places of the figures.

¶ Thus, it will happen sometimes in friendship that there is a halting of words between friends; and this will be when the unfortunate planets pass through the place. And it will happen in enmity sometimes [that there is peace] when the fortunate planets pass through the place of the aspect.

¶ He means to say that when we know friendship will be weakened between friends, it will be because of the movement of the malefic planets when they pass through the places that gave the friendship; and if the friendship was firmly established, they will not be able to take it away. Similarly, when we know that enmity between enemies is weak and easily removed, and we find at some turn that the fortunate planets pass through the places of enmity, we shall judge that the enmity itself turns back into love and peace.

¶ Wherefore every mode of friendship and enmity exists in three ways. That is, that the lords of these two qualities cause this either from birth, or for the sake of profit and loss, or for the sake of anger and joy.

¶ And the manners of love and enmity are three: so that those who are in two states, for which they love one another, will do so either by the will they have toward each other, or because they will be of one counsel for the sake of profit or loss, or for the sake of pleasure in one thing or for sadness.

¶ Those who love and hate each other are of as many manners as there are things for which they love or hate. For each of them has one reason why he loves or hates; and the human things from which love and enmity come are three. The first is for the sake of the will which they have in harmony as one. The second is for the sake of profit or loss. The third is for the sake of the pleasure which one has from the other, or for the contrary; and for these reasons there are three manners of love and enmity.

¶ When all these aforementioned places, or as many as possible of them, stand by one another, friendships will be gathered from all these superior things. But if they do not agree with each other, enmities will be collected for them. And if their love or agreement—or the agreement of the highest sort—was only between the two places of the luminaries <note term="luminaries">The Sun and the Moon.</note>, it will necessarily produce that same affection which is called true and highest friendship, in which one must especially consider [the outcome]. An enmity, however, that is necessary and which can be the worst, which will never cease, will be born from there [if they are in discord].

¶ When all things or many of them are in accord, they will give love; and when they are in discord—that is, one with another—they will give enmity. And if there is harmony or contrariety between the luminaries, love, harmony, and will shall be comforted; and this is a good friendship in which a man can trust, and it is a very bad enmity that will be destroyed at no time.

¶ The places he mentions are the places of the luminaries, the Ascendant, and the Part of Fortune. And if the places of the two luminaries are in accord in two births, they will give friendship between those people through harmony and through safety <note>original: "recapto"</note>; and this is a good friendship in which one can trust, and there will be as much love as there was harmony between the two luminaries. And if the places of the luminaries are in discord or contrary, or if they do not behold each other, they will give enmity; and this enmity will be between them through discord and [lack of] safety. And such enmity is very bad, because it is never removed. And Ptolemy gave us in this saying the first manner of love and enmity.

¶ Likewise, when their agreement or its contrary is between the two places of the Part of Fortune for each party, it is from there that profit will be made; the cause of gain or loss will proceed.

¶ Similarly when there is harmony or contrariety between the places

# Treatise

The **Part of Fortune** <note>original: "ptis fortune"; a mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being</note> will indicate whether this relationship results in profit or loss.
¶ When the locations of the Part of Fortune are in agreement in two birth charts, there will be love between them for the sake of profit and wealth, or for some thing that one shall receive from the other. And when these locations are contrary or in discord in the two births, this will produce enmity and ill-will between them because of the damage that will come to one from the other, or because of some loss. This is the reason for love based on profit and enmity based on loss.
¶ And if this occurs between the two **Ascendants** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, we shall say that what is produced happens because of anger or joy.
¶ And if it is between the two Ascendants, it will be for the pleasure that one has from the other.
¶ This is manifest and requires no further explanation.
¶ It is also fitting for us to observe the modes of the places in which this fellowship of the figure exists, as well as what rises above them, and the planets that aspect them.
¶ And it happens that we look to the places where the shared portion of the figure falls, and we look to see which of them rises above those places and which planet aspects them.
¶ After he has given us three reasons for friendship and three others for enmity, he wishes to give us further information on what the status will be in each of these cases. This rule is taken from the state of the four designated places.
¶ For in those births where the planets that rise above the common places of the figure are in nearly the same sign, or in that sign which rises above it, we should assign the strength, durability, and sincerity of the friendship or enmity to those rising planets. But in births where the aspect of the planets appears fruitful and suitable, it is not improper to attribute the results of the friendship or the improvement of the enmity to the planets aspecting them.
¶ Thus, in births where the planets exalted over the shared places of the figure are in one sign or nearby, or in the sign that rises above it, the strength and firmness of the love or enmity belongs to that planet. In births where there is a good and stable aspect of the planets, the progress and goodness of the friendship or enmity is judged by those planets.
¶ He means to say that for planets that are exalted above the principal places, if it happens that they are in one sign or nearby in both births—such as when those in one person's birth are in one sign and they rise toward the sign in which the planets stand in the other person's birth—by such a constellation he teaches us to know the facts of the friendship and enmity. Thus, if they are strong, powerful, and in agreement, the friendship will be strong and powerful; likewise the enmity. If they are weak, the relationship will be similarly weak. Also, by the status of the planets aspecting the principal places in both births, if it happens in both births that they are in one sign or nearby, or if it happens that those in one person's birth are in a sign that rises toward the location of the sign where the planets of the other's birth stand, we can know by such a constellation the status of the friendship or enmity. Thus, if they are strong and well-disposed by their birth, the friendship or enmity will be strong; if they are weak, the matter will likewise be weak.
¶ Regarding the qualities of common friendship and enmity that are temporary and in some cases hourly—indeed, even momentary—one may find in each of these two births the "mode of the planets" (that is, the timing). In these times, it is not useless to observe when the **Hyleg** <note>original: "alhileg"; the point in a chart that acts as the "giver of life" or vital indicator</note>, moving away from the locations of the stars in one birth, passes through the locations of the stars in the other birth; for according to this, there will be particular friendships and enmities.
¶ And it is fitting that we speak of the fact of future association and separation at a certain time; and after it diminishes because of

<column-break/>

the movements of the planets that will be in the two births. This will occur because of the "ascensions" <note>the rising times of zodiacal signs</note> to which the Hyleg of one birth applies itself toward the location of the planets in the other birth, because through this, love and enmity will happen particularly between them.
¶ Friendship and enmity that lasts for a short time is said to be judged in the two births by the Hyleg of each birth. Thus, when the projection of one reaches such a place as stands in the birth of the other, or to a place that accords with it. Similarly, when the **Profection** <note>original: "alynthbe"; from the Arabic *al-intiha*, an astrological technique where a chart is "advanced" by one sign per year</note> or a similar thing reaches it: if there is harmony there, a particular friendship will happen because of it; and if they are in discord or are contrary, a particular enmity will happen.
¶ Those relationships that did not know a shorter term for their permanence before this separation will not find a limit to their duration of time until they join with other stars.
¶ The minimum that it will last is until that movement is completed, and the maximum it can last is until it reaches another planet among the planets that follow.
¶ Particular friendship, which is called "association," and likewise particular enmity that happens between two people, will last according to the time in which the movement of the Hyleg of one birth applies to the location of the Hyleg of the other birth. And Ptolemy <note>original: "ptol'."</note> gives us three things in this matter: the minimum time it can last, the maximum time the association and love (or the enmity) can last. And this will be as great a time as the Hyleg moves, as we have said. The maximum it can last is from the time in which the movement of the Hyleg of one birth applies to the place that accords with another such point in the other birth, until it applies to another planet that cuts it off; and it is manifest that this happens when it is a contrary planet.
¶ Therefore, **Saturn** and **Jupiter**, when one of them reaches the place of the other, will judge the friendship between them to be based on agriculture and inheritances.
¶ When Saturn or Jupiter, whichever it may be, passes through the place of the other, love will happen between them through the labors of the field or through the goods of the dead.
¶ This will be when one of them is the Hyleg in the birth of one person and the other is the Hyleg in the birth of the other. And this mode is just as he spoke in other manners after this. Saturn and Jupiter signify such a thing because they are both in agreement as being masculine and of the diurnal **Haiz** <note>original: "haiz"; a condition where a planet is in a sign/hemisphere of its own nature (e.g., a masculine planet in a masculine sign during the day)</note>, and because the house of each of them is in **Sextile** <note>an aspect of 60 degrees, considered harmonious</note> to the house of the other.
¶ **Saturn** and **Mars**, however, when one occupies the place of the other, will generate spontaneous quarrels and discords between them. But from **Saturn** and **Venus**, an association and affection of kinsmen will be produced, except that it will be terminated very quickly. **Saturn** and **Mercury** will signify association and mixing in the affairs of life, as well as giving and receiving, trading, and similar things. Through **Jupiter** and **Mars**, by occasion of wealth, or any lordship or arrangement, association and love will be produced between them. Through **Jupiter** and **Venus**, they will love each other because of women, or because of divine service, or through houses of prayer, or from perpetual foundations, or from things similar to these.
¶ When Saturn passes through the place of Mars, or Mars through the place of Saturn, a quarrel and harm will happen between them by will. And association will happen through Saturn and Venus because of parents, and yet it is quickly cut off. And association will happen through Saturn and Mercury in merchandise and in gaining something. And it will happen through Jupiter...

# Book Four

<margin>
That which occurs through **Saturn** and **Mars** <note>original: "saturnū 7 martē"</note> is because they are of contrary complexions. What occurs through Saturn and **Venus** is due to the harmony of their unions. Through this, a partnership on the part of the parents arises, but it is quickly severed because one is a fortune <note>a "benefic" or lucky planet (Venus)</note> and the other an infortune <note>a "malefic" or unlucky planet (Saturn)</note>. That of Saturn and **Mercury** is because the house of each is in a **trine** <note>an aspect of 120 degrees, considered harmonious</note> aspect to the other. That of **Jupiter** and Venus is because they are of concordant natures, and because the house of each is in **sextile** <note>an aspect of 60 degrees</note> to the house of the other; similarly, Venus has great power in **Pisces**, which is the house of Jupiter, and for this reason, it grants such things as he described. That of Jupiter and Mars is because the house of each is in a trine aspect to the house of the other.
</margin>

And through Venus, love arises on the part of women, and by reason of oratory, or pilgrimages, or prophecies. And love will occur through Jupiter and Mars by reason of honor or the governing of the people.

¶ Jupiter and Mercury will indicate a spontaneous partnership by occasion of the **dialectical sciences** <note>logic and formal debate</note> and prophecy. Mars and Venus, so to speak, will associate people together through debauchery, adultery, or fornication, or through the crime of sodomy; however, this bond will be brief, because one of them is a fortune and the other an infortune in terms of durability. Mars and Mercury will signify enmities, deceptions, and quarrels between people by occasion of incantations and **necromancy** <note>original: "nigromantie"; magic involving communication with the dead</note>. Venus and Mercury, however, will bring about a partnership between people in the matters of life concerning craftsmanship, or music, or books, or women.

¶ And a partnership will occur through Jupiter and Mercury by reason of the sciences, logic, and philosophy coming from the will. And a partnership will occur through Mars and Venus on the part of lust, harlotry, and fornication, and this shall not last long. And through Mars and Mercury, there will occur the discovery of an enemy, contentions, and accusations regarding handiwork <note>original: "facturis"; often implying magical charms or crafted items</note> and the like. And through Venus and Mercury, a partnership and friendship will be held in life for the sake of some craftsmanship, or for music, or for writings, or for women.

<margin>
That relationship of Jupiter and Mercury is because Mercury signifies the **rational soul** <note>original: "aĩaʒ rōnalē"</note> and Jupiter its apparatus. What he said regarding Mars and Venus is because when Venus participates with Mars, she gives rise to falling in love, fornication, lust, and such things. When these two signify in births either friendship or enmity, it will be because of these things which **Ptolemy** said. Because they are of contrary natures, that matter is not stable nor will it last. That of Mars and Mercury is because Mercury signifies sounds, handiwork, and deceptions; when mixed with Mars, it becomes an infortune, and for this reason, no good comes from them. What he says of Mercury and Venus is because Mercury inclines toward the nature of the planet to which it is joined; we know it signifies subtlety, knowledge of numbers, and arithmetic, while Venus signifies every beautiful and delightful thing. When their natures are mixed in friendship or enmity, it will be by reason of one of those things which Ptolemy mentioned. He did not name the participation of the other **hylegs** <note>original: "byleg"; the planet or point that acts as the "giver of life" in a chart</note> because they are always in the dignities of these five planets. For this reason, it will be that which one signifies: the four hylegs signify friendship, or enmity, or love, or hatred, and that which the lords of their places signified, being one of the things Ptolemy spoke of regarding the states of the five planets.
</margin>

¶ We ought to know the increase and decrease in the commonality of friendship and enmity by the vigor derived from the qualities of the places in which they exist, with respect to the four primary places over which they have lordship and power.

¶ And it is fitting that we know the increase and decrease; it shall be in the strength of love or enmity according to the state of the places that are accepted in comparison to the four principal places.

<margin>
He wants to say that the increase or decrease in love or enmity can be known from the state of the places of **profection** <note>a system of moving the chart forward one sign per year</note>, which is **ataçir** and **alintia** <note>astrological methods of "direction" or timing</note>, according to how the places of the four hylegs go at the hour of both births.
</margin>

<column-break/>

can be known from the state of the places of profection, which is **ataçir** and **alintia**, according to how the places of the four hylegs go at the hour of both births.

<margin>
For if they are in the **angles** <note>the four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>, or with the **Part of Fortune**, or with the **Luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note>, that which they signify will be clearer and more evident.
</margin>

¶ So if they are in the angles, or with the Part of Fortune, or with the two Luminaries, what they signify will be more apparent and manifest.

<margin>
He wants to say that when the profection of one of the two births—or the alintia—reaches any angle of the other’s birth, or the place of their Part of Fortune, or the place of either of the two Luminaries, their significance in friendship or enmity will be more manifest through public greatness.
</margin>

<margin>
And if they are far removed, it will not be manifest; and to indicate whether it will harm or help can be known from the state of the planets aspecting the aforesaid places—namely, what kind of good or evil it will be.
</margin>

<margin>
The aforesaid places are the four places signifying love and hatred, friendship and enmity.

¶ Now, to treat of servants in their love or abhorrence of their masters toward them: they will indicate this from the sign that is specifically in the **unfortunate place** <note>the 12th house</note> by natural constitution, which the planets have with each other that aspected that place at the very hour of birth, or those which were in that same place or in its opposite. This is especially true if the planets that rule that sign agree with the places of lordship and power in the fellowship of the figures, or if they are of the same kind with them.

<margin>
The judgment of servants—whether they will love or hate their masters—can be known from the sign that will be in the **place of labor** <note>the 12th house</note>, and from the natural concord which the planets have when aspecting this place at the hour of birth itself, or at the hours when they come to it, or those which are opposite to it. Necessarily, this applies if the planets ruling the sign are in concord with the principal places of their births by participating with them in the figure, or if they are of this same kind.
</margin>

¶ We have already said the judgment of them is one of the things from which a household is composed. And Ptolemy does not see fit to give a specific chapter to this, because they are a part of one's wealth. After he narrated in this chapter the things signifying the love or hatred that servants have for their master, and when it happens that a man buys a suitable or unsuitable servant, he said that the rule for this is taken from the sign in the place of labor: and this is the **twelfth house**. Similarly, it is taken from the planets that join this house at the hour of birth, and when the **ataçir** or **alintia** of the hyleg reaches this place. If there is concord between these things according to the hyleg at the hour of birth, they will signify that the servants love their masters and the masters love them; if it is the contrary, it will be the contrary. And if you have understood whatever we have glossed in this chapter, you can understand it easily without any further gloss. However, regarding the **sixth house**, which many say is the house of servants: we have already said that Ptolemy rejects the power of all that is below the earth, and we said that the twelfth house is of greater power than the sixth. Since this is so, it is fitting that the sixth house signifies beasts only. And when a servant has a known birth, it happens that the participation between his hyleg and the hyleg of his master is observed, according to what Ptolemy gave you in the chapter on friendship and enmity.

### Treatise

...he will have status in those things: whether he will gain or lose, or if he will have danger or peace in them.

The matter of travel <note>original: "peregrinatio," referring to journeys, pilgrimages, or living abroad</note> is understood from the qualities of the luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> and their relationship to the angles <note>the four cardinal points of a horoscope: the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</note>. It is understood most of all from the qualities of the Moon. For when the Moon is occidental <note>setting in the west</note> and far from the angles, it will indicate travels and changes from place to place.

¶ The fact of travel and journeys can be known from the state of the two luminaries in comparison to the angles, and of Mars from the state of the Moon. Thus, if the Moon is in the west or inclining away from the angles, it shows the undertaking of journeys and movement from one place to another.

The rule of journeys is taken from the Sun and Moon according to how they stand with the angles, and more from the Moon than the Sun. If the Moon is in the west, or has declined from the 10th house <note>the Midheaven</note>, or is in places "falling" from the angles <note>known as cadent houses</note>, or generally in the falling quarters, it will signify that the native <note>the person whose birth chart is being read</note> will move himself from one place to another.

¶ Similarly also, when Mars is occidental or when it has declined from the zenith <note>the point directly overhead</note>, and its distance from the luminaries is that of an opposition <note>180 degrees</note> or a square aspect <note>90 degrees, literally "aspect of a quarter"</note>, it will sometimes bring this about.

¶ And Mars does the same when it is in the west, or has declined from our zenith, being separated from the two luminaries by the distance of an opposition or a square. This is because Mars agrees with the luminaries in one way and disagrees in another. The way it agrees with them is that the house of the Moon, **Cancer**, is the 9th sign from **Scorpio**, which is the house of Mars; and **Leo** is the house of the Sun, and **Aries**, which is the house of Mars, is the 9th sign from the Sun. <note>In astrology, the 9th house traditionally governs long-distance travel and religion</note>. The way it disagrees with them is that Aries is in the square of Cancer, and Scorpio is in the square of Leo. And because of this, it is consistent that when Mars is well-placed at birth in the west, or in the entire falling quarter—which includes the 7th, 8th, and 9th houses—and if it is in the quarter of the Sun and Moon or in opposition to them, it signifies the undertaking of journeys and changes.

¶ And if the Part of Fortune <note>a calculated mathematical point in a chart representing prosperity and well-being</note> falls again in signs signifying travel, his whole life and his works and acts will be in foreign places.

¶ Similarly, if the Part of Fortune happens to be in signs that grant journeys, his whole life and his movement will be in strange and foreign places.

¶ Ptolemy teaches us that the reason for journeys is the declination of the two luminaries from the angles, and especially the Moon, and similarly Mars. He shows that the places giving journeys are the West, the 8th, and the 9th houses, and generally the places falling from the angles, and specifically the western angle <note>the Descendant</note>. Thus, when we find the signifiers of travel—which are the Sun, Moon, and Mars—in the places of travel, and we similarly find the Part of Fortune in these places, his whole life and his labor will be in foreign lands. And this clearly shows that if the two luminaries, Mars, and the Part of Fortune are in other places that do not give journeys, that native will never go on journeys, nor will he leave his own place. And if some of them are in the places of travel and some in the places of staying <note>original: "locis mor[ae]"</note>, the native will travel between them.

¶ But if the "Fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus</note> aspect the aforementioned places, or proceed toward them, or follow them, the things that he performs during his travels will be suitable, rare, and profitable. His return from travel will also be fast and easy, nor will he ever be hindered by anything.

¶ And if the Fortunes look upon the places we mentioned, or are in the signs following them, the works he involves himself in in foreign lands will be noble and pleasing, and he will return to his own place quickly without any disturbance.

<column-break/>

He means to say that when the Fortunes look upon the places of the signifiers of travel, or go toward them by their own motion, or place themselves in their position because of the equinoctial motion <note>the daily rotation of the sky</note>—for example, so that the signifier is in the 9th house and a Fortune is in the 10th—in this way the Fortune goes to the place of the signifier. Whatever good it brings, it will grant luck in journeys, and he will return safe and sound quickly.

¶ But if the "Infortunes" <note>malefic planets like Saturn and Mars</note> aspect them, those works of his will be laborious and harmful, full of fear, and he will return slowly from his travel.

¶ And if the Infortunes aspect them, those works will be with the labor of loss and danger, and he will return late.

¶ He means that when the Infortunes aspect the place of the signifier of travel, or go toward it, or follow it through the equinox or through the proper motion of the Infortune, they signify that the journeys will be with labor, and the deeds he does there will be with danger and loss, and the return will be slow. And here he has given us the specific indications of good fortune in journeys and bad fortune. Because of this, we understand that if the Fortunes and Infortunes are mixed, the matter will be mixed, and the one that is stronger will prevail.

¶ The mixture of this matter will always appear according to the plurality of planets that are associated with these places in the figure <note>the birth chart</note>, just as we showed in the previous sections.
The mixture of this will be taken from the plurality of planets participating in these places in the figure, as we have demonstrated.

¶ Now we have shown many times in the past chapters how a man can consider the mixture of the fortunate and unfortunate planets: namely, what will happen through each of them, the magnitude of what they will perform, and similarly when it will happen. Therefore, according to this, there is no need to provide a commentary on this word of Ptolemy.

¶ If the luminaries are in any of the two eastern quarters, they will more frequently undertake journeys toward the regions of the East and the South. If they rotate in either of the two western quarters, or in the West itself, his travel will appear toward the North and the West.

¶ And when the luminaries are in the part of the eastern quarters or in the East, their many journeys will be toward the regions of the East and the South. And if they are in the western quarters or in the West itself, the journeys will be toward the regions of the North and the West.

¶ The "eastern quarter" he spoke of in this place is the half of the firmament that is ascending; it is one of the four quarters. The 10th, 11th, and 12th houses are one, and the another quarter is the Ascendant, the 2nd, and the 3rd. The two western quarters are the other half. Since this is so, it follows that we should join what he mentioned in the second part regarding the trigons <note>the four elemental groups of zodiac signs: Fire, Earth, Air, and Water</note> with what he said here. Thus, the trigon of **Aries** <note>Fire: Aries, Leo, Sagittarius</note> signifies the region of the North and East; the trigon of **Taurus** <note>Earth: Taurus, Virgo, Capricorn</note> signifies the South and East; the trigon of **Gemini** <note>Air: Gemini, Libra, Aquarius</note> signifies the North with the East; and the trigon of **Cancer** <note>Water: Cancer, Scorpio, Pisces</note> signifies the South with the West. Each of these trigons signifies those parts of the inhabited world that are opposite to its own part. Similarly, if any northern planet like **Jupiter** applies to the signifier of travel, it will signify the northern region. Similarly, if a southern planet like **Venus** applies to it, it will signify the southern region. And if a western planet like **Mars** applies to them, it will signify the western region; and if **Saturn** is in the eastern parts, it will signify the eastern region. The **Sun** helps in the eastern parts and the **Moon** in the western parts. It is necessary that you mix all these things together—one with the other—and then you will know for certain toward which part they will go, or where the journeys will be. And if they signify more in one part than another, you will judge for each according to the state you see. In these words of Ptolemy lies one point: he already said at the beginning of this chapter that the signifiers of travel are the two luminaries and Mars. He said in this place that if it happens that the luminaries in the birth chart are in the two eastern quarters, the journeys will be toward the South and East. And it is manifest that if they are in the first quarter of these two, it does not signify...

# Fourth Book

...they will signify journeys in any way. But what we respond by saying is that the significators <note>planets that represent a specific topic in a horoscope</note> of journeys are three: the Moon is strongest, then the Sun, then Mars. ¶ But if the signs themselves which signify travel—or their lords—are of a single form <note>fixed or singular signs</note>, the journey will happen occasionally. ¶ Let it be known concerning signs of one figure and of two: it is useful to ask what is meant by "one" or "two" figures. This is because many which are of one figure are of one kind, while those of two are of another. For Venus, Mars, and Saturn are of one figure; Mercury and Jupiter are both of two figures. And because of this, some astronomers have said that Jupiter signifies a law in which there is a duality or trinity, and Saturn signifies a law in which there is unity. Similarly, it can be because of a single figure if the planet stands in a sign of one figure, or two figures if it is in a sign of two, or if it aspects itself with more than one planet, or if the journey is through one sign or between two degrees, and similar things. The signs giving journeys and pilgrimages from one land to another are those in which the significators of journeys stand.

¶ He [Ptolemy] wants to say that if Mercury is with any of the fortunes, or with both of them while being the lord signifying the journeys, it will become a "fortune" by combination and will affirm its significance; and because of this, that traveler will have gains and good things which Ptolemy described. ### Chapter 8: On the quality of the native’s death.

**P**ost after he taught all the rules by which we can know the state of a man regarding good or evil, he wishes in this chapter to demonstrate the rules by which we can know the state of his death.

¶ Because after a brief explanation of the aforesaid things, the qualities of death are to be observed by us from those things we predicted in life: whether death occurs from the "projection of rays" <note>Aspects or mathematical lines of influence sent from one planet to another.</note> or from the arrival of the significator at the western angle <note>The descendant, or the 7th house cusp, where planets "set."</note>; it is fitting for us to know this.

**Q**uod regarding what he says, that death will be through the meeting of rays, he means death which is signified by the direct *ataçir* <note>term: *ataçir* — a method of "directing" a planet through the zodiac to predict the timing of events.</note> of the *hyleg* <note>term: *hyleg* — the "giver of life," a specific planet or point in a chart used to determine longevity.</note>; and that which he means by the governor applying to the degree of the west is for death which will be through the "converse *ataçir*" of the *hyleg*, until it reaches the degree of the western angle.

¶ Thus, if death was through the projection of rays, or through the meeting of that which opposes it, it is appropriate that we inspect the places that meet when we wish to know the state of death. ¶ Concerning what he says, "it is appropriate that we inspect," he means that we should look at that degree which "cuts off" <note>The *interficiens* or killing planet/point.</note>, what kind of state it will have, and in what degree the cutting off will be.

¶ Because according to the planets that follow the aforesaid places—if any follow—or according to the planets that first go to them if no planets are found following them, the quality of death will be discerned; if we have accepted the properties of the planets' configurations with their natures in the science of the differences of accidents, especially if we consider the qualities of the aforesaid place of the west, which they have from the signs and the natures of the "terms" <note>term: *terms* — also called "bounds," these are specific degrees within a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet.</note>.

¶ Ptolemy teaches us in this statement the state of the "killing degree" <note>The *gradus interficiens*.</note>; so that this state is composed of five things. The first is the nature of the planet standing in that degree, or which projects its rays into that degree. The second is the nature of the planet standing near that degree which goes toward it first, either by its own course or through the motion of the equinox. The third is the nature of the figure <note>The aspect or geometric relationship.</note> which is made by the mixing of one of these things with another. The fourth is the nature of the sign in which that degree is, or in which the planet is that regards that degree or goes toward it. The fifth is the nature of the term to which that killing degree belongs. And if it happens that the degree itself has only one of these five things, its state will be according to what the term was alone; or its state will be composed of two of these five, or three, or four, or five. Whatever comes of these, death will be according to the nature of the state which the killing degree has. And Ptolemy taught us the property and nature of each of these things separately, one by one, just as he was accustomed to do in other past matters; and we should know how to compose these things so that we may know what the state of death will be like.

¶ This is because **Jupiter**, signifying temperance, generates much blood; and when blood overcomes the body, these infirmities happen, arriving from "repletion" <note>An excess of bodily fluids or humors.</note>. And thus you understand something of physics: you can well know all this, and the foul stench will be because of the putrefaction of the humors.

¶ If **Mars** should be its lord, the end of life will be imposed by occasion of persistent fever, or continuous tertian fever, or a sudden stroke, or <term>nephritis<note>Inflammation of the kidneys.</note></term>; or by <term>empyema<note>A collection of pus in a cavity, usually the lungs.</note></term> or any disease of the blood vessels, or abortion, or childbirth, or <term>erysipelas<note>A bacterial skin infection, historically called "St. Anthony's Fire."</note></term>; or by a death-bearing sickness, or from all infirmities coming from febrile fervor or superfluous heat.

¶ And if it is **Mars**, death will be because of continuous and acute fevers and through those called <term>hemitritaeos<note>original: "emitrites"; a specific type of semi-tertian fever.</note></term>, which happens because of paroxysms coming at the [specified] hour; and for pain of the kidneys, and for spitting blood; likewise for a flux [of blood] from removing children <note>Referring to complications of miscarriage or difficult birth.</note>; and for the <term>paroxysm of choler<note>An outburst of "yellow bile," the humor associated with heat and anger.</note></term>, and through all infirmities that kill with a strong fever and great heat.

¶ Continuous fevers are those that burn and glow much, which are called <term>causon<note>A Greek term for a highly inflammatory, burning fever.</note></term>, and the like. The semi-tertian is that which is made of phlegm and choler, and generally **Mars** causes infirmities which are from great heat and dryness.

¶ But if **Venus** should be the mistress of death, we pronounce that life is terminated by a vice of the stomach, or the liver, or the heart; or by the passing of blood, or by shifting abscesses, or <term>fistulas<note>Abnormal passages or tunnels in the body tissue.</note></term>, or [poisonous] potions, and all diseases occurring from a superfluity or malice of the humors.

¶ And if it is **Venus**, death will happen because of coldness of the stomach, liver, and heart; the flux of blood and abscesses moving through the body and fistulas; and by hindering the midsection; and through all things coming from many humors and their corruption.

¶ This is because **Venus** creates a temperament tending toward moisture, just as much blood is mixed with moisture; "sweet phlegm" and the things she does are composed of much repletion and moisture.

¶ If **Mercury** should be its lord, death will occur by perturbation of the mind, or mania, or melancholy, or "precipitation" <note>Likely referring to falling from heights or sudden seizures.</note>, or epilepsy; or by cough, or an overabundance of spitting; or by all diseases proceeding from excessive or incongruous dryness.

¶ And if it is **Mercury**, death will be by epilepsy, as

<column-break/>

through the folly which men bear, or through the loss of the senses by well-known evil thoughts, or by a fall, or much coughing and vomiting; and through all infirmities which are made from great dryness, or through the damnation and corruption of that [dryness].

¶ This is because **Mercury** is the significator of the senses and the brain, and his <term>complexion<note>The specific balance of qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry) in a person or planet.</note></term> is inclined toward dryness. And regarding the simple things he said in these five planets, they are the signification of their natures. It is similarly manifest what the signification of the <term>terms<note>Subdivisions of zodiac signs that have specific planetary rulers.</note></term> is, in which the "killing degrees" are located; for the signification of any degree is such as the signification of the planet whose term it is in which it stays.

¶ However, for those whom nature has enjoined death in the aforesaid manner: when the planet which is the disposer of death shall be in its own proper and natural qualities, or those very similar to them, and no other planet—by whose occasion an evil and grave death occurs—is elevated above them, life shall be taken away [naturally].

¶ And those who die a "death of itself" <note>Natural death.</note> divide themselves from life well when the planets that govern death are in their own natural and appropriate state; nor should another planet from those that give death from the "part of the place" be elevated above them.

¶ **Ptolemy** divided death into two kinds: one is coming from infirmities; the other is from a matter in which the physician has nothing to see <note>Meaning a death where medical intervention is irrelevant, like an accident.</note>, such as he who dies by the sword, spear, a fall, fire, or the bite of a wild beast, or drowning in water, and many other occasions; and in each of these he shows the reason. But death coming in which the physicians have something to see—which is called "death of itself"—happens when the planets governing death are safe from the <term>infortunes<note>The "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars.</note></term>, and in their own dignities and powers, and when no contrary planet is elevated above them. But death coming in which the physicians have nothing to see—and which **Ptolemy** calls "death by the part of the place"—is that which happens when the planets who rule death are unfortunate, weak, or in alien dignities contrary to them, or if other contrary planets are elevated above them.

¶ But death which is inferred by force and not by the law of nature will happen when both <term>infortunes<note>Saturn and Mars.</note></term> rule the place of death: so that they remain in that same place, or in its fourth or opposite aspect; or if either of them has dominion and power over the place of the Sun, or the Moon, or both.

¶ And the death will be laborious with pains and "dragging" when the rulers over the place of death are two infortunes together: whether they are in the same place, or in its square or opposition in longitude; or if one of them wishes to be the mistress over the Sun or Moon or both.

¶ A "pained and dragging" death—that is, vexatious or laborious—can be a "death of itself" or a "death of the place." And **Ptolemy** gave us in this place the reason for the labor and pain: it will be because two infortunes rule in the killing degree; or because one rules in the degree and the other over one of the <term>luminaries<note>The Sun and the Moon.</note></term>; or because both rule over both luminaries. And the same follows if you understand this regarding the other <term>hylegs<note>The "giver of life," a specific point in a chart used to calculate longevity.</note></term>; and the matter will be stronger when both rule over a certain hyleg, or over the killing degree; and this is of all the most unfortunate dominion.

¶ But an evil and iniquitous death will happen because of the conjunction of the two infortunes; its magnitude will proceed through the testimonies of the luminaries.

¶ And the death will be evil by the conjunction of the two infortunes, and it will be a "great death" through the testimonies of the two luminaries.

¶ An evil death is that which is with pain and labor; and this is because of the conjunction of the two infortunes in giving death; and it will be a "great death" when the two luminaries testify to the infortunes giving death, or to the planets governing death.

# Treatise

¶ But the quality of death itself will occur according to the aspects of other planets and the signs in which the <term>malefics<note>The "unfortunate" planets, traditionally Saturn and Mars, which were believed to bring hardship or death.</note></term> are found.
¶ And the state of death will likewise be determined by the aspect of other planets and by the signs in which the malefics stand.
¶ The state of death will be according to what the other planets signify when they apply to the place of death or to the killing planets, and according to the sign in which the malefic planet stands which kills and cuts the <term>Hyleg<note>Original: *byleg*. The "giver of life," a specific point or planet in a birth chart used to determine the life force and longevity of the native.</note></term>.
¶ For when **Saturn** is in a <term>quartile aspect<note>A 90-degree angle between planets, considered a tense or challenging relationship.</note></term> to the **Sun**, or in its opposition, and is in its own *alaiz* <note>Original: *alaiz*. Likely a corruption of the Arabic *al-hayz*, a condition where a planet is in its preferred sect and quadrant of the chart.</note>: if it is in a <term>fixed sign<note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius. These signs were associated with stability, persistence, and physical solidity.</note></term>, the person will be crushed by the ropes of death by stoning at the hands of the people, or will be afflicted by strangulation or deadly punishments. And when it is <term>occidental<note>Setting in the west, or following the Sun.</note></term> and the **Moon** follows it, we should know that the same will happen.
¶ Thus, when **Saturn** is in the fourth part from the **Sun** or in its opposition in a different *baiz* <note>Original: *baiz*. Another variation of *hayz* (sect/condition).</note>, if it is in fixed signs: death will be by manual stoning by the people, or by burning or punishment; and it will be similar when it is in the west and the **Moon** follows it.
¶ When **Saturn** is in the quartile of the **Sun** at the hour of birth, or in its opposition, and it is the planet that cuts the **Hyleg**: it will signify, if it is in a fixed sign, death by stoning at the hand of the people; and the same will be signified if it is in a fixed sign and in the west at the hour of birth and the **Moon** follows it. And all <term>suffocation<note>Original: *suffocatio*. Used here to describe a medical inability to breathe.</note></term> is the inability to draw breath: and this can happen because of the closing of the passages through which the breath exits, or it can be due to humors falling into the lungs, or suffocation while eating and drinking.
¶ But when it exists in signs whose figures resemble the shapes of wild beasts, he shall perish by the bites of wild beasts.
¶ And if it is in signs of the figures of wild beasts, death will be because of the mauling of a wild beast.
¶ When **Saturn** is in quartile to the **Sun** or its opposite, or in the west with the **Moon** following it, and it is the cutter of the **Hyleg** and in a sign of wild forest beasts: death will be by the snatching of a wild beast.
¶ If **Jupiter** bears witness to it and exists in an unfortunate state in their assembly on a notable and solemn day: he shall be condemned to be devoured by the mouths of beasts.
¶ And if **Jupiter**, being unfortunate, testifies to it, he will cast that native to wild beasts in a place where people gather on holy, sounding, and festive days <note>A reference to execution by beasts in a public arena or circus.</note>.
¶ When **Saturn** signifies the snatching by a beast, and **Jupiter** being unfortunate testifies to it: it will signify what **Ptolemy** said. And it is manifest that the testimony of the two <term>luminaries<note>The Sun and the Moon.</note></term> signifies deaths that are brief, public, and great.
¶ If it remains in the opposition of the other luminary which holds the place in the <term>Ascendant<note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth.</note></term>: he will be cast down to death in prison.
¶ And if it is in opposition to whichever of the luminaries it may be, and that same luminary is in the Ascendant, he will die while imprisoned.
¶ He means to say that when **Saturn** is the cutter <note>Original: *abscisor*. The killing planet or Anareta.</note>, and it happens that one of the luminaries is in the Ascendant: the native will die in prison.
¶ But if **Mercury** is joined to it in the figure: in the figures of the **Serpents** of the celestial sphere, or in signs whose figures are of ravenous beasts: he will be torn apart by the bites of poisonous animals.
¶ And if it has a participation with **Mercury** in the figure, and if it is in the figures of the **Serpents** that are in the sphere or in signs that are of the figures of forest animals: death will be because of the striking of poisonous crawling animals.
¶ He means that **Saturn** signifies a great death because it harms one of the luminaries and has participation with **Mercury** in the figure; and if there is with it any <term>fixed star<note>Distant stars, as opposed to the "wandering" planets.</note></term> of those that are in the figures of serpents on the same circle, or it is in a sign of the figure of forest beasts, death will be because of the striking of poisonous reptiles.

<column-break/>

¶ If **Venus** however stands with them: he will die by a deadly drink through the treachery of women.
¶ And if **Venus** is with them, it will be death by a mortal poison killing him, or by a wild beast that will kill him.
¶ If the constellation signifies what was said about poisons, and **Venus** testifies to it: those poisons will be what he said, because **Venus** signifies hidden and secret things, and similarly has the signification of women.
¶ If it claims a place for itself in **Virgo** or in **Pisces**, or in <term>humid signs<note>Signs associated with the element of water.</note></term>, and is associated with the **Moon** in the figure: he will end his life by drowning.
¶ And if that place is in the sign of **Virgo** or **Pisces**, or that which is a humid sign, and it has participation with the **Moon** in the figure: death will be because of submersion in water.
¶ When **Saturn** is the cutter and harms the **Moon**, and is in any of the places which **Ptolemy** said: it will signify that death will be through drowning in water, and there it signifies much humidity and a great death.
¶ But if it is in **the Ship** <note>The constellation Argo Navis.</note>, he will be deprived of life by the stormy tossing of the sea. And if it is with the **Sun** in either of the two <term>solstitial signs<note>Cancer or Capricorn.</note></term>, or in signs having the figures of four-footed animals, or is in opposition to **Mars** instead of the **Sun**: he will be destroyed by the fall of a ruin.
¶ And if it is in this place which is called "the ship": death will be by the surging of the sea. And if it is with the **Sun** in either of the two solstices, or in signs having the figures of quadrupeds, or in opposition to **Mars** instead of the **Sun**: death will be because of something that falls upon him.
¶ When **Saturn** is joined with the **Sun** or in opposition to **Mars**, and is in any of the signs he mentioned while being the cutter: death will be through something falling upon the native.
¶ If however it is in the <term>Midheaven<note>Original: *celi medio*. The highest point in the chart, the 10th house.</note></term> or its opposition: he will be cast down from a height and die.
¶ And if it is in the middle of the circle above the earth or below the earth <note>The 10th or 4th houses.</note>: death will be on account of a fall from a height.
¶ When **Saturn** harms the **Sun** while being the cutter and is in the 10th or 4th house: death will be through a fall from a high place. These are the "great deaths" which **Saturn** signifies when it is the cutter and one of the luminaries is impeded by it; and according to this you can judge all deaths that happen through **Saturn**.
¶ **Mars**, however, when it is in the fourth or opposite aspect to the **Sun** or the **Moon**, and in its contrary *alaiz*.
¶ And **Mars** when it is in opposition to the **Sun** or **Moon**, or in their quartile in a different *baiz*.
¶ It is fitting that you understand "different *baiz*" in the way I shall tell you: which is that the **Sun** and **Moon** give life; and when **Mars** signifies the cutting of the **Hyleg**, and they aspect each other with one of them as the other **Hyleg**: the aspect will be in a different *baiz*.
¶ If it rotates in signs of human form: because of wars and uprisings occurring among his own kinsmen or by fighting: he will perish by the cutting off of his head, or he will bring his own hand against himself because of women, or he will be killed by the hands of women. That, however, will happen when **Venus** again bears witness to it.
¶ And if it is in signs of the figure of men: that death will be through <term>beheading<note>Original: *degulamentum*.</note></term> through war which happens between one people and another, or through battle, or that he will kill himself with his own hand because of women, or that women will kill him: and this will be if **Venus** testifies there.
¶ If **Mars** is contrary to the **Sun** or **Moon** in *baiz*, and is in a sign of human figure, it will move that native toward such a spirit that it makes them fight.

The governor of death is the lord of the degree of the killer.
¶ The intervening accidents in quantity or quality will be multiplied when both malefics have authority in the killing places. ¶ And the accidents by which death arrives will be doubled in quality or quantity when two malefics have dignity in the killing places; and he in whose birth the state of the planets was in this manner will not be covered nor buried, but will be eaten by wolves, dogs, or evil birds. If two malefics are in the places of such figures as we have said, and no benefic bears witness to the killing places, it [the body] will be among those [placed] under the earth [without] fortunes.
¶ The doubling of which he spoke is manifest in arithmetic: because a thing is twice as much as one to two, or three to six: and quality and quantity is the thing shown. For quality refers to the accidents by which death happens, and quantity refers to the quantity of punishments: so that if one of the malefics is cutting the <term>Hyleg<note>Original: *byleg*. The "giver of life," a specific point in a birth chart used to calculate longevity.</note></term> in some degree and is itself the governor of that degree, it will signify what Ptolemy said. But when he said "and no benefic will bear witness to the killing place while the fortunes are under the earth," he means that when the benefics bear witness to the cutting malefic, which signifies the native is not buried: this will be when the benefics are above the earth; yet if they bear witness while being under the earth, they will signify that he will be buried and covered.
¶ When the planets that are lords of the killing places are in declining places, and **Mars** is with the **Moon** in the aforementioned places, and remains in the fourth [house] or the opposite of these places: he will obey the law of death among foreigners.
¶ And death will be in a foreign land when the planets ruling over the killing places are in inclined places: and especially the **Moon** in those places which we said, or in the fourth of its places or their opposition.
¶ When the lord of death or the abscisor, whichever of them it may be, or both are in the places of travel: it will signify that death will be in a foreign land: and this thing is confirmed; and if the **Moon** is in the places of travel or aspects them from the 4th [house] or opposition. For it is useful that you return many times to this chapter and look until you have understood well all its reasons diligently: and that you can mix the significators and mix the constellations: one, that is, with another: and so it is fitting that you do in every chapter of this book. For when you have done this, you will know a good part of this art. Yet if with this you know something of natures and physics, and know well how to equate the planets and know something of their four-part states according to what was demonstrated in the <term>Almagest<note>The famous 2nd-century mathematical and astronomical treatise by Ptolemy.</note></term>: no one will be able to conquer you in this art, nor will you need any book except this one.

<meta>This page continues the philosophical and methodological introduction to the fourth book of the treatise. # Treatise

->**On the Study of Man and All His Deeds**<-

Of man and all his deeds. For through this study, all things can be known that ought to be before they exist: thus, one will prepare so that a matter may grow in good if it was good, and if it was evil, the evil may be diminished. For such a thing as is found in this [science] helps much toward the good; through it, the will of a good man rests easy and he will not labor for that which he cannot have. And although the human will has a desire to know future things, even if one does not take delight in this, it is a great good and a rest for him; for he will not have cause to suffer over things he knows he will eventually have, nor will he labor for those things he knows he ought to possess. And since there is a great perfection in the knowledge hidden in these books, we have a great reason to learn and know it, and to take much delight in understanding what is hidden within it. For when we understand it and find it to be certain through experience and certain rectification, we will trust more in those things that signify what is to come. We shall know both general things that happen to people in common and those specific things that happen to each individual. 

Indeed, he who composed this book <note>Referring to Ptolemy, the author of the *Tetrabiblos*.</note> covered the words he spoke in <term>quadrivial<note>The Quadrivium: the four high sciences of arithmetic, geometry, music, and astronomy/astrology.</note></term> terms, just as the ancient sages were accustomed to do. They did this so that noble sciences would not be revealed or uncovered to those who are of vile souls and evil morals. Thus said **Hippocrates**: "The more you govern bodies that are not clean, the more you will increase their sickness." And **Plato** said: "The more you teach evil souls science and wisdom, the more you increase their capacity for evil." And the ancient sages who lived before **Aristotle** spoke the words of science through metaphors so that they might conceal them, as **Plato** did. But after **Aristotle** saw that these words could be understood in different ways, it pleased him to explain <note>original: *glossare*</note> and not simply compile the sciences in a hidden manner so that those with evil souls could not understand them, while those of good souls would understand them for certain when they sought them out. 

And after everyone, **Ptolemy** came after all those philosophers and took the way of **Aristotle**, and he compiled this art in a very concealed way. And we have opened many things from those he concealed and have demonstrated them; he who is a philosopher acts as a mediator. We have not spoken in our explanations <note>original: *glossauimus*</note> in such a way that those who boast of knowing this art—yet are very far from it because they have evil souls and poor understanding—might use it. However, we have spoken for those who have a great will and a desire to gain good character and virtues, which grow more every day.

<margin>And it pleases me to say in this place the words that **Haly** <note>Likely Haly Abenrudian (Ali ibn Ridwan), the commentator, referencing his own medical background or citing Galen.</note> said in the 5th treatise of his book on the pulse.</margin> 

And he said that through much great study, he perceived many things in the pulse that he had not perceived before. And these are his words: **Haly** said here that this kind of science exists in many minds; yet when I was studying the movement of the pulse and other things pertaining to the pulse, I did not know it well at first. But by studying well with many minds, laboring and thinking with great doubts about these hidden things, I became experienced. I did not give up my study or my investigation; rather, the more I proceeded in it, the more my will to progress and study increased. And it seemed to me that I was beginning to perceive the knowledge of the pulse. After I studied and labored, I understood better that I perceived the knowledge of the pulse not with a weak knowledge, but with one that was quite certain, so that I knew by experience that which could be attained. After I understood this knowledge, and how quickly I began to grasp all things pertaining to the pulse, I cannot tell you; I felt like a man standing in a slippery place to whom a great light suddenly appears at that hour. 

Holding my voice <note>original: *vocem meam*; perhaps meaning "keeping my word" or "maintaining my focus."</note> and believing it to be true and not empty, a great perfection followed. For as soon as one begins to seek these things, let him not despair of attaining them for certain, and let him not stop studying so that he may know something in time. For in a man who studies and labors much in a thing, such a virtue <note>original: *virtus*; here meaning a faculty or power of the mind.</note> grows in him that he does not realize when it happens; it will always grow and improve, and he will not know when it began. Thus, this power will appear in his work and quickly give fruit, so that he will be easily restored for all the labor he spent. And if you wish to say, as people do, that the "capital and the profit shall return as one," **Haly** called us to this by the word that comes to those laboring through good virtues: how to conduct themselves well in all things they wish to attain. For great study gives such fruit in good things that it will restore however much labor a man had, plus a great profit. Study increases such a power in a man that he can attain the things he seeks; and when the power comes, the man does not know it until he finds himself possessing it. Therefore, I desire this instruction <note>original: *castigamentum*</note> more than any other, so that it may grant good things and virtues to my friends who seek them. And to him who wishes to guard and seek this art and science, it is necessary that he look upon what **Haly** said in this place and study it intensely.

<column-break/>

Let him not be weary, nor let him despair; for he will be well able to know this art in such a way that he may trust in what he judges regarding future things with such confidence that he will have no doubt. And if anyone should doubt, saying that he is not perfect in his study, after he has signaled in a man's birth chart <note>original: *nativitate*</note> what is to be, it cannot be otherwise, nor can one escape it. To this I respond: if you had understood what the philosophers have demonstrated, and what is said perfectly in the prologue of this book and in this chapter, we would be free of your doubt. For we have already demonstrated to you in what has passed that there are certain works of many incisions <note>Likely referring to the "cutting" of planetary rays or influences.</note> that cannot fail; these come about through a very great and potent virtue. But among those things that are changeable are those that come about through a weak virtue. Thus, when we find in someone's birth chart a virtue signifying that he will be wise, and another signifying he will be a lover of pleasure, and another that he will be sensible, I say that through long and continuous study, the virtue signifying wisdom and sense will increase, and the virtue of pleasure will be brought back to these good things, so that he will take great delight in them. 

For everything you say could be true if a man were destined to labor at something; and since it is man's nature to labor and study, it follows that he should study and labor in those things he wishes to attain. **Haly** explained this reasoning very well in a passage he spoke after the first one. **Haly** said: "And those who come after me, by as much as they arrive through study and perseverance in the knowledge of the pulse, they shall have the skill to know it in a long time, but with less cost than the time in which I labored for it; and they shall labor there less than I have labored, because I am teaching the way by which they may go straight to knowing what they want more easily." 

However, there is one necessary condition there: one must keep away from the greed for gaining riches and from vain glory. For these are two things that a man loves much. And he said afterward that this which I speak of in this book is not enough for men who wish to learn it simply by setting themselves to hear and use it; rather, it is necessary that they be very sharp and of great perseverance, and such men as these are few. Nonetheless, I shall do as **Ambraclides** <note>Possibly a corruption of a Greek name like Archytas or Anaxagoras.</note> said: "I commend one more than ten thousand, and I desire to be with that one man more than with those ten thousand who are not worth as much as that one." For the truth cannot be judged by a great crowd of people; it can, however, be judged by a few who are intelligent and have sense. And I speak only with such a one, who desires and loves the truth, whether he lives in my time or comes after me. 

**Haly** said: "If you who read this our book wish to be such a one as **Haly** the physician said—a studious lover and persevering seeker of truths—you should apply yourself to knowing all future things when you wish to know them, through everything we have explained <note>original: *glossavimus*</note> and shown to you from the words of **Ptolemy**." This is a very great gain, and from it you can have very good fruit. However, if you love riches, and your wealth must come through agriculture and trade, that fruit will not be for those who come after you; but if you love wisdom and goodness and wish to seek them, you can arrive at a great thing if you have understood the instruction of **Haly** which we mentioned in this state, and similarly what we testify. 

For although **Haly** the physician gave instruction, he nevertheless gave an example to all others of how they should conduct themselves if they wish to know any noble thing. For it happens that a man receives these things with great study and perseverance, not studying one single time but many times; and with this, you will apply yourself to what you desire. However, it is fitting that the thing he seeks be possible. And we have shown in the commentary <note>original: *glosa*</note> of the first treatise those things that a man can attain through this science; and similarly we have shown it in the commentary of the second, third, and fourth treatises. Nothing remains for us to speak of except the divisions of the times of life, which increase and decrease in the things given by the celestial bodies in birth charts; and from here on, we wish to explain this.

Life is divided into parts: and each of the planets governs its own part, or another planet participates with it in the governing.
