# Book Four
sig: m 3

...follow the same path: those things which are to be observed in the division of nativities <note>A "nativity" is a birth chart used to predict a person's life path.</note> and attended to in particular matters according to the fated modes, as it falls to us to add further.

**After** we have provided a way for inquiring generally into the manner of various things, so that we may come to know all their natural properties according to what we distinguished in the preceding text, it is now fitting for us to join with that same manner all things pertaining to the judgment of the partitions of life's ages, according to nature and the ways we have given for particular matters.

**Much** has been taught through the art of natural philosophy <note>original: "artē phīce"</note> regarding all the things of which this art is composed, providing a general demonstration of the rules and "roots" <note>The fundamental principles or foundations of the science.</note> of this entire craft. It is applied so that we might know all universal things; that is, the author applied those rules and roots to the completion of all the parts of which this entire art is generally composed. And when he says it is fitting to "join with it in this same manner," he means according to the ways of philosophy. What remains for us is the influence that celestial bodies have on the partition of a life. When he speaks of "according to nature," he refers to the natural science reached through philosophy; the "ways" he mentioned for particular things are the rules and roots he provided regarding birth charts.

**Just as** the judgments and estimations of particular things—which were taken from the aforementioned places in the explanation of birth charts—are presented, so too are the greater judgments and estimations taken from the regions themselves. These are the judgments in which the particulars observed in birth charts are generally contained: such as the forms and figures of bodies, the qualities of the soul, and differences in customs and laws. It is fitting for those who observe these things naturally to always adhere to the primary circumstance, which is more relevant than the others, so that they are never deceived by similarities in birth charts. For instance, if one were to say that a person born in Ethiopia <note>Used here as a general term for sub-Saharan Africa.</note> was adorned with white skin and straight hair, or that their soul's qualities were more domestic, or that they were more inclined to reason or were great investigators of things—or if they affirmed that the inhabitants of a wild foreign land possessed tame souls, or were muted and disagreed with reason—they would be in error. Likewise, one might be deceived concerning the customs and laws proper to each nation. For example, regarding marriages, if one should judge that Italians were decreed to marry their own sisters, it would be necessary to add to the judgment whether they were born in Egypt; or if one predicted that Egyptians would marry their mothers, that person would fail if the subject were born in Persia <note>The author is highlighting that what is a "fated" marriage in a birth chart must be interpreted through the lens of local legality; a "forbidden" marriage in one culture might be the "standard" relative indicated by the stars in another.</note>. It is fitting first to observe these general qualities in one's judgments and estimations, and then to add the particular quantities by which they will judge, so that the increases and decreases occurring in these things may be understood from this.

**And** just as the judgments of particular things were taken from the place we mentioned in the judgments of birth charts, the greater judgment is that which is taken from the inhabited regions and lands. In this judgment, all particular things pertaining to birth charts enter generally, such as the forms of bodies and their contours, the state of the souls, the diversities of customs, laws, and habits. It is fitting for one to study these things and always determine them within their own proper reason, which has a greater right to determine its own nature than all others, so that no one errs in the revolution of birth charts. For example, we might say that a certain person was born in the land of Ethiopia, and

<column-break/>

he will be of white color and smooth hair; or another born in the lands of Germany and Gaul, and he will be fair-skinned and curly-haired; and the latter are of gentle character and love the teaching of the sciences of things, while those in other lands are wild like beasts and animals and poorly instructed. For one could err in such things due to the temperaments <note>original: "crates," likely referring to the bodily humors or physical makeup.</note> or the customs and laws pertaining to a certain people. Thus, in marriages, it might be judged and said: "this man from Italy shall be joined to his sister," but one ought to say this only if the person was born in the land of Egypt. Or one might say of a man of Egypt that he will be joined to his mother, yet this would only be true if he were born in Persia. Generally, I say that we must first accept universal things insofar as we wish to judge, and afterward, we shall join the particulars with them; through this, we will understand how every matter will increase or decrease.

**Whatever** we have shown in this discourse, we have also shown entirely in the past commentaries <note>original: "glosīs"</note>. For the author taught us in this place the things that cause those who practice this art to err when they wish to judge nativities. He recounted these things individually so that when we know them, we will know how to guard ourselves against them and be freed from error when we wish to judge particular things pertaining to any birth chart. It has already been shown through the previous writings that those things which come from celestial bodies are divided into three parts. The first of these is that the judgment is decisive <note>original: "incisus"</note>; this comes from a great and powerful force that overcomes any other path. Following this are those things which come from a weaker force. The third, following that, are those things which come from a second, even weaker force; this is the force that can be changed and altered because of laws, customs, habits, and intentions. Because of this, it is necessary for one who wishes to look into this art to place his focus on four judgments pertaining to each of these virtues, and to look at one significance alongside another, and he shall judge according to the prevailing force. He can do this if he knows the things that cause one to err, which are of six kinds: first is the form of bodies; second, the figure of bodies; third, the state of the soul; fourth, customs; fifth, laws and habits; sixth, the region from which one comes. Regarding the first, second, and third kinds, he has already demonstrated their force in the treatise: how the signs and all other celestial figures give each nation of every climate its own property. Because of this, the practitioner of this art, when he finds that the celestial bodies signify a specific fortune for someone born, should look at that fortune alongside the general fortune pertaining to that nation of that climate where the person was born. He must do the same for the second and third kinds. For it is manifest that the figures of the people of any climate have a certain general similarity to one another, and likewise the customs of their souls. You should not judge that a person born in Ethiopia will be white; rather, you should say he will be less black than those of his own land. Nor should you judge that any Ethiopian or any Scot <note>original: "scoto"</note> will be exceptionally virtuous <note>original: "p̄bō," likely *probus*.</note> unless he transfers himself to another climate. <gloss>The virtues of celestial bodies are changed through the fourth and fifth kinds, which are customs and habits, because stronger things overcome lesser things, and the primary stronger virtues overcome the secondary weaker virtues.</gloss> Celestial bodies, however, change and transform the fourth and fifth kinds from one thing into another; as for instance, their position might make men mariners or laborers of the earth. Similarly, one born among wise men will be led by that custom to have something of the manner of wise men. And he who is born and nurtured among thieves will be led back by that very custom to do some of their works. Similarly, laws and habits change and transform outcomes. For example, the Jews are given a law regarding whom they may marry from among their kin; if the stars signify he will be joined to his sister, we shall judge for certain that he will be joined to her. Yet, if to one who is given a law that he may marry kin with certain persons excepted, and the stars signify he will marry a relative, we shall judge that he will marry a relative not prohibited by his law. Similarly, if you have a law where one is joined only to one woman...

# Treatise

...can only be joined to one. Similarly, one who is not subject to a law does not enter into a marriage. The sixth category among those things that cause error arises from the matter from which the birth comes: so that the good and prosperity of fathers reaches the sons, and that of the sons reaches the fathers; and you shall see this similarly in all other cases. Now, **Ptolemy** <note>Claudius Ptolemy, a 2nd-century scholar whose work "Tetrabiblos" formed the basis of Western astrology.</note> gave us a general rule regarding those things that cause error. And what he said is that we should first look at general statuses when we wish to provide a judgment, and afterward we will join with them other particular factors, so that we may know the increase and decrease that will happen there. He means that we must first take the general significance signifying any of those things—that is, once we know them, we will add the particular significance to them. Through this mixture, we will know the things pertaining to the status itself in every condition.

The reason for those six categories is that a grand and powerful virtue signifies each of them, so that in the forms of any climate and the figures of their sections, the category, customs, and matters are manifest: laws and the matter from which they come to signify were through great fires and strong eclipses, and similarly through the conjunctions of degrees. It is manifest that a greater power overcomes a lesser one. For example: when we see someone going to war, we will look to see if he has in his nativity an "abscission" <term>abscissio: a "cutting off" of the light or life-force, often used to predict the end of life</term> of the <term>hyleg: the "giver of life," a specific planet in a birth chart used to calculate lifespan</term>. If he has it, we will see that he could die in that very war. If he has no such cutting off of the life-giver, we will look at the hour of the war to see if the **fortunes** <note>Benefic or "lucky" planets, typically Jupiter and Venus.</note> testify to it, and we will judge that he shall escape. If the **infortunes** <note>Malefic or "unlucky" planets, typically Mars and Saturn.</note> testify, we will judge that he will die in the war. We will also see if he will be victorious; and if they are not favorable, we will judge that he will be struck and wounded. This is the manner in which we ought to judge in particular matters pertaining to each individual, by adding those things to the general ones.

Similarly also in the division of the times and hours of the native <note>The person for whom the horoscope is cast.</note>: such as the temporal divisions of years and days which provide similarities with each subsequent future event. Their qualities should be inspected so that they are never deceived by general occurrences which they have observed in nativities. It is necessarily fitting that a boy might work or take a wife, or do that which can only be done by one of greater age; or that a man of decrepit age might be judged to beget offspring or perform acts possible only for youth. Rather, it generally happens to them that they should add those things which they have grasped through the observation of times, from the years coming upon them, to those things which resemble them and can happen in those times.

It is fitting in every way that we do the same in the partitioning of the times of the native's life. We ought to place these after the diversity of temporal ages, and it even happens for any of the accidents that occur. Let us look into them in a way that we do not err at any hour in the general and simple accidents that we observe in nativities. Thus, we should not say that a small infant will perform great works or be married, or do any of the works that only a great man can do, or that an old man whose strength is annihilated will have a son, or do any of those things that only a boy can do. Yet it is fitting that we join to all of this those things which we understand from the judgments of times with those things that are suitable to them, for things suitable to those ages can happen in them.

**Ptolemy** gave us in this saying the things that cause error in judging those things that happen in the parts of a man's life. The rule he taught us is that we should look at what the stars signify in any time of life, and that we should adapt it to two things: one, the general things which signify great virtues; the other is the statuses pertaining to the native in all his ages, according to what his nativity signifies. For example: when we find that the stars signify for someone that he will be married this year, or will go on travels and journeys, we will look to see if this agrees with the significance of the "root" of the nativity <note>The original birth chart or foundational state.</note> and his age, and we will judge according to the greater power. What Ptolemy said

<column-break/>

in this is manifest if you look closely.

Because the same way—which is the same as the mode and the same and single order—holds for all temporal differences. For there is a universal nature embracing all men, which bears a similarity to the order of the **seven planets**.

For this is the one way and rule for all temporal diversities, and the one same course which follows a universal nature that encompasses all men, resembling the order of the seven planets.

He means to say that the natural life of man is divided into seven parts arranged according to the order of the seven planets.

This way or order takes its beginning from the first years and from the sphere closest to us, that is, the **lunar sphere** <note>The Moon's sphere, considered the closest to Earth in the geocentric model.</note>, and it is unfolded in the extreme years at the last sphere of the planets, which is called the sphere of **Saturn**. It must also be known that things happen in individual years that share a similarity with the nature of that planet which is in direct control of that year. The observation of this matter is necessary for understanding the general quality of each of these times. Their particular differences will be known from the properties inherent in them.

This course begins from the first age and the first sphere which is most around us, and this is the sphere of the Moon. It applies until the last age and the last sphere of the planets which is called the sphere of Saturn. It happens for certain in any part of the art that what occurs shares the nature of that planet resembling that same age. If it is a matter we ought to inspect to know the status of any time generally, then the particular diversities can be known from the proper things that are found.

He means to say that each of the seven ages agrees with the nature of the planet governing that age generally, and that many particular diversities happen in the status of any age, according to what is signified by the planets governing each year, day, month, and hour in that age. Since this is so, it is fitting that we first teach the facts of each of the seven ages, and afterward we will teach the rules by which we can know the particular diversities. It is manifest that **physicians** <note>original: "phici"</note> divide the life of man into four parts: they have set the first part as the whole of childhood (and this is divided into the time of infancy and others); they have set the second as the whole time of youth; they have set the third as the whole of old age; and they have set the fourth as the whole of senility <note>Extreme old age or dotage.</note>. When one looks well into the partitioning of life, it is naturally divided into seven parts, just as the astrologers have divided it. Nevertheless, the division of the physicians agrees with the rule of physics, because the art of physics looks only at things manifest to the senses and sight.

For because the **Moon** <note>original: "luna"</note> disposes and rules the first four years of the infant—which number resembles the four years we understand—the infant receives a tenderness and weakness of body and rapid growth. In this age, there is also a greater and more frequent watery nourishment, a light alteration of its form, and its soul is held as weak and imperfect, according to what happens from those things that occur concerning the part of the infant's soul on account of the Creator <note>original: "opificem"</note>.

Thus the Moon is the governor of the age of infancy, and this is in the first four years in a more tender time. They are as such as I said was stated regarding the four kinds; and because of this, the body of the infant is moist and not well completed, growing quickly, and its food is for the greater part liquid, and its appearance changes quickly, and its soul is not yet complete nor so strong as pertains to the accidents that come...

# Book Four

...they come on behalf of the operative part of the infant's soul. We have already shown in the chapter on life that the **greater years** <term>greater years: in astrology, the "maximi" or longest orbital cycles attributed to planets, used to predict long-term fate</term> of the **Moon** are 108. It is demonstrated through astrology that the Moon runs its circle through the firmament in approximately 27 days; and if we divide 108 by 27, it results in the four years of the Moon which **Ptolemy** <note>original: "Ptol."</note> spoke of. Since the Moon resembles the state of an infant—being close to the earth, possessing much humidity, and changing its appearance quickly—it is fitting that the Moon should be the governor of the infant for twice four years <note>The text here discusses the calculation, though the standard Ptolemaic age for the Moon is the first 4 years.</note> in a similar way. For the strength of an infant's body is not yet firm because it is close to birth, and its nature is very fluid and changing due to excessive moisture. Because of this, many astrologers believed that a birth should not be judged until these first four "humid" years have passed. However, **Ptolemy** maintains that we ought to judge the birth from the hour one is born, because nothing happens to the newborn at any time except by the significance of the planets; one who understands this well can know what will happen to the child at any time, and how an infant might die in these four years without a specific indication of this in the birth chart.

And since the second planet, which is called **Mercury**, is the master of the disposition of the following 10 years—which are the years of childhood—they are called the "second years" because the master himself rules the number of half of 20 years <note>original: "rr. annox," referring to Mercury's "minor years" which are 20; half of that is 10.</note>. Within this span of years, the effects of the intellect and the reasoning of the soul become manifest; the child enters a stage as if he were a plant of instruction, and the roots of the soul's qualities are planted in him. In these years, through those things which are adapted to his character, discipline and learning shine forth, and he rises up, awakened to the practice of his first skills.

Because of this, the governor of the 10 years following those [first four] is the age of childhood, and it is the second age; it is ruled by the second planet, **Mercury**, who is master of half of 20 years. Therefore, the person begins in this age to understand and to have reason, as if the branches of wisdom and the roots of virtues were being planted in his soul. The properties of the works he will perform through learning become apparent in them, and he will go forward understanding the first manner of his craft.

The age of childhood certainly lasts from the beginning of the fourth year until he applies himself to a woman; this can be until the completion of 14 years. We have taught that the **minor years** of Mercury's course are 20, and the greatest portion that can be there is half; because of this, **Mercury** has two concordances with the age of childhood: one because he is the master of the second sphere, so it is fitting he has the second age; the other because he has half of 20 years, which is 10, and that is the length of the age of childhood. In this age, the soul's power takes hold and gives substance, and the time begins when the seeds of works and of his own virtues are planted in it. These things that are planted will be drawn out according to the habits he practiced in this age; and the habits he uses will be according to the environment, the law, and the custom suitable to the people of that climate, and according to the doctrine in which the person was educated.

And because **Venus** presides as ruler over the disposition of the subsequent 7 years—which are the years of adolescence and are called the third age—and since this number of years matches her own orbital period <note>original: "circūuolutiōis equanť," referring to Venus's minor years being 8, but here applied to a 7-year period of growth</note>, the flow of semen and the gathering of its abundance takes its beginning, and the adolescent is moved toward the acts of Venus [love and procreation]. We say this is the time in which the soul takes on a sort of "surging" likeness <note>original: "bolis̄mā," likely from the Greek *embolismos*, implying a sudden interruption or turbulent insertion of passion into the life cycle.</note>, touching hardly a minimal portion of abstinence and reaching for the greatest impulse of desire in all possible matters of Venus; they run into a tempestuous lust, deception, and blindness of mind in all they wish for.

And because the governor of the third age, which is the age of adole-

<column-break/>

scence, arriving in the 7 years after those we have mentioned, is **Venus**, according to the years of her own proper course; because of this, the movement of semen begins in this age, and the passions <note>original: "ira," though likely referring to the heat of passion in this context</note> which perform their journeys from it are changed toward acts of lust. In this age, the souls are "canine" <note>original: "canine," perhaps implying a lack of restraint or a biting, restless hunger</note> and have little abstinence; it is the age of falling in love and of desiring whatever pertains to lust; the person deceives himself and ruins himself for such things, whatever they may be, that enter his will.

**Venus** has with this third age concordances of her sphere, and another concordance of her minor course which is as many years as this age has. For we find that **Ptolemy** placed in the *Chapter on Life* that the body of Venus is around the 8th degree and the body of Jupiter at the 12th, as we showed in that place; and we find here that this matter follows and gives as many years to each of these two beneficial planets as each holds, so that they naturally signify that many years. And since one thing has diverse significations in the way of having a signification in any of them according to what is fitting for each state, he himself revealed in the *Chapter on Marriages* that **Venus** by her own proper nature is the mistress of the entire nature of lust; and because of this, she signifies in this age the things he spoke of in such a general signification.

And because the **Sun**, the master of the middle sphere, disposes one set of 19 years—which are noted in the fourth place and are the middle in order—and is said to be in charge of those assigned to youth; we decree that the youthful soul has a concern for works of power and the fruitful disposition of life, as well as its direction. We say the soul is altered from mocking, playful, and deceptive qualities toward the health of the soul, the preservation of modesty, and the desire for honor.

Because the master of the fourth age, which is the middle one in the arrangement, and the master of the middle sphere is the **Sun**, and the number of his years is 19, he makes it so that souls are masters in all their deeds and take power over them. They are drawn to direct and govern the necessary things of life, so that they might be upright and quiet, and changed from the wanderings, games, and great error [of youth] toward abstinence, peace of soul, and its honesty, loving honor.

The **Sun** has three concordances with this age: after the concordance of his sphere, the second concordance is of his minor years with the length of time of this [fourth] age; for the **Sun** is the prince of all the planets. In this age, a man is stronger and of greater virtue, because it is the age of youth; and because the **Sun** naturally signifies all natural things that do not incline more to one side than another, it is found that in this age he signifies things that are natural to man, because with them and through them the world is youthful; and these are the things he narrated.

After the **Sun**, however, because **Mars** rules for 15 years in the fifth place—which are the years of robustness and vigor and are equal to the number of his own proper rotation—the weight of life, impediment, and adversity weigh upon the person. Their souls, along with their bodies, endure anxieties and impediments; the decline of the body is almost felt and understood; and the man will perform great works from which labor will come to him, the completion of which he seeks before the approach of his death.

And **Mars** rules in the fifth age after the Sun, and it is the age in which there is pride and magnanimity; and these are 15 years, as many as his proper course. For in this age many "pestilences" <note>metaphorical for hardships or intense trials</note> happen; and the strength of life happens in the souls, while anxieties and sorrows happen in the bodies...

# Treatise

...so many: and he proceeds in understanding and sensing the diminishing of the body: and it makes a man work more at those tasks in which he must labor and suffer; and before he dies, he has to accomplish these things.

**Mars** has two correspondences in this age. One is the correspondence of its sphere with the fifth age <note>The "fifth age" is the age of the Sun (maturity), roughly ages 35 to 56. Mars traditionally rules the following stage.</note>. The other is the correspondence of its minor cycle with the length of this age. And **Ptolemy** says this brings "magnanimity" <note>original: "magnanimitatem"; here meaning greatness of spirit or courage</note> because of sense and wisdom: for a man knows and learns through the experience of things. Because Mars, by its nature when it participates with the **Sun**, inclines a man toward works of its own nature, it happens that the works and habits a man had in the age of the Sun incline toward those things which Ptolemy said concerning the works of Mars.

Next, however, we assign the twelve years of old age—equal to his own proper rotation—to **Jupiter**, who claims the sixth place for the old man. During these years, a man withdraws from the labors of the body and from exhausting work, as well as from the anxiety of manual labor. He no longer commits his soul to danger; instead, adopting a healthy habit of mind, he will study how to preserve himself well. By his greatness of spirit, he will neglect shameful things and be seen as provident, desiring good in all things, as well as a speaker and a consoler. In this time also, he will be most concerned with liberty, honor, and a good reputation, along with modesty and reverence.

We find that the sixth planet, which is **Jupiter**, governs the age of old age; and these are 12 years, just as his own cycles are. Then a man is drawn to perform things for himself: he does not wish to labor or suffer, nor to put himself in danger. Instead of his previous life and place, he is drawn toward a good life and good journeys; he removes his soul from vain things and evil company. He thinks on all things honest and good, and he honors and gladdens himself. In this age, he is led back to gaining honor, fame, and goodness, with modesty and an entirely good existence.

**Jupiter** has two correspondences in the age of old age, which is the sixth age from the beginning of the 57th year until the end of the 68th year. The first is the correspondence of its sphere. The second is the correspondence of its minor cycle <note>The "minor cycle" of Jupiter is 12 years, which matches the duration of this "age" in the text's system.</note> with the quantity of this age. If you have understood the previous glosses well, you should understand these words of **Ptolemy**.

After these come the years of **Saturn**, arranged as if placed at the very end, which are the years of decrepitude <note>original: "senij"; referring to extreme old age or the final stage of life</note>; they do not terminate until the exit from the vital places. Our bodily movement becomes colder, our delight becomes heavy, and our appetite diminishes; likewise, the nature of man undergoes a swift decline. This quality strips away the life of man: it impresses hindrance, sadness, and a meager sustaining of things because of the weakness of his movements.

The final age belongs to **Saturn**, which is the age of decrepitude until the end of life. This is the age in which coldness and heaviness occur: the movement of the body and the taste for delights decrease, and nature declines swiftly. For in this state, human life is completed; infirmities and sadness happen to a man, and he cannot sustain things because all his movements are failing.

Because there are very few who pass 100 years of life, those who reach these days are like those who lose all their works. **Ptolemy** gave the seventh age to **Saturn** and did not pass beyond it; for when

<column-break/>

we add the minor cycle of **Saturn**, which is 30 years, the number reaches 98 years. After this, we return to the **Moon**, which signifies the cycle of this work. This signifies a debility of the soul in the body just as in the age of infants, but much more so: for the face of Saturn changes the coldness and superfluity of humors to the nature of the Moon, which changes quickly and has much moisture. It happens that after Saturn, the Moon has 25 years—equal to her minor cycle—and not just 4 years; for that number of 4 years was placed in the age of infancy because it was fitting there. For this reason, I firmly hold that teeth are born again a second time for those passing the age of Saturn <note>A reference to the folk belief that the extremely elderly enter a "second childhood" where they might grow new teeth or hair.</note>. And because very few reach this eighth age, Ptolemy did not speak of it and included it within the seventh age.

These, therefore, are the properties of the qualities of the times which appear according to the general things of nature.

In this manner are the states of the times according to general and universal nature.

**Ptolemy** wishes to say that the general accidents pertaining to any part of the life of any man are those things which he narrated through the natures of the planets.

As for the particular properties of the times: since we ought to observe them only from the properties of the birth <note>i.e., the individual's natal horoscope</note>, we have considered that which appeared universal to us from the **Hyleg** <term>Hyleg: from the Persian 'haylāj', the "life-giver" or "releasor." A specific point in a horoscope used to determine the duration of life.</term> which is the ruler. However, our observation in these matters did not bring knowledge from any one of them individually, but from all of them, just as was done in the span of life.

For in the manner of particular states which happen through the times—which are fitting to be according to the births—we take them universally from the principal **Hylegs** which we mentioned before. We shall not take the meaning from just one of them, as we do regarding life, but from all the Hylegs.

After **Ptolemy** gave us the rules for general and particular accidents, he divided the rule into two parts: one is universal and the other particular. The universal is always taken from the **Atazir** <term>Atazir: a method of planetary direction where points are "moved" through the zodiac to predict the timing of events.</term> of the four Hylegs. The particular is always taken through the **Almuten** <note>original: "alynthie"; likely referring to the planet with the most dignity at a certain point</note> and through the cycles of the planets in years, months, and days.

For that **Hyleg** which is taken from the **Ascendant** <note>original: "ascendente"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note>, we use for accidents happening to the body and for journeys.

We shall work through the Hyleg taken from the **Ascendant** regarding accidents in the bodies and in future journeys.

He wishes to say that the degree to which the Atazir of the Ascendant reaches in any year signifies that which happens to the body concerning health and sickness. And because it is equal to the degree of the Atazir of the West <note>The descendant</note> signifying journeys, it is fitting that we take the significance of journeys from this degree and its opposite.

Those things which are considered from the **Part of Fortune** <note>original: "parte fortune"; an Arabic part or mathematical point in the chart representing prosperity</note>, we use for matters of substance.

And we shall work through the Hyleg taken from the **Part of Fortune** in matters pertaining to riches.

He wishes to say that when the Atazir of the Part of Fortune reaches a point, the significance of riches and substance is taken.

From the **Moon**, we observe the qualities of the soul and marriages. Those things which are perceived from the **Sun**, we take for matters of worth and high status; from the **Midheaven** <note>original: "medio celi"; the highest point in the sky at birth</note>, we find them in all other qualities of one's being.

# Fourth [Book]

...particular qualities as we follow in works, friends, and children.

¶ **And** we shall also operate through that which is received from the Moon regarding the states of the soul and marriages; and through that which is received from the Sun regarding honor and nobility; and through that which is received from the Midheaven <note>original: "medio celi"; the 10th house, representing career and public life</note> in other particular states, such as offices, children, and friendships.

¶ **He means to say** that the degree to which the *ataçir* <term>ataçir: an Arabic astrological term (at-tasyir) for "direction" or "profection," a method of advancing a point in a chart to predict the timing of future events</term> of the Moon applies will signify in that same year the states of the soul and marriage. And the Sun's direction signifies honor and nobility by their properties, because the Sun is a greater prince than the other planets. Similarly, as we have demonstrated, the 10th house signifies offices and children; it receives the significance pertaining to them from the degree to which its *ataçir* reaches. And since this is so, it follows that we should perform the *ataçir* for the seven planets, and for the twelve houses, and for the Part of Fortune, taking the specific indication of those things which they demonstrated in the root of the birth <note>original: "radice natiuitatis"; the natal chart</note> from the place to which the *ataçir* of each of them arrives. This is what Ptolemy wished to show in this place, and Hermes has already demonstrated this similarly in one of his books. Ptolemy will demonstrate all these *ataçir* later on, and how the significance is taken from them, and how the parts of life are divided.

¶ **For we**, acting in this way, do not understand more than one single planet—whether it be a benefic <note>original: "fortuna"</note> or a malefic <note>original: "infortuna"</note>—as the master of the matter, which we do not doubt to be just and proper.

¶ **And** since we shall operate in the manner we have predicted, there will be no disposer of a thing except for one single planet, whether it be a benefic or a malefic, and this is correct.

¶ **He means to say** that when we perform the *ataçir* of the planets, the houses, and the Part of Fortune, each of them will apply to a degree which is under the disposition of a single planet, whether it be a benefic or a malefic. And Ptolemy gives the reasons why we must perform the *ataçir* of each of the aforesaid and not omit any of them.

¶ **Since** at the same hour, contrary accidents often occur: as when someone loses one of his relatives, whose heir he becomes; or an illness lies heavy upon him, and yet he is seen to be living at leisure or has procreated offspring; and similar accidents frequently happening in the body and in the soul, in riches and power, as well as in other good or evil accidents. One and the same quality arises so necessarily that in all these things a man incurs good or evil. Yet in times of intense fortune or misfortune, it is perhaps possible for something similar to happen when all the benefics or malefics equally meet all the *alhyleg* <term>alhyleg: also called "hyleg," the point in a chart that signifies the life-force or the person themselves</term> or many of them, which clearly happens successively. Because of this, human nature can hardly reach the intensity of both at once, due to a sudden decline and an exit from balance <note>original: "tempeꝛie"; a state of tempered balance or health</note> occurring from the alteration of good and bad things. Therefore, in the predicted manner, the matters of all the *alhyleg* places are understood.

¶ **Because** many times contrary accidents happen at one and the same time, so that a man will lose some relative of his and inherit some substance from him; or an illness will happen to him, and then honor will come to him, or his service will be vacant, and children will be born to him, and many other accidents which occur. For the states of the body

<column-break/>

and soul, of riches and honor, and good and bad accidents are not all entirely of one single kind. All these things may be fulfilled in or for a man, or all may be lacking. It is possible, however, that something happens which seems or is likened to such in times that are greatly and excessively unfortunate, or greatly fortunate. For it happens to men's *hyleg*, or the majority of them, that they arrive at all the benefics or all the malefics; and this happens rarely, because the nature of man is not sufficient to endure such things, for he is quickly inclined and recedes from balance because of the swift changing of good and bad things. And in this predicted way, we shall divide the activity of the *hylegs*.

¶ **It is useful** that we understand in this ninth chapter that when he says "hyleg," he means for a specific matter or for the house having significance in some specific thing in the natal chart, and that will be the "hyleg" of that matter. The course of his word runs upon one thing: that when you have performed the *ataçir* of the significator of any matter, we will find the degree to which it applies signifying one thing, while another degree to which the significator of another matter applies signifies something else. For example: we will perform the *ataçir* of Mercury for the significance of the rational soul, and we will perform the *ataçir* of Mars for boldness and the magnanimity of the heart. We will find that the place to which Mercury and Mars apply will be strong and powerful, and the place to which the Moon applies will be in the term of a benefic. Whence, in such a case, we will judge that the subject of such a birth will seek out philosophy at this time, and in lowly things he will have good temperance, and Mars will add to him strength of heart and a misfortune <note>original: "exfortunium"</note> through him.

¶ **And** regarding the points meeting the *alhyleg* places, they are not only to be considered as the end of life <note>original: "exitus vite"</note> (as in the space of life), but we judge that everything must be looked into. Likewise, we should observe not only their bodily, opposite, or square <note>original: "tetragonalem"</note> meeting, but also those joined to them by trine and sextile.

¶ **And** regarding the points meeting the *hylegs*, it is not fitting that we take only the "killing" places <note>original: "loca itersiciẽtia"; points that signify the end of life</note> as we do for the length of life; rather, let us take them all. It is not fitting that we take only the places meeting bodily, or by opposition, or the fourth [square]; rather, we shall similarly take those meeting by the third [trine] and sixth [sextile].

¶ **We have** already shown in the chapter on life that the "killing" places are those in which the malefics are, or their rays—Saturn and Mars—and the degree of the setting [Descendant]. And Ptolemy says that it is not enough in the *ataçir* of any significator to look only at the "killing" places; rather, we must look at other aspects which corrupt and harm, so that we may know through this what will happen in any time throughout the whole life.

¶ **The times** also in each *alhyleg* we shall first attribute to the planet existing in that same degree of the *alhyleg*, or to the one associated with it in the figure. If no planet remains in that degree, and none is associated with it in the figure, it follows that we assign it to the closer planet preceding that degree, until we reach that which regards the predicted degree by the following degree. Let this be the aspect from this one to that one according to the succession of the signs; thereafter, let the following times be given to the aforementioned...

...until we are joined to that which follows. And we decree that this must be done similarly in all cases.

**E**ndowing the first period in any *hyleg* <term>hyleg: the "giver of life," a specific planet or point in a horoscope (like the Sun, Moon, or Ascendant) used to calculate the length of life and major life shifts</term> to the planet that is in the actual degree of the *hyleg*, or which shares in its configuration. And if no planet is in that same degree, or does not share in its configuration, it is proper that we give its place to the nearer degree before it, until we reach that which will aspect the degree following its own degree; and let that aspect be according to the order of the signs. After this, we will give the time that comes next to that which we have mentioned, until we reach the one that comes last; and so we shall do in all things.

**G**ravity is found in these words. He means to say, however, that if you look at the degree of the *hyleg* which you wish to direct, and there is some planet at the hour of birth or the rays <note>original: "rady"; the astrological aspects or beams cast by a planet</note> of some planet, that planet itself will be the "ruling dispositor" until the direction reaches another degree in which there is some planet or the rays of a planet. That second planet will then be the dispositor of the *hyleg* until the direction reaches a third planet or its rays; and that third planet will be the dispositor of the *hyleg*. You shall proceed in this manner, and the planet which it meets—namely the *ataçir* <term>ataçir: from the Arabic *at-tasyir*, meaning "direction"; a method of moving a point in the chart forward by a certain number of degrees to represent the passage of years</term>—in that time will be the dispositor of the *hyleg*. It will hold as much of the lifespan as the degrees that are between the degree where it began to dispose until the degree of the next dispositor that follows.

**P**lanets existing in their own *terms* <term>terms: (Latin: *termini*) specific subdivisions of an astrological sign, where different planets hold more power than the sign's primary ruler</term> shall also be established by us as some of those planets which we have observed and placed as quasi-dispositors.

**E**nd we shall take one of the planets through which they operate in the place of the dispositor of the planets that are in their own terms.

**V**ult—He means to say that the lords of the terms dispose of life similarly to the final periods, because each of them disposes of the *hyleg* as long as the division lasts in its own term. And when you wish to know how long its other time will last, we look at how far the *ataçir* is after it enters that term until its exit from life, and that planet will be the lord of those years. And if it happens to be in that same term or aspects it, it will be the dispositor of the *hyleg*—namely, the lord of the house—through two parts: one because the *hyleg* reaches the term itself, and the other because it is the lord of the term. And in this way we shall do in the terms of the houses, exaltations, and triplicities <note>original: "triplicitatum"; the four groups of three signs associated with the elements: Fire, Earth, Air, and Water</note>.

**A**ccounting of the years, moreover, is conveniently given by the number of degrees of longitude. Therefore, for the *hyleg* taken from the Ascendant, the number of years will be assigned equal to the number of times of the *ascensions* <term>ascensions: the time it takes for a sign of the zodiac to rise above the eastern horizon; this varies depending on the latitude (climate) of the birthplace</term> of the climate in which the birth occurred. For the *hyleg* found from the Midheaven, the years shall be granted whose number equals the number of times of the transit through the Midheaven. In other *hylegs* taken from elsewhere, we shall proceed in this order: according to their proximity to the angles, we shall take the number of the rising or setting ascensions, or the transit through the Midheaven, just as we explained in the narration of the span of life. In this aforementioned way, therefore, the ruling factors of the final times will be discovered.

**C**onveniently, we should give the number of degrees of elongation as the number of years of the *hyleg's* term. For that which is taken from the Ascendant, we will give as many years as the ascensions of the climate in which the birth occurs; and for the *hyleg* taken from the Midheaven, we will give as many years as the number of times of the transit through the Midheaven.

<column-break/>

And this is the matter in other *hylegs* accepted through other things according to this [rule] and according to their priority: for those which are near the angles, we shall take from the number of ascensions or descensions, or from the transit through the Midheaven, as we demonstrated in the things we narrated regarding the time of life. In such a way, we will know the universal temporal positions.

**S**i—If you have understood what we narrated in the chapter on life, you will understand this easily. For what Ptolemy <note>original: "Pto."; Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century author of the *Tetrabiblos*, the foundational text for this commentary</note> means to say in this is that we add the number of completed years that have passed in life to the ascensions of the *significator* <note>original: "significatoris"; the planet or point that "signifies" a specific topic like health or wealth</note> and the circle of hours in which it is. We place all of that in the arc of ascensions of that circle, and where it arrives, there will be the place of the "division" of the significator. The method of how we calculate this number is that if the Ascendant was the significator, we add the number of past years to its ascensions in the town where he was born, and afterwards we place this in the arc. And if it was in the Midheaven, we add the number of past years to its ascensions in the "direct circle" <note>original: "circulo directo"; the celestial equator or right ascension</note> and place that in the arc. However, if the significator is in other places, we will count the hours of elongation of that same significator; afterwards, we take its ascensions in the direct circle and its ascensions in the town, and add to either ascension the number of past years. We place this in the arc over two places, and two different degrees will result for us. We take a sixth part of that which is between those two degrees and multiply it by the hours of elongation of the significator. We add this to the degree that resulted for us through the ascensions of the direct circle if it is less than the degree that resulted for us through the ascensions of the city; and if it is more, we subtract it from it. That which results after the addition or subtraction is the place of the division of the significator. It is manifest that the hours of elongation of the 11th house from the angle of the Midheaven are 2; the hours of elongation of the 9th house are 4; the hours of elongation of the 12th house from the angle of the Midheaven are 4; and the same for the 8th house. The partition of the houses opposite to these is of the same quality. This is the way we can know the places to which the *hylegs* arrive in any year. However, how the *hylegs* come to a planet or the rays of a planet, we revealed in the chapter on life.

**D**ominatrices—The ruling mistresses of the years' affairs will be known when we have taken the number of years from birth. Starting from each of the places of the *hyleg*, we project one year for each of the signs according to their succession; the lord of that sign in which the number terminates will be reserved.

**E**t—And we shall know the disposition made for the years by taking the number of years from birth and projecting them from any of the *hyleg* places according to the order of the signs, giving one year to each sign. We shall take the dispositor from the sign in which that same number falls.

**J**ā—We have already shown there that all the *hylegs* he narrated in this chapter mean the significators of things that are to be signified in the birth. And what he wishes to narrate in this saying is the *profection* <term>profection: (Latinized from Arabic: *al-inthiha*) an ancient technique where a point in the chart is advanced by one sign for every year of life</term>, so that each sign disposes for one year. Thus the revolution of a sign occurs once every 12 years until the end of life; all astrologers know this.

**H**oc—We shall do this same thing in the months. For taking the number of months that have passed since birth, we will project 28 days for each of the signs starting from the places that dispose of the year.

**E**t—And we shall do such as this in the months: for we shall take the number of months from the month of birth and project it from the places disposing in that year; and we will give 28 days to each sign.

**V**ult—He means to say that when we know the sign of the profection of the year for any significator, and we wish to know the sign of the profection of the month, we look...

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for calculating the timing of life events using "profections"—an astrological technique where the chart is symbolically rotated by a certain amount for each year, month, or day. It specifically details how to divide the 360-degree zodiac into periods of time to identify which planet "rules" a specific moment in a person's life.</meta>

### Fourth Book

...the past months of that year: for any month of 28 days, we will extract the number of months from the sign of the *profection* <note>original: "al-inthiha" (Latinized as alyntbie), a technique where the positions of the natal chart are advanced by one sign per year, and then subdivided into months and days</note> of the year, giving each sign one month. Wherever that number falls, that is the *profection* sign of the month. Thus, there will be 13 months of profection, because 13 [lunar] months follow one after another so that the first month of the second year falls in the second year of the profection. These 28 days have another logic: they are the average between the number of days in a lunar month and the number of days in which the Moon travels through the 12 signs. It turns out that the days of a profection month are 28 days, 2 hours, and 3 [minutes]; however, Ptolemy <note>Claudius Ptolemy, the 2nd-century mathematician and astronomer whose work "Tetrabiblos" is the foundation of this text</note> omitted the 2 hours and the third so that the number would be easier to handle.

¶ Similarly, we shall do this with days. Taking the number of days from the day of birth, we will extract them from the locations of the months, assigning two days and a third to each sign.

¶ We do the same for days by taking the count from the day of birth and extracting them from the locations of the months, giving each sign two days and a third.

¶ It is appropriate that each sign be two days and a sixth part of one day, so that the profection of days is continuous with the profection of the month. I believe the scribe who first copied this book made an error, and that error has remained ever since. For when we give each sign 2 days and a sixth part of a day, it comes to 12 degrees, 52 minutes, and about three hours for each degree <note>original: "grata vnius gradus"</note>. This whole calculation is quite easy, and anyone can understand it simply.

¶ Furthermore, it is proper for us to observe the distance between the existing locations of times. This provides no small help in the knowledge of future events occurring within those times.

¶ And it follows that we should look at the profections <note>original: "profectas"</note> falling in the locations of times, because this greatly assists in predicting events that will happen over time.

¶ The locations of times are the places in which the indicators <note>original: "signatores"</note> of the root <note>The "root" refers to the original natal horoscope or birth chart</note> change, where the division of the *hyleg* is located, and where the profection applies.

¶ We shall therefore observe the existence of Saturn in the locations of universal times; Jupiter in the locations of years; the Sun, Mars, Venus, and Mercury in the locations of months; and the Moon in the locations of days.

¶ We will also see how Saturn falls in the locations of universal times, how Jupiter falls in the locations of years, how the Sun, Mars, Venus, and Mercury fall in the locations of months, and how the Moon passes through the locations of days.

¶ The locations of universal times are the spaces that fall between the direction <note>original: "directio," referring to the *ataçir* mentioned on the previous page</note> of the *hyleg* from one planet or its rays until it applies to another planet or its own rays. Similarly, they are the "terms" <term>terms: specific sub-divisions of a zodiac sign ruled by different planets</term> in which the division of the *hyleg* falls. The locations of years are the signs of the profection of the *hyleg*; the locations of months are the signs of the profection of the indicators of months; and the locations of days are the signs and degrees of the profection of the indicators of each day and hour.

¶ From the planets of universal times, we will consider the "lords" <note>the ruling planets</note> over the existence of the future, and its completion.

¶ And we will judge by the planets governing the universal times regarding the existence of an "accident" <term>accident: in this context, an event, circumstance, or change in a person's life</term> and its fulfillment.

¶ This means that the strong indicators that have power in the participation of life are the planets governing the *hylegs*. These planets govern in two ways: one is the planet from which the *hyleg* separates or to which it applies; the other is the lord of the "term" of the profection.

¶ We will also look at the lords of particular times, observing the likeness of things existing in those places to see whether there is an increase or decrease; for this will be the cause of the strength or weakness of the accidents.

¶ And we will judge the governors of particular times by whether they help or harm that event. According to the concordance of many things falling in those locations, they will either strengthen the accidents

<column-break/>

or they will weaken them, according to their discordance.

¶ This means that we will judge by the lords of the profection and by the planets that were in the locations of the times. If they are in agreement with the governors of the universal times, they will help them in their significance; if they are contrary, they will harm them.

¶ For the indicator of the general quality and the space of time is the location of the *hyleg* and every universal time that is the lord of the terms. This is because each of these stars in the birth itself had a likeness to the locations of the stars that previously held the governorship.

¶ In general, that which signifies the universal state for a quantity of time is the location of the *hyleg*, the distribution of universal times, and the lord of the time; for each of these planets was a precursor in that same birth from the beginning, along with the locations of the governing planets.

¶ This means that the universal signifies of accidents proper to all parts of life are taken from the locations of the *hylegs*, and from the place where the governor of the universal time applies in that period. It is clear that during that time, there is a concordance in the root of the birth between each of these things and the locations of the *hyleg* to which the direction <note>original: "ataçir"</note> applies. When the *hylegs* apply there, whatever that concordance signifies will happen.

¶ But whether the quality of the accident is good or evil depends on the properties of the natural qualities of the lords of the times and their "complexion" <note>the mixture of their elemental qualities, like hot, cold, wet, or dry</note> in doing good or evil, as well as on their likeness or contrariety to the ruling thing from the beginning.

¶ We will know if an accident is good or contrary through the state of the nature of the governor of the times and its complexion in working good or evil, and through its concordance or discordance from the beginning with that which it governs.

¶ This means we will know the mode of the accident and what it will be like in any part of life through the planets operating at that time, through the mixture of one with others, and by what they signify according to the participation they had with the governor in the root of the birth.

¶ At what specific time the future event will occur is judged from the qualities of the signs ruling the year and month, which have opportunities based on the locations of the future events. It is also judged from the qualities occurring when the planets, as well as the Sun and Moon, are in the signs of the year and month. For the planets that reached those aforementioned locations from the hour of the beginning—which is called the birth—and were suitably associated with them in the figure of the hour of existence, will signify good in the future thing. When the Moon is in the contrary position, it will announce evil for it.

¶ And we can know at what time that accident will specifically appear through the state of the signs governing that year and month, or by seeing if it aspects the locations signifying that accident. This is also known by the state when the planets, Sun, and Moon enter the signs governing the times of years and months. For planets that agree with the aforementioned locations from the beginning of birth—when they enter these locations, if there is concordance—will bring about a suitable good in 그 thing; and in the contrary case, evil.

¶ When the planets and the figures of the "retreating" <note>referring to retrograde motion or receding aspects</note> stars are suitable and helping any indicator of the root, they signify that the thing will be completed, whether it be good or evil, until the time of concordance is demonstrated. However, if the planets and the indicators of the root similarly reach that which the *hyleg* signified in the root of the birth, that accident will be helpful; and if it is contrary, it will be harmful.

¶ But those which are unsuitably associated with them—for example, in opposition <note>180 degrees apart</note> or in a square aspect <note>90 degrees apart</note> or in the contrary "balance" <note>original: "balaiç"</note>—will be the cause of adversity.

### Fourth Treatise

¶ And if the particular indicators agree with the general ones, such that they are in opposition beyond what was in the harmony of the sign <note>original: "baiz," from the Arabic *bayt*, meaning a house or zodiac sign</note>, they will produce evil.

¶ Whenever any of those celestial bodies is in accord with some significator <note>a planet or point that "signifies" a specific area of life, like wealth or health</note>, evil will come through that cause. We have already shown the significators of the years which are present, and the signs and degrees to which the *hylegs* <note>the "givers of life," the most vital points in a birth chart</note> of the profection <note>original: "alyntbie," from the Arabic *al-intihā'*, a technique where the chart is advanced by one sign per year to time events</note> apply.

¶ In other qualities, they will produce nothing.

¶ Nor will they produce anything in other states.

¶ Those "other states" in which they do nothing are those where the significators apply to such places that neither add to nor subtract from their power.

¶ If these same planets have power in those times, they will experience an excess and increase of future good or evil. This will happen even more when they have power over the occasion itself, even if they lacked it at those times when they were only shown. Indeed, this is because they were the dispositors <note>planets that "rule" the sign where another planet is located</note> at the beginning of the birth <note>the "nativity"</note>.

¶ And if they rule in the times and places already mentioned, the nature of that accident <note>an "accident" in this context refers to a specific event or occurrence in a person's life</note> will prevail; it will be strengthened, whether it be good or evil. This will be even stronger when they do not rule simply because they are lords of the times, but also because they are the dispositors in the root of the birth.

¶ When they rule any part in the disposition of any year, and are in the places of the disposition or aspect them, the nature of that accident will prevail and grow greatly, whether good or evil; and it will be stronger if those same parts were dispositors in the root of the birth.

¶ And so that good or evil may happen equally to the native <note>the person for whom the horoscope is cast</note> in all his affairs, it sometimes occurs either because all the types of *hyleg* or the general causes concur in one and the same place, or because they are separated from one another and encounter things at the same time, or because all or many of the fortunes <note>benefic planets like Jupiter and Venus</note> or misfortunes <note>malefic planets like Saturn and Mars</note> meet together.

¶ That native will succeed in all things or fail in all things when all the manners of *hylegs*, or the greater part of them, are in one and the same place or spread out, and it happens at one and the same time when they all meet the fortunes, or all meet the misfortunes, or the greater part of them.

¶ He has already taught us that each planet, the twelve houses, and the "Part of Fortune" <note>a calculated point in the chart representing prosperity</note> have their own significance in all the states of the native. And if all apply at one time to some fortune or fortunes, all the states of the native will be fulfilled and turn toward the good; and this is the best fortune that can be. But this rarely happens. And if all apply to some misfortune or misfortunes, the native will fail in all things; and this is the greatest misfortune that can be, and this also rarely happens. 

Indeed, I have heard for certain of a man who had great riches and many sons and vassals. When a great flood of water arrived, it took away all his riches, sons, and vassals. He alone escaped upon a camel with one of his sons whom he took in his arms. When he believed he was in a place safe from the flood, he descended from the camel; the camel fled. Leaving his son there, he followed the camel. Then a lion came, took the son, and ate him. When the man wanted to catch the camel, the camel struck him in the eyes, so that he remained blind and deprived of his sons and vassals.

¶ In this way, then, according to the natural mode of the matter, we prognosticating the things of the times. As for the particular souls by which the qualities of the temporal future are predicted, the collection of things happening to them is multiform and the narration is heavy. We have judged it most suitable to set forth the narration in this place, because from the beginning of this book we proposed to explain the work of general nature and its stars alongside particular things, as a likeness of the rational species...

<column-break/>

...in the mixture of the good.

¶ This is the path we must travel regarding the nature of the times. However, the particular ways through which we must inquire into the states of particular accidents—to tell of that which will happen—are many and of many kinds, and they are difficult to teach, especially in this place. For the purpose of this book is to show the general works mentioned before, and how they agree with particular things according to the estimation in the mode of demonstrating the mixtures of these matters.

¶ The particular ways of inquiring into the state of accidents are such that we return to each signified time of life, whether in years, months, or days, and to what number comes to that significator. It is like this: when such and such a planet is the lord of the profection <note>original: "alyntbie"</note> and is in a good state, it will signify such and such a thing; and if in a bad state, such and such; and when it participates with such and such a planet, it will signify such and such a thing. And because the significators of the times are many in each of the *hylegs* as has been demonstrated, the matter is of many kinds. Because of all this, it is heavy to narrate; therefore it pleased Ptolemy to omit the reasoning of it, as the rules and roots which he taught throughout the whole book are sufficient. 

I wonder how men did not understand this reasoning, those who hindered us with the multitude of books they compiled on the revolutions of births <note>solar returns, or annual charts</note>. I swear by God that none of them could ever make a revolution in which they did not place judgment on chance and fortune, and narrate different significations for one thing and one hour. If this science is such that we wish to judge it, we speak of some good thing—whether it will be truth or a lie—or if one of them says the lord of the *fardaria* <note>a system of planetary periods where each planet rules a certain number of years in a fixed sequence</note> signifies good in this year, and afterward the lord of the division signifies a mediocre state between good and evil, and between these judgments he places other things, he thinks he has said much and judged a right judgment. But it is impossible for one of these to happen, namely good or evil [simultaneously]. 

Ptolemy dislikes such a path, because it does not suit any of the arts. It remains that those astrologers who understood this book of his will be able to judge whatever thing they wish, and what kind it will be and at what time. They will know for certain what each thing will be and at what time. And different things can indeed happen at one and the same time, as Ptolemy narrated, yet those things will not be of one kind nor in one matter. For example: a man might gain wealth <note>original: "fubar," likely a corruption of the Arabic "substantiā"</note> and lose it at the same time. This happens when a fortune participates with a misfortune in some signification. It falls to the astrologer to say that this man will gain substance in such a time from such a thing, and will lose it from another thing; and with this, he will verify his word in each of the two things.

¶ The general matters of nativities having thus been explained, we think it not improper to place an end to this book in this place.

¶ And after we have perfected the judgment of births in the final mode, we think it convenient to place an end to this book here.

¶ When he said "in the final mode," he means to say that whatever he put in this book are the rules and roots by which this art is composed.

¶ Here ends the fourth book of Ptolemy on the rooted discernment of future things through the stars, and those things occurring in this world of construction and destruction.

### The Science of the Projection of Rays

<note>This section begins a technical guide on calculating the "aspects" or rays planets cast toward each other across the sky.</note>

When you wish to know the projection of the rays of the stars, you should know the ascending degree and, based on it, the four angles <note>the Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</note>. Then consider the degree of the Midheaven in its longitude from the beginning of Capricorn, and also the longitude of its part from the same angle in the direct circle. You will subtract one from the other, and what remains you shall call the equated longitude. After this, you shall add to the ascensions of the degree of the planet in the direct circle the part of the radiation which occurs from a sextile <note>60 degrees</note>, a square <note>90 degrees</note>, or a trine <note>120 degrees</note> aspect, if you wish to find the "sinister" <note>left-handed or forward-moving</note> radiation. Or you shall subtract it from the degree of the part if you observe the "dexter" <note>right-handed or backward-moving</note> ray. What remains will be the place of the first radiation. Then you shall add or subtract it from the ascensions...

If the planet is between the degree of the Ascendant and the degree of the Midheaven, you shall subtract the predicted equation of radiation from the place of the second radiation. But if it is between the degree of the Midheaven and the degree of the descendant <note>original: "occidētis"</note>, you shall add it to the first radiation. I wish in this place to give you an example of three births <note>nativities</note>, so that you may better understand everything we have spoken about. The first is my own birth. I was born in the "third climate" <note>A geographical band including North Africa and Egypt</note> in the place where Ptolemy divided the land of Egypt into two parts when he spoke of the shape of the earth. The latitude of that place is 30 degrees. It was in the year 356 of the era of Yazdegerd <note>A Persian calendar starting in 632 AD; this date corresponds to roughly 988 AD</note>. The angles and the locations of the planets at that hour were exactly as shown in this figure.

## On the status of the father.

I looked first at the status of my father, or his being. I found the Sun in the 5th house in Aquarius. Since he was in the 11th <note>unclear: "vedi ei viz medianā"</note>, and because he was in the opposition of his own house, he was weak. Because of this, it signified that my father was of a status lower than average among his peers. I also found the rays of the square aspect <note>90 degrees</note> of the Moon before him; the Moon being in the 8th house without an aspect to the Ascendant, which signified the weakness of the father. I also looked at Saturn, the governor of the Sun, whom I found participating in the 10th house following the 9th, between two "fortunes" <note>benefic planets, likely Jupiter and Venus</note>. This signified that my father would go, by virtue of the birth chart, into "Romaria" <note>likely meaning Byzantine or Roman territories</note>, that is, on a pilgrimage. He held a religious rule. Because the Moon was in the 10th house from the Sun and in its "fall" <note>a position of astrological weakness</note>, and separated

from a fortune and going toward a square of Mercury and Mars, it signified that harm would happen to him from the King's side because of an involvement with the King's scribes. And because the Moon aspects the "Part of Fortune" <note>a calculated point representing prosperity</note>, it signifies that this harm happened to him in his riches and substance. Afterward, I set the Sun's place as his Ascendant and it became the *hyleg* <note>the planet that "gives life" or determines the lifespan</note>, and I calculated its *ataçir* <note>term: ataçir - an Arabic term for "profection" or "direction," a method used to predict when life events will occur</note> until it reached Mars. The sextile rays of Venus were with him in the 11th house, because of which the life was not "cut off" <note>abscisio - a term for the end of life</note>. Afterward, I directed his *ataçir* to the left trine of the Moon in the sign of Pisces. Because this was in a sign of "short ascension" <note>signs that rise quickly over the horizon</note> and the Moon was in a "commanding" sign of "long ascension," and she was an enemy to the Sun in the root of the birth, she had to "cut off" the Sun. Because she was in the 10th house, the "cutting off" was due to a fall. Because it was in a "humid" sign, he had with this a flux of the belly <note>diarrhea or dysentery</note>, and he died at the start of his 31st year. He passed through all these things.

## On the status of the mother.

Afterward, I looked at the status of my mother and found the Moon in the 8th house. The sextile rays of Jupiter and the square of the Sun surrounded her from behind, and before her was the square of Mercury and Mars. The Moon being in its "fall" and the participation of Jupiter with the Moon signified that my mother would live a long time. The status of the Moon showed her poverty and weakness in her condition, since the Moon was in its fall and did not aspect the Ascendant. Since it was a daytime birth, I looked at Venus, whom I found in the 9th house near the division of the 10th, going toward the "infortunes" <note>malefic planets, Saturn and Mars</note>. This signified that my mother would be poor. I set the place of Venus as her Ascendant, and the Moon fell in the 11th from it; it was fit to be the mother's *hyleg*. Because Jupiter signified a long life for her, the time passed in which the *ataçir* of the Moon reached the right square of Mars, nor did any "cutter" remain for her except Saturn. Her life would reach more than 50 years after the birth. I similarly calculated the *ataçir* of Venus and found that it reached the Sun in the 37th year; at that time, a "cutting off" fell upon my mother, and she escaped from it only with the greatest infirmity. I similarly directed Venus to the square of the Moon, and the "cutting off" fell in the 43rd year, and she died. This was due to "much urine" which she was always passing, from the drying out of the body; that same infirmity lasted a long time in that year.

## On the status of brothers.

I looked afterward at the status of the brothers and I found Jupiter in the 10th house, which signifies brothers only older than myself. Because Jupiter was in its fall joined with Saturn, it signified his poverty and the weakness of his status, and that he did nothing for his own profit. Jupiter signifies him to be good and clear-headed. Because the sextile ray of the Moon fell in the 10th without an aspect from the "infortunes," it signified one sister. The 11th house gave no brother because the Sun was in it. Because of this, I had only one sister and one brother. I wish to stop speaking of these things regarding the nature of the birth, and I will speak of what it signified for me, and what God granted me through the utility He placed in me.

## On the sex of the native and twins.

The Ascendant demonstrated that it was a male, and the place of the Sun and the Moon showed the native would be male. Because these two things and the Moon were in signs of a single figure, the native was born alone without another <note>not a twin</note>. Because Jupiter was the lord of the "term of opposition" before the birth and in the 10th, and the principal places were safe from the "infortunes," there was no blemish or defect in me. Life lasted for me a good time. To know how long it would be, I calculated the *ataçir* of the Sun because it was in the 11th, and I found it applied to the left square of Saturn in Pisces at the end of 57 years. The "fortunes" aspected that place in the root of the birth. If the place of Saturn does not strike this spot, I shall escape until the square, because then the *hyleg* would reach its own square. However, if Saturn strikes the place of division in that year, I shall not escape. I will demonstrate these things to you hereafter.

# Concerning the Three
