Because Saturn was the lord of the place of Mars and Jupiter, and its rays were in the angles <note>The "angles" are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, the most powerful points in a chart.</note>, it demonstrated many rheums <note>An old medical term for watery discharge from the eyes or nose</note> and much acidic phlegm <note>One of the four "humors" of medieval medicine; an excess was thought to cause illness.</note>.

->¶ On the state of the native’s soul.<-

Afterward, I examined the state of the soul and I found Mercury looking upon the Ascendant <note>original: "ascendēs"</note> and the Moon looking upon the Part of Fortune <note>A mathematical point in a chart representing luck and well-being</note>, such that one looked at the other; and the degree of the preceding opposition was rising. From this, all these things demonstrated the liberation of my rational soul from the damaging infirmities of the senses. Both the signs of Mercury and the Moon, which were fixed, signified that my sense would be stable, and of good wisdom and good intellect, and that I would be patient of labor and weariness. For the aspect <note>A specific geometric relationship between planets</note> of Jupiter to the Moon and of Venus with Mercury signified a disposition fitting these signs: namely, the retaining of anger for a long time, and deep conception <note>Deep thought or planning</note>. Because Mercury and Mars were western <note>Setting in the west</note> while Mars was in union with the Moon, they signified sharpness, a good intellect, and natural sense; they also signified pain and labor in entering into secrets and philosophy. Saturn, who was the lord of both, signified honesty and fitness, and that I would govern myself by my own counsel and would perform good and famous works, and complete them. Jupiter indeed gave me goodness and good virtues; Venus and Mars gave me abstinence <note>Self-restraint</note> and good morals, and other things which are determined in the preceding glosses.

->¶ On the state of the native’s wealth.<-

I afterward examined the state of my wealth and I found, according to the manner of the signification, that Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, and the Moon—who presided in the governance of the Part of Fortune and in the aspect they had with it—signified that riches would come from the gifts of friends, and from the labor and pain of human offices. For Saturn gave labor of the lands and of the sea <note>original: "marinariā"</note> and by reason of women; and because he presided with Jupiter, it signified something of an inheritance from the dead. And because Mercury was the lord of the boundary of the Part of Infortune <note>A point representing hardship</note>, it signifies science and trades; and all these things were within me. However, the beginning of my wealth was after I held schools of philosophy; and thereafter one of my friends placed me in a certain office, and I held his place, from which I had utility and profit. And because it was in the 10th <note>The house of career and public standing</note>, it was such an office from which I drew the greatest utility, namely for philosophy. And because the Sun was in the 11th and its strength was less than middling, it was as we said before; for it was in opposition to its own house and the sign was masculine, and Jupiter looked upon the Moon and the Part of Fortune existing with Saturn, who was the lord of the place of the Sun in the 10th house at the beginning of Capricorn. Jupiter likewise was of middling standing. All these things signified a middling prosperity in temporal things and the necessities of life; and at times joys and sorrows were mixed together.

->¶ On the native’s mastery.<-

And because Jupiter was in the 10th and Mercury was the lord of the boundary and was joined, the virtue <note>The astrological power or influence</note> of Jupiter was with that of Venus and Saturn, and similarly that of Venus with that of Mars. The virtue of Jupiter was mixed with that of the Moon because they look upon each other from a sextile <note>A 60-degree angle, considered harmonious</note>; and the virtue of the Moon was similarly mixed with that of the Sun. Because of all this, the Sun, Mars, Saturn, Mercury, and Venus all disposed my office; and it is manifest that they agree with my character and my wealth. Because of this, my ministry <note>My career or service</note> was philosophy and astronomy. In my youth, I did other weak works consistent with these things. Afterward, my status began to increase until I began to hold schools of philosophy, since Jupiter was in the 10th and looked upon the Moon, being the lord of the house of Venus. Saturn disposed him, as he was conjoined with Venus; and because Mars is the lord of the exaltation of the 10th and is himself western, looking toward Venus, there is also in the 10th a certain fixed star named the <term>Falling Vulture</term> <note>Now known as the star Vega</note> located in that same degree of the 10th. Composed of the nature of Venus and Mercury, these things signified all my offices which I have narrated.

->¶ On the native’s marriage.<-

I afterward examined the state of my marriage and I found the Moon in the 4th, western, which signified that I would marry late. Because she looks at Jupiter existing in the 4th, eastern, it signifies that I would love girls and that my wives would be beautiful, though less than middling in lineage. It signifies the parts to which the Moon is joined; and because she was much joined to the part, it signified having many wives, and that their children would be virgins and girls. And because she was in the 4th of the Sun, it signified that I would be divided from them. And because Venus goes toward Mars and was near Saturn, it signified that I would much love women,

<column-break/>

and yet there was a measure of abstinence in them. And because Jupiter was opposite Venus, and the lord of her house was likewise Saturn, and Jupiter was powerful in the 10th, it signified <note>unclear: "lipiditatẽ"</note> <note>Possibly 'limpiditatem' (clarity/purity) or 'cupiditatem' (desire)</note> and that I would act legally and according to the law. I never knew a woman except according to the law through marriage; and especially because Jupiter looked upon the Moon. And because the Moon was in a place in which she had some dignity, and Mars was her disposer <note>The planet ruling the sign the Moon is in</note>, showing the 9th and 12th, it signified that I would be married and have many others who were purchased <note>Likely referring to domestic servants or concubines, common in the legal structures of the time</note>. And because the Moon looked at the Sun in the 4th, it signified that it would not be profitable for me to be with the women with whom I was joined matrimonially, nor with the others whom I might have.

->¶ On the state of the native’s children.<-

And I found Jupiter in the 10th, which gave one male son; and because he was with Saturn, that same son died a few days from his birth. And because the Moon looked at the 10th and cast her rays before the Sun, and the Moon is female and in a female sign, and in a female 4th, it signified 7 female daughters. And because the Sun was in one of their places and the rays of Saturn in the other, not one of them lived; one lived a little more than 7 years, and another a little more than one year. And because the Moon went in a circle with the Part of Fortune, it signified that I would have 3 daughters: two from Venus and another from the Moon.

->¶ On the native’s journeys.<-

Afterward, I examined his journeying; and I found the Moon in the 4th, falling <note>In a cadent house, which indicates movement</note>, and she signifies journeys. And because the Moon was in a trine <note>120-degree aspect</note> of merit, western, and Venus was likewise in the 9th <note>The house of long-distance travel</note> joining herself with Mars, it signifies that my journeys would be for the most part toward the southern region. And because the Moon looked at Jupiter existing in the 10th, it signifies that they would be safe and provide me with food.

->¶ On the quality of the native’s death.<-

I afterward examined what sort of death it would be, and I found that Saturn was the lord over it, and it is manifest to me that it would be by a flux of humors and because of dysentery. And because the fortunes <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> surrounded him, it signifies that death will be natural in itself, in my own house and among my kinsmen. According to those things which we have narrated to you, you will be able to judge in other nativities. I wished to set forth my own nativity because I have proved the whole of it in myself, and not by hearsay.

->¶ On the second nativity.<-

Now, however, I wish to name two other nativities, whose entire state I knew well, and a great part of which I proved myself. One of them was in <term>Al-Fustat</term> <note>The historic center of Cairo, Egypt</note>, and the places of the planets were according to what appears in this figure.

Because Mercury was of the temperament of Saturn and moved upon one circle with the Ascendant, it signifies great speed; he would expose his body to labor, working his lands and estates along with other tasks.

### On the native’s children.

### On the length of the native’s life and the quality of his death.

**It is clear** that the degree of the Ascendant was his <term>hyleq: the planet or point in a chart that acts as the "giver of life"</term>; and the Moon was his "cutter" <note>The "abscisor" or "cutter" is the planet that determines the end of life.</note> because it was in the partition of the Ascendant, in its fall, and in a watery sign. This sextile falls in a sign of long ascension, and for this reason, it is the cutter without a doubt, due to the great cold and moisture that joined upon the light of the Moon. 

It is clear that when the ray of misfortune is the cutter and it is "exalted," it signifies a fall and ruin. Because the Moon was the cutter while being in the Ascendant, and Saturn was the lord of its exaltation and triplicity, and Venus was the lord of the 8th house <note>The house of death.</note> and the Ascendant, they signified that he would kill himself. Mars and Saturn, however, diminish two parts of these, and because they are joined with Jupiter, 4 years remain. Similarly, it is the same distance as between the sextile of Saturn and the degree of the Ascendant when we reduce it by its ascensions. 

This native lived for 24 solar years, 5 months, and six days. Then, having become angry with his mother because of a girl, he went to a bridge and threw himself into the Nile and died. At that very hour, I took the Ascendant, and it was the 4th degree of Virgo, where Mars was in the root of the birth chart. I cast the "revolution" <note>A solar return chart calculated for the year of death.</note> of the year in which he died and found that the <term>al-yntbia: an Arabic term for "profection," a method of moving the chart forward one sign per year to find timing</term> reached the position of Saturn in Scorpio. The profection of the month reached Pisces, in opposition to the position of the Sun, and Saturn looked upon it from the fourth house of the revolution. Mercury was in that same degree at the 4th hour of Saturn. Mars on that day was in the 4th degree of the Ascendant of the birth root and of Mercury. Similarly, on this day Saturn was in the 4th degree of the conjunction and Mercury was in its opposition, and it was made unfortunate by Saturn; and Saturn was in Pisces, which is a watery sign. Both luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> were afflicted and unfortunate in the revolution; there was also a solar eclipse that year in the fourth house of the Moon's place at birth, with Mars being in opposition to it. These examples are sufficient for the things we wish to tell you, so that you might understand them better. Therefore, it is expedient for you not to labor over any other book but this one. ### On the partition of the times of these three births.

**Now**, however, I wish to tell of the partitions of the times of these three born; and first, I wish to say one general word. ### On the partition in the second birth.

**Lest** I extend this too much, I wish to speak of these other two births, so that you may take an example therefrom. It happened to the native of the second figure that one revolution in one year signified great and fierce pressures <note>original: "feritas"; likely meaning harsh legal or financial penalties.</note> upon a society of scribes. However, there was no "infortune" there in the root chart, which is why less evil happened to him than to the others. For this reason, he was not struck nor much dishonored; they made a pact with him for 500 maravedis <note>original: "mar."; a medieval Spanish coin.</note> which he paid. They did not wish to make such a pact with others, for some of them paid 800 maravedis and some more. After that unfortunate year had passed, he was freed and returned to his office just as he was before.

<header>Ptolemy's Hundred Sayings</header>

# Here begins the book of the Hundred Sayings of Ptolemy, with the commentary of Haly.

<image-desc>Woodcut decorative initial 'D' depicting a scholar (Haly) in a doctoral cap speaking to another man (Jesus) who holds a book.</image-desc>

**P**tolemy said: I have already written to you, Jesus <note>original: "Iesu"; likely referring to Syrus, the traditional student addressed in Ptolemy’s works, rather than the religious figure.</note>, books regarding how the stars operate in this world: and they are books of great utility for those who wish to know the future. This work is the "fruit" <note>The "fructus" or "Centiloquium" is a collection of 100 aphorisms summarizing astrological wisdom.</note> of all those books, and it has been proven many times; however, it will not be understood except by those who have labored in other books and have learned many other sciences. Therefore, receive it with a good spirit.

### The first Sayings regarding the knowledge of those things that provide true judgment.

<image-desc>Woodcut decorative initial 'S' depicting an astronomer using an instrument (possibly a quadrant or sighting device) to observe the heavens represented by circular spheres.</image-desc>

**T**he science of the stars is from you and from them: the astrologer, however, ought not to speak of things specifically, but generally, as one who sees something from a distance. For so does he who considers a thing according to its matter and does not come to a certain knowledge of it. ¶ Through "matter" <note>The physical, changing substance of a thing.</note> we have a doubtful knowledge of a thing; through "form" <note>The essential, defining nature of a thing.</note>, however, we have certainty. These judgments which I hand down to you are the middle ground between "necessary" and "possible." When I said these judgments are between the necessary and the possible, I mean this is the case for him who considers the natures of things and the work of the stars. ¶ But those who possess knowledge of the future from the better part of the soul are closer to the truth because of the power of the soul dominating in them, even if they do not have much science of this art.

### The exposition of Haly upon the first Saying.

**W**hat Ptolemy said—"From you and from them"—signifies that whoever desires to know future things must proceed by two ways. One is that he should look at the movements of the stars, and the works that are done in things according to their movement. This is what the ancients wrote concerning the indications of their movements: and let him join to these whatever shall be proven in his own time. Therefore he said, "From them." The other way is when someone has this science through divine inspiration; such a person will be able to give many judgments. For it is a marvel if some give true judgments when we find neither the indications nor the reasons for those judgments—neither in the configuration nor in the operation—but what they see flows from their hearts. We see many of these people, and this way, when it is pure, is called "divine" by the philosophers. Therefore Ptolemy says: concerning the science of those things that happen under the circle of the moon, some have it through doctrine <note>study and training</note>, others through divine inspiration. When, however, a man possesses both these ways, he shall be accounted among the wise, and shall be found truthful in judgments. If, however, he lacks one of these, he shall be judged less wise. ¶ As for what Ptolemy said—the astrologer ought not to speak specifically but generally—he said this because this science is only based on proof and opinion or operation. And because this matter, to which the whole work of the stars belongs, is changeable from one thing to another, he said: "Not specifically, but generally." Just as we call the effect of fire "heat," so we call the effect of other things "heat-producers," even though the specific effect of fire is called "combustion." ¶ Ptolemy said: "From the better part." He spoke according to the power of the soul by which we are rational; in that power is the knowledge that recognizes what ought to happen. And because we have anger and desire surrounding this power, and because the need to be worried about worldly things takes the knowledge of the future away from us; yet if we separate this way from all worldly

<column-break/>

things, we could foreknow the future, just as we have seen hermits and many others who predict the future because they do not then use the senses of the body, but the power of the soul alone, by which they sometimes announce the future. The indications of things that we see in dreams happen from this power, and because of what we have said, there are many other signs in it. Of those who foreknow the future by themselves, not all know in the same way: for some from the heart alone; others from another sign which they see in the one asking the question; others from a few words spoken to them. And others by many, many ways. Ptolemy said: the change of the worldly is tempered to this and to that by the super-celestial bodies.

->ADDITION.<-

**T**he science of the stars is from you and from them. It is not necessary for that expert to judge according to the form of particular effects, just as it is not necessary for a scholar to receive the form of individual sensory things, but rather in the genus <note>the general category</note> appropriate to it. This is the method of one judging above matter and its quality, because he cannot signify the form of the future which is in the agent and the form of truth, while investigating this form from the side of the matter of the receiver and the recipient. Therefore, the reception of the forms of judgment in this world will be better within truth and investigation: that is, in those things where it is necessary to seek natural induction and the work of possibility. But those who find this science from the more subtle part of themselves know the form of truth from the divine truth which is in them astronomically <note>referring to celestial harmony</note>; even if it is not in them from the science of the subject of the majority.

**T**he doctrine of the stars is from you and from them: nor is my doctrine such that because of this "form," the act is individual; nor is it appropriate for the one perceiving to take an individual form or position, but rather to take a form appropriate to it in its genus. Moreover, this is the method of judging above matter and quality. It is least possible for him to speak upon the form which is in "act" <note>the actualized, physical result</note> as that which is in the soul with this form. Rather, there is an inquiry from the side of matter, and the act will thus be the form of judgment to be taken in this work from those things occurring by the course from the soul and the inquiry. Namely, in that which prevails over it: the revolution of natures and the light or trace of the effect. Therefore, those who find previous knowledge from the better part in them have approached it from the form of the soul which is in them from divine power; not because there is in them some other doctrine as the foundation of a great thing.

### The second Saying, on the movement of the circles.

**W**hen the "chooser" <note>An astrologer performing an "election," or picking an auspicious time for an event.</note> chooses the best, there will be no difference between him and one who has this by nature.

**M**any men have thought that Ptolemy was speaking here about the "elections" which astrologers choose at the beginning of works. But it is not so; rather, he wished to prove the reasons of those who said that the celestial circles were not living beings <note>original: "animalia"; in medieval thought, the spheres were often considered to be moved by living intelligences or souls.</note> but were like one of the four elements. They held this opinion because they saw them always moving from the east to the west, and a living being does not move thus, but rather goes here and there. But because the circles are powerful over all that are under them, therefore they chose for themselves the better movement: that is, the circular, because that movement has no "contraries" <note>In Aristotelian physics, circular motion is perfect because it has no opposite direction to conflict with it.</note>. That is, there is nothing that can pull them backward; and therefore everything that does the best, and can always do the same, and does not know anything better to be, always does that.

### The third Saying, on the appearance of a star’s effect when it was strong at someone’s birth.

**H**e who does any work from nature or artifice will find in his nativity a planet very strong from the nature of that same thing.

**P**tolemy will teach in this book, in Chapter 6: what such stars are, and the strengths flowing from them, and their works in living beings, and what the elements are in bodies. And therefore, when any star is strong in the birth of someone, he desires the work of that star in that person; and he will quickly learn it skillfully and perfect it. The strength of a planet is that it be in one of its "dignities" <note>A place in the zodiac where the planet has specific power, like its Home or Exaltation.</note>, and in some "angle" <note>One of the four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th.</note>, and in some good state relative to the Sun: that is, the three superior planets <note>Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn</note> should be rising in the morning, and the two inferior ones <note>Venus and Mercury</note> setting in the evening.

### The fourth Saying, on the secondary qualities of stars and their judgment.

**T**he soul which gives judgments from nature will judge based on the secondary qualities of the stars; and its judgment will be better than his who judges based on the primary stars.

**I** have already told you how the soul has this from nature; now I tell you that the secondary qualities of the stars are from the work which it does...

<header>The Hundred Sayings</header>

...under the lunar circle, such that there are inferences regarding stars with tails <note>original: "stella cum caudis"; referring to comets</note> and circles <note>halos</note> that sometimes appear around the sun; and many other things that happen near the lunar circle. The Arab <note>likely Abu Ma'shar, a famous Persian astrologer known in the West as Albumasar</note> named all these in the book he composed concerning the signs of these "secondary stars"; and others have named them because of their effects. But the indication of these is not worth as much as the indication of the primary stars. Nevertheless, a soul that possesses this by nature will judge better through the secondary stars than another would through the primary stars.

### The fifth Saying: on the transformation and prohibition of coming evil according to the stars.

The best astrologer will be able to prohibit much of the evil that is to come according to the stars once he has foreknown their nature; for in this way he forewarns the person to whom the evil is to come so that they might be able to endure it.

Indeed, the same operation is not equal for all recipients, and we can use the receivers to accept more or less of the influence. Therefore, when an astrologer fears that an evil may happen, he redirects it into the opposite of the coming evil, so that when the evil itself happens, it does not strike him as much as it would if it happened unexpectedly. For example: if someone were naturally well-tempered, and we knew their nativity <note>birth chart</note>, then if we saw some infirmity coming to them from the nature of Mars <note>associated with heat and inflammation</note>, we would turn their temperament <term>complexionem: the balance of the four humors</term> toward coldness; thus, when the illness arrives, it would find the body in a state of balance. He shall operate similarly in other matters when he foreknows what is to come from their nature.

### The sixth Saying: in which matters "elections" are very profitable, and in which they are of little use.

Elections <note>the practice of choosing a specific time to begin an action to ensure a favorable outcome</note> are profitable when the strength of the time or the election is greater than the excess that exists between the two receivers. If, however, it is less, its profit will not appear as much, although it may help somewhat.
The indication of the nativity and the strength of the election: when they agree in signifying something good, that same good will increase for the election. If, however, they disagree, the strength of the stronger one will appear. For the nativity is likened to the body, and the election is likened to the thing that assists the body, such as food and medicine, which are external to the body. Sometimes we see that medicine entering the body, if it finds it healthy, will increase its health. If it finds it sick, it will restore it to health. But if it finds it heavily burdened by illness, it may not seem to profit the person at all, even if it actually helps slightly. In this way you should discern between nativities and elections. If both the nativity and the election are good and profitable, the good election will be effective. If the nativity is known and is very bad, the election will not seem to profit him, even if it does so slightly. And the "receiver" is the matter upon which the election operates, whether it be a body, one of two armies, or one of two litigants. 

Ptolemy taught us in this chapter what many astrologers have ignored: that when we wish to consider one of two armies, we ought to know what lies between both in terms of people and strength, and take the ascendant of one of them if the birth time is unknown. And we must consider what lies between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Seventh House, and which of them is stronger. If the Lord of the Ascendant is stronger while the Lord of the Seventh is either equal or slightly below him, then we ought to involve ourselves in making an election for him. But if it is much worse, we should not involve ourselves much in his election, because the profit of the election will not be apparent, even if we have succeeded. And Zael <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician</note> mentions this in his Book of Elections.

### The seventh Saying: on the knowledge of someone’s virtue from the nature of the soul itself.

A man will not be able to give judgments according to the temperament of the stars unless he is one who well knows the power of the soul and the natural temperament.

The temperament of the stars is this: their natures operate in their conjunctions and aspects. For conjunction and aspect operate on the power of the soul and in the works we perform in this world. Ptolemy has already taught us great words on this in the third part of the *Quadripartitum* <note>Ptolemy’s "Tetrabiblos," the foundational text of Western astrology</note>, because there he taught us how we recognize the quality of a soul from someone’s birth. It is necessary for an astrologer to be very bold in the knowledge of the soul and its three powers, and in that which flows from them, whether good or evil: justice or injustice, generosity or greed, truth or lies, loyalty or betrayal, 

<column-break/>

pride or humility. When he has understood how all this flows from the soul, then he ought to look at the stars and see how this comes to the soul from the stars, and to know all of this fundamentally. This part of the science is better than all other parts contained in this science; he who knows it well deserves to be called a "perhicus" <note>likely a corruption of "peritus," meaning an expert or skilled practitioner</note> or a teller of truth.

### The eighth Saying: on the dignity of the soul’s foreknowledge.

A wise soul will assist the work of the stars in the same way that a sower assists natural strengths.
A wise soul is that which knows what we have said regarding the strengths of the heaven; and its assistance consists in this: when it recognizes that some good is to happen to someone, it perceives how to adapt things for them so that the coming good happens greater and better than it would have happened unless he had forewarned them, as we have already spoken sufficiently about this in the fifth chapter.

### The ninth Saying: regarding the celestial images of every earthly creature.

The faces <note>original: "vultus"; the forms or appearances</note> of this world are subject to the celestial faces; and therefore the wise who made "images" <note>astrological talismans or amulets</note> looked at the entry of the stars into the celestial faces, and then they would perform what they ought to do.
In this chapter, Ptolemy wishes to reveal many secrets of images. He said the "faces" that are in this world are the species of animals and the species of planets. And therefore he says that for all these species, there are similar faces remaining in heaven that govern them. For example: the celestial Scorpio governs earthly scorpions, and the celestial Serpent governs earthly serpents. And the wise makers of images watched how the planets emerged from under the rays of the sun and how this "face" entered, and they placed it in the Ascendant, and they "concealed" <note>sculpted or engraved</note> the face that was entering. That is, they sculpted it into stone and mixed other necessary things with it; and by adapting or constructing it, they did what they wished. 

That power in the stone would last for many years. I saw in the time of King Lamozche <note>likely a reference to a Cuman (Chumanorum) leader</note> an attendant who came to us from the Romans and was called a wise man; he had become a Saracen in Egypt... <note>text becomes slightly fragmented</note> skilled in geometry, who made images that moved artificially; he also knew the nature of stones and herbs. One day while I was with him, we heard his squire crying out because a scorpion had stung him. Immediately, he took from his pouch seals that had the scent of incense; he offered one to him and made him carry it, and as soon as he drank [a solution made with it], the squire recovered. Then I looked at those seals, and in each one I saw the face of a scorpion impressed. I asked him what he had used to seal them. Then he showed me a gold ring whose stone was a "beçabar" <term>Bezoar: a stone-like mass found in the stomachs of animals, highly prized in the Middle Ages as an antidote to poison</term>, in which the face of a scorpion was sculpted. I asked him at what hour he had sculpted that stone; he told me he sculpted it while the Moon was in Scorpio in one of the four angles <note>the strongest positions in a chart</note>, and he sealed the chewed incense with it in that same hour. There were other things he sealed with the seal, and I thought the power was in the incense, but it was effective in other things as well.

### The tenth Saying: in which things "misfortunes" are useful.

It is necessary to use "misfortunes" <note>original: "infortunis"; referring to the malefic planets Saturn and Mars</note> in elections just as skilled physicians use poisonous substances in a competent quantity.
Unskilled astrologers place the "fortunes" <note>the benefics, Jupiter and Venus</note> as the significators in all their elections, and they make them strong and reject the "misfortunes," making them weak without considering the nature of the lord of the election or the species for which the election is sought. And thus the planets that are believed to help actually hinder. The learned, however, first look at the places in elections according to the nature of the person for whom they choose, and the thing for which the election is made. If the person's nativity is known, they make the significance of both chapters strong—the thing for which the election is made and the person for whom it is made—whether it be a fortune or a misfortune. They look at what is in his nature and character, and the purpose of the election, and they make the planet that agrees with him strong in the election, whether it be a fortune or a misfortune. And for this reason, Ptolemy urged us to operate through misfortunes in elections, because through this, certain things that are necessary for us are accomplished in certain hours regarding heat and deceptions, when truth cannot punish the guilty, and other similar things. He also likened misfortunes to sharp spices...

...than poison. Therefore, just as a wise **physician** <note>original: "phicus" for "physicus"</note> employs each of these species and their penetrating and attractive powers in the members to be purged and in bodies suitable for them, so a wise **astrologer** employs the powers of the **unfortunate planets** <note>malefics, such as Mars and Saturn</note> in those things we have enumerated according to their magnitude. And Ptolemy exhorts us that whoever works through them should beware of them, and he spoke as much as was appropriate.

**¶ The eleventh Saying: regarding not only reason but also the memory of experiments.**

¶ Do not choose <note>an "election," or selecting a specific time to act</note> except for one whose intention has become clear to you through **experience** in the nature of the one for whom you are choosing; and unless you know the end of that intention in it through the **figure of the nativity** <note>birth chart</note> of the one for whom it is entirely chosen; and so that you may compare what exists between the power of the <term>Almuberez</term> <note>original: "alcamiā nē," likely a corruption of "Al-muberez," referring to the state or prominence of a planet</note>, namely, whether it is **direct** or **retrograde**. And it is necessary that your speech be based upon that which you judge, namely, in any judgment: lest you observe only the nature of the sphere, lest you be likened to one reading books and ignorant of the language of the speech; nor should anyone trust in such similar things.

¶ Ptolemy intends that it is not only necessary for astrologers to be mindful of their own experiments but also those of the ancients, so that through them they might perceive the quantity of **good fortunes** and **misfortunes**. And let him approach through this what he has understood regarding future figures; nor should it be enough for him to speak only upon its general type—as when he sees a good fortune, he might say that the **querent** <note>the person asking the question</note> will end his affair in prosperity. However, when he sees a misfortune, he might say that the querent will end his existence in evil. He would then be like someone reading a page to another, knowing nothing beyond the literal writing; rather, he should determine the quantity, so that he may say what will happen to this person just as it happened to that one, and compare it to one of the figures which he himself has exemplified through experience.

**¶ The twelfth Saying: on the magnanimous and the pusillanimous, and on the coldness of the soul itself.**

¶ **Love** and **hatred** remove men from rectitude <note>uprightness or accuracy</note>.

¶ The **magnanimous** <note>great-souled</note> man thinks little of great things. ¶ The **pusillanimous** <note>small-souled</note> man, however, magnifies small things; and there is an equality between both.

¶ There are two infirmities of the soul, which are **love** and **hatred**; by philosophers, those who hold these are excluded from good discussion and scrutiny of a matter. For through love, one will spare many things which ought to be scrutinized. They scrutinize with hatred that which will never be completed because of a bad significance. For this reason, gifts were given to philosophers and astrologers by the **kings of the Greeks**, so that their judgments might be firm and they would not fear anyone, and their anxieties would be removed. Nor would honor, dignity, or riches turn them from the path of rectitude. The **magnanimous** man signifies boldness and the perfection of nature. One who is such a person thinks little of grand things because of the excellence of the soul over the body; he does not discuss them but passes over them because of his spiritedness. The **pusillanimous** man, however, signifies a weak soul; he occupies himself with the smallest things, so that long consideration of them hinders him from greater things—namely, celestial things—because of the concealment of the soul. But the one commended by the ancients in all science is the middle between both these natures.

**¶ The thirteenth Saying: on the secondary stars regarding the affirmation of the judgments of the stars.**

¶ When the spherical power has sent something down, take testimony upon that from the **secondary stars**.

¶ **Secondary stars** are the effects that occur in this world—namely, in the air—produced by the stars. The observer of the judgments of the stars must know what this teaches—that is, what it shows—and confirm it through that which the stars indicate. An example of this is: the stars may have indicated for a certain people that the **spring** of that year would have many infirmities. We then looked at that winter, and it was full of continuous rains and events such as wind and thunder. And **physicians** signify through this the destruction of things in that spring. Therefore, the significators, both the agents and the patients, have agreed; and they are corroborated through this as they consider what they have judged. When the stars signify something, and a secondary star affirms it, the astronomer is more 

<column-break/>

certain. And if not, he is not so certain.

**¶ Saying 14: on the malice of the significators.**

¶ The fourth error of the astrologer will be when the **seventh house** and its lord are impeded.

¶ Since the **Ascendant** and its lord are the significators of the querent <note>the person asking</note>, the **seventh house** and its lord will be the significators of the matter which is sought. Therefore, when they are **unfortunate** <note>afflicted by malefic planets</note>, they signify the malice which the astrologer will encounter in that matter for which he is asked. And the first part is more likely: that an error will occur for him regarding the matter sought. Indeed, when the seventh house and its lord were unfortunate, the astrologers of India would postpone the interrogation and even fear to speak about it for fear of error.

**¶ Saying 15: on the diversities of the Ascendants of various things, namely: cities, buildings, and enthronements.**

¶ The Ascendants of the **enemies of a kingdom** are **cadent** <note>falling away from the angles, often indicating weakness</note> from the Ascendant of that same kingdom. And the Ascendants of those **ruling** in that kingdom are its **angles** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful</note>. The Ascendants of those **serving** in that kingdom are in the **succedent** <note>following</note> houses of the angles. Furthermore, the Ascendants of **cities** at their building indicate all things that happen to them. But the Ascendants in the **ordering of affairs** of those same cities pronounce all that will be done under their rule; and the Ascendant of the **appearance of any sect** <note>religious or philosophical movement</note> indicates to cities what happens to them in those matters, and demonstrates whatever is to be in those cities under that sect.

¶ **Cadent** signs are those where one will not be in an angle after an angle; and they are four: the 3rd, 6th, and 9th <note>and 12th</note>. It is known to every astrologer that when the Ascendant of a birth—or one of its angles—is the Ascendant of the **beginning of a kingdom**, or one of the angles of the kingdom, and it is a birth suitable for a kingdom, it will complete the kingdom for him—namely, for the son of a king in that kingdom. And there will be honor for him in that one and not in another. Indeed, the **kings of old** observed the births of everyone born in their kingdoms; and whenever they perceived a birth suitable for the kingdom, and its Ascendant was in the house of their enemies—either the 6th, the 8th, or the 3rd—they would **kill him** as a child, because his kingdom would be outside their kingdom. But if it were the Ascendant or another of the angles of the kingdom, and he was born suitable for the kingdom, he himself would be powerful in that kingdom. And his state would be like the state of a minister. Furthermore, the **great Ascendant** <note>of a city</note> is under its rising when someone begins to place the first stone in it. And that signifies that which is to be for all those dwelling there—its exaltation and destruction—namely, when a king acquires that city. And the Ascendant of the ordering or the acquisition of a king indicates the strength of the kingdom in the good and evil of that prince and their children, and the weakness when the king is in it. The Ascendant of a **sect** is that in which the sect itself begins to prevail over the sect of that city and those dwelling there receive it; and that signifies how long its existence will endure and what will happen because of it.

**¶ Saying 17: on the difference of being fortunate or unfortunate in fearful places or fortunes in turn, and their significance.**

¶ When **good fortunes** <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> preside over **fearful places**, they will bring harm from just men. If, however, they look upon that impediment of fortune by a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>—namely, if they are the <term>Almudebir</term> <note>a planet having primary authority over a chart or period of time</note> or are in that place—that fear will be nullified; and speak in this manner regarding the four combinations.

¶ His intention is that it is impossible [to judge] unless the fortunes or misfortunes dominate each other in fearful places. And here there will be **four combinations**. First: that good fortunes preside over fearful places, and evil will come from good men—just as the righteous testify regarding it for the sake of confirming the truth—and they will harm him. Second: that misfortunes preside over fearful places, and evil will be done to him by unjust men known for robbery. Third: that good fortunes preside over the places of fortunes, and benefit, honor, and sublimity will come from good and just men. Fourth: that misfortunes preside over the places of fortunes, and there will happen...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the "Centiloquium," specifically discussing the interaction between fortunate and unfortunate planetary aspects and how they influence the outcomes of human endeavors. # The Hundred Sayings
<note>original: "Lentiloquium," a likely misspelling of "Centiloquium"</note>

...and utility from the evil and the unjust. A fortunate **aspect** <note>an angle between planets</note> toward any of those four parts—namely, the mixtures—increases the good and diminishes the evil. An unfortunate aspect toward them increases the malice and diminishes the good. Another has said: when the **fortunate planets** <note>benefics like Jupiter and Venus</note> are in "dreaded places," it is through the lordship of a house, an **exaltation** <note>a sign where a planet is particularly strong</note>, or some other dignity. Dreaded places are the bodies or rays of **unfortunate planets** <note>malefics like Mars and Saturn</note>, which the significators of births reach through **direction** or **perfection** <note>advanced timing techniques in astrology</note>.

<margin>Saying 17: On error in the judgment of life, actions, and passions.</margin>
¶ Scrutinize the nature of the origin or the subject—its life, actions, and passions—before you put forward a judgment concerning it.

¶ Ptolemy intends in this chapter that an astrologer, when a **nativity** <note>birth chart</note> has been presented to him, ought not to judge anything regarding that life, or any state of it, unless he has first investigated what its origin is. For it is possible that it is the birth of a beast, or of this [beast], and its lifespan will not be like that of a human life. And the same can be said of its actions and passions, all of which vary as the origins or substances vary.

<margin>Saying 18: On the conjunction of the luminaries in the same minute, and the essence of fortune in the ascending degree.</margin>
¶ When the **luminaries** <note>the Sun and Moon</note> are in the same minute, and the fortunate planets are in the ascending degree, the person's fortune will be in the acquisition of substance. Similarly, if the Moon is in the minute of opposition to the Sun, and a fortunate planet is in the degree of the **seventh house** <note>the house of partnership and others</note> from the ascendant; it will be the reverse when an unfortunate planet is in the place of a fortunate one.

¶ All astrologers used to refuse to involve themselves in anything where the two luminaries were in the same number. And when a fortunate planet is in the minute of the **ascendant** <note>the eastern horizon at birth</note>, the **Part of Fortune** <note>a calculated point of prosperity</note> will then be bodily with the fortunate planet, and his work will then result in prosperity and profit. If, however, an unfortunate planet is in the place of fortune, it will result in loss for him. And when a fortunate planet is in the minute of the seventh house at the hour of the opposition of the Sun and Moon, the Part of Fortune is with the fortunate planet, and this is useful. But if an unfortunate planet is in its place, his harm will be multiplied. And therefore they say: the loss will be multiplied, because then the **ascendant** is hindered—that is, the fortune in the seventh. This is a sound exposition of the master's opinion.

<margin>Saying 19: On the purgations of the Moon with Jupiter present.</margin>
¶ If anyone takes a **purgative** <note>laxative or cleansing medicine</note> while the Moon is with **Jupiter**, its work will be shortened and its effect will be diminished.

¶ The effect of medicine is not natural to the body; rather, it draws things out by overcoming many natural virtues. When the [vital] nature is stronger than that medicine, it will prohibit the medicine's effect. The proof of this matter is as follows: smelling fragrant things comforts the nature. In the very rush of the medicine, the effect—namely, nature—is weakened. Jupiter, however, comforts the nature and increases it in his conjunction with the Moon, providing the strength that prohibits the effect of the medicine.

<margin>Saying 20: On wounding when the Moon is in the sign of that member.</margin>
¶ To touch a limb with iron while the Moon is in the sign of that limb is to be dreaded.

¶ The ancients have already reached the conclusion that the Moon increases the humidity in every limb corresponding to the sign it enters. To touch limbs with iron is to wound them. To add humidity to a wound multiplies the harm.

<margin>Saying 21: On giving purgatives in humid signs, and the lord of the ascendant under the earth, and vice versa.</margin>
¶ To take a purgative when the Moon is in **Scorpio** or **Pisces** <note>water signs</note>; and also when the lord of the ascendant is joined to a planet that is below the earth by conjunction or a favorable aspect. If, however, the lord of the ascendant is joined to a planet existing in the **midheaven** <note>the highest point of the chart</note>, he will suffer nausea, and the medicine will be moved [upward], and it will not stay in him.

<column-break/>

¶ The **humid triplicity**—that is, the aquatic signs—is entirely beneficial to the drinker of soluble medicine. Because when medicine enters the body, the humidity in those limbs does not hinder its strength. When at the hour of taking the medicine the lord of the ascendant is joined to a planet existing below the earth, it will move the medicine downward, and its action will be useful. When the lord of the ascendant is joined to a planet existing above the earth, it will move toward the upper parts; he who took it will suffer nausea, and its effect will be diminished.

<margin>Saying 22: On avoiding fixed signs in those things which we intend to change and alter.</margin>
¶ To make or wear new garments while the Moon is in **Leo** is to be dreaded, especially if she is hindered.

¶ By "make" he intends cutting and sewing. By "wear" <note>original: "exercere"</note> he means putting them on and using them. **Fixed signs** <note>signs like Leo, Taurus, etc., which represent stability</note> are to be avoided in all works that we intend to alter; and especially the sign of Leo, because while this sign is fixed, it signifies a multitude of victories in all things that are undertaken, but a "bad dominion" <note>malicious control</note> in them.

<margin>Saying 23: On the significance of the planets toward the Moon from their different positions in the circle or ascendant.</margin>
¶ **Almusechelet** <note>a term for planetary configuration or suitability</note>—otherwise known as the figuration or agreement of the Moon with the planets in a birth—makes the natives mobile or moving; in this it signifies that if it happens that the planets are strong in themselves, it signifies that he may exert himself in more than he knows. And the appearance in which there will be exertion will be from the state of those planets in the visible **angles** <note>the 1st, 10th, 7th, and 4th houses</note> or those succeeding them. Its utility will come from their good fortune, and in this way it bestows what remains of the parts.

¶ *Almusechelet* is spoken of in two ways. One is the aspect. The other is its state in the circle relative to the Sun. What he intends in this place is the *almusechelet* of aspects which come from the angles of the figures: which are the **trine**, **square**, **sextile**, and **opposition**. He also said that the planets give motion to the light according to their natures. The Moon signifies the parts within us receiving the forms of things and their times. Thus, through an aspect of **Jupiter** to her, justice is made. Through an aspect of **Mars**, command. Through an aspect of **Saturn**, patience. Through an aspect of **Venus**, cheerfulness. And through an aspect of **Mercury**, wisdom and discretion. And each one of the planets strengthens its own work in the lord of the birth according to the quantity of its strength in itself—namely, when it has increased in number and magnitude in its **Hayz** <note>a specific planetary dignity where a planet is in a sign/sect matching its gender</note>. Then it will appear as he desires; that is, if it is in the visible angles or in the houses succeeding the angles, it will appear. If however they are not appearing, they are called "oriental from the Sun," as in the angles. It will benefit him according to the quantity of his fortune, and the strength of the planet will be associated with the Moon; and what is composed from them will come from strength, desire, good fortune, and that to which the division has reached. There are eight modes signifying those things we have commemorated, and they are these:
1. Strong, appearing, capable, and helping.
2. Strong, appearing, and harming.
3. Strong, hidden, and helping.
4. Strong, hidden, and harming.
5. Weak, appearing, and helping.
6. Weak, appearing, and harming.
7. Weak, hidden, and helping.
8. Weak, hidden, and harming.
¶ Because there are four states of the stars: either strong, weak, fortunate, or unfortunate. Moreover, the form of the stars is threefold: manifold, full, or diminished. They are **manifold** when they come with many dignities. **Full**, as in their own houses or better figures—like Saturn in Aquarius and so on. **Diminished**, as in others. Strength is also: ascending in the North, or in the hall of ascent in the circle from the earth; increase of motion; the first station; being outside of combustion <note>not too close to the Sun</note>; being direct in an angle or in succeeding houses; being oriental; and in the oriental quadrants of the circle of the Sun likewise; and in masculine signs, except for Libra.

<margin>Saying 24: On dreaded ascendants because of an eclipse of the Sun and Moon in the angle of a nativity and revolution.</margin>
¶ An eclipse of the luminaries in the angles of a birth or of **revolutions** <note>solar returns or yearly charts</note>...

# Ptolemy

revolutions of years are hindered according to the nature of that sign in which the eclipse occurs—that is, according to the house and the time in **B**: the rule is that the proportion between the ascending degree and the degree of the eclipse is to the hour of that event as the whole time is to the whole duration signified by the eclipse, with each hour representing a month.
¶ His intention is that if the Sun or Moon, or their eclipse, occurs in an angle <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</note> of a human nativity, or in the angles of the revolutions of their years, something horrific will follow in the place signified by that sign. For example, if it was the angle of the house of the kingdom, it will be in the kingdom. If it was the angle of the house of life, it will be in his body. Speak in this same manner concerning the other angles, except that the angles of revolutions are lighter than the angles of nativities. As for the hour when the event ought to happen most intensely, look at how many hours the eclipse lasted; and if it was a solar eclipse, I set it in the number of its hours, using a fraction of an hour according to the same proportion. Then look at that whole time, how many years it may be and what fraction of a year, and take from it an amount based on the distance between the ascending degree and the place of the eclipse out of 180 degrees. An example of this is that we find the Moon eclipsed in the first degree of Capricorn, which is the Midheaven <note>The highest point in the chart, governing career and status</note> of the nativity, and the duration of the eclipse is 3 hours. We know, therefore, that the kingdom of the native will be weakened for 3 months. We find the whole time to be 90 days. We then look at the distance between the ascending degree, which is the beginning of Aries, and the degree of the Midheaven, and it will be half—90 degrees—out of the 180 equal degrees. Let us therefore take half of the 90 days; and thus, 45 days after the eclipse, the heavy event it signifies will happen. Work in the same way for an eclipse of the Sun.

### Saying 25: On the direction of significators.

¶ You shall direct the significators when they are in the Midheaven of any city by the ascensions of the **right circle** <note>The celestial equator</note> according to the order of the signs; and when they are in the degree of the ascendant, by the degree of the ascensions of that same city. For those between these points, consider the ascensions of the degrees according to the proportion of their falling; and for the two places opposite to them, do the same. You shall direct the **parts** <note>Arabic Lots, like the Part of Fortune</note> backward, because the more their motions increase, the more the principles themselves are retarded.
¶ He intends that the **direction** <note>A method of predicting the timing of events by "moving" a planet forward in the chart</note> of significators, when they are in the degree of the Midheaven, should be according to the succession of the signs and according to the ascension of the right circle. If they are in the ascending degree, according to the succession of the signs, but by the ascensions of the city. If they are between those points, follow the same succession and the ascensions that are equated between them in the number of degrees. The direction of the Parts—namely, Fortune and others—is against the motion of the wandering stars <note>The planets</note>. The reason for this is that their change is like the motion of the circle moving the other fixed stars; for the degree of a Part belongs to the degree of the firmament and moves within it. Indeed, the motion of the whole is against the succession of the signs.

### Saying 26: On the concealment of a person or an action.

¶ The strongest concealment occurs when the significators are **incorporated with the Sun** <note>Combust, or hidden by the Sun's brilliance</note>, or are below the earth, or in a place not congruent with their house or **exaltation** <note>A sign where a planet's power is heightened</note>. The strongest it can be is when the significators are moving from their **fall** <note>The sign where a planet is weakest</note> toward their exaltation, and that planet is in an angle—that is, in a nature suitable to itself—namely, in a sign or an angle in the fourth or seventh house, which signify concealment, in which there is a sign suitable to the nature of the significator.
¶ Many have fallen into great error through a poor understanding of this chapter. What he intends here is that which is hidden: it is either a person or their action. Just as some-

<column-break/>

-one fearing a prince or someone who might pursue him would hide himself. An "action" is when someone reveals their secret to another which they wish to be hidden and made known to no one else. In these cases, the judgments are different. For when it is an action, it is more useful for the significators to be moving toward a **conjunction** <note>Alignment</note> with the Sun and to be in the house of the "end of the matter" <note>The 4th house</note>. In the case of a person, however, let these things be removed, for these conditions judge that he who hides himself will die upon the very gallows. But in the concealment of a person, it is praiseworthy for the significator to have already passed the degree of conjunction and not yet have emerged from all the rays. And when the significator goes from its fall to its exaltation, it signifies that he will appear in his strength and good perseverance, and that the end of the matter will be praised. Significators are seen signifying those things which ought to be hidden.

### Saying 27: On the signs of Venus in the ascendant of a nativity in various members and of other planets.

¶ Venus makes the native attain pleasure in the limb that is signified by the sign in which she is at the hour of birth; and the other planets give whatever they give in this same manner.
¶ The ancients agreed on this: that Venus causes pleasure to be attained, and there is no doubt of it, because her place is most suitable for pleasures. And I have often seen some in whose nativities Venus was in Aries and their ascendant was in the same; their pleasure was in seeing famous things, because sight is in the head, and the head is signified by Aries and the ascendant. And I saw her in Leo for some who were great lovers of women, because Leo holds the heart, in which there is love. And I saw her in Libra for some who were very lustful, because Libra governs the private parts; and their libido was incestuous according to the fortune or misfortune of the aspect toward her.

### Saying 28: On the strengthening of a nature composed of the natures of two wandering stars.

¶ When it happens to you that the Moon is joined bodily to two planets, seek its bodily conjunction with one of the **fixed stars** whose nature is mixed from the natures of both.
¶ When it is necessary to strengthen a nature composed of the natures of two wandering stars <note>planets</note>, and it is difficult for us to have a significator—whether it be the Moon or another planet—in aspect to them, we look to one of the fixed stars whose natures are composed of the natures of those wandering stars, and we investigate so that the Moon or the significator is joined bodily to it. This is so clear it needs no example; you will find such things in the 9th chapter of the first book of *Al-Abra*.

### Saying 29: On knowing the dignity of the native and his death or end through the nativity.

¶ Fixed stars give great goods, exceeding measure; but many times they end in evil.
¶ The most praiseworthy of those things we intend to know in nativities after origin and nourishment is the dignity of the native. Its signification is from the oriental planets and their leaders, provided they are significators of the native and strong in an angle—that is, in the degree of the angle or near it within 3 degrees. And it is already signified that the native may reach the dignity of his parents, but no more. But when there is one of the fixed stars which are called **Beibenie** <note>original: "bei bemie," likely from the Arabic *al-biya-baniya*, referring to the primary stars of the first magnitude</note>—that is, the "hearts" of the fixed stars, such as the Heart of the Bull <note>Aldebaran</note>, the Heart of the Lion <note>Regulus</note>, and the Heart of the Scorpion <note>Antares</note>—namely, those of the first magnitude in the circle of signs. Also, all those of the first magnitude are called the hearts of other stars that are larger and in their first quantity. If these are in the ascendant, or in the angle of the Midheaven, or with the Lord and the **Hyleg** <note>original: "neuba," referring to the giver of life</note> of the nativity from the luminaries—namely, the one with dignity, such as the Sun by day or the Moon by night—and with the Part of Fortune, his existence will be exalted to the greatest dignity, until he counsels the kings of a great kingdom, even if he be of vile and unknown lineage.

### Aphorism 30. On the succession of kinsmen to the throne.

The labor of kinsmen of kings to succeed to the kingdom requires that his birth chart [nativity] agree with the state of the celestial circle at the hour in which the king himself was enthroned.
Know that unlearned astrologers observe the births of a king's kinsmen, and when they find a birth diminished by the fact that the planets are not oriental <note>Planets rising before the sun, considered more active</note>, or not in the power of an "angle" <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a chart</note>, and other such things, they conclude that he will not succeed to the kingdom. They overlook what is paramount: that the Ascendant of his birth, or the Midheaven, should agree with the Ascendant or Midheaven of the hour of the king's coronation; or it should be related to the Ascendant of the "minor" or "middle" conjunctions <note>The alignment of Jupiter and Saturn, used to predict the rise and fall of empires</note> which signified that religious sect or dynasty.
Indeed, I remember when I was one of those unlearned astrologers, still a young man: a certain servant of King Bumai Rogoei <note>original: "Bumai rogoei"; likely a corruption of an Arabic name, possibly Al-Mahdi or a court official</note> came bringing the birth chart of Aaron <note>Harun al-Rashid (r. 786–809 AD), the famous Abbasid Caliph</note>, the king's son, asking if it could be determined whether this child would succeed his father in the kingdom. And when I made my prediction, I found his "heavy" planets <note>Slow-moving planets like Saturn and Jupiter</note> were occidental and falling away from the angles and the sun; I could not see from where I might signal the father's kingdom to him. Thus I delayed giving judgment until I had inquired more studiously. 
After a short time, I asked a certain old man called Laleth <note>original: "Laleth filiũ alimelit elcemini"; likely a Latinization of an Arabic name like Al-Khwarizmi</note>, a man skilled in giving judgments. When he looked at the figure, he asked whose birth it was; I said Aaron, the king's son. He said, "He will obtain the place for nearly 10 years in the kingdom, and he will be under the power or governance of another, or he will be subject to someone." I asked how he grasped this. He, holding me back with talk, did not want to show me. However, when I did not cease to honor him with gifts [bribes], he said: "His Ascendant is Scorpio, and the sun is in Virgo." And it was exactly so when the prince entered into his kingdom. And Aaron succeeded his father and reigned for nine years and some months, for the sun in Virgo held the place of the Midheaven. And similarly, Rababachat Almanfoz <note>The Caliph Al-Mansur</note> judged that he would obtain the empire while he was his guest, and Almanfoz was then in the greatest poverty, in the days of the Benumeie <note>The Umayyad dynasty (Banu Umayya)</note>. All these things I have recorded in a certain book of mine.

### Aphorism 31. On the state of the king in his kingdom, and what happens to him and his household in life.

When the "direction" <note>A timing technique moving points in the chart by one degree per year</note> of the significator of the kingdom reaches a star that "cuts" <note>A malefic planet that interrupts life or power</note>, that king or a powerful man in the realm will die. And every star that is in the sign of the *alynthie* <note>original: "alynthie"; from the Arabic *al-intihad*, referring to "profections" or yearly revolutions of the chart</note> of the annual revolution signifies the death of a powerful person in the kingdom that same year, according to the nature of the star.
He means by this that the degree of the Ascendant at the beginning of the reign—and also in any high office—when it is directed through the ascensions of that country in which the kingdom is, at one degree per year: when the direction reaches a "malefic" [unfortunate star], harm will come to some great man, according to the star's nature. For the Ascendant is the "midheaven of the wealthy." When it reaches a "benefic" [fortunate star], prosperity occurs. Also, every star in the sign of the *alynthie* (the annual revolution) from the years of the reign will kill a powerful person similar to that star. 
If it is **Saturn**: he will be of a hidden mind, not revealing what he has in his soul. 
If **Jupiter**: he will be a judge or similar official. 
If **Mars**: he will be spirited, or a leader of soldiers. 
If the **Sun**: he will be a king from among the kinsmen or the powerful. 
If **Venus**: it will be a woman of great fame. 
If **Mercury**: he will be a wise man or a scribe. 
If the **Moon**: he will be one of the king's household servants or ministers. 
If the star is oriental and rising in its apogee <note>The highest/furthest point in its orbit</note>: it will be a young man. If it is occidental and descending: it will be an old man. And according to the length of its stay in 

<column-break/>

the angle, and according to the strength of its being, its exaltation, or other dignity, such will be the honor and power of this person (that is, the one dying). And according to the fortune of the star, such will be the substance or wealth of the dying man.

### Aphorism 32. Regarding the significance of two birth charts in relation to concord, friendship, and enmity.

The concord of two people in any matter is found by the placement of that matter in both birth charts. If it is in a praiseworthy state, there will be good concord between them; whoever is stronger in that place will be the actor and leader, and the weaker will be the passive subject.
He means that if two people are to agree in one work or business, the astrologer must look at their significators for that business. If all are in agreement, they will agree in everything; if in none, they agree in nothing. If one of them "looks" at the other in a trine or sextile aspect <note>Beneficial angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, it signifies agreement. But if the aspect is a square or opposition <note>Tense angles of 90 or 180 degrees</note>, it signifies the greatest discord. If they do not "aspect" each other at all, concord will never be perfected. The one stronger in his house and angle will be the victor over the other.

### Aphorism 33. Regarding the significance of two birth charts in love, based on the Sun and Moon and their aspects.

Friendship and enmity are determined by the exchange of the places of the two "luminaries" <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> in the two birth charts, and from the similarity of their Ascendants. The "obedient sign" indicates the strongest friendship.
He means that when the Sun in one person's chart is where the Moon was in the other's, and vice versa, and the Ascendant of one is in a sextile or trine aspect to the other, deep affection will be established. The sign "obeying" the other will show the stronger love and inclination.

### Aphorism 34. On the difference between a human birth and that of another animal, by the degree of the *almusteuli*.

The *almusteuli* <note>original: "almusteuli"; from the Arabic *al-mustawli*, meaning the "Almuten" or the planet with the most dignity over a certain point</note> over the place of the conjunction will be in a similar degree to the angle of every human born, using the angles present during that conjunction; the same applies to the "prevention" <note>The Full Moon preceding the birth</note>.
Ptolemy’s knowledge in the *animodar* <note>A method for rectifying a birth time to find the exact minute of birth</note> is that the place of the *almusteuli* over the preceding New or Full Moon always agrees with an angle of a human's birth chart. A degree that does not match this will not be the Ascendant of a human. I have tested this in the births of brute animals, and I never found an angle—whether the Ascendant or the Midheaven—equal to the degree of the *almusteuli* of the preceding conjunction.
The sense of this chapter is that in a human birth, the degree of the Ascendant or Midheaven must be the same number as the degree of the *almusteuli* of the preceding syzygy <note>New or Full Moon</note>. If this is not the case, it is not the birth of a human, but of some other animal.

### Aphorism 35. Regarding the cold, temperateness, or heat of winter.

When a star reaches any of the four quarters of the year at a place in the zodiac where the Sun is not, and the quality of the air changes: if the star is in accord with that quality, it will strengthen that quarter...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the "Centiloquium," following the discussion on the succession of kings and the agreement between birth charts and coronation charts.
