->Ptolemy<-

...fourth: and in this manner always speak in all matters.
¶ He intends that when a star has reached any of the winter signs, and if it is a cold star like **Saturn**, it will strengthen and increase the cold of that winter. And if it is a warm star, it will temper the nature of that winter. If that star is warm and reaches a warm sign, it will increase the heat of that summer; and so it shall be in the others, namely in the dry and the moist signs.

### Aphorism 36. On which buildings fixed stars should be employed, and on which the wandering planets.

¶ Use the **fixed stars** <note>Stars that do not move relative to each other, like the constellations</note> in the layout of cities, and the **planets** <note>original: "erratice," the wandering stars</note> in the construction of houses. All cities founded while **Mars** was in the Midheaven <note>The highest point in the sky at a given time</note>—or any fixed star of a "martial" nature <note>original: "ex albemenia eius nature"; 'albemenia' is a corruption of an Arabic term referring to a star's complex or nature</note>—their leaders shall perish by the sword.
¶ He intends that fixed stars of a nature similar to **Jupiter** or **Venus** should be in the Ascendant of the city's founding, in the Midheaven, in the "house of the end of things" <note>the 4th house</note>, and in the 7th house. The wandering planets should be "looking" at them <note>forming an astrological aspect</note> to influence them. Because the "Almuten" <note>original: "almultuuli"; the planet with the most dignity or power over a specific point</note> in the appearance of cities must be of the greatest slowness and stationary, so that their foundation may be prolonged and their destruction delayed. Indeed, fixed stars signify greater things than planets do: give one fixed star to cities, and planets to houses. Then he said: if Mars or a fixed star of a martial nature is in the Midheaven, many of its princes will perish by the sword. For the Midheaven is the "Ascendant" of its princes <note>meaning the point that governs the rulers</note>, and Mars in such a place ends their time by the sword.

### Aphorism 37. On knowing the whole being of the native, and his end, through the ascensions of the birth.

<margin>Note</margin>
¶ When it happens that someone’s Ascendant is **Pisces** or **Virgo**, it is the greatest occasion of his power; he whose Ascendant is **Aries** or **Libra** will be stronger at the time of his own death; and **Scorpio** or **Taurus** at the time of illness; and in this manner it differs in the other Ascendants.
¶ Ptolemy tells us that any two houses that are [ruled by the same planet] are almost as one, whether they are the Ascendant of the birth or of a question. The other house over which the planet rules is like a physical conjunction of one head with the lord of the other. By this we know that what the Ascendant signifies is moved toward what the other house signifies. For example, if Virgo or Pisces is the Ascendant, then **Gemini** or **Sagittarius** will be the royal house <note>Because Mercury rules both Virgo and Gemini, and Jupiter rules both Pisces and Sagittarius</note>. And the person born, without great labor, will advance himself in royal matters. Similarly, if Scorpio is the Ascendant, Aries will be the 6th house <note>the house of illness</note>; and if Taurus is the Ascendant, the 6th house will be Libra. Then [the lord] will be the cause of his illness. In the same way, if the Ascendant is Aries or Libra, it will be the occasion of his death, because Scorpio or Taurus will be the 8th house <note>the house of death</note>. If the Ascendant is **Capricorn**, the native will be the cause of the preservation of his own money and profit. If the Ascendant is **Aquarius**, he himself will be the cause of men’s enmities—that is, because of Capricorn being in the 12th house <note>the house of secret enemies</note>.
Behold, I knew a certain man whose Ascendant was Aries, who became insane from his excessive illness. Before he lost his senses due to the multitude of "vapors," he felt as if he were suffocating around the arteries—which is the sign of Aries. One day, taking a knife from his writing desk, he cut his own throat, severing the arteries; the blood did not stop flowing until his life ended. In this city, I also saw a man whom the son of Ametrillo <note>original: "ametrillois"; likely a reference to an Arabic ruler like Al-Ma'mun</note> appointed to found the Great Mosque <note>original: "melchidā"; likely from the Arabic 'masjid'</note>, which he delayed. Therefore the Emperor, being indignant, made him come before him. When he arrived, the Emperor asked why he left the work unfinished; the man, through his misfortune, answered foolishly and moved the King to anger. Because of this fall from grace, he died; his birth Ascendant had been Libra. Ptolemy said: "a man shall be," etc. Because it does not *always* happen that everyone with these Ascendants must be the cause of their own death. But when the Lord of the Birth is also the "Killer," he will kill himself. If the chart signifies he will die in his own place, it will happen accordingly. And if they are badly placed

<column-break/>

in the 8th house, it signifies the native will be killed. If "Fortunes" <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> are there or look upon it, it signifies he will die in his own bed.

### Aphorism 38. On the significance of Mercury in the houses of the elders in a birth chart.

¶ When **Mercury** is in any of the houses of **Saturn** <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note> and Mercury is strong in its own state, it gives a goodness of intelligence or a deep understanding of fundamental things or the principles of the arts. And if it is in the two signs of **Mars** <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, it will give strength and sharpness of mind, or the goodness of sudden eloquence—and also dishonor; and the stronger of the two places is Aries.
¶ He in whose nature Mercury is present will be sharp; it will add sudden eloquence beyond his own thought, and his prudence will be greater in hearing, understanding, and meditating. Its presence in a falling and dry sign <note>Aries</note> demands speed and agility where it is joined to "Fortunes" among the planets and fixed stars. That is, he will understand with such haste that he understands things before they are even heard or spoken; it will seem as though he understands, even when he does not. And when it occurs in a temperate sign inclining toward cold and moisture, it fixes his mind on whatever he involves himself in, and he will be diligent in it. In those two signs which are Capricorn and Aquarius, it is with its own temperament: something that Saturn attributes to them from the "hiding of the soul" <note>meaning introversion or deep thought</note>. Therefore it must be as Ptolemy said. Its place in Aries gives him a "burning," because of what he has gained from Mars in sharpness and agility; it is not so in Scorpio because of its moist nature, which breaks the nature of Mars. Indeed, when Mercury is in Capricorn or Aquarius in a birth chart, the Indians choose that person to practice the sciences, because they have tested this often, and it never deceives them.

### Aphorism 39. On the bad state of the 11th house in the enthronement of kings.

¶ A "falling" state of the 11th house and its Lord during the enthronement of kings signifies that evil shall happen to his advisors and his substance. In the same way, a bad state of the 2nd house—which is the house of substance—signifies that the people will gain very little with that king.
¶ Astrologers have already agreed that the 10th house in every royal arrangement is the place of the King himself; the 11th is for his helpers and his wealth; the Ascendant is for his person; and the 2nd is for the wealth of the people. Therefore, the 11th house hinders the advisors, and the 2nd house hinders the wealth of the people if "Malefics" <note>Mars or Saturn</note> are there physically or by aspect, or if the "Tail of the Dragon" <note>The South Node of the Moon, considered unlucky</note> or any evil fixed stars are present; or if its Lord is falling or "combust" <note>too close to the sun</note>, or if the Moon is weak.

### Aphorism 40. On the indication of the strength of "Malefics" in the Ascendant of a birth regarding those things in which nature is declared.

¶ When "Malefics" <note>Mars or Saturn</note> are in the Ascendant of a birth, the native will delight in tasteless things and bitter flavors. Such a person's delight will also be in things with terrible odors and other similar things.
¶ Astrologers are in agreement that when the Lord of the Ascendant alone rules the birth and no other participates, the nature of the native will be according to what is said of that planet. If it is Saturn, it signifies the native delights in the taste of vinegar and harsh things. If it is Mars, he will delight in sharp and bitter things and turbid wine; his delight will also be in terrible smells, so much so that he prefers the heat of dung in intercourse over a good and sweet scent; and foul, stinking fish will seem flavorful to him. Indeed, I saw a certain rich man whose birth lords were Mars and Saturn; they were strong, and he delighted in eating sea monsters that were unsalted and stinking, and he cooked them in an oven. He even swore that when he had intercourse with beautiful and sweet-smelling women, his "rod" <note>his penis</note> failed him; but with a vile and smelly woman, he would be strengthened.

### Aphorism 41. On the indication of those going and returning and their profit.

Lentil. Ptolemy.

->Centiloquium<-

¶ Beware of the <term>infortunes</term> <note>malefic planets, usually Saturn or Mars</note> in the 8th house and its lord for one departing on a journey; and in the 2nd house and its lord for one returning.
¶ The 7th house is the place toward which the traveler tends. The 8th house from that <note>the 2nd house of the original chart</note> indicates what will happen to them there and what they will gain there. The Ascendant, however, is the place to which the traveler returns; and the 2nd house signifies what they will obtain there. Let the Moon always be "fortunate" <note>well-placed and well-aspected</note> in a good house from the Ascendant. Know that in changing one's house, if **Jupiter** is in the 2nd house and the **Moon** is in a good and suitable relationship to that same 2nd house, the person will always be enriched.

**Aphorism 42. On the significance of the planets regarding illnesses based on their state in the root birth chart.**

¶ In cases of illness, if the **Moon** is in the sign where an <term>infortune</term> <note>malefic planet</note> was at the hour of birth—or in its opposition or square <note>difficult astrological aspects of 180 or 90 degrees</note>—the illness will be difficult. But it is much more severe if an infortune was in that sign at the hour the illness began, or in a position deemed "praiseworthy" <note>influential</note> in the chart. When the Moon is in the place of a <term>fortune</term> <note>benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus</note> at the beginning of the illness, the sickness will be mild; unless the temperament <note>original: "complexio"</note> of the illness matches the nature of that fortune, which would then nourish the disease. Tell this only after you have determined the severity of the illness, as we said in Chapter 12 of the third book of *Albraza* <note>original: "albraza"; likely a reference to a specific astronomical or medical tables book</note>; for in that book it is taught to which temperament an infirmity belongs.
¶ This is now made clear to us by **Haly** <note>Ali ibn Ridwan, a famous medieval commentator on Ptolemy</note> in his second treatise on the book of *Critical Days* <note>original: "libri dierum criticorum"</note>; and he said that the learned Egyptians do the same. But according to **Ptolemy** in the 13th chapter, he taught us that if a planet is an evil <term>hinc</term> <note>original: "hinc"; likely a typo for "hinc" or "hinc" in the sense of 'from here' or 'in this place'</note> to the temperament of the illness, its malice will be diminished. If, however, a "fortune" <note>benefic</note> is suited to the illness, its good influence will be lessened. He said this excellently: judge according to the magnitude of the illness; for if it is slight, the illness will not reach a great state.

**Aphorism 43. On the significance of "fortunes" or "evils" regarding lust that occurs within or outside the law.**

¶ Matters that occur according to a natural state, such as marriage, and according to the laws, are destroyed by the <term>infortunes</term> <note>malefics</note>. Matters, however, that occur according to nature but not according to laws—or those which occur neither naturally nor according to laws—are destroyed by the <term>fortunes</term> <note>benefics</note>.
¶ He means that for marriage to be beneficial, the fortunes should be in the "inception" <note>the beginning of the union</note>. They should be joined with the <term>significator</term> <note>the planet representing the person or the marriage</note>; whereas the infortunes cause harm. In a marriage, they are destroyed by the infortunes. In fornication, however, which occurs naturally but not according to laws—as well as among <term>sodomites</term> <note>those engaging in "unnatural" acts</note> and women who "rub themselves against each other" <note>original: "mulieribus se pfricantibus"; a medieval reference to lesbianism</note>, all of which are outside nature and laws—the fortunes harm them, while the infortunes help them. It is necessary for the astrologer to know each of these things: which is natural and which is outside nature. And as I have said of marriage, so it is in other natural matters, and regarding sufficiency or abundance in things outside nature.

**Aphorism 44. On the significance of the Ascendant of an infirmity being contrary to the birth chart.**

¶ When the Ascendant of an illness is contrary to the figure of the birth chart, and the year of the "profection" <note>a predictive technique where the chart is advanced by one sign per year</note> has not reached that birth figure, it will be very bad.
¶ By "contrary," he means that the Ascendant of the illness is the 7th house of the birth chart, or the end of the house under the earth <note>the 4th house</note>, or the house of death <note>the 8th house</note>; this will then be horrible unless the figure of the yearly revolution is similar to it; in that case, the infirmity will be lighter.

**Aphorism 45. On the significance of the character of the born person through the Ascendant and the significator.**

¶ In every birth where neither the Ascendant nor its significator is in a **human sign** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, the first half of Sagittarius, or Aquarius</note>, the person will be among those who do not associate with other men.

<column-break/>

¶ When it is a human Ascendant, the person will be social and domestic with others, according to the human form. When it is in the form of wild animals <note>bestial signs like Leo or Aries</note>, he will be like a tyrant and furious among them. Nor does he wish to be like any of his parents. It will be the same way if the birth is by day and the **Sun** is the <term>hyleg</term> <note>the "Giver of Life" point</note> and is in a human sign; or if the birth is at night and the **Moon** is the hyleg and is in a human sign, or in some other [praiseworthy] position. Since in a daytime birth the Sun will be the lord of the <term>neuba</term> <note>original: "neuba"; likely referring to a lot, a turn, or a planetary period</note>, and in a nighttime birth, the Moon will be the mistress of the neubas; thus regarding the lord of the birth's neuba from its hyleg.

**Aphorism 46. On the significance of the fixed stars and the status of superior and inferior planets and the Moon in the root birth chart.**

¶ The greatest fortune in a birth comes from the fixed stars, namely the <term>albehenia</term> <note>stars or constellations of a specific nature</note>, and the angles of the <term>allure</term> <note>likely "al-urūsh," an Arabic term for the foundations or supportive configurations of the chart</note>, that is, the conjunctive and the leading ones, and from the placement of the "Part of Fortune of the Kingdom" in the Ascendant.
¶ We have already mentioned the manner of fixed stars and angles in Aphorism 29. The bad state and the *allure* were explained in Aphorism 30. The "leading" status <note>original: "ductoria"</note> means that the heavy planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, Mars</note> are in a praiseworthy state, being "oriental" <note>rising before the Sun</note> in the angles. Light planets <note>Venus, Mercury</note> that are "occidental" <note>setting after the Sun</note> are praiseworthy. For there are some that are occidental and unpraiseworthy; these are the light planets that are occidental to the **Moon**. Let the "Part of Fortune" fall into the "enthronement of the kingdom" in the Ascendant of the birth. "Leading" status means the three superior planets are oriental to the Sun and in an angle; then they are praiseworthy. If they are occidental, they are unpraiseworthy, but not greatly so. The inferior planets, however, are praiseworthy when occidental to the Sun. If they are oriental, they are unpraiseworthy. With the Moon, it is the reverse: for the superiors are praiseworthy when occidental to the Moon, but unpraiseworthy when oriental to her. And the inferiors are praiseworthy if they are oriental to the Moon, and unpraiseworthy if occidental to her. "Ponderous" <note>heavy/slow</note> planets are those surrounding the Sun while oriental in the angles.

**Aphorism 47. On the benefits, obstacles, and injuries between people based on bad or good status.**

¶ When a malefic in someone's birth chart falls physically onto the place of a "fortune" <note>a benefic planet</note> in another's chart, it signifies that some horrible evil will come to the one whose chart has the fortune from the one whose chart has the malefic. The type of evil will be from the nature of the planet. The area in which it happens will be from the nature of its house. In this manner, it happens in all "participations" <note>connections between charts</note>.
¶ Participation occurs when a malefic is in the place of a benefic, or a benefic is in the place of a benefic, or a malefic in the place of a malefic. A malefic in the place of a benefic hinders the owner of the benefic and helps the "owner" of the malefic. A benefic in the place of a benefic signifies that each will benefit his companion. And a malefic in the place of a malefic signifies that each will hinder his companion. The harm will come from the nature of the malefic. If it is **Saturn**, the harm will be hidden, like an accuser or a blasphemer. If it is **Mars** <note>abbreviated as "nis"</note>, it will be of "thickness," that is, of choice and invasion <note>violence</note>. The benefit of the matter comes from the house where it falls: if it is in the royal house, it will be on behalf of the king; if in the house of substance <note>the 2nd house</note>, it will be in wealth, and so on for the others.

**Aphorism 48. On the suitability of subjects with their lords.**

¶ When the 10th house of the minister's Ascendant—that is, the king's—is the king's Ascendant, or if the minister's Ascendant is another's, they are companions; and when the <term>almutaz</term> <note>Almuten; the planet with the most power in a chart</note> comes over one of them, with the almutaz over the other in harmony and agreement of signs, it will signify the adaptation of their being and little discord between them.
¶ He means by this that a minister, or a follower, or a captive, or a wife, when they are in their natural places relative to the king, or the leading lord, or the husband, there will be [harmony].

**Aphorism 49. On the power of subjects or associates over their lords or partners.**

¶ When the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the servant is the same as the Ascendant of the lord, the servant will rule over his lord; or he who associates himself as a follower will rule over his partner. And similarly, if the lord of the 6th house <note>the house of servants and labor</note> of someone’s birth chart is in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>the highest point of the chart, representing career and authority</note>, there receiving its disposition from the lordship of the Ascendant of that same birth chart, he will have good mastery over his servants; and in this way, it confers similar results to these.

¶ The <term>Midheaven</term> <note>original: '10e' for the 10th house</note> is more prominent in strength than the other <term>angles</term> <note>the four primary points of a chart: Ascendant, Midheaven, Descendant, and Imum Coeli</note>, because it is entirely visible, which is not the case in the other three angles. And when the Ascendant of the servant or follower is [placed there], signifying that his state is better than that of his lord, or his position, he will rule over him. The receiver of an astrological "disposition" is stronger than the one giving it to him. Therefore, the reception of the disposition of the servant’s significator and the lordship of the lord’s Ascendant signifies a good partnership or closeness of the lord with him, and that the servants will honor him. This must also be the case among brothers and sons, and in those who follow this pattern.

**Aphorism 50. On the conjunctions of the planets and their utilities, increase, and decrease.**

¶ Do not forget that there are 120 conjunctions <note>mathematical combinations</note> among the <term>erratic stars</term> <note>the planets</note>; for in them lies the greatest knowledge of those things that happen in this world, which undergo increase and decrease.

¶ These 120 conjunctions are contained in every possible combination reached by the 7 planets. These are: Binary <note>pairs</note>, Ternary <note>groups of three</note>, Quaternary <note>groups of four</note>, Quinary <note>groups of five</note>, Senary <note>groups of six</note>, and Septenary <note>all seven together</note>.

### ->Groups of Seven.<-

**¶ One group of seven.**
Saturn. Jupiter. Mars. Sun. Venus. Mercury. Moon.

**¶ Aphorism 51. Regarding the direct and ascending [position] of the Moon: in the hour of birth, from the hour of the falling of the seed <note>original: "casus spermatis," referring to conception</note> to that same place, the average stay <note>the gestation period</note> is increased or decreased in the greater and lesser [stays].**

¶ The place of the Moon at birth is the same degree ascending in the circle at the hour the seed fell into the womb. And the place of the Moon at the hour the seed fell is the degree ascending at the hour of birth.

¶ In this, the <term>physicians</term> <note>natural philosophers or medical doctors</note> are in agreement, though the stay of those born in the wombs of their mothers varies and is not the same for all. Among them, therefore, the average stay is 273 days. This occurs when the Moon and the ascending degree have completed equal orbits during the time of the stay—that is, for those born in the mother's womb—and the Moon is then found in the ascending degree of the birth. The greater stay is 288 days, which is a time increased beyond the average stay after the orbits are completed, by less than one orbit. Through this, the Moon is found beyond the ascending degree. The lesser stay is 257 days, which is a subtraction from the average time, and that subtraction is less than an orbit; through this, the Moon is found subtracted from the ascending degree. This is calculated beyond the degree in which the Moon was at the hour the seed fell, which will be the ascending degree at the hour of birth. The astrologers have recorded these stays of births in their books with long-winded discourse, as they are very necessary to them in their judgments. For these stays show us the location of the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> at the time of the woman's conception. And that is the first beginning of a birth, from which we discern the <term>complexion</term> <note>the balance of bodily humors: blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile</note> of the body, the shape of the limbs, and many things that happen to the person before they leave the womb. Those who lived before Ptolemy labored excessively in the investigation of the falling of the seed. But Ptolemy revealed to us briefly and by an easy path that the place of the Moon at the time of birth is the Ascendant of the conception. And the place of the Moon at the time of conception is the ascending degree of the birth. Toward which both the Ascendant and the Moon return to their place in equal orbits during the average stay, or are increased or decreased in the greater and lesser stays.

**¶ Aphorism 52. On the height and shortness of the newborn through the place of the significator and the Ascendant.**

¶ Tall <term>significators</term> <note>the planets ruling the birth or specific traits</note> will be at the summit of their circles, and their Ascendant will be in the beginnings of the signs. Short significators, however, will be in the lower part of their circles, and their Ascendant will be at the end of the signs. You may also be aided by other factors, such as the <term>oriental</term> <note>rising before the sun</note> planets, their <term>stations</term> <note>points where a planet appears to stop moving</note>, and through signs signifying height—which are signs of many <term>ascensions</term> <note>signs that take longer to rise over the horizon</note>—or shortness, which are signs of few ascensions.

¶ By "significators," he means the planets of greatest dignity in the Ascendant of the birth. The "summit of the circle" is the point furthest from the center of the earth. The <term>rectors</term> <note>guides or calculators</note> of the planets know this: when the average course of diversity and the cusp are at nearly one minute, it signifies that the newborn will be tall. This is after the astrologer has considered what we mentioned about the state of the <term>revolution</term> <note>the annual return or cycle</note>. He should also look at the father and mother regarding height; if they were tall or average, judge for the child accordingly. If both were tall, judge for height. If both were short, judge for a middle ground in height—specifically if the significators are at the summits of their circles. The ascending degree of the birth signifies height when it is in the beginning of the ascending sign, up to its 5th degree, and the ascensions of the sign are greater than 30 degrees, and the

<column-break/>

lord of the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>the highest point of the chart</note> or the lord of the Ascendant is oriental. But if the significators are in the lower part of the circle and in a state contrary to all we have listed, the person will be at the extreme of shortness. The "lower part of the circle" is the shorter line drawn from the place of the star to the center of the earth. Once you know the state of the parents in height and shortness: if they were tall, the child will not be at the extreme of shortness, but will be average. If the significators are at their closest distances <note>perigee</note>, and the Ascendant is at the end of the sign, and the lord [of the Ascendant] is in the western Midheaven, and if all factors do not agree, predict an average height.

**¶ Aphorism 53. On thinness and fatness, lightness and slowness of motion of the newborn through the significators of the lord of the Ascendant.**

¶ When the significators of the Ascendant have no <term>latitude</term> <note>distance north or south of the ecliptic/celestial equator</note>, the person will be lean. If they have much latitude, the person will be fat. If the latitude is southern, their movement will be light <note>nimble</note> despite that fleshiness. And if it is northern, they will be heavy in movement. When the significator is in <term>retrogradation</term> <note>appearing to move backward</note>, or in direct motion, or at its stations, it will act similarly.

¶ What was said above regarding significators refers to the lord of the Ascendant and the lord of the matter questioned. When a planet is with its <term>center</term> <note>original: "geriçar," likely a corruption of a term for the epicycle center or heart</note> at the same minute [as the ecliptic], the newborn will be lean. If it has latitude, it will add flesh in proportion to its latitude. Therefore, if the latitude is southern—which is when it is less than 180 degrees before the point of the <term>head</term> <note>the North Node</note>—its movement is light, because this part is hot and makes all things light. And if it is northern—which is after the point of the head by 180 degrees—because this part is of great coldness, it weighs down whatever is produced in it; the newborn will be heavy in their movement. Retrogradation signifies fatness because the planets are then cold and moist. Likewise for the first station. Direct motion and the second station signify leanness, because the planets are then said to be hot and dry. It is necessary for the astrologer not to hasten in judging any of these until he has most certainly investigated the state of the parents in fatness and leanness, just as we revealed in the preceding section.

**¶ Aphorism 54. On the significations in buildings.**

¶ No building whose significators are then planets existing under the earth will be raised up.

¶ Astrologers agree that the movements which move works and bodies according to their natures are proportional to the movements of the stars. Since this is necessary, if we wish to raise a building, let us place the significator above the Ascendant of its beginning in a conjunction of stars existing above the earth. For a conjunction of planets under the earth spreads its stability and its erection <note>meaning it stays grounded or low rather than rising high</note>.

**¶ Aphorism 55. On those things which happen to a ship from the state of the planets.**

¶ The hindrance of Mars in ships is indeed diminished when it is not in the Midheaven or the 11th house, because in these two places, whatever is in the ship will be lost through the mastery of pirates over it. And if with this the ascending degree is made unfortunate by the fixed stars <term>albebenis</term> <note>prominent or projecting fixed stars</note> which are of the nature of Mars, the ship and whatever is in it will be burned.

¶ Of all the varieties of unfortunate natures, some frequently expel the forces of others. The hindrances that occur at sea belong to Saturn. But the hindrances of Mars, when it is in the Ascendant or presides over it, are minor; however, its presence in the Midheaven or the 11th house—because one of these, the tenth, is a plague to the ship, and the other to the things possessed within it—brings fear of pirates. When the fixed stars of the nature of Mars in the Ascendant make it unfortunate along with those things we said before—that is, if it is in the Midheaven or the 11th—the ship will be burned. And so with all varieties, etc. End.

### **C** Aphorism 56. On the increase of bodily humors and their deepening.

**C** The <term>humors</term> <note>original: "humiditates," the four vital fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—thought to govern health</note> of the body increase in the first quarter [of the lunar cycle]. In the second quarter, however, they recede. And they follow this same proportion in the remaining two quarters.
**C** This means that the bodily humors increase from the hour of the <term>conjunction</term> <note>when the Sun and Moon meet in the same degree</note> until the fourth aspect <note>the square aspect, or 90 degrees</note> of the Sun and Moon; they emerge from the internal parts so as to become apparent, acting like rivers whose waters are rising, and this increase is called an "accession." From the fourth aspect until the full moon, they contract from the extremities of the body back to the interior; they are like rivers whose waters are receding. From the full moon until the second fourth aspect, they behave as in the first quarter. And from the second fourth aspect until the next conjunction, they recede according to the proportion of the second quarter.

### **C** Aphorism 57. On the significance of the doctor, the illness, and the medicine.

**C** When Saturn and its Lord are afflicted <note>meaning poorly positioned or weakened by other planets</note> in the case of the sick, remove the doctor from the patient.
**C** According to the astrologers, the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and its Lord signify the state of the sick person. The seventh house and its Lord signify the doctor. When these are "unfortunate" <note>under bad planetary influence</note>, they signify the confusion and error of the doctor. In such a case, remove the doctor or change the medicines for the patient. <term>Zael</term> <note>Sahl ibn Bishr, a famous 9th-century Jewish astrologer</note> distinguished this differently: the Ascendant refers to the doctor; the tenth house to the patient; the sixth house to the infirmity; and the fourth house to the medicine.

### **C** Aphorism 58. On the significance of the year's conjunction and the strength of a single year to the greatest cycle.

**C** Look to where the place of the "minor conjunction" <note>original: "alkirem minoris," from the Arabic "al-qiran," referring to the meeting of Saturn and Jupiter</note> falls from the Ascendant of the year in which that conjunction occurred. According to the distance in signs between that place and the Ascendant, there will be years until the "greater cycle" begins.
**C** Ptolemy intends that one must look at the Ascendant of the year in which the minor conjunction falls. There are indeed different types of conjunctions. The **Minor** is the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter until they meet a second time, lasting nearly 20 years. The **Middle** is when Saturn and Jupiter meet in one <term>triplicity</term> <note>a group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> until they move to another, lasting about 240 years. The **Major** is when Saturn and Jupiter cycle through all four triplicities and return to the one where they started, lasting nearly 960 years. Once you know the Ascendant of that year or the sign of the conjunction, look at the signs or degrees between those places; count every sign as a year and every degree as a portion of a year. By "alkirem," he means the physical meeting of bodies, not just an aspect.

### **C** Aphorism 59. On the errors of those making judgments and their instruction.

**C** When you are asked about a person who is absent, do not judge them to be dead until you have ruled out drunkenness; let no wound suggest itself to you that is actually just a bloodletting; nor should you assume acquired wealth until you have ruled out money held in trust for someone else. The same logic applies to all judgments.
**C** We have already said in the first explanation of this book that the one who treats judgments works through forms that are close to the truth, and we have shown this to be true. Therefore, in the strength of judgments, there is no clear distinction between one who is sleeping and one who is dead; or between one who is wounded and one who has been bled; or between one who was entrusted with money and one who earned it. Indeed, I heard from my father (may God spare him) that when he was with those hiding from the face of the Emperor <term>Al-Ma'mun</term> <note>the 9th-century Abbasid Caliph</note>, along with Pabzaaz the son of Almohedi, they were visited daily in secret by Albacen son of Habzae—an astrologer and disciple of Rauchi. This astrologer instructed that a very large bronze basin be brought, filled with water, and a small stool placed inside it. He advised the man to sit upon it for the greater part of the day.
He ordered this so that he might cause the Emperor’s astrologers to err regarding his hidden location. They indeed reported that he was "in the middle of the sea." Eventually, a rumor spread that he had escaped by sea, but it was just a trick of the judge; this is what Ptolemy warns us to avoid.

### **C** Aphorism 60. On critical and determinable days of the sick.

**C** The <term>Alhabarim</term> <note>from the Arabic "al-bohran," meaning critical days</note> are surely and certainly the hours in which changes in diseases are declared, quickly turning for better or worse. These are the locations of the Moon in the angles of a square within the celestial circle. The alterations that precede and indicate these changes are the locations of the Moon in the angles of sixteen-sided figures. This applies after the illness has stabilized without outside interference
<margin>\ /</margin>
and when nothing external has happened to disturb the patient, such as food, anger, labor, or the like. If we find "fortune" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> in the aforementioned angles at the hour the sickness began—among both fixed and wandering stars—it signifies a prosperous change. If we find "infortune" <note>malefics like Saturn or Mars</note>, it signifies an adverse change, unless the infortune itself is contrary to the nature of the illness. The Moon in these angles signifies acute diseases. The Sun signifies long-lasting ones. Similarly, every planet signifies according to its own nature.

**C** Ptolemy in this aphorism has taught us the cause of the <term>critical days</term> <note>specific days during an illness when a "crisis" occurs, determining survival or death</note>: what they are, which ones determine good or evil, and the order of their changes. **C** The usefulness of this is greater for physicians than for astrologers. This is because many physicians agree on the determination of illnesses (as we said in another book), noting the changes or the "battle" between the nature of the sick person and the disease. These occur at the 4th, 7th, and 11th days, which add to this cycle. Doctors usually only determine these by hearing or tradition from past experiments. But Ptolemy has uncovered the cause and made clear why it happens. According to Ptolemy, the cause is when Nature is overcome by the disease at its start—that is, when the pain begins and prevents Nature from operating normally. Nature does not fight the disease in that hour when it is conquered, but waits until the Moon is in a place contrary to the disease by aspect, or until the opening of the signs in which it was at the beginning of the disease. Then it rouses Nature to fight the disease. Just as a prudent accuser waits to challenge the accused until his strength is weakened and he is in a place lacking helpers, Nature rouses itself in the 4th sign from where the illness and the Moon began. This is because the 2nd sign from any sign, and the 4th, are contrary to its nature, as is the 7th. These places signify enmity because of the contrariety of signs and aspects, for opposites are cured by opposites. The time between the start of the illness and the Moon's entry into the degree of the square (based on the rising of signs and the projection of rays) is 7 days. This is calculated by adding 180, 90, 45, or 22.5 degrees to the Moon's position at the start of the infirmity. Then it is reduced to equal degrees, and when the Moon is at that degree, it will be in the aforementioned angles of the celestial equator. This is what he means when he says: "By the projection of rays, it is 7 days." In the same way, the time between the Moon at the start of the illness and its opposition is 14 days. Between the start and the fourth left aspect is 21 days. In this way, the cycle of other days proceeds; these points are the angles of the square, and other points indicate the octagon and the sixteen-sided polygon. Other points are indicative of opposites or squares, reaching the point that cuts each arc subtended by a side of the square...

¶ **Aphorism 61.** On the comparison of the Moon to the planets, just as the body is compared to the virtues.

¶ The Moon is proper to the body because of its similarity in operation.

¶ Since the Moon gives its disposition to all planets, and no planet gives its disposition to her, she is likened to the body through which the virtues <note>the powers or faculties of the soul</note> operate; the body does not operate itself through them. For this reason, she is the proper indicator for the body in <term>interrogations</term> <note>horary questions</note> and other matters.

¶ **Aphorism 62.** On the change of the air through the state of the <term>Almuten</term> <note>the planet with the most power in a chart</note> over the lunar angles and the proportion of figures in the revolution of the year and other charts.

¶ When you have set the minute of the **conjunction** <note>when the Sun and Moon meet</note> as the beginning of the **albalurae** <note>a technical term for the calculation of planetary centers</note> of the centers or points, you shall judge the alteration of the air in that month. The judgment will be based on the Almuten over the angles of all those charts, for that planet will conquer the nature of the air, once you have set aside the nature of the current season.

¶ Ptolemy divides the lunar month for us into four variations. The **first quarter** is from the degree of conjunction to the degree of the fourth aspect; and the Almuten over the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>the rising sign</note> of the conjunction will rule that quarter. The **second quarter** is from the degree of the **square aspect** <note>original: "atrabie," from the Arabic "at-tarbi"</note> to the minute of the **opposition** <note>the Full Moon</note>, and its disposition belongs to the Almuten over the Ascendant when the Moon was in the degree of the square aspect. The **third quarter** is from the degree of opposition to the degree of the second square aspect, and its Almuten is over the Ascendant of the opposition. The **fourth and last quarter** is from the second square aspect to the next conjunction, which belongs to the Lord of the Ascendant when the Moon was in the second square. Look, therefore, to the nature of the Lord of the Ascendant and the strongest of the planets, and judge the alterations of the air in that quarter according to the nature of that significator. For this reason, he rightly said to set aside the present season in judging the air. For if the significator indicates rain in a certain week, and it is in a summer month, there will be moisture in the air with a certain light and humid breeze, but without actual rain. Likewise, the nature of the **alboarā** <note>the center points</note> is like the nature of the square angle; when the Moon is in it, a medical crisis occurs, as was said above. This is the highest point in the short circle. The sense of this chapter is that what a **major conjunction** signifies is known when it ought to happen through a 

<column-break/>

**medium conjunction** in this manner: in a major conjunction, a chart is to be made and its Almuten similarly found. Then, the other three charts for the three remaining medium conjunctions occurring within that major conjunction must be made. Then it must be seen which of those three matches the first; and so the event will occur in that medium conjunction. If it does not match any of those three, then it signifies the event will happen in that medium conjunction as a whole, and thus it is known in what part of the world it will happen. It will also be known in which quarter of the medium conjunctions it will happen; thus the medium conjunction divides or distinguishes or apportions the major conjunction. After that, twelve charts for the twelve **minor conjunctions** must be made, which occur within the medium conjunction in which the event signified by the major was indicated. Whichever of these matches the chart of the medium conjunction, you may say that the event signified in the medium will happen in that minor conjunction; thus the minor divides the medium. Then, twenty charts for twenty years should be made, which fall within the minor conjunction. Whichever of those twenty matches, the event signified by the medium conjunction will occur in that year; thus the **revolutions of the years** determine what was broadly signified by the medium conjunction. Similarly, the four charts of the **four quarters of the year** determine in which part of the year the event signified in the annual forecast will occur; for in whichever quarter matches the annual chart, the event will happen in that part of the year. Similarly, the three conjunctions of the Sun and Moon that occur in each quarter—if it is a conjunctional quarter—or the three **preventions** <note>original: "prouentiones," the Full Moon or opposition</note> if it is a preventional quarter, show specifically in which part of that quarter the event signified by the quarterly chart will happen. For whichever of those matches the quarterly chart, the event will occur in that conjunction. Similarly, when the event signified by a conjunction ought to happen is known by the four charts made when the Moon reaches the four angles of the conjunction's chart, as was said in the third aphorism before this one. Thus, when any chart is brought to you, you ought to compare it to the chart of the conjunction or prevention, and the chart of the annual revolution, and the chart of the minor conjunction, and the chart of the medium conjunction, and the chart of the major conjunction. This is more effective because if the minor chart does not match the major one closest to it, the event will not be as strong.

# Ptolemy

¶ He intends to explain the whole through division: because the greater indicates the whole, and it is not enough for us unless they are explained. Therefore, the **revolutions of the years** <note>The annual return of the Sun to its position at birth</note> are made to explain the generalities that are in the birth chart. And there is a greater utility in this: because the <term>minor hyleg</term> <note>original: "alchibē minoz"; the planet acting as the giver of life</note> profits where it reaches the <term>minor profection</term> <note>original: "alynthie"; a method where the chart is advanced by one sign per year</note> which is the profection of the middle hyleg. And what the middle profection promises where it reaches the greater profection; therefore, if one proceeds in this way, one will not avoid what is not in the revolution, of which there is no explanation. In the minor conjunction, there is the distinction of the middle conjunction; and in the middle, the distinction of the major conjunction. When, therefore, you speak in the distinction, verify its whole: and do not make your speech a revolution, since it is of a weaker explanation.

¶ **Added Explanation.** He intends by "division" the explanation of the aforesaid. Since the major announces the totals, which are not excused unless they are explained. And according to this, the revolution of the year falls, distinguishing the sums that are in the birth. And the greatest help in this is, for example, that what the minor conjunction promises is not useful except as far as what it reaches from the middle conjunction. And similarly, what the middle conjunction promises is not useful except as far as what comes from the major conjunction. For when the term runs this course, it is preserved from being a relative for which there is no explanation, nor in which there is a declaration.

¶ **Aphorism 65.** On the consideration for grasping a true judgment in any question.

¶ After the strength of the significator of the inquiry has been fixed or made manifest, look at its strength in the **ascendant** <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the revolution of that same year. And in the ascendant of the <term>minor hyleg</term> <note>original: "alchibē minoz"</note>. And in the sign to which the <term>profection</term> <note>original: "alyntbie"</note> reaches in that year: and according to its strength in all these, or its weakness, proceed with the judgment of the signs.

¶ When subtle astrologers knew the strength of a planet in an inquiry from its strength over the ascendant and the reception of its disposition from favorable places in the inquiry, it was not enough for them until they looked at the state of that same planet in those things which Ptolemy mentioned in some part: and if they found it in any, it was placed before all other planets. And there was he who spoke according to it, secure that his judgment would be true and certain. If, however, it was void of significance from these, the astrologers diminished its significance according to the amount it lacked these parts, and they placed the masters of those places as participants or sharers with it. And I saw Lalita <note>Likely a Latinization of an Arabic name like Al-Khayyat</note> son of Al-Walid who, in every inquiry, would not set any significator other than the master of the **conjunction or prevention** <note>the New or Full Moon immediately preceding the event</note> in which it was, if he had lordship or dignity in the ascendant: and he made him a participant with the master of that inquiry: and if he found that lord of the conjunction or prevention in an **angle** <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the most powerful positions</note>, no one else would participate with him. And he was very truthful in giving judgments.

¶ **Aphorism 66.** On the nature of the significance of death, health, or other accidents, namely by the <term>divider</term> <note>original: "algebutar"; a planet that "distributes" a period of life</note>, profection, and division.

¶ Do not cut short <note>i.e., predict death</note> by direction alone, unless the donations of the significators are complete: and they signify the direction to be true through that which the <term>profection</term> <note>original: "alyntbie"</note> of the birth has reached.

¶ He intends that when we have calculated the degree of the ascendant of the birth for each year, and it reaches a bad place, we ought not by that alone to signify the death of the native without the **direction** <note>a timing technique</note> of the <term>hyleg</term> <note>life-giver</note> and <term>alcochoden</term> <note>life-length giver</note>. And if it reaches that which both directions reach for the perfect "gifts of years," there will be no doubt in his death. If, however, you do not cut it short: by that <term>profection</term> <note>original: "alyntbie"</note> it can be understood for the profection and also for the division, namely by the <term>divider</term> <note>original: "agelbutar"</note>. And thus when the profection or the <term>divider</term> <note>original: "agelbutar"</note> agree in good or evil with the direction of the degree of the ascendant, then that which they reached will happen to the native: since these three signify the state of health in the illnesses of the native: and this is what he says.

<column-break/>

¶ **Aphorism 67.** On the inquiry into the origin of any native before judgment to avoid error.

¶ Remove in every judgment that which the native cannot receive according to the form of the agent, namely, the star.

¶ He intends that when we see prosperity in births or inquiries, we should look to the receiver of it, who is the native or the master of the inquiry, and we should not judge the perfection of the significance for him until we know his **origin** <note>social status, gender, or species</note>: and there will be a division between him and another: namely between a native and a native who will be more suitable to receive that proximity by lineage and nobility as in the 1st and 7th aphorism of this book: and I have already repeated this in another explanation of the words of this book by itself which suffices.

¶ **Aphorism 68.** On the impediment of the functional limbs and other illnesses.

¶ When an **infortune** <note>a malefic planet like Saturn or Mars</note> is **oriental** <note>rising before the Sun</note>, it will signify an impediment. And when it is **occidental** <note>setting after the Sun</note>, it signifies illnesses.

¶ He places a difference between an **impediment** and **illnesses**: because impediments are permanent defects of the limbs of which we do not trust that they can return to their proper action, such as blindness, deafness, and lameness. Illnesses are said to be when the limbs depart from their temperament and the proper office of the natural thing, and we do not despair that they may return to that in which they were. And he said that when an infortune hinders some limb and is oriental, its effect will be less because it is oriental.

¶ **Aphorism 69.** On the loss of the eyes.

¶ When the Moon is in opposition to the Sun mixed with **nebulous stars** <note>cloudy clusters like Praesepe or the Pleiades</note> or joined to them, it signifies inseparable diseases in the eyes. And similarly if the Moon is occidental and in an angle: and both infortunes, namely Saturn and Mars, are rising before the Sun, and those—that is, the Sun and Moon—are opposed, the native will lose both eyes.

¶ The greatest impediment in the two luminaries is when two infortunes are rising, one before the Sun and after the Moon, and one is in opposition to the other, namely the Sun in opposition to the other and vice versa. ### Aphorism 71. On the masculine or feminine character of those born.

In the births of men, when the two luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon</note> are in a masculine sign, their actions will be natural to their sex. In women, however, they will be immoderate and unnatural in their being. In the same way, Mars and Venus affect sexual intercourse as we have said: when these two stars are oriental <note>original: "orientales"; rising before the Sun</note>, they aid in masculinity. When they are occidental <note>original: "occidentales"; setting after the Sun</note>, they aid in femininity. Saturn adds impurity. Mercury aids the impulse of pleasures. And in this way, they contribute to their opposites—namely, those things I have just mentioned.

When the luminaries in a man’s birth are in two masculine signs and in two masculine quarters, or in the same masculine quarter, the man will perform all things pertaining to men. When the places of the luminaries are feminine in a man's birth, his nature will be effeminated, his desire will be feminine, and he will not be able to restrain or hold back his tears. When the places of the luminaries are masculine in the births of women, their actions will appear similar to men, and they will not be subject to men. When Mars and Venus are in masculine signs, they signify that the manner of intercourse for every birth is according to nature. If they are oriental, they signify what is noted in women who, on account of much masculinity, may even have intercourse with boys. If they are in feminine signs and Saturn aspects them while they are hidden, the intercourse will be unnatural. Perhaps this will continue until the native asks that others perform it with him, for then he will be effeminated, and this is because of Saturn. If the native is a woman and the place of Mars and Venus is masculine and they are oriental, she will flee men and intercourse with men will be hateful to her, and she will choose to rub against girls <note>original: "fricare puellas"; a medieval reference to lesbianism</note>. If the place of Mars and Venus is feminine and they are occidental, she will love intercourse with men, and her manner will be natural. If Jupiter is in the place of Mars, the intercourse of the man and woman will be according to the laws. If Mars alone presides without aspecting Jupiter, their many sexual acts will not be according to the precepts of the law.

### Aphorism 72. On the roots of opinions in judgments.

The rearing <note>original: "nutritio"</note> of a child is proven by the lords of the triplicity <note>A group of three zodiac signs belonging to the same element</note> of the Ascendant. From the lords of the triplicity of the lord of the *anauba* <note>original: "neuba"; a term related to the Hyleg or life-giving planet</note>—namely, the luminary of the time—we know the sustenance of the native or his way of life.

Ptolemy tells us in this book of rules the "roots" of opinions in the judgments of astronomy. He recites the "branches" in the fourth book of the *Tetrabiblos* <note>original: "alabza"; likely a corruption of the Arabic title for Ptolemy's work</note>. The first intention of those observing the rearing of a child is to look at the lord of the triplicity of the birth’s Ascendant, so they may know its strength by its presence in one of the angles, ensuring it is free from malefic parts. He adds in the second place the strength of the benefics in the Ascendant, and many other things which astrologers count regarding rearing. There are four years of rearing, and there are three lords of the triplicity. Therefore, each one governs one year and one-third part of a year. Ptolemy also mentioned that if these are not present, we can achieve nothing else with other factors; for if these things Ptolemy posits are lacking at birth, no other thing can be of use, even if they seem helpful. Therefore, I understand this in everything he says in this correct book. For this reason, all that he says in this book are called "roots," and those things he says in the *Tetrabiblos* and what others have said in their books are called "branches." Thus, if these roots are missing, those branches do not help in rearing, even if other things are added in time and prosperity comes in rearing, which is seen in the book of births through the lords of the triplicity of the Ascendant. Similarly regarding sustenance: if the lord of the *anauba* is in the birth—that is, the Sun by day and the Moon by night—if it is in the angles or in places where they can be the *hyleg* <note>original: "albyleg"; the planet that grants life</note>. Also, the degree of the Ascendant in conjunction, and the Part of Fortune in prevention.

<column-break/>

Whichever of them is the *anauba* <note>original: "neuba"</note>—namely the Sun by day or the Moon by night—another is the degree of the Ascendant in conjunction and the degree of the Part of Fortune in prevention. Even if the Sun and Moon are not the *hyleg*, since each of these is called *anauba*, one must work from the lords of the triplicity of one of them. If the first lord of its triplicity is safe, it will signify good sustenance in the first third of life. The second signifies what will be after that until the second third of life. The third signifies what remains of life. There are also some who attribute the goodness of sustenance to other sources: from the goodness of the second house and its lord, or from the Part of Fortune and its lord. But he introduced what was strongest in goodness above all others.

### Aphorism 73. On the quality of the native's death.

When Mars is bodily joined to the head of Algol <note>original: "capiti algol"; the star Beta Persei, historically associated with misfortune and decapitation</note>—namely, the star that is in Taurus—and no fortune aspects the cutting degree <note>original: "gradum abscindentem"; the degree indicating the end of life</note>, nor is it in the fourth house, and the lord of the life-giving luminary <note>original: "anauba luminariū"</note> is opposite Mars or in its fourth aspect, the native's head will be cut off. Because if the luminary is in the middle of heaven, he will be hanged. If malefic planets aspect each other from Gemini and Pisces, his hands and feet will be cut off.

Ptolemy has already recited to us that when Mars is bodily joined to the head of Algol in a man's birth, he will lose his head. But he added something by which his wisdom is greatly perceived. For he said that a "good death" is signified if a benefic aspects the cutting degree—that is, the western horizon—and if a benefic is in the 8th house. For according to astrologers, this removes an evil death. If this is the case, the native will die of a hot disease in the head while in his bed. I myself heard from a certain man named Seualet—son of Accele, son of the fortune-teller called Ebzoamal, who preceded the son of Aali—who was very courageous at sea and in sailing. When he wanted to enter Tabriz <note>original: "tybriz"</note>, which was very tumultuous with winds stirring the waves, and someone rebuked him, he said: "I do not fear death at sea for myself. For Jupiter was in my birth in the house of death and oriental, which prohibits death for me by the command of Almighty God." And he said he saw him die in his bed. It also happened that a certain servant showed me the birth chart of his master's son; I found the Sun in the middle of heaven, and he was the lord of the life-giver <note>original: "anauba albyleg"</note>—that is, the Sun was the *hyleg*—and Mars was in the fourth aspect to it. Saturn was also in the angle of the earth <note>the 4th house</note>, and his Ascendant was Pisces. Therefore, I deferred judgment, saying: "It is necessary to wait until the days of rearing are complete." The boy grew, and as he was very diligent in investigating his own affairs, I heard nothing that would make me fear the cutting off of hands and feet and hanging <note>original: "infurcationē"</note>, since he was modest and mild. But when he reached his 30th year, certain fugitives entered his house, because they were accused of something he supposedly did while in Egypt. They were caught in that house, and he, along with them, lost his hands and feet and was hanged; and I saw him without hands and feet and hanged. I brought all this forward to confirm the words of Ptolemy.

Mars is the principal cause of wounds and scars. The whole head belongs to the Ascendant, of which the face is a part; therefore, do not be surprised if there is a mark on the face.

### Aphorism 76. On the indication of various dangers and the manner of death for the native.

When **Saturn** is in the Midheaven <note>The highest point in the sky at the moment of birth, representing public life and career.</note>, and the planet which is the giver of life <note>original: "ananba"; likely a corruption of the term for the Hyleg, the planet that determines the lifespan.</note> for the Sun or Moon is in opposition to it, and if the fourth sign <note>The 4th House, which in astrology represents the "end of matters" and the grave.</note> is a dry sign, the native will die from a fall or from heavy things falling upon him. And if it is a humid sign, he will be drowned. But if the fourth sign has a human form <note>Zodiac signs depicted as humans, such as Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius.</note>, he will be strangled or die from being beaten with clubs, unless a planet of Fortune is in the eighth house <note>The house of death; a "fortune" here acts as a protector.</note>; for then the things we mentioned will happen, but he will not die from them.

This is due to the influences of **Saturn** when it is above the earth—namely, in the Midheaven—and when that planet which is the giver of life is beneath it, and the fourth sign is dry. And if it is humid, he will be submerged, and so on. But Ptolemy removes some of the danger in this useful point: he says that it might destroy an evil death, and this happens when a planet of Fortune is in the eighth house. The accidents we mentioned will indeed happen, but the person will not die.

### Aphorism 77. On the state of the body and the alteration of its makeup; on agility, cheerfulness, and loss.

Direct the degree of the Ascendant <note>A technique of "directing" or moving points in the chart forward in time to predict when events will manifest.</note> for accidents of the body; direct the degree of the Part of Fortune for its possessions; direct the degree of the **Moon** for the state of the body together with the soul; and the degree of the **Sun** for the power of its princes; and finally, direct the degree of the Midheaven for those matters in which one works—counting one year for every single degree.

Although this aphorism seems plain, it leaves us in doubt regarding the degree of the Ascendant and the degree of the Moon. Through the degree of the Ascendant, we know about the alteration of the state of the body and its composition, namely what will be renewed upon it regarding illness and health. And we will direct the degree of the Moon toward that which will pertain to the body regarding cheerfulness and agility, and how it obeys the soul. The direction of the Part of Fortune pertains to what is acquired or lost. And we will direct the degree of the Sun for the power or dignity which one will have from his prince or king, for better or worse; for if the degree of the Sun or its rays meets a planet of Fortune, his honor toward his lord will increase. But if it meets a malefic planet or its rays, his honor will be diminished. The direction of the degree of the Midheaven is not done in the same way, for the direction of the Sun is for you and all those who are joined to you, while the direction of the Midheaven is for you and all those whom you rule. The direction is as we said: when it is in the Midheaven, you direct by the ascensions of the direct circle; when it is in the Ascendant, by the ascensions of your own region. If it is in neither of these, you use both types of ascensions. Direct the degree of the Midheaven for the work one performs, and the degree of the Sun for the dignity one has from his king; these things are in the last chapter of the *Book of Al-Abram* <note>Likely referring to a work by the Jewish scholar Abraham Ibn Ezra.</note>.

### Aphorism 78. On the significance of a planet when it reaches the place where it promised something at birth.

A planet is assigned to a place where it promised nothing, nor to a place where the birth [direction] has not reached.

Unlearned astrologers used to suspect that a malefic planet, when in the Ascendant or the Midheaven or any other place in the birth chart or figure, always causes evil, and a benefic always causes good. But it must be observed in the birth, the revolution <note>A chart for the person's birthday each year.</note>, and the interrogation <note>A chart cast to answer a specific question.</note>: if a planet promised good or evil at the beginning of that birth, or the year's revolution, or the interrogation, it will fulfill it when it joins with it or aspects it. But if it reaches a place where it had no aspect at the beginning, its influence will not appear there. Whenever a planet reaches any degree through direction, it will act according to its nature, whether it be good or evil. Likewise, planets in the birth, question, and revolution promise something in the places where they were at the beginning or which they aspected. But in places where they were not, or in places they did not aspect at the start

<column-break/>

of the birth, revolution, or interrogation, they promise nothing. Therefore, when a planet is bodily in these places—namely, those it did not behold at the start—and when it is not in the places where its direction or the direction of the Ascendant of the birth reaches, it performs nothing.

### Aphorism 79. On the significance of the birth of one who will destroy the king’s wealth.

When **Mars** is in the eleventh house and its significance is strong in the Ascendant, the master of the birth <note>The person whose chart it is.</note> will be unfaithful to his prince or king.

The eleventh house is the second house from the royal house <note>The 10th house represents the King; the house following it, the 11th, represents the King's money and resources.</note>. It is the house of his substance. When Mars is in that house, it signifies that the person in charge of that substance will be of the nature of Mars. If Mars also has some testimony in the Ascendant, it signifies that the native himself will be the cause of that loss.

### Aphorism 80. On the significance of the foulness of the native’s sexual intercourse.

When **Venus** is bodily joined with **Saturn** in the birth, and they have dignity in the seventh house, the native will engage in unclean intercourse. And this applies in other houses and in the conjunctions of every planet with either of the two malefics <note>Saturn or Mars.</note>.

Venus is the primary cause of sexual intercourse, and especially when she is in the seventh house, which is the house of marriage. Therefore, when she is bodily joined to Saturn, she will incite the native to prefer sodomy <note>original: "stuprum posteriorem anteriori"; literally "the back over the front."</note> and self-stimulation. But if Saturn is oriental <note>Rising before the Sun.</note>, he will love friction with boys and will prefer dark-skinned people over those who are fair or blonde. If there is a misfortune from the incorporation of Mars, it signifies that the native is not jealous; he will sleep with many boys, and also with another man and his own wife at the same time. It will happen that he commits fornication with his own children, and he will act against them and against the law, and other things pertaining to uncleanness, and he will be a transgressor of the law.

### Aphorism 81. On the significance of the end of the timing of things.

Death <note>or "The End"</note> is determined from seven parts or seven ways. First, the distance between both significators <note>Planets representing the person or the question.</note>. Second, the relationship between them—namely, by their aspect and similarity in the figure. Third, when one of them reaches the place of the other. Fourth, the distance between one of them and the place where the nature of the thing sought resides (for example, if the question is about a wife, look at the 7th house). Fifth, what results from the "gift" of the planet after adding or subtracting years. Sixth, the change of the significator's figure through direction, orientality, and similar factors. Seventh, when the planet reaches a place that accords with its own nature.

By "times," he means the timing of intentions, questions, and undertakings. For the first way is to take the distance between both significators in degrees. Turn these into days and parts of time. Second, see if the Lord of the Ascendant <note>The planet ruling the rising sign.</note> goes toward a conjunction with the Lord of the thing sought; its perfection will occur when the conjunction is complete. Third, find when the Lord of the Ascendant reaches the place of the object, or the Lord of the object reaches the degree of the Ascendant. These will be days or other parts of time. Fourth, the distance between one of them and the place of the interrogation through its motion... and not just by the number of degrees. See how many days it takes for the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the house of the object to travel to that house. Fifth, look at what the Lord of the interrogation is able to receive from the "gift" of time, just as one looks at the "Alcobodeu" <note>A corruption of "Alcocoden," the planet that determines the number of years a person will live.</note> in a birth chart to see how many years it gives, and then see what the benefics or malefics add or subtract. Look at what remains after the addition or subtraction of the planets.
