**Aphorism 82. In which indications one should not judge.**

When the significators are equal in a matter and in its contrary—namely, that there are as many strong significators who deny as those who grant, and they are equally strong—look to the Ascendant of the **conjunction** or **prevention** <note>The New Moon or Full Moon immediately preceding the question.</note>. If they are equal there as well, do not be in a hurry to give a judgment.

Astrologers, when looking into any inquiry, always judged by the first thing that occurred to them; therefore they fell into error quite often. Truly, in this art, the experts discuss the strengths of the significators, the concord of the inquiry, and the discord. Afterward, they judge by the stronger one. To make this clear, I will provide an example. Someone asked us about a journey he wished to make; we found the significators of the inquirer and the significators of the journey between the fourth and seventh houses, and they indicated a delay or a staying still. We also found the significator of the inquirer going to a conjunction with the significator of the journey; from this, we indicated a journey. For **Saturn** was in the 3rd house from the Ascendant, and this indicated a staying still. It was necessary, therefore, before we spoke, to discuss all the significators of the staying and the journey: for if they were equal, we would not judge; but if one were stronger than the other, we would judge by that one. Hence Ptolemy says: when the significators are equal, observe the significators of the conjunction or prevention that was born in its Ascendant; and do with that as you do with the lord of the inquiry. If you find the condition and mode to be in agreement, we will not judge the same, but we will defer until the inquiry is repeated.

**Aphorism 83. On the indication of those things that happen through the hour of acquisition, and those that happen through the hour of enthronement (that is, through the Ascendant).**

The hour of the **acquisition of dignity** <note>The moment someone is granted a title or office.</note> is for that which will be between him and his prince. But the hour of his **enthronement** <note>original: "itronizationis"; the moment he actually takes his seat of power or begins the job.</note> is the manner of his conduct in his work.

Astrologers have agreed that the hour of acquisition is for the one who acquires it and for the one who is over him. And the hour of his enthronement is for the one who has acquired it and those who are under him. And this is the difference because of the distance of the place in which the one who acquires it and the one who gives it reside. The matter in this is so clear that it needs no explanation. The hour of enthronement is that when someone is placed in dignity or office. When someone gives honor to another, through the Ascendant of that hour we see what is between the giver and the receiver—that is, whether he gives it to him in a good hour. But for the hour in which he is enthroned, the Ascendant indicates what happens to him in that dignity.

**Aphorism 84. Concerning that which happens regarding the matters of one enthroned in office or dignity.**

When the lord of the Ascendant of the enthronement of any office or dignity is **Mars**, and he is in the second house or joined with the lord of the second house,

<column-break/>

he destroys the substance of those whom he rules, especially if the lord of the second house is **Jupiter**.

The second house from the Ascendant at the hour of the acquisition of dignity is the house of the substance <note>Wealth or resources.</note> of those whom he rules. Whenever Mars is in it, and he is the lord of the Ascendant, it signifies that he will seize their substance and their state will be bad with him. Whenever Jupiter rules the second house, the work of Mars in it will be greater than if Saturn ruled it. For in other cases, when Saturn rules a place, he guards that place and expels from it and resists the hinderer. Jupiter, however, draws back from quarrels and gives liberally to the one who asks of him, nor does he endure wickedness to guard his own things. And therefore, in this place, the "malefics" <note>Planets like Mars or Saturn, usually associated with hardship but here seen as more protective of resources.</note> are more useful.

**Aphorism 85. On the substance of the enthroned or the prelate in the quality of his expenses or acquisition.**

When the lord of the Ascendant commits <note>A technical term for the transfer of planetary influence.</note> or pushes his disposition to the lord of the second house from a **laudable state** <note>A favorable planetary position or aspect.</note>, the steward or prefect will consume or spend much. But if it is from an **unlaudable state**, he will lose it. Whenever the lord of the second house commits to the lord of the Ascendant by disposition, he will profit. If it is from a laudable state, it will be from the proper will of the people. If indeed from an unlaudable state, it will be against the will of the people and with their anger.

Ptolemy places the Ascendant and the 2nd house in the aforementioned word for the people and their substance. And in this, he teaches us their indication—namely, of the Ascendant and the second house regarding the perfection <note>The completion or success of a matter.</note> and its substance. Hence he leads into error those to whom the science of the stars is hidden: the Ascendant of the enthronement of a prefect signifies the prefect himself. The second house truly signifies the people and their substance, and all that the prince rules. And there is no doubt: if Mars is the lord of the Ascendant when the dignities are not in misfortune, he dissipates and hinders whatever is in the second house regarding the things of others, and he will save what belongs to the Ascendant, which he rules; and in this way, the error contained in the previous word is resolved. What he says in this aphorism is well known: that the commission of the disposition of the lord of the Ascendant to the lord of the second from a laudable state—that is, if it goes to its conjunction from a **sextile** or **trine** aspect <note>Favorable 60-degree or 120-degree angles.</note>—signifies that the prefect will spend much by his own will. But if the conjunction is from an unlaudable state—that is, from a **square** aspect or **opposition** <note>Difficult 90-degree or 180-degree angles.</note>—it will signify loss, not by his own will. And whenever the lord of the second house goes to a conjunction with the lord of the Ascendant from a sextile or trine aspect, he will profit by the good spirit of those from whom he received it. But if the lord of the second is joined with the lord of the Ascendant from a square or opposition, he will profit by seizure against the will of the givers, because it is by force.

**Aphorism 86. On the four planets through which growth and destruction occur, and the three through which the character of individuals is held.**

The **Sun** <note>original: "☉"</note> is the origin of the vital virtue, which is of the heart. The **Moon** <note>original: "☾"</note> is the origin of the natural virtue of the liver. **Saturn** <note>original: "♄"</note> is the origin of the receptive virtue. **Jupiter** <note>original: "♃"</note> is the virtue of growth and vegetation. **Mercury** <note>original: "☿"</note> is the virtue of the phantastic imagination and thought. **Mars** <note>original: "♂"</note> is the irascible and attractive virtue. **Venus** <note>original: "♀"</note> is the concupiscible <note>Related to strong desire or lust.</note> and appetitive virtue. Therefore, Mercury, Mars, and Venus in a nativity signify the character of the native and their skills.

Philosophers have agreed in this: that individuals who undergo effect and destruction are branches of these roots, either according to the quantity of their operation in strength and weakness or in operation—as individuals are branches of earth, water, fire, and also air. And the growth and detriment of these individuals occur from their virtues according to their mixture in strength. Indeed, all character traits that exist—generosity, greed, truth, lying, fidelity, and infidelity, and similar things—arise from the mixture of the characters of these three. ...of Mars, of Venus, and of Mercury. And similarly the masteries <note>The "magisteria" or professional skills governed by specific planets.</note>. And we have already commemorated all of this sufficiently in another book outside of this one. The intention of this chapter is: that through the four planets—namely the **Sun**, the **Moon**, **Saturn**, and **Jupiter**—the increase and destruction of every individual living being occurs. <margin>Word 87. On the division of months and the revolution of the year up to the ascendant.</margin>
The time of the change of signs in the revolution, regarding the **profection** <note>original: "signi pfectionis"; a technique where the chart is "advanced" by one sign per year or month.</note> of the sign, is 28 days and 2 hours, and nearly 18 minutes of one hour. From the perspective of the ascendant of the hemisphere—that is, in the East—it is 28 days and nearly a fifth of a day. The solar month is the change of the Sun from the degree in which the birth occurred into a similar degree in another sign.
He wishes to show us how many days this is. It should be noted that the signs are measured from the profectional ascendant and from the observed ascendant of the revolution. And these are the points of the degrees of the Sun in other solar months near the truth. The sign in which the solar year began—which we revolve into the ascendant—will be the second from the one in which the previous year began. And as we direct from the beginning of a sign to its end, 13 signs will be completed in the solar year in which the native will change, and his state will be signified. Therefore, when we divide 365 days and a quarter of a day by 13 signs, the result is 28 days and 2 hours, and nearly 18 minutes of an hour. This is the time in which the profection moves in each sign until it moves from that one to the sign that succeeds it; and this is called the **Profectional Month**. That which is from the perspective of the ascendant is the "bota" <note>likely a corruption of a term for the "attainment" or "measure"</note> of its revolution. Since the year, which consists of nearly 365 days and a quarter, when distributed through 13 signs and nearly a tenth of one sign—from the minute of the observed ascendant in the revolution up to the ascendant in which the following year begins—each sign will receive 28 days and nearly a fifth of a day. The times of the solar month are various. They are from the entry of the Sun into the minute in which the hour of birth occurred until it reaches the same minute in the second sign from it. We have already made clear the specific property of each of these parts in our books of judgments.

<margin>Word 88. On the direction of the Part of Fortune in the revolution of years.</margin>
When we wish to determine the **Part of Fortune** <note>A calculated point in the chart representing prosperity and health.</note> in any of the years of revolution: we take the distance from the place of the Sun to the place of the Moon in the nativity, and we project it from the degree of the ascendant of the year of the revolution.
Ptolemy has gathered the knowledge of this word in such a way that it is not necessary for us to add anything to his statement. **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrological poet.</note> also commemorated this and called it the "Part of the Moon." For this, some criticized him, being ignorant of his intention. But this is how to direct the Part of Fortune in the year of revolution to the fortunes and misfortunes, as well as to their rays <note>Aspects or geometric angles.</note>.

<margin>Word 89. On finding the house of uncles and the house of sons and brothers.</margin>
The uncle's house is the 7th, and the paternal uncle is from the 7th, and in this manner for the others.
He intends that since the 4th house is the house of the father, the 7th house is the house of grandfathers <note>The 4th house from the 4th house.</note>. While the 3rd is the house of brothers, the 3rd house from the house of brothers (which is the 6th house) will be the house of uncles <note>Specifically the father's brothers.</note>; and similarly, the 7th will signify the sons of brothers, because it is the 5th house from the house of brothers.

<margin>Word 90. On knowing the substance of a hidden thing.</margin>
When the **significator** <note>The planet representing the object of the query.</note> aspects the ascendant, the kind of hidden thing will be from the substance of the ascendant. But if it does not aspect the ascendant, the kind will be from the substance of the place of the significator; and the **Lord of the Hour** will signify the color of the thing. The place of the Moon will signify its time;

<column-break/>

that is, if she is above the earth, it will be new; if she is beneath the earth, it will be old. From the Lord of the Part of Fortune, its length or shortness will be signified to you. From the Lord of the **Term** <note>original: "termini"; a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign.</note> of the degree of the 4th house, and from the Lord of the Term of the degree of the Midheaven—specifically from whichever of them is in an **Angle** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, the strongest points in a chart.</note>—and from the Lord of the Term of the Moon, the nature of the thing is known.

The significator that Ptolemy intends is not the Moon, nor the one that presides over the ascendant at that time. Rather, it is the planet in which the strengths of the dignities in the ascendant and in the places of the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> are joined, and which is **Void of Course** <note>original: "vacuus cursu"; making no further aspects before leaving its current sign.</note>—that is, joined to no one—and has not mixed its disposition with another. But if by chance the one presiding over the ascendant (and the other places I have enumerated) is joined to another, then look to that one, and then again to another. The one to whom the final conjunction reaches, if it is not joined to any other, will be the significator. After he has found it, the strength of its place and its own internal strength provide the signification. Also, as for the kind of substance: if the ascendant is **Earthy**, the hidden thing will be of the earth or growing from the earth. It will be **Aquatic** or from the sea if it is an aquatic sign; and it will be something made by fire if it is **Fiery**. The same applies to the place of the significator. The "Lord of the Hour": by "hour," he means the times—12 in the day and as many in the night—on the day of the year. Ptolemy also saw that when the Moon is above the earth, the object is new, and when below the earth, it is old. Others have suspected that when the significator is **Oriental** (rising before the Sun), it is new, and when it is **Occidental** (setting after the Sun), it is old; and in this way, the planet that is between these places, which is not joined to another but another is joined to it, will be the significator. Regarding the signification of long and short: speak of this according to what someone has taken. For example, if someone took something whose parts are short and closed it in their hand from among living things, such as a piece of a hazelnut shell, one of which is long and the other short. Where Ptolemy spoke of the Terms, he spoke of his own <note>The "Ptolemaic Terms," a specific system of planetary bounds.</note> and not of others. And its nature is what its action signifies, such as whether it is a "passion" <note>In the sense of a physical property or state.</note> when it is dry or moist.

<margin>Word 91. Regarding the worse signification for a sick person.</margin>
The most detestable thing in the signification of a sick person is for the significator of the question to be entering **Under the Rays** <note>original: "sub radios"; becoming "combust" or hidden by the Sun's light, indicating weakness or death.</note>, or for the Part of Fortune to be unfortunate.

When those things we mentioned in the preceding chapter are fulfilled in the significator, it belongs to the sick person. That is, that it be the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the places of the luminaries, and alone—meaning Void of Course, as was said in the preceding chapter. And when it wishes to be **combust**, it changes toward the loss of work or action, and toward destruction. As for the Part of Fortune, when it is unfortunate, it destroys life; and no one's life is destroyed nor do they lose their actions unless they are being prepared for death.

<margin>Word 92. On the lessening of the impediment of the malefics in their Hayz.</margin>
Saturn when Oriental harms the sick less; Mars when Occidental harms the sick less. And in this manner, there will be an increase in the prosperity of Jupiter and Venus in the North and the South.

He intends that the impediments of the **Malefics** <note>Saturn and Mars.</note> are lessened when they are in their **Hayz** <note>original: "baiz"; a state of planetary dignity.</note>. The East belongs to Saturn; the West to Mars; Venus has the South; Jupiter has the North. When we find a planet in its Hayz—in those parts, in the ascendant of the sick person, or in another place over which it presides—the evil of its impediment will be lessened, and it will increase the fortune and prosperity of its being. ### Word 93. That we should observe the first conjunction of kings, and then the following conjunctions, and compare them together so that we do not err in judgment.

Do not presume to equate the charts before knowing the similarity of the things placed; for kingdoms—that is, the significations of kingdoms—change or vary in every conjunction. And when you have made certain of the orders, you shall give to the king and to those whom he rules what is due to them in each and every time; and you shall be safe from error.

This means that when present-day astrologers were in a comparison regarding the being of kings and the Sun, they only considered the state of the wealthy and noble. Through **Jupiter** however, and through other wandering stars <note>term: "wandering stars" <gloss>planets</gloss></note> in a comparison of evils, they signified the alteration of kings according to the alteration of the charts or the fortunes of those planets. They also set forth the change of a matter—namely, what happens through one planet after another—and they allowed them to operate according to their own nature. An example of this: because a kingdom has changed to **Mars**, the state of the kingdom will thus be altered in his time according to his own alteration; and the work of the **Sun** is changed or diminished, as is whatever else was marked by others in the state of kings besides Mars. Thus **Ptolemy** urged us to observe the kingdoms; that is, that we ought to observe the first conjunction <note>likely referring to the Great Conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn, which medieval astrologers used to predict the rise and fall of dynasties.</note> which signified the kingdom, then every subsequent conjunction, and compare or equate them together: and thus we will not err. And also those things through which he rose—that is, the planets through which the kingdom rose—as well as those over whom the king rules, and those who "elected" him—namely, the citizens—so that we may be diligent in observing the movements of those citizens, and in the opposition of each thing—namely, of a star in its place in the chart of the conjunction. For the astrologer who neglects this will err in judgment, because he does not proceed along the proper path. And it is not what the physicists call the "being of kings" <note>original: "esse regum"</note> or their forms. In the comparison of the state of kings, they judge the king's state through the Sun alone, and the state of the wealthy through Jupiter and other stars. And according to how the Sun and other stars change in different signs and places, so they judged. And in this there was error; because they neglected the change of the king and kingdom which happens in every conjunction. For kings change according to the nature of the **tenth sign** <note>The Midheaven or 10th House, governing sovereignty and career.</note> and its lord, and the state of the wealthy changes in every conjunction.

### Word 94. On the place that signifies what is in the mind of the one asking.

The strongest location of the **significator** <note>The planet representing the person asking the question.</note> in an inquiry will signify what is in the mind of the questioner.

The significator of the questioner is the one we spoke of in Word 90; and the place in which he is regarding the inquiry is that which is in his mind. For example, if he is in the house of the king, he asks about the kingdom. If however he is in the house of journeys, he asks about a journey; and so on for the other houses.

### Word 95. On the significations of the figures or fortunes in the faces of the signs they inhabit.

Forms always happen so that the degree which rises is similar to that which the native desires. And similarly, that which rises in every **face** <note>term: "face" <gloss>A ten-degree division of a zodiac sign, also called a decan.</gloss></note> of these figures or forms is similar to his work in another. And we have already explained this in another place: namely, in Word 40.

The figures or forms that rise with the faces are written in the **Book of Dargene** <note>possibly a reference to a work on talismans or fixed stars.</note>. The Indians commend these and prefer them over other judgments. I myself have seen certain people who judged by them in matters that happen to a native. I also knew a certain man whose birth-ascendant was the first face of **Aries**. And his current significators were in the **terms** <note>term: "terms" <gloss>subdivisions of a sign where a specific planet has dignity.</gloss></note> of **Saturn**. His clothing was splendid, clean, and well-scented, and he lived magnificently. It happened one day while I was sitting with him—for he was an acquaintance of mine—that I said to him: "These garments are indeed contrary to your significators" <note>Saturn usually signifies dirty, dark, or old things; the man's clean clothes contradicted his Saturnian influence.</note>. And I said and responded to him: "It is no disgrace to do what nature requires; but it is the greatest disgrace when bad habit

### Word 96. In which lands or places fall the retrogradations or directions of planets: and the effects of an eclipse: and in which births or revolutions and in the sign over the aforesaid.

### Word 97. On the revealing of a hidden thing through the lord of the conjunction or prevention having more parts in the ascendant.

The Lord of the conjunction or prevention <note>the New Moon or Full Moon</note>: when it is in the angle of the thing sought, it will complete the matter. And similarly that which we wish to remain durable or stable. And when the aspect has hidden itself, and it is in the angle of the midheaven, that which is hidden will appear.

The Lord of the conjunction or prevention is the planet having the most parts <note>dignities or degrees</note> in the ascendant of the conjunction or prevention: namely, with those and in its degree: and it revolves with human effect. And I have already revealed this in Word 65: and it is from its own nature to uncover hidden things and alleviate difficulties. For this reason, when it is in the midheaven of the hiding of any thing: that which is hidden will appear.

### Word 98. On the lord of the angle of the ascending year: and of the four months: and the sign regarding the seeds and fruits, and their price.

The Lord of the angle of the conjunction and prevention, as well as of the quarters of the year: when it is strong, their state will be what it signifies: namely, if it is in the angles or in the succedent houses. And when it is weak, it will be of little value: namely, in the cadent houses. And similarly whether it is fast in its course or slow.

The lord of all the angles of the ascendant of the year and of the four months among the wandering stars <gloss>planets</gloss> is the one which has the most parts: namely, in those places. For as Ptolemy speaks of the lord of the conjunction or prevention, I also explain it regarding the lord of the quarters of the year. You, therefore, mix them according to the judgment of the book. And each of them has a signification over seeds and fruits: and therefore he says when one of them presides in an angle, the price of all things it signified will be increased. If, with this, it is fast in its course, it will reach the height of the price increase. If it is slow, it will be medium in its price.

### Word 99. On the darts and sparklings of the stars.

The <term>Alnaezic</term> <gloss>meteors or "shooting stars"</gloss>, that is, the "darts" and those having "hair" <gloss>comets</gloss> are among the secondary effects of the stars and are not of the stars themselves.

I have already revealed in the previous sections that secondary stars are things that happen from the stars in the air, and the Arabs call them *asubuli* and *alnaezic*: and they are "darts," because they resemble them in the speed of their motion. And it is certain that they are of the secondary things and not of the stars themselves.

### Word 100. On the change of the air, winds, rains, rivers, and the state of the condition of nations.

The <term>Alnaezic</term> <gloss>meteors</gloss> signify dry vapors: when, therefore, they are in one part of the sky, they signify winds happening in that same part. And if they are scattered in all parts, they signify the diminishing of waters: namely, by dryness and the disturbance of the air, and armies coming to that climate, seeking the kingdom of that region. And they are against that which people have agreed upon: that is, they are contrary to the law in which the people of that

<column-break/>

climate agree. Regarding those having "hair" <note>original: "comas"; referring to comets</note>: and they are those between which and the sun there are twelve signs, when they appear having much hair and are ascending or appearing in one of the angles of the kingdom or the king: his king shall die, or a powerful man in it. And if they are in a house following an angle <gloss>a succedent house</gloss>, his treasures will be destroyed and he will change his counselors. But if they are falling from the angles <gloss>cadent houses</gloss>: namely, of the kingdom, prisons and illnesses will be multiplied, and their death will be very sudden: namely, for the most part. And a loss in counsel will happen to the people of that climate. If they do not have hair: namely, if they are "bald" <note>original: "sudau ciaba"; likely a corruption of an Arabic term for a specific type of comet</note>, a traitor or a heretic will rise against the king. Therefore, when you find one with hair that is moving, it always moves only from the west toward the east: a traitor will come from far away to that climate. But if they are immobile: the traitor will be from some city of the same climate.

Aristotle already revealed in the book *On High Works* <note>original: "de operibus altis"; the Latin title for Aristotle's *Meteorology*</note> that dry vapors, when they reach the ether, become beneath the ether: and they are the *alnaezic*. It is not, therefore, to be wondered at if their appearance signifies the drying up of waters: since Aristotle mentioned in the aforesaid book *On High Works* that the substance of wind is dry vapor: it will signify, when there are *alnaezic* in one part, that there will be winds in that part. And when the *alnaezic* are scattered in every part, it will signify the diminishing of waters: because when dryness is multiplied in the air, the waters are diminished.

For it is remembered: that in the night of the 290th year of the Arabs, many *asubuli* <gloss>meteors</gloss> were diffused. And they occupied the whole air, and men were terrified <note>original: "extincti sunt"; literally "extinguished," implying they fainted or were overwhelmed</note>, and it lasted more than four hours: after a not insignificant time had passed of the same year, men suffered immoderate thirst: and the Nile of Egypt reached only 13 cubits. And the quantity was diminished by 4 cubits to the disadvantage of men: and the price of the harvest increased: and the people were disturbed with a vehement disturbance: and the reign of the king of Egypt <note>original: "protolo. regis"; likely a scribal error for the contemporary ruler</note> was ended.

Similarly, in the 300th year of the Arabs: they were diffused in every part of the air: and the Nile was again diminished: and a way was opened over Egypt from the west: that is, from the land of the Arabs through *beu baça*: and it happened then through clear light. And a great impediment happened to those resisting, and those rising up with them: namely, the Egyptians. Regarding those having hair <gloss>comets</gloss>: one ascended having hair: namely, <term>quauet bai</term>; the Egyptians suffered much. And it was in one of the angles of the conjunction in which the kingdom of the sons of <term>abeqs</term> was begun. Therefore, <term>abeqs aneçir</term> died.

<margin>Year of Christ 710, Oct 17</margin>
In the year 92, a certain one ascended having hair: and it lasted 11 nights: and it moved every night with a sensible motion. Therefore the son of *alchalig* entered after this in a short time: and he was profitable to Egypt and its parts. And whatever Ptolemy said happened then in Egypt. This is what I preferred to explain from the book. And I believe that he is suitable in his reasons: and that his explanation is perfect. I say to you that this is worthy of being committed to him whom you teach: and remove it from him whose intention is only to possess it. And he who thinks he knows it by heart if it is placed in his chest: for it is difficult for such a person to labor so that he may learn it. Therefore, he should be removed from this book, and from those similar to it. For it would be the greatest of errors if it were handed over to him. And I pray to God that He may gather you: since the translation of this book is perfected on the 17th day of the month of March, the 12th day of the month of *Jumada al-Thani*: in the year of the Arabs 530 <note>AD 1136</note>.

**The book of Ptolemy of the four treatises <gloss>the Tetrabiblos</gloss>, with his Centiloquium and the commentary of Haly: ends happily.**

<meta>This page transitions from the preceding discussion of eclipses into the "Centiloquium of Hermes," a famous medieval collection of one hundred astrological aphorisms. <center>The One Hundred Aphorisms</center>

### Here begins the book of the One Hundred Aphorisms of Hermes.

<image-desc>A large decorative historiated initial 'D' depicting a scholar, likely Hermes, seated at a desk with books and astronomical instruments.</image-desc>

<margin>Counsel</margin>
**Hermes says:** After God, the Sun and the Moon are the life of all living things. The births of many people do not have a <term>hyleg</term> <note>original: "hyleg"; the planetary point that determines the length of life</note>. But because the Sun and Moon behold their <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> with favor, their life is prolonged by that same freedom. 1.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
All daytime births are strengthened by the Sun when it is aligned with favorable planets. Nighttime births are strengthened by the Moon when she is beheld by favorable planets. If this is not the case, but there are still good planets in the <term>angles</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart</note>, then the birth is fortunate. 2.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
When Mars is the lord of the ascendant and is in the tenth house, it grants the native dignity and power, which they will use with injury and cruelty; this is truly called a misfortune rather than a fortune. 3.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
Jupiter, when aligned with malevolent planets, changes their malice into good. Venus cannot do this unless she is aided by Jupiter; therefore, in increasing good and prohibiting evil, Jupiter is considered a much better planet. 4.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
The astrologer cannot make a proper mixture of the stars' meanings before they know their friendships and enmities. Their friendship and enmity are threefold: one according to their nature, another according to their houses, and a third according to their <term>aspects</term> <note>the geometric angles between planets</note>. 5.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
Venus is opposed to Mercury. For Mercury embraces speech and disciplines, while Venus embraces pleasures and delights. Similarly, Jupiter is opposed to Mars: the former desires mercy and justice, while the latter desires impiety and cruelty. 6.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
For great princes, make the Sun or one of the <term>superior planets</term> <note>Saturn, Jupiter, or Mars</note> the significator. For scribes and peasants, use the inferior planets, and especially the Moon. 7.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
An aspect cannot diminish the significance of a <term>conjunction</term> <note>when two planets are at the same degree</note>. However, a conjunction diminishes the significance of an aspect. For a conjunction is stronger than an aspect. 8.

<margin>Caution</margin>
Do not define or choose anything when Scorpio is in the ascendant, nor when the angles are <term>oblique</term> <note>distorted or poorly aligned</note>. Or if Mars is in them, for the outcome of your definition will turn out false; especially since Scorpio is a sign of falsehood. 9.

<margin>Note</margin>
Even a favorable planet is hindered when it is in the 6th or 12th house and obstructed by malevolent planets. 10.

<margin>Question</margin>
Rumors told when the Moon is in the <term>first face</term> <note>the first ten degrees</note> of Scorpio are lies and fabrications. 11.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
The judgments of all astrologers sometimes turn out untrue, either because of the error of their instruments, or because of the ignorance of the person asking the question, or when the Sun is near the degree of the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>the highest point in the sky</note>, or when the figures that grant or deny the matter are equal. 12.

<margin>Election</margin>
While the Moon is in the south and descending in Scorpio or Pisces, do not begin to build. For a building of this kind will quickly be destroyed. 13.

<margin>Note</margin>
It is necessary for Mercury to be strong in births—by its location among people and by its alignment with other stars—so that the native may have dignity. For Mercury is a weak planet by itself. 14.

<margin>Interrogation</margin>
In the <term>signs of two bodies</term> <note>mutable signs like Gemini or Pisces</note>, victory is good and defeat is bad; indeed, both are doubled. 15.

<margin>Interrogation</margin>
Do not define anything until you know the intention of the person asking. Many do not know how to ask, nor can they express what they intend. 16.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
When you are asked about a father, look to the 4th house; about a brother, the 3rd; about a son, the 5th; about a wife, the 7th. But if you are asked on behalf of a sick person, look at nothing other than the ascendant. 17.

<margin>Election</margin>
When the Moon comes to the <term>square aspects</term> <note>90-degree angles</note> of favorable or malevolent planets, both the hindrance and the help will be doubtful; it is to be feared that the malevolent may hinder and the favorable may be unable to help. 18.

<margin>Election</margin>
At the beginning of journeys and returns, let the Moon not be in the ascendant, nor in the 4th, nor in the 9th house, even if she is not otherwise hindered. When entering a city, she should not be in the ascendant, the 7th, or the 4th house. Similarly, not when entering a house. 19.

<column-break/>

<margin>Note</margin>
The accidents of a man are foreknown in three ways: either from his own birth, or from the birth of his firstborn son, or from an interrogation <note>a "horary" question</note> known through deep feeling and concern. 20.

<margin>Election</margin>
Every undertaking made with a retrograde planet is quickly destroyed if the Moon is joined to it; and it comes to a worse state when she is hindered. 21.

<margin>Rule</margin>
The state of kings and princes is taken from Saturn and the Sun, and from the planet residing in the 10th house. The state of the king's helpers is taken from the 11th house, and the state of the peasants' helpers from the 2nd house. 22.

<margin>Rule</margin>
The departure of a king or prince for a journey is entirely rejected when Cancer is in the ascendant. 23.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
Gemini and Sagittarius obey the <term>Head and Tail of the Dragon</term> <note>the North and South Nodes of the Moon</note> more than other signs; and therefore they cause more serious evils in them than in other signs. 24.

<margin>Note</margin>
In the births of women, when the ascendant is one of the houses of Venus with Mars residing in them, or one of the houses of Mars with Venus residing in them, the woman will be immodest. The same will happen if she has Capricorn in the ascendant. 25.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
The Sun receives the virtues of the planets when it is joined with them in the ascendant or in the house of the Midheaven; by night, the Moon does the same when joined with the same in the aforementioned places. 26.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
Jupiter dissolves the malice of Saturn, just as Venus dissolves the malice of Mars. 27.

<margin>Interrogation</margin>
When there is a question about a woman in general, take the meaning from Venus. Specifically, take it from the 7th house. If for an enemy in general, from the 12th; specifically, from the 7th. 28.

<margin>Election</margin>
In the departure of anyone for battle, but especially for kings, let the ascendant be some house of the superior planets or of the Sun; and let both the sign and its lord be strong. Let the lord of the 7th house <note>the enemy</note> be weak and hindered by bad stars. 29.

<margin>Election</margin>
The Moon joined to Saturn or Jupiter, increasing in light and in number, will be good for all things. But if she is diminished, she will be bad for all things. Understand the same regarding Venus and Mars. 30.

<margin>Election</margin>
In loans and deposits, beware that Jupiter is not <term>under the rays</term> <note>too close to the Sun</note> or hindered by bad stars. If it is so, and not received from that hindrance, no restitution or only a small amount will follow. 31.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
Benefic planets moving toward an alignment with malevolent ones reduce some of their malice through whatever figure; more so through good figures, less so through bad ones. Malevolent planets moving toward an alignment with good ones in a square or opposition reduce some of their goodness; but from other aspects, nothing is changed. 32.

<margin>Rule</margin>
When Saturn passes from one sign into another, <term>diacobontes</term> <note>likely meteors or bolides</note> appear in the sky, which the Arabs call <term>assub</term> <note>Arabic: al-shihāb, meaning "shooting stars" or "meteors"</note>, or certain other signs of the nature of fire. 33.

<margin>Rule</margin>
The temperance of the air happens from the conjunction of Jupiter and the Sun, especially when that conjunction is in airy signs. From the conjunction of Saturn and the Sun comes cold. And from the conjunction of the Sun and Mars in a <term>bicorporeal sign</term> <note>a "double-bodied" sign like Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note> in the time of spring, there comes darkness of the air, and illnesses frequently occur. 34.

<margin>Rule</margin>
In summer, when the Sun enters the <term>terms</term> <note>a specific division of a sign</note> of Mars, there is heat. In winter, there will be drought and a lack of rain. 35.

<margin>Note</margin>
Calculate the <term>hyleg</term> and <term>alcocoden</term> <note>original: "alcocoden"; the planet that determines the number of years a person will live</note> in the births and questions of men, and their <term>directions</term> <note>a method of timing life events</note>, and especially in the questions of kings and great men. For through these, their accidents are known, whether they be good or bad. 36.

<margin>Note</margin>
When the ascendant is in a good state but its lord is in a bad one, it indicates health of the body but anxiety and sadness of the soul. If it is the other way around, define it the other way around. 37.

<margin>Commentary</margin>
Always note the configuration of the stars, not by the signs, but by the rays. 38.

<margin>Election</margin>
Use the Moon in curing eyes when she is waxing in light and free from the aspect of malevolent planets. 39.

<margin>Question</margin>
If the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>a calculated mathematical point in a chart</note> is with a malevolent planet in the 4th, 9th, or 12th house, and favorable planets are far away, it indicates death to the sick. 40.

<summary>This page introduces the Centiloquium of Hermes, presenting the first forty astrological aphorisms. These rules cover foundational principles of life expectancy (hyleg), planetary interactions, and specific advice for medicine, construction, and statecraft.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the "Centiloquium of Hermes," a collection of one hundred astrological rules. The previous page established the foundational importance of the Sun and Moon and the power of Jupiter to mitigate the malice of other planets. This page details specific planetary configurations affecting health, social status, and the timing of actions.</meta>

<header>Of Hermes</header>

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ Good or evil things will be lasting when the <term>significator</term> <note>the planet representing the person or matter in question</note> is stationary and in an <term>angle</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a chart</note>. Conversely, they are easily changed when the same is retrograde and in houses falling away from the angles. 41.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ The lord of the 7th house and the lord of the 8th house have the same power in hindering. Likewise, the lord of the 6th house has the same power as the lord of the 12th. 42.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ With Mars being "western" <note>setting after the sun</note> in Cancer and not looking toward Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, or the Sun, the native will be a bloodletter <note>original: "flobotomator"; a person who performs phlebotomy or medical bleeding</note>. But in the same way, with Mars being in Capricorn, he will be a corrupter of men and a lover of bloodshed. 43.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ It happens that even a skilled astrologer errs when he is ignorant of the significator of the person for whom he is making a choice <note>an "election," or choosing the best time for an action</note>. 44.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ Saturn elevated above Venus by a <term>square</term> aspect <note>a 90-degree angle, usually considered challenging</note> makes the children unchaste, and in women, impatient. If, however, Venus is elevated above Saturn, she makes them easy toward women and prone to lust. 45.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ If at someone's birth Mercury is in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note>, "oriental" <note>rising before the sun</note>, and swift in its motion, then the native shall be eloquent and learned in the liberal sciences. The same will be true if Mercury is in Sagittarius, in its own <term>terms</term> <note>specific degrees of a sign over which a planet has secondary dignity</note> in such a manner. 46.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ Of the <term>angles</term> <note>the four most powerful houses in a chart</note>, the first is the horoscope <note>the ascendant</note>. The second is the Midheaven. The third is the Western angle <note>the descendant</note>, and the fourth is the Angle of the Earth <note>the bottom of the chart</note>. Of the remaining places, the first is the 11th house, then the 2nd, after that the 5th, then the 9th, then the 3rd, and after that the 8th. The 6th and 12th houses are the worst. 47.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ Unless a benevolent planet <note>such as Jupiter or Venus</note> prohibits it, whatever Mars gives, he takes back. 48.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ You shall adapt the planets to the persons to whom you will make a petition. 49.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ When the horoscope or a planet is found in the 30th degree of a sign, its significance is in the following sign. If it is in the 29th, it will be in that sign itself. For the power of a planet is considered in three degrees: namely, the one it is in, the one preceding, and the one succeeding. 50.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ It is necessary to consider future things from the <term>conjunctions</term> of planets, but the present or past from their separations. 51.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ If Jupiter is in Cancer, far from the ascendant, and not hindered by anything, the native will indeed be rational and very skilled in science. However, he will love a solitary life and will receive no praise for his knowledge. 52.

<margin>Revolution</margin>
¶ Many inconveniences occur in the world when an eclipse of both luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> happens in one month, especially in those places where their special significance lies. 53.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ When the Moon is in the <term>combust way</term> <note>original: "via combusta"; a specific section of the zodiac considered unlucky, roughly the end of Libra and beginning of Scorpio</note> at the time of beginning a journey, the traveler will fall ill on his journey or suffer some grave troubles. 54.

¶ In the <term>directions</term> <note>a method of predicting life events by moving planets forward in time</note> of both wandering stars <note>planets</note> and fixed stars, it is necessary to consider the time. 55.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ The father's estate passes to the son when Saturn is fortunate and looks upon the lord of the ascendant with favor, and even more so if he is the lord of the 4th house. 56.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ When benevolent planets are in signs where they have no <term>dignity</term> <note>essential strength like being in their own sign or exaltation</note>, their kindness is poured out onto others. 57.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ If Mars is the <term>almuten</term> <note>original: "almutaç"; the planet with the most combined dignity and power in a chart</note> at birth and is not joined to benevolent planets, it signifies that the native will suffer fire. 58.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ A benevolent planet grants immense happiness when it is received in its own house. A malevolent one, however, abstains from much malice when it is so received. 59.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ The native will be sick and weak when Mars is elevated above Saturn. If, however, Saturn is above Mars, he will be strong and stout. 60.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ If the man's Part of Marriage falls in <term>obedient signs</term> <note>the signs from Libra to Pisces</note>, but the woman's in <term>commanding signs</term> <note>the signs from Aries to Virgo</note>, the woman will indeed rule the man, and the man will obey the woman; if it is the reverse, the business will be the reverse. 61.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ Out of favor, if the lords of the <term>triplicity</term> <note>the three signs of the same element</note> and the joining of light are joined to each other—the first to the second, and the second to the third—they signify lasting prosperity and liberation from sorrows. 62.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ When Mercury is in Pisces in <term>deep degrees</term> <note>original: "gradibus puteosis," also called "pitted" degrees; traditionally considered difficult or weakening points in the zodiac</note>, it makes the natives unwise or mute. Jupiter, however, in the houses

<column-break/>

of Mars and in deep degrees, makes them filthy and needy, and harmed by military persons. In the houses of Saturn, especially in Capricorn and in deep degrees, it makes them rigid and hateful to all. 63.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ Mercury receives the nature of Mars when existing in his houses; and if he is configured to him while falling away from an angle, the native will be a lover of hunting and will love to play with dice. If, however, he is not falling, he will be warlike and a soldier. 64.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ It is unfortunate for the wandering planets to be "under the rays" when they are within 12 degrees of the Sun, unless they are in the same degree with it. When they pass 12 degrees, emerging as oriental, they are strong. 65.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ The Head <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> works terrible evils with malevolent planets, for it increases their malice. It works many good things with benevolent ones, for through it their kindness is increased. The Tail <note>the South Node of the Moon</note>, just as it is in position, so it is opposed to the Head in its significance. 66.

<margin>Nativity</margin>
¶ If someone has Mercury in the 6th house of the nativity, he will be converted from his faith to another. And he who has the <term>Part of Fortune</term> hindered will not be firm in his faith. 67.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ The first sign has dominion in significations when the significance of a thing occurs through two signs. 68.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ The beginning of every matter is taken from the Moon; but every end from the lord of her house. 69.

<margin>Revolution</margin>
¶ If Jupiter in the <term>revolution</term> <note>a chart for the start of the year</note> of the years of the world is in his own house or exaltation, oriental in an angle, and free from evils, it signifies a scarcity of grain. 70.

<margin>Interrogation</margin>
¶ It is to be feared for the sick when the Moon and the lord of the ascendant are hindered by the lord of the 8th house <note>the house of death</note>. 71.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ By no means should you begin a quarrel, contention, or lawsuit when the Moon is in a bad state. For if it happens in such a way, you will without doubt be defeated. 72.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ Every rebel beginning to rebel at the start of the year will obtain dominion without difficulty. 73.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ While the Moon is in <term>ruminant signs</term> <note>signs representing animals that chew cud, like Aries, Taurus, or Capricorn</note> or joined to a retrograde planet, it is not good to use purges; for these bring on vomiting or other injuries. 74.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ Oriental planets exhibiting good or evil things give them quickly; occidental ones, however, give them slowly. 75.

<margin>Revolution</margin>
¶ The degree of the conjunction of the luminaries is the midpoint of the eclipse's duration. 76.

<margin>Prognostication</margin>
¶ In the revolution of the years of the world, many difficulties will be present when Jupiter and Saturn are in their <term>exaltations</term> <note>the signs where a planet is most honored</note>. 77.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ Be suspicious and careful when a benevolent planet is with a malevolent one, and do not trust much that the malice of the evil one is entirely turned away. 78.

<margin>Counsel / Nativity</margin>
¶ The twelve signs depend on the ascendant; and indeed the ascendant signifies the state of the body, but its lord signifies the state of the mind. Therefore, strive in every way that the ascendant and its lord are not hindered. 79.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ When planets are in fixed signs, they signify a lasting thing. In <term>bicorporeal signs</term> <note>the "double-bodied" or mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note>, they signify a doubtful thing; in movable signs, a changeable thing, either for good or for evil. 80.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ In clandestine matters, use the Moon when she is not going under the rays of the Sun, but emerging from them. 81.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ To cut or put on new clothes while the Moon is in a fixed sign, and especially in Leo, is horrible and dangerous; also when she is in conjunction or opposition with the Sun, or hindered by malevolent planets. 82.

<margin>Interrogation</margin>
¶ The Moon has great power in <term>interrogations</term> <note>horary astrology, or questions asked of the stars</note> unless the ascendant is Leo, Sagittarius, or Aquarius. Then, certain of these take away her significance, especially when they are in Leo or Aquarius. 83.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ Saturn is still "under the rays" as long as a distance of 15 degrees exists between him and the Sun. The same is understood for Jupiter. 84.

<margin>Election</margin>
¶ The Moon in Cancer is entirely rejected for marriages, and similarly in Virgo, except in the marriages of widows. 85.

<margin>Counsel</margin>
¶ A malevolent planet, when it is oriental in its own house or exaltation, is better than a retrograde and hindered benevolent planet. 86.

<meta>This page concludes the "Centiloquium of Hermes," a collection of one hundred astrological rules, and begins a new treatise attributed to Hermes concerning the "Beibenie" or fixed stars and their influence on human destiny.</meta>

<header>The Book of Hermes</header>

<margin>Nativity</margin> ¶ There will be an impediment regarding that part of the body signified by the sign that was afflicted at the time of birth. 87.

<margin>Counsel</margin> ¶ Great prosperities occur when the <term>lords of the triplicity</term> <note>three signs of the same element shared by a planet</note> of the luminary <note>the Sun or Moon</note> which holds authority are in <term>angles</term> or <term>succedent houses</term> <note>the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note> in their proper places and far from the gaze of <term>malefics</term> <note>unfavorable planets, usually Saturn or Mars</note>. And if the lord of the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> is in a good state, the good will be even greater and more abundant. 88.

<margin>Counsel</margin> ¶ Planets achieve the same through a <term>trine</term> <note>a harmonious 120-degree aspect</note> as they do through a <term>sextile</term> <note>a 60-degree aspect</note>; however, the sextile aspect is less effective in good or evil than the trine. 89.

<margin>Counsel</margin> ¶ Saturn brings evil with slowness. Mars, however, brings it suddenly; therefore, Mars is considered worse than Saturn in its ability to do harm. 90.

<margin>Prognostication</margin> ¶ It is called a "great conjunction" when the three <term>superior planets</term> <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars</note> join together in one of the royal signs; they then create the most powerful kingdoms when they are aspected by the Sun. 91.

<margin>Election</margin> ¶ A hidden word that is sought after is revealed immediately when the Moon and the planet she <term>applies</term> to <note>moves toward in aspect</note> are in "vocal" signs <note>signs associated with the human voice, like Gemini or Virgo</note> and in the 5th or 3rd houses, or in opposition to them. 92.

<margin>Nativity</margin> ¶ A malefic planet increases its malice in the 8th house; a <term>benefic</term> <note>favorable planet, like Jupiter or Venus</note> in that same place exhibits neither good nor evil. 93.

<margin>Nativity / Revolution</margin> ¶ Good or evil will never be perfected unless the benefic or malefic planets have aspected the Moon by a <term>square</term> <note>a challenging 90-degree aspect</note> in the birth chart or in the <term>revolution</term> <note>a yearly update of the chart</note>. 94.

<margin>Nativity</margin> ¶ If Mercury is afflicted in the 6th house, the native will die in prison. If Saturn is in the 12th house, he will be imprisoned; and if Venus is in the 8th, he will suffer a fall from a high place. 95.

<margin>Infirmity</margin> ¶ One must be fearful at the start of a sickness when the Sun by day and the Moon by night are afflicted. 96.

<margin>Counsel</margin> ¶ The significations of the stars always vary when their <term>latitudes</term> <note>distance north or south of the ecliptic</note> vary within their configurations to one another. 97.

<margin>Interrogation</margin> ¶ The Moon in the 4th, 7th, 9th, or 12th houses indicates the reasons for which an interrogation was made. She indicates the same if she has just separated from Mercury. If, however, the ascending sign is <term>bicorporeal</term> <note>a "double-bodied" sign like Gemini or Pisces</note> and the Moon is likewise in a bicorporeal sign, the same cause will be sought after again. 98.

<margin>Nativity</margin> ¶ In its own house or its <term>exaltation</term> <note>a sign of special strength</note>, a malefic planet—though with slowness—eventually provides a good end. If, however, that same planet is afflicted in the ascendant, even if in its own house or exaltation, it nonetheless brings an impediment and an evil end. 99.

<margin>Counsel</margin> ¶ The outcome of all beginnings and all doubtful events is determined through these significations: namely, through the 4th house and its lord, and through any planet that might be in that house. Likewise, through the luminary that holds authority and its lord, and through the planet to which that luminary is joined and its lord. 100.
¶ Use these and the other things I have handed down to you, most illustrious one, and by using them with sobriety, you shall never err. With the help of God. Amen.
¶ Here ends the Book of a Hundred Aphorisms of Hermes.

¶ Although I have seen a great part of the stars behave differently in the tables of King Alfonso <note>the Alfonsine Tables, a major medieval astronomical work</note> than what is written in this booklet—both regarding their latitudes and their positions—I nonetheless did not wish to write them otherwise than I found them harmoniously in the copies, lest I be accused of presumptuously changing the words of the greatest Hermes, to whom this booklet is ascribed by such a title.

Hermes said: I shall speak to you of the matters of fortune. Wherein you shall have joy and great profit from them; and the same is true of the secret matters which he placed and composed in the stars called <term>Beibenie</term> <note>from the Persian 'biyabani,' referring to specific fixed stars used in medieval astrology</note>. # Regarding the Strength of the Stars

...tudes and he will be more handsome than all the handsome. And Hermes said that if you find any of these <term>Beibenie</term> <note>original: beibenijs; from a Persian term for "fixed" stars used in medieval astrology to denote prominent stars that do not move like planets</note> in the 9th or 7th <note>the houses of travel and marriage</note> in anyone’s birth chart, it will work toward travel or toward marriage. And I have worked with them, and I did not find their effect to be strong; therefore, I did not write a judgment on them. And when I took the <term>Part of Form</term> <note>original: parte forme; an astrological calculation or "lot" used to determine physical appearance</note> in someone’s birth chart according to the Beibenie, look to the lord of the triplicity of the Sun in day births, and in night births the lord of the triplicity of the Moon; and thus you will arrive at what you seek, if God wills.

Here ends the book of Hermes the philosopher on the strength of the stars which are called Beibenie.

### Here begins the Hundred Aphorisms of Bethem. 1.

I shall begin this book regarding the habits in the judgments of the stars. 2.

3. Know that when planets are <term>retrograde</term> <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, they are like a man who is sick: dazed and anxious.

4. A <term>cadent</term> <note>original: Cladens, error for cadens; a planet in a house that "falls away" from the main angles, such as the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th</note> planet is like a dead man who has no movement.

5. A <term>combust</term> <note>original: Clombustus; a planet too close to the Sun, thought to be "burnt" by its heat</note> planet is like a captive: imprisoned and disgraced without power.

6. ¶ A planet standing still <note>stationary</note> before retrogradation is like a healthy man from whom health departs, but a little of it remains.

7. ¶ A planet standing still before direct motion is like a sick man after he recovers and sees the beginning of his health.

8. ¶ A planet <term>besieged</term> <note>original: obsessus; caught between two other planets</note> is like one fearing between two enemies—that is, when it is between two <term>malefics</term> <note>original: infortunas; typically Saturn or Mars</note>.

9. ¶ When it is between two <term>benefics</term> <note>original: fortunas; typically Jupiter or Venus</note>, it is like a man eating and drinking, secure from all evil and fear.

10. ¶ When malefics aspect a planet from the fourth house <note>a "square" aspect</note>, or it aspects them, it is like a man whose death, vengeance, and marking <note>original: decoratio; likely used here in the sense of a brand or public marking of fate</note> begin.

11. ¶ When a planet is in the aspect of its enemy, it is like a man fearing his enemy.

12. ¶ When it is with its enemy, it is like a man fighting with his enemy.

13. ¶ When it is with a planet that is a friend and similar to itself, it is like a man to whom hospitality and an embrace are offered.

14. ¶ When it is in the house of its friend, it is like a man with his companion.

15. ¶ When it is falling <note>cadent</note> from its own house or from the house of its <term>exaltation</term> <note>a sign where a planet's influence is heightened</note>, it is like a man absent from his home or his city.

16. ¶ When it is in its own house or the house of its exaltation, it is like a man in his own home: his judgment and will are perfected, and what he wants to happen is completed.

17. ¶ When a planet is retrograde in its own house or the house of its exaltation, it is like a sick man in his own home.

18. ¶ When it is combust in its own house or house of exaltation, it is like a man whom his lord or king has imprisoned in his own house.

19. ¶ When it is falling <note>cadent</note>, it is a vexed and timid man.

20. ¶ A fortunate planet <note>benefic</note> when it is retrograde is as if unfortunate; and a fortunate planet falling from the <term>angles</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> or the ascendant is like a man hoping for fortune and not finding it.

21. ¶ A fortunate planet when it is retrograde and with an unfortunate planet turns from fortune to misfortune, and it strengthens the present misfortune.

22. ¶ An unfortunate planet when it is direct in its own house and is with a fortunate planet turns from misfortune to fortune.

23. ¶ When a planet is in the last [degrees] of a sign, it is departing or retreating.

24. ¶ When it is in the first degree of a sign, it is of weak strength in judgments and questions.

25. ¶ From the first degree to the 15th degree it is approaching; but from the 15th to the 25th it is complete.

26. ¶ If it is in the last part of a sign it is departing: and then it is like a man leaving a house in which he has stayed.

27. ¶ A <term>wild</term> <note>original: agrestis; possibly referring to a planet in a "feral" sign like Leo or a planet without essential dignity</note> planet in the ascendant in which it has authority is singular in judgment and disposition.

28. ¶ A planet in a house not its own is like a man in a stranger’s house who is knocking; his judgment is already suppressed, nor does he have authority.

29. ¶ When it is with the Sun, its strengths are weak and its judgment is diminished.

30. ¶ A planet being in the last part of a sign and retrograde transmits

<column-break/>

its judgment, and its light is weakened, and its brightness is taken away from it.

31. ¶ When it is retrograde in its own house and in the 7th degree from the Sun, it is like a man in his own house and over him is a guard—that is, a man more powerful than he—and he desires to flee for fear of him and of disgrace and pride.

32. ¶ A planet in the house of its enemy is like a man in the house of another between whom hatred and anger have already arisen.

33. ¶ A planet direct in its own house, free from infirmity and misfortunes, signifies the perfection of questions and investigations, and the completion and attainment for the asker.

34. ¶ When the Moon <term>separates</term> <note>moves away from an aspect</note> from planets, it signifies things of the past.

35. ¶ When the Moon <term>joins</term> <note>original: continuat; moves toward an aspect</note> with planets, it signifies what is to come.

36. ¶ From the Moon separated from Saturn, bindings and sadnesses happen, as well as the discovery of evil and falls.

37. ¶ From the Moon separated from Jupiter, joy and gladness happen: friendship, the confirmation of dowries, increase in family, children, servants, and inheritances; also addition to wealth, the multiplication of fortunes, and the dissolution of misfortunes and falls.

38. ¶ From the Moon separated from Mars, there happen quarrels and oppositions, bad rumors, pains, bindings, deaths, the shedding of blood, false testimonies, children of fornication and of prostitutes, the removal of jealousy; as in <term>lectronibus</term> <note>meaning unclear; possibly a corruption of "elections"</note> the granting of the forbidden, masculine intercourse <note>homosexual acts</note>, proposals to women, the drinking of raisin wine and wine from any intoxicant, wounds, the cutting off of offspring, and the preparation of syrups which make children descend from the womb to the vulva and the level ground <note>referring to abortifacients</note>.

39. ¶ From the Moon separated from the Sun, there happen illnesses, anxiety, fear, death, imprisonment, the discovery of evil, and marking <note>dishonor</note>, pains, falls, sickness, binding, captivity, cavalry, armies, people, and terrifying things.

40. ¶ From the Moon separated from Venus, there happen fornications, jokes, laughter, gestures, songs, silk garments, colorings, and varieties.

41. ¶ From the Moon separated from Mercury, things happen according to the quality of Mercury’s joining with a benefic or malefic.

42. ¶ The Moon joined with any of the planets signifies the future according to the Moon’s joining with those planets.

43. ¶ The Moon being fortunate in the morning is praiseworthy; whatever was asked on that day concerning business or birth, it will be pleasing and fortunate for the asker.

# Bethem on the Hours of the Planets

...truth, and to seek <term>marriage</term> <note>original: piugiuz, a contraction for conjugium</note> and access to nobles: and for those who rule the kingdom to lay the foundations of buildings: it is favorable to go out for any of these deeds; on that day the doer shall rejoice. 58.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in the 4th house of Mars is unfavorable for every work: especially for meeting a king or seeking business; it is not good to marry then; a sick person will die or blood or a wound will issue from him. 59.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in the 4th house of the Sun is a day to be blamed in every deed: especially for meeting a king or nobles and seeking from them what concerns business and legal causes. 60.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in the 4th house of Venus is a praiseworthy day in every work: especially to withdraw with a woman; to put on new clothes; to practice noble things; games; <term>marriage</term> <note>original: piuviū; likely a scribal variant of conjugium</note>; seeking refuge; sexual intercourse; the purchase of beasts and servants; to enter the baths; to decorate; and to go out to seek rest. 61.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in the 4th house of Mercury is a good day for applying oneself to selling, buying, and mingling with kings; the accounting of a great house; and to read books and sciences. 62.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in <term>sextile aspect</term> <note>an angle of 60 degrees, usually considered harmonious</note> to Saturn is a good day to meet old men and farm managers: to look into their legal causes, business, and affairs: and to proceed in the decoration of one's own things: to agree on the determination of all business: and for a man’s hearing: and for certain friendship: and to mingle with great men: and to be associated with their sons or counselors. 63.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in sextile to Jupiter is a good day; and on that day, it is good to agree to meet with <term>alcaides</term> <note>original: alcaideis; from the Arabic al-qadi, meaning a judge or local governor</note>: the judgment of the just; to seek a number and every good work: to marry: to go on a journey: to mingle with nobles and high men: to secure great things: to manage the kingdom: and to be present at weddings and marriages. 64.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in sextile to Mars is a good day: the best thing in it is to meet leaders and providers of arms: to distribute the army's weapons; to provide for wars: it is good for <term>bloodletting</term> <note>original: ventofare; likely a vulgar Latin form of ventosare, referring to cupping or lancing</note> and to take or divide horses. 65.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in sextile to the Sun is a good day: especially to meet old men, farm managers, and the providers of the city: to meet kings, the king's princes, and nobles: to seek business: to assemble the kingdom: and to go about one's business. 66.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in sextile to Venus is a good day in every work: especially in mingling with women and youths, or eunuchs, or great ladies: to seek any friendship or marriage; the preparation of spectacles: and to put on new clothes. 67.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in sextile to Mercury is a good day: for games and the agreements of dowries; for accounting; for meeting farm managers and providers; and in every work and for trading. 68.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in <term>trine aspect</term> <note>an angle of 120 degrees, considered the most favorable aspect</note> to Saturn is a good day in every work: it is especially praiseworthy to meet the old men of the whole kingdom and the king: on this day, to till the lands and found buildings and to look into ancient things. 69.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in trine to Jupiter is a good day in every work: especially seeking the truth and determining every good work and the love of God: it is good to meet kings, <term>alcaldibus</term> <note>judges</note>, and nobles. 70.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in the 3rd [trine] to Mars is a good day for quarrels and hunting: to meet kings: it is good to buy beasts: to arrange for wars: to send messengers: for presentations in war: and the selection of the battle line and small units. 71.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in trine to the Sun is a good day in every work: it is better on this day to meet old men and the king; to provide for the work of the land and for any work: it is good to meet noble princes: to bind banners: to assemble the kingdom, and for every good deed. 72.

<margin>F</margin> ¶ The Moon in trine to Venus is a good day in every work: it is better on this day for questions regarding the binding of marriage: and it is suitable to put on new clothes: to prepare to go to tents and legal causes: for the betrothals of lovers; to buy beasts and maidservants: to meet with elders: to look into feasts and weddings: and to work on <term>images</term> <note>astrological talismans or icons</note> and the causes of love. 73.

<margin>E</margin> ¶ The Moon in trine to Mercury is a good day to bind agreements, to meet farm managers and scribes, and to provide for all deeds. 74.

<margin>in</margin> ¶ Saturn in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> brings misfortune to the question for the querent, especially if it is <term>retrograde</term> at the time of the question: it delays, and burdens, desolates, and breaks. 75.

<margin>in</margin> ¶ Saturn in the 10th house [the midheaven] regarding the querent's land: business is sought with effort, even if done with fortune: and corruption happens in the matter. 76.

<margin>in</margin> ¶ Saturn in the 7th house corrupts the question and causes corruption of the business to reach the querent: and it changes the business from one misfortune to another. 77.

<margin>in</margin> ¶ Saturn in the 4th house causes fortune to reach the question in the beginning of the matter: but it drags the unfortunate toward corruption. 78.

<column-break/>

¶ Jupiter dissolves what Saturn binds. 79.
¶ Similarly, Venus dissolves what Mars binds. 80.
¶ The Moon separating from fortune dissolves what Mercury binds. 81.
¶ The superior planets [Saturn, Jupiter, Mars] that are in opposition to the Sun impede and corrupt business: and they impede questions. 82.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ Saturn in the 4th house from the Sun signifies the progress of business: however, it terminates in misfortune and corruption. 83.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ Saturn in the 4th house from Jupiter or in its opposition takes away evil and dissolves his oppression or influence. 84.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ Saturn in the 4th house, or in opposition, or in conjunction with Mars prohibits joy and precipitates business and corrupts and impedes the question. 85.

¶ Saturn in the 4th house of Venus: or in conjunction: or in opposition: completes every question in what is illicit and in disobedience: and if it were according to a diversity of obedience, I say we have conquered—it will return, take away shame, and corrupt. 86.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ Saturn in the 4th house of Mercury: or in opposition, or in conjunction: corrupts the question: and desolates business: and causes an excess of superfluity. 87.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ Jupiter in the 4th house of Saturn: or in opposition: or in conjunction: forbids its corruption: and turns it from misfortune to fortune. 88.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ Jupiter in the 4th house of Mars: or in conjunction, or in opposition: prohibits its generation and corruption and oppression. 89.

¶ Jupiter in the 4th house of Venus, or in conjunction, or in opposition, signifies the fulfillment of the question: and brings a sense of gratitude with it. 90.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ Jupiter with Mercury in the 4th house: or in conjunction, or in opposition: signifies the perfection of questions: and the determination of business and its perfection and the addition of fortune and good things. 91.

¶ When a planet of fortune [a benefic] is in the ascendant: and fortune is also in the 2nd house, the querent will be transformed from misfortune to fortune. 92.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ When a planet of fortune is in the ascendant: and in the 2nd house is a planet of misfortune [a malefic]: the question will change from fortune to misfortune. 93.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ When a strong planet is in the ascendant and in one of the <term>angles</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, the question will change from fortune to misfortune. 94.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ When the degree of the ascendant is in the <term>Combust Way</term> <note>original: via combusta; a specific unlucky stretch of the zodiac, typically late Libra and early Scorpio</note>, the business and the request will be corrupted. 95.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ When misfortune is in the 10th or 4th from the ascendant, hearts will tremble and misfortune will happen, and the question will be deprived and will fail. 96.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ When a planet of misfortune is in the ascendant: and in the 2nd house there is fortune, the question will be completed and the business will be concluded with joy and famous profit. 97.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ When a planet of misfortune is in the ascendant: and in the 2nd house there is misfortune, the question will fail and proceed toward misfortune. 98.

¶ When the ascendant decreases in its ascensions: and its lord is in a descending place in the 6th or 12th house, the querent will hope for things which he will not pursue: and when fortune is in the 3rd from the ascendant and misfortune is in the ascendant: the querent will have little application to the business. 99.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ A planet which, when it happens, is losing its time of ascension: the querent will pursue misfortune at the end of his business after its determination and attainment. 100.

<margin>a</margin> ¶ When a planet of misfortune is <term>received</term> <note>an astrological relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</note> in the angles, it will give and apply itself to the querent's business: yet it will take away from him what it gave: the knowledge of reception is when a planet is in its own house: or in the house of its exaltation, safe from misfortune.

->Here ends the Hundred Aphorisms of Bethem.<-

### Follows concerning the hours of the planets: and first regarding the hour of Saturn.

**When** it is the hour of Saturn, it is good to buy things of a heavy nature: such as iron, tin, lead, and all metals: and stone: and black cloths: and to begin to dig gardens: and to devise certain frauds against enemies: but it is not good to bleed the blood: nor to take medicine: nor to speak to a person of power: nor to a hypocritical monk named Plato <note>original: plato monacho hypocrite; this may be a specific historical reference or a corruption of another word</note>: nor to a fisherman: nor to a hunter: nor to speak to any friend: nor to construct or build any wall: indeed, it is not good for any man to begin anything: nor to form any partnership: nor to take a wife: because they will never be in accord: nor to cut cloths: nor new...
