->**On the Hour of Jupiter**<-

In the hour of Jupiter <note>Astrological hours are not 60 minutes long, but rather a 12th of the time between sunrise and sunset.</note>, it is good to buy and exchange silver: and to handle all business pertaining to silver: and to trade in water-colored <note>original: "aquri coloris," likely aquamarine or pale blue</note> cloths: and to build bridges and houses for the sake of prayer: it is also good to begin a journey with lords, even for the purpose of trade: it is good to begin a voyage by sea: and it is good to take medicine and to let blood: and to speak of harmony, peace, friendship, and power: and to buy chestnut-colored horses: and steel weapons are good: and to set up a loom for weaving: and to plow and sow a field: also to dig a well: to construct a wall and to build. Why say more? All good works should be begun in the hour of Jupiter.

->**On the Hour of Mars**<-

In the hour of Mars, it is good to buy weapons: and iron-shod horses and all horses fit for war: to arm galleys: to begin a journey for the sake of war, whether by land or by sea: and to buy all red-colored cloths: but to take medicine and to let blood or to begin a journey for the sake of any trade is not good: furthermore, all works pertaining to fire are good, such as those of smiths, cooks, and bakers. And as we said of the hour of Saturn <note>referring to a previous section not on this page</note>, it is not good to begin a partnership, nor to confirm a marriage or take a wife.

->**On the Hour of the Sun**<-

In the hour of the Sun, it is good to buy gold and all things of a golden color and golden horses: and it is best in this hour to speak to a king and to all powerful people: and it is good for parents to begin a journey for the sake of war and to begin a battle: and it is good to trade in yellow-colored cloths: but to take medicine, to let blood, to begin a journey for the sake of trade, to take a wife, or to enter into a partnership, or to act or negotiate is neither good nor bad.

->**On the Hour of Venus**<-

In the hour of Venus, it is good to buy women <note>likely referring to female servants or slaves in a medieval context</note>, pearls, and all ornaments for women: and golden rings: and to invest in all women's things: to become betrothed and to take a wife is most perfect: also to buy white horses and white garments: and to take medicine and let blood: it is good to speak to queens and noblewomen.

->**On the Hour of Mercury**<-

In the hour of Mercury, it is good to buy all painted and written things: furniture: millet: panic grass <note>a type of cereal crop</note>: and all garments of various colors that pertain to the use of men and all kinds of spices: it is good to buy cotton: silks or raw silk: and all works made of silk: and to begin a legal plea: to take a wife and form a partnership: it is also excellent to take medicine and let blood: to make a journey for the sake of trade: to buy piebald horses: and weapons of two colors, yellow and gold: and to buy green-colored garments: it is good to set up a loom.

->**On the Hour of the Moon**<-

In the hour of the Moon, it is good to buy honey: oil: figs: chestnuts: nuts: almonds: wool: flax: hemp: barley: the meat of pigs and of all animals except sheep: it is also good to buy birds pertaining to Mercury <note>perhaps songbirds or messengers</note>: and all beasts that pertain to the butcher's stall: to swear oaths: it is good to perform deceptions, betrayals, frauds, and clever tricks: also, it is not good to begin works for which you desire stability; but for those for which you desire speed, it is good to begin.

->**On the Rising of the Triplicities: and first on the rising of the first Triplicity.**<-

If <term>Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius</term> <note>The Fire Triplicity</note> should be rising: because these signs are fiery: it is good under their rising to begin those things which pertain to fire, such as using tongs, kindling fire, coloring gold, silver, lead, tin, or brass: and smithcraft. And every work for which you desire speed: to sail: to hold horse races: to send a messenger: to raise sails: to dig a well: to find treasures: and many things which cannot be numbered.

->**On the Rising of the 2nd Triplicity.**<-

If <term>Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn</term> <note>The Earth Triplicity</note> should be rising: because they are earthy signs: it is good under the same rising to do all works that pertain to the earth: such as plowing the land: buying lands and houses: measuring and dividing the earth: garments: and to buy timber from which you wish to make ships and all buildings: and to do all works for which you wish to have stability, perseverance, and durability.

->**On the Rising of the 3rd Triplicity.**<-

If, however, <term>Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius</term> <note>The Air Triplicity</note> should ascend: because they are airy signs, under their ascent it is good to do what pertains to the air: such as placing a mast in a ship and erecting it: 

<column-break/>

preparing and extending the yards and sails: and all works that pertain to a ship: the running of horses and galleys: and it is good to begin a journey.

->**On the Rising of the 4th Triplicity.**<-

But if the ascendant should be <term>Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces</term> <note>The Water Triplicity</note>: because they are aquatic signs: under their rising it is good to do all things that pertain to water: such as casting nets into the water: and practicing every kind of fishing: to bathe and to construct baths: and to make dams for a mill: and to direct water courses: and many things which cannot be numbered.

->**On the hour of Saturn and its rising sign.**<-

This must be observed all the more diligently: that if it be the hour of Saturn, and a sign of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note> is ascending, it is marvelous for doing all things which were said of the hour of Saturn: and understand the same for all other hours and signs: and if you can, harmonize the hours with the signs, for that is best: and what we said of Saturn, understand thus for all other planets.

---

->**Here ends Bethem on the hours of the planets.**<-

The Judgments or Propositions of Almansor. Here begin the chapters of the stars presented to the Great King of the Saracens by Almansor the astrologer: and translated by <term>Plato of Tivoli</term> <note>A 12th-century Italian scholar and translator known for bringing Arabic astronomical and mathematical works into Latin.</note>.

### Ptolemy's Compendium

Mirex, you asked that I satisfy your wishes: I have in no way refused to undergo the labor. You have written; I ask that you receive this with a favorable mind.

<margin>1.</margin>
¶ The arrangement of the signs: as I shall say, the beginning starts from Aries: one is diurnal <note>day-active</note>: the other is nocturnal <note>night-active</note>. One is masculine: the other feminine. One is light: the other heavy.

<margin>2.</margin>
¶ The <term>exaltation</term> <note>a sign where a planet is thought to have its greatest power</term> of any of the seven planets is said to be in that place where its substance suffers from another principle. For example, the Sun's exaltation is in Aries, and it is the <term>fall</term> <note>the sign opposite the exaltation, where a planet's power is weakened</term> of Saturn. For the Sun possesses brightness, while Saturn possesses darkness: as Jupiter's is in Cancer, in which Mars falls. One of these desires justice, while the other signifies injustice: and thus Mercury's is in Virgo: which is the fall of Venus. For one signifies science and philosophy; the other signifies the delights of the causes, and whatever is the flavor of the body.

<margin>3.</margin>
¶ The significance of the parts of the circle, O Great King, is over one thing alone: thus a sign of the fiery part signifies over fire. The earthy over the earth. The airy over the air: and the aquatic over the waters.

<margin>4.</margin>
¶ Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius are the hot and dry triplicity: bitter, fiery: diurnal, masculine: and signifies red bile <note>cholera rubea</note>.
¶ Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn: the earthy triplicity: cold, dry. Nocturnal, feminine, and signifies black bile.
¶ Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius: the triplicity is airy: hot: moist: sanguine: sweet: diurnal.
¶ Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces: the aquatic triplicity: cold: moist: phlegmatic: tasteless: nocturnal.

<margin>5.</margin>
¶ The <term>Fortunes</term> <note>the "benefic" planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> are generous and faithful. The <term>Infortunes</term> <note>the "malefic" planets, Saturn and Mars</note> are stingy and unfaithful.

<margin>6.</margin>
¶ The Fortunes will give nothing to anyone with labor. But whatever the Infortunes give, they will shorten and take away.

<margin>7.</margin>
¶ When two Infortunes are joined together, a perfect Fortune is made from them: just as from the conjunction of two Fortunes: and this is according to the sayings of Ptolemy.

<margin>8.</margin>
¶ Of all the <term>aspects</term> <note>the geometric angles between planets</note> of the planets, the best is the trine and sextile. The worst is the square and the opposite.

<margin>9.</margin>
¶ The trine and sextile aspect of the Infortunes does not help, just as the square and opposite of the Fortunes does not hinder.

<margin>10.</margin>
¶ Among many signs of life, the <term>hyleg</term> <note>the "life-giver," a specific point in a birth chart used to determine longevity</note> signifies much and long life: and pure intellect and the greatest vigor.

<margin>11.</margin>
¶ Whoever has Mercury in the root of their birth in the house of Mars will be of bad suspicion and hasty in his business.

<margin>12.</margin>
¶ Whoever has Mercury in the root of their birth in the house of Saturn will be of great intellect: of long thought: a wise man and a philosopher.

<margin>13.</margin>
¶ He will never be poor and destitute whose lord of birth is Jupiter.

<margin>14.</margin>
¶ Whoever has Infortunes in the ascendant will suffer a shameful mark on the face.

# The Propositions of Almansor

<margin>N</margin> <note>N: Nativitas (Birth rules)</note>
15. A person’s eyes cannot escape a grave impediment if both luminaries <note>The "luminaries" are the Sun and the Moon.</note> were hindered at the time of their birth.

<margin>N</margin>
16. He will not lose his senses in whose birth the Moon was moving toward Mercury.

<margin>N</margin>
17. When the benefics <note>original: "fortunae," referring to Jupiter and Venus</note> favor the birth, the native will be generous and beloved. If, however, the malefics <note>original: "infortunae," referring to Saturn and Mars</note> favor it, he will be greedy and abhorred.

<margin>N</margin>
18. He over whom Saturn presided in his birth will be filthy, and he over whom Mars presided will be foul-smelling.

<margin>M</margin> <note>M: Mors (Death)</note>
19. In whosever birth the malefics are in the eighth house <note>The eighth house in a chart governs death and inheritance.</note>, he shall die a bad death. If, however, the benefics are there, he is destined to pass away in his own bed.

<margin>N</margin>
20. He will not collect money, nor will he hoard treasure, unless the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 4th house are the same planet. Likewise, he will not gain money or riches, nor live splendidly, unless the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 10th house <note>The 10th house governs career and public standing.</note> are the same.

<margin>N</margin>
21. There can be no affection between two people unless the luminaries are exchanged in the root of their births <note>original: "in radice natiuitatis"</note>—that is, so that one is in the place of the other in the companion's birth. They are, however, hateful to one another who are born when the planets are in opposition, or in signs that are opposite, or in square aspects, or when the lords of the signs are in such a manner, or the luminaries behold each other in that way.

<margin>C</margin> <note>C: Cosmos/General conditions</note>
22. The Lord of the fifth circle <note>The "circles" likely refer to the planetary spheres; the 5th is Venus.</note>, namely Venus, signifies dampness and rain, just as the Lord of the sixth, namely Mercury, signifies journeys, changes, and pilgrimages.

<margin>E</margin> <note>E: Electiones (Choosing times)</note>
23. He who approaches a king when the Moon is in Aquarius will neither be received nor cared for by the king in any way. If, however, he approaches him when she is in Pisces, the king will turn his face away from him.

<margin>E</margin>
24. Bloodletting will not be good when the Moon is in Gemini; likewise, it will not be good to use cupping glasses on the belly when the Moon is in Taurus.

<margin>E</margin>
25. The best signs for taking laxatives and purgatives are the water signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note>; but of these, Scorpio is the best. Cancer, however, is considered the worst.

<margin>E</margin>
26. The best sign for partnerships is Leo. The worst, however, is Aries.

<margin>N</margin>
27. The fixed stars grant great gifts and raise one from poverty to a sublimity that the planets alone cannot achieve.

<margin>N</margin>
28. He will be a perfect physician in whose chart Mars and Venus are in the sixth house. He will be a good singer whose Mercury is retrograde with Venus in the same sign.

<margin>R</margin> <note>R: Rain/Weather</note>
29. The Lord of the fifth circle, namely Venus, when she is in the first degree of Cancer, will cause rain.

<margin>N</margin>
30. When the heavy planets <note>Saturn and Jupiter</note> are occidental to the Sun, they give integrity near the end of life; and vice versa.

<margin>N</margin>
31. He who buys anything while the Moon is between the head of Cancer and the end of Sagittarius will buy dear and sell cheap. It is the opposite, however, when she is from the beginning of Capricorn to the end of Gemini.

<margin>E</margin>
32. Circumcision is not good when the Moon is in Scorpio, just as vomiting is not good in Leo.

<margin>N</margin>
33. The nature of the sign in which Venus is placed will be attributed to the native. For when she is in Leo, she gives love; in Taurus, singing; and in Scorpio, sexual intercourse. The reason is: Leo governs the heart, Taurus the throat and neck, and Scorpio the genitals.

<margin>N</margin>
34. Whoever has Mercury in the twelfth house will be wise and a great philosopher.

<margin>N</margin>
35. If at the root of the birth the Moon is hindered, and all the Lords of the Triplicities <note>Groups of three signs belonging to the same element.</note> have fallen—namely the Hyleg <note>The planet that "gives life" or signifies the lifespan.</note>, and especially the first Lord of the Triplicity of the Ascendant—and if a benefic is in one of the angles, it indicates a short life for the native.

<margin>C</margin>
36. The Lord of the fifth circle, namely Venus, dissolves what the Lord of the third—which is Mars—binds. However, the Lord of the second—namely Jupiter—dissolves what the Lord of the first—namely Saturn—binds; and this significance is over great matters.

<margin>N</margin>
37. When all the Lords of the Triplicities fall, but one of the fixed stars of the first or second magnitude <note>Magnitude refers to the brightness and power of a star.</note>, which is of the same nature as the Lords of the Triplicities, is in one of the angles, it will benefit the native's upbringing and he will survive it.

<margin>N</margin>
38. When the malice of Mars falls upon the Moon while she is increasing in light, it is equal to that which falls upon her from the malice of Saturn

<column-break/>

while she is decreasing in light. This chapter signifies great things; and one will not be known to be a heretic except by the Lord of the second circle. And the Lord of the fourth circle signifies matters concerning kings.

<margin>N</margin>
39. In the elections of kings, the signs of the higher planets are commended; just as in the elections of the powerless, the signs of the lower planets are commended.

<margin>C</margin>
40. Those things which indicate a higher fortune are: Jupiter, the Part of Fortune, the Part of Giving, also the second house and whatever is in it and its Lord; likewise the Lord of the Triplicity of the luminary which has authority; and also the Lord of the tenth house and whatever is in it.

<margin>N</margin>
41. When the significator is between the Ascendant and the tenth house, it will be days and hours. When between the tenth and the seventh, it will be weeks and months. When between the seventh and the fourth, it will be years.

<margin>N</margin>
42. When the Lord of the first circle, namely Saturn, is in fixed signs <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>, he will cause mortality and scarcity; this the wise have experienced.

<margin>E</margin>
43. When you wish to choose a time for someone and you cannot delay: if the Moon is hindered, place the planet that is hindering her as the Lord of the Ascendant.

<margin>C</margin>
44. The best *ictisal* <note>term: "ictisal" (Arabic for 'connection' or 'application'), describing when a faster planet approaches a slower one</note> is in longitude and latitude. The benefics strengthen a good nature and make a bad nature trivial. The malefics, however, do the opposite.

<margin>C</margin>
45. Of whichever planet the nature is superior, its action will not cease until its return <note>The completion of its cycle back to its original position.</note> is there.

<margin>F</margin> <note>F: Fortitudo (Strength/Elections)</note>
46. When you cannot delay an election, place the Ascendant and its Lord in safety; also place the names of the benefics in an angle, and what is even better, in the tenth house.

<margin>E</margin>
Non nocet mars in peregrinationibus aquaz: sicut nec saturnus in peregrinationibus terraz.
Mars does no harm in journeys over water, just as Saturn does no harm in journeys over land.

<margin>F</margin>
47. In journeys, fixed signs are disparaged; however, movable signs are commended.

<margin>C</margin>
48. When a malefic aspects the significator and is retrograde and cadent <note>A "cadent" planet is in a weak house, away from the main angles of the chart.</note>, and also peregrine <note>term: "peregrine" (a planet with no essential dignity or "home" strength in its current position)</note> in the place where it is—that is, having no dignity of its own—and is in a sign contrary to its nature, it brings evil to the significator that no one can cure except God alone.

<margin>C</margin>
49. When Mars approaches the Earth, he is pacified with Jupiter; Saturn likewise is pacified with Venus; and when the Moon approaches the Earth, it is an ascension of two parts into one part.

<margin>C</margin>
50. The Moon only "remembers" <note>original: "recordatur," perhaps meaning harmonizes or reflects</note> when she is increased in light and number; every luminous star also harmonizes with her.

<margin>C</margin>
51. When Mars is weakened, Venus is comforted; just as Jupiter is when Saturn is weak. It diminishes the malice of the malefics when they are in any of their own dignities, and vice versa.

<margin>C</margin>
52. When a malefic receives a benefic <note>term: "reception" (when a planet is in a sign ruled by another)</note>, it will not hinder it; especially when it does not aspect it from a square or opposition, nor is in the same sign. The greatest hindrance of the parts is when they are in peregrine places.

<margin>C</margin>
53. Every planet, when joined with the Sun at the same point, moves there with haste; when it approaches the Sun, it goes step by step.

<margin>C</margin>
54. The strongest testimony is the *ictisal* (application) of the Moon to a planet that is in the Midheaven <note>The highest point of the chart.</note> or in the Ascendant.

<margin>C</margin>
55. Cancer is the significator over very moving waters; Scorpio over the running waters of streams; and Pisces over immobile waters, such as pools and wells.

<margin>I</margin> <note>I: Impetus (Quick actions)</note>
56. Every matter that is done quickly and destroyed quickly, and which is repeated, is under the signification of Mars.

<margin>C</margin>
57. Everything that is done quickly and suddenly destroyed, and remains destroyed for a long time, is of the nature of Saturn and Mars.

<margin>N</margin>
58. For whoever is of royal stock: if in the root of his birth there were two Suns <note>Perhaps referring to the Sun in a dominant position and a "solar" fixed star.</note>, he will be contrary to kings and will be separated from them in his works.

<margin>M</margin>
59. Whoever has the Moon at the hour of birth in Taurus at the minute of ascension, and the Sun in Leo in the Ascendant at the minute of ascension, shall arrive at great exaltation.

<margin>C</margin>
60. Those things which happen in this world are known and investigated from the great strength of the superior significator and from its elevation; and if that is not [clear], from the planet to which all other planets have gone.

<margin>N</margin>
If any of the planets signified something in the root of the birth, when the division and the Lord reach it, its sign will appear...

It covers topics ranging from physical health and character traits to the timing of rain and the behavior of kings based on planetary positions.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the numbered "Propositions" or astrological rules attributed to Almansor. # Propositions

61. ...fication, whether it be good or evil.
<margin>N</margin> <note>N: Nativitas (Birth rules)</note> 62. ¶ When the Lord of the 10th house moves backward (retrograde) from the <term>Ictisal</term> <note>original: "Ictisal," an Arabic astrological term for "application," where a faster planet approaches an aspect with a slower one.</note> of the Lord of the Ascendant, the native will not receive support from his superior. When the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are rising, and the two benefics <note>The "benefics" are Jupiter and Venus, planets thought to bring good luck.</note> likewise gaze upon each other, the native will be very strong and powerful, and no one shall ignore his command.
<margin>N</margin> 63. ¶ From the degree of the Ascendant, one knows the accidents of the body; from the degree of the Part of Fortune, one knows the substance of the soul. From the degree of the Moon, the shadows of the body depend. From the degree of the Sun, his health is known; but from the degree of the Midheaven <note>original: "medy celi," the highest point in the sky at birth, governing career.</note>, his mastery and works are distinguished. To each degree, give one year.
<margin>N</margin> 64. ¶ He will be fortunate and of good character, as well as powerful, whose year of revolution is similar to his birth chart (root), and whose celestial circle is in the same state in which it was in the year of his birth.
<margin>N</margin> 65. ¶ The daily life of the native is understood through direction; otherwise from the movement of the Lord; otherwise from day to day. The native's life is understood from the movement of the Lord of the sign of the year's profection <note>A technique where the chart is "turned" one sign per year.</note> within the established terms of the Lord of the sign of the <gloss>alynthe</gloss> <note>A term related to the calculation of the "hyleg" or life-giver.</note> of the year.
<margin>C</margin> <note>C: Combinations or General Rules</note> 66. ¶ When Saturn rises in the highest part of its circle (that is, at its apogee) and the Moon joins the Sun at the end of the month, and she moves toward him, it signifies an increase in whatever matter belongs to the nature of the sign in which he resides.
<margin>C</margin> 67. ¶ When a planet is in the very minute of the degree of the eastern horizon, and the Moon is joined to it in that same place, the natural action of that planet will appear, whether it be good or evil.
<margin>C</margin> 68. ¶ When any planet rules a particular year (among the years of the world), its significance will appear in that degree where the Moon is exalted; then a king shall be elevated in that region and in the climate signified by it.
<margin>N</margin> 69. ¶ The hindrance of Mercury by Saturn is said to impede the tongue of the native, or make it worse if they are joined together bodily.
<margin>Q</margin> <note>Q: Questio (Inquiry/Horary rules)</note> 70. ¶ How great will be the fear for a sick person when the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> are below the earth at the hour of the inquiry.
<margin>N</margin> 71. ¶ When both luminaries are in the same degree of their exaltation in their own dominion, free from the malefics <note>Saturn and Mars.</note>, the native will be a king of the whole world; his seed shall inherit his lands and hold them for a long time.
<margin>N</margin> 72. ¶ When the Ascendant of a birth is the Midheaven of the world, and the sign is a "moveable" one—namely Aries or Cancer—and the degree upon the line of the Midheaven is the same degree in which the Sun or Jupiter is exalted, his name shall be spread across the whole earth, and his fame shall be made known.
<margin>C</margin> 73. ¶ These are the things to be prepared (or adapted from them): the Ascendant, the Part of Fortune, the luminaries, the signs of their conjunction and their Lords, the Lord of the hour, and also the location of the thing sought and its Lords.
<margin>P</margin> <note>P: Profectiones (Yearly progressions)</note> 74. ¶ From the Lord of the exaltation and the dividers, as well as the Lord of the other dividers of the rays, and from the Lord of the year—and from the movement of the planets in their places and their aspects—the accidents of the world are known in the revolutions of the years.
<margin>N</margin> 75. ¶ When the Lord of the 10th house is in the 8th house <note>The house of death.</note>, it is feared that the mother of the native will die from that birth.
<margin>C</margin> 76. ¶ When the Lord of the 4th house is hindered by the Lord of the Ascendant, there will be fear for the father of the native.
<margin>N</margin> 77. ¶ A planet is of no use when the Lord of the Ascendant is in a "fortunate" place but moving backward (retrograde), or hidden under the Sun's rays; likewise, if he is with the 7th house or its Lord, the one who first began to fight will prevail in battle.
78. ¶ A malefic planet heats its own place and hinders it; the Sun, however, heats but does not hinder.
<margin>E</margin> <note>E: Electiones (Choosing the right time)</note> 79. ¶ Take care that a king does not go out to battle when the Lord of the Ascendant is going toward the Lord of the 7th house <note>The 7th house represents the enemy in war.</note>.
<margin>R</margin> <note>R: Res (General Matters)</note> 80. ¶ When Mars is with the Sun in the northern signs, there will be greatest heat; similarly, when the Sun goes to Saturn in the southern signs, there will be greatest cold, and vice versa.
<margin>N</margin> 81. ¶ When the malefics reach a certain place, they will not do harm if their significance was not present in the "root" (the birth chart); likewise, the benefics will not help when there is no significance from them in the root.
<margin>R</margin> 82. ¶ Impediments that are to come in the years of the profection will happen when the "year of the world" reaches the bodies of the malevolent planets; give one year to each sign.
<margin>C</margin> 83. ¶ The misfortune of Saturn is greater when it is in feminine signs; but that of Mars is greater when it is in masculine signs.
<margin>E</margin> 84. ¶ No one should attack a city whose Lord is the Lord of the Ascendant of the year of the world.

<column-break/>

<margin>E</margin> 85. ¶ It is necessary in every undertaking to adapt the celestial circle to the nature of that which one is about to begin.
<margin>C</margin> 86. ¶ The <term>Ictisal</term> <note>Application (moving toward an aspect).</note> of the Moon to Mars from the houses of Venus is not commended; nor to Jupiter from the houses of Saturn and Mercury; nor to the Sun from the houses of Saturn.
<margin>C</margin> 87. ¶ It is among the greater fortunes when planets are diurnal (of the day) and eastern of the sun in masculine signs; and when nocturnal planets are western of the moon.
<margin>C</margin> 88. ¶ When the Lords of the triplicity <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element (Fire, Earth, Air, or Water).</note> of the luminary of the day are diurnal and eastern, and those of the night are nocturnal and western, and they are increased in light, it shall be a great sign of fortune and happiness.
<margin>C</margin> 89. ¶ The Eastern point (Ascendant) signifies children, youths, and the beginnings of all things; the Midheaven signifies kings, lords of the law, judges, and leaders of battles. The Seventh house signifies the elderly and the deceased, as well as women, enemies, and all things of beauty. The Angle of the Earth (4th house) signifies fathers and lands, and the place where an infant is born; it also demonstrates the hour of death and the grave.
<margin>N</margin> 90. ¶ The planets that give great riches are three: namely Jupiter, the Sun, and Mercury.
91. ¶ Every undertaking by one who has great wealth must be weighed; in all mid-points where a conjunction or prevention is hindered, let him beware of this.
<margin>R</margin> 92. ¶ A universal question is like a birth; therefore, revolve its years and judge upon them.
<margin>N</margin> 93. ¶ Saturn rejoices in Aquarius; likewise Jupiter in Pisces; Mars also rejoices in Scorpio; Venus in Libra; and Mercury in Virgo.
<margin>N</margin> 94. ¶ If the <gloss>Heuçahar</gloss> <note>The Dragon's Head, or North Node of the Moon.</note> adds to the nature of every planet that is with it, so the Tail <note>The Dragon's Tail, or South Node.</note> diminishes the nature of every planet that is with it.
<margin>N</margin> 95. ¶ The strongest significance over the being of the father is the firstborn; and those who follow will likewise give some significance.
96. ¶ The <term>Algebuthar</term> <note>The planet with the most dignity or "power" in a specific matter.</note> is stronger in the case of life. The <term>Alcocoden</term> <note>The planet that "gives years" and determines the length of life.</note>, however, is stronger in other matters. The Lord of the Rays is stronger than the <gloss>algebuthas</gloss>, and perhaps they will be equally strong.
<margin>N</margin> 97. ¶ When a native dies before one day and one night have passed, he is as one aborted, and shall have no significance in anything.
<margin>N</margin> 98. ¶ Kings whose business is done quickly, and who avenge themselves quickly, and who quickly fulfill what they desire, are those whose Ascendant in the beginning of their reign was a fire sign; and similarly the Midheaven—or if one was fire and the other was air.
<margin>N</margin> 99. ¶ When the Lord of the Ascendant is in a good place in the "terms" of a benefic, and the Lord of that term is bound to him in good standing, it will give him integrity, a kingdom, and every good thing.
<margin>N</note> 100. ¶ When a significator is in the Midheaven, it shall be directed through the rising of the "direct circle." In the Ascendant, however, through the rising of the specific region. In what lies between the two, through both; this specific chapter was narrated by <term>Alchindus</term> <note>Al-Kindi (c. 801–873 AD), a famous Arab philosopher and astrologer.</note>.
<margin>N</margin> 101. ¶ It is a sign of fortune and prosperity when the Lord of the Sun's house, the Lord of the Moon's house, and the Lord of the Ascendant are eastern, are in the "angles" (the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses), and look upon each other from good places—that is, from a trine or sextile aspect.
<margin>N</margin> 102. ¶ He is very powerful whose Sun is in the Midheaven in a fire sign, and the Moon is in Taurus, with her aspect being on the left side.
<margin>N</margin> 103. ¶ Those who are very rich and will abound in wealth, and are of great name, are those for whom the Lord of the 2nd house <note>The house of money and possessions.</note> is in its exaltation or its own house, moving toward the Lord of the Ascendant; especially so if it is Jupiter.
<margin>N</margin> 104. ¶ The life of all living things is according to the degrees of the Sun and Moon; and this is given from the highest according to the <gloss>astapha</gloss> <note>Likely referring to the "stationary" points or specific planetary positions.</note>.
105. ¶ When a benefic is in the places of Mars, and the significator goes toward it, or it toward the significator, it cuts off [the good] just as the malefics do.
<margin>N</margin> 106. ¶ Turn your eyes away from a chart in which Mars is in an angle, especially when the Ascendant is Scorpio.
<margin>E</margin> 107. ¶ When someone wishes to take something away, if the significator is looking at Saturn, he will take it away with great difficulty.
<margin>C</margin> 108. ¶ If someone requests something while the Head <note>The North Node.</note> is in the Midheaven with Jupiter, and the Moon is moving toward him—or if, having separated from him, she goes to the Lord of the Ascendant—or if the Lord of the Ascendant goes toward him: he shall not fail to obtain what he seeks shortly.
<margin>E</margin> 109. ¶ It is not good for one wishing to wage war, nor for a king making a journey, when the Lord... <note>Text cut off at bottom of page</note>

<meta>This page continues the numbered astrological aphorisms (Propositions) of Almansor. The previous page concluded with Proposition 108 regarding the vitality and strength of the "native" (the subject of the horoscope). This page completes the text with observations on war, rumors, planetary cycles, and the specific configurations that produce prophets or kings, ending with a formal colophon by the translator Plato of Tivoli.</meta>

### Almansor’s Propositions

<margin>t</margin> ¶ ...of the ascending [sign]: and in the eighth [house]: and if it should be in its exaltation. 109. <note>original: "exaltatione," a sign where a planet's influence is most powerful.</note>
<margin>t</margin> ¶ The Sun is not good in the ascendant at the hour of war: nor with the lord of the ascendant: unless the ascending sign be Aries or Leo. 110.
<margin>Q</margin> ¶ In that part where the Sun and Moon are made fortunate: victory shall be for those who petition: as if they form an aspect from the ascendant all the way to the <term>midheaven</term> <note>the highest point in the sky</note>: or from the ascendant to the fourth [house], the seeker shall win; if it be in other places: the adversary shall overcome. 111.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ It must be considered a greatest impediment <note>original: "ipedit̃ũ," obstacle</note> that things are in the power of a sign in which a planet is falling: or retrograde <note>appearing to move backward</note>, or in a bad position relative to the Sun. 112.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ Signs signify bodies: Planets truly signify those things which move the bodies: the locations of the planets in the circle and their substances: and their locations from the Sun signify work and destruction. 113.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ In whosever birth Jupiter shall be the receiver of the strengths of all planets: and if he himself should commend them and his own strength to Saturn: and should be received by him: and moreover be oriental and ascending in an <term>angle</term> <note>one of the four most powerful houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th</note>: the native shall be great and powerful in this world: and also be of good character: even his name shall rise in the world. 114.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ Beware lest Saturn be with the lord of the ascendant or in other places of exaltation: for he is worse than the <term>Tail</term> <note>The "Dragon's Tail" or South Node of the Moon, considered a point of depletion.</note>. 115.
<margin>Q</margin> ¶ Rumors are true if the signs of the angles of the news are fixed signs: and the Moon and Mercury are in fixed signs: and if the Moon also has separated from the <term>benefics</term> <note>Jupiter and Venus, the "lucky" planets</note>: and also if a benefic be in any of the angles: when you find it thus, this indication neither fails nor can it fail. 116.
<margin>t</margin> ¶ The first hour of the day until the completion of three hours belongs to the blood. The second three to red choler. The third to black choler. But the last three to phlegm: and similarly in the night. It is the same way in the quarters of the lunar month. Moreover, the quarters of the year belong to the Sun. 117. <note>This links the four humors of the body—blood, yellow bile, black bile, and phlegm—to the hours of the day and cycles of the moon and year.</note>
<margin>N</margin> ¶ He whose lord of the ascendant is to the right of the Sun: and is elevated above it: that is, it holds victory and already completes its "orientality," so to speak: he shall be a friend of kings and powerful men: also rich and of great name. 118.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ Do not hasten in judging when planets are joined: unless you first consider the nature of the sign: in which they are shining. Whether it be of their likeness: or not. For if it be of their likeness, you shall strengthen their indication. 119.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ When the lord of the 2nd [house] of the ascendant: or the 2nd of the Moon: or the 2nd of the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>a calculated point representing prosperity</note> is surrounded by benefics, he shall be more fortunate than any other. 120.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ When two <term>malefics</term> <note>Saturn and Mars, the "unlucky" planets</note> are in the 4th degree of the house and in the same term, the native shall be unfortunate: and exceedingly miserable. 121.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ When planets are in the angles, those things which are signified by them shall appear: whether it be good: or bad: the indication of every 4th circle is a year. But of the seventh circle it is a month. 122.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ When the angles of the ascendant are <term>movable signs</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note> and two malefics are in the angles: the whole life of the native shall be miserable. 123.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ When the Moon is in the angles, it shall strengthen its whole indication, especially if it has any authority in the ascendant. 124.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ A sudden change cannot be except from Mars: just as a great delay cannot be except from Saturn. 125.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ The state of all good things changes from good to bad: or from bad to good. When the signs and figures of the planets change: which signify over them, from ascent into descent and vice versa. 126.
<margin>R</margin> ¶ Jupiter and Saturn change things and overturn them: and it shall be the beginning of variation. When they change from one <term>triplicity</term> <note>a group of three signs belonging to the same element</note> to another: in conjunctions: and from one figure into another. 127.
<margin>e</margin> ¶ There are two better conjunctions: one of which is of the luminaries [Sun and Moon]. The other is of the two heavy planets [Jupiter and Saturn]: masculine planets are those which act: feminine ones are those upon which it is acted: and similarly also in the signs. 128.
<margin>R</margin> ¶ Look to the ascension of the planet and the degree of its exaltation and the degree of its fall <note>original: "casus," the sign where a planet is weakest</note>. For these are what signify people and their works. 129.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ If you find a significator in the angles that is masculine and in a masculine sign: and the contrary significator feminine: and in a feminine sign. He whose sign is masculine and in a masculine sign shall act upon him, that is, he shall overcome the other. 130.

<column-break/>

<margin>c</margin> ¶ Indications are in two modes substantially: namely, and accidentally: and in both ways they shall signify the number of the seven planets. 131.
<margin>R</margin> ¶ When two malefics join: and the Moon with Saturn in latitude, there shall be famine and death. If truly with Mars, kings shall change and there shall be much shedding of blood and battles in the place which shall be signified by that sign, and this does not fail. 132.
<margin>R</margin> ¶ From the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter in movable signs, the change of the state and the world shall be known: and again from their conjunctions in fixed signs. 133.
<margin>R</margin> ¶ When two benefics join and the Moon joins Jupiter in latitude, there shall be justice: and it shall direct matters on earth. If however to Venus, there shall be liveliness: joy: health of bodies and prosperity. 134.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ When Venus and Mars are in the same point with the Sun in the place of Venus and her term: the words of the native shall be received by men: and shall be rejected by none. 135.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ A hermit and as if a prophet: also one whose words are received, is he in whose birth Jupiter and Venus are in the same degree with the Sun. 136.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ Famous kings in this world: and those whose commands are not despised: are those whose Jupiter and Moon are in the same point of the ascendant at their apogee <note>original: "augem," their highest or most distant point in orbit</note>. 137.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ He in whom there is the greatest vigor and great power is he for whom the Sun is in the midheaven with Saturn in a masculine sign, oriental. 138.
<margin>Q</margin> ¶ When the Moon and other significators are moved from the angles, they shall not complete those things themselves unless it be from travel and from nothing else. 139.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ When there is no <term>ictisal</term> aspect <note>original: "ictisal," an Arabic term for the application or joining of planetary influences</note> between any of the planets and the significator, and both are in the same circle: or from parallel circles in the <term>nadir</term> <note>the point directly opposite a celestial position</note> or <term>anabat</term> <note>likely a transliteration of an Arabic term for "ascent" or a specific direction</note> or in the equinoctial path, it shall be better than an aspect of application. 140.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ Every planet has two signs except for the luminaries: of which each has only one house: because their light is the darkness of Saturn: Therefore their houses are placed as contraries. 141. <note>Sun and Moon rule one sign each (Leo and Cancer), while the other planets rule two.</note>
<margin>c</margin> ¶ Benefics are faithful and prosperous when they are in their places of exaltation and direct: as well as increased in light. 142.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ In the great and exalted riches of kings, or in their beginnings, it is praised that the luminaries be in the terms of the benefics gazing upon one another and that every one of the terms be from the nature of the matter being started. 143.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ The matters of the circle which encompass all things: and which are greatest: are seven: from which the first of the creation of men is the year of the great Sun: and they are 1. 4. 1. 0. <note>These digits likely refer to a specific astronomical cycle or year date.</note> Moreover when any beginning ascends in the term of the ascendant of the root of any inception and finds two minutes of the two heavy planets. Second, the hour of the year in which they join in the signs: the Ascendant of the revolution of the year of the world: also the Ascendant of the conjunction or prevention: which will happen also in the hour of birth or of the question. 144.
<margin>N</margin> ¶ No good or evil will happen to anyone: unless when the nature or likeness of the triplicity of the signs of the planets changes, which are the significators of that place. 145.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ When two climates differ, the aspect of the planets and their rays differ. 146.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ When two latitudes truly differ: the circles of its circular motion differ. Moreover, in this chapter, no one has spoken so perfectly. 147.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ The impediments of the two <term>nodes</term> <note>the points where the Moon's orbit crosses the Sun's path</note> are worse for the inferior planets than for the superior. 148.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ The figure of the circle in questions is of great likeness to the likeness of the soul of the seeker. 149.
<margin>c</margin> ¶ When Jupiter is in Aries, moving direct without a bad aspect of the benefics, he shall give strength and a kingdom in which no injustice shall be done. 150.

Sahl was a prominent 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician who wrote in Arabic; this text represents the Latin medieval tradition that brought his work to Europe.</meta>

# The beginning of the introductory book on the principles of judgments by Sahl the Ishmaelite.
## On the division of the signs and on the triplicities. Chapter 1.

<image-desc>Large decorative initial box featuring a drop cap 'I' surrounded by floral motifs, with several lines of text contained within the same bordered space.</image-desc>
<insert>
In the name of God, the pious and merciful. Sahl ben Bishr the Ishmaelite said: Know that there are 12 signs, and of these, 6 are masculine and 6 are feminine. Aries, therefore, is a masculine sign among the signs of the day, and Taurus is feminine among the signs of the night; and similarly, a feminine sign follows a masculine one until the end of the signs.
</insert>
And of these, six are signs of direct ascension—that is, possessing a straight rising—and six are of tortuous ascension—that is, a crooked rising. And the signs of direct ascension are from the beginning of Cancer to the end of Sagittarius, because the latitude of each of them is greater than its longitude, and they rise in more than two equal hours; for this reason, they are called directly ascending. And the signs of tortuous ascension are from the beginning of Capricorn to the end of Gemini, because the latitude of each of them is less than its longitude, and they rise in less than two equal hours; for this reason, they are called tortuously ascending. And of these, 4 are called "mobile" <note>modern astrologers call these "cardinal" signs</note>: namely Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; and they are called mobile because when the sun enters the beginnings of those signs, the season changes into the substance of the following season. And 4 of them are "fixed": namely Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; and they are called fixed because when the sun enters their degrees, the season is fixed in its essence and does not change—that is, if it was hot, it will be hot; if it was cold, it will be cold; if it was spring, it will be spring; and if it was autumn, it will be autumn. And of these, there are four "common" <note>also known as mutable signs</note> which are called *deue* in Arabic <note>original: "deue," likely a corruption of the Arabic "dhu-jasadayn," meaning "two-bodied"</note> and *deyn* in Greek <note>original: "deyn," likely "disōmos," also meaning "two-bodied"</note>—that is, they are called "of two bodies"; these are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces. And they are called common because when the sun reaches the middle of them, the weather is mixed, such that its first half may be hot and the other cold, or the first half cold and the other hot. And some of them are called "quadrupeds": namely Aries, Taurus, Leo, Capricorn, and the end of Sagittarius. Among these signs, some are fiery: namely Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius, and this is the first triplicity. And the second triplicity is earthy, and they signify whatever is in the earth or born from the earth: namely Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. And the third triplicity is airy, and it signifies men and winds and whatever might be in the air: namely Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius. The fourth is aquatic [watery], and it signifies waters and whatever is in the waters: namely Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. And some of the signs are called "dark": namely Libra and Capricorn. And there is a certain place in the signs called "combust" <note>literally "burnt," referring to the Via Combusta, a specific stretch of the zodiac considered difficult or unpredictable</note>, which is the end of Libra and the beginning of Scorpio. And some of these signs have a "half-voice" <note>original: "oĩmidiã vocẽ"</note>: namely Virgo, Capricorn, and Aquarius. And some of them have "voices": namely Taurus, Aries, Gemini, Leo, Libra, and Sagittarius. And among them, some are "without voices": namely Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. And some are "half" or "common" in the procreation of children—that is, they are neither entirely fertile nor entirely sterile: namely Taurus, Gemini, and Aquarius. And some bring many children: namely Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. Some, however, are sterile: Aries, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius, and Capricorn. And some of them signify mountains and more difficult places: namely Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. And some signify habitable and flat places—that is, rural areas and those that have been cultivated: namely Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. Others, however, signify sandy places: Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius. Some also signify humid and watery places, or those that are near water: namely Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. Therefore, the fiery signs signify fires and all substance pertaining to or made by fire, and they signify nobles. And the signs of seeds <note>the earthy signs</note> signify the earth and everything that is raised from the earth. The aquatic signs signify humid places and every work involving moisture. And the signs that produce many children signify gatherings of men. The triplicity of Aries [Fire], then, is hot and dry; it possesses by nature red bile <note>one of the four humors</note> and represents the East among the parts of the world. The lords of this triplicity are the Sun by day and Jupiter by night, and their partner by day and night is Saturn. The triplicity of Taurus [Earth]

<column-break/>

is cold and dry; it possesses by nature black bile and represents the South among the parts of the world. Its lords are Venus by day and the Moon by night, and their partner by day and night is Mars. The triplicity of Gemini [Air] is hot and moist; and by nature it possesses blood <note>the sanguine humor</note> and represents the West among the parts of the world. The lords of this triplicity are Saturn by day and Mercury by night; their partner also by day and night is Jupiter. The triplicity of Cancer [Water], however, is cold and moist; it possesses by nature phlegm and represents the North among the parts of the world. The lords of this triplicity are Venus by day and Mars by night; their partner by day and night is the Moon.

### Chapter on the substances of the twelve signs, and what every sign signifies.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'S' with white strapwork on a dark background within a square border.</image-desc>
Know that we find for every interrogation <note>a question asked of an astrologer</note> or sought-after matter a sign by which is signified whatever good or evil may be in that same interrogation, according to the methods explained by the sages regarding the significance of questions and matters from the substances of the twelve signs and the natures of the seven planets and the houses from which matters are taken, just as the planets have their own natures and significations, which we intend to describe, God willing.

### The first house of the ascendant and everything in it concerning interrogations and other matters from the twelve signs.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'P' with white strapwork on a dark background.</image-desc>
The first house, the beginning of which rises or ascends in the East at the hour of an interrogation, or a birth, or the beginning of any work. This signifies life and death, because it is the ascendant of that life with which one's life enters the world when leaving the mother's womb. For this sign rises from the lower part of the earth to its upper parts, as if from darkness into light; and similarly, the newborn leaves the darkness of the womb for the light of this age, and from the narrowness of the uterus to the expanse of the air. It reveals the questioner's inquiry from the secret of their heart; what was previously hidden shines forth and is made open. It signifies, therefore, bodies and life, and every beginning and movement of the body, and whatever might happen from any accident, as well as the initiation or outcome of every matter, and every mobile thing, whether rational, and the beginning of all things.

### Concerning the second house.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'S' with white strapwork.</image-desc>
The second house from the ascendant does not behold the ascending sign <note>it does not form a traditional aspect like a trine or square</note>. It signifies the gathering of substance, the maintenance of life, those who serve, as well as takings and givings [possessions].

### Concerning the 3rd house.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'T' with white strapwork.</image-desc>
The third house, which does not entirely fall away from the ascendant, signifies brothers and sisters, neighbors and kinsmen and their condition; also patience and counsel, faith and religion, disputes in sects, letters, embassies and messengers, as well as pilgrimages and dreams.

### Concerning the 4th house.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'Q' with white strapwork.</image-desc>
The fourth house, however, being the "angle of the earth" <note>the Imum Coeli, the lowest point of the chart</note>, signifies fathers and their condition, origins and roots, ancestry and prisons, lands and rural areas, villages and cities, and every building, every roof, and anything hidden—whether hidden treasures or mountains—and what will happen after death—that is, what happens to the deceased regarding burial, whether the body is dug up, cremated, placed on a gallows, or cast out in some place, and other things that happen to the dead. It signifies their end, as well as houses and lands—that is, inheritances and everything buried under the earth.

### Concerning the 5th house.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'Q' with white strapwork.</image-desc>
The fifth house follows the angle of the earth and is the place of love, because it is of the same triplicity and joy as the ascendant. It signifies children and everything in which there is trust; also messengers and gifts, honor and the petitioning of women, friendships and friends, cities and the condition of their citizens, and the fruits of inheritance.

### Concerning the 6th house.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'S' with white strapwork.</image-desc>
The sixth house is "falling" from the ascendant and does not behold it. It is a malignant place and signifies illnesses—both curable and incurable—and the causes of illnesses, as well as servants and maidservants, injustices, and moves from place to place.

### Concerning the 7th house.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'S' with white strapwork.</image-desc>
The seventh house is the "western angle" <note>the descendant</note> and signifies marriages, legal matters, disputes, partnerships, and agreements made between two people; also the person who seeks and who...

<margin>¶ On the 8th house.</margin>
### The eighth house follows the western angle <note>In astrology, "succedent" houses follow the "angular" houses</note> and signifies death and killing and lethal poisons: and fear: and whatever is inherited from the dead: and everything that perishes through labor and sadness; also wars and contentions and handmaidens or the helpers of adversaries or of those in conflict; and also things entrusted: that is, those which are handed over for safekeeping: and the management of estates, laziness, and cleverness.

<margin>¶ On the 9th house.</margin>
### The ninth house is <term>cadent<gloss>falling away</gloss></term> from the ascendant and signifies pilgrimages and journeys and the worship of the deity: and all houses of religion: philosophy and the perfection of all things: the wisdom of the stars <note>original: sapiam astroꝝ; referring to astrology</note>: and divinations: letters and envoys and embassies: or rumors: dreams: faith: and divine wisdom: and holiness as well as religion: and all things past and receding: and the path from honor or the work of one's purpose: and things of the future, namely the foreknowledge of future events.

<margin>¶ On the 10th house.</margin>
### The tenth house is the angle of heaven <note>The Midheaven or Medium Coeli</note>: and it signifies the king or the kingdom, exaltation and empire: glory: and memory: or the voice of praise: also mothers and substance that has been stolen or taken away: judges: princes and the prelates of all: and every form of mastery or profession.

<margin>¶ On the 11th house.</margin>
### The eleventh house follows the angle of heaven and signifies friends: trust and fortune: the substance of the king and his revenues or tributes: and his soldiers and attendants: and the power that succeeds a king or prince by hand: and it signifies praises and children.

<margin>¶ On the 12th house.</margin>
### The twelfth house is cadent from the ascendant and does not "behold" it <note>It forms no major geometric aspect to the 1st house</note>: it signifies enemies and labors: lamentations and sadness: whisperings: deceits: envies and cunning, malevolence and pilgrimages: malice: labors: prisons: and beasts.

<margin>¶ On the division of the circle and the dignities or strengths of the houses.</margin>
### The more worthy and more laudable places of the orbital circle, following one another in order of strength, are distinguished as follows. The circle is divided into 12 signs: of which four are called angles: that is, the ascending sign, the 4th, the 7th, and the 10th. These signs are like the corners of heaven which signify everything that is present among things: that is, the presence of matters and strength in every thing. From these, 4 are called "succedent" or following the angles: that is, those ascending after them: the 2nd, 5th, 8th, and 11th. These signify everything that is in the future: and whatever is being made: and succeeds from things. And the remaining four are called "cadent" from the angles because they have receded and fallen away from the corners: which are the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th. These signify whatever has receded and departed from things by the will of God. The strongest of all places in the circle is the ascendant: and its sign is worthier than all signs: and a planet that is in it is stronger than all planets: and especially if that same planet is in its own house or in its <term>exaltation<gloss>a sign where a planet's influence is heightened</gloss></term> or <term>triplicity<gloss>a group of three signs of the same element</gloss></term> or in its <term>term<gloss>a specific degree range within a sign</gloss></term> or in its <term>face<gloss>a ten-degree segment of a sign</gloss></term>. Then the angle of heaven <note>10th house</note> follows in strength: then follows the western angle: that is, the seventh from the ascendant: then follows the angle of the earth: that is, the 4th from the ascendant. After these, the 11th house from the ascendant follows this house in strength: and after this the 5th house, then the 9th. These seven places are more laudable and stronger: the 1st place is better than the 2nd, the 2nd better than the 3rd, and so on. After these, those signs which are known to be good are chosen. The 2nd sign from the ascendant, because it is the place of the "Joy of the Moon." Then the second place from the ascendant: because it rises after the ascendant. In the 8th sign from the ascendant there is impediment and great misfortune: because it is the house of death: and it does not behold the ascendant. The remaining signs of the circle, namely the 6th and 12th, are worse than all places and inferior: and any planet that is in these places will have no perfection: because the 6th sign from the ascendant is the place of infirmities and vices and of all diseases, both separable and inseparable: and it is cadent from the ascendant: nor does it behold it: and it is the place of the "Joy of Mars." And the 12th from the ascendant is the place of enemies and labor and sadness: and it is cadent from the ascendant;

<column-break/>

nor does it behold it: and it is the place of the "Joy of Saturn." For that planet <note>Saturn</note> rejoices in lamentation and weeping and tribulation. And note that every sign "beholds" the 3rd before itself: and the 3rd after itself which is the 11th: and this aspect is called <term>sextile</term>: because it holds the sixth part of the circle: that is, 60 degrees out of the 360 degrees of the whole circle. For example, a planet that is at the beginning of Aries beholds that which is in Gemini before it: and that which is in Aquarius after it. And it beholds the 4th before it and the 4th after it (that is, the 10th): and this aspect is called <term>quartus</term> <note>the square aspect</note>: because it holds a fourth part of the circle: that is, 90 degrees. Each also beholds the 5th before it and the 5th after it (that is, the 9th): and this aspect is called <term>trine</term>: because it holds a 3rd part of the circle: namely, 120 degrees. It also beholds the 7th by <term>opposition</term>: and this is an aspect of enmity: and if a planet is in these signs, they are said to behold one another.

<margin>¶ On the aspects of the planets.</margin>
### These are the aspects of the planets: that is, conjunction, sextile: and square, trine, as well as opposite. For a <term>conjunction</term> is when two planets are joined in one sign: and there are 12 degrees or less between them: and this is the limit of a conjunction. A sextile aspect is from the 3rd sign and from the 11th. A square aspect is from the 4th sign and the 10th. A trine aspect is from the 5th sign and the 9th. Indeed, the opposite aspect is from the 7th sign. Therefore, among these aspects, the conjunction and the opposition are stronger and have more powerful effect and enmity: these aspects signify enemies openly causing harm: and they signify partnerships and participations. The square aspect is medium: that is, it does not entirely uncover enmities. And the second sextile aspect: that is, the one made from the 11th, is stronger than the first sextile aspect. And the second square aspect: that is, the one made from the 10th, is stronger than the first square aspect: and among the trine aspects, the 9th house (that is, the second aspect) is stronger than the first trine aspect: and this aspect is called <term>elevation</term>: that is, higher. Those signs which are "disjunct" do not behold one another: nor does a planet in them behold another; they are these: the 2nd, 6th, 8th, and 12th signs. All others besides these behold one another.

<margin>¶ On the effect and detriment of the planets.</margin>
### Know that whether the stars signify something to be done or not, it happens in 16 modes: and they have <term>Alichel</term> in Arabic: which in Latin sounds like "perfection" <note>Arabic: al-ittiṣāl, application/perfection</note>. <term>Alibd</term>: that is, "deterioration" <note>Arabic: al-iṭ’ām, corruption</note>. <term>Alcitfal</term>: that is, "conjunction." <term>Alinciraf</term>: that is, "separation" or the disjunction of planets from their conjunction. <term>Annael</term>: that is, "translation." <term>Algemee</term>: that is, "gathering" or "collection": which sounds better. <term>Almenei</term>: that is, "forbidding" or "prohibition." <term>Alcohol</term>: that is, "reception." <term>Hairalcobol</term>: that is, "non-reception." <term>Halaacen</term>: that is, "void of course" <note>original: euacuatio cursus; when a planet makes no further aspects before leaving a sign</note>. <term>Airebad</term>: that is, "return." <term>Dapha alchia</term>: that is, "pushing of power." <term>Dapha aredir</term>: that is, "pushing of disposition and nature." <term>Alcidetib</term>: that is, "virtue" or "fortitude." <term>Adof</term>: that is, "debility." <term>Uanuelhalcamar</term>: that is, "the state of the Moon."

<margin>¶ Explanation of alichel.</margin>
### <term>Alichel</term> is when a planet is in an angle or in a house following an angle. <term>Alibd</term> is when a planet is cadent from the angles. <term>Alcitfal</term> is when a light and swift planet seeks a conjunction with another slower and heavier planet: and if the swifter planet is within fewer degrees and the slower one has been there for a long time: until it joins with it: and it is in such a minute through an aspect. <term>Mutatil</term>: that is, "joined" or "glued together," it is called so until it separates from it by the space of one degree: and then it is called <term>iuerisafif</term>: that is, "it separates from it." But if planets are joined in one sign: a planet is not said to be separated from another until it passes it by the space of half its orb: that is, of its light: because every planet has an orb of light: and particular parts: and half of those same parts is before the planet itself: and the other half after it: in which space, while the planet passes another, it is called "separated" from it.

<margin>¶ Knowledge of the lights or orbs of the planets.</margin>
### Know that the orb of the light of the Sun is 30 degrees: the half of which is before it: that is, 15 degrees before the Sun itself: and 15 degrees behind. When there are between the Sun and any of the planets degrees from one up to 15, then it casts its light upon it and joins with it. And the light of the Moon is 12 degrees before and 12 behind: and the light of Venus and Mercury is 7 degrees before and 7 behind for each of them; by the quantity of this light, one planet joins to another. The light of Saturn and Jupiter is 9 degrees before and 9 behind for each of them. The light of Mars, however, is 8 degrees before and 8 behind. When a planet beholds another and strikes its degree with its light, it is seen to be joined to it: and unless it strikes it with its light, it is not called "joined" to it: but "going to a conjunction" until it begins to be joined to it: and if a planet should be in the end...

### ¶ An exposition on the recession or separation of the planets.

The **Exposition** of the recession <note>The movement of a planet away from another</note> or separation of planets occurs when a <term>lighter planet<gloss>a faster-moving planet, like the Moon or Mercury</gloss></term> passes another <term>weightier planet<gloss>a slower-moving planet, like Saturn or Jupiter</gloss></term>, and begins to have a greater degree both in aspect and in conjunction. For an aspect is from sign to sign, but a conjunction is said to be from degree to degree. This science is according to **Messahallab** <note>original: "Messahallab"; referring to the 8th-century astrologer Masha'allah ibn Athari</note>, whose name means "he whom God willed to be a master."

### ¶ On the translation of light.

**Translation** of light from planet to planet occurs when a lighter planet separates from one weightier planet and joins to another; then it effectively joins them and carries the nature of the first to the other to which it is joined. An example of this: suppose the <term>ascendant<gloss>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term> is Virgo, and a question is asked regarding marriage. The Moon is at the 10th degree of Gemini, Mercury is at the 8th degree of Leo, and Jupiter is at the 13th degree of Pisces. The Lord of the Ascendant <note>Mercury, who rules Virgo</note>, who signifies the person asking the question, did not "see" <note>An "aspect" or line of sight in astrology</note> Jupiter, who is the Lord of the house of marriage <note>The 7th House, ruled by Pisces/Jupiter</note>, because Mercury was in the eighth sign from him. Look then to the Moon, which I found at the 10th degree of Gemini, having separated from Mercury and joined to Jupiter; she carried the light between the two. This signified the successful completion of the matter—that is, the receiving of the wife—through the hands of messengers and those running between the two parties.

**[Astrological Chart: A square chart showing the Moon at 10° Gemini, Mercury at 8° Leo, and Jupiter at 15° Pisces. The signs are arranged counter-clockwise from Taurus to Aries.]**

### ¶ On the collection of the light of the planets.

**Collection** of light <note>original: "Coniunctio luminis"; often called 'collection' in English astrology</note> occurs when the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the matter being asked about both join a planet weightier than themselves, which collects their strength and light and receives their natures. For example: a certain question was asked regarding a King, whether he would acquire a kingdom or not. The ascendant was Libra, whose mistress is Venus; she, the significator of the question, was at the 10th degree of Aries. The Moon, mistress of the royal house <note>the 10th house</note> which signifies the kingdom, was at the 12th degree of Taurus. They did not see each other. However, Jupiter was at the 15th degree of Cancer, in the angle of heaven <note>the Midheaven</note>, that is, in the royal house. Both the Moon and Venus were joining him. Therefore, Jupiter collected the light—that is, the rays of both—in the place of the matter sought, which is the place of the kingdom. This signifies the acquisition of the kingdom through the hands of some leader or bishop, or through the hands of some beloved man to whom both planets would gladly grant the advancement.

<column-break/>

**[Astrological Chart: A square chart showing Jupiter at 15° Cancer and the Moon at 12° Taurus. The signs are arranged counter-clockwise from Gemini to Taurus.]**

### ¶ On the prohibition of light, which occurs in three ways.

**Almana** <note>From the Arabic 'al-mana', meaning prohibition or prevention</note>, that is, prohibition, occurs in three ways. The first is called the "cutting off of light" <note>original: "abscisio luminis"</note>. This occurs when, between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the matter sought, there is some other planet at a lower degree than one of them, and a conjunction is made with that planet before the conjunction with the Lord of the matter can occur. For example: let the ascendant be Virgo, and the question be about marriage. Mercury, Lord of the Ascendant and significator of the questioner, is at the 10th degree of Cancer. Jupiter, Lord of the seventh house and significator of the bride, is at the 15th degree of Pisces. Mars was at the 13th degree of Aries. Therefore, Mars cut off the light of Mercury from Jupiter, because Mars was in the 5th sign <note>The 5th sign from the ascendant, but here context implies the 8th house relative to the matter</note>, namely the "substance of the woman" <note>The 2nd house from the 7th, which is the 8th house of the whole chart</note>. This signified that the destruction of this matter would arise from the description of the dowry.

**[Astrological Chart: A square chart showing Mercury at 10° Cancer, Jupiter at 15° Pisces, and Mars at 13° Aries. The signs are arranged counter-clockwise from Gemini to Taurus.]**

¶ The second mode is when a light planet and another weightier one are both in one sign, and a third planet is between them in that same sign, seeking the conjunction of the weightier one; this planet takes away the conjunction of the first. For example: let the ascendant be Cancer, and the question be about marriage. Let the Moon be at the 8th degree of Gemini and Mars at the 10th degree of the same sign. Let Saturn be at the 12th degree...

<header>On Interrogations</header>

...two of his before Mars. Mars therefore separates the Moon from Saturn; he takes away their conjunction and destroys their purpose <note>In horary astrology, the "purpose" or "cause" refers to the successful outcome of the question asked.</note>.

<image-desc>A square astrological chart divided into twelve triangular houses. The zodiac signs are labeled around the perimeter: Gemini (containing "Moon 9, Mars 10, Saturn 12"), Taurus, Aries, Pisces, Aquarius, Capricornus, Sagittarius, Scorpio, Libra, Virgo, Leo, and Cancer.</image-desc>

¶ The third mode occurs when a <term>light planet<gloss>a faster-moving planet, like the Moon</gloss></term> joins another <term>weightier planet<gloss>a slower-moving planet, like Saturn</gloss></term> in one sign; and if another planet joins that same weightier one through an <term>aspect<gloss>a mathematical "look" or angle between signs</gloss></term> while being at a lower degree than the light planet. The light planet that is in the same sign as the weightier one therefore prohibits the conjunction of the other which is looking on through an aspect. When it has passed, its conjunction will be true; and this mode similarly prohibits the outcomes and returns them just as the others preceding it. An example of this is: if the <term>ascendant<gloss>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term> were Cancer, and an <term>interrogation<gloss>a question asked of the stars</gloss></term> were made regarding marriage; the Moon, the lady of the ascendant—who is the signifier of the person asking—would be at the 15th degree of Scorpio, and Mars at the 18th degree of Taurus, and Saturn at the 23rd degree of the same Taurus. Mars was above the degrees of the Moon (that is, in more degrees); therefore he cut off the aspect between the Moon and Saturn and prohibited their conjunction, because Mars was joining Saturn in one sign, and a conjunction of this kind is stronger than a conjunction by aspect. For an aspect does not destroy a conjunction, but a conjunction destroys an aspect; and an aspect does not cut off another aspect, but it does prohibit the outcome. A conjunction, however, cuts off an aspect. Sometimes one planet is joined to another, but before it reaches it, it joins a different one; and when it has been joined to that one, the first conjunction is destroyed.

<image-desc>A square astrological chart with zodiac signs labeled. In the house for Taurus, it reads "Saturn 23, Mars 18." In the house for Scorpio, it reads "Moon 15." Other signs labeled include Gemini, Aries, Pisces, Aquarius, Capricornus, Sagittarius, Scorpio, Libra, Virgo, Leo, and Cancer.</image-desc>

<column-break/>

¶ Similarly, if a planet joins another planet in one sign and sends its "disposition" to another—that is, joins another who is in a different sign—and after the conjunction of this one through an aspect it reaches the one with whom it shares a sign and is joined to it, the judgment shall be according to the planet that is with it in the same sign. An example of this: if the Moon were at the 10th degree of Taurus, and Mars at the 20th degree of the same Taurus, and the Moon were joined to Venus through an aspect before she was joined to Mars, and Venus were at the 15th degree of Cancer; although Venus was at a lower degree <note>meaning the Moon would reach Venus's degree mathematically first</note>, the judgment would nevertheless be referred to Mars because he was with the Moon in one sign. This kind of conjunction is stronger than an aspect, as we have said; this is the exposition of what we said: that an aspect does not annul a conjunction, but a conjunction annuls an aspect.

<image-desc>A square astrological chart with zodiac signs labeled. In the house for Taurus, it reads "Moon 10, Mars 20." In the house for Cancer, it reads "Venus 15." Other signs labeled include Aries, Pisces, Aquarius, Capricornus, Sagittarius, Scorpio, Libra, Virgo, Leo, and Gemini.</image-desc>

### ¶ On the reception of the planets.

**Reception** <note>original: "receptio"; a core concept where a planet is "hosted" by the ruler of its current location</note> of planets occurs when a planet is joined to a planet from its own <term>house<gloss>the primary zodiac sign a planet rules</gloss></term> or its <term>exaltation<gloss>a specific sign where a planet's power is heightened</gloss></term>; then the latter receives the former with good will and "perfect reception." There is also another reception below this (that is, a minor one) when a planet is joined to a planet that is the lord of its <term>triplicity<gloss>a group of three signs belonging to one of the four elements</gloss></term> and its <term>term<gloss>a small subdivision of a zodiac sign</gloss></term>; or the lord of the term and the <term>face<gloss>a ten-degree subdivision of a sign</gloss></term>. That is, when it is joined to a planet that has two or more of these minor dignities in its location; then it will be a true reception. If, however, it has only one, there will be no reception there. Therefore, say here that whatever differs from these rules is rejected by the skilled astrologer and is considered as nothing.

An example of this is if the Moon were in Aries and were joined to Mars, who is the lord of Aries; then Mars would receive her because she is in his house. Or if she were joined to the Sun, the Sun would receive her because it is the house of his exaltation. Or if she were in Taurus and joined to Venus, or in Gemini and joined to Mercury: this is perfect reception.

Reception of triplicity, however, is such as if the Moon were in Virgo in the term of Venus and joined to the same Venus, and Venus were the lady of the Moon's triplicity and the lady of her term. Or if the Moon were in Gemini in the term of Saturn and joined to Saturn, Saturn would receive her because he is the lord of the triplicity and the term. And when the Moon or a planet is in such a likeness, it shall be "received." This is the opinion of **Messahallab** <note>original: "Mesebalah"; Masha'allah ibn Athari</note> regarding the reception of triplicity and term. And if the Moon in this likeness were joined to any planet, and that planet itself were joined to the lord of the house in which the Moon is, or to the lord of her exaltation, the Moon would be received. And if the Moon were <term>void of course<gloss>moving through a sign without making any mathematical aspects to other planets</gloss></term>, and after this she passed into another sign and were joined to the lord of the first sign or the lord of its exaltation, the Moon would be received. And if she were joined to a planet that was not the lord of the first sign or the lord of its exaltation...
