...of his <term>interrogation<gloss>a question asked of the stars</gloss></term> hinders it. But these are the places in which there is neither reception nor conjunction: when the Moon, or the lord of the <term>ascendant<gloss>the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</gloss></term>, is joined to a planet that has no <term>testimony<gloss>original: "testimonium"; a presence in the local zodiacal dignities</gloss></term> in the place of the Moon or the lord of the ascendant—that is, it possesses no <term>dignity<gloss>astrological "rank" such as house or exaltation</gloss></term> there—then it does not recognize nor receive it. Similarly, if the Moon or the lord of the ascendant is joined to a planet in its <term>descension<gloss>also called "fall"; the place where a planet is weakest</gloss></term>, it will be like someone coming to another from the house of his enemies; that planet does not receive the Moon nor love her. An example of this is: if the Moon were in Aries and joined to Saturn; or in Capricorn and joined to Jupiter; or in Cancer and joined to Mars; or in Libra and joined to the Sun; or in Virgo and joined to Venus; or in Pisces and joined to Mercury. And if any <term>significator<gloss>the planet representing the person or the matter in question</gloss></term> is in its descension and joined to a planet that has no power in the place of that significator—meaning no house or exaltation—you will see that matter come to nothing, just as if an unknown garment were given to someone asking for one. And if a planet is joined to another planet in its descension, or if the <term>pushing planet<gloss>original: "planeta pulsans"; the faster planet applying to a slower one</gloss></term> itself descends, it makes the matter descend and diminishes what will come from it.

->On the void of course planet.<-

### Explanation
The <term>void of course<gloss>original: "vacuus cursu"</gloss></term> occurs with the Moon and its orbit, or when a planet is void and seems to be like an exile; it is then called void of course when it is joined to no other planet, and no other planet is joined to it.

->On the explanation of returning.<-

### Explanation
<term>Returning<gloss>original: "redditus"</gloss></term> occurs when a planet or the Moon is joined to a <term>retrograde planet<gloss>a planet that appears to be moving backward in the sky</gloss></term> or one <term>under the sun's rays<gloss>combust; too close to the sun to be seen or effective</gloss></term>; it returns to the other what it received from it, and thus destroys the cause. There is also another mode of returning, judgment, and destruction: when a pushing planet—that is, a <term>light planet<gloss>a fast-moving one</gloss></term>—is <term>falling<gloss>original: "cadens"; located in a weak house, like the 6th, 8th, or 12th</gloss></term> from the ascendant and joins a <term>weighty planet<gloss>a slow-moving one</gloss></term> that is also falling; it then returns to it what it received and destroys its <term>disposition<gloss>the management or outcome of the matter</gloss></term>. This signifies that the interrogation itself has neither a beginning nor an end. An example of this is: if the ascendant were Cancer and the Moon were in Sagittarius (the sixth house, which is falling from the ascendant) and joined to Mars; and Mars himself were in Gemini (the twelfth house from the ascendant, also falling); then this signifies the destruction of both the beginning and the end of this interrogation.

<image-desc>A square astrological chart with twelve segments representing the houses. The signs are labeled in a counter-clockwise direction, starting from the center-left: Cancer (1st house/Ascendant), Leo (2nd), Virgo (3rd), Libra (4th/Lower Midheaven), Scorpio (5th), Moon (6th/Sagittarius), Capricorn (7th/Descendant), Aquarius (8th), Pisces (9th), Aries (10th/Midheaven), Taurus (11th), and Gemini (12th, containing Mars).</image-desc>

¶ And there is another mode of returning: when a light planet is joined while in an <term>angle<gloss>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses; the strongest positions</gloss></term>, but it joins a planet falling from the ascendant. In this case, there will be a beginning to the cause—because the planet that is joining, which signifies the beginning of the matter,

<column-break/>

was in an angle—but it will have no end; for the <term>receiver<gloss>original: "receptor"</gloss></term>, who signifies the end of the matter, was falling. The one that joins is the light planet, and from it comes the beginning of the matter. The receiver is the one that is weighty, and is called the "receiver of the disposition," while the light one is called the "pusher of the disposition."

->On the pushing of virtue.<-

### Explanation
The <term>pushing of virtue<gloss>original: "pulsu virtutis"</gloss></term> of this matter is when a planet is joined to another while in its own house, or its <term>triplicity<gloss>a set of three signs of the same element</gloss></term>, or its exaltation. For example: if the Moon were in Cancer or in Taurus and joined with Jupiter or another of the planets, she would push her virtue to him, because she pushed (or committed) her disposition from her own house and exaltation. The rest of the planets do the same when they push their disposition from their houses or exaltations.

->On the pushing of disposition and nature.<-

### Pushing
of the disposition and nature occurs when a planet is joined with another planet while in that other planet's house or exaltation, and pushes its disposition or its nature to it. An example is when the Moon or any of the planets is in Aries and joined to Mars, or in Gemini and joined to Mercury. When the Moon is in Taurus or in Cancer, she pushes both—that is, her virtue and her disposition—and when she is not in these two signs, she still pushes the disposition.

->On the fortitude of planets.<-

### Explanation
The <term>fortitude<gloss>strength or dignity</gloss></term> of planets—which will lack any hindrance or impediment to completing a cause when they have received and promised—occurs in 11 ways:
1. First: when a planet is in a good place from the ascendant—that is, in the angles or the houses succeeding the angles—because they "look upon" the ascendant.
2. Second: when it is placed in any of its parts or dignities—this means in its own house, exaltation, triplicity, <term>term<gloss>a specific segment of a sign ruled by a planet</gloss></term>, <term>face<gloss>a ten-degree segment of a sign</gloss></term>, or its <term>joy<gloss>a specific house where a planet is traditionally happy</gloss></term>.
3. Third: when its motion is <term>direct<gloss>moving forward, not retrograde</gloss></term>.
4. Fourth: when no "malefic" planet—meaning Mars or Saturn—is with it in the same sign, or joined to it, or looking at it by <term>opposition<gloss>180 degrees apart</gloss></term> or <term>square aspect<gloss>90 degrees apart</gloss></term>.
5. Fifth: when it is not joined to a star falling from the ascendant, or to a planet in its descension, or if it is not in its own descension.
6. Sixth: when it is received.
7. Seventh: when the higher masculine planets—which are Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars—are <term>oriental<gloss>rising in the morning before the sun</gloss></term>; and when the feminine planets—Venus, Mercury, and the Moon—are <term>occidental<gloss>appearing in the evening after sunset</gloss></term>.
8. Eighth: when the planets are in their own light—meaning masculine planets by day and feminine by night.
9. Ninth: when the planets are in <term>fixed signs<gloss>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</gloss></term>.
10. Tenth: when the planets are in the "heart of the sun"—within one degree of the sun—because then the fortunes (benefics) increase their fortune and good, and the malice of the malefics is strengthened <note>Original: "maloꝝ confortatur malum"; being in the heart of the sun, or cazimi, was often thought to protect a planet from the sun's usual "burning" heat.</note>.
11. Eleventh: when masculine planets are in masculine <term>quadrants<gloss>sections of the sky</gloss></term> from the ascendant—that is, from the Midheaven to the Ascendant, or from the fourth house to the seventh; and feminine planets in feminine quadrants—that is, from the seventh to the Midheaven, and from the Ascendant to the fourth; and when masculine planets are in masculine signs and feminine planets in feminine signs. 
These are the testimonies by which planets are strengthened and have no hindrance to hurt them in completing the cause when they have received and promised.

->On the debility of planets.<-

### Debility
of the planets occurs in 10 ways, creating an impediment for them in <term>nativities<gloss>birth charts</gloss></term> and interrogations.
1. First: when a planet is placed falling from the angles and does not look at the ascendant—that is, in the 6th or 12th houses.
2. Second: when a planet is retrograde.
3. Third: when it is under the sun’s rays.
4. Fourth: when it is joined to malefic planets by conjunction or opposition—meaning in the same sign or in the seventh from it—or by square aspect (from the fourth sign).
5. Fifth: when it is <term>besieged<gloss>original: "obsessus"</gloss></term> between two malefics—that is, when it separates from one malefic and joins another.
6. Sixth: when a planet is in its descension, or joined to a planet that is in its own descension.
7. Seventh: when it is joined to a planet falling from the ascendant, or when it is separated from a planet that was receiving it.
8. Eighth...

...Eighth, that a planet be in a house in which it has no testimony <note>original: "testimonium"</note>—that is, any dignity, etc.—so that it is <term>peregrine<gloss>a planet with no essential dignity in its current position, like a traveler in a foreign land</gloss></term>; and already following the Sun—that is, before the Sun. Ninth, that a planet be with the <term>Head or Tail<gloss>the North and South Nodes of the Moon, often associated with increase and decrease</gloss></term>, if there is no latitude to it. Tenth, when planets have hindered themselves—that is, when they are in the opposition <note>the 180-degree aspect</note> of their own houses, which is a certain hindrance to them. These are, therefore, the chapters in which there is hindrance or detriment to the planets, which occur in <term>nativities<gloss>birth charts</gloss></term>, in <term>interrogations<gloss>charts cast to answer a specific question</gloss></term>, and in other works. Therefore, observe these modes which we have spoken of regarding a planet that receives the disposition and that promises the cause.

---

->¶ On the faults of the Moon and her bad state.<-

### Vitia
Therefore, the faults <note>original: "vitia"</note> of the Moon and her bad state, by which the detriments of things are created in every interrogation and in every beginning, occur in ten ways. And the first is that the Moon be <term>combust<gloss>burned up by the Sun’s proximity</gloss></term> within the rays of the Sun, not yet passing twelve degrees; and similarly after the Sun, but this is lighter. Second, that she be in the degrees of her descension <note>also called "fall," her weakest sign</note>, or be joined to a planet in its descension. Third, that she be in opposition to the Sun within twelve degrees, not yet coming to the degree of opposition. Fourth, that she be joined to the "evils" <note>the malefic planets, Mars and Saturn</note> or they behold her from a square aspect, or from an opposition; or that she be <term>besieged<gloss>original: "obsessa"; trapped between two difficult planets</gloss></term> between two evils, separated from one and joined to the other. Fifth, that she be with the Head or Tail <note>the lunar nodes</note> in one sign, and there be less than twelve degrees between them. Sixth, that she be in the twelfth sign from her own house—which is the sign of Gemini <note>the 12th sign counting from Cancer</note>—or be at the end of the degrees of the signs which are the <term>terms<gloss>specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign</gloss></term> of the evils. Seventh, that she be falling from the <term>angles<gloss>the most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</gloss></term> or be joined to a part falling from the angles. Eighth, that she be in the <term>Combust Way<gloss>original: "via combusta"; a specific section of the zodiac, usually late Libra and early Scorpio, considered unlucky</gloss></term>; this is at the end of Libra and the beginning of Scorpio. Ninth, that she be "feral" or <term>void of course<gloss>original: "cursu vacua"; making no further connections to other planets before moving into the next sign</gloss></term>. Tenth, that she be slower in her course—that is, when her equation is diminished; or when her light is diminished, which is at the end of the lunar month. These are the aforesaid faults of the Moon and her hindrances, under which no work should be begun—that is, while the Moon is thus, no work is authorized to be begun, nor is she praised in a nativity nor in a journey. 

Know also the state of the Moon in the increase of this light and its diminution—that is, when she waxes and when she wanes. For while the Moon increases, if Mars beholds her from the fourth sign <note>a square aspect</note> or from the seventh <note>an opposition</note>, or if he is with her in one sign, Mars hinders her, because she will then be hot <note>in the humoral system of the time</note>. On the contrary, if Saturn is with her and she is waning, or if he beholds her from a square or opposition, he hinders her. For when the Moon is fuller of light—that is, in the beginning of the month—and is hot, Saturn does not hinder her because he is cold, but Mars hinders her because he is hot. And when she has less light—that is, at the end of the month—she will be cold; then Mars does not hinder her because he is hot, but Saturn hinders her because he is cold. 

And know that Saturn in diurnal nativities and interrogations that are asked in the day, and in the beginning of the month, and in masculine signs, hinders less; and he is not called a hindered planet <note>original: "planeta impeditus"</note>... <insert>in feminine signs he hinders more</insert>. And Mars in the night, and in feminine signs, and at the end of the month, hinders less; and in the day, and in the beginning of the month, and in masculine signs, he hinders more. And neither a planet, nor the Moon, nor a sign is called hindered until the evils are with it, or behold it from the fourth, seventh, or tenth sign. Nor is a planet or the <term>ascendant<gloss>the sign rising on the horizon</gloss></term> called fortunate until the "fortunes" <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> are in the angles of that same part, or in the angles of the ascendant.

---

->¶ On besieged planets.<-

### Expositio
The definition <note>original: "expositio"</note> of besieged planets is: that a planet be between two evils, separated from one of them and joined to the other, without the projection of the rays of another planet between them—that is, so that no other planet throws its rays between them. And this is stronger and worse if the separation and conjunction occur within seven degrees or less. An example of this is: if Mars were in the tenth degree of Cancer, and Saturn in the 18th degree of Aries, and the Moon in the 13th of Libra; the Moon is then separated from Mars by a square aspect and joined to Saturn by an opposition; then the Moon will be besieged, because she is separated from the light of Mars and joined to the light of Saturn.

<column-break/>

->¶ On a planet in its own light.<-

### Dicitur
A planet is said to be in its own light when, for example, Mars is the <term>significator<gloss>the planet representing the subject</gloss></term> at night, as he is nocturnal; and Saturn in the day is said to be in his own light, as he is diurnal.

---

->¶ On the testimonies of the planets.<-

### Expositio
This is also the explanation of those things which are said concerning the planets that have testimonies, or parts, or dignities. If a planet is in its own house, or in its exaltation, or its <term>triplicity<gloss>a group of three signs belonging to the same element</gloss></term>, or in its term, or in its <term>face<gloss>a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</gloss></term>, it is itself "profiting" when it is in a sign in which it has testimonies.

---

->¶ On the joys of the planets.<-

### Expositio
Furthermore, the "joy" <note>original: "gaudium"</note> of the planets occurs in four ways. First, their joy is from the circle: Mercury joys in the ascendant <note>1st house</note>, the Moon in the third, Venus joys in the 5th, Mars in the 6th, the Sun in the 9th, Jupiter in the 11th, and Saturn joys in the 12th. ¶ Second, the joy which a planet has from its strength in its own houses: For Saturn joys in Aquarius because it is a masculine sign; and Jupiter joys in Sagittarius, Mars in Scorpio, the Sun in Leo, Venus in Taurus, Mercury in Virgo, and the Moon joys in Cancer. ¶ Third, that the diurnal planets joy when they are in the east—that is, when they rise in the morning; and the nocturnal planets joy when they appear in the evening in the western hemisphere. ¶ They also give a fourth mode of joy: that Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars joy when they are in the masculine part of the circle, which is from the <term>midheaven<gloss>original: "medium celi"; the highest point in the chart</gloss></term> to the ascendant, and from the fourth sign to the seventh. The Moon and Venus, however, joy when they are in the feminine part, namely from the 7th to the midheaven, and from the ascendant to the "angle of the earth"—which is the fourth sign. Mercury, however, joys in both parts—that is, when he is with masculine parts he joys in the masculine part, and when he is with feminine ones he joys in the feminine part, because of the diversity of these planets and their houses.

---

->¶ Here begin the principal judgments, and they are 50.<-
->¶ First, on the reception of disposition through the Moon.<- I.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'L' containing a scholar seated at a desk with an open book, pointing upwards, framed by classical architectural elements.</image-desc>
**The Moon** is the significatrix—that is, the Moon, whose circle is closer to the Earth than the circles of all the planets, is similar to the things of the world more than all the planets. Do you not see how a human begins by being small, then grows until they are finished? The Moon does similarly. Therefore, consider the Moon as the significatrix of all things, because her health is the health of every thing, and her detriment is the detriment of every thing. She "knocks"—that is, she commits her disposition to that planet upon whom she throws her rays, and to whom she is joined from the <term>planets<gloss>original: "de p'ltis" (de planetis)</gloss></term>, and she changes her state to that planet. That planet is called the "receiver of the disposition" because it receives what had been committed to it. Therefore, the Moon herself is the "bearer" <note>original: "delatrix"</note> of these planets, and she herself pacifies them and carries from some of them to others.

---

### II.
->¶ What evil or what good the planets signify.<-

**Other** planets signify detriment and evil because of the excess or superfluity of the power of cold or heat prevailing in them and hindering them. But if a good planet <note>a benefic</note> is in the house of an evil one <note>a malefic</note> or in its exaltation, it receives it and restrains its malice from it; or if there is an aspect of the evils from a trine or sextile aspect, it also restrains from this, because it is an aspect of friendship without any enmity. The "fortunes," however, because they are of a temperate nature and equal complexion—that is, because they are tempered by heat and cold—always profit and excel, whether they have received [others] or not; but reception in them is more useful and better.

---

->¶ Three judgments on the hindrance of the planets.<- III.

**There are** two modes of the stars: namely, good and evil. Therefore, wherever you see evil planets, speak of evil; and wherever you see a "fortune," speak of good. IIII.

**And it is called** a hindered planet until an evil one throws its rays upon its light according to the quantity which I told you concerning their <term>orbs<gloss>the range of degrees within which a planet's influence is active</gloss></term>. Joined...

...if it has passed the boundary <note>original: "terminum," referring to the 'Terms' or 'Bounds,' a specific division of a zodiac sign</note> of the malefics <note>the planets Mars and Saturn</note>, it is called "beholding the evil" and cannot hinder; and when a malefic planet has passed through a complete degree, it strikes fear but without a physical impediment, for the malefic planet cannot act since it is separated from it. Likewise, when a <term>fortuna<gloss>a benefic or "lucky" planet, like Jupiter or Venus</gloss></term> has passed a planet and is separated from it by a full degree, the thing is hoped for but not completed. And every hindering planet, when it is <term>cadent<gloss>falling away from the "angles" or corners of the chart, thus weakened</gloss></term> from the ascendant, sends fear but does not hinder. Likewise, when the benefics are cadent from the ascendant, the thing is hoped for, but not completed. V.

**A planet** when it is in the <term>angles<gloss>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful areas of a chart</gloss></term> of the malefics—that is, when it is with one, or in the fourth from it, or in the seventh or tenth—it will be like one who fights for himself against the tribulation and evil that descends upon him. And when it has passed it and been separated from it by a full degree, as I told you before, it has already escaped the hindrance of that evil, and the malefic can send nothing except fear. Keep these chapters well, for they are from the secrets of <term>interrogations<gloss>horary astrology, the art of answering specific questions based on a chart cast for the moment the question is asked</gloss></term>.

### ¶ On the Moon being void of course. VI.

**The Moon** when it is <term>void of course<gloss>making no further aspects to other planets before it leaves its current sign</gloss></term>—that is, joined to none of the planets—signifies emptiness, annulment, and a return from that same cause, as well as the hindrance of that cause.

### ¶ On the conjunction of the Moon with the planets. VII.

**The conjunction** of the Moon signifies what is to come and what is hoped for in matters, according to the nature of the planet which receives the Moon’s disposition <note>that is, the planet the Moon is moving toward</note>. That is, if it is a benefic, it signifies good; and if it is a malefic, evil.

### ¶ On the separation of the Moon from the planets. VIII.

**The separation** of the Moon from a planet signifies what is past, and what has already receded, according to the nature of that planet from which the Moon is separating.

### ¶ On a planet in its descension. IX.

**A planet** when it is in its <term>descension<gloss>also called "fall," the sign opposite its exaltation where it is most weakened</gloss></term> signifies sadness, imprisonment, and distress.

### ¶ On a retrograde planet. X.

**A planet** that is <term>retrograde<gloss>appearing to move backward from Earth's perspective</gloss></term> signifies disobedience, contradiction, reversal, retraction, and diversity or discord.

### ¶ On a stationary planet. XI.

**A planet** in its station signifies evil and that which has already happened.

### ¶ On the malefic planets. XII.

**The malefics** <note>Mars and Saturn</note> signify difficulty, pressure, and haste in the work.

### ¶ On a planet slow in course. XIII.

**A planet** when it is slow—that is, when it walks slowly—postpones its number or its promise. That is, it causes a delay in the count or its promise, as much in good as in evil. It does similarly when it is in the houses of Saturn or Jupiter; but in the houses of the light planets <note>the Moon, Mercury, and Venus</note>, it hastens.

### ¶ On the conjunction of the Moon with planets in the same minute. XIIII.

**When** the Moon is joined to any planet and has perfected its conjunction—that is, when it is with it in one minute of a degree—look to what is to come regarding that interrogation from the planet with which the Moon is joined after this.

### ¶ On a planet being at the end of a sign. XV.

**A planet** when it is in the final degree of a sign has already had its strength recede from that sign, and its strength will be in the next sign. It is like a man who has placed his foot upon the threshold of a gate wanting to go out; for if the house falls then, it will not hinder him. If, however, the planet is in the 29th degree, the strength of that planet will be in that same sign, because there are three degrees for every planet in which its power is expanded: namely, the degree in which it is, the degree which is after it, and the degree which is before it.

### ¶ On a planet that seeks but does not follow through on a conjunction. XVI.

**A planet** sometimes seeks a conjunction, but does not achieve it in its own sign until it is followed by the

<column-break/>

planet through its own haste. And when it has followed it into another sign and has not been joined to another, the cause is completed. But if it is joined to another when it has changed signs, and afterwards joined to the first, the cause will not be completed, because it has already been mixed with the light of the other planet. XVII.

**A planet** wishing to be joined to another planet in one sign, but unable to catch it in that same sign until it goes out into another sign: if it catches it in the other sign, the cause is then completed, unless it is joined to another first. But if it is joined to another by <term>aspect<gloss>a geometric relationship like a square or trine, rather than being in the same spot</gloss></term>, this does not hinder it for the reason I told you: because a conjunction made by aspect does not annul a conjunction made by body <note>two planets in the same degree</note> in one sign. But a bodily conjunction annuls one made by aspect; and aspect does not cut off aspect, but rather prohibits the cause, whereas a bodily conjunction cuts off the aspect entirely.

### ¶ On a malefic planet well-disposed. XVIII.

**A malefic** planet when it is <term>oriental<gloss>rising before the Sun in the morning</gloss></term>—that is, when it appears in the morning in the east in its own house or its <term>exaltation<gloss>a sign where the planet is exceptionally strong</gloss></term>—and is not joined to another malefic that might hinder it, is better and more worthy than a benefic that is retrograde and hindered.

### ¶ On malefic planets being the lords of the causes. XIX.

**The malefics** when they are the lords of the causes <note>the planets ruling the matter in question</note> and the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is joined to them by a <term>fourth aspect<gloss>a square, or 90-degree angle</gloss></term> or opposition—that is, from the fourth sign or the seventh—they bring about the cause, but they destroy it in the end. And if those who are joined to the benefics are malefics, it will be better than if they were the ones receiving the disposition—that is, if the malefics themselves should knock <note>make an aspect</note> and be joined to them.

### ¶ On malefic planets in the ascendant. XX.

**A malefic** when it is in the <term>ascendant<gloss>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term> in its own house or in its exaltation is restrained from evil; but if it is retrograde in the ascendant, its evil is strengthened and its diversity and variation are multiplied.

### ¶ On a planet being in a sign similar to its nature. XXI.

**A planet** when it is in its own habit and likeness among the signs, it will be suitable for it. That is, if Saturn is in his own house or exaltation, or in a cold and dry sign; or if Mars is as I told you, and in a hot sign, he will be good. But if it is in a sign contrary to its nature, it will be evil for it, like water and oil which do not mix nor embrace. But if it is in a sign similar to itself, they mix and embrace, like water and milk.

### ¶ On benefics beholding malefics. XXII.

**Benefics** when they behold <note>make an aspect to</note> malefics, they diminish their hindrance.

### ¶ On malefics beholding benefics. XXIII.

**Malefics** when they behold benefics from a fourth aspect or from opposition, they diminish their good fortune.

### ¶ On benefics cadent from the ascendant. XXIIII.

**Benefics** when they are cadent from the ascendant or retrograde, they will be hindered and similar to malefics.

### ¶ On planets when they are received. XXV.

**Planets** when they are <term>received<gloss>Mutual Reception: when two planets are in each other's signs of dignity</gloss></term>, if they are benefics, their good will be stronger; and if they are malefics, their hindrance will be less.

### ¶ On malefics in a peregrine or non-peregrine sign. XXVI.

**Malefic** planets when they are in a <term>peregrine<gloss>a sign where they have no dignity or "rights"</gloss></term> sign—meaning they are not in their own houses, nor exaltations, nor triplicities—they increase evil and their hindrance is magnified. But when they are in signs in which they have <term>testimony<gloss>some form of essential dignity</gloss></term>, they are restrained from evil, and there will be no hindrance at all.

### ¶ On malefics when they are lords of matters and well-disposed. XXVII.

**The malefics** when they are in their own houses and are the lords of the matters, or in their exaltations, or triplicities, or in their own terms, and in the angles or in the houses following the angles, their strength will be like the strength of the benefics. Understand what I have told you.

# On Interrogations

¶ XXVIII. Concerning fortunes being <term>peregrine<gloss>a planet is "peregrine" when it has no essential dignity or "standing" in its current zodiac sign, like a traveler in a foreign land</gloss></term> or not.
**When fortunes** <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> are in a sign in which they have no testimony <note>original: "testimonium," meaning they lack any of the five essential dignities</note>, their luck and goodness are diminished; and when they are in a sign in which they have testimony—that is, in their own houses, exaltations, triplicities, or <term>terms<gloss>specific degrees within a sign ruled by a particular planet</gloss></term>—their fortune is magnified, they bring matters to completion, and they increase what is good.

¶ XXIX. Concerning planets in a malign place or existing <term>under the rays<gloss>within 12 to 15 degrees of the Sun, where the Sun's light "burns up" or hides the planet's power</gloss></term>.
**When** both fortunes and malefics <note>the harmful planets, Saturn and Mars</note> are in a malign place—that is, in any of the houses I have mentioned before—or are robustly "under the rays," they signify small and despicable things and cannot fully signify good or evil because of the weakness that is in them. For when a planet is <term>combust<gloss>burned up by being within 8.5 degrees of the Sun</gloss></term> under the rays or in opposition to the Sun, it will be weak; in this position, there is no utility or other good for the benefic planets, nor any evil for the malefics. This is because the fortunes signify only a tiny bit of good when under the rays, and likewise, when a malefic is under the rays, its power to hinder will be lessened.

¶ XXX. Concerning planets existing in their <term>dignities<gloss>the "essential dignities" are positions in the zodiac where a planet is particularly strong, such as its Home or Exaltation</gloss></term>.
**Every** planet, whether a fortune or a malefic, when it is in its own house, or exaltation, or in its triplicity, etc., turns whatever evil is in it into good. Marvel, therefore, at what I have told you, and take from it the measure for making judgments.

¶ XXXI. Concerning malefics existing in the <term>angles<gloss>the most powerful houses of a chart: the 1st (Ascendant), 4th, 7th, and 10th</gloss></term>.
**When** malefics are in the angles of the ascendant and hinder by a <term>fourth aspect<gloss>a "square" aspect of 90 degrees, considered tense or difficult</gloss></term> or by opposition, they will be strongly evil in their ability to harm. Their affliction will be greater, especially and specifically if they are stronger than the planet they are oppressing or hindering—that is, if they are in a stronger position or possess some dignity. But if they look upon a planet from a <term>trine<gloss>a harmonious 120-degree aspect</gloss></term> or a <term>sextile<gloss>a helpful 60-degree aspect</gloss></term>, they are restrained from evil and their hindrance is diminished.

¶ XXXII. On the consideration to be held regarding the locations of planets.
**A fortune** does not always signify anything except good fortune, and a malefic signifies nothing always except evil, because of the excess of its nature and the malice of its <term>complexion<gloss>the inherent temperament or elemental makeup of the planet</gloss></term>. It is necessary, then, to look at the locations of the planets—that is, their places relative to the ascendant and the signs in which they are located. Even if a planet is malefic, if it is in its own likeness, or in its own light, or in its house, exaltation, or triplicity, or in a good house from the ascendant, it signifies good.

¶ XXXIII. Concerning a fortune when it is poorly disposed.
**If a fortune** is not in its own light—that is, if it is one of the nocturnal planets <note>Venus or the Moon</note> and is the significator during the day, or if it is one of the diurnal planets <note>Jupiter or the Sun</note> and is the significator at night—or if it is peregrine from its sign, or <term>cadent<gloss>falling away from the angles, thus weakened</gloss></term> from the ascendant, or under the rays, it hinders and does not profit.

¶ XXXIIII. Concerning that which Jupiter and Venus can change.
**When Jupiter** looks upon a malefic, he changes its nature into good; but Venus cannot turn back a great matter—that is, the evil of Saturn—unless they both look upon Jupiter. For Jupiter unties what Saturn knots <note>original: "soluit quod nodat Saturnus"</note>; that is, if Jupiter joins with Saturn, he breaks his malice and changes it. Venus unties what Mars knots.

¶ XXXV. Concerning what the "pulsation" <note>original: "pulsatio," the energetic contact or aspect between planets</note> of planets toward each other signifies.
**When** a malefic "pulses"—that is, is joined to another malefic—it is turned, meaning it changes one evil into another evil. If a malefic joins a fortune, the evil is converted into good. If, however, a fortune joins a fortune, good is turned into even more good. And if a fortune joins a malefic, one finds evil following after the good; in this way, you must weigh the mixture of matters.

¶ XXXVI. Concerning that which liberates fortunes from the misfortunes of the malefics.
**When the Moon** and the Lord of the Ascendant are hindered by a conjunction, a fourth aspect, or an opposition from the malefics: if the fortunes then join with them by a fourth aspect, whatever they find—even if it is destruction—the fortunes will solve it and liberate them from it. Similarly, if they are joined to malefics by a fourth aspect, but the fortunes look upon them by a trine aspect, that person will escape whatever

<column-break/>

destruction meets him and will not fall into another.

¶ XXXVII. Concerning a planet outside its dignities and falling from the angles.
**When** a planet is not in its house, exaltation, triplicity, term, or in its <term>joy<gloss>a specific house where a planet is said to be "happy" or most effective</gloss></term>, and it is cadent from the angles, this will be a bad sign without any utility; there is nothing of good in the hindrance of such a planet.

¶ XXXVIII. Concerning a planet under the rays toward the west.
**When** a planet is under the rays toward the west—meaning when it sets in the evening—its strength is weakened, as was said regarding the superior planets. Indeed, there will be no strength for it or its light, and its hindrance will be less if it is a malefic. If it is <term>retrograde<gloss>appearing to move backward in the sky</gloss></term>, it will be slow in all matters.

¶ XXXIX. Concerning a planet under the rays within 12 degrees.
**When** planets are under the rays, they are weak in all things. This occurs if there are fewer than 12 degrees between them and the Sun, unless the planet is in the same degree as the Sun, for then it will be strong. <note>This refers to "Cazimi," or being in the heart of the Sun.</note>

¶ XL. Concerning a planet with the Sun.
**When** a planet is 12 degrees away from the Sun in the morning in the east, it will be strong in every beginning and in every work; and when it is lengthened from the Sun by 15 degrees, it will then be even stronger—that is, it will be in the greatest strength it ought to have. If the planet is before the Sun in the west—that is, if it rises in the evening in the west—and there are between it and the Sun 15 degrees down to seven, it then begins to be weakened from seven degrees until it is in the "heart of the Sun" <note>original: "in corde solis"</note>; then the planet is as weak as it can possibly be. But when it is in the heart of the Sun, it becomes strong by the heart of the Sun; this is understood to mean when it is in the same degree as the Sun.

¶ XLI. Concerning a peregrine planet.
**When** a planet is in peregrination—that is, when it is not in any of its dignities, such as exaltation, <term>face<gloss>the smallest division of a sign, also called a decan</gloss></term>, etc.—its mind and nature are said to be "hot" <note>agitated or unsettled</note>. But if it is not in its house or exaltation, yet is <term>direct<gloss>moving forward normally</gloss></term> and in a good house from the ascendant—either in the <term>Midheaven<gloss>the 10th house, representing career and public life</gloss></term> or in the eleventh house—it will be good. If the Moon joins any planet, that planet to which she joins is said to be the "receiver of the disposition" <note>the planet that takes over the Moon's influence</note> of the Moon; and thus the reception proceeds up to Saturn, for above Saturn there is no planet that receives a disposition.

¶ XLII. Concerning the receiver of the disposition.
**When** the receiver of the disposition is occidental <note>setting in the west</note> by 12 degrees or less before the Sun, it will be weak and broken, and that which it judges is not completed. If it is oriental <note>rising in the east</note>, it will be strong, prudent, and perfect in judgment. An impeded planet is like a building: when it has fallen, it is rebuilt and improved, and it becomes good.

¶ XLIII. Concerning a planet in the eighth house.
**When** a planet is in the eighth house from the ascendant: if it is a fortune, it works neither good nor evil; but if malefics are in that same place, their evil is magnified.

¶ XLIIII. Concerning a planet in the beginning of a sign and in the beginning of an angle.
**A planet** when it is at the very beginning of a sign will be weak until it is established in it and travels through six degrees. A planet does not "fall" from the angles until after it has passed five degrees beyond the angle cusp. For example: if the angle is at 10 degrees of Aries, every planet that is within the boundary of five degrees is falling and is not considered to be in the angle.

¶ XLV. How a planet after an angle is understood to be in the angle.
**Every** planet that is up to 15 degrees after the angle cusp will be considered as if it were in the angle; if it increases beyond those degrees, it will have no strength. For example: if the angle were at 10 degrees of the sign Aries, then every planet from that same 10th degree up to the 25th degree of Aries is considered to be in that same angle. If it adds more than 15 degrees, it will not be in the angle. But <insert>Zabel</insert> says that up to 25 degrees after the angle, the planet will be in the angle.

¶ XLVI. What planets in signs signify regarding the stability of a matter.
**When** planets are in <term>fixed signs<gloss>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which represent endurance and lack of change</gloss></term>, they signify fixedness—that is, the infirmity and stability of a matter...

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions of Sahl ibn Bishr (Zael) regarding horary astrology—the art of answering specific questions based on the time they are asked. ...matters about which the inquiry is made: and when they are in <term>common signs<gloss>also known as mutable signs: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</gloss></term>, they signify the dissolution of matters and repetitions, and one thing will be joined to another, or something else of that sort. And when they are in <term>moveable signs<gloss>also known as cardinal signs: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn</gloss></term>, they signify the speed of change or the transformation of matters into good or evil.

### ¶ XLVII. What the signs signify in inquiries.

**A fixed sign** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius</note> signifies the form—that is, the firmness—of the inquiries and the matters about which the inquiry is made, and every fixed, very firm, and stable thing; and it is an aid to a good inquiry. And common signs signify things that cannot be done or which are repeated a second time. And a moveable sign signifies the speed of a matter's transformation into something else.

### ¶ XLVIII. On the stationary planet.

**A planet**, when it returns to <term>retrogradation<gloss>the appearance of a planet moving backward in the sky</gloss></term>—that is, when it is in its first station—signifies the dissolution of a cause and disobedience. And when it stands for direction—that is, when it is in its second station <note>the pause before a planet resumes "forward" motion</note>—it signifies direction after the slowness or hardness of the matter. And every planet that is the significator and intends to go direct—that is, if it is in its second station—signifies the renewal of the actions of things, and their action, strength, or direction. And if it is in its first station, intending to go retrograde, it signifies their destruction, slowness, and dissolution.

### ¶ XLIX. On an inquiry made while the Moon is hindered.

**Know** that on the day when the Moon is <term>hindered<gloss>afflicted by difficult aspects or poor placement</gloss></term>, everything inquired about on that day will be hindered, unless the malefic <note>a harmful planet like Saturn or Mars</note> hindering her is "falling" from the ascendant <note>placed in a weak house</note> and is weak, and the Moon then has no part in the ascendant. For when a malefic hinders the Moon and is himself falling from the ascendant, he induces fear and anxiety. And when he is in the <term>angles<gloss>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful</gloss></term> or in the houses following the angles, he strikes fear into the body.

### ¶ L. On the planet to which the Moon joins, on the Moon itself, and on the lord of the ascendant in the opposite of its own house.

**Know** that the planet to which the Moon is joined signifies what is to come and the outcome of the matter. If she is joined to the "fortunes" <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note>, it signifies a good outcome. And if she is joined to malefics, it signifies a bad outcome. And know that when the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is in the opposition of its own house—that is, in the seventh house from its own—the "lord of the inquiry" <note>the person asking the question</note> will shrink from the cause about which he asks, for it will be heavy for him. Know all this.

### ¶ What follows is regarding inquiries: and first, concerning inquiries of the ascendant—that is, the first house.

**When** you are asked about any inquiry, you shall begin to look as I have told you before. For I have already established for you the method by which everything is taken. Therefore, do not seek to deviate to another; nor should you insert a cause about which you were not asked into the cause about which you are asking, lest you bring confusion upon yourself—like one who asks about marriage. And if you look at the Moon, she will ask you about another matter that then seemed right to her. But if you have reflected before considering various matters, it is right and proper that you take each matter from its own beginning. Nor is it permitted for anyone to ask about two things of the same kind in one inquiry. And do not look at the stars except for someone who comes to you in hope, or out of necessity, or in sadness, and who comes to you anxious or with great effort. For he who comes to you knowingly, as if "heated" or merely to test you, do not look for him; because the result follows the quantity of the inquirer's anxiety regarding the matter about which he asks. Be careful, therefore, in these chapters: for the inquiry will be more useful when a man asks about himself, or sends someone else to ask for him who is truly anxious about his matter. Know, therefore, the intentions of men, because the consideration of the work happens according to the anxiety and intention of the inquirer. For he who inquires, and his intention was in that inquiry during all...

<column-break/>

...his time, the locations of the planets at the hour of inquiry signify his well-being for all his time. Similarly, if his intention is to inquire about something in his year, his month, or his day, or any such thing, it will be so. Understand, therefore, their intentions before consideration, because every inquirer only asks about what overcomes him from the nature of the circle <note>the zodiac</note> along with his own being, about which he asks from the "complexion"—that is, the combination—of the circle with his being through some fortune or malefic. For there are branches and parts. He, therefore, to whom the fortune of his lord of the ascendant and the Moon occurs or agrees, is fortunate; and he to whom their hindrance corresponds is hindered; because no man asks in a state of the significator's hindrance—that is, the Moon and the lord of the ascendant—at the hour of inquiry or birth, unless he is a hindered and "bad" man—that is, unfortunate and troubled—or a man who is destined to find evils. Similarly, no one asks about fortune unless he is fortunate and a man who is destined to have fortune. Do not fear if you are asked about various inquiries under one <term>ascendant<gloss>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</gloss></term>, because matters turn out differently: for if many of them agree in one state—that is, in evil or in good—fortune or misfortune will be theirs. For we see some who are fortunate, and others like them who are also fortunate.

### ¶ A question concerning the durability and improvement of a matter.

**If, however**, you are asked about any matter that ought to profit, improve, and be stable: look at the conjunction of the lord of the ascendant with the lord of the matter, and the reception of the receiving planet—namely, the planet that "receives" the disposition, whether it be the lord of the matter or the lord of the ascendant—specifically, the one that is heavier <note>moving more slowly</note>; and look at its freedom from those things I have told you regarding the hindrances of the planets.

### ¶ A question concerning the instability and changeability of a matter.

**If, however**, there is an inquiry concerning the instability of a matter or movement: such as a pilgrimage, a change, the departure of a prisoner, or someone’s escape from tribulation and sadness. Look for these things from the place of instability: that is, from those houses "falling" from the angles and from the "retreats" <note>the cadent houses: the 3rd, 6th, 9th, and 12th</note>.

### ¶ A question concerning whether any matter pertaining to the twelve signs will happen or not.

**And if** you are asked about any matter among the things that are in the twelve signs, consider the ascendant, its lord, and the Moon as the significators of the man who asks you, the sign of the thing sought, and the lord of that sought thing. After this, look at the lord of the ascendant and the Moon, and the stronger of them—namely, the one who is in an angle and who aspects the ascendant—and begin with that one. If any of them is joined to the lord of the matter, that matter will be completed by the request of the inquirer. And if you find the lord of the matter joined with the lord of the ascendant, the matter itself will be completed with the ease and eagerness of the inquirer, without a request or any special opportunity. And if you find the lord of the ascendant or the Moon in the "place" <note>the house</note> of the matter, or if you find the lord of the matter in the ascendant, the matter will be completed unless the ascendant is hindered and its lord is in its descent <note>detriment or fall</note> or combust; in that case, it will not happen. And if you find the lord of the ascendant or the Moon joined to any planet in the place of the cause, or if you find the lord of the cause joined to any planet in the ascendant, and that planet has "testimony" there by house, exaltation, triplicity, etc., it will be completed. And if none of all these things we have said occur, look then at the <term>translation of light<gloss>when a fast-moving planet connects two others by aspecting them in succession</gloss></term> to the Moon or to any of the lighter planets. If you find it separated from the lord of the ascendant and joined to the lord of the matter, or separated from the lord of the matter and joined to the lord of the ascendant, the matter is completed by the hands of messengers and those who run between both parties. And if you do not find between them a planet that carries the light of one to its partner, then look for a <term>collection of light<gloss>when two planets both aspect a third, heavier planet, which "collects" their influence</gloss></term>. If you find the lord of the matter and the lord of the ascendant are both joined to one planet that is heavier, and that planet aspects the place of the matter, or is in the ascendant or in the <term>midheaven<gloss>the 10th house, representing success and authority</gloss></term>, the matter will be completed by the hands of a judge or a man to whom they are sent. <header>On Inquiries</header>

The outcome of all things occurs in three ways. First, from the conjunction of the <term>Lord of the Ascendant<gloss>The planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</gloss></term>, the Moon, and the <term>Lord of the Matter<gloss>The planet ruling the specific subject of the question, such as money, love, or health</gloss></term>. Second, when someone carries the light between them—that is, a planet separates from one of them and is joined to the other; then the matter is completed through the hands of "envoys" <note>This is known as the "Translation of Light."</note>. Third, from the collection of light—that is, when both are joined to some heavier <note>original: *ponderosiori*; meaning a planet that moves more slowly through the zodiac</note> planet which collects their light, receiving the strength of both of them. In this case, its judgment will be acceptable between them, or it represents a man who will assist in that same matter. From these three primary chapters, then, the outcome of matters is produced. After this, look (as I told you before) to the <term>receptor of the disposition<gloss>The planet that receives the influence or "management" of another planet through an astrological aspect</gloss></term> from any of them who is a heavier planet, whether it be the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Matter. If the planet that collects the light is free from <term>malifics<gloss>Mars and Saturn, traditionally viewed as challenging influences</gloss></term> while in the <term>angles<gloss>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses of a chart, where planets are most powerful</gloss></term> or the houses following the angles, and is not <term>retrograde<gloss>appearing to move backward</gloss></term>, nor <term>combust<gloss>too close to the Sun, which "burns up" its power</gloss></term>, nor falling from the angles, the matter itself will be completed after it is obtained. However, if the receptor is retrograde, the matter will be dissolved after the person thought they had obtained it.

### Question whether a matter will happen with ease or with hardship.

**And if** you are asked whether one will obtain it with ease or with hardship: Look if there is a conjunction from the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Matter from a <term>trine<gloss>a harmonious 120-degree angle</gloss></term> or a <term>sextile<gloss>a pleasant 60-degree angle</gloss></term> aspect; the acquisition will be with ease. If the conjunction is from a <term>square<gloss>a 90-degree angle indicating friction</gloss></term> aspect or from their <term>opposition<gloss>a 180-degree angle indicating direct conflict</gloss></term>, the acquisition will be after hardship, difficulty, and delay.

### Question whether one will obtain the thing by request or will have it without asking.

**And if** you are asked whether one will obtain it through a request <note>original: *petitionem*</note> or if it will come to them voluntarily without any request: Look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If they join themselves to the Lord of the Matter, it will be with a request. But if the Lord of the Matter joins the Lord of the Ascendant, it will come voluntarily. Likewise, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the place <note>the zodiac sign or house</note> of the matter, it will be through the request and effort of the inquirer—that is, with his distress, and so on. If, however, the Lord of the Cause is in the Ascendant, people will exert themselves for him in that matter, and it will be given to him spontaneously. If the inquiry is about the appointment to some honor, it will come voluntarily, and he will not need to go to the gates of kings for it. If the outcome of the matter is from the translation of light, it will be through envoys and those who run back and forth between them. If the Moon has separated from the Lord of the Ascendant and is joined to the Lord of the Matter, the mission will begin from the inquirer. If the Moon has separated from the Lord of the Matter and is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, an envoy will come to him, and effort will be spent on his behalf in this. If the acquisition of the matter is from a collection of light, the acquisition will be through some judge who intervenes between them, or through one who enters into the matter until the acquisition is finished. And know that if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joins a planet in that planet's <term>fall<gloss>original: *descensione*; a sign where a planet's influence is weakened or "fallen"</gloss></term>, it signifies the detriment of the matter—just as if they were joined to Mars in Cancer or Jupiter in Capricorn, for these destroy matters. Similarly, if they are joined to planets in their fall which do not "receive" them, it signifies the poor disposition of the lord of the inquiry in what he wishes to do, and that the matter will not be completed. An example of a "fall" is if the Moon joins some planet in the third degree of Scorpio, which is the fall of that same Moon, or in the sign of Cancer, which is its fall <note>The text here contains a common scribal error; Cancer is the Moon's home, whereas its "fall" is traditionally Scorpio.</note>. And know that if a malefic is the Lord of the Matter and the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to it from a square aspect or opposition and it does not receive them, the inquirer will wish the matter not to happen because of the evils, tribulations, and labors that come upon him in that same matter. If, however, the conjunction is from a trine or sextile aspect, this will be diminished. And if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Matter are the same planet—that is, if the same planet rules both the inquirer and the object—and it is "received" (meaning it is joined to the lord of its house or exaltation) or is in a position free from malifics, the matter will be completed; otherwise, the matter will be destroyed. Similarly, if the Moon is joined to it and is safe from defects, it will be completed.

<column-break/>

### Testimonies of the signs in the outcome of a matter.

**And know** that the testimonies of the signs in the outcome of matters are: that the Ascendant be a <term>fixed sign<gloss>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius; signs of stability</gloss></term> or a <term>common sign<gloss>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces; signs of transition</gloss></term>, and the angles be stable. That is, that the <term>Midheaven<gloss>original: *medium celi*; the 10th house</gloss></term> be the 10th sign and the <term>Angle of the Earth<gloss>the 4th house</gloss></term> be the 4th sign; and not that the Midheaven falls in the 9th sign, nor the Angle of the Earth falls in the 3rd sign. This is the explanation of stable angles.

### Testimonies of the planets in the outcome of matters.

**The testimonies** of the stars in the outcome are three, which are sought from the Lord of the Ascendant, the Moon, and the Lord of the Matter. If two of them are free from the aforementioned malifics—that is, the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Matter—two parts of the matter will be completed. If only one of them is safe, a third part of the thing he asked for will be completed. This means if he has one testimony, he will have a third; if there are two testimonies, he will obtain two parts of what he sought; and if three testimonies are joined—that is, if the Lord of the Ascendant, the Lord of the Matter, and the Moon are all safe from retrogradation and combustion, and from malifics, and from fall or detriment—he will obtain everything he sought. And if they are received with their two testimonies, and the one who received them was also received himself, his "good" is increased beyond what he asked for. Know these inquiries, for they are joined to and fit all matters.

An example of such a matter is an inquiry made for a kingdom, whether it would be acquired or not. The Ascendant was 20 degrees of Gemini; the Midheaven was the 1st degree of Pisces; the Sun was in 12 degrees of Cancer; the Moon in 19 degrees of Virgo; Mercury in 27 degrees of Gemini; Mars in 8 degrees of Taurus; Venus in 3 degrees of Leo; Jupiter in 20 degrees of Pisces in its "first station" about to turn retrograde; and Saturn in 6 degrees of Gemini. I looked, therefore, in this inquiry at the Ascendant and its lord and the Moon, who are the significators of the inquirer; and at the Midheaven and its lord, who are the significators of the kingdom about which the inquiry was made. The Ascendant was Gemini and Mercury was in that Ascendant, specifically at the end of the sign. Jupiter, who was the Lord of the Matter, was in the Midheaven at the 20th degree. I found the Lord of the Ascendant separated from the Lord of the Matter. I then looked at the Moon, which I found in the Angle of the Earth <note>the 4th house</note> joined to Jupiter by opposition. This signified the acquisition of the matter through effort and difficulty because they were joined from opposite sides. If they had been joined by a sextile or trine aspect, the acquisition would have happened with ease. And it was the Moon joining the Lord of the Matter, signifying that this would happen through the request and effort of the inquirer. If it had been the Lord of the Matter joining [the Moon], the acquisition would have happened by the initiative of the one who ordered it, without the request or difficulty of the inquirer. I also looked at Jupiter, who was the "receptor of the disposition," and I found him in the Midheaven in his first station, wanting to turn retrograde. This signified the dissolution of the matter which he desired, and that its detriment would happen quite soon. This would come from the king's side because Jupiter was the lord of the tenth house (which is the royal house) and signified the king. If the receptor of the disposition had been the Lord of the Ascendant and he were impeded, I would say the detriment would come from the inquirer and from his own work. Because the Lord of the Ascendant was moving from his own house into the <term>house of substance<gloss>the 2nd house, relating to wealth and assets</gloss></term>, it signified the speed of the inquirer's change, and his journey for the investigation of substance to the place where he would stay. And he would not receive this, because when he leaves his sign he will join Mars, and Mars will not receive him. Thus, it signaled that in his departure he would do such work through which detriment and sadness would come upon him, because Mars was the lord of the sixth from the Ascendant—which is the house of servants and illnesses. It signified that what I said would come from the side of servants and low-born persons, and from illness. And because Jupiter was the Lord of the Matter who wanted to turn retrograde and was with the <term>Tail<gloss>original: *cauda*; the South Node of the Moon, often indicating loss or drains</gloss></term>, it signified the dissolution that would come upon the man from whom the matter was requested, and a multitude of complications... <note>The text cuts off here at the end of the page.</note>

### Chapter on the Conjunction of the Ascendant.

**And** it is not proper for this to be lacking from him in births <note>natal charts</note> and inquiries <note>horary charts</note> likewise: and this indeed ruins inquiries and ruins the life of the native: <term>Masha'allah<gloss>An 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer often cited in these texts</gloss></term> indeed says that he cuts off the hidden things: and it is that you should look at the star that is shining or "winning" in births and inquiries, and the star with which the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Matter is joined: or with which the Moon is joined: since the Moon is the partner of the Lord of the Ascendant: or she is shining or winning in the inquiry over the Ascendant and its Lord and the Lord of the Matter. Consider, therefore, the star joined to that with which it is joined. For if it is joined with a <term>malific<gloss>A planet traditionally viewed as harmful, usually Saturn or Mars</gloss></term> which does not "receive" it: or with a <term>retrograde star<gloss>A planet that appears to be moving backward in the sky</gloss></term>: or with a <term>cadent star<gloss>A planet in a weak house, away from the main angles of the chart</gloss></term>: or with a <term>combust star<gloss>A planet so close to the Sun that its influence is "burned away"</gloss></term>: or with an unfortunate star of cut-off light, it ruins the matter. And if it is joined with a star and that star is safe: and that star has a conjunction: we will look at the star with which that star is joined until the conjunctions are diminished: then we will look at the conjunction with it. And if there is one "cutting off" <note>original: *abscindens*; a planet that prevents a conjunction from completing</note> according to what we described in the first parts: the matter will be ruined after it is set right. And if there is no one cutting off: then the inquiry is completed. And if it is joined in the beginning of the matter with a malific: it cuts off with corruption: but if there is <term>reception<gloss>A favorable relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</gloss></term> with the malific without a <term>square<gloss>A challenging 90-degree aspect</gloss></term> and without <term>opposition<gloss>A 180-degree aspect</gloss></term> and without hostility: the matter is completed which is without opposition and without square. And if it is joined in the beginning of the matter with a <term>benefic<gloss>A planet traditionally viewed as helpful, usually Jupiter or Venus</gloss></term> and it has no conjunction with a malific: the matter is completed. And if it "transfers" between both stars and light <note>Translation of Light</note> and the star to which it transfers the light is cadent over a malific not received: the matter is ruined. And if it "collects" the light of two stars <note>Collection of Light</note> and the one collecting between both of them is a malific: the matter is ruined. And if it is receiving one of them and not receiving the other, it is ruined.

### The Second Sign or Second House and whatever is in it concerning inquiries.

**When** you are asked about any substance <note>wealth or property</note> that is separated: whether it may be found by the one who asked you about the substance or not. Look at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon, who are the significators of the querent, and the sign of the substance and its Lord, who are the significators of the substance: if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are joined to the Lord of the house of substance: or the Lord of the house of substance is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant: or you find the Moon carrying the light from the Lord of the house of substance to the Lord of the Ascendant: or from the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the house 

<column-break/>

of substance, he will obtain the substance. Likewise, if Jupiter or Venus, which are benefics, are in the house of substance, the substance will be found. And if there is none of these things which I have said: nothing will be found. If, however, there are malifics in the house of substance (which is the 2nd from the Ascendant), it signifies loss in the substance of the master of the inquiry. And if the Moon is <term>void of course<gloss>The Moon makes no further aspects before leaving its current sign, indicating no progress</gloss></term>, then the querent will not cease being in such a state until he dies.

### Inquiry concerning the manner of profit.

**If**, however, you are asked in what manner there will be profit: look at the receptor of the disposition: whether it be the Lord of the Ascendant: or the Lord of the matter itself. That is, the one who is "heavier" <note>original: *ponderosior*; moving more slowly</note>: who, if he is in the Ascendant or in the 2nd, he will find and acquire from the works of his own hands. And if he is in the 3rd, from brothers and from friends: and if he is in the 4th, from the father or from parents or from lands or from inheritances. And if he is in the 5th, from sons or from others in whom he has trust. And if he is in the 6th, from illness and from his own people or from lowly persons: and if he is in the 7th, from women (if it is a feminine sign) or from war or contention (if it is masculine): and if he is in the 8th, from the remains of the dead and from ancient things. And if he is in the 9th, from pilgrimage and from sects or places of prayer: and if he is in the 10th, from kings and magistrates or from nobles. And if he is in the 11th, from friends and business or trade. And if he is in the 12th, from enemies. And if it is a sign of four-footed animals: or if it is from the signs of men: from prisons: and their inhabitants. These are the natures of the 12 signs; in whichever you find a benefic, the acquisition will be from the substance and nature of that sign: and in whichever you find malifics, from that same thing will be loss and confusion. Look thus in all matters so that you may know in what manner there will be ease and what kind of dispersal.

### The Third Sign or Third House with its inquiries.

**When** you are asked about the state of a brother, look at the 3rd sign, which is the sign of the brother, and its Lord, and the aspect of the benefics and malifics present to it: if you find the Lord of the third from the Ascendant in the 6th: which is the house of illness, or joined to the Lord of the sixth: say that his brother is ill. Likewise, if the Lord of the sixth is in the 3rd. And if you find the Lord of the third in the 8th or in the 11th, his brother will be fearful. And if he is impeded in the 12th, his brother will have illness and sadness. And if he enters into "combustion" <note>near the Sun</note>, he will not escape from this. Likewise, you shall announce concerning the substance of the signs: and if he asks you about his father or mother, from the fourth: and about his son, from the fifth from the Ascendant: and about his servants, from the sixth: and about his wife, from the 7th, just as I told you before, if God wills.

### The Fourth Sign or Fourth House and concerning its inquiries.

**When** you are asked about land, or a house, or an inheritance which someone seeks, whether he will obtain it or not: look at the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, which are the significators of the querent, and the 4th sign and its Lord, which are the significators of the land. If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon are joined to the Lord of the 4th, or the Lord of the 4th is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant: or if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the 4th: or the Lord of the 4th is in the Ascendant, he will obtain it: and if the Moon transfers the light from one of them to the other, he will obtain it through the hands of messengers.

### Concerning what kind of inheritance is acquired: and concerning the building and everything that is in it.

**If** you are asked about any inheritance being acquired, what its condition is and the condition of its building: and whatever is in it: you shall arrange the Ascendant for the hour in which you are asked about it: and place with it the significator of the farmers; that is, those who work in it as farmers: and the 4th sign signifies the land: and the 7th sign signifies whatever is in it from the things following <note>the soil</note> which are beneath the trees: and the Midheaven <note>10th house</note> signifies whatever is in it from the trees. And if there is a malific planet in the Ascendant: the farmers themselves will be thieves and deceivers: and if it is direct, they will remain in the land. But if it is retrograde: they will flee from it. And if there is a benefic in the Ascendant: the farmers will be just and faithful. And if that benefic is direct: they will not leave the land. If, however, it is retrograde: they will leave. And if there is a benefic in the Midheaven—
