<column-break/>

[Saturn] <note>original: "tuna"; almost certainly a typo for Saturnus, as the Moon is never retrograde</note> signifies a multitude of trees. If it is direct <note>moving forward through the zodiac</note>, the trees will be strong and abundant in fruit. If it is retrograde <note>appearing to move backward</note>, they will suffer hindrance, and the buyer will be frustrated and see all the fruit of the trees fail. If it is poorly placed in the Midheaven <note>the 10th house, representing the height of the matter</note>, it signifies a scarcity of fruit; and if it is retrograde, it signifies that little will remain of them. If there is no planet in the Midheaven, look to the Lord of the Midheaven. If that planet aspects the Midheaven, there will be trees there. If it is oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note>, the trees will be newly planted. If it is occidental <note>setting after the Sun</note>, the trees are from an ancient planting. If the planet is direct, they will remain. If it is retrograde, they will not remain but will be destroyed. And if the Lord of the Midheaven does not aspect its own place—that is, if it is in the 2nd, 6th, 8th, or 12th house from the Ascendant—the land will be without trees.

After this, look to the 7th sign <note>the 7th house</note> just as I told you regarding the Midheaven. For the substance of the land itself, look to the 4th sign from the Ascendant. If it is Aries, Leo, or Sagittarius, the land will be mountainous and require much labor—that is, needing much cultivation. If it is Taurus, Virgo, or Capricorn, the land will be flat. If it is Gemini, Libra, or Aquarius, it will be of two types—that is, mountainous and level. If it is Cancer, Scorpio, or Pisces, it will be watery or near water. And if the 4th sign is common <note>mutable</note>—that is, Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces—the land will be of two types: there will be both mountains and fields.

When you wish to bring forth the land or its parts, or wish to settle it, or choose such a thing: look to the matter of the seller from the Ascendant, and the buyer from the 7th house. Look to the purpose of the work and its cause from the Midheaven, and the end of the matter from the 4th sign. If a Fortune <note>a beneficial planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> is in the Ascendant, the seller will be fit and diligent. If a Malefic <note>a harmful planet like Mars or Saturn</note> is there, he will repent of having sold it and will withdraw from the deal, or he will wish to sell it with craftiness and it will not profit him. If a Malefic is in the 7th house, the buyer will turn back—that is, he will repent and not pay. If he does pay, he will enter into strife and loathing, and it will not profit him. If a Fortune is there, the buyer will be useful and fit. If you find a Malefic in the Midheaven, or if it aspects it with an aspect of enmity <note>a square or opposition</note>, the business will not be directed well. If a Malefic is in the 4th house or aspects it, the end will result in great evil. If it is a Fortune, the end will be good and praiseworthy, if God wills.

---

¶ The 5th sign or Fifth House with its inquiries. First: whether he will have a son from that woman or not.

### Whether he will have a son from that woman or not.

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'S' containing a woodcut of a seated figure in a scholarly robe, holding a book or scroll.</image-desc>If anyone asks you whether he will have a son from this woman or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If they are joined to the Lord of the House of Children <note>the 5th house</note>, or if the Lord of the House of Children is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the House of Children is in the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the House of Children, or if you find a planet that transmits light <note>acts as a cosmic intermediary</note> between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Children, he will have a son. If there is a transmission of light there, there will be a delay in this. After this, look to the receiver of the disposition, which is a heavy <note>slow-moving</note> planet; if it is free from Malefics—that is, if it is not joined to them, nor they to it—and it is not falling from the Ascendant nor combust <note>too close to the Sun</note>, the son will live. But if the aforementioned planet is retrograde or combust, or falling from the angles <note>in a weak house</note>, he will perish afterward. If you find Jupiter in a good place from the Ascendant, and he is not hindered nor under the Sun's rays, it signifies conception. If a Malefic planet is with Venus, it does not signify conception. If the Moon is joined to Malefics, know that she will not become pregnant. If you find a Fortune in the 5th, which is the House of Children, the woman will become pregnant. If Malefics are in it, or if they aspect it by opposition or square aspect, it does not signify pregnancy.

### Whether a son will be born to him or not.

And if a woman or man asks whether a son will be born to them or not: look to the Ascendant; if Fortunes are in it or if the Lord of the Ascendant aspects the Ascendant, or is in the 10th, 11th, or 5th house—and if Jupiter is in an excellent place—a son will be born. If the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 4th or 7th house, and Jupiter is in a good place, a son will be born to him after a delay from the time of his inquiry. If you find a Malefic in the Ascendant or it aspects it from opposition or a square aspect, it does not signify pregnancy.
<meta>catchword: fueritas</meta>

<column-break/>

Jupiter falling <note>in a weak house</note>, or in the House of Death <note>the 8th house</note>, or under the Sun's rays, signifies a scarcity of children, and that they will last but a short time if they are born. To be certain, look to the 5th house from the Ascendant, which is the sign of children; if Fortunes are in it, a son will be born to him quickly. If a Malefic is in it, yet you see some good in the inquiry, there will be a son, but his death will soon be seen. If you find Jupiter oriental in an angle <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house</note>, a son will be born to him quickly. If he is occidental in an angle—that is, if he appears in the evening in the west—and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a suitable place, he will be born late and after some delay.

### Whether a woman is pregnant or not, and whether she will give birth or not.

If you are asked about any woman, whether she is pregnant or not, and whether she will give birth or not, or if it will be completed for her or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon, who are the signifiers of children. If you find the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon in the House of Children, and the Lord of the House of Children is in the Ascendant free from Malefics, say that she is pregnant. And if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon "knock"—that is, if they commit their disposition to some planet in an angle—there will be pregnancy, and it is better if it is received <note>by "reception," a supportive planetary relationship</note>. If they are joined to a planet falling from the Ascendant, it signifies loss and that the pregnancy is in vain, especially if the Ascendant is a moveable sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, or if a Malefic is in an angle, or if the Moon is joined to a Malefic; for all these things signify loss. The receiver of the disposition—that is, the heavier planet that receives all disposition from the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon—when it is free from Malefics—that is, if it is not joined to them, nor they to it—and it is in a good place, the pregnancy will be successfully completed.

### Whether the pregnancy is true or false.

And if someone asks about a pregnancy, whether it is true or false—that is, whether it will come to effect or be in vain: look to the Lord of the Ascendant; if it is joined to a planet falling from the Ascendant and not receiving it, it signifies loss. Similarly, if it is joined to a retrograde planet. But if the Moon is received or the Lord of the Ascendant is in a good place from the Ascendant, it signifies pregnancy.

### Whether a pregnant woman will give birth to twins or not.

If you are asked about a pregnant woman, whether she will give birth to twins or not: look to the Ascendant of the hour in which you are asked; if it is a common sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, or if there are two fortunate planets in the Ascendant or in the House of Children, she will be pregnant with twins—that is, she carries twins. Similarly, if you find the Sun and the Moon in common signs. But if the Ascendant is not a common sign, nor is the sign of children common, and none of what I have said is present, nor are the Luminaries <note>Sun and Moon</note> in common signs, she carries only one.

### Whether she will give birth to a male or a female.

If you are asked whether she will give birth to a male or a female: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Children; if they are in masculine signs, there is a male in her womb. If they are in feminine signs, there is a female in her womb. If one of them is in a masculine sign and the other in a feminine sign: look to the sign in which the Moon is found and the planet to which the Moon is joined. If the Moon is in a masculine sign and is joined to a masculine planet, she will bear a male. If the Moon is in a feminine sign or is joined to a feminine planet, she will bear a female. And know that Mercury, when he is oriental—that is, when he rises before the Sun—will be male; and if he is occidental—that is, when he rises after the Sun—he will be female, if God wills.

## ¶ The 6th sign or Sixth House with its inquiries.
## And first: whether a sick person will be healed or will die.

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'S' containing a woodcut of a person lying in a bed (a sickroom scene).</image-desc>If you are asked about a sick person, whether they will be healed or die: look to the Ascendant. If a Malefic is in the Ascendant, the medicine of the doctors will not profit him. If a Fortune is in the Ascendant, the medicine of the doctors and their care will profit him. And if a <term>fortune</term> <note>original: "fortuna"; a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> is there, health will come to him without any other treatment by which he might be cured. But if a <term>malefic</term> <note>original: "malus"; a harmful planet like Mars or Saturn</note> is in the 4th sign <note>the 4th house from the Ascendant</note>, it will increase the strength of his medicine—that is, the medicine will actually aggravate his condition. ### ¶ After this, look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon from that planet which is in an <term>angle</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</note> and aspects the Ascendant. 

If it is free from malefics and is not in the aspect of the Lord of Death <note>the planet ruling the 8th house</note>—especially in the 4th or 7th house, which is the house of death as it is the eighth sign from the Ascendant—and is not <term>under the rays</term> <note>invisible due to being too close to the Sun</note>, it signifies health. If it is joined to benefics, it also signifies health; but if that benefic is <term>retrograde</term> <note>appearing to move backward through the zodiac</note>, it signifies a long-lasting illness, though the patient will eventually recover. And if the Moon is not above the earth, but is joined to a planet that is above the earth, it signifies health. But if it is above the earth, it signifies health unless the planet receiving its disposition enters <term>combustion</term> <note>original: "combustionem"; being so close to the Sun that the planet's power is "burned up"</note>, for then it signifies death. 

And if the Moon is above the earth and is joined to a malefic below the earth, it signifies death. If the Moon joins the Lord of the Ascendant, and the latter is increasing in light and number <note>growing brighter and moving faster</note>, it signifies the swiftness of health and the improvement of the body. If the Lord of the Ascendant is below the earth and the Moon is joined to a planet in the 9th house from the Ascendant, which is falling away, it signifies death. If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the House of Death and the Moon is hindered, it signifies death. If one carries the light from the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the Eighth House, it is to be feared, for it is an evil sign. 

If it is received <note>a technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</note>, the illness will be prolonged. If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the Eighth by a <term>trine aspect</term> <note>an angle of 120 degrees, usually considered harmonious</note>, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in an angle, then when the Lord of the House of Death reaches the degree of the Ascendant, it will signify death. If some planet returns the light of the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the Eighth, and the Lord of the Ascendant is <term>cadent</term> <note>falling away from power</note> while the Lord of the Eighth is in an angle, it signifies death. If the Lord of the House of Death is in the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is hindered, it signifies death. If the planet receiving the disposition is hindered, it signifies a "breaking"—that is, a relapse after health. 

The presence of the Lord of the Eighth in the angles is also evil. If the Lord of the Ascendant is not above the earth and is joined to the Lord of the Eighth in the 4th house and in the house of death, it signifies death. If the Lord of the Eighth does not aspect the Lord of the Ascendant, but some planet returns their light, and the Lord of the Ascendant is cadent while the Lord of the Eighth is in an angle, it signifies death. If the Lord of the Ascendant enters combustion—that is, if there are fewer than 12 degrees between it and the Sun—it signifies death. Likewise if it is <term>combust</term> and not received. 

¶ If a planet does not "knock" on the disposition—that is, if there is a receiving planet that is free from combustion and the Moon is safe—it signifies escape from death. If the House of Illnesses is a <term>movable sign</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>, the sick person will be relieved at one time and worsened at another. If it is a <term>common sign</term> <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, the illness will change from one kind to another. If it is a <term>fixed sign</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>, it will remain in one state. 

If the Moon is separated from an <term>oriental planet</term>—that is, appearing in the east in the morning—the illness will be new and fresh. If the Moon is separated from an <term>occidental planet</term>—that is, appearing in the evening—his illness is already prolonged. If it is joined to an oriental planet, it signifies a quick outcome. If the Moon is joined to an occidental planet, the illness will be prolonged; it is better if it aspects the Lord of the Ascendant of the benefics and the planet itself is in a good place relative to the Ascendant. The aspect of malefics to it will be worse if it is from a square aspect or from opposition, or if it is in the same sign with it. If the Moon is joined to a retrograde planet, it signifies a long duration of the disease. If it is joined to a slower planet, it signifies an aggravation and doubt when it returns.

### ¶ On critical days by the position of the Moon.

**Know** also the position of the Moon on the 7th day from the beginning of the illness or the question about it, and on the 14th, 21st, and 28th days. For on whichever day the Moon reaches the malefics or the Lord of the House of Illness, the patient will grow worse on that day; and when it reaches the benefics or they aspect it, health and rest from the illness will happen to him. To know the 7th day of the illness, you shall add 90 degrees to the position of the Moon and calculate from the degree where that number falls—that will be the Moon's place on the 7th day. For the 14th day, add 180 degrees to its place; this is the opposition of the place it was in on the day the illness or question began. For the 21st day, add 270 degrees; and on the 28th day, the Moon returns to its own place—that is,

<column-break/>

to the sign and degree in which it was at the beginning of the illness or question. As many times as the Moon is joined to any benefic on these days, so many times will the sick person find rest and improvement; and as many times as it is joined to a malefic, so many times will his pain and heaviness increase.

### ¶ Whether someone is sick or not.

**If you are** asked about any man, whether he is sick or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If they are in the 6th house from the Ascendant (which is the house of illnesses) or joined to the Lord of the Sixth, or in their <term>descension</term> <note>the sign where the planet's power is weakest</note> or combust under the rays, say that he is sick; otherwise, he is not.

### ¶ Whether a servant will be freed from servitude or not.

**And if** a servant asks whether he will be freed from servitude or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If you find either of them separated from the Lord of the Midheaven, or from the Sun, or from the malefics, and they are not joined to any of those I mentioned, say that he will be free; otherwise, he will not.

### ¶ Question if a free servant will serve another.

**And if** a servant asks you, saying, "Shall I go out from the hand of my master to another or not?" Look in this case to the Lord of the Ascendant: if it is in an angle and is not joined to a planet falling away from the Ascendant, he will not go out from his master's hand. If it is joined to any planet in the 9th or 3rd house, it signifies his departure. But if the Lord of the Ascendant in an angle is hindered by opposition or by conjunction, or by a square aspect, or enters combustion, he will die before he goes out from his master.

### ¶ Question whether the current master is better for the servant or the future one.

**And if** a servant asks you, saying, "Is my master with whom I am better for me, or the one I want or to whom I am going?" Look at the Lord of the Ascendant: if it is <term>received</term> in the sign in which it is—that is, if it is joined to the Lord of that sign or its exaltation—his master with whom he is, and the place where he is, is better for him. If the planet he seeks is signified as illustrious, then the one to whom he wishes to go will be better for him. 

Then look at the planet from which the Moon separates and the planet to which the Moon will be joined. If the planet from which the Moon separates is a benefic, his master with whom he is is better for him. If the one he joins receives the Moon, the one he seeks will be better for him. If it does not join anything, look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon: if either of them is received in the sign in which it is, or is received in the sign where its Lord of exaltation or <term>triplicity</term> <note>a group of three signs belonging to the same element</note> is, his master with whom he is is better for him. If it is received in the second sign from where it is, or if it is coming toward it, then the one to whom he is going will be better for him than his master; and God knows best.

### ¶ A universal question about changing things from place to place: which is better, where one is or where one moves.

**Similarly**, you shall judge for a man traveling regarding his state in the land where he is, or his state in that to which he is going—that is, when he arrives there, will it be better for him? Likewise, look at the <term>revolution</term> <note>the timing of a change</note>—that is, in the change of all things, such as moving from mansion to mansion, a man moving from house to house, from land to land, or from one job to another. Whenever you are asked about two things, which of them is better, look into it just as I have told you.

### ¶ About buying a servant, whether the purchase will be completed or not.

**Whenever** you are asked about purchasing a servant, whether his acquisition will be completed or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If they are joined to the Lord of the Sixth from the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Sixth is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, the purchase will be completed. If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the 7th house, or the Lord of the Sixth is in the Ascendant, or you find a planet carrying the light between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Sixth, he will obtain that which he asks about. And if none of these things I told you are present, he will not obtain it.

### ¶ About one seeking a maid-servant, whether he will have her or not.

**And if** you are asked by a man who seeks a maid-servant from another: the Ascendant, its Lord, and the Moon will be for the seeker; the 7th house and its Lord will be for the one being asked. The 11th sign from the Ascendant will be for the maid-servant. Look for the conjunction of the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon with her, or for the translation of some planet between them, just as I told you in this chapter.

# On Questions

### Column 1

->Whether a master will have the property of a deceased servant.<-

**And if** you are questioned concerning the remains <note>the estate or property</note> of a deceased servant, whether the master will obtain them or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant <note>the planet ruling the rising sign, representing the master</note> and the Moon. If they are joined to the Lord of the seventh house from the Ascendant—which is the second house from the house of servants <note>The 6th house represents servants; the 7th is the 2nd house relative to the 6th, thus representing the servant's money</note>—he will obtain it. Similarly, if the Lord of the seventh is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the seventh is in the Ascendant, or the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the 7th, or if you find a planet <term>transferring light</term> <note>original: "deferentem lumen"; a faster planet moving from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with another</note> from one of them to its partner, he will obtain it.

->Whether the inquirer will have possession or not, namely of a servant.<-

**And if** you are likewise questioned concerning a possession, whether it will come to the one who questioned you or not: look to the 3rd sign from the Ascendant, which is the 10th house from the house of servants. If you find the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon joined to the Lord of the third from the Ascendant, or you find the Lord of the third joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, he will obtain it. Similarly, if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in the 3rd, or the Lord of the third is in the Ascendant, or there is a planet transferring light between them—that is, from the Lord of the Ascendant to the Lord of the third, or from the Lord of the third to the Lord of the Ascendant—he will obtain the predicted possession through the hands of <term>envoys</term> <note>original: "legatorum"; messengers or intermediaries</note>.

->The 7th Sign or the 7th House with its questions: and first, whether a marriage will be perfected or not, and what the agreement between them will be like after it is perfected.<-

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'A' containing a woodcut illustration of a man and a woman (a couple) facing each other.</image-desc>
**When** you are questioned about a marriage, whether it will be completed or not, and if it is completed, how the agreement between them will be: or if it is not completed, by whom the separation or divorce will happen. Assign the Ascendant, its Lord, and the Moon to the inquirer; and the 7th sign and its Lord to the woman. If the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to the Lord of the 7th, or is in the 7th, he will obtain the woman. Similarly, if the Lord of the seventh is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Lord of the 7th is in the Ascendant, the matter will happen with ease, and it will be more by the will of the woman than the man. And if the Moon is transferring light between them, envoys will run between them, and the effect of the matter will be through their hands. After this, look to the <term>receiver of the disposition</term> <note>the planet that 'receives' another into its dignity</note>; that is, the heavier planet. If it is <term>afflicted</term> <note>original: "impeditus"; hindered by a bad aspect</note> by malefics from a 4th aspect <note>a square aspect, 90 degrees</note> or an opposition, or if it is <term>falling</term> <note>original: "cadens"; in a weak house like the 6th, 8th, or 12th</note>, the matter will be destroyed after it had been set straight.

->Question concerning an obstacle or detriment: in what way it will be.<-

**And if** you are questioned in what way the detriment will occur: look to the malefic itself which hinders. If it is the Lord of the 2nd from the Ascendant, or the 8th, the detriment will be on the part of the description of the <term>dowry</term> <note>original: "dotis"</note>. And if it is the Lord of the 12th from the Ascendant, the detriment will be from a reproach of the woman's noble birth. And if it is the Lord of the sixth, it will be on the part of the man's noble birth. And if it is the Lord of the fourth, it will be on the part of the fathers. And if it is the Lord of the third, it will be on the part of the brothers. Understand the remaining signs in this way according to their <term>essences</term> <note>original: "substācias"; their natural significations</note>. And if there is a planet <note>original: "p̃lta", abbreviation for planeta</note> [standing] apart from the conjunction of the Lord of the Ascendant between them, the detriment will be from the substance of its house: that is, if it is the Lord of the 2nd house or the 8th, there will be an entanglement on the part of the description of the dowry. And if it is the Lord of the third, it will be on the part of the brothers; and the 4th on the part of the father and parents; and the 5th because the woman was [previously] married and has a son, and there will be an occasion [for dispute]. And if it is the Lord of the sixth, it will be from illness, or from a vice of her body, or on the part of servants. And if a malefic is the planet that carries the light between them, it will be on the part of the envoys.

->Question concerning the quality of their minds.<-

## Concerning the quality of their minds: look to the conjunction that is be- / tween the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the thing sought. If they as- / pect each other from the 7th sign, which is the aspect of opposition, they signify malice of mind and a multitude of contention. And if the aspect is from the 4th [house], they signify goodness of mind, though sometimes there will be contention there. And if it is a trine or sextile aspect, they signify affection and a good quality of mind. And similarly if the Moon is <term>received</term> <note>a planet being in a sign ruled by the planet it aspects</note>. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is in an angle and the planet is <term>heavy</term> <note>ponderous, or slow-moving</note>—that is, the receiver—the man will be exalted, showing off and conquering the woman; and whichever of them you find falling or "knocking," that one will be conquered and subjected to the Lord, namely of the Ascendant or the Lord of the matter. If, however, they are joined in one sign, they signify contentions. And if the Moon is aspecting the Ascendant and is afflicted, there will be vileness between them. And if a malefic is in the Ascendant, this will be on the part of the man; and understand the other signs according to their essences in the same way. When you see the Sun afflicted, the hindrance will be upon the man; and if Venus is afflicted, it afflicts the woman; when, however, the Moon is afflicted, it will afflict both.

### Column 2

->Question concerning a woman who flees from her husband: whether she will return or not.<-

**And if** you are questioned concerning a woman who has gone out from her house because of the anger of her husband: whether she will return to her house or not. Look to Venus and the Sun, which are the significators of the man and the woman. If Venus is above the earth in an excellent place from the Ascendant, and the Sun is below the earth, it announces the return of the woman to her house with strong delay and hardship. And if the Moon, at the hour she went out of her house or at the hour of the question, is already passing the conjunction <gloss>that is, after the middle of the month</gloss>, her return to her house will be in haste. And if the Moon is increasing in light <gloss>that is, in the beginning of the month</gloss>, her return will be with slowness. And if Venus, the Lady, should go out from her house while retrograde and <term>occidental</term> <note>setting in the west after the sun</note>, her return to her house will be of her own spontaneous will and she will be repentant. And if she is <term>oriental</term> <note>rising in the east before the sun</note>, emerging from under the [sun's] rays and retrograde, she will return, and her husband will be repentant of her going out. And [if the chart says] he will not repent for that which he did as he repented in the first chapter, she herself will repent of her return, but he will not repent for that which he did as he repented in the first chapter.

->Question concerning a woman: whether she is a virgin or deflowered.<-

**And if** you are likewise questioned concerning a woman, whether she is a virgin or deflowered: look at the Ascendant at the hour you were questioned, and its Lord, and the Moon. And if they are in <term>movable</term> <note>cardinal</note> or <term>common</term> <note>mutable</note> signs, she is deflowered, for she has already married. And if the woman thought herself to be a virgin but was deceived and her virginity was taken. And if the Moon is in a common or movable sign, and the Ascendant and its Lord are in a fixed sign, she has already been troubled by someone and her virginity was not well taken <note>this may imply an attempted or incomplete encounter</note>. And if the Moon is with Mars in a movable or common sign, her virginity was already taken in a friendship with men. And if Saturn is in the Ascendant with the Moon in a common or fixed sign, he to whom she was joined used her unnaturally <note>original: "ex nāz" (extra naturam)</note>, and her virginity was not taken [normally]. And if you find Mercury or Jupiter in the triplicity of Venus, or Mars has fallen away from her in an angle and does not aspect her, and Mars is in Aries or Leo or Sagittarius, she will be a virgin.

->Whether a woman has a son or not.<-

If, however, <term>fortunes</term> <note>benefic planets</note> are in common signs, her son will be from justice <note>legitimate marriage</note>. And if both—namely fortunes and malefics—are mixed in movable signs, she will be saddened by her sons.

->Regarding a pregnant woman: whether [the child] is from fornication or not.<-

And if Mars or Saturn or Mercury aspects it, her son will be from fornication. And if the fortunes aspect it, her son will be from justice, and he will be legitimate.

And if any of them is joined to Mars and is in any of his houses, she already loved the man who seeks her, and she wants him to have her. If, however, any of them is joined to Jupiter, she once loved a man higher and nobler than herself, and she still loves him. And if [the significator] is joined to Mercury, she loves a young man more beautiful than her husband, younger in age, and he is a scribe and a merchant. ### ¶ On the contention of two, which of them shall win.
<note>original: "De contentione duorum quis eorum vincet"</note>

**And if** you are questioned concerning a contention that exists between two, which of them shall win and obtain the victory: set the Ascendant and its Lord and the Moon for the inquirer <note>the person asking the question</note> and the 7th house and its Lord for the opponent <note>the adversary</note>. After this, see if both planets are joined together by a **sextile aspect** <note>an angle of 60 degrees</note> or a **trine aspect** <note>an angle of 120 degrees</note>: they will be reconciled before the contention <note>meaning they will settle before the trial or fight</note>. And if they are joined by a **quartile aspect** <note>a square, or 90 degrees</note> or by an **opposition** <note>180 degrees</note>: they will not be reconciled except after war and strife. And if both should come into one sign, there shall be peace between them without the intervention of another and without anyone else entering between them for the sake of making peace. And if the Lord of the Midheaven <note>original: "dominus medii celi"; the ruler of the 10th house, representing the judge or king</note> regards them and there is a conjunction with him before one of them is joined to the other, they will not be reconciled until they come before the king. And if the Moon <term>transfers light</term> <note>original: "transtulerit... lumen"; when the Moon moves from an aspect with one planet to an aspect with the other, acting as a bridge</note> between them, it will be the beginning of peace by the hands of envoys. After this, observe the location of both planets and the Lord of the Ascendant, namely the Lord of the matter <note>the querent</note> and the Lord of the seventh, and their strength; for by this you will understand the strength of those who contend. For he is stronger whose significator is in an <term>angle</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart</note>; and whoever among them is "received" <note>an astrological relationship where one planet is in a sign ruled by the other</note> will have many helpers. And know that the beginning of peace will come from the "pulsating" planet, to wit, from the one who seeks the conjunction and is lighter <note>faster-moving</note>, or from a planet in a <term>cadent house</term> <note>the weaker houses: 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th</note> if it is lighter. And know that the Lord of the 7th, when he is in the Ascendant, signifies the strength of the inquirer; and the Lord of the Ascendant in the 7th signifies the strength of the one about whom the question is asked: for to them goes the victory. And if one significator is **retrograde** <note>appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, it signifies weakness and flight from the business, and also lies for the one whose significator it is. For example, if the Lord of the Ascendant is retrograde, there will be weakness for the inquirer. If however the Lord of the 7th is retrograde, there will be weakness for the opponent. If however the Lord of the Midheaven regards them and is retrograde, it signifies the injustice of the judges and the contention will be prolonged. Similarly if one significator is separated from the other—I mean the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the matter. And know that the Luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note>, if one of them is joined to a significator or is in its house, that party will be stronger and more worthy. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, the master of the inquiry will seek help from the king. If however the Lord of the Midheaven is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, the king will help him without his asking. And if the Lord of the 7th is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, the opponent will request help from the king. If however the Lord of the Midheaven is joined to the Lord of the 7th, the king will help the opponent. When you know the strength of each from the other, and you know they will not be reconciled: look to the king as the judge who judges between them from the Lord of the Midheaven. Then see which of them his significator regards: that is, whether the aforementioned Lord of the Midheaven (who is the significator of the king or judge) regards the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the 7th. And know that the king or judge is with the one whom he regards. And if there is a <term>peregrine</term> planet <note>a planet with no essential dignity or "home" in its current sign</note> in the Midheaven not regarding them, and the Lord of the Midheaven does not regard them: they themselves shall appoint someone to judge justly between them. If Saturn is in the Midheaven and is himself the Lord of the Midheaven: the judge will not judge justly nor truly. And if Mars hinders Saturn: the judge will be blamed for this and will be defamed. And if Mars is in the Midheaven: the judge will be fickle, very fast, sharp, and swift. If however it is Jupiter: the judge will be just. And if it is Venus: he will be fickle and of good spirit, and easily suspicious. And if it is Mercury: he will be sharp of sight. And if the sign of the Midheaven is <term>common</term> <note>a "mutable" sign like Gemini or Pisces</note>: the first judge will not finish their judgment until they go to another judge.

### ¶ Question concerning buying and selling, what will become of it.
<note>original: "Questio de emptione et venditione quid erit de ea"</note>

**And if** you are questioned concerning the buying or selling of any thing: Look in this to the Lord of the 7th and the Lord of the Ascendant. If they are joined, there will be a transaction between them; and the ease will be on the part of the "pulsating" one who is lighter. If however they are not joined and you find between them a planet returning

<column-break/>

light from one to the other: there will be a transaction by the hand of some man who enters between them. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 7th, the buyer will be pursuing the seller. If however the Lord of the 7th is in the Ascendant: the seller will be pursuing the buyer. And if there is a **Fortune** <note>a benefic planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> in the Ascendant, it signifies the ease and truth of the person selling the thing. If however a **Malefic** <note>Saturn or Mars</note> is in it, it will signify his hardness, slowness, and lies. If however a Fortune is in the 7th: it signifies the ease and truth of the buyer; and a Malefic signifies the opposite. And if the Moon has not separated from any planet but is joined: the seller will sell a possession or thing which he did not buy, but possessed from someone; but if he bought it, he has not yet given the price for it. If however she is separated and not joined to any planet: there will be delay and a plea in the purchase. If however the planet from which the Moon separates enters into **combustion** <note>comes too close to the Sun, losing its power</note>: the seller will die before his substance returns to him.

### ¶ Question concerning a fugitive from substance or other lost thing, whether they shall be found.
<note>original: "Questio de fugitiuo a substantia vel alia re perdita si inueniēt"</note>

**And if** you are questioned concerning a fugitive and concerning substance or any lost thing: set the Ascendant and its Lord for the inquirer, and the Lord of the fugitive, whether the fugitive is his own <note>a servant</note> or another. The 7th however and its Lord and the Moon are for the fugitives and the lost thing. Then see if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the 7th: the inquirer will obtain the fugitive through inquiry and his own effort. Similarly if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 7th. And if the Lord of the 7th is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, or the Lord of the 7th is in the Ascendant: he will come of his own spontaneous will before he leaves the land. If however you find the Moon separated from the Lord of the Ascendant and joined to the Lord of the 7th: he will come to the master by an informer who will show him where his servant is. And if she is separated from the Lord of the 7th and joined to the Lord of the Ascendant: the servant will send an envoy to his master to seek safety for himself. And if after this the Lord of the 7th is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant: the servant will return to his master of his own spontaneous will. If however the Lord of the 7th is joined to a Malefic planet in an angle: the fugitive will be captured. But if the Lord of the Ascendant regards a Malefic or the Lord of the 7th: his master will obtain him, but will return property for him. And if either of the Luminaries <note>Sun or Moon</note> is joined to the Lord of the 7th, the place of the fugitive cannot be hidden. If also the Lord of the 7th is <term>under the rays</term> <note>original: "sub radiis"; hidden by the Sun's light</note>: it signifies the finding of the fugitive. And if the Lord of the Ascendant regards him, he will be captured. If the Lord of the 7th is joined to a Malefic: the same fugitive will be captured. And if he is joined to a Fortune, he will not be captured unless that Fortune enters under the rays or becomes retrograde or is hindered; for if it enters into combustion, it will signify his death. And if he is joined to a Malefic and he himself enters under the rays into combustion, his corpse will be found. And if the Moon is joined to a Malefic, he will obtain the fugitive. If however she is joined to a retrograde planet, he will return by himself of his own spontaneous will. And if she is joined to a stationary planet <note>original: "planete stanti"</note>—that is, one which is in its station in an angle or in the house following an angle—the fugitive or wanderer does not move from his place until he is captured. But if the planet is in its first station <note>beginning to go retrograde</note> wanting to go backward, the fugitive will be captured and bound with chains and returned to his master. And if it is in the second station <note>about to go direct</note> when it wants to go straight, he will be captured in part and overcome; after this he will escape from that captivity, and can be captured again. And if the planet to which the Moon is joined is **direct** <note>moving normally</note>, he will be returned without chains. If however the Moon is under the rays and joined to Mars, the fugitive will be burned by fire. And if she is joined to Saturn, he will die in water. If however the Moon regards the Lord of her own house, the property of the fugitive will be seized. And know that when a Malefic is in the 9th house, the fugitive will be captured and brought back. And if a Fortune is there, he cannot be captured. And if the Moon is increased in light and number, his capture will be delayed; and in the waning of the Moon, he will be captured more quickly.

### ¶ Question concerning the location of a fugitive and lost thing, or of the location of a theft.
<note>original: "Questio de loco fugitiui et perditi aut de loco latrociny"</note>

**And if** you are questioned concerning the location of a fugitive and lost thing, or concerning the location of a theft: observe the place of the Moon. If she is in the Ascendant, the fugitive will be in the eastern part. And if she is in the Midheaven, the fugitive will be in the southern part. And if she is in the 7th, he will be in the western part. And if she is in the 4th, he will be in the northern part. And if she is not in any angle: look to the part of the sign, namely in which the planet is, and judge according to the part of the place of the Moon and the sign in which she is.

### ¶ Question if the return of the fugitive to the place from where he fled is better for him than going where he wants.

**As if** a fugitive asks you <note>the astrologer</note> whether his return to the place from whence he came will be better for him than going where he wants: look to the Moon. If she is separated from Malefics, his return to the place from where he fled will be bad for him; and if she is separated from Fortunes, his return will be better. **And since it is asked concerning theft, whether the inquirer himself will obtain it or not.**

**If you are questioned** concerning a theft, and whether it will be obtained when you ask or not: Place the Ascendant <note>the sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and its Lord <note>the planet ruling that sign</note> and the Moon for the inquirer. Place the seventh house and its Lord for the thief, and the Midheaven <note>the 10th house, representing the action or the judge</note> for the act of theft, and the Angle of the Earth <note>the 4th house</note> for the place of the theft. If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the seventh house, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the seventh house, the inquirer will obtain what is sought—that is, the thief along with the investigation. And if with this conjunction the Lord of the second house from the Ascendant—which is the house of property <note>original: "substantia"</note>—is under the Sun’s rays <note>meaning the planet is too close to the Sun to be seen, indicating something hidden</note>, the inquirer will obtain the thief with his investigation, but he will not recover the stolen property. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the seventh house, or the Lord of the seventh is in the Ascendant, the thief shall return what he has stolen. And if with this conjunction the Lord of the second from the Ascendant—who is the Lord of the house of property—is under the rays, the thief will be found, but the stolen property will not be found. And if the planet has emerged from combustion <note>the state of being hidden by the Sun's light</note>, a part of the stolen property will be found. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to a planet in the Angles <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, and it is even better if it is in the Midheaven, the inquirer will catch the thief. If however it is joined to a planet in a falling house <note>original: "cadenti"; houses that do not aspect the Ascendant</note> not regarding the Ascendant, it signifies the departure of the fugitive. And if that planet regards the Ascendant, there is hope—that is, he can have confidence. And if the Lord of the seventh is under the Sun’s rays, it signifies the capture of the thief, and it is even better if the Lord of the Ascendant regards him, because it signifies that the master shall have the thief. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, the Lord of the property shall threaten him through the King or through some other person to be feared. And if they—the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the seventh—do not regard each other, the King or another shall take the property for which he who inquired asked. And if the Lord of the seventh is joined with the Lord of the Midheaven, he will help the thief to return it. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined with the Lord of the Midheaven, the King will help the owner of the property. And if the Moon transfers the light between both significators—that is, between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the seventh—it signifies the capture of the thief. And if the Lord of the seventh is joined to the Lord of the third house from the Ascendant, the thief will go out of the region. If however he is in an Angle from the Ascendant, he will not depart from his place. Through the aspect of malefic planets to the seventh house or to the Lord of the seventh, know that trouble will occur to the thief. And if the Moon is joined to malefic planets, it signifies the loss of the property. And if she is joined to a fortune <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> and that fortune is hindered under the Sun's rays, it signifies the loss of the property. And if she is joined to a planet in the Ascendant or in the seventh house, and that planet is free from malefics, it signifies the recovery of the property. And if the luminaries <note>the Sun and Moon</note> regard each other by a trine or sextile aspect, it signifies the recovery of the theft and the returned thing. If either of the luminaries—that is, the Sun or the Moon—is in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven. If however they regard each other from a square aspect <note>90 degrees</note> or opposition <note>180 degrees</note>, the recovery will be after desperation and entanglement. And if either luminary regards the Part of Fortune <note>an Arabic Part calculated from the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant</note> or is with it in one sign, the theft will be found; and more quickly if the Sun regards it. If however the Moon regards the Part of Fortune or is joined to it in one sign, there will be some delay in its recovery. But if neither luminary regards the Part of Fortune or the Ascendant, and the luminaries do not regard each other, the theft will never be found.
**How to know regarding that which went away or perished, whether the stolen property will be found or not.**

**And if** you wish to know whether that which went away will be found or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If either of them is joined to the Lord of the second house from the Ascendant, or if some planet has returned its light to him—that is, if it carries the light between them—it signifies the recovery of the property. Similarly, if some planet has joined their light—that is, if both are joined to some heavier planet <note>a slower-moving planet like Saturn or Jupiter</note>. Because if the Lord of the second, who is the significator of property, is in the Ascendant, it signifies recovery, though after a little while. Similarly, if the Lord of the second from the Ascendant is joined to a planet that is in the second sign from the Ascendant. And if the Lord of the second from the Ascendant does not regard it, the property will perish. Similarly, if the Lord of the eighth from the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the seventh, who is the significator of the thief; and if the Lord of the seventh is joined to the Lord of the second, it signifies the loss of the property. But if the Lord of the eighth, who is the significator of the thief's property, is joined to the Lord of the second, who is the significator of the inquirer's property and those things which he lost, he will find the property and take a portion of the thief's property; and it is even better if the Lord of the Ascendant regards them. For if the Lord of the Midheaven regards them, the King shall take what I have said. And if the Lord of the eighth is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, who is the significator of the King, the thief will appease the King with gifts. If however the Lord of the second from the Ascendant does not

regard the Ascendant or its Lord, the property will be lost entirely and there will be no mention of it. If however the Lord of the second from the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the third, seventh, or ninth, or to some planet in them, or if the Lord of the seventh is in them: it signifies the departure of the stolen property from the region. And know that when both luminaries are under the earth <note>below the horizon</note>, the thief will be unknown forever. If however the Moon is in the Ascendant and its Lord, and the Sun regards them, that which went away or perished or was taken by theft shall be found and returned quickly; and more easily if the aspect is a trine.

->Question of the thief, whether he be a stranger or not.<-

**And if** you wish to know whether the thief is a stranger or not: look to the luminaries. If both are in the Ascendant, the thief will be from the household. And if one of them regards the Ascendant and the other does not regard it, he will be associated with them but not from the household. Similarly, if you find the Lord of the Ascendant in the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the seventh is with the Lord of the Ascendant, the thief will be from the inhabitants of the house. And if the luminaries are in their own houses <note>the signs they rule</note>, or in the houses of the Lord of the Ascendant regarding the Ascendant, or if it is the Lord of the Ascendant himself: the thief will be from the inhabitants of the house. And if he is in his own triplicities <note>a group of three signs of the same element</note>, the thief will be from their relatives, but he does not stay with them in the house. And if he is in his own terms or faces <note>smaller subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note>, he will be an intimate from the inhabitants of the house, and it is thought that there is some relationship between them and he frequents them. And if two luminaries are in any matter we have mentioned, and one of them regards the Ascendant and its Lord, he himself is an intimate to the people of that house and frequents them. If however some luminary regards the Ascendant and does not regard the seventh, he did not enter the house before that time when he stole, unless one luminary is in a common sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>; then he has already entered it again with those inhabitants doing it, because a common sign signifies repetition. But if one luminary regards the Lord of the Ascendant and does not regard the Ascendant, he will be known to the inhabitants of the house, but he has not entered the house specifically. But if the house of the Ascendant has already fallen from the degree of the Ascendant and another planet is with it in that sign in which the degree of the Ascendant is, the thief will be closer, from certain of the inhabitants of the house. If however the Lord of the seventh is in the ninth from his own house, the thief will not be from that region. But if he is in the sixth or the eighth from his own house, it will be a male or female servant. If however he is in his exaltation, the thief will be a noble. And if he is in his own house, he will be from the inhabitants of the house known among them. And if he is in his triplicity or in his term or in his face, he will not be known in his region, but nonetheless he will be known in the neighborhood and in his dwelling.

# Zabel
<note>Likely referring to Sahl ibn Bishr, a 9th-century Jewish astrologer and mathematician whose works were foundational to medieval European astrology.</note>

[If the Moon] is at the beginning of the month: the thief will be a youth. If it is in the middle of the month: he will be of middle age, that is, a mature man. And if it is at the end of the month: he will be an old man. If, however, the Sun is the significator <note>The planet representing the person or object in question</note> and is between the Ascendant and the Midheaven, the thief will be of young age; and thus you shall not cease to increase the age until you arrive at the Angle of the Earth <note>The 4th House, representing the northern point of the chart</note>, which is the place of the end of life.

### Investigation of the place where the theft is located.

If you are asked about the location of the theft, look to see if the sign is an Earth sign. If it is Cancer or its triplicity <note>The group of three signs belonging to the same element; here, the Water signs: Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces</note>, the stolen item will be buried near water, and that will be its place. If it is Taurus or its triplicity <note>The Earth signs: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn</note>, it will be in a place of oxen or cows; for Taurus signifies a place of cows nearby, Virgo signifies a place of harvests and grain, and Capricorn a place of sheep. And if it is Gemini or its triplicity <note>The Air signs: Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius</note>, it will be in a home, or in a chest, or in a place higher than the ground. 

If the theft is inside a house and you wish to know its location within that house: look to the Lord of the fourth house and the planet that is there. If it is Saturn: it will be in the latrine of the house, or in a more remote, unclean, deep, or dark place. If it is Jupiter: it signifies a place of woods or an oratory <note>A small chapel or place of prayer</note>. Mars signifies the kitchen or a place of fire. The Sun signifies the courtyard of the house or the sitting room of the master of the house. Venus signifies the sitting room of the women. Mercury signifies a place of painted buildings and books, or a place of grain, or a granary in Virgo. And if it is the Moon: it will be next to a well, a cistern, or a laundry. Know that when the stolen item is in the fourth house from the Ascendant, the theft will be in a clean and beautiful place, and it was committed by someone noble. If, however, there is a malefic <note>An "evil-doing" planet, usually Saturn or Mars</note> in that place: it will be in a horrid and foul-smelling place, and was committed by someone ignoble. <insert>Whether the stolen thing be one or many.</insert>

And if you are asked about the number of stolen items: whether it is property or something else that is possessed. Look at the signs that are between the Moon and Mercury. If there are even signs between them, there will be a gathering or more than one item. If there are odd signs between them, it will be a single thing.

### Whether he who is under suspicion is the thief or not.

If you are asked about a man caught under suspicion, whether he was the thief or not: look at this just as you look at rumors to see if they are true or not. Use the Moon also as a witness; if she is afflicted by a malefic, he himself is the thief. If you are asked about any man whether he has stolen anything or not: look to the Lord of the Ascendant and the stronger Moon. If they have taken <note>original: "acceperit"</note> anything from the malefics—that is, if they have separated from them—he has stolen it. This is even truer if he is separated from the Lord of his own house, that is, from the Lord of the second house from the Ascendant <note>The house governing personal wealth</note>. If he has not taken anything from the malefics, he has stolen nothing.

### Investigation into what the stolen thing is.

If you are asked what the stolen thing itself is: look at the place of the Moon by its signs and terms <note>A "term" is a specific subdivision of a zodiac sign ruled by a particular planet</note>. If she is in the term of Saturn, it will be of those things necessary for working the earth. If Saturn is then in the Ascendant or in the tenth house in Taurus or its triplicity (such as Virgo and Capricorn). If it is in the fourth house from the Ascendant or in the seventh, it will be another substance. And if it is falling <note>original: "cadens," meaning in a weak house</note> from the Ascendant and no luminary <note>The Sun or Moon</note> regards it, or if it is in Aries: it signifies the malice of that thing and its worthlessness, such as a horrid or foul-smelling thing. 

If Saturn is in Gemini or its triplicity, there will be two substances. And if Jupiter is in the Midheaven looking at Saturn: one of those substances will be gold. If it is in the term of Jupiter: look at the planet and its place; if any planet regards it, the thing itself will be gold or silver, or anything made by fire. If Venus regards Jupiter or if Jupiter is in her term: it will be a pearl. If Jupiter is in Taurus or its triplicity, the thing will be useful to the rich, or clothing—that is, whatever it is, it will be made of clothing or pertains to clothing. If it is in Gemini or its triplicity (like Libra and Aquarius): it will be a living substance or something proceeding from animals. If it is in Cancer or its triplicity (like Scorpio and Pisces): it will be something extracted from water, such as a pearl. And if the Moon is in the term of Mars, the thing itself has already passed through fire

<column-break/>

or in some way fire has touched it. If the Moon regards Venus: a dye has already been worked into it. And if the Moon is in the term of Venus and in Aries or its triplicity: it will be gold or silver. If it is in Taurus or its triplicity, or in Cancer and its triplicity: it will be an ornate garment or a type of precious silk woven with various colors and different patterns. And you shall know the quality of the substance and its beauty from the place of Venus in the signs; for if she is in Gemini and its triplicity, that thing will not be made of animal substances. If Venus has emerged from under the Sun's rays <note>meaning she is far enough from the Sun to be visible</note>, it will be a new thing. If she is retrograde <note>appearing to move backward</note>, or at the end of her course, or diminished in number, it will be an old and worn thing. 

If she is in Aries and its triplicity: it will be coins. If she is in Gemini and its triplicity: those coins were taken from a small bag or from some vessel covered in red leather. After this, look at the place of the Moon: if she is in Aries, it will be a thing placed upon the head and face. If she is in Taurus: it will be an ornament or a thing hung on the neck, or a precious substance. If she is in Gemini: it will be coins if Mercury regards her. If he does not regard her, it will be made of hides. If she is in Cancer: it will be a thing raised from the water, or something moist or soaked. If she is in Leo and the Sun regards her: it will be gold or silver. If the Sun does not regard her: it will be iron or brass <note>original: "auricalcum"</note>. 

If she is in Virgo and Mercury regards her: it will be coins. If he does not regard her: it will be clothing. If she is in Libra and Venus regards her: it will be a thing sold by weight and of good scent, or things with which women adorn themselves. If she does not regard her: it will be an animal, and a commodity such that there is blood in it. If she is in Scorpio and Mars regards her: it will be gold or silver. If he does not regard her: it will be copper or something worked by fire that is shiny. If she is in Sagittarius and Jupiter regards her: it will be more than one substance, or a dyed thing. If he does not regard her: it will be a cheap thing, less than what I have said, and not precious. If she is in Capricorn: it will be an ancient or stinking and cheap thing. If Saturn regards her: it will be of the substance of the earth and seeds. If she is in Aquarius and its Lord regards her: it will be an animal or extracted from animals. If Jupiter regards her: it will be gold or silver. If the Sun and Mercury regard the Moon: it will be coins and they will be in leather. And if she is in Pisces and Jupiter regards her: it will be pearls or amber or something produced from water. If he does not regard her: it will be silk and of various colors.

### Concerning what the taken or stolen thing is and the manner of the thing.

And if you are asked about a thing taken by theft, what it is and its manner: if you wish to know the manner of the stolen thing, then consider if the Lord of the term in which the Moon is situated is going toward Venus and the Sun regards her: then they are denarii <note>Roman silver coins, used here as a general term for money</note> or gold in which there is a carving or image, or purple cloth, or something similar made of precious, praiseworthy fabrics of good manufacture. And if it is Venus and the Moon regards her: then it is a thing from her domain in which there are shapes and things of good manufacture made of cloth, such as scarlet cloths and those dyed from hemp and herbs and similar things. 

And if Mercury regards her: it is from those things of good manufacture such as cloths made of... <note>original: "ets," likely a scribal error for "aetis" or "textis"</note> and those which come from animals such as a hood and silk and wool; and those things that are such, and which have been made with industry, decorum, and right measurement. And if Mars regards her: then it is a thing in which there are fabricated shapes or what is made with fire and iron and similar things. And if Saturn regards her: it is an ancient thing in which there are shapes or dyes or a decorously fashioned stone; and it is of those things made of clay or stones and similar things. And if Jupiter regards her: they are things in which shapes are made from the hides of an animal and similar things. 

And if the Lord of the Moon’s term is Mercury: then they are books. And if the Sun regards him: they are from the decorations of a book or a throne of kings; and perhaps there is some gold in them or a description on something made of gold. And if the Moon herself regards him: then they are things in which there are papers, or of clever inventions, or of taking and giving, or of agriculture and similar things; and perhaps it is silver or inscriptions in silver. And if Venus herself regards him: then they are books and things in which there is carving and good formation; and perhaps there is silver and gold in them, or a similar description in silver and gold. And if the Sun and Jupiter regard him together: then it is a precious substance of those which kings receive or make and with which women are decorated; and perhaps there is with them a sublime fragrance of spices which is sharp, such as musk and amber and aloeswood <note>original: "xylogloes"</note> and things that are so. # On Interrogations
<note>Latin: *De interrogationibus*. In astrology, an "interrogation" is a formal question posed to an astrologer to be answered by a chart cast for the moment of the query.</note>

...their [meaning] and the books in which there are praise, exaltation, and parables of the just. And if the planet looking upon it <note>aspecting it</note> is **Saturn**, they are books containing songs and exorcisms, and things in which there are no truths; and perhaps there are in them fabrications of iron or stone upon which there are inscriptions.

$\mathbb{R}$ If it is **Retrograde**, it is of a twisted shape, or there is a break or a blemish in it from its twisted path. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If it is not [clear] because of its effort in adherence, let the diversity be judged by that which excuses it.

$\mathbb{R}$ If it is in a **Succeedent Angle**, it is between strength and weakness, and between fitness and unfitness. 

And if it is **Fortunate** <note>associated with Jupiter or Venus</note>, it is healthy and of good nature. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If it is **Unfortunate** <note>associated with Saturn or Mars</note>, it is foul, harmful, or blemished. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If it is in its [proper] **Figure**, it is fitting in its goodness. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If it is outside its Figure, it is unfitting in its goodness, or there is an accident in it that hinders it. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If it follows the diversity of what I have told from the aspect of its Lord, then diversify the judgment by which you judged according to the aspect of its Lord. Likewise, the rectitude <note>direct motion</note> or retrogradation of the **Lord of the Inquirer** <note>original: "dñi hoī"</note> testifies to a similarity, as does the **Lord of the Moon** and all things that testify from the dispositions of the Lord of the Moon.

### $\mathbb{C}$ A question regarding the partnership of two people and what its end will be.

**And if** you are interrogated about the participation and partnership of someone: Look to the **Inquirer** from the Ascendant, and to his **Partner** from the 7th house. Look to their **Being** from the Midheaven <note>The 10th House, representing the success of the venture</note> and their **End** from the Angle of the Earth <note>The 4th House</note>. 

If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in **Movable Signs** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, there will be disturbance in their participation, but it will endure afterward. 

And if they are in **Fixed Signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, their partnership will be durable. 

If, however, they are in **Common Signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, their participation will be with profit, or their society will be with security and faithfulness of each to the other. 

And if there is a **Malefic** <note>Mars or Saturn</note> in the Ascendant, injury, lies, and separation will come from the Inquirer. 

Likewise, if there is a Malefic in the 7th, injury will come from the Partner. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If the Moon is joined to the Lord of her own House, they will separate with affection and profit. 

If, however, she does not aspect him, they will separate through the suspicion they have for one another. 

If there are Malefics beneath the earth <note>in the 4th house</note>, they will separate because of the poor opinion they have toward each other. 

And if there are **Benefics** <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> in the Midheaven, their profit will be multiplied. 

If, however, there is a Malefic there, their profit will be diminished. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If the Moon is joined to the Lord of her house in one sign, or if both are joined to a Malefic, they will not separate except by death.

$\mathbb{C}$ Regarding one wishing to go to a Great Man, whether he will find him or not.

$\mathbb{R}$ If he is in the **Second Angle** <note>a Succeedent House</note>, he will be near his place. 

$\mathbb{R}$ If he is **Cadent**, that man will not be in his place.

### $\mathbb{C}$ Regarding a leader setting out for war, or someone inquiring anxiously for him.
