# On Conflicts and War

**Column 1:**

If the lord <note>The planet that rules the sign on the house's edge</note> of the ascendant <note>the 1st house, representing the person asking the question</note> is among the superior planets and is falling away from the ascendant, and the lord of the 7th house <note>representing the enemy or opponent</note> is in an angle <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are positions of great strength</note> and is among the inferior planets, do not judge the querent <note>the person asking</note> to be the victor until you look to see what the lord of the 7th house joins. For if it joins a planet in an angle that receives it, the enemy will be the victor; he will overcome the querent and have power and victory over him according to the strength of that part to which the lord of the 7th is joined. 

But if the lord of the 7th is strong and joined to a falling planet that hinders it, the lord of the 7th will not cease, for the enemy here will have strength for a long time in his own place of choice. And when it is moved from that same place, it is weakened, and it will not stop being weak until it is hindered by the "malifics" <note>the planets Mars or Saturn</note>—namely, the lord of the 7th—or is combust <note>so close to the Sun that its power is "burned up"</note>; and then the enemy will perish. 

If indeed it is joined to no planet in the sign in which it is, it will change into the second sign; after this, look at its conjunction with planets and do not judge by the strength of the inferior planets except by the goodness of its place relative to the ascendant, and by its liberation from the planets that hinder it, and by the help of other planets toward it. 

And if the lord of the ascendant is in the 7th, it signifies the strength of the enemy, because the querent is likened to the conquered; it is even more grave if the lord of the 7th looks upon <note>aspects</note> him, because it signifies that the enemy will overcome the querent. And if the lord of the 7th is in the ascendant, it signifies the strength of the querent; and if the lord of the ascendant looks upon him, the querent will overcome the enemy. 

And if the lord of the ascendant is in the 8th <note>the house of death</note>, or is joined to the lord of the 8th, or the lord of the 8th is joined to him: it signifies the death of the querent. Similarly, if the lord of the 7th is in the 2nd house from the ascendant <note>which is the 8th house—the house of death—relative to the enemy's 7th house</note>, or is joined to the lord of the second, or the lord of the second is joined to him, it signifies the death of the enemy; and this is more certain if the lord of the house is hindered by malifics and does not receive the one "knocking" on it—namely, the one joining it. 

And if the lord of the ascendant is joined to the lord of the Midheaven <note>the 10th house, representing the King or the Judge</note>, or the lord of the Midheaven is joined to the lord of the ascendant, or the lord of the ascendant is in the Midheaven: it signifies the strength of the querent in his kingdom, and that he will overcome the one who contends with him. This is even better if he is a "receiver" in an angle, because the opponent will be conquered; for no one will be able to stand against him, nor will the opponent have any confidence in his kingdom, and he will overcome the one who contends with him. 

Similarly, if the lord of the 7th from the ascendant is in the 4th house, or is joined to its lord, or the lord of the 4th is joined to him and he is a "receiver" in an angle: the enemy will be joined, and no one will be able to stand with him, and he will fear the kingdom of the querent. And if one of the significators is joined to any planet in an angle, or to the lord of an angle, it is even better if he himself is in an angle: because then they signify the strength of the lord of that same significator. 

And similarly if one of the two significators is in an angle, free from malifics, and "received," it is even better if it is in a fixed sign. And if it is not free from malifics and is in a moveable sign, it signifies death for him shortly after the acquisition. 

And when the lord of the ascendant is in the 12th house from the ascendant, it signifies the flight of the querent. Similarly, when the lord of the 7th is in the 6th house, it signifies the flight of the enemy. And if one significator is retrograde, it signifies the ruin and weakness of the lord of that same significator. And if the lord of the 10th is in the ascendant, it signifies that the King provides help to the querent. Similarly, if it is in the 7th from the ascendant, it signifies that the King helps the enemy. 

If, however, one of the luminaries <note>the Sun or Moon</note> offers its disposition to one of the significators—that is, if it is joined to him—it signifies the strength of the lord of that same significator, and that he has help from the King. And if the Moon is separated from the lord of the ascendant and joined to the lord of the 7th, victory will go to the enemy. 

And know that when Saturn is in an angle at the hour of the interrogation, if there is no testimony for it, it signifies the prolongation of the war until it recedes from there; and it is more certain if it is retrograde, because the war will then be repeated often. And if the Moon is with Mars, and the fortunes <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> are falling away from her: then the querent will be killed or captured. 

And if the Sun is with the Head or Tail <note>the North or South Nodes of the Moon</note> when the war begins, there will be a great slaughter of both armies; and there will be no peace between them. For if the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 7th are with the Tail <note>the South Node</note>, only a few will remain from both armies. 

Look for the strength of the war and its terror from Mars and his place from the ascendant, and from that which looks upon him; and look for the smallness or greatness of the slaughter from the Moon, and from her condition and her place. And look for the condition of the leaders and their age from the two significators. Look to the planet from which Mars is separating; set this as the significator of the querent and the beginner [of the conflict]. And look to which planet Mars is joining; set this as the significator of the enemy. After this, look at one of the two significators: for he who was in a moveable sign will be weaker, and from him flight is feared; and he who was in a common sign signifies that the lord of that significator will be persevering in war; and the sign 

<column-break/>

will signify the stability of the matter which will remain so. Next, look at their strength as I shall tell you: if one of the significators is in his exaltation, he will be stronger than if he were in his own house <note>domicile</note>; and the house is stronger than the triplicity; and the triplicity is stronger than the term; and the term is stronger than the face <note>these are the "Essential Dignities," a ranking of how much power a planet has based on its zodiacal position</note>. From both planets, the more worthy is the one who looks upon the lord of his own house, because then he doubles his strength. And then a planet will be more cunning when it is in its descension, or in the place of its enmity, and the lord of its house does not look upon it. 

And if one of the two significators is in his exaltation, the lord of that significator will be a King. If however he is in his own house, he will be from the relatives or household of the King. And if he is in his triplicity, he will be from the sons of nobles. If he is in his term, he will be below those. And if he is in his face, he will be below that one. And if the lord of the house of the significator is looking upon him, it signifies the boldness of the leader and his soldiers, and that he is faithful to the King. If however the lord of his house does not look upon him, he will not be well faithful. 

And whichever of the significators is retrograde and hindered himself, he provokes toward falsehood; and whichever of them is direct and fortunate, he provokes toward truth and faith. Look also to Mars: if he is in his exaltation or in the exaltation of the Sun, the war will be manifest and will be famous. If however he is with the fortunes in the Midheaven, he will strengthen the war until it is heard in the East and the West. And if he is in the ascendant, it will be as I told you. And if he is in the western angle <note>the 7th house</note>, there will be cunning and stability there, and the battle will multiply. If however Mars is in a fixed sign and not in an angle, the war will be as mentioned above. And if he is in a common sign, the war will be often repeated and will multiply. If however he is in a moveable sign, the war will be strong. And if he is in his own house or triplicity, it will be moderate. And if he is in his descension, the war will not be magnified but will be separated in a short time; and announce according to what you see of the strength of Mars and his weakness. 

And know that when the Moon is in the ascendant and Mars in the 7th, or conversely Mars in the ascendant and the Moon in the 7th, he who goes to battle and he who begins it will be killed. And look at the multitude of soldiers and helpers from the aspect of the planets to the significators and from their presence in their own houses; and set the 2nd sign and its lord as the significators of the querent's soldiers; and the 8th and its lord as the significators of the enemy's soldiers; and the 11th sign and its lord as the significators of the King's helpers and ministers. The 5th, however, and its lord are the significators of the city and those who are in it. 

If however there are fortunes in the 2nd sign from the ascendant, or they look upon it and the lord of the 2nd is in a good place, they signify the strength of the querent's soldiers and their fidelity and help to him. Similarly, through the 8th from the ascendant, the strength of the enemy's soldiers is signified. And if there are fortunes which are in the 2nd or 8th from the ascendant in a common sign, or in a sign of many children <note>fruitful signs like Pisces or Cancer</note>, or in a moveable sign, announce a multitude of his soldiers. And if a planet is oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note> in the 2nd house, or the lord of the 2nd is oriental, many times the querent asks for the truth. If however he is retrograde, they will disobey him. 

And if you find a malific in the 11th from the ascendant or the lord of the 11th retrograde, the King's counselors and his helpers are always traitors, especially if a malific planet or Mercury is in the 8th from the Sun, and the Tail is with the Sun; because the King even with his associates is a great evildoer, very harmful or injurious. 

When, however, you wish to know if two leaders will be pacified, look at the planet that signifies this: if he is in his own house, the one who enters between them will be from among themselves. And if he is [not] in his own house, he will be a foreigner. If indeed it is Saturn, it will be an old man. And if it is Jupiter, he will be noble and great. If however it is Mars, he will be a leader from their leaders, and he wishes for evil and even feels a lie. And if it is the Sun, it will be a King or the head of a pilgrimage. 

And if it is Venus, he will be a refined man not having discipline or genius. And if it is the Moon, it will be a man who comes between them with goodness and justice. And look for betrayal and cunning in Mercury; if he is hindered by the aspects from both planets, there will be betrayal and cunning added from each of them—namely, toward his associate. And if Mars is with Mercury, that same cunning and betrayal will appear openly; for it will be made public and cannot be hidden. The planets are also witnesses when they look upon each other and when they are in one sign. And if the Moon and Saturn are witnesses to the ascendant, judge that betrayal has already been or will be. Similarly, when Jupiter provides testimony to the Moon and the ascendant, they signify good. If however Venus provides testimony to the Moon and the ascendant, they do not signify betrayal. <header>On Inquiries</header>

**Column 1:**

Mercury ascending or with the Moon signifies cunning and perdition. For even the "peacemaker" <note>A planet acting as an intermediary between two conflicting planets</note> who was between them—namely Mercury—if he is found under the rays <note>original: "sub radijs"; this means the planet is too close to the Sun to be seen, weakening its power</note> and the Moon is with Mars or with the planet from which Mars is separating, that peacemaker will be captured. And if Mercury himself is oriental <note>rising before the Sun</note>, distress will find him, yet he shall be liberated from it. If Mercury is in a common sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, the peacemaker running between them will not be one alone. If a malefic planet <note>Mars or Saturn</note> is exalted above Mercury, he will find grave sentences and be afflicted; but if a fortune <note>Jupiter or Venus</note> is exalted above him, he shall escape. If Mercury is joined to Mars, he will be one who is afflicted by warriors. If it is the Sun, it will be the King or the head of the armies. 

You should know the cause from which a war is stirred: when you wish to know, look to Mars. For the planet from which Mars separates signifies the one beginning the war, and the one to whom Mars joins signifies the adversary. If he is separated from the fortunes, the initiator and the querent <note>the person asking the question</note> seek the truth. If he is separated from the malefics, he does not seek the truth. If Mars is joined to the fortunes, the enemy seeks the truth; but if he is joined to a malefic, he does not seek the truth.

And if Mars is in the ascendant <note>the 1st House</note>, the war will be for the sake of victory. If he is in the 2nd, it will be for the sake of substance <note>wealth or resources</note>. If in the 3rd, for the sake of faith and religion. If in the 4th, it will be for the sake of land. If he is in the 5th, it signifies that the war is for substance, and that it is between neighboring leaders, and perhaps they will be pacified; or it will be a war for the sake of a woman or a city—especially if you find the Moon joined to Mercury out of affection, then the war is for the sake of a city, to which they travel wishing to take it. If he is in the 6th, the war will be for a weak thing, and there will be much killing or wounding. If in the 7th, it will be for the sake of an old enmity, and they do not seek substance. If in the 8th, it will be for the sake of an old matter, an inquiry of blood. 

But if the Moon aspects the Lord of the Midheaven <note>the 10th House, representing the ruler or the goal</note>, this will be for the sake of the substance of the kingdom, and the killing will be multiplied in both peoples. If in the 9th, for the sake of faith. If the Moon is in the Midheaven and joined to Mars by a 4th aspect <note>a square (90 degrees), usually indicating friction</note> or by opposition, or is with him in one sign, the war will be for the honor of the King or the magnification of the King, and for the inquiry of the kingdom. If in the 11th, it will be for friends and for those who are lesser than the King. If in the 12th, the war will be for an old enmity, but there will be no war; for Mars in the 12th does not signify war, because it is "cadent" from an angle <note>falling away from the strong points of the chart</note>; for those who travel to them will be heard and obeyed, if God wills.

### ¶ Inquiry whether the army is large or small.

**And** if you are asked about an army, whether it be large or modest: take the number of signs between the Moon and Mercury. If the number is even, the army will be large. If the number is odd, the army will be small. After this, look in all matters of war to the 15th chapter, which is universal for all things of war: this is so that you may know that the ascendant is the significator for those beginning the war and its cause; and what it was that stirred that war; and whether it began with truth or with a lie. 

The 2nd house from the ascendant signifies whether there will be a war or not, and whether it will be for profit or loss. 
The 3rd from the ascendant signifies arms, and in which kinds of arms there will be victory and attainment, and which kinds of arms are not necessary in the war itself. 
The 4th from the ascendant signifies the place in which the war will be: whether it will be in the fields, or the mountains, or on the shore of the Great Sea, or near a river; or if there are fruit-bearing trees or a grove in that same place. 
The 5th from the ascendant signifies the probity and facility of the soldiers, their movement, and their boldness or laziness. 
The 6th from the ascendant signifies the animals of the soldiers, and what they are: whether they are horses, asses, mules, or camels. 
The 7th signifies the enemy and the work of "alnagenie" <note>likely siege engines or catapults for throwing stones</note>, and whether the war is with cunning, ingenuity, and conspiracy. 
The 8th signifies wounds, captures, death, breaks, and the flight of the victors. 
The 9th signifies the work of spies and the knowledge of the enemy's king, and his rumors and cunnings. 
The 10th from the ascendant signifies the custom or the act of the greater leader and the other leaders who are under his command. 
The 11th signifies their arrangement, and how their battle lines and groups will be, and how they set fires and their arrangement against the enemy. 
The 12th signifies the city and those who besiege it and fight against it. 

Therefore, look to these 12 places and the places of their lords, and the aspect of those malefics or fortunes who look upon each house among them; and what is within them, whether it be a fortune or a malefic; and who aspects the lord of each house. After this, speak according to what you see from the aspects of the fortunes

<column-break/>

and the misfortunes, and regarding their strength and weakness. For when a fortune aspects a sign, it signifies fortune and good for that same sign; but a malefic, when it aspects from the 4th aspect or opposition, or is in the same sign, sends hindrance and evil into it—namely, into those things which pertain to that sign according to the significations I have explained to you in this chapter.

### ¶ The 8th Sign or eighth house with its inquiries: and first whether an absent person or any man lives or not.

**When** you are asked about an absent man or any other man, whether he lives or is dead: look to the lord of the ascendant and the Moon. If they are in the 4th house from the ascendant, or in the house of death (which is the 8th from the ascendant), or if they are combust, or in their "siege" <note>enclosed between two malefic planets</note>, or with the lord of the house of death, or with the lord of the 4th house, he will be dead. And if you find any of them so, look to the aspect of the malefics and fortunes toward them. If the lord of the ascendant is retrograde in the 4th, or retrograde in its "descension" <note>its place of weakness or fall</note>, or retrograde in the house of death, or separated from the lord of the house of death by retrogradation: look if he returns to the degree of combustion; if so, he will be dead. 

And if the Moon joins a planet under the earth <note>below the horizon</note>, he will be dead; but if she joins a planet above the earth, he lives. And if you find the lord of the ascendant in the 12th with malefics, or if a malefic aspects him and either of the luminaries <note>the Sun or Moon</note> is hindered, you shall judge death for him. If any malefic is in the same sign with the luminaries (which are the Sun and Moon) without the aspect of the fortunes, it signifies death. Similarly, if the Moon is with Mars in the 4th and a fortune does not aspect her; and similarly when the Part of Fortune is with malefics in the 4th from the ascendant, or in the 6th or 12th, and the fortunes do not aspect them, they signify death. 

And know that whatever is above the earth signifies life, and whatever is below the earth signifies death. Therefore, when you find the lord of the ascendant combust under the rays and no fortune aspects him, and the Moon is below the earth falling from the ascendant in the 3rd or 6th: know that he about whom the question is asked is dead—especially if it happens that the Moon is in Scorpio in its 3rd degree, hindered by Saturn, because that naturally signifies death; then you shall verify the death of the one about whom the inquiry is made.

### ¶ The 9th Sign or 9th house with its inquiries: and first whether there is a pilgrimage or not: and if it cannot be completed, what prohibits it.

**When** you are asked about a pilgrimage <note>or a long journey</note>, whether it will happen or not, and if it cannot be completed, what it will be that hinders or prohibits it: look to the lord of the ascendant and the Moon, who are the significators of the querent; and the ninth sign and its lord, who are the significators of the pilgrimage. If the lord of the ascendant or the Moon is in the 9th, or one of them is joined to the lord of the 9th, the pilgrimage sought by the person will not be horrible. And if the lord of the 9th is in the ascendant or is joined to the lord of the ascendant, a journey will happen to him which cannot be frustrated at all. 

But if the condition of the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 9th is not as predicted, and some planet has returned or carried their light to one another, it signifies the pilgrimage by "translation of light" <note>original: "translatio luminis"; when a faster planet connects two slower ones</note>. But if this is not so, and you find the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 9th joined to a heavier planet and that planet aspects the house of pilgrimage, it signifies the pilgrimage; if it does not aspect, he will not go. Likewise, if the lord of the ascendant is in an angle and joined to a planet that is on the left side of the ascendant (that is, between the ascendant and the 3rd house) and it is free from malefics, it signifies the pilgrimage. 

But if the lord of the ascendant and the Moon are joined to any planet in an angle, he will not go. If the significators are joined to each other—namely the lord of the ascendant and the lord of the 9th—and there is a malefic "pilgrim" <note>a planet in a sign where it has no essential dignity</note> in the ascendant hindering the lord of the ascendant or the lord of the 9th, there will be no pilgrimage. This will happen on the part of the man—that is, on the part of the querent—something will happen to him that disturbs and prohibits his pilgrimage. If that malefic is in the 7th, the hindrance will come from that same land to which he wished to travel or from the matter he was seeking, and it will frustrate and prohibit his pilgrimage. If the malefic is in the Midheaven, gravity <note>trouble or weight</note> will come to him from the King or from one who is above him or rules him. 

And if the lord of the ascendant is joined to the lord of the house of the journey, and is afterwards joined to a malefic by opposition or by conjunction or by a 4th aspect, or is with him in one sign: announce the distress that will occur to him after the pilgrimage according to the quality of the enmity of that sixth planet <note>likely referring to the lord of the 6th house</note>—namely, if it is the lord from the ascendant, he will be ill.

# On Interrogations

If indeed the Lord of the 3rd or 9th house is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant <note>the planet ruling the rising sign</note>, someone else will work on his behalf and he will be freed without his own petition. If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the 12th house and is to the left of the Ascendant, it signifies his escape from prison. ¶ After this, look—once you have finished looking at the Lord of the Ascendant and its conjunction with the stars, and the conjunction of the stars with it—at the place of the signifier, which is the Moon. If she is in a movable sign <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn</note>, it signifies speed of liberation, except for Cancer, which is slow because it is her own house; Aries and Libra are faster in liberation than Capricorn, and he shall not tarry in prison and will find many helpers there. Capricorn, however, signifies slowness, solitude, and sadness, and that enemies are working so that he may be held in chains. And if she is in a fixed sign <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius</note>, it signifies slowness of exit, and the slowest of all is Aquarius. If, however, the Moon is in a common sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, and he is not freed before the Moon departs from that sign, his imprisonment will be prolonged; and even more so if it is a house of Jupiter <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note> and Jupiter himself does not look upon them. In the houses of Mercury <note>Gemini or Virgo</note>, if there is an imposition, he will find good and joy in that very prison. Then look at her conjunction if she is in an Angle; if she is joined to a part on the left of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Ascendant bears witness, it similarly signifies liberation. And if the Moon is falling <note>in a cadent house: 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th</note> and is joined to any part in an Angle, it signifies a prolongation of prison, unless that part is the Lord of the 3rd or 9th; then he will be freed when that part is changed. And if it is falling, and joined to a falling part which is the Lord of some Angle, he will be in hope of going out until that part enters one of the Angles of the Ascendant, and then they will despair. But if that to which the Lord of the Angle is joined is in the 3rd or 9th sign, it will be better and easier for the exit. And if she is joined with the Lord of any of the Angles, and specifically with the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies slowness. And if the Lord of the Ascendant enters under the rays <note>becomes invisible due to the Sun's proximity</note> and a malefic planet is in the 4th house, he rarely lives. If that malefic is Mars, he will be killed after he goes out of prison. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant has already passed through combustion <note>the area closest to the Sun</note>, he will be afflicted by a strong infirmity; and when any of the malefics are in any Angle, the further you see it from the degree of the Sun, the lighter his infirmity will be, and the more quickly he will be freed. And if he is joined to the Lord of the 8th from the Ascendant, or to a malefic in the Angle of the Earth <note>the 4th house</note>, he will die in prison. And if he is with Saturn or Saturn looks upon him with strength, it signifies prolongation of prison, sadness, and impediment to his substance and body. If indeed he is with Mars, it signifies impediment and binding; and if the Moon is then impeded, he will be found in distress but will not be flogged; and if the Moon looks upon the Lord of her house, it will be easier; if she does not look, it will be harder. After this, look at the state of the inquirer from the Lord of the Ascendant, and the state of the one he contends with from the Lord of the 7th. If they look upon each other from a trine or sextile aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, he who provokes the other will seek him with lightness and patience, desiring peace and safety. If indeed they look upon each other from an opposition or a 4th aspect <note>a square, 90 degrees</note>, he will seek him with gravity and importunity, and will be very persevering in the petition for his justice.

### Question regarding the arrival of an absent person

**When you have been questioned** regarding the arrival of an absent person, look at the Lord of the Ascendant and its place. If it is in the Ascendant or in the 10th, or if it commits its disposition to a part which is in them, it signifies his arrival. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 9th or in the Midheaven <note>10th house</note> or commits its disposition to a part in them, it signifies his arrival. If indeed the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 7th from the Ascendant or in the Angle of the Earth <note>4th house</note>, there will be hardship and delay in his arrival, and it signifies that the absent person is in the land where he is and is not yet departing from there. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 9th or the 3rd from the Ascendant, and is joined to a planet in the Ascendant, he is on the journey wishing to return. Similarly, if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 8th from the Ascendant, or in the 2nd, and is joined to a part in the 10th, he is in the Midheaven <note>already nearby or in a prominent position</note>. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is falling and is not joined to any part in an Angle, nor looks upon the Ascendant, it will be bad, because

<column-break/>

it signifies slowness. And if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to a retrograde planet, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is retrograde and looks upon the Ascendant, it signifies his arrival. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is impeded, it signifies hardship and a prolongation of the arrival. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is not as I have said, look at the signifier which is the Moon; if she commits her disposition to the Lord of the Ascendant in the Ascendant or near the Ascendant—that is, within 11 degrees—it signifies speed of arrival. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is in the 7th and in the house succeeding it <note>the 8th house</note>, it will be prolonged. If, however, the Moon is separated from the Lord of the 4th, or the 7th, or the 9th, or the 3rd, and is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, it signifies the arrival. Also, if she is separated from a planet which is to the left of the Ascendant—that is, under the earth—and is joined to a planet to the right of the Ascendant—that is, above the earth—it signifies the arrival. If indeed the Moon is falling and is joined to a planet to the right of the Ascendant in the tenth, it signifies arrival with delay; because when the Moon is to the right of the Ascendant and impeded, it signifies hardship and the retention of the arrival.

### Question regarding a vision or dream

**The knowledge** of this is that you should always consider the 9th sign; then, if you find a star <note>a planet</note> in it, make it the signifier of the goodness or malice of the vision. If, however, you do not find a star in it, then consider the 10th; and if you find a star in it, then it is the signifier of the goodness of the vision. And if you do not find stars in it, then consider the Ascendant. And if you do not find a star in it, then consider the 7th. And if there is no star in it, then consider the 4th. If you do not find a star in it, then consider the 3rd; for if you do not find any of the stars in this place, then the vision is not sound and is a vanity of a useless dream; and he does not see the thing itself or has forgotten it. And if you find any of the stars in one of the aforesaid places, then know what it is: if it is Saturn or the Tail <note>the South Node, *Cauda Draconis*</note>, then he sees a terrible thing from those that cause fear. Then look at whose house that star is in; then that which makes him fear and terrifies him is of the nature of the house of that part. For if it is the Lord of the 11th house, then that which terrifies him are enemies or their kinds; and similarly it is said for the remaining houses. And if the signifier of the vision is Jupiter, then he saw kings, and officials, or those who are sublime and greater than all who resemble the nature of Jupiter. If, however, it is Mars, then he will see hunting, or a duel, or being joined by law, or an alteration, or a fight, or flesh, or blood, or arms, or instruments, or those which are similar to the nature of Mars. And if it is Venus, then he saw clothing and cloths and a good, beloved thing, or aromatic and delightful things, or pearls, or women, or girls, or boys <note>original: "pueros sodomiticos"; referring to objects of pederasty or young male attendants</note>, and other things that pertain to the nature of Venus. And if it is Mercury, then he saw aromatics, or moneylenders, or certain people praying; or coins, or images, or voices; or certain people buying and selling and changing, which are similar to the nature of Mercury. And if it is the Sun, then he saw that he was flying between heaven and earth, or he saw light, or fire, or a king, and things similar to the nature of the Sun. And if it is the Moon, then he saw a woman, or a male, or old women, or a river. And if it is the Tail <note>South Node</note>, then he saw darkness, and dust, and whispering, and murmuring. And if it is the Head <note>North Node, *Caput Draconis*</note>, then he saw greenery, and fragrance, and gold, and similar things. And if the sign in which the signifier is located is feminine, and the star signifies something of fear, then he saw a high, elevated place, or a high, overhanging rock or cliff; or that he himself falls from a height, or an elevation into a place and oppression, or a stormy wind. And if the star that signifies fear is in an earthy sign, then he is as if stoned or besieged, or falling into a pit, or in a dark and narrow place where he finds an exit. And if it is in a fiery sign, then he saw suspension, or burning, or a flame, or fire, or gloom, or blackness. And if it is in a watery sign, then he saw drowning, or a flood, or an ebb and flow, or the sea, or endangerment. ¶ Then look with which star the Lord of the Ascendant and the signifier of the vision are joined; for if both are joined, or one of them with a Fortune <note>Jupiter or Venus</note>, then no harm will follow him from what he saw. And if they are joined with an Misfortune <note>Saturn or Mars</note>, then harm will follow him from that vision according to the nature of the house of the planet joined. For if it is the Lord of Wealth, harm will follow him in his wealth. And if it is the Lord of the 7th, it follows...

¶ The tenth sign or 10th house with its interrogations. And concerning the kingdom in which someone has trust, whether they will obtain it or not.

### If you are asked about a kingdom in which someone has trust, whether they will obtain it or not.

Look at the Lord of the Ascendant <note>the planet ruling the rising sign</note> and the Moon; if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to the Lord of the 10th <note>the planet ruling the house of career and authority</note>, and the receiver <note>the planet in whose sign another is located</note> regards the Midheaven <note>original: "mediū celi", the highest point of the chart</note>, it signifies the attainment with profit and effort: and with the petition and insistence of the one asking. Similarly, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is in the 10th house and not impeded <note>not afflicted by "bad" planets like Mars or Saturn</note>. If, however, the Lord of the Midheaven is in the Ascendant or is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, they shall obtain the kingdom without petition or opportunity. It will be the same if the Lord of the Midheaven is joined to a fortune <note>a "good" planet like Jupiter or Venus</note> in the Ascendant. But if none of these things I have said occur: and you see a planet returning their light—that is, transferring light from one to another <note>a technique where a faster planet connects two slower ones</note>—then the interrogator does not seek the matter by himself, but seeks someone to work for him in this; if the receiver of the disposition looks toward the Midheaven and is free from evils, he shall obtain it. If, however, he is impeded and does not look toward the Midheaven, the good things will be dissolved after the direction <note>a method of timing</note>. ¶ And know that a malefic <note>a "bad" planet</note>, when it impedes from the 4th house or from an opposition, the Lord of the interrogation is turned back from his companion by a second turning back <note>retrogradation</note>, they destroy the interrogation; but from a trine or sextile aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, they impede less when they turn back. And if some planet joins the light of the Lord of the Ascendant and the light of the Lord of the Midheaven—that is, if both are joined with it and that planet itself is in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven: then look at the Moon: for if she is joined by a good or beautiful turning back both to the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 10th, there will be an attainment. If, however, she is joined to none of them and is free from evils, he shall obtain and have the help of many good people. But if the Moon is not as predicted: and there is a planet that joins the light in the Midheaven, or looks at it, and is not falling <note>in a weak house</note>, nor departs from that same sign until the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 10th join it, and it is free from evils, he shall obtain it entirely.

->¶ How to know concerning any matter if it will be obtained or not.<-

### When you see the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the tenth house joined.

Look at the Moon, if she has committed her disposition and her strength to one of them, and she is received and free from evils: announce it fully and hope for the effect. If, however, she has committed her disposition to none of them but is received, it will be slower; but if she is not received nor impeded, look at the receiver of the disposition from them: if he is free from evils and looking at his own house, he shall obtain the part of those things which he sought. And if he is impeded according to what I said about the impediment of the Moon, he shall not obtain it; and if the Lord of the tenth is joined to the Lord of the fourth, and the Lord of the fourth to the Lord of the Ascendant, he shall obtain it. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the fourth, and the Lord of the fourth is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, he shall obtain it after despair. And when the Lord of the Ascendant receives the disposition of the Moon, the petition for the kingdom will be easier. And know that when the Lord of the Ascendant is in his own house, he shall be established over the land in which he is; and if he is in his exaltation <note>a sign of special strength</note>, he shall be established over many lands, and those of chief dignity. If, however, he is in his triplicity <note>one of the three signs of the same element</note>, it signifies a great work, but he will not be in his own land where he is; but if he has no testimony <note>astrological strength</note> in his place, he will be unknown in the land for which he asks. ¶ And know that perhaps the Lord of the Ascendant and the tenth will be one planet, as if the Ascendant were Virgo and the 10th Gemini <note>both ruled by Mercury</note>. And if it is so, and that planet itself is received, and the Moon similarly commits her disposition to it, and the planet is received: and the Moon is likewise received and in a good place, looking at the place of the matter or her own houses: he shall obtain the part of those things he sought. But if it is not received and the Moon is impeded: he shall not obtain what he sought. And perhaps the Lord of the Ascendant will not meet the Lord of the tenth: as if Leo were the Ascendant and [Scorpio] the right angle; then look at the place of the Sun and Venus each by itself: for if they are received and look at the Midheaven, they signify the perfection of their affairs. If, however, one of them is received and the other is not: look at the Moon; if she commits her disposition and strength to the one who is not received, he shall obtain it; but if she is not received and the Moon is impeded and not received, nor looks at any other

And if a planet joins their light in an Angle and does not depart from its place until it joins him, it signifies the perfection and attainment of those things he sought.

¶ After this, look at the Moon: if she is received and looks at the Midheaven, her strength and fortune are already perfected. And if the Moon is joined to the light of the Lord of the Midheaven or passes through it and is joined to its body and looks at the Midheaven, he shall obtain it. And know that a vice <note>affliction</note> of the Moon and the Lord of the Midheaven signifies a diminution of the matter in the work: and it is worse if the receiver of the Moon's disposition is impeded: for it signifies the detriment of the work. And if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Midheaven, it will help toward perfection. If, however, the Lord of the Midheaven knocks for strength <note>pushes power</note> to another planet's disposition so that it receives them, and that planet has strength in its own place and the place of the matter, but does not look at the Midheaven, the matter will not be perfected in the way he seeks. And when the significator is inimical to its own house, it signifies hardship and revolution in the petition of the matter; and its enmity is when it is in the 12th house from its own, or in the 2nd, or in the 6th, or in the 8th. And if it looks at it from the 7th, it signifies opposition. And know that the Lord of the Ascendant is the signifier of those things that happen to the Lord of the kingdom from praise or blame, and other things concerning him. And the Lord of the 7th is the signifier of his public work <note>original: "opīs clutu", perhaps "famous work"</note>; and the Midheaven and its Lord are the signifiers of those things done in the kingdom, both good and bad. And the 11th and its Lord are signifiers of those who succeed him in his work, that is, in the kingdom; and the 9th and its Lord are signifiers of those who were before him. And the 4th and its Lord are signifiers of those things which are the end of the work. Seek the signification of its acquisition and its substance from the sign of the 2nd and its Lord, and from the Part of Fortune and the goodness of its place; and scribes from the sign of the 2nd and its Lord; and from the 11th and its Lord is rendered his friends; and his brothers from the sign of the 3rd and its Lord; and his servants from the 6th and its Lord; but his enemies from the 12th and its Lord. Look through the aspect of the fortunes and the malefic planets to these places; wherever there is a fortune, there will be good joy and gain; and wherever he finds a malefic, there will be impediment and fear and the removal of hands from obedience, and war.

->¶ How [to know] on what the king will spend the substance he has collected.<-

### And if you are asked on what he will spend the substance he has collected.

Look at the Lord of the house of substance <note>the 2nd house</note>; if it is Mars, he will spend it and scatter it in every bad work: such as war and luxury and drunkenness and other such things. And if it is Saturn, he will agitate his mind and hoard his own substance and that of others. If, however, it is Jupiter, he will spend it for the love of God in alms or in every good work. And if it is the Sun, he will lose <note>original: "damnabit", likely meaning spend or waste</note> it with his parents and in the acquisition of nobility. And if it is Venus, he will make his soul use every delight. And if it is Mercury, in buying or selling while seeking profit. If, however, it is the Moon, she will work according to the nature of the planet to which she is joined. And if she is void of course <note>not making any aspects before leaving the sign</note>, he will spend it until it is consumed. And the Lord of the Ascendant signifies his end, because it is the rise from the 10th and its deposition. If you find, for example, the Lord of the Ascendant either in the 12th or 6th or 18th <note>likely a scribal error for the 8th</note>, it signifies the foulness of his deposition; and it is more foul if it is in the 6th or the 12th, for then it signifies that he will be angry with himself and suspicious, and it will be brought about that he who is appointed after him will rise against him. But if the Lord of the Ascendant is received, it will take away the evil—that is, he will not suffer any martyrdom <note>great suffering</note> nor be bound. If, however, he is not received and is impeded with what I have said: what happens to him after his deposition will be worse than the deposition itself. And if the Lord of the 12th is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, and he does not receive him: the aforementioned ruler shall be bound; and more strongly if he is in any Angle; for if he is in the 10th, he shall be bound in his kingdom in the eyes of all, and placed before them. And if he is in the Ascendant, it will be as I said. If, however, he is in the 4th, it will be in secret, but still in his honor. If, however, he is in the 7th, he shall be committed to the citizens of that same honor, and find from them distress. But if he is falling from the Angles on the right of the Ascendant and is mixed with the 12th, he shall not be bound in his honor.

<header>Concerning Interrogations</header>

...noting his [the significator's] path until it leads to the land in which he is to be held. If the planet is to the left of the ascending degree, he will be bound or restrained during his journey. And if it is joined to the Lord of the 8th house <note>the house of death</note> after its separation from the Lord of the 12th house <note>the house of imprisonment and hidden enemies</note>, it signifies his death during his captivity. If, however, it is joined to the Lord of the 12th house after the Lord of the Midheaven <note>Medium Coeli, the 10th house of status</note>, he shall find his kingdom again after his imprisonment. And know that Mars also signifies imprisonment, just as the Lord of the 7th house does, if he is an enemy to the Lord of the Ascendant: that is, if he is the Lord of the 2nd, 8th, 6th, 7th, or 4th houses. The Lord of the 8th is "hotter" <note>more dangerous or potent</note> because it signifies death during captivity. 

And look for the "malific" <note>a planet that brings challenge, like Saturn or Mars</note> which hinders the Lord of the Ascendant: if it is Saturn, the restriction and suffering I spoke of will come from the prison and from the striking of wooden beams <note>likely the stocks or wooden instruments of punishment</note>. If the hindering planet is Mars, it will be from chains, iron punishments, and the striking of lashes.

### A question regarding the state of a king, asked by the one who appointed him.

## If you wish to know the state of a king from the person who established him in power: look at the person asking the question <note>the querent</note> through the Ascendant and its Lord; and look at the one he appointed through the 7th house and its Lord. If the Lord of the 7th receives the Lord of the Ascendant <note>original: "recepit", an astrological relationship where one planet hosts another in its sign</note> or transmits its strength to him through a trine, sextile, or square aspect, their affairs will be very well joined. And if the Moon carries light between them, that which is desired between them will come to pass. If it sends concord between them, the Moon commits its disposition to the receiver from a place of favor. "Malifics" are altogether cunning: working through the square aspect or opposition; "fortunes" <note>benefic planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> also work through the square aspect and opposition. If the significators of the Lords are not joined to one another, and no star carries light between them, then that which is between them will not be as they wish.

### A question regarding which land the lord of the kingdom is from.

## If you wish to know from which land the lord of that kingdom comes: look at the sign of the Midheaven <note>the 10th house</note>. If a planet is there in its own house, he will be from the common or middle-class people of that land. If it is in its exaltation <note>a sign where a planet's power is heightened</note>, he will be from the more noble people. If it is in its triplicity <note>a set of three signs sharing an element</note>, he will be below that status. If it is not in its own house, exaltation, or triplicity, he will be a foreigner. If the planet is "oriental" <note>rising before the sun</note>, he will be from the citizens of the East. If it is "occidental" <note>setting after the sun</note>, he will be from the citizens of the West. If it is in the 4th house from the Sun, he will be from the citizens of the North; if it is in the 10th from the Sun, he will be from the citizens of the South. If the planet is "peregrine" <note>having no essential dignity or "homeless"</note> in the sign where it sits, and does not aspect its own house or exaltation, he will not be of noble birth. If there is no planet in the sign of the Midheaven, speak of the Lord of the Midheaven just as I told you before.

### A question regarding his entry into his seat of power.

## Look at the hour of his entry into the seat of his kingdom: when he sits on the throne of his empire and begins to command and to prohibit. If his entry is by day and the Sun is with Saturn, judge that he will be swiftly deposed from that work in the kingdom. But if the "fortunes" aspect the Sun and the Lord of the Ascendant, and the Sun is in a favorable place from the Ascendant and in a fixed sign, his leadership will be prolonged and he will see what he desires within it. If, however, the "malifics" aspect the Sun—specifically if the malific is Mars and is exalted above him from the Midheaven, and the Sun is in the Ascendant in a movable sign—some citizen of that kingdom will oppose him and terrify him many times, or his end will be by death and killing. If you find Jupiter in the Midheaven and it is fortunate, and the Sun is in a strong and favorable place, his state will be one of exaltation, growth, fame, and the gathering of wealth. 

If you see the Sun in the 8th or 6th house, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in the Ascendant or Midheaven and is himself a "fortune," the affair of that prince will be excellent, but it signifies the death of the one who appointed him. And if his entry into the kingdom is at night, look at the Moon just as I told you regarding the Sun. Look for the Moon's safety from the malifics; if it is clean of them and in a good place, it signifies the health of his body. If, however, the Moon is with the malifics or joined to them, he will be deposed from his honor quite quickly and will have a very great and powerful grievance. If the Moon is with the "Head" or "Tail" <note>the lunar nodes, Rahu and Ketu</note> and there are four degrees or less between them, he will not succeed in that work. If there are more than four degrees between them, his hindrance will be less, until it passes the degree of his liberation from their evil. Also look at the Moon, the Ascendant, the Lords of those houses, and the aspects of the fortunes and malifics toward them. If the fortunes and their Lords aspect them, and their Lords are in good places, and the malifics are "falling" <note>in cadent houses, where they are weak</note> and the fortunes are in the Midheaven, the prince himself will see

<column-break/>

what he loves. But if the Moon and the Lord of its house are in bad places, he will find evil in that region. After this, look at the Ascendant at the hour of his entry: if its degree is in the "terms" <note>specific subdivisions of a zodiac sign</note> of the malifics and a malific aspects that same term of the Ascendant, he will be weak in that work and a most wretched crime will overcome him. If, however, the degree of the Ascendant is from the terms of the "good" planets, the end will be good; but if the lord of the end is malific, the end is bad. If a malific is in the Ascendant and a fortune is in the 4th house, the beginning of that affair will be evil and its end will be good. 

If you find the "Tail" <note>the South Node</note> in the Ascendant and the Lord of the Ascendant is in a bad place, and there is a malific in any of the "angles" <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, and the Moon is hindered by malifics, there will be low-born and vile ministers who will destroy his empire; he will not cease being sad, troubled, and in fear for as long as he remains in that work. If you find a good fortune in the Ascendant at the time of entry, or the Lord of the Ascendant in the Midheaven, and the Lord of the Midheaven is in a strong place free from malifics, it signifies the goodness of that prince and the prolongation of his leadership. If, however, a malific is in the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant is malific, and the Lord of the Midheaven is in a bad place, judge that he is to be deposed quickly. If you find the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Midheaven in the 12th or 6th house, judge his fall to be happening in haste—unless Jupiter is "oriental" <note>visible in the morning sky</note> in the Ascendant or Midheaven, because this can delay his deposition for a little while. 

After this, look at the sign of the Midheaven and its Lord, where it is and what aspects it. If the Lord of the Midheaven is in an angle and the fortunes aspect it, it signifies the goodness of his state. If a fortune is in the Midheaven, he will reach better and more worthy things than he hoped for, and he will be considered worthy; his empire will be powerful and his profit will multiply. If, however, a malific is there, he will find great restriction in that work; whatever he gains will be taken from him through suffering, imprisonment, and deposition in the king's anger. If a fortune aspects the Midheaven and no malific is there, the work will be long-lasting and good. But if a malific aspects it, it will destroy the work itself. If both a fortune and a malific aspect it, see which of them is closer by degrees: that one will overcome the other, though the other will take a portion from him. 

If Mercury is with Jupiter in the Midheaven, his work will abound through wisdom, counsel, reason, and ingenuity; through this, he will have a name and fame, and his work will increase for the one he serves, spreading through the regions—especially if he aspects the Moon. If the Sun is in the Midheaven with them without any aspect from malifics, it signifies the long-lasting sound of his name and the achievement of his work in all he desires, and a long life during that time. It will be similar when Jupiter is with the Moon in the Midheaven and Venus is in an excellent place; whenever you find a fortune in the Midheaven, his restriction will be diminished and he will find good. If, however, a malific is there, and the Lord of the Midheaven and the Lord of the Ascendant are "falling" <note>in weak houses</note>, he will last only a little while in his work. Whenever you find "death" in the 7th house from the Ascendant and no fortune is in the Ascendant, he will die in that same work. If Saturn is there, but a fortune is in the Ascendant or the 7th, he will not die or be killed in that work. If a fortune is in the 7th, he will be deposed gracefully with honor and safety. If a fortune is in the 4th house, he will be healthy in body and his end will be according to what he desires. If, however, a malific is there, he will find evil and hindrance after he is deposed from his work, including prison, suffering, restriction, and a long imprisonment. If a fortune aspects the 4th, he will escape after the tribulation and restriction he found. If no fortune aspects the malific that was in the 4th, he will endure punishments and die in that same prison. But if the Lord of the 4th is in the Ascendant or the 10th, or in other excellent places clean of malifics, and the Lord of the Moon's house is similar, it signifies a good end to that work.

### A question regarding the stability of a king or his withdrawal.

## If you are asked about the stability of a king or his withdrawal: look at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the 10th house. If they are joined and there is a receiver of the disposition...

<meta>This page continues the astrological judgments of Sahl ibn Bishr (Zabel) regarding the stability and fate of a ruler. It follows the previous discussion of whether a king will be imprisoned or lose his status, focusing here on the specific planetary conditions for a king's return or the total loss of his realm.</meta>

# Zabel

...the devotion of those in an angle <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the most powerful points in a chart</note> will not move the king himself, nor shall he depart from his kingdom. And if the receptor of the dispositor <note>the planet that rules the sign where another planet is located</note> is in the "left" of the ascending degree—that is, under the earth <note>the 4th house, representing the depths or the end of a matter</note>—he will depart from the kingdom but shall return. For if the receptor of the dispositor is himself "received" <note>a favorable relationship between planets where one "welcomes" the other into its home sign</note>, it signifies the speed of his return with honor. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Tenth <note>the Midheaven, representing the king's power</note> transfer their light from one another—that is, if they are separated from each other—it signifies the departure of the king. 

If the Moon "pushes" its dispositor from a slower part of its course in an angle, he will remain in his kingdom until that planet is "combust" <note>weakened by being too close to the Sun</note> or hindered in its place, or until it recedes; then it shall signify the taking away of his kingdom. If the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of his own "fall" <note>the sign where the planet loses its dignity</note>, he will perform a work in which he shall perish. If the Lord of his "fall" is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, a lie shall be told about him, and whatever he has done well, let him live with it. And if he is joined to the Lords of the Midheaven and the Lord of his own "fall," the governor or the general himself shall destroy his region. If, however, the Lord of the house of "fall" of the Lord of the Midheaven is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, his region shall be destroyed. 

And if the Lord of the Ascendant pushes its dispositor into a planet in an angle, the Lord of that kingdom shall endure in his kingdom; it is even better if the receptor of the dispositor is in another of the angles except the 4th, because that is opposite the 10th and its third. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to any planet in the 9th from the Ascendant, or in the 3rd, or with their Lords, there will be no doubt regarding his departure from his kingdom. But if it is afterwards joined to any planet in an angle, he shall return to his kingdom after his departure. 

And if the Lord of the Midheaven is in his own place, the king himself shall not depart from his kingdom if the Moon is joined to him. If Jupiter is in an angle and is in that planet's place, or if the Moon or the Lord of the Ascendant receives him, he shall remain in his kingdom until Jupiter encounters a "malific" <note>a planet like Mars or Saturn that brings hardship</note>, or becomes combust, or recedes from his place. 

And know that when the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Midheaven are joined, and the receptor of the dispositor is in a good place, neither combust nor received, but does not "aspect" <note>look toward or form a geometric relationship with</note> the Midheaven, that prince shall be established over a kingdom that is not his own, but another's. If, however, he aspects the Midheaven, it signifies his stability in his own kingdom. If the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are in angles in "moveable signs" <note>Cardinal signs like Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn, which signify change</note> and the Moon is not received, the king shall depart.

**¶ A question concerning him who has departed from his kingdom, or an absent king: whether he shall return.**

### And if you are asked about a man who has departed from his kingdom, or about an absent king, whether he shall return to his kingdom or not: look into this just as I told you in the first chapter regarding the conjunction of the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Midheaven with each other. If they are joined, and the receptor of the dispositor among them aspects the Midheaven, the king himself shall return to his kingdom. If, however, he does not aspect the Midheaven, but the Moon is joined to a planet in the Midheaven, he shall return. 

Even if the Lord of the Ascendant is "retrograde" <note>appearing to move backward, which often symbolizes returning or reconsidering</note>, he shall return again to his kingdom. And if the Moon, along with what I told you above, is in a moveable sign, it will be quick for them. If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is not retrograde, and the Moon is joined to a planet in the Ascendant or in the Midheaven, he shall return. 

Similarly, if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, and if it is joined to the Lord of the house of pilgrimage <note>the 9th house of travel</note> from the Ascendant, the Lord of the Ascendant seeks departure of his own accord. And if the Lord of the Midheaven is joined to the Lord of his "fall," it signifies the removal of the king, even if he is in the angles. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of his "fall," it also signifies removal; but if the Lord of the Midheaven is in his own place, the one who was removed shall return to his kingdom. 

And if the Lord of the Midheaven is separated from the light of the Lord of the house of the "end of things"—that is, the

<column-break/>

4th house from the Ascendant—he shall return. If, however, he is joined to it, he shall be removed. If the same Lord of the 4th is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, he shall persevere in his kingdom and another kingdom shall be given to him. If, however, the Lord of the 4th is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, he shall not be removed, and the kingdom shall come to him without him asking for it. 

And if the Lord of the Ascendant is separated from the Lord of the 4th, it signifies the stability of the kingdom if the king has been removed. Similarly, if the Lord of the 4th is joined to him, and if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Midheaven are joined, and the Lord of the Midheaven does not aspect his own place, he shall be established over another land which he shall rule.

**¶ After this, look at the significator, namely the Moon. If she is joined to the Lord of the Midheaven, and the Lord of the Midheaven aspects his own place, he shall return; it is even better if the Moon is in a moveable sign.** 

And if she pushes her dispositor to a planet in a "foreign" place in the "left" of the Ascendant, he shall be removed. If, however, the significator is received, he shall return to his kingdom; if he is not received, he shall be removed. And if the Moon is joined to a planet in the 9th house from the Ascendant, it foretells the departure of that king. If, however, that planet is a "fortune" <note>a planet that brings good luck, like Venus or Jupiter</note> and is in a moveable or fixed sign, he shall return to his kingdom. 

If, however, it is in a "common sign" <note>a mutable sign like Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>, he shall go to his own kingdom and to the former kingdom, and he shall remain for three years, because the receptor of the Moon’s dispositor does not fall until it comes to the 12th house from the Ascendant. He shall be in better work in the second year and in the great fulfillment of his will, unless a malific first encounters the Midheaven and turns retrograde in it before the predicted hour; and if a malific encounters that same place, it shall destroy his kingdom. 

And if the Moon is joined to fortunes or is received, he shall be praiseworthy in his kingdom. If, however, she is joined to malifics, he shall be reviled. And if she is joined to a planet in the 10th, he shall depart and work for two years. If she is joined to a planet in the 11th, he shall remain for one year—provided that a malific does not encounter the Midheaven or become retrograde. If she is joined to a planet in the 5th from the Ascendant, he shall remain for two years and depart in the third year. If she is joined to a planet in the 4th, he shall remain for one year and be removed in the second. 

And if you find both the Moon and the Lord of the Midheaven to be "impeded" <note>afflicted by bad aspects or positions</note> by a physical conjunction in an angle, he shall never return to his work, and he shall be deposed and remain a deposed person according to the measure of the place of work. If, however, you find the Moon and the Lord of the Midheaven to be "unfortunate," but they are in common signs, another work shall be added to his work and he shall be strong in his work; and if he has gone out from his work, he shall return to it.

**¶ A question of whether one shall arrive at a kingdom or not.**

### And if anyone asks you whether he shall arrive at a kingdom or not: look at the Lord of the Ascendant and its significator, which is the Moon. If they are joined to the Lord of the Midheaven or to the Sun, or if they are in the Midheaven, say "Yes"; otherwise, "No."

**¶ The eleventh sign or the 11th house with its questions. And first, whether one will obtain the thing he hopes for.**

### When you are asked about any thing that is hoped for and in which there is trust, or concerning positions from kings or honors: look at the Lord of the 11th from the Ascendant. If he is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to him, he shall obtain that thing in which he had trust. 

If the conjunction is by a "trine" or "sextile" aspect <note>harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees</note>, it will be as I have said, with ease. If, however, it is from a "square" aspect <note>90 degrees</note> or "opposition" <note>180 degrees</note>, it will be through difficulty. And if the Lord of the 11th is in an angle and the Moon is received, you shall receive that trust just as you wished. 

And if the receptor of the Moon’s dispositor is in a common sign, he shall obtain a small amount of what he hoped for; and if it is in a moveable sign, there will be difficulty in what I have said. If, however, it is in a fixed sign, he shall obtain what he hoped for perfectly. If you find the receptor of the Moon’s dispositor to be impeded, the thing itself shall be destroyed after its attainment. If the receptor of its dispositor is received, he shall obtain more than he hoped for. And if his Lord of the Ascendant is received, he shall have everything he wants.

**¶ A question of whether someone may be joined to his friend or not.**

### And if he asks you about one whom he says is a friend, and says, "See whether we shall be joined or not": look at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If they are joined to the Lord of the 11th from the Ascendant, they shall be joined; and similarly if the Lord of the 11th is joined with the Lord of the Ascendant. If, however, the conjunction is from a trine or sextile aspect, there shall be joy in their joining...
