### ¶ The sign of the 5th or the 5th house with its elections: and first, on fathering a male or female child.

When you wish to choose the hour for procreating—that is, when you wish to lie with your wife so that you may father a male child: let the Ascendant <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at a specific moment.</note>, its lord, the Moon, and the lord of the house of children <note>The 5th house.</note> be in masculine signs, or in the masculine fourth part of the circle <note>Astrological quadrants were often designated as masculine or feminine.</note> at the hour of conjunction. Do not place any planet in the Ascendant at that hour, nor in the sign of children, unless it is a masculine planet. And if you wish for a daughter: let these significators be in feminine signs and in the feminine part of the circle. If you cannot manage this and these significators are divided—that is, if some are in masculine signs and others in feminine—let the lord of the hour and the reception of the Moon <note>A condition where planets "accept" each other's influence by being in signs they rule.</note> take part with those that have more testimony in masculine signs; if you desire this and it is in the masculine part, the child will be a son according to this.

### ¶ An election for removing a dead fetus from the womb.

And if a child has died in the womb and you wish to bring it forth: let it be when the Moon is waning in light and in number, descending from the girdle of signs <note>The celestial equator or the ecliptic plane.</note> toward the 7th sign—that is, from the Midheaven <note>The highest point of the chart.</note> to the 7th house—beholding the "fortunes" <term>Fortunes: the planets Jupiter and Venus, considered helpful or lucky.</term> from a trine or sextile aspect along with an aspect from Mars. This is even more effective and worthy if it is the sign of the Moon, and the Ascendant is from the feminine signs that are of "direct ascension" <note>Signs that take longer to rise, associated with smoother outcomes in some traditions.</note> and not in "tortuous" signs <note>Signs that rise quickly or "crookedly" at an angle to the horizon.</note>.

### ¶ An election if you wish to hand a son over to instruction or send him to a place where some mastery is taught.

And if you wish to hand over a son to discipline, or if you wish to send him to a place where some mastery or service is taught, let your election be thus: let the Moon behold Mercury, and let them both be free from the "malics" <term>Malics: the planets Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with hardship.</term>. Let the Ascendant be Gemini or Virgo <note>The two signs ruled by Mercury, the planet of education and skill.</note>. Let Mercury be "oriental" <note>Rising before the sun.</note> and in the Ascendant; let him not be descending, nor retrograde, nor in his own station, nor in his "fall" <note>A sign where a planet's influence is weakened.</note>, nor let him be impeded. Let the lord of Mercury's house be his "son" <note>Likely referring to a planet Mercury is currently applying to or receiving.</note>. Do not place the Moon descending and waning in light, because that causes the instruction to be delayed; and let the lords of those houses behold them.

### ¶ The sign of the 6th or the 6th house with its elections: and first, on expelling devils and phantasms from a place.

When there is in any place or house some devil or infestation of evil inhabitants, or if some terrible thing has followed it that is to be feared, or if some phantasm appears, and you wish to remove it from its place or from some person by a charm, or by some other inquiry or ingenuity: beware that the Moon or the Ascendant is not in any of these signs: namely, Leo, Cancer, Scorpio, or Aquarius. Rather, let the Moon be in others besides these, separated from the malics and joined to the fortunes.

### ¶ An election for taking medicine or applying a plaster or any other medicament to any limb.

And when you wish to choose a time to provide medicine for those who are ill—that is, for those with spasms—or for taking medicine for pain in the belly, or for making a plaster: let it be when the Ascendant is Libra or the Moon is in Libra, joined to the fortunes. Do not place any of the malics in the "angles" of the Moon <note>The four critical houses relative to the Moon's position.</note>. If this cannot be done, let it be from a trine or sextile aspect without opposition and without the projection of two rays from a square aspect <note>A 90-degree aspect, considered tense or difficult.</note> or entry "under the rays" <note>Being too close to the Sun, which "burns" or hides a planet's power.</note>; for if it is so, it will cause pain and impediment. But if you wish for a cure of the head and whatever descends from it—such as a gargle or vomiting—let the Ascendant be Aries, or the Moon in Aries or Taurus. Let the Moon be waning in light and joined to the fortunes. Beware of the aspect of the Sun from a square aspect or opposition, specifically in Aries, because of the heat of the Sun. For medicines that are put into the nostrils, such as fumigations and sneezing-powders, etc., let it be when the Moon is in Leo or Virgo joined to the fortunes. Let her not be joined to the malics, nor to a retrograde or impeded planet. And if you wish for a cure of the body's hands and feet, let the Ascendant be Capricorn or Pisces or Aquarius, or the Moon in them joined to the fortunes. And if you wish for a cure of some chronic disease: let your election for acting be when the Moon is in

<column-break/>

Taurus or the other signs of that "triplicity" <note>The Earth signs: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn.</note>. Taurus is the best of these because it is of the "earthly" diseases. Let the Moon be clean of the malics, and let the fortunes be in the angles of the Moon from Taurus; this will be stronger and better so that the chronic infirmity may recede and not return to the one who suffers it. Beware specifically that the Moon is not joined to Saturn, because that signifies a prolongation of the infirmity. 

And Masha'allah <note>original: "Messahallach," an 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer.</note> said: Look, in every cure, to the place you desire for the site of the infirmity in the body. For if it is in the part of the head, throat, or chest, cure it when the Moon is in Aries, Taurus, or Gemini, which is the upper part. And if it is in the part of the belly and internally in the pubic region, cure it when the Moon is in Cancer, Leo, and Virgo. But if the disease is in the lower part—namely, in the anus—and in the lower part of the body, cure it when the Moon is in Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius; and let the Moon be joined to the fortunes and increasing in light and number. And if the disease is from the knee downward to the foot, cure it when the Moon is in Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. It is also said that every pain from the head to the pubis should be cured when the Moon is between the Angle of the Earth <note>The 4th House.</note> and the Midheaven—that is, ascending from the Angle of the Earth to the Midheaven through that part of the circle. And if it is from the pubis to the lower part of the feet, you shall cure it when the Moon is between the 10th house and the Angle of the Earth—namely, descending from the 10th to the Angle of the Earth, which is the lower part of the circle. Let the Ascendant be fortunate; if it is so, it signifies that the person will be healed and profit thereby. 

And if there is some blister or something in the eye, and it is necessary to touch it with iron <note>Perform surgery.</note> or to scarify it, or if there is a growth over it, or if it is in any place of the body where it is necessary to touch it with iron—such as the cutting of a vein—let this be when the Moon is increasing in light and number, except for bloodletting with cupping-glasses; for then you should place the Moon waning in light and number, joined to the fortunes. Let Jupiter be above the earth in the Ascendant, or in the 11th, 10th, or 9th house. Beware of its conjunction with Mars when the Moon is increasing in light and number. If you cannot place Jupiter in these locations, let it behold the Ascendant. Beware that the Moon and the Ascendant are not in "fixed signs" <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius—signs associated with permanence and lack of change.</note> or Gemini, mixed with Mars—that is, having some communion with Mars. Beware also of the "rising" of the Moon; this is when the Moon passes the Sun by 12 degrees. Similarly, in the "puncturing," let Mars not be in the Ascendant when this happens, and similarly Saturn, unless it is at the beginning of the month and the Moon is increasing in light and number; for if you cut anything from the body or pierce it, it will putrefy, and the bloodletting or piercing will not profit the patient. Do not cut a vein nor pull teeth when the Moon is in a "movable" or "common" sign, unless the Moon is clean of the malics or a fortune is strong with the Moon, or the Moon is joined to it by a trine or sextile aspect. 

As for pains in the eyes that are touched with iron—such as phlegm or white spots and other infirmities cured with iron—let this be during the increase of the Moon and its number, according to what I told you before this chapter. Let the Moon be clean of Mars specifically in the treatment of the eye; for if Mars beholds it, you must abstain. But if Saturn beholds it, then if the Moon is increasing in light and number at the beginning of the month, it does not impede. When it is removed from the conjunction, let the Moon behold Mars from a trine aspect, and let her be joined to a fortune. Do not give Mars any strength in any treatment of the eyes, for the wise men have discovered the impediment of Mars in the head. They also said: in everything cured with iron, look to its power in the body and do not place the Moon or the Ascendant in that sign <note>The sign ruling that specific body part.</note>. Do not touch anything with iron when the Moon is in a "common" sign, nor in a "movable" sign.

### ¶ An election for shaving the head with a medicament.

When you wish to shave the head with *annoza*—that is, to remove the hair or other things with a certain kind of medicament <note>Likely a depilatory paste.</note>—let it be when the Moon is in feminine signs, waning in light. If you cannot do this, do not place her in "hairy signs"—such as Aries and Leo and other "bestial" signs. Let the lord of the Ascendant be descending from the Midheaven to the Angle of the Earth.

### ¶ An election for the purchase of slaves.

And when you wish to make a purchase of slaves, beware lest the Moon be joined to the malics, or let a malic be under the earth. Let it not be in a movable sign, because that signifies that the slave will be unfaithful to the master and will not remain stable in one state; or...

...he will be a fugitive if the Moon is separated from the **malefics** <note>Saturn and Mars, traditionally viewed as planets that bring challenges or "bad luck."</note> and joined to the **fortunes** <note>Jupiter and Venus, the "benefic" planets that bring favor.</note>, and if she is in Libra, this is useful, especially at the 15th degree, which is even more favorable. In **fixed signs** <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius, which represent stability.</note>, the servant will be patient, enduring, and honored by his master, except in Scorpio; for then he will be a whisperer and an accuser, and weak in speech. In Leo, he will be greedy, and because of the gluttony of his belly, he will suffer stomach pains and be a thief. Let the Moon be in **common signs** <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces, which represent change and flexibility.</note>, for this is praiseworthy, except in Pisces; for then he will plot treachery and infidelity against his masters in his mind, and will disparage them when he is away. And fear the conjunction of the Moon with the malefics; for when she is joined to them, it signifies that the servant will be sold.

->### A question on granting freedom.<-

**And when you wish** to make a servant free, beware of the Moon’s presence in the 1st and 2nd signs, as stated in the 5th book of **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, a 1st-century astrologer whose work heavily influenced medieval practice.</note>. When you wish to return a servant to freedom, let it be when the Moon is clean from vices, increasing in light and in number <note>Waxing toward a full moon and increasing in its daily travel speed.</note>, and joined to the fortunes. Let the fortune itself be **oriental** <note>Rising before the Sun.</note> and increasing; for if it is **occidental** <note>Setting after the Sun.</note> and increasing, he will find good, but pains will happen to him, and he will not cease to fail until he dies. In the increase of the Moon’s light, if Saturn is in the body <note>Conjoined with the Moon.</note> and increasing in number, it signifies the finding of substance <note>Wealth or property.</note>. Let the Sun and the Midheaven <term>Midheaven</term><note>The highest point in the sky at a given moment, representing status and career.</note> be clean from the malefics; for if they are impeded, the master will find some impediment according to the nature of the sign. Let the hour of liberation be when the **luminaries** <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> look upon each other from a **trine** or **sextile** aspect <note>Harmonious angles of 120 or 60 degrees.</note>, so that there may be concord and affection between the servant and the master, and he will receive good from him. For the **square** aspect <note>A 90-degree angle, considered tense or difficult.</note> is mediocre, and the aspect of **opposition** <note>180 degrees.</note> signifies that the servant will contend with his master. Whoever makes a servant free when the Moon is impeded, servitude would have been better for him than that freedom. Therefore, place the Moon in fixed signs.

->### The 7th sign or 7th house with its elections: and first, on marriage.<-

<image-desc>Ornamental drop cap 'C' containing a figure of a person, possibly a woman.</image-desc>**When you wish** for an election for marriage: beware lest the Moon be in the 1st or 2nd houses, and beware lest she be in signs that are not useful for this, which are Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn, and Aquarius. Beware of signs in which the malefics and the **Tail** <note>The South Node of the Moon, often associated with loss.</note> are located. When you wish to establish a woman <note>Likely referring to a betrothal or a permanent domestic arrangement.</note>, let it be when the Moon is joined to the fortunes and in a **moveable sign** <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn.</note>; and the sign of Libra is the best of all those. In establishing a union, beware lest the Moon be in a fixed sign. However, for the **conjunction** <note>The physical act of intercourse.</note>, when one goes in to his wife to use her, beware lest she be in a moveable sign or a common one. Rather, let this be when the Moon and the Ascendant are in a fixed sign; Leo and Taurus are better than the others. Scorpio and Aquarius are useful for the woman. Half of Taurus is better at its beginning than at its end; half of Gemini is worse at the beginning, and the end is good. Aries and Cancer are also bad. Leo is praiseworthy, except that each partner will not cease to destroy the **substance** <note>The personal wealth or estate.</note> of their companion. Virgo is useful for a woman who has already been married, whether to a virgin or not. Libra is also bad. The beginning of Scorpio is useful, but its end is bad, for it signifies that their society will not be prolonged. Sagittarius is also bad. Let it be the beginning of Capricorn; its middle and end are good. Aquarius is also bad, and Pisces similarly. There is no utility in marriage when Venus looks upon the malefics. Let the marriage be when Venus is in the houses of the fortunes and in their **terms** <note>Specific degrees within a sign ruled by a particular planet.</note>, joined to the lord of her own house. If the lord of her house is a malefic, let her be separated from him, and let Jupiter be elevated above her, or let Venus join him from a trine aspect. Let the Moon, Jupiter, and Venus look upon each other from a trine or sextile aspect; the trine aspect is twice as good, especially in the **water triplicity** <note>The signs of Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.</note>. Let the Moon be increasing in light and number and free from the malefics. Let Venus always be in her **exaltation** <note>The sign where a planet is most powerful; for Venus, this is Pisces.</note>, her triplicity, or her **joy** <note>A specific house where a planet is said to be happy.</note>, or in conjunction with Jupiter or Mercury; and let Mercury be fortunate and strong. Similarly, arrange the Sun as I have told you before; for from the Sun and the Ascendant the condition of the man is known, and from Venus, the Moon, and the 7th sign, the condition of the woman is known. Beware of the aspect of the malefics to them from a conjunction, square aspect, or opposition. And if it is a woman already married, let the Moon be in common signs and work

<column-break/>

according to what I told you before. Let the Ascendant at the hour of joining be from the signs I told you, or let the Moon be in these. Do not place any of the malefics in the Ascendant, nor let them look upon it with enmity; let one of the fortunes be in the Midheaven. And Dorotheus said: then a son will be granted to them in the same year they join. For if a fortune is in the degree of the Midheaven, the woman will become pregnant at the first conjunction.

->### Election for going out to war.<-

**Knowledge** of choosing one of the houses of the higher planets, of which the house of Mars is stronger when it is in sextile or trine aspect to the Ascendant. Let the lord of the Ascendant be in the Ascendant or in the 11th house. Beware of the 4th, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th houses. Let the lord not be **combust** <note>Too close to the Sun, which "burns" and weakens the planet’s power.</note> or **cadent** <note>In a weak house (3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th) that "falls away" from the power centers.</note>, nor joined to a cadent planet that does not **receive** <note>An astrological relationship where one planet welcomes another into its territory.</note> him. Make the lord of the Ascendant join the lord of the 7th, or place him in the Ascendant or in the second house with Mars. And if you wish for them to join <note>Likely referring to the armies meeting.</note>, make them conjoin in the **angles** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which represent high activity.</note> so they may meet each other, and war will fall between them. Place a fortune having a **part** <note>A calculated mathematical point, like the "Part of Fortune."</note> in the Ascendant against Mars, so that it may prohibit him from the Ascendant. Do not go to war unless Mars is in an aspect of friendship with the lord of the Ascendant, or is himself the lord of the Ascendant and is strong in a good place, neither impeded nor combust, and in signs of **direct ascension** <note>Signs that take longer to rise, associated with easier outcomes.</note>. Beware not to place him anywhere but in the **bounds** <note>Small degree-segments of a sign.</note> of the Ascendant so that he may be an aid to him whom you send to war. Also, arrange the Moon when you send soldiers to war, for she is freed by the command of God. Arrange also the 2nd house and its lord for the soldiers beginning the action, and the 8th and its lord for the soldiers of the enemy. Do not place the lord of the 8th in the 7th or 8th, but place the lord of the 8th in the 2nd or 11th. Place the Part of Fortune and its lord in the Ascendant or the 2nd; do not place them in the 8th or 7th. Do not place the Ascendant and its lord in an impeded state when you begin this matter. Similarly, consider the dignity of the twelfth Moon <note>Likely referring to the Moon's mansion or age.</note>, for it is necessary in matters of war to arrange the stars of war: namely Mars, Mercury, the Moon, and the lord of its house. Look to the arrangement of the hours and do not be negligent in this, nor let them be forgotten. And know that when you have wisely led both armies to war as I have said, victory will be seen for the one who was born at night and in whose nativity Mars held a Part; for Mars is the lord of wars and to him wars are committed. And perhaps they will make peace or abandon the war—that is, when the place of their departure for war was good.

->### Election in buying or borrowing or restoring instruments of war, and in destroying a place or some instrument.<-

**And when you wish** to buy arms and instruments of war, let this be when Mars is in his own house, or in his exaltation or triplicity, at the end of the month. For the wise beware lest the Moon be with Mars at the beginning of the month; it is more useful at the end. And if you wish to destroy your camps, let the inception be when Mars is unfortunate and lacks strength. And when you wish to destroy any instrument of war, begin this when Mercury is impeded and without strength. And when you wish to destroy a land, begin when the Moon is unfortunate and lacks strength. And when you wish to destroy an opposing force of war, let it be when Mars is impeded and without strength. And when you wish to destroy a place of idols or a place in which one prays, let this be when Venus is impeded and without strength.

->### The 8th sign or 8th house with its elections.<-

Let it be commended, however, when the Moon is waning in number and increasing in light, and let the Moon not be joined to a planet **under the rays** <note>Near the Sun, indicating hidden things or death.</note>; for this signifies the speed of death. And it is more cunning when the Moon is with Mars, or in his square or opposition, or if Mars is in the Ascendant, or if he looks upon it with enmity; for this signifies that the commendation shall not be annulled. And mostly...

### The 9th sign or 9th house with its elections: and first concerning travels.

## Do not fail to direct travels based on their nativities <note>The birth chart of the individual.</note> and upon the ascensions—that is, the ascendant of every birth—and its angles. Let the Moon be in its ascendant or in its midheaven <note>The 10th house, the highest point in the sky.</note>. And coordinate the Lord of the matter <note>The planet ruling the specific goal of the journey.</note> which you seek; and coordinate the Lord of the year—that is, of the profection sign <note>A technique where the ascendant is moved forward one sign per year.</note>—and the Lord of the natal ascendant and of the revolution <note>The solar return chart for the year.</note>. But if you are ignorant of what I have said, look to the person who has come to you: see where the Lord of the matter they seek is located in relation to the Lord of the ascendant. After this, indicate to him an hour similar to his nativity or to his interrogation <note>A "horary" question asked of the astrologer.</note>. This means you should not place the ascendant of the question and its Lord falling away <note>In a "cadent" or weak house.</note> from the ascendant of the departure.

Let the ascendant of the departure be the 10th from the ascendant of the question or nativity if you seek a kingdom. If you seek a refusal or negation, let it be the 11th from the ascendant of the question. Similarly, in every matter you seek, make that specific sign the ascendant: let the Moon be in the angles <note>Houses 1, 4, 7, and 10, which are the strongest.</note> or in the houses following the angles <note>Succedent houses: 2, 5, 8, and 11.</note>. If she is free from the malefics <note>Saturn and Mars.</note>, let her be looking toward <note>In aspect to.</note> the ascendant. If, however, she is hindered, make her fall away from the ascendant. Let the Lord of the ascendant and the Lord of the Moon’s house be in angles, and let the Moon look toward the Lord of her own house. And beware that you do not place the Moon with the malefics, nor in an aspect of the malefics from a square or opposition; for the aspect of the malefics to the ascendant is lighter than their aspect to the Moon in a primary journey. Conjunctions with Mars at the beginning of the month signify a thief or fire. Beware that you do not always place the Moon in the 4th house; instead, place her in the 5th. For if she is fortunate in this place, there will be less labor in that journey, great profit in his affairs, and more progress. There will also be less weakening of his body, an easier path, and more safety for what is with him and what is accomplished. The presence of the Moon in the ascendant during entry or exit is also terrible; for sickness or heavy bodily labor is feared for the traveler. But if she is in the 11th or 10th: if it is so, he will find good from it. If she is in the 9th, 3rd, or 5th, it signifies labor and small progress. Similarly, the western angle <note>The 7th house.</note> and the 4th angle signify a scarcity of good along with labor and slowness.

And if you seek nobles and judges or the authors of sects—that is, bishops and others of that sort—let there be a conjunction of the Moon with Jupiter in the angles or in a good place from the ascendant. If, however, your departure is for the leaders of battles <note>Soldiers or generals.</note>, let the conjunction of the Moon with Mars be in a trine or sextile aspect. Beware of his conjunction in the angles; let him be low <note>Weakly placed.</note> in the houses following the angles. And if your departure is to those of advanced age or to the ignoble, let her conjunction be with Saturn out of friendship <note>Trine or sextile aspect.</note>, and let Saturn be in the houses following the angles. If your departure is to women, join the Moon to Venus and let her be in a masculine sign. If you can place her in the locations I have previously described for participation, do so. And if your departure is to scribes, merchants, or the wise, let the conjunction be with Mercury. Beware that Mercury is not then under the rays <note>So close to the Sun that he cannot be seen, which weakens the planet.</note> or retrograde, or that the malefics look upon him. For whenever the star to which the Moon is joined, or the planet in the opposite of the ascendant, or the Lord of the 7th house is slow, retrograde, or impeded, it signifies entanglement or hardship in those very ways. If the journey is by water: let the Moon be in water signs <note>Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces.</note>, free from the malefics, and let the ascendant of the exit not be with Saturn. In a journey by water, beware of the Moon’s conjunction with Saturn from an angle. Beware of Saturn being in a water sign, and let him not be fixed in the ascendant of the departure nor with the Moon. If this cannot be avoided, then let the Moon be joined to a fortune <note>Jupiter or Venus.</note> or in its aspect from a trine

<column-break/>

or sextile aspect, or from an angle, so that it may take away the malice of Saturn regarding shipwreck, impediment, or a heavy storm. In the sailing of the sea, do not place the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note> in an impeded state; for if the chart is well-fitted and safe from the malefics—even if not favored by the fortunes—it signifies safety and prosperity. If, however, it is impeded, the man himself will be dead or lost in his journey. Do not sail the sea when the Moon is in the "dark-moon" of Saturn <note>original: "interluniu saturni" — likely a period when the Moon is in a difficult phase relative to Saturn.</note>, for this is terrible. But if you sail the sea for the sake of business, coordinate Mercury and the Moon specifically; let them be looking toward Jupiter from Cancer or Pisces. For Scorpio is terrible in the sailing of the sea because of the place of Mars and his enmity toward those sailing the sea. Also, fear the terms <note>Specific degrees of a sign ruled by a planet.</note> of the malefics in the sailing of the sea; for in sailing along the coasts there is less danger than in sailing the open sea.

If the journey is on land: let the Moon not be in aquatic signs, and let her be clean from the malefics. Beware of the aspect of Mars in a coastal journey, just as I warned you to beware of Saturn in a sea journey. Beware that there is no journey of any kind when the Moon is in Scorpio. Know that earthy signs are healthier for one who wishes to travel on land, and aquatic signs for one who wishes to sail the sea. Saturn is of greater impediment in the sea, and all the more so if he does not look toward Jupiter. Beware of a journey by land or sea when the Moon is in the final part of the sign of Libra. Know all of this.

### Election for a traveler entering a region or city.

## The preparation of a region for the entry of a traveler: Know that when you wish to prepare the region which you are entering, you must coordinate the sign from the ascendant when you enter whatever region or city you wish. When you have done this, you have prepared the region. You ought to coordinate the ascendant and its Lord, and the Moon and the Lord of the 2nd house if you can. Place a fortune there, and let it be above the earth in the 9th, 10th, or 11th house. Never place it under the earth in the 4th, 5th, or 6th; for this is terrible in travel and in every work you seek in that region. Let it be above the earth, whether it be a fortune or a malefic; and strive so that the Lord of the Moon and the Lord of the 2nd are above the earth. Do not place them under the earth, for this is not praiseworthy unless what you seek in that region is a matter you wish to hide so it does not appear until it is finished. Then, let the Moon be with the Sun between 12 and 15 degrees. Beware that the Moon is fortunate from the time she leaves the Sun's rays up to three degrees; for this is better and more praiseworthy for everything you need in concealment.

And if you seek a kingdom in that region: coordinate the midheaven and its Lord, along with the 2nd house from the ascendant and the Moon. After this, look at what **Dorotheus** <note>Dorotheus of Sidon, an ancient authority on electional astrology.</note> said regarding the Moon's place in the signs for a journey by water. If she is in the first face <note>The first ten degrees of a sign.</note> of Aries: whether the planets look toward her or not, it signifies the capability of the matter. If she is in Taurus, there will be less impediment from Mars; but if Saturn looks toward her, he will impede it and cause a shipwreck. In the second face of Gemini, it signifies slowness, then safety. In Cancer, safety from every impediment. In Leo, it signifies trouble, and all the more if a malefic looks toward it. In Virgo, it signifies prosperity, slowness, and a return. In Libra, when she has passed 10 degrees, you shall not travel by land or sea. In Scorpio, it signifies sadness. In Sagittarius, it signifies that he shall return before the journey is finished. In the beginning of Capricorn, some small good. In Aquarius, it signifies slowness and safety. In Pisces, it signifies impediment and destruction. If a malefic looks toward her, it will increase the detriment. If a fortune looks toward her, it will improve the impediment and strengthen the good. Know this.

### The 10th sign or 10th house with its elections: and first on going with a king to a region over which he presides.

## When you wish to set out with a king or prince to regions which he already rules, let this be when Jupiter is in the ascendant or in the 9th; for this signifies that he who goes will find good and joy in that journey, and he will see what pleases him. Beware that you do not place Jupiter in the 4th; for this is terrible. Let the Moon from one of the angles and Venus testify to this. Beware that Saturn and Mars are not in the ascendant or in any of the angles; do not place the Moon under the rays, and beware that she is not with the malefics.

### ¶ Election for elevation to kingship.

**And when you wish** to be elevated and moved to kingship: let the Ascendant be with the rising of Leo. And let the Sun be in Taurus in the Midheaven <note>The 10th house, representing the highest point of status and authority.</note>; and let the Moon be in the Ascendant joined to the fortunes <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter or Venus.</note> or to the Lord of the Midheaven.

### ¶ Election for placing a king on the seat of empire.

**And when you wish** to introduce a king into the seat of his empire: let the Ascendant be a fixed sign <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, or Aquarius, which represent stability.</note> and the four angles <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> likewise; and let the Lord of the Midheaven be free from evils <note>Malefic planets, usually Saturn or Mars.</note>; and the Lord of the Ascendant in a good house, received <note>A technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by another, creating a hospitable relationship.</note>, and the Lord of the 10th should not look upon the 11th out of enmity <note>A 'square' or 'opposition' aspect.</note>; and let the Moon be looking upon the Lord of her own house out of friendship <note>A 'trine' or 'sextile' aspect.</note>; and let the Lord of the fourth sign likewise look upon the fortunes. But if you are unable to do what I have said above, let the Moon be received and the Lord of the 4th be in a strong place looking upon the fortunes; but if you cannot do this: make it so that he falls away from the Ascendant by his aspect, and place the fortunes looking upon the 4th sign and the Midheaven.

### ¶ Election for making a provost over revenues.

**And when you wish** to choose a good man to be a provost <note>An overseer or official.</note> over revenues: let the Moon be joined to Saturn at the beginning of the month out of friendship, and let her be in the house of Saturn with a fortune looking upon her; for this signifies stability. And that the work may be stable: let the Midheaven be a fixed sign so that the work may be consistent.

### ¶ Election in strengthening a principality.

**And when you wish** to strengthen a principality or a duchy: let the Moon be in the houses of Mars <note>Aries or Scorpio.</note> made fortunate; and let her be looking upon Mars out of affection with the fortunes at the end of the month, joined to them. And she will be more worthy for the strengthening of the duchy—which is below a kingdom—when the Moon is pure and not in the houses of the evils nor in Cancer, unless the Moon is pure in the Ascendant at the point of war; and let the Ascendant be in the houses of Mars; and better and more useful for these is Scorpio on account of the strength of Mars and his stability in it.

### ¶ Election for opposing the king.

**And if you wish** to be an enemy to the king: and you yourself are the one who opposes: let it be the Ascendant when the Moon has increased in light; and let the Moon and the Ascendant be pure from the evils; and the Lord of the Ascendant in the best place from the Ascendant in any of his dignities, as one upright and safe from evils, whether it be a fortune or an evil planet; and let the Lord of the 7th <note>The house of open enemies.</note> be in a bad place from the Ascendant, not looking upon the fortunes nor the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon.</note>.

### ¶ Election for appeasing a king angry with you.

**If indeed** he is angry with you or hostile, do not appear before him unless the Moon is failing in light and the Ascendant and its Lord and the Moon are all hindered; and let the Lord of the 7th be fortunate in a good place from the Ascendant, so that this may be stronger and in favor of your affairs.

### ¶ The 11th sign or 11th house with its elections: and first in making friendship.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'C' containing stylized floral scrollwork.</image-desc>

**When you wish** to make a friendship with someone: let the Moon be pure from the angles of the evils; and let the Lord of the 1st be looking upon the Ascendant out of friendship; and place the Moon joined under the part <note>The 'Lot' or 'Arabic Part'.</note> of whom you seek, such as Venus for women; and Mercury for scribes and all circles <note>Likely referring to social or professional circles.</note> according to what will come from this.

### ¶ Election in requesting some thing from any man.

**And when you wish** to request some thing from any man: let the Lord of the Ascendant be looking upon the Ascendant out of friendship; and let the Ascendant be a fixed or common sign <note>Common signs are Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces.</note>; and let the Lord of the Ascendant be in it or in its triplicity or in a 4th aspect <note>A square aspect.</note>. And beware of the opposition; or let not the Moon be joined to the evils; or let her not fail to look upon the Lord of her house. For if the Moon does not look upon the Lord of her house: that thing will not be completed. Therefore always seek the thing when the Moon is increased in light and number and the Lord of the Ascendant is direct <note>Moving forward, not retrograde.</note>; and the Moon joined to the fortunes. If, however, the fortune is direct and the Moon joined to augmented fortunes: it will increase. And beware lest Mercury be in a bad state: for if he is hindered: though he be received: it signifies trouble or sadness and hardship and a second return in the petition <note>Meaning you will have to ask twice or go back on your word.</note>.

<column-break/>

Therefore dismiss foulness and place the Moon joined to the part to which your matter pertains: as the Sun for a king; and Mars for leaders and warriors; and similarly for the rest of the Lords of the circles.

### ¶ The 12th sign or 12th house with its elections: and first in buying beasts.

<image-desc>Ornamental woodcut initial 'C' with stylized leaf patterns.</image-desc>

**When you wish** to buy a beast: let this be when the Moon is with the fortunes; and she herself is direct and in the oriental Ascendant. And beware of the conjunction of the evils: for then fear for the beast, even if it has been tamed and already worked. Buy it when the Ascendant is a common sign; and the Moon is in a fixed sign on account of the field <note>Original: 'agrium'</note> and Scorpio; and let that to which it is joined be a direct Ascendant so that the beast may increase in price and body; for if the Ascendant is retrograde: there will be a decrease in the body of the beast, but it will increase the price. And if it is a direct descendant: it will be increased in body but the price does not benefit it. If indeed the beast is untamed: let the Ascendant be a common sign; and the Moon in a movable sign joined to a fortune. After the Ascendant, do as I told you in the previous chapter.

### ¶ Election in going out to the hunt.

**And if you wish** to go out to the hunt, go out under a common sign; and let the Lord of the 7th be failing and descending; and let it be in the houses succeeding the angles <note>The 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses.</note>; for if it is falling <note>In a cadent house.</note>: it signifies that the prey will escape after you have caught it; and let the Moon in every departure for the hunt be separated from Mars and made fortunate in the best place from the Ascendant; and do not go out to the hunt when the Moon is at the end of the signs; nor void of course <note>When the Moon makes no more aspects before changing signs.</note>, nor in a movable sign. And beware lest the Lord of her house does not look upon her: for if he looks upon her: it will signify for him will and ease in falling; and place Mercury pure from the evils in the hunt of Mars. If, however, you wish for the hunt of the mountain: let the Moon be in Aries or its triplicity. If indeed it is the hunting of birds: let the Moon be in Gemini and its triplicity joined to Mercury; or separated from that same Mercury; and let him be descending: because the Ascendant is better. And if you wish for the hunting of the sea: let the Ascendant be a common sign; and its Lord in a watery sign. And beware lest the Ascendant be a fiery sign. And let the Moon be looking upon the Lord of her house. And know that the hindrance of the Moon with Mars in the hunting of the sea will be worse and of less profit. Therefore beware of the hindrance of Mars in the hunting of the sea, and beware of the hindrance of Saturn in the hunting of the shore. And know that when Venus and the Moon are good and Mars does not hinder them in the hunting of the sea: the hunt will be doubled for its master; and it will be multiplied and he will gain from all of it a very great profit; and the hunt will prosper for its master. Let the Moon therefore be joined to Venus; and let Mercury be with them also; but if Mercury is hindered by Saturn: the Ascendant will not profit. And beware lest Mars be in a watery sign: and let not the Moon be joined to him; or let Venus be separated from Mars.

### ¶ Election in fleeing and whatever you wish to do secretly.

**If however you wish** to make a flight or perform a secret work: and all who wish to flee or be hidden: let this be when the Moon is joined to the fortunes and separated from the evils; and let the Moon be joined to Saturn under the rays <note>Combust, or very close to the Sun.</note> and let her be joined to the fortunes at the time of her departure from under the rays; for the luminaries, when they have risen over any matter, uncover it and make it appear. Therefore beware of their aspects in a similar way.

### ¶ Election in seeking a fugitive.

**And when you seek** a fugitive: let the Moon be joined to the evils in the Ascendant or let her go out from under the rays; and let her encounter an evil in that same departure from a 4th aspect or opposition or conjunction; and do not place the Moon nor the part of the receivers of the disposition in the 4th house.

### ¶ Election in writing letters: and it is concerning elections that are not in the 12 signs.

**When you wish** to write a letter: let this be when the Moon is joined to Mercury, pure from the evils: and let Mercury be strong and fortunate, not retrograde nor hindered; and let him and the Moon be pure from the evils.

### ¶ The little book of Zabel on elections is completed.

# On the meaning of time

### ¶ Here begins the book of the same author on the meaning of time for astrological judgments.

->**Know** that the earth excites motions: therefore, the beginning of a motion occurs within the circle [of the zodiac] until its end—a time in which an hour is fitted to every motion, from its beginning until it finishes with a conjunction that is either favorable or unfavorable to it.<- Whether the sign be good or bad, all motions proceed according to what I shall tell you, if God wills. ¶ **Know** that the change of figures and the destruction or conversion of motions in the universal circle is a sign of what is established in time, whether of good or evil. The "perversion" or change of figures refers to the movement of the planets from east to west, and from west to east; from north to south, and vice versa; and from there into latitude and longitude. The motion of the circle that moves from east to west is as a single circuit once in a day and night. The explanation of motion in longitude is this: that all planets are separated from the Sun and are extended from it by 180 degrees. This is when they pass the body of the Sun; then they are "oriental" <note>original: "orientales"; planets rising before the Sun</note> from position B <note>likely referring to a diagram not present here</note> until the completion of 360 degrees, they are "occidental" <note>original: "occidentales"; planets setting after the Sun</note>. And this motion I spoke of from east to west is accidental, not substantial. The rising of the planets in the part of the circle's motion signifies the "speed of time": this is between the Ascendant and the 10th house, and between the 7th and the 4th. Their setting—that is, when a planet is between the 4th house and the Ascendant, or what exceeds that, which is between the 10th and the 7th—if located there in the circle, it signifies "slowness and delay" according to the sayings of the ancients. 

Messahallach <note>Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a leading Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer.</note>, however, differs from them—that is, he disagrees with them in part B: he defines the "higher place" of the circle as whatever begins to be elevated from the circle and hastens to ascend and appear; this is from the 4th house backward to the 10th. He calls this higher part "fitting" for the beginning of the circle's motion in ascending. But after it is between the 4th and the 10th backward toward the slow part and descending toward the beginning, he calls it the [slow] part because of the start of the circle's descent and its inclination, slowness, and appearance. And this definition is more true than the others by proof. Furthermore, the "eastern point" is the degree of the Ascendant; the "western point" is the degree of the seventh house; and the "10th point" is the Midheaven <note>original: "celi medium"; the highest point of the southern sky</note>. The fourth point is the "Angle of the Earth" <note>original: "angulus terre"; the Imum Coeli or bottom of the sky</note>. Motion in latitude is when a planet is ascending in the north or descending in the north, or ascending in the south or descending in the south. The "change of planetary figures" is also the conjunction of a planet with the Sun until the hour of its rising; from this, in its first station, is a "time." And from its first station until the end of its retrogradation, and the beginning of that second station, and the beginning of direct motion, is a "change of time." From its direct motion until the conjunction of the Sun is a "time." And from the motion of the upper circle backward to the Sun in its arrival at the degrees of the planets and signs is a "time." And from the motion of the upper circle which is from east to west, and their change to the places of the planets by body or light, is a "time." And from the direction of the degree of the Ascendant or any of the planets—assigning to each degree a year, a month, a day, or an hour, forward or backward to some planet, to its rays, to the degrees of the signs, or to the parts—this is "time." And Messahallach and Abuabal gbarat <note>likely "Abu Ali al-Khayyat," a student of Masha'allah</note>, the "consultant," have already said this. For they said: direct the degrees in longitude and latitude, forward and backward. Therefore, all motions of the circle by which times are known are made from these motions.

### ¶ Special knowledge of times.

**Know** that the signs of "light planets" <note>fast-moving planets like the Moon, Mercury, or Venus</note> and the signs of "heavy planets" <note>slow-moving planets like Saturn or Jupiter</note> will result in times of days and months for the light ones. The signs of the heavy planets will be years. Furthermore, in "fixed signs" <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note>, if the significator of time is there, it will signify years. When it is in "common signs" <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, it will signify months; in "movable signs" <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>, it will signify days. Also, a fast location from the Ascendant signifies the speed of time (that is, the upper part); a slow location in the circle, which is the descending part, signifies slowness in time. The Ascendant and the 10th house signify speed in time. The seventh house signifies months and is slow. The Angle of the Earth is slow and signifies years. When the planet that is the significator of time is in common signs, it doubles the time.

<column-break/>

### ¶ Chapter on the discovery of the signification of time.

**Know** also that you should not take the time from just any planet, however strong it may be, unless it is the "significator" <note>the specific planet representing the person or matter being asked about</note> of that thing, or has some part in the signification of the matter—except for the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note>, which naturally signify times in a way the others do not. You shall take the time from the Lord of the Ascendant, or from the Lord of the matter, or from the receiver of their "disposition" <note>the planet ruling the sign where another planet is located</note>, or from the planet to which one of them is joined (if they do not aspect each other). Or take it from the luminaries, or from the receiver of the Moon's disposition—whichever is stronger and more worthy in the interrogation and which "overcomes" the most in it; appoint this one as the significator of time. 

If a similarity deceives you—that is, if you are unsure how to choose the significator because there are many similar ones—always set one of the luminaries as the significator, specifically the one that aspects the Ascendant. If you find a significator of time, Saturn is more worthy than the luminaries <note>This likely refers to cases of long-term duration</note>. If you take it from the luminaries, take it from the one that aspects the Ascendant. 

And know that all times in interrogations <note>horary questions</note> are determined in five ways:
1.  **First:** Look at the degrees between the "pusher" and the "receiver" by light or by body; assign to each degree a year, or months, or a day, according to the speed or slowness of the location.
2.  **Second:** Look at when the "carrier" reaches the one to whom the message comes by body, by degrees, and by minutes—that is, when a light planet reaches a heavy planet by body.
3.  **Third:** Look at how many degrees of longitude are between the one who joins and the one who is joined, and set these as days.
4.  **Fourth:** Count from the Ascendant to the place of the receiver of the disposition, or from the place of the receiver of the disposition to the Ascendant, assigning a sign to each month.
5.  **Fifth:** Look at how many "minor years" <note>a fixed number of years assigned to each planet in traditional astrology</note> the significator of time has; the time will be according to that quantity in months or years.

These are the five ways. Time from the Moon is one month or two months. For Venus and Mercury: the matter for Venus is 10 months or 8; for Mercury, five months or even 3 months. When Mercury is in charge of the disposition, if there is a "cutting off" <note>abscissio; a planet interfering with an aspect</note> upon it, it signifies 20 months. For Venus, 8 years; for the Sun, one year and 19 months; for Mars, 10 and 8 months or 15 years; for Jupiter, 12 months or 12 years; and for Saturn, 30 months or 30 years.

¶ The science of knowing the "time of the 5 modes" in speed and slowness—that is, which of them is slower or faster. Slowness and speed are according to what I have said.

¶ **Know** that when the "pushing" planet or the "receiver" are both in the eastern part from the Ascendant, it is necessary that the planets themselves be oriental and faster in their course. Therefore, assign every degree you find between them at the hour of the explanation. If two planets are between the Midheaven and the 7th house, they signify months according to the number of degrees between them. If both planets are between the 7th and the 4th, it signifies years and months when the two planets agree with each other in their harmony from the Ascendant. But if they differ, and the planet is oriental (fast) in itself but occidental (slow) from the Ascendant, it signifies a medium duration. Therefore, set the time thus: if the time is from the degrees between them, assign one day to each degree. If that passes, assign a month to each degree, as I said. Mix the times together according to what I have explained to you from the part of the Ascendant, the substance of the planet, the sign it is in, and the figure of the planet. After this, test the measure in slowness and speed, and you shall not err, if God wills.

¶ And know that in this [science] are the "roots" <note>basic principles</note>. Perhaps there will be a specific time without these roots because the Moon, when she is in the place of the thing sought, or aspects the place of the thing, or is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, or aspects the Lord of the matter—the place of the matter signifies the effect of that very thing on that same day.

And if the question is a quick one and signifies days, but the day indicated by the degrees of the planets' parts is one of delay: then do not set a month for it until the orbit of the Moon has passed, which perhaps will separate from one of two planets and enter between the Lord of the Ascendant <note>The planet ruling the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> and the Lord of the Matter; or it will enter the Ascendant or the place of the matter; and that same hour and day shall be the attainment of the thing. And perhaps the time is from the degree of the significator to the degree of the Ascendant for each degree; or perhaps the time will be from the Sun’s entry into the degree of the Ascendant, or the place of the matter, or the place of the Lord of the Matter. The matter will be moved and come to its perfection through its own working in the times while it enters the quarters; and therefore the <term>aspects</term><note>The geometric angles between planets</note> have compared it to the soul. After this, look at the times of all things in the twelve signs according to what I shall tell you, if God wills.

### ¶ Chapter on a person's life in the Ascendant.

When you are questioned about a person's life according to the sayings of the ancients: look at the Ascendant at the hour of the questioning and its Lord, as well as the Lord of the conjunction or prevention <note>The New Moon or Full Moon</note> that occurred before the questioning. Take the strongest of these significators of the matter who has more testimony: for he himself will be the <term>Alimbutar</term> <note>original: "alimbutar"; also known as the Almuten, the planet with the most dignity or power in a specific place</note>, which is the significator of the hours. Direct him just as you direct the <term>Hyleg</term> <note>original: "albyleg"; the "life-giver" planet used to calculate longevity</note> to the conjunction of the malefics <note>Usually Saturn or Mars</note> and their aspect, giving one year to each degree according to the ascensions of that city. If the "fortunes" <note>Benefic planets, usually Jupiter or Venus</note> have not cast their rays to that same term, the questioner shall die in that same year. Indeed, the stronger of the rays and the most infecting is that which is from the fourth aspect <note>A square aspect of 90 degrees</note> or the opposition; for perhaps they will kill when the fortunes also protect their rays at that same term. And if that Alimbutar is "received" <note>A technical term where one planet is in a sign ruled by another</note> or if the Hyleg is beneficial, then if the planet that is in charge is in an oriental angle <note>The 1st House</note>, it will give its "greater years." If it is in the "succedent" houses of the angles, it will give "middle years." If indeed it is falling from the angles, it will signify its "lesser years." And <term>Masha'allah</term> <note>original: "messahallach"; a famous 8th-century Persian Jewish astrologer</note> said: look at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon; if they are joined to the malefics, or one of them is, or they are in <term>combustion</term> <note>Being too close to the Sun, which weakens a planet</note>: take all the degrees that are between them and the malefics or the combustion and save them. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is in a "fixed" sign: give one year to each degree. If it is in a "common" sign: give one month to each degree. If indeed it is in a "movable" sign: you shall take one day for each degree. What results from the Lord of the Ascendant will be the number of life; what results from between the Moon and the malefics or the combustion will be the number of sufferings.

### ¶ Chapter on the house of substance.

Regarding the time for a question about substance <note>Wealth or property</note>: namely, when one will find or obtain it. When you wish to know this: look at the number of degrees that are between both significators. Know that the time of it will be according to the number of those degrees in days, months, or years, according to the speed of that quantity or its slowness. Look also at when the Lord of the house of substance enters his own house or the Ascendant; or let him be joined to Saturn, and then it shall be. The time for the third and fourth houses is found within the other chapters.

### ¶ Chapter on the house of children.

When you are questioned about a pregnant woman, when she will give birth: look at how many degrees are between the Lord of the house of children and the angle from the signs and degrees; assign one month to each sign, and one day to each degree; and in that same hour she shall give birth, if God wills.

### ¶ Chapter on the house of illness.

Regarding the time of health for the sick: do not let the Moon fall in her course until she looks at her own place. And if she is impeded while going to the degree of the malefics, or the degree of the house of death: direct her to the degree of the malefics. Then, if the Moon is joined to the malefics before she reaches the degree of the house of death, death is to be feared for him before the Moon reaches the house of death. If it is the malefic Saturn, according to the degrees that are between

<column-break/>

them: they will be months; and between her and Mars, days or months according to the quantity of strength and the speed or slowness of the place. And do not neglect the degree of combustion.

### ¶ Chapter of the 7th sign regarding the times or hours of war from the sayings of Theophilus.

When you wish to know the time or the hour in which war is to happen: look at the hour in which the Moon is joined to the Sun. If they are in opposition, the war will be hastened. If indeed there are 20 degrees between the Moon and the conjunction: the war will be delayed. And if the Moon is with certain of the planets in her own house: there will be war quickly, and especially if the Sun regards her. And if the dignity of the Moon is in the Ascendant or in the 10th house, or with the Sun together with the Lord of her own house, or with a planet that is already rising: this will signify the speed of the war. And he also said: when you wish to know the hour of the battle <note>original: "pzely" / "prelii"</note> and when it will be finished, look at the luminaries <note>The Sun and Moon</note>. If they look at each other from a trine aspect and look at the Ascendant, it will bring about war quickly. If indeed they look at each other from a fourth aspect <note>square</note>, it will not happen quickly; the battle will endure, and it will be moved from its own place into the proper place of the one receiving it. And if they look at each other from an opposition, the battle will not be finished quickly. And if a "fortune" <note>benefic planet</note> is in the middle of heaven, it will bring about war in those very quarters. And if the Sun at the hour of the question is in the fourth aspect of the Ascendant, or if they look from the opposition I told you: the effect of the war will be in those very oppositions and from their triplicities. And if Jupiter and the Moon are joined, looking at the Ascendant in the same way the Sun was looking at the hour of the question. Also look at the "part of faith" and the planet that is with Mars or in its 4th aspect: if they are fortunate, it will happen quickly; if they are malefic, the war will not be settled and it will be grievous and prolonged. But if the fortunes are lords of the part, they will not cause delays when one of the armies is defeated, according to what you see from the place of fortune in the part. And Hermes said: look at the end of the cutting-off of war and of all things according to the luminaries and the Ascendant, and the last of their degrees to the fortunes and malefics; then you shall know the times of things and their cutting-off in years, months, or days. And he also said: look at the delay of victory and its speed in the place of Saturn and Jupiter. If the course is faster, victory will belong quickly to him in whose climate Mars is among them, whether he be oriental or occidental. But if the course is slow, victory will be slow and their business will be prolonged, and it will not be easily cut off. And if their significator is direct after Mars from Saturn and Jupiter, his strike will be in the land that is between both. If they are in a "common" sign, there will be war in the whole land and it will be many times over. If it is in a "fixed" sign, there will be a small and light war. In "inferior" signs, indeed, it will be grievous and will destroy the affairs of the world, and things will be turned back as they were before. This opinion is from the secrets of the Victors of Hermes.

### ¶ The commemoration of the eighth house has already preceded in the chapter on life.

### ¶ Chapter of the ninth sign on travels from the sayings of the ancients.

When you wish to know the hour of the return of a traveler to his relatives and to his own house: look at the start of the journey at the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon. If you see malefics in the fourth aspect or in opposition to them, his journey will be prolonged and his return will be delayed. And if they are joined to fortunes, it signifies the speed of return. If they are joined to fortunes after malefics, he will find [trouble] in his journey, but afterward he will escape and return to his relatives. The return and the delay are perceived through those fortunes and malefics. And if you find the Moon at the start of the journey in the Ascendant, his delay in that same journey will be prolonged, especially if the Moon is in the house of Saturn or in his term. And when you find the Sun at the start of the journey not impeded: then when he comes to his fourth aspect, or his opposition, or returns to the place where he was, it signifies the return for the one who is traveling. And if he was not impeded in that same sign, it is [better] when you direct the Sun in its place in the "root" <note>The birth chart or start chart</note> and in a trine or fourth aspect of its place. And if the Sun was impeded in the root, his delay will be according to the exit of that malefic and the arrival of some fortune to the place.

## On the return of a traveler. Masha'allah said.

<image-desc>Ornamental initial 'I' with a simple rectangular frame containing vertical scrollwork.</image-desc>

In the hour of the traveler's arrival, look to the Moon and the Lord of the <term>Boze</term> <note>original: "boze"; likely a Latinization of the Arabic term *al-bazz*, referring to specific astrological lots or "parts."</note> to see which of them is stronger. And if the stronger of them is between the 10th and the 4th house, take what is between it and the Ascendant. If, however, the Lord of the Boze is an "evil" planet <note>Mars or Saturn</note> that has gone out into the degrees, they will be hours; and if the Moon is stronger, take the thirteenth part of what has gone out, and what comes of it will be days. And if you do not receive a signification from those, and the Lord of the Ascendant is in the opposite of what I said, and the Moon is the Mistress of the Boze, take what is between her and the Ascendant: and what comes of it will be the days, and then he shall come. Likewise, if the house of the Ascendant is in the middle of the sky <note>The Midheaven or 10th house.</note> or returning to the Ascendant: and if the Moon has more testimonies and is strong, and the Lord of the Ascendant is not looking at <note>Forming an aspect with</note> the Ascendant nor the Lord of its own house: his return will be according to this. And if the Lord of the house of the Moon is in a bad place, and the Moon is in a good place from the Ascendant, and she does not look at the Lord of her house: the time of the return will be according to the degrees between her and her house, if God wills.

## Chapter on letters and rumors.

<image-desc>Historiated initial 'C' depicting two men in a scholarly setting. One man is seated at a high-backed chair or desk, seemingly consulting a text, while another man stands before him.</image-desc>

When you are questioned about a letter or about rumors as to when they will come: look at Mercury. If he is in the Ascendant or in the 12th house wishing to enter the Ascendant, or if the Moon is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the house of the Moon, or the Lord of the house of the Moon is joined to him, or if Mercury is the Lord of the Ascendant, the letter will come. And if he is not in the Ascendant at the hour of his entry into the Ascendant, it will come. And if the Moon is joined to Mercury at the hour of their conjunction, or at the hour of the Moon's arrival at the Ascendant, the letter will come. And if the Moon is carrying [light] from Mercury to the degree of the Ascendant and the Lord of the Ascendant, that will be the time when the messenger reaches the one to whom he carries it. And if you are questioned about a letter as to when it was written: look at the degrees which are between the Moon and the planet from which she is separating, and say that the letter was written according to the number of those degrees. Similarly, look at the degrees you find between the Moon and the planet to which she is joined, and the time of the letter’s arrival will be according to them.

## Chapter of the tenth sign regarding the king, from the sayings of Masha'allah.

<image-desc>Decorative initial 'A' featuring elaborate foliate and floral scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>

Look at the hour of the departure of that king whose entry you knew, or the time in which he received the kingdom’s testament, or the hour of his interrogation: and from these you shall know the length of his stay in office, and what shall be clarified within it. And from the hour of the confirmation of his election, you shall know his honor and victory. However, whenever the planet that signified the kingdom becomes <term>combust</term> <note>original: "combustus"; when a planet is so close to the Sun that its light is "burned up" and its power weakened.</note> in any angle of the Ascendant, the king himself will be removed. And if it is not in the Ascendant, look further. Look at the royal house; if you find a planet there having testimony: then when an evil planet is retrograde there, or the Lord of the descent of the Lord of the royal house, and it then looks at the planet from which you had the signification, the king will be removed. If, however, you do not find a planet in any of these hours or places, look to what the Sun is joined. If it is joined to Saturn and Mars: then when it arrives at the degree of that which it is joined in an angle, the king will be removed. And if it is joined to Jupiter, his departure will be when Saturn arrives at the place of the Sun, or at its opposition, or at its quartile aspect <note>A 90-degree angle, considered a stressful or challenging position.</note>, or if it is retrograde in that same place. Similarly, if Venus is joined to him. And if the Sun is remote, as I said, and is in the 11th or 9th house having testimony: then if Saturn or Mars is retrograde in that same place or in its opposition, the king will be removed. And do the same by night with the Moon as you did by day with the Sun: but do not look

### The little book of Zabel regarding the significance of time for judgments is finished.

### Here begins the book of Masha'allah called "On the Reception of Planets": and it concerns interrogations, which John of Seville translated from Arabic into Latin.

<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'I' featuring a scholar or author figure pointing toward text.</image-desc>

# A certain man among the wise found a book from the books of the secrets of the stars, from those whose treasures the kings had possessed; he set it forth and made clear its intention regarding all things which men need in their affairs concerning **interrogations** <note>A branch of astrology, also called Horary, where a chart is cast to answer a specific question</note>. And it was from him who established and made clear in the matters of interrogations: whether a thing is so or not; and when it will be, if it ought to happen; and when it will appear that it is not; and if it ought not to happen, what prohibits it from being; and through whom it happens, and whence it ought to happen. The knowledge of this matter and its explanation is in the 7 planets, and in their 12 houses, and in the exaltations of the 7 planets, and in their falls, and in their conjunctions; also in their separations and in their **receptions** of one another; and in the return of reception and the "striking" of their disposition from one another. And the one to whom the disposition reaches will be the indicator, by the command of God; if it is in a state of the effect of the thing, it will signify its effect. And if it is in a state of prohibition, it will signify its prohibition by the command of God.

->On the reception and conjunction of the planets.<-

<column-break/>

<image-desc>Large decorative drop cap 'S' with white vine scrollwork.</image-desc>

# Know that reception occurs from the **exaltations** <note>Signs where a planet is exceptionally strong</note> and **houses** <note>Signs where a planet is "at home"</note> only, in the case of whether things exist or not: that is, when some planet of the seven is in the exaltations of another planet, or in its house, and it joins to it by the known **aspects** <note>Geometric angles like trines or squares</note>; or if both are in one sign and one of them (one of the seven) is in the exaltation of its companion to whom it is joined; then it is joined to it by its "body" <note>a physical conjunction in the same degree</note>. 

An example of this matter is: Let **Saturn** be in **Aries** at 20 degrees, and **Mars** in 15 degrees of the same Aries; then Mars is joined to Saturn by its body, and Mars "receives" Saturn into his house <note>Aries is the home of Mars</note>, but Saturn does not receive Mars <note>Saturn does not own Aries</note>. This happens when there is no other planet in the known aspects that is closer to the degree of Saturn's conjunction (that is, by a degree before Mars). If there is a planet in the known aspects or in Aries that is closer to Saturn's conjunction, that one will be more worthy of the conjunction with Saturn than Mars. For a true conjunction is degree by degree, whether regarding a conjunction or an aspect. 

Another example of conjunction and reception: when Saturn is in Aries at 20 degrees, and Mars is in **Capricorn** at 10 degrees, and no planet is closer to Saturn's conjunction degree than Mars. When Mars is joined to Saturn degree by degree, then they receive each other through their houses. For Mars receives Saturn because it is in his house <note>Saturn is in Aries, Mars's house</note>, and Saturn receives Mars because he is in his house <note>Mars is in Capricorn, Saturn's house</note>. 

Similarly, exaltations are like houses; but exaltations are of greater authority in a kingdom—that is, when dealing with a king, the lord of the exaltation is stronger than the lord of the house. When the Sun is in Aries at 10 degrees and Mars is in Capricorn at 10 degrees, the Sun then joins Mars: and Mars receives the Sun because it is in his house; but the Sun does not receive Mars, because he is not in the Sun's house. 

Similarly with the rest of the seven planets. Whichever of them is joined to its companion by house or exaltation, through known aspects or in one sign, and "commits" its disposition to it: if the one to whom it is committed receives it, he perfects his matter by the command of God. In this aspect, the Sun does not receive Mars, because he is not in its house nor its exaltation; but Mars himself receives the Sun because it is in his house. 

And if the Sun is in **Libra** in the first degree, and Saturn is in Aries in the 25th degree, and no planet is in Aries nor in any of the aspects closer to Saturn than the Sun, and Saturn does not exit Aries until the Sun joins him degree by degree: then when the Sun is joined to Saturn degree by degree, the Sun receives Saturn, and Saturn receives the Sun. For each one receives his companion in this place through exaltations <note>The Sun is exalted in Aries; Saturn is exalted in Libra</note>. 

And if they are in **opposition** or a **square aspect**, it signifies error, labor, anxiety, and contrariety; but in a **trine** and **sextile** conjunction, it signifies ease and subtlety. When the Sun is joined to Saturn and Saturn receives the Sun, and Saturn himself is received by the Sun from their houses or exaltations, they will make peace and the cause will be perfected by the command of God. Similarly, all planets of good fortune with other fortunes increase the good, and the "evils" with other "evils" become good because of reception—that is, they do good, and their evil and hindrance recede. The fortunes with the "evils" make peace and their evil recedes and the matter is perfected, except from a square aspect or from an opposition, which contains some labor and error. 

If, however, the Sun is in Aries and Saturn is in Libra, as I said to you regarding conjunction, there will be enmities, contrarieties, ignorance, and denials; and neither of them receives his companion. All planets act similarly. For conjunction occurs through the known aspects: from opposition, from trine, square, and sextile aspects, and from a body conjunction; and this happens in the known houses. Whatever is between two signs separated from conjunction—that is, when a planet enters a second sign before the planet traveling toward it joins it—it is not joined to it. 

And know that conjunction happens in this way: whichever of the seven planets is **light** <note>fast-moving, like the Moon or Mercury</note> joins the **heavy** <note>slow-moving, like Saturn or Jupiter</note>, and the heavy does not join the light; because the light follows the heavy, and the heavy does not follow the light. For a conjunction happens degree by degree when the light joins the heavy degree by degree: then it is joined to it and commits [its disposition]...

# On Interrogations
