...and he commits his disposition <note>original: "dispositionẽ"; the management or power over the outcome of a situation</note> to it: after this, he separates from it and does not cease to look upon it from the time he is joined to it until he is separated from it. For a **conjunction** <note>original: "coniunctio"; when two planets meet in the same degree of the zodiac</note> is truly an aspect: because for as long as a planet is going toward another planet in its light and its nature, it will be looking at it until it casts its light upon it degree by degree: then it will be a true conjunction, and he commits his matter to it. After this, he separates from it, and that is the end of that aspect. In this way, a planet will indicate that which is not yet. When it is going toward a conjunction, and when it has been separated from it, it will indicate that which has passed and that which has already been done. Namely, the star will indicate by the star from which it is separated that which is in the past, and it indicates by the star to which it is joined that which is to come.

## ¶ Questions of the Ascendant: and first concerning any matter: whether it will be completed or not: and concerning any rumor, whether it is true or not.

When, therefore, you are asked about any matter, whether it will be completed or not, or about any rumor, whether it is true or not: take the shadow <note>the "shadow" refers to calculating the positions of the stars/casting a chart</note> immediately at the same hour that the word goes out of the mouth of the one seeking the matter. And let the man who seeks the matter be the one asking for himself, or let him write it in a letter with his own hand; but if he does not know how to write, let him send such a person to you who is concerned about his matter. And do not ask another thing along with it, until you have understood that one; and let this not be done except for a matter about which there is great concern, or in a very necessary matter. And it is not fitting for a wise man <note>an astrologer</note> to look for himself, but it is necessary for him to ask another. 

And when the sign of the **Ascendant** <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question</note> and its degree are clear to you, and the sign of the Midheaven <note>the highest point in the sky</note> and its degree, and you have noted the seven planets and their dispositions by the command of God in their degrees, and in the houses in which they are, and in their minutes with a most certain number, pure from which nothing small or great falls away: then look to the **Lord of the Ascendant** <note>the planet that rules the rising sign, representing the person asking the question</note> and the **Moon**. And whichever of them you find to be stronger, work through it and let the other be its partner. This means you should begin by looking at the Lord of the Ascendant: and if it looks upon the Ascendant sign, it will be itself among the strength of its testimony; work through it, and let the Moon be its partner from whichever place she may be. 

And if the Lord of the Ascendant does not look upon the Ascendant, look whether it is joined to a planet which from its own place looks upon the Ascendant sign and returns its light to that Ascendant; or if it is joined to a planet falling from the Ascendant <note>original: "cadẽti"; located in a "cadent" house, which is astrologically weaker</note>, and that falling planet itself is joined to another looking upon the Ascendant sign, which may lift it up and return its light to the Ascendant sign. For if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to a planet looking upon the Ascendant sign, or that same Lord of the Ascendant is joined to a planet, and that planet itself is joined to another, which returns its light to the Ascendant sign, let it relieve it. And if there should be a conjunction from one planet among the seven planets, the work among them shall be the same: namely, one returns and lifts up the light of that one to another, until it reaches the last of them. 

But if the Lord of the Ascendant pushes <note>original: "pulsat"; a technical term for a planet transferring its influence</note> its light to the Ascendant sign, work through it, and let the Moon be its partner. And if the Lord of the Ascendant sign does not look upon the Ascendant, nor is joined to a planet looking upon the Ascendant and returning its light to it and pushing it (for its aspect to the Ascendant is pushed, and its "fall" is when it does not look upon the Ascendant, nor returns light to a planet looking upon the Ascendant), if the Lord of the Ascendant does not look upon the Ascendant, it will then be hindered and bad. Then work through the Moon just as you worked through the Lord of the Ascendant. And know that according to the quantity of the hindrance that has entered upon him—that is, upon the Lord of the Ascendant—so much will enter upon the matter. Therefore, work through the Moon: for if she looks upon the Ascendant or has returned its light to others of the planets at the Ascendant, work through her and let the Lord of the Ascendant be her partner. 

Look at the Moon: if she looks upon the Ascendant sign, work through her, and let the Lord of the Ascendant be her partner, on this condition: namely, if the Lord of the Ascendant does not look upon the Ascendant nor is joined to any of the planets which return their light to the Ascendant, see to which of the planets the Moon is then joined, and work through her, and let the Lord of the Ascendant be her partner. And if the Moon does not look upon the Ascendant nor is joined to any planet that returns its light to the Ascendant, or if the Moon is looking upon the Ascendant and is not joined to any planet—that is, if she is **void of course** <note>original: "vacua cursu"; moving through a sign without making any major aspects to other planets</note>—and the Lord of the Ascendant does not look upon the Ascendant, 

<column-break/>

and he also is void of course: then look which of them ought to exit more quickly from the sign in which he is, and which one is less in degrees—that is, which has fewer degrees until the exit—and then you shall change to the sign and [the matter] from its place. After this, look to which of the planets it is first joined, and judge by this. And all planets change; but a lighter planet <note>a faster-moving one like the Moon or Mercury</note> is more worthy of change than a ponderous one <note>a slower one like Saturn or Jupiter</note>, because the void of course of the planets indicates negligence—that is, the malice of the matter and its slowness. And every planet with the emptying of its course indicates a great deal of slowness. Likewise, a small number of degrees that a planet has to travel in the sign in which it is also indicates a great deal of slowness after the interrogation, or the speed of the effect of the matter. Therefore, whichever exits more quickly from the sign in which it is will be quicker in the matter; but the light and the ponderous, when they are void of course, indicate the slowness of matters and their negligence. 

The light of Venus, therefore, [if she finds] the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon void of course, joining themselves to no one, foretells the slowness of the matter and its prolongation, and that it must be postponed according to what you have seen. And see to what the Moon is joined before her exit from the sign in which she is, and by that judge the effect of the matter by the command of God. And let the Lord of the Ascendant be her partner according to his strength or weakness in the place where he is. Let the planet which is in the Ascendant also be a partner to them in the work, as well as the planet which is in the **house of the matter sought**. For if it is in agreement <note>original: "cõfoꝝ"; conforming</note> with the sign in which it is and is **received** <note>original: "receptus"; a state of hospitality where the ruler of the sign "accepts" the planet</note>, it indicates the goodness of the matter and its dignity. And if it is not in agreement with the same sign in which it is, nor is received, it indicates the hindrance of that same matter and its worthlessness. 

However, the effect of a matter and its prohibition <note>failure of the matter to happen</note> does not come from that which is in the Ascendant, but comes from the part of the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, and from the stars to which they are joined and their conjunction, and the reception and the return of their reception. And know that the Moon becomes a partner of the Lord of the Ascendant, in whatever place she may be, by the command of God. Therefore, when you find the Lord of the Ascendant hindered, work through the Moon just as you work through the Lord of the Ascendant.

## ¶ A question concerning the death or life of the inquirer in the year of his interrogation.

Now, if you look for a man who has asked you about his life—namely, whether he will die in that year or not—look for him just as you would look for a sick person. Look to what the Lord of the Ascendant is joined: for if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to a **planet of fortune** <note>a benefic planet, like Jupiter or Venus</note> and that same fortune is the disposer to which the disposition has come, and does not return it to another, and that same fortune is not the Lord of the **House of Death** <note>the 8th house of the zodiac</note>, say that he will not die in that same year by the command of God. 

And if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to a bad planet or the Lord of the House of Death, of whatever kind he may be—whether he be bad or a fortune—and the Lord of the Ascendant himself is not received, nor does that same bad planet or the Lord of the House of Death (whether he be bad or a fortune) receive him: look at the Moon, and if she is also bad, he will die by the will of God in that same year. Then look when the Lord of the Ascendant will join that bad planet or the Lord of the House of Death which did not receive him, degree by degree, and set those as days. Because if it does not happen then, it will be when he is mingled with it by his body <note>a physical conjunction</note> and reaches its degree, and is joined to it by his body degree by degree: then he will die. 

But if the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to a planet which receives him, then the sick person or the inquirer will escape death in the same year by the command of God, and the sick person will recover from his illness by the command of God. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is hindered, work through the Moon just as I told you concerning the Lord of the Ascendant, and indicate through her just as you judged through the Lord of the Ascendant, for she will commit prosperity and health from illness. Look when the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the planet that signifies his health degree by degree, and set those degrees as days—namely, of the conjunction. For if it does not happen then, it will be when he is joined to it by his body in the sign in which he is, and is joined to it in some place or in one of the angles; if he is very remote from it, then he will escape if God wills. 

If, however, the Lord of the Ascendant is joined to the Lord of the House of Death, or the Lord of the House of Death is joined to him, he will die by the will of God; and the Moon is not considered in the 13th <note>possibly a reference to the 13th lunar mansion or a specific degree</note>. And if the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and not hindered, and the Moon is joined to the Lord of the house...

# On Interrogations

He is the lord of your matter: and he presides over it by God’s command. The good fortune of the planets and their malice or hindrance—as well as their "reception" <note>original: "receptio"; a condition where a planet is in a sign ruled by another, which "receives" or supports it</note> or lack thereof—will indicate to you the ease or difficulty of the matter, as well as its fulfillment or prevention. But the end of a matter will be where the "conjunction and commission of disposition" <note>original: "cōiunctio ⁊ cōmīssio disposit-tionis"; the point where one planet passes its influence to another through a mathematical aspect</note> finishes. For the planet with whom this disposition is perfected is the lord and author of the matter. Similarly, concerning all things: when the disposition reaches a planet that "receives" it, the matter improves and is perfected by God’s command; and when it reaches a "fortune" <note>original: "fortunā"; a beneficial planet like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it profits in its disposition. And when its disposition is perfected and it has committed it to another, the disposer himself will operate according to the quality of his nature and his condition, at God’s nod.

¶ Another inquiry <note>original: "iterrogatio"</note> in which **Leo** was the Ascendant. Its departure was from the **Ram** (Aries), which received it from the **Bull** (Taurus); and the Moon herself joined **Jupiter**, and Jupiter received her, and he was received by her. **Mercury** also signified that which the Moon had signified.

¶ Another inquiry in which **Leo** was the Ascendant at 28 degrees; and the Midheaven was the **Bull** (Taurus) at 20 degrees; and **Saturn** was in the **Ram** (Aries) at 4 degrees and 45 minutes; and the **Moon** was in the Ram at 28 degrees and 27 minutes; and **Jupiter** was in the Bull at 9 degrees and 13 minutes; and **Mars** was in the Bull at 15 degrees and 18 minutes; and the **Sun** was in the **Water-Bearer** (Aquarius) at 24 degrees and 35 minutes; and **Mercury** was in the Water-Bearer at 4 degrees <note>The transcription says 'z', likely a 4 or 2</note> and 16 minutes in direct motion; and **Venus** was in the **Goat** (Capricorn) at 11 degrees and 39 minutes, as is shown in this figure.

¶ I examined this inquiry by God’s command: the Ascendant was **Leo**, and the **Sun** was in the seventh sign, in the house of marriage, "void of course" <note>original: "cursu vacuus"; meaning the planet makes no further major connections before leaving its current sign</note>, that is, joined to no one. I also examined the **Moon**, which I found to be void of course, joined to no one. I therefore examined which of them was stronger in their place, and both were looking at the Ascendant. But the Sun was in an "angle" <note>original: "angulo"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, considered the most powerful positions in a chart</note>, stronger than the others. I also examined which of them was further along in degrees in the signs where they were, and which of them would leave its sign more quickly, and it was the Moon. I worked through the Moon first; though if both were joined, or if the Sun were joined to someone, I would begin with the Sun because it was in an angle. But it was void of course. I observed the Moon, however, which I found having more degrees than the Sun, and she was about to leave the sign she was in more quickly. I began, therefore, to judge by the Moon, then by the Sun. After this, I examined to which of the seven planets the Moon was joined at the first of her departure from the sign she was in to the second sign. The Moon was joined in the second sign to **Mercury**, and the Moon committed her disposition to the same Mercury. Mercury, however, was joined to **Saturn**; Mercury also committed his disposition to Saturn, and he was "received" by him through his position, because he was the lord of that place. Saturn, therefore, signified health for him by God's command, because

<column-break/>

Saturn received Mercury into his house. After this, I examined what the **Sun** would join first when it departed for the next sign; and the Sun was joined to **Jupiter**, who is the lord of the "house of death" <note>the 8th house</note>; but he received the Sun into his house. The Sun also signified health and prosperity by God’s command because of the reception by Jupiter, who was receiving him. If Jupiter had not received him, this would have been a testimony of death, because Jupiter was the lord of the house of death. When the lord of the house of death is joined to the lord of the "house of life" <note>the 1st house or Ascendant</note> and commits his disposition to him, it will signify death by God’s nod, unless there be something else that the Lord wills. For whether a "fortune" <note>benefic planet</note> or an "infortune" <note>malefic planet</note> is the lord of the house of death, it signifies death, because it is an enemy to the lord of life—unless there is a "reception" between them which drives away death. For example, if the lord of the house of death receives the lord of the house of life, or receives the "bearer of the disposition" from the lord of the house of life, then the reception is strong. And if the lord of the house of life receives the lord of the house of death, the reception will be weak; nevertheless, the lord of the house of death does not destroy him entirely, by God’s command. After this, look to see if you find the lord of the house of life and the Moon both signifying health: begin with the one who arrives more quickly at the planet that signified health to him, provided he is stronger in his place and the other participates with him. If you find one of them signifying life and the other death, the significance of the lord of life will be stronger and more worthy; for life shall not suffer detriment except through the detriment of both, and the lord of life rules this matter as does the Moon. But they are always participants in every matter, nor does any of them properly have any matter without its companion. Therefore, when one of them perfects a matter and the other has suffered detriment, the one who suffered detriment will affect the one who perfected it and the matter itself, out of necessity, according to the quantity of the companion's detriment.

And know that when you look into death and sickness, the lord of death and the lord of the "house of sickness" <note>the 6th house</note> are the worst enemies to the lord of life, above all other planets—unless it is one and the same lord: for example, if the lord of the house of life is also the lord of the house of death, then he will not hinder himself, even though he may be "bad" <note>malefic</note>; instead, the other bad planets will hinder him. And know that whatever planet of the seven you find as the lord of the house of life, it will not hinder itself, even if it is bad; but the other bad planets will hinder it. And know that whatever planet of the seven you find as the lord of the house of life, it will not hinder itself in that which is bad. And whatever planet you find as the lord of the house of death, it is an enemy of the lord of the house of life; even if it is a "fortune," it nevertheless destroys life if it is the disposer—unless it receives or is received; then it takes this away by God's command. Likewise, the lord of life will not hinder itself whether it be a fortune or bad. And if the lord of the house of life were Saturn or Mars, and the lord of the house of death is not reconciled with the other lord of life except through reception, then death is an enemy to life unless their lord is one. Then look to see to whom the lord of the house of death and the lord of the house of life commit their disposition, or who is joined to them, and judge according to this. If the lord of the house of death and the lord of the house of life commit their disposition to a bad planet that does not receive them, it will signify death, if God wills. And if he commits his disposition to a bad planet and that bad planet receives him, he shall be delivered by God's command. And if the lord of life and the lord of the house of death commit the disposition to a fortune, the sick person shall be delivered from death by God's command, and the fortune will not hinder him whether it receives him or not.

After this, I looked at the lessening of the sickness and its increase: I looked, namely, at the lord of the house of sickness for this sick man, and it was **Saturn**, who is not joined to anyone; for Saturn is joined to none of the planets, nor is he separated from any of them, because he is the heaviest <note>slowest-moving</note> of all. I looked, therefore, to see which of the seven planets was joined to him, or which of them was separating from him—specifically from Saturn, who was more significant in the sickness. I found **Venus** separating from Saturn, who was the lord of the house of sickness, by seven degrees. Because Venus was in the house of sickness, her separation from Saturn signified the lessening of the sickness. And she was joined to **Mars**, who receives her, and she receives him; for he received her from his "exaltation" <note>a specific zodiac sign where a planet's influence is heightened; for Mars, this is Capricorn</note> and she received him from her house.

# Mashallah

...both signified by their swift lightness the arrival of safety by God’s command. In this way, look also into pain and death.

### Questions of the Second House. And first, on whether wealth is to be found, and of what kind it may be.

If you wish to know about the nature of wealth, and someone asks you whether they will find <term>substance</term> <note>original: "substāntiam"; refers to physical wealth, money, or property</note> or not: and if the question is general—meaning the location of the wealth is unknown and it is not being sought from a specific person—look to the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the question, representing the person asking</note> and the Moon, and to the House of Substance, which is the second house from the Ascendant. 

When you have established the Ascendant and its degree, look to the Lord of the House of Life <note>The ruling planet of the 1st House</note>. If you find him "looking" at the sign of the Ascendant, or if any of the planets transmit his light to the Ascendant, work through him. If this is not the case, and the Moon is as I described to you regarding the Lord of the Ascendant, work through her. And if neither of them looks at the Ascendant, and no planets are joined that might transmit their light to the Ascendant, you shall note the planet that has progressed the most degrees in the sign where it sits, and which is due to exit most quickly into the second sign; then work through that planet. 

For if the stronger of these is joined to the Lord of the House of Substance—who is the ruler of the second house—the person will find the wealth and obtain it. This is true whether the planet is <term>received</term> <note>original: "receptus"; a favorable condition where a planet is welcomed by the ruler of the sign it occupies</note> by the Lord of the House of Substance or not, and whether the planet is a "fortune" or an "infortune" <note>Benefic planets like Jupiter/Venus vs. Malefic planets like Saturn/Mars</note>. For the conjunction of the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon with the Lord of the matter is itself the achievement of the goal; nothing forbids its effect, if God wills it, unless the Lord of the House of Substance commits his "disposition" to another planet. In that case, see if that planet is "evil" (malefic); if it receives the Lord of the House of Substance, it will complete the matter. 

And if it is a "fortune," it will also complete the matter and the wealth will be found, whether it receives it or not, provided that the disposer is in a strong place or in the "angles" <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most powerful positions in a chart</note>. For "reception" makes things happen, and there is no way it can fail to occur, whether the matter is prolonged or shortened—that is, whether the time is long or short. The angles hasten the matter and make it strong, and the second houses are useful; but the "cadent" houses <note>Houses that do not "aspect" or see the Ascendant</note> which do not look at the Ascendant delay the matter and put it off. Yet "reception" cannot be nullified, even if it is delayed by God’s command. 

Now, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to the Lord of the House of Substance, or to a "fortune" in the House of Substance, or to an "evil" planet that has a "part"—that is, dignity—in the House of Substance (even if it does not receive the Lord of the Ascendant), or to an evil planet in the House of Substance that has no dignity there but receives the Lord of the Ascendant: the matter will be achieved. And if the Lord of the Second House (the House of Substance), or a planet that is in that same house, is joined to the Lord of the Ascendant, the matter will happen without any difficulty and will be perfected by God’s nod. 

The conjunction of the Lord of the Ascendant with planets signifies the seeking of the matter by the questioner before it is given; but the conjunction of the Lord of the House of Substance with the Lord of the House of Life signifies that the matter will come without seeking, and there will be more than what is hoped for. 

Now, if the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon are not joined to the Lord of the Second House, nor to any planet acting in its place (that is, one descending in that house), look then to what the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined. If both or one of them are joined to a "fortune," and that planet has not committed its disposition to another, and it is in an angle or a strong place, the matter will be perfected and the wealth found, whether that "fortune" receives it or not. 

And if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to an "evil" planet, if that planet receives him, the matter will be perfected; if it does not receive him, it will be destroyed. This is if the evil planet is its disposer and author, because an evil planet causes the loss of things if it does not receive. "Fortunes" make things more useful by God’s command even if they do not receive; for if they do receive, the good will be greater, and if they do not, they still work for good and do not hinder, by God’s command. But if a "fortune" commits its disposition to an "evil" planet that does not receive it, the matter will suffer loss when the disposition reaches the evil planet; but if it receives it, the matter will be perfected.

<column-break/>

### Question on lent money, whether it will be restored or returned to you from his own wealth.

If you ask someone for wealth that you lent, or if you seek for them to give to you from their own wealth, or however you may demand it: the Lord of the Ascendant and the Moon will be the seeker. The one from whom it is sought will be the Lord of the Seventh House. The House of Substance for the seeker will be the second house from the Ascendant. The House of Substance for the person from whom it is sought will be the second from the seventh—that is, the eighth house from the Ascendant, which is also the House of Death. 

And if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined to the Lord of the House of Death (who is the Lord of the wealth of the person being asked), or to a planet that is in that same house, as I told you in the preceding chapter: he will acquire the thing he sought. 

And if there is no cause of conjunction between him and the Lord of the wealth of the aforementioned debtor—that is, between the Lord of the Ascendant and the Lord of the House of Death—and he is not joined to any planet in that house, as I said in the upper chapter; and if the Lord of the House of Death (the Lord of the sought wealth) is not joined to the Lord of the Ascendant or to any planet in the Ascendant that is "agreeable" to it (whether it be an evil planet or a fortune, and its "agreement" is reception or having some dignity in the Ascendant): then look to what the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined. If one or both of them are joined to an evil planet that receives them, or to a fortune in a strong place, the matter will be perfected and he will find it by God’s command.

### Question of whether one may have the King’s wealth, or not.

And if the questioner asks you about the King’s wealth, whether he may have it or not: look for him according to what you looked at for his own wealth (the questioner’s) and for the wealth of the person sought—that is, from the eleventh house <note>The 11th house is the 2nd house (wealth) relative to the 10th house (the King)</note>—and indicate accordingly by God’s nod.

### Question on the time of having the thing: namely, when that thing will be had.

If he asks you when this will be, look to the planet to which the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon is joined, or the planet that joins to the Lord of the Ascendant, or a "fortune" that has a closer reception from the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon, or an "evil" planet that receives the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon in the house of the signified matter—that is, the planet that signifies the effect of the matter. 

Then, if the effect of the matter is through a conjunction of the known "aspects" <note>Mathematical angles like square, trine, or sextile</note> and not by "body" <note>A physical conjunction in the same degree</note>: look at when the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon casts its light upon the "significator" <note>The planet representing the goal</note> degree by degree. Calculate the time according to the number of degrees between them: however many degrees there are, set that many days. 

But if it does not happen then, it will be when the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon reaches that significator and is joined to it by "body" in the sign in which it sits, degree by degree; or when the significator reaches the Lord of the Ascendant. If there is a conjunction between them in one sign, and the Lord of the Ascendant is "heavier" <note>slower-moving</note>, then the matter will be by God’s command. And this will be in a strong place: in the angles or in a place where the Lord of the matter "rejoices." 

But if it is not at that hour, it will be when the "author" of the matter reaches the Sun and is "oriental"—that is, when it begins to rise after its exit from under the Sun's rays. For then it will be renewed, and it will renew its matter, if God wills. And if it is under the Sun's rays, it will be when it exits from under the rays. Look at the day when this will be by the degrees between both: if the stars are "lighter" than the Moon—namely Mercury, Venus, and the Sun—set days for them according to the degrees between them, until one casts its light upon the other degree by degree, which is the "true conjunction." Then look at the degree in which the author of the matter was when the seeker was joined to him degree by degree. When the Lord of the Ascendant or the Moon reaches that degree, the matter will be perfected by God’s command.

The stars then work good and evil by the will of God when they are in a strong place, in higher and fixed places; for these are what fix and confirm matters, both good and bad, by God's will; they also move them at the time of their effect. 

Set your heart, therefore, to knowing the "fall" of the planets from the <term>angles</term> <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, which are the most active parts of a chart</note>, and their "erection" or their height in those same angles, regarding the movement of things, their reception, or their stability and confirmation. If the leadership of this man had not occurred when Venus reached the degree of the Ascendant in the East, I would say it would be when Venus reached the degree of the fourth sign, or the 7th degree, or the degree in which Saturn was at the hour of the interrogation, or when the Sun overtook Saturn and became "oriental" <note>Rising before the sun, considered a position of strength</note> and moved out from under the Sun's rays and was renewed; it would then renew the matter which it oversaw. The arrival of Venus at the degree in which the Moon was is a strong thing. 

This man went out to the work he presided over when Venus reached the degree of the ascending sign. Know that the delay in this matter happened because the Moon was in the fourth angle and was joining Saturn, from whom you knew the effect of the matter; and Saturn was in the 10th angle, in the place of the matter and the place of the kingdom. If the Moon had been in the 7th angle, the matter would surely have happened faster; and if she had been with Saturn in the 10th sign, it would have been faster still; and in the ascending sign, it would have been faster than all other places. 

And know that the strength of the Lord of the Ascendant and the strength of the Moon make things slow or hasten them, or their weakness if they are weak. For if they and the planets they join are in angles, the matter will hasten by God’s command. If one of them is cadent and the other is in a strong place—that is, the planet that joins or the one to which it joins—it will similarly impede this matter and make it slow according to the amount of its "fall" and the impediment that enters upon it in the place where it is. 

Know that planets "falling" from the angles cause every matter that is not yet done to delay; it is waited for so that it may be done. But planets falling from the angles are good and best for every good thing whose departure is expected, such as a journey when it is viewed for a traveler or a pilgrim, or a king whose fall and the departure of his kingdom is viewed, or a man in charge when he will depart from his rank. For every good or evil thing that will depart and be taken away from its master, look at the recession of the strong planets that rise in the four angles. Of these, the most worthy and swift in doing good is the Ascendant; second in effect is the Midheaven (the tenth angle); third is the seventh house (the house of union or marriage); and fourth is the angle of the earth (the house of fathers). 

Among the "middle" houses <note>succedent houses</note>, the most worthy is the house of hope (the eleventh house), and it is swifter than the house of marriage or the house of fathers in accomplishing things. Second is the house of journeys (the ninth); third is the house of children (the fifth); and fourth is the house of brothers (the third). These are good and praiseworthy. 

The "falling" houses <note>cadent houses</note>, however, are worse than all other houses: namely, the house of death (the eighth), the house of sickness (the sixth), and the house of enemies (the twelfth). And the house of substance <note>money and possessions</note>, which is the second from the Ascendant. These houses are "enemies" of the Ascendant which do not "behold" <note>They do not form a traditional geometric aspect to the 1st house</note> the Ascendant; and the outcomes of such a matter are few and profitable only in a small way. For nothing was found in it except a modest thing. Nevertheless, he received it by command, and his delay lasted until he returned to the house...

...his [rights]. Within 15 days, there occurred the instability of his right and the strength of his work, because the <term>fall</term> <note>original: "casus," a state of planetary weakness</note> of his planets was in the <term>angles</term> <note>The four pivotal houses of a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>. ### Chapter on the Knowledge of the Life of the Native

<margin>Finding the <term>Hyleg</term></margin> <note>The "Giver of Life," the specific point in a birth chart that represents the person's physical vitality</note>
<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'C' featuring a seated figure, likely a scholar or astrologer, within a square frame with floral ornamentation.</image-desc>
When you wish to know the life of a <term>native</term> <note>The person born at the time the chart was cast</note> by God’s command: if he was born in the day, take it from the Sun. If the Sun is in the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The 1st house, representing the eastern horizon</note>, or in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>The 10th house, the highest point in the sky</note>, or in the <term>Setting</term> <note>original: "adtr," likely a corruption of "ad terra" or referring to the 7th house</note>—which is the 7th house from the Ascendant—or in the 11th house, and has not moved more than 5 degrees from the <term>cusp</term> <note>The starting point of an astrological house</note> of the house in which it resides; and if it is <term>received</term> <note>A supportive relationship where the ruler of a sign hosts the planet currently in that sign</note> by the Lord of the house or the <term>exaltation</term> <note>A specific sign where a planet's power is greatly magnified</note> of the sign it is in, then it will be useful as the Hyleg. And the planet that receives it will be the <term>Alcocoden</term> <note>The "Giver of Years," the planet that determines the length of life based on the Hyleg's strength</note>; and it is this planet that signifies the nature of the birth—that is, make it the giver of years, months, or days, and direct the division of those years, months, or days from the degree in which the Hyleg is found. 

But if the Sun is not in any of the places I have told you, or if it is in them but is distant from the degree of its place by more than ten degrees, or if there is no connection between it and the Lord of the house or the exaltation, then it will not be useful as the Hyleg. Leave it then, and look to the Moon. If the Moon is in the four angles or in the houses following the angles—which are the 11th, 2nd, 5th, and 8th houses (these are the eight places)—and it is not distant from the degree of its house by more than 5 degrees, and it is joined to the Lord of the house or the exaltation in which it resides, it will be useful as the Hyleg. Direct then the division of years, months, or days by God’s command. 

If the Moon is not in these eight named places, or is more than 5 degrees from the cusp, or is not joined to the Lord of the house or exaltation, it will not be useful as the Hyleg. Look then to the degree of the <term>Part of Fortune</term> <note>A mathematical point in a chart calculated from the positions of the Sun, Moon, and Ascendant</note>. If it falls in any of these eight places and is not more than 5 degrees from the cusp, and the Lord of its <term>term</term> <note>A specific subdivision of a sign ruled by a planet</note> or the Lord of its house is joined to it, it shall be useful as the Hyleg. In that case, the Lord of that house who is joined to it will be the giver of years, months, or days, and you shall direct the division from the degree of the Part of Fortune. But if the Lord is not joined to the Part of Fortune, then the Part of Fortune itself becomes the Hyleg, and the donation of years is known from its Lord. 

If the Part of Fortune is not in these eight places, or is too distant, leave it. Look then to the degree of the <term>syzygy</term> <note>original: "pūnctionis," referring to the New Moon or Full Moon</note> of the Sun and Moon before the birth. If it is in these eight places and its Lord is joined to it, it shall be the Hyleg. If the child was born exactly at the conjunction, the degree of that conjunction shall be the Hyleg. If that is not useful, leave it. Similarly, look to the degree of the <term>prevention</term> <note>original: "puentionis," referring to the Full Moon preceding birth</note>. If that degree

<column-break/>

is in the aforementioned eight places and not more than 5 degrees from the cusp, it will be useful as the Hyleg. If its Lord is joined to it, that Lord signifies the donation of years, months, or days. If the degree is in the right place but the Lord is not joined to it, the degree of the Full Moon itself will be the Hyleg. 

And if the degree of the conjunction is in those eight places but is too distant from the cusp, it will not be a useful Hyleg; leave it then and look to the degree of the Ascendant, for it shall be the Hyleg. Its Lord shall be the giver and significator of years, months, or days. If the Lord of the Ascendant is not joined to the degree, then the degree of the Ascendant itself shall be the Hyleg. 

You shall work at night just as you work during the day, equally in all hours; but in the day you begin with the Sun, then the Moon, then the Part of Fortune, then the conjunction or Full Moon, and finally the degree of the Ascendant. When you have projected these points, and your location is in the degree of the Ascendant, the life of the child will not be prolonged unless the Ascendant is free from the <term>casting of light</term> <note>Aspects or rays of influence</note> of the "malefics" <note>Planets traditionally considered harmful: Saturn and Mars</note>. Do not neglect the <term>B</term> <note>original: "B̄," likely an abbreviation for a specific astrological operation or "Beibeniae" (fixed stars)</note> when you find the Lord of the birth, so that you may look at the extension of the planets' rays to the Hyleg. The rays are a powerful thing, unless a "benefic" <note>A lucky planet: Sun, Venus, Jupiter, or Moon</note> looks upon it, for the aspect of the good ones breaks the strength of the evil ones—provided the evil ones do not have more degrees than the good. Do not neglect the "hurling" of the malefics' rays at the Hyleg; but when the planet ruling the birth is strong, the Lord of the birth shall not perish, by God's command. Even if he encounters hardships and labors, he shall be delivered from them by God’s command.

### Chapter on the Years of the Alcocoden

<margin>Finding the Alcocoden</margin>
<image-desc>Decorative drop cap 'E' featuring a standing figure with a staff or similar object in an ornate square frame.</image-desc>
And when you have found the one who rules the birth in the Ascendant, the Midheaven, or the 7th angle, and it has emerged from under the Sun's rays <note>meaning it is no longer "combust" or blinded by the Sun's light</note>—that is, it is not direct under the rays, nor in its descent—it will give its **Greater Years**. 

If it is in the 4th angle (which is under the earth) and it is in its own term, house, exaltation, <term>triplicity</term> <note>A group of three signs belonging to the same element</note>, or <term>face</term> <note>A 10-degree subdivision of a sign</note>, and it is <term>oriental</term> <note>Rising before the Sun</note>, it will give its **Greater Years**. 

If it is in the 11th or 5th house and is oriental and dignified by term, house, exaltation, triplicity, or face, it will give its **Greater Years**. 

If it is in the 11th or 5th house and is oriental but NOT in its own term or other dignities, it will give its **Middle Years**. 

If it is in the 2nd or 8th house and is in its own term, exaltation, house, triplicity, or face, it will give its **Middle Years**. 

If it is not in its own term or dignity, but is also NOT in its descent, nor in a "pit," nor in a place where it is "sad" <note>A planet is "sad" when it is in a sign or house contrary to its nature</note>, it will similarly give its **Middle Years**. 

If it is in the 9th house and is oriental and dignified, it will give its **Middle Years**—provided it is a day birth and the ruler is Saturn, or a night birth and the ruler is a nocturnal planet. 

If it is in the 6th or 12th house and not in its descent, it will give its **Lesser Years**. If it is in its descent in the 12th or 6th house and is <term>retrograde</term> <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky</note>, it will give **Months**...

# On Interrogations

...months according to the number of his minor years <note>In traditional astrology, each planet is assigned "major," "middle," and "minor" sets of years to determine life span. Minor years are the shortest duration.</note>; that is, in the place of every single year, he shall give months. And if he is under the rays of the Sun <note>original: "sub radijs solis"; this refers to "combustion," where a planet is too close to the Sun to be seen, weakening its power</note>, retrograde in his descent, and in the 12th or 6th [house] from the Ascendant, he shall give days according to the number of his minor years; that is, in the place of each single year, he shall give a day.

And if you find the one who rules the birth—namely, in an angle—to be retrograde or under the rays of the Sun, he shall give his middle years. And if he is in the houses following the angles <note>known as "succedent" houses</note>, being retrograde or under the Sun’s rays, he shall give his minor years. And if he is falling away from the angles <note>known as "cadent" houses</note> and is retrograde under the Sun’s rays, he cannot give minor years, but shall give a month in the place of one year. 

And when the ruler has given the years, and all the <term>fortunes</term> <note>the benefic planets, Jupiter and Venus</note> behold him by a square aspect, or opposition, or by a sextile or trine aspect, or are with him in one sign, they increase [the years] for him according to the quantity of degrees that are in the hourly time of that degree in which he is, by one year for each degree—provided that the planet which increases them is not retrograde or under the Sun’s rays. And when the planets that signify increase are in the 6th or 12th [house] from the Ascendant, they increase nothing.

And if any of the <term>malefic</term> <note>the harmful planets, Saturn and Mars</note> planets behold the ruler by any aspect—namely the 4th, 10th, trine, 7th, or sextile—or if it is with him, wherever it may be, it shall diminish for him according to the number of degrees that are in the hourly time of that degree in which he is in decline, which was the birth, by one year for every single degree of the hourly times.

And I found in a certain book, though I have not proven it: that when you find the <term>Tail</term> <note>the South Node of the Moon, considered a point of depletion</term> not far from the ruler of the birth—within 8 degrees—it will diminish a fourth part of the years of that ruler. And if it is the <term>Head</term> <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, it will likewise diminish a fourth part of the years.

And know that the extension of the rays of the planets is made from equal degrees. But give the years to the <term>Hyleg</term> <note>the planet or point acting as the "giver of life"</note> through the degrees of ascension, and do not neglect the granting of years from the Ascendant through the degrees of ascension.

And know that when you calculate the granting of years, months, or days from the degree of the Hyleg, or from the degree of the Ascendant, for every single degree a year, or month, or day—wherever you find evil, it shall be observed where the degree you have drawn from the Hyleg or the Ascendant has reached. And know that if any of these four fortunes behold the degree reached by the grant you calculated from the Hyleg or the Ascendant, he shall escape and be delivered from death—unless there are malefic degrees that behold the place where the division has reached more than the [benefic] degrees. That is, if the malefic degrees are more than the degrees of the fortunes, this signifies that the native shall endure until the degrees you directed from the Hyleg pass the degree of the fortune; and when these have passed and reach the malefic degrees, it shall then signify death.

And know that when a birth occurs, and the ruler of it is in a strong place, if a malefic planet projects its rays upon the degree of the sign of life, or upon the degree of the Sun, or the degree of the Moon, or the degree of the Hyleg—whatever it may be—the native shall not succumb to death until the ruler of the birth completes the number of years he signified according to the quality of that place in which he was: namely, from the major, middle, or minor years, or months, or days, or hours, if God wills it.

And I will explain to you the <term>casting of rays</term>; understand it. Some think the casting of rays is such that a planet which is in the 10th [house] receives rays from that which is in the 4th from it. And that which is in the 4th from it projects its rays to the one in the 10th from it. And therefore it is called the "casting of rays" in these four ways I have mentioned: because that which is before it in the 4th projects rays to that which is placed after it in the 10th before this one which is in the 4th; because that which goes before it projects its warm rays to the part placed behind it similarly. For example, that which is in Aries beholds that which is in Cancer, and that which is in Cancer projects its rays to that which is in Aries.

And the greatest part of the wise men agreed to place those five degrees which are before the degree of the Ascendant within the strength of the Ascendant; in which, 

<column-break/>

when the Sun is present, they say it is useful for it to be the Hyleg when it is received; and the Moon similarly, and the others from which the Hyleg is similarly found. However, regarding the ruler who signifies the granting of years: when he is remote from the degree of the Ascendant, and is in the 5th degree before the angle, they said he cannot give major years, but they give middle years. 

And it seemed right to us thus to prepare this book: so that one might know the ruler and the Hyleg, and after this, one might know what he signifies concerning years, months, days, or hours. When we have learned what he holds concerning these, we shall direct from the degree of the Hyleg to the square aspect of the malefics and their opposition toward death; afterward, we shall then see whether any fortune projects its light upon the place of the malefic degree, or not. If there is some fortunate planet projecting its light upon the place of the malefic light, he shall be delivered after suffering. After this, you shall direct it also to the square aspect of the other malefic, and to its opposition; and the malefics give testimony when they are weakened in a trine or sextile aspect. 

When, however, he would signify concerning the degrees from the Hyleg up to the light—that is, to the rays of the malefic—we say that they shall be years, or months, or days, or hours, according to what the ruler signifies. And when you know the division which the ruler signifies—whether they are years, or months, or days, or hours—you shall direct that division from the degree of the Hyleg up to the 4th aspect of the malefics and their opposition toward death. 

A certain leader <note>original: "duce"</note> whom the King of Africa appointed, with another speaking

I observed this interrogation by the will of God, and its planets were as I tell you.

# Messahallach

...and in all the <term>angles</term> <note>The four most powerful houses in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note> to the lord of the interrogation who is in a more worthy place—namely, the place of the lord's exaltation and of the kingdom. And then the Sun was joined [to them], and Venus was in her own house; and she received them from her own house with a strong <term>reception</term> <note>A favorable relationship where planets "host" one another in their respective signs</note>. The Sun also received her through his light. These testimonies regarding his fortune were joined to him by the will of God, and this signified the strength of the lord of the interrogation over his enemy, the stability of his honor, that he would obtain his kingdom, and that he would partly manage that which had been committed to him by his emperor and would be in his hand. There would be nothing he would not obtain by the will of God.

After this, I looked at the one who was in Africa, who was suspected of being a rebel, contrary, disobedient, and destined to be deposed. [I looked] at the <term>nadir</term> <note>In this context, the point directly opposite the Ascendant, marking the 7th house of enemies</note>—that is, from the opposite of the Ascendant and from its lord, and from the planet to which the Moon was joined. The nadir was the sign of Gemini, and none of the seven planets were in it. Its lord was Mercury, one of the inferior planets, and he was <term>retrograde</term> <note>Appearing to move backward in the sky, usually a sign of weakness or reversal</note> and <term>cadent</term> <note>Falling away from the powerful "angles" of the chart, indicating lack of influence</note> in the 12th sign from the Ascendant. After his period of direct motion, he was joined to Saturn by an opposition aspect. However, Saturn was cadent in the 6th sign from the Ascendant and was also retrograde.

Therefore, Mercury signified through his retrogradation and descent—and through his conjunction with a cadent and retrograde planet—the annulment of those things which that enemy and idler had entered into. Rather, it would be the annulment of all his affairs and the dissolution of his power. His fall in the 12th house from the Ascendant, and Saturn's fall in the 12th from the nadir, signified the weakness falling upon the enemy and adversary—namely, the strong one—and the dispersion of that gathering, the fall of his name or his memory, the annulment of what he prepared and collected, and their destruction by the will of God.

After this, I looked at the lord of the interrogation and the planet from which the Moon was separating. The Moon was separating from Jupiter, who is the lord of the Ascendant, and Jupiter was in the "angle of heaven" <note>the 10th house, representing career and authority</note>. He is among the higher planets, holding the highest place after Saturn. Jupiter signified, by the command of God, through the height and goodness of his placement, the strength of the lord of the interrogation, the stability of his honor, the obtaining of his princedom, and those things about which he had asked concerning honor—namely, the leadership which his emperor and ordainer had committed to him by the command of God.

Then I looked at him who was thought to be a rebel and to be deposed because he had been disobedient. [I looked] at the planet to which the Moon was joining. The Moon was joining Mars, and Mars was cadent in his descent and retrograde—that is, in the 8th house from the Ascendant, which is the 2nd from the nadir, the place of "helpers"—that is, the soldiers of the one suspected of rebellion and his subjects. The conjunction of the Moon and Mars, and the retrogradation of Mars and his fall in descent, signified the dissolution of the works of that enemy and adversary, his turning back from the counsel he had entered, his repentance over what he had set in motion, his subjection, and the loss of his honor by the command of God.

And the Moon’s location in the 7th sign from the Ascendant (which is the place of the soldiers and helpers of the one asking the question, and also the place of his subjects) signified that the Moon is the mistress of the significator of the enemy and adversary, and she is the significatrix of his soldiers and helpers. The Moon was joined to Mars by opposition, and each of them received their companion with a strong reception. Therefore, by the will of God, the entry of the Moon (who signifies the helpers of the enemy and adversary) into Capricorn (which is the place of the helpers of the lord of the interrogation and the place of his subjects) signified the petition of the enemy's soldiers... namely, the fulfillment of their hope of acquiring subjects, and that they would receive a portion of what they expected by the will of God, and that they would enter into obedience and the aid of the lord of the interrogation. This would happen after they received the things in which they had hope—namely, the gifts they expected to receive by the will of God. The location of the Moon in Capricorn and Mars in Cancer also signified that they would not receive everything they hoped to receive, or as they thought they would. The conjunction of the Moon to Mars by opposition signified that the soldiers of the adversary would be in petition for subjects in the position; for this was their intention, and this they sought by the will of God.

After this, I looked at the opposing enemy to see what would become of his being and the being of the one who succeeded him. I looked at Mercury, who was the significator of the enemy; namely, to whom he was joined 

<column-break/>

and who was joined to him. I found him to be joined to Saturn after his direct motion by an opposition, which is an aspect of contrariety and enmity. Saturn was the lord of the 2nd house of the interrogation and the lord of the 3rd of the same, which are the places of his soldiers, brothers, and helpers. There was no reception between them. This signified that the enemy himself would find certain people opposed to him who would return the favor to him and dismiss his word—that is, his obedience—from among his brothers and soldiers by the will of God.

After this, I looked at which of them would have victory and the obtaining of the kingdom. I looked at the lords of those houses, because their significators were cadent from the angles. We saw that for those who fought against the enemy (from Mercury) and the adversary (from Saturn) and from the lord of his house: Saturn was cadent and retrograde, and the mistress of his house was Venus. Venus was in the ascending angle, <term>combust</term> <note>original: "combusta"; hidden and weakened by being too close to the Sun's light</note> under the rays of the Sun. Her location in the angle in Sagittarius (because it is a common sign) signified a repetition of the battle by those who opposed the enemy—that is, that those who opposed the enemy would repeat the battle against him twice or more, and they would happen upon the zeal of battle. The combustion of Venus signified their consumption, flight, and destruction by the will of God.

After this, I looked at the same opposing enemy to see what his strength and victory would be toward those who opposed him. I looked at him through his significator and the lord of his house. His significator was Mercury, and the lord of his house was Mars. Mars was in Cancer in his descent and retrograde, and this signified weakness in the beginning of his work by the command of God. I also looked to see whether Mars was joined to anyone who might comfort him, or if any planet was joined to him who might help him. I found the Moon joined to him from the exaltation of Mars, and each of them received their companion with a strong reception. This, therefore, signified the victory of the opposing enemy over his enemies, and that he would subject them to himself and take whatever they had in their hands of the kingdom by the command of God.

Then I looked at what would happen between the lord of the interrogation and the opposing enemy, and how the lord of the interrogation would obtain the kingdom, and whether he would have it through battle or through peace. I looked, therefore, at Jupiter, who was the significator of the lord of the interrogation, and Mercury, who was the significator of the opposing enemy who was suspected of being a rebel. [I looked to see] from which part of the circle they beheld each other. I found each of them projecting his light upon his companion from a <term>sextile</term> aspect <note>A harmonious 60-degree angle</note>—namely, of peace, quiet, and concord. And this signified the success of the lord of the interrogation among those whom he ruled, and his exaltation over [the rebel] would be through peace and through "lightness" <note>likely meaning ease or lack of hardship</note>. The enemy who was suspected of being a rebel would seek security and peace, because Mercury was returning to Jupiter, and he was the lighter of the two stars. Therefore, he was joined to this by the will of God.

->Here ends the book of Messahallach on interrogations.<-

Here begins the epistle of Messahallach, briefly elucidated, regarding the matters of lunar eclipses, the conjunctions of the planets, and the revolutions of the years. And in it there are twelve chapters. 

The first chapter is on the nature of the circle and the stars and how they operate in this world. The 2nd chapter is on the diversity of the "trace"—that is, the work of the stars—in the regions of the earth. The 3rd chapter is on the signs and their natures, namely hot and cold, and which of them are fixed or movable, diurnal or nocturnal. The 4th chapter is on the revolution of years. The 5th chapter is on the eclipse of the Moon and its significance. The 6th chapter is on the change of times through the movement of the planets in the signs—namely, of the heavy planets. The 7th chapter is on the eclipse of the Sun and its significance. The 8th chapter is on the conjunction of the planets and its work. The 9th chapter is on the conjunction...

<meta>This page transitions from the specific political "interrogation" regarding an African rebellion onto a new, more general treatise by the astrologer Messahallach (Masha'allah ibn Athari). It begins with a general cosmology before detailing the astrological principles of weather, seasons, and global events.</meta>

...conjunction of the higher planets. 10th month in the great conjunction. 11th month in the middle conjunction. 12th month in the minor conjunction.

### ¶ The first chapter on the nature of the circle and the stars, and how they operate in this world.

Messahallach said: When the most high Lord made the earth in the likeness of a sphere, and made the circle of the higher spheres revolving around it, and placed the earth fixed and immobile in the middle of the circle—turning neither to the right nor to the left—He placed the four elements as mobile things, and made them move through the motion of the seven planets. The Head of the Dragon <note>The North Node of the Moon, associated with karmic or fated events</note>, the signs, and all the stars participate with the seven planets in their works and natures. Therefore, the work of the planets in this world is like a magnet and iron; because just as iron is drawn by this stone across a known distance, so every creature and all things that are upon the earth are affected by the motion of the planets. For all things upon the earth—whether the fortune or hindrance of seeds or animals, their flourishing or destruction—happen from the motions of the planets and their works. The greatest proof of this is the diversity of men in their being, and in their fortunes and misfortunes. And because we see some rational people deprived of goods, while some fools enjoy goods, does this not have some signifying cause? For fortune and misfortune happen without the choice and will of those who suffer them—namely the fortunate and unfortunate—and all this, by the nature of God, is the work of the planets and their [conveyed] fortune and misfortune.

### ¶ The second chapter on the diversity of the traces of the stars' work in the regions of the earth.

Know that the work of the planets is diverse according to the diversity of <term>climates</term> <note>Geographical zones or latitudes</note>; because in certain climates some planets become bringers of fortune, while in another climate they are bringers of evil, in different orders. Therefore, every rational person ought to understand the reasons of the climates and regions; such as the region of the Ethiopians where there is always heat, and the land of the Slavs <note>original: "sclauoꝝ", referring to Northern and Eastern European peoples</note> where there is always cold. When the planets signify excessive cold to the citizens of Ethiopia, it tempers their air; but when they signify this to the Slavs, it will corrupt their air and their habitation will perish. For this reason, the science of the reasoning of climates, regions, and atmospheres is necessary. Know also that the science of the stars is very difficult; and what most worthily should be known from it is the general and the particular—namely the revolutions of the years and eclipses—and to understand the significations of all these things. This cannot be done except through the knowledge of the natures of the signs, and what each one signifies regarding regions, provinces, and all things. We have already spoken of this in our other books, but now I will speak of the property of these things briefly, and now we begin with God's help.

### ¶ The third chapter on the natures of the signs.

The signs are twelve. In each sign there are 30 degrees; in each degree 60 minutes; and in each minute 60 seconds; and so on down to the size of a point—that is, even unto infinity. These are their names: Aries, Taurus, and the rest. They have significations over Fire, Air, Water, and Earth. For three of them are fiery: namely Aries, Leo, and Sagittarius. Three are earthy: Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn. Three are airy: Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius. And three are aquatic: Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces. The fiery signs are hot, and the aquatic are cold; the earthy are also cold, and the airy are hot. Know that all hot signs are masculine and the cold are feminine; all masculine signs are diurnal [of the day], and the feminine are nocturnal [of the night]. There are also four <term>moveable</term> <note>Cardinal</note> signs in which the seasons change: Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn. There are four <term>fixed</term> signs in which the season is established: Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius. Four also are <term>double-bodied</term> <note>Mutable</note> or common, in which two seasons are joined: Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces. These are the natures of the signs; understand them.

<column-break/>

### ¶ The fourth chapter on the revolution of the years.

When you wish to know what happens in the world regarding rains, winds, and so forth: establish the <term>Ascendant</term> <note>The sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> of the Sun's entry into the first point of Aries <note>The spring equinox, used to cast a "year-ahead" chart</note>, and establish the seven planets at that same hour. Having made the figure [the astrological chart], consider which of them presides over it. If it is a planet of fortune, the weather will be favorable; but if it is an evil or hindered planet, the world will be corrupted. Do similarly for the quarters of the year and its months. Know that when several planets are joined in aquatic signs at the revolution of the year, they will signify a multitude of rain; in fiery signs they will signify a superfluity of heat and dryness or sterility of the earth; in airy signs they will signify a multitude of winds; and in earthy signs they will signify frost and snow. Similarly, in the quarters of the year, when planets are in cold places, they will signify the weight of cold and the lessening of heat. Know also that when Mars and Saturn preside over the chart and the fortunes do not <term>aspect</term> <note>Form a geometric relationship with</note> them, they signify a multitude of war and the destruction of the world. So also when Mars is the lord of the summer quarter and is in any of the houses of Mercury, he will signify a multitude of rains and pestilences. Know that the weight of dryness and sterility of the earth or scarcity of grain does not happen except from the conjunction of planets in fiery signs. Understand this and test it according to what has been told to you, and you will find it so.

### ¶ The fifth chapter on the eclipse of the Moon and its signification.

Messahallach said: You must consider the eclipses of the year, both lunar and solar, and know the Ascendant of the middle of the eclipse and the planet that presides over that same Ascendant and its chart. If that planet is evil, it will signify hindrance and destruction; if it is a fortune, it signifies favor. Know that when a lunar eclipse occurs in cold signs, it signifies the weight of cold; and in aquatic signs, a superfluity of rain—provided the season matches (namely, if it is winter). If it is summer, it signifies a tempering of the air. Understand and test the rest likewise. Understand also that when the fortunes aspect the Moon and <term>receive</term> <note>A favorable relationship where planets "host" one another</note> her, her signification in those things she signifies will be toward good and profit.

### ¶ The sixth chapter on the change of seasons through the movement of the planets.

Messahallach said: When you wish to foreknow the variety of seasons over the various things of this corruptible world, know the signs of the <term>heavy planets</term> <note>The slower-moving outer planets: Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars</note>, whether they are hot or cold. If they are hot, they will signify heat in summer and a tempering of the air in winter. If they are in cold signs, they will signify cold in winter and tempering in summer. Similarly, when planets are joined in aquatic signs, it signifies superfluous rains and the corruption of the air through those same rains in winter, but a tempering of the air and a multitude of dew in summer. According to this, test it, for you will not err. The heavy planets are Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars; you ought also to join the Sun to them. Know that the heavy planets, when they are directly over some region, will signify dryness as well as sterility of the earth; but when they are distant from it, they signify a multitude of rains. I want it to be understood that "proximity" means when they are in northern signs, and "distance" means in southern signs. Know also that when the heavy planets are all <term>oriental</term> <note>Rising before the Sun</note>, they will signify dryness; and when they are <term>occidental</term> <note>Setting after the Sun</note>, they will signify a multitude of rains in winter and tempering of the air in summer. Similarly, at their rising, they signify favor of the air in winter and excessive dryness in summer.

Messahallach
<meta>catchword: It begins</meta>

### ¶ Chapter 7 on the solar eclipse and its significance.

Messahallach <note>The Latinized name for Masha'allah ibn Athari (c. 740–815 AD), a Persian Jewish astrologer and astronomer who was a leading figure in early Abbasid Baghdad.</note> said: Know that in a solar eclipse, it cannot happen without some great event being signified, according to the magnitude of the eclipse itself: that is, if it covers a quarter of the sun's body or more. The knowledge of those things that happen from a solar eclipse is found thus: you must know the <term>ascendant</term> <note>The degree of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of the eclipse.</note> of the middle of the eclipse, and the planets that are dominant over the eclipse's figures. If these planets are <term>malefic</term> <note>Specifically Saturn and Mars, traditionally associated with hardship and destruction.</note>, they will signify evil, loss, and the death of kings and the wealthy. But if they are <term>benefic</term> <note>Specifically Jupiter and Venus, associated with growth and prosperity.</note>, they will signify good fortune and the success of those kings. Know also that when a solar eclipse occurs in Aries, it will signify the death of kings and the wealthy, as well as drought or sterility of the earth and famine; and it is the same in the other fire signs <note>Leo and Sagittarius.</note>. In the water signs, however, it will signify a multitude of rains and damage caused by them. Understand that if the benefics aspect these points, they will diminish the evil; but if the malefics aspect them, they will increase the evil and diminish the good fortune. Know also that when the Sun or Moon acts as the <term>hyleg</term> <note>The "Giver of Life," a specific point in a chart used to determine longevity.</note> or the <term>alchochoden</term> <note>The planet that rules the hyleg, used to calculate the length of a person's life.</note> and is weakened, it signifies great danger or grave illness for the person to whom they belong, unless the benefics provide relief.

### ¶ Chapter 8 on the conjunction of all the planets and their effects.

Messahallach said: The conjunction <note>When two or more celestial bodies appear in the same area of the sky.</note> of planets signifies the events of this world and its affairs. These are considered at the time of the conjunction of the higher and lower planets: if the benefics signify fortune and a good outcome, they will dominate the figure of the conjunction; if, however, the malefics dominate, they will signify evil and a bad outcome. Know also that when they are joined in any of the signs, they signify a multitude of losses according to the nature of that sign. That is: if the conjunction is in the water signs, it will signify damage from rains, and so on for the other signs. If they are joined in feminine signs, they will signify pestilence and death among female animals; and the same is said for masculine signs. Know that conjunctions and eclipses of the <term>luminaries</term> <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note> when they occur in <term>fixed signs</term> <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius; signs associated with stability and endurance.</note> will signify the long duration of evil and its damage; if they are in <term>mutable signs</term> <note>Aries, Cancer, Libra, and Capricorn; signs associated with change.</note>, they signify a short duration of evil and damage; but if they are in <term>common signs</term> <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces.</note>, they signify a moderate evil—and say the same for good things.

### ¶ Chapter 9 on the conjunction of the higher planets.

Messahallach said: Know that the greatest and most wonderful things happen from the conjunction of the higher planets <note>Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars.</note>, and this occurs because of the slowness of their motion. When these three are joined in one <term>term</term> or <term>face</term> <note>Sub-divisions of a zodiac sign used to refine astrological power.</note> and the Sun aspects them, they signify the destruction of religious sects and kingdoms, their transformation, and great events according to the power of the strongest among them who dominates their signs. This is their "Great Conjunction," which signifies prophecy, the destruction of certain climates, and momentous things, especially if any of the lower planets assist them. Know that the strongest among them will be the significator. If it is a benefic, it will signify fortune. If it is a malefic, it will signify evil and tribulation. Understand also that when these planets are joined in their <term>exaltations</term> <note>Signs where a planet's influence is considered most powerful and positive.</note>, they will signify good and a favorable time, though also a multitude of wars and the showing of miracles. But if they are joined in their <term>falls</term> <note>Signs where a planet is considered weak or hindered.</note>, they will signify loss, drought, sterility of the earth, and famine, unless they are otherwise made fortunate. Know that when they are joined in a fire sign, they signify sterility of the earth; in a water sign, a multitude of rain; in an air sign, the strength of winds; and in an earth sign, an excess of cold and loss. When they are joined in masculine signs, they signify the loss of male animals, and likewise for females.

<column-break/>

### ¶ Chapter 10 on the Greater Conjunction.

Messahallach said: we have already stated that principal events happen from the Greater Conjunction, which is the conjunction of the higher planets. But there are other conjunctions of these higher planets that signify even greater events. For the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter is the "Greatest Conjunction," and this signifies major events and changes in religious sects. Knowledge of the events is gained from it by looking at the ascendant and the planets at the hour of their conjunction, and which of them rules the figure. If it is a benefic, it signifies good and a favorable time. If it is a malefic, it signifies loss, drought, sterility of the earth, and wars. Know therefore that when Jupiter is stronger than Saturn, he signifies a good place in that conjunction. If, however, Saturn prevails, he signifies loss and tribulation. Know that their conjunction in fire and air signs signifies drought, sterility of the earth, and difficulty in childbirth; in earth signs, the destruction of seeds and famine. In water signs, it will signify an excess of rain and pestilence, provided they are hindered. If, finally, they are fortunate, they will signify an increase of good in all they signify, and a lessening of evil. Also, know that when a Greater Conjunction occurs in any of the <term>angles</term> <note>The four most powerful points in a chart: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses.</note> and especially in the <term>Midheaven</term> <note>The highest point in the sky, representing kingship and public career.</note>, it will signify the appearance of a king or a prophet from the direction of that sign. If that sign is fortunate and its lord is in a good state, it signifies his triumph and dominion. If it is hindered and its lord is weak, it signifies his death and downfall; and the conjunction should be feared after the known years of that conjunction which we have mentioned elsewhere.

### ¶ Chapter 11 on the Middle Conjunction.

Messahallach said: the "Middle Conjunction" is the conjunction of Mars and Saturn. This signifies the events of wars, conflicts, and disagreements. When you wish to know these events, look to the ruler in the figure of their conjunction: if it is a benefic, it signifies good and a favorable state. If it is a malefic, it signifies evil and its hindrance. Know also that their conjunction in the signs of men <note>Zodiac signs depicted as humans: Gemini, Virgo, Libra, and Aquarius.</note> signifies a multitude of human illnesses. Their conjunction in any of the angles of the year signifies long-lasting conflict between kings and a multitude of wars; and the matter will last until they are joined another time. Their conjunction in fire signs signifies drought and sterility; in air signs, winds; in water signs, a multitude of rains; and in earth signs, frost, snow, and much cold. Know also that when benefics aspect them, they diminish the evil, and malefics increase it; test this as I have told you, and you will find it true if God wills.

### ¶ Chapter 12 on the Minor Conjunction.

Messahallach said: the "Minor Conjunction" is the conjunction of Jupiter and Mars. This signifies events resulting from rains and snows, the corruption of the air, and war. If a benefic prevails in their conjunction, it signifies fortune; if a malefic, evil. Know that when Jupiter and Mars are joined in the ascendant of the year or in any of its angles, it signifies the upheaval and change of a king, unless the benefics aspect them. Know also that whenever a benefic is joined with a malefic, the nature of the stronger one will appear. And when a malefic is joined with another malefic, the evil will abound, unless the one presiding over the conjunction is a benefic. Understand: this is the last of what we have set forth in this book from the secrets of the science of the astronomers. 

¶ The book of Messahallach is completed, translated by John of Seville <note>A prolific 12th-century translator who turned many Arabic scientific texts into Latin.</note> in Limia from Arabic into Latin, under the praise of God and by His help.
